Heading: Urdu-medium girls’ school in Old Delhi in a shambles - Indian Express
Content:
NOIDA police have begun investigations in the murder case of Conrad Dominic Xavier, the HCL call centre employee whose body was found in Sector 27, Noida, on Sunday. The family of the victim claimed that Xavier had spoken to his mother the night he was killed and had told his parents that he would resign shortly to be with them.

Talking to Newsline, his father Valentine Xavier said his son was thinking of returning to Purulia in West Bengal, where his family lives, to assist him.

"Xavier spoke to his mother around 11.45 pm. He was planning to come back home after resigning from the call centre. He was a simple, obedient boy," said his father.

According to Vijay Singh, station house officer, Sector 20 police station, Xavier used to live with his sister Susan in Sahibabad. Police are suspecting that someone close to the victim might be involved in the murder. "There were no signs of forced entry in the room where Xavier was found murdered. We are interrogating his friends and acquaintances. His colleagues of Xavier in HCL are being questioned as well," said Rajiv Narayan Mishra, first circle officer, Gautam Budh Nagar.

Xavier's colleagues said that he was a jovial person. "We knew he had a girlfriend with whom he had broken off sometime back. They had gone for a vacation a month ago and upon their return he said that they were no longer together. His sister Susan Xavier told us that on Saturday Xavier had gone to a hospital with a close friend and had come back late," said a colleague on condition of anonymity.

Meanwhile, the body was handed over to the family of the deceased. Officials at the Delhi airport, however, refused to let the body be boarded on a plane on Monday, as the family could not produce death certificate. "We did not know the procedure and brought only the postmortem report with us. We are trying to get the certificate by tomorrow and then fly back," said Arnold Xavier, the victim's uncle.

Heading: BJP eyes 40 seats in unauthorised colonies - Indian Express
Content:
Chashma Building in Ballimaran, which houses an Urdu-medium girls' school, is in a decrepit state. The building, rented out to the government in 1958, has visible cracks on its walls and high tension wires nearly touching it.

Shop owners on the ground floor said water seeps in through the ceiling. Plaster and concrete fall off the school's parapets onto the narrow street.

Around 700 girls attend the Government Girls' Senior Secondary School located in the bend of the narrow street. It is the only higher secondary school for girls in Ballimaran ward.

"The building is in very bad shape," said Mudasser Ali, a shopkeeper whose house is across the road. "If the building collapses, one cannot imagine the amount of damage it will cause."

Crumbling buildings are not uncommon in Old Delhi area. After several old buildings collapsed, the MCD was to draft a comprehensive policy for dangerous buildings in the city and take steps to ensure that they were repaired at intervals. In Old Delhi alone, there are more than 40,000 buildings that are more than 60 years old, according to the MCD.

Most of these stand neck-and-neck on busy one-lane streets. Though Chashma Building was let out in the 1950s, the building itself was built more than 60 years ago, said residents.

One of the owners of the building, Dr Ausafur Rahman, said he has approached government officials regarding the condition of the building, but no action was taken.

After a newspaper reported the building as "dangerous" last year, Rahman took the matter to court and filed a case against the Delhi administration, the MCD and the L-G.

No decision has yet been taken, nor has he heard from officials, Rahman said. "If the building is dangerous, the liability is on us. Children play on the roof. There are cracks," he said. "We wanted school to continue. But now we are concerned. In all these years, no repairs have been made and now it is too late. It will have to be demolished, he said.

The building was rented to the government at a nominal rent and is considered a landmark building — the area being lined with shops selling and repairing glasses.

Rahman said he wants the building to be vacated and demolished. For Sidra Sadiq, who attends a government primary Urdu-medium school in Ballimaran area, this is not good news. If this school is closed, she will have no place to go.

The only other school for girls in the area -— the Panama Building School — was moved to a site near Jama Masjid in 1979 after the building was declared dangerous. In the school, one can see cracks on the floor, the walls and even the staircase.

Teachers, however, said the building was not dangerous. The school was whitewashed a couple of months ago. But for the area's residents, that hardly helps.

Heading: E-mail threat to blow up Preet Vihar market, police on alert - Indian Express
Content:
While maintaining that the BJP's attempt will be to secure all 70 Assembly seats in the approaching elections, senior leaders of the party say field workers have been given instructions to work at getting as many votes as possible in unauthorised colonies — which have so far been traditional Congress seats.

Senior leaders in the present Opposition feel the Congress "has bungled" as far as unauthorised colonies in the Capital are concerned. The colonies constitute a part of as many as 40 assembly seats and some, like Badarpur and Sangam Vihar, even fall in the South Delhi seats. "We believe these seats will be an easy capture. Even if they are not, we can strive to wrest them from Congress hands. It is true that some amount of work is going on in these colonies but that is being carried out by the BJP-led MCD."

"After the municipal polls, Sheila Dikshit had announced that these colonies will be regularised within a month but they have been unable to do so. We feel they have lost the trust of the people and we have already issued instructions to our workers to put an extra effort in these areas. While we will be fighting on other issues as well this particular issue has also become very important,"said BJP state president Dr Harsh Vardhan.

There are approximately 50 lakh people who live in unauthorised colonies in Delhi. On February 7, 2007, the DDA for the first time came out with a Masterplan which included unauthorised colonies in its mapping. The very next day, the Union Cabinet of the UPA government passed a decision to regularise all unauthorised colonies in Delhi.

On October 5, 2007 the Urban Development Ministry came out with guidelines on how these colonies were to be regularised and instructed Delhi government to carry out the regularisation process within six months.

The development was to be carried out under the supervision of the Delhi government, the MCD was to carry out actual implementation of all development work and the DDA was to issue notifictions of change in land use as and when the state government forwarded the list of colonies. The Delhi Government then issued full-page advertisements asking for various RWAs and colonies to apply for this regularistion.

On March 4, 2008, the Ministry issued a second round of guidelines and gave Delhi government another six months to declare regularisation.

Sources say on May 11, 2008, the State government requested the Centre that they be allowed to issue provisional certificates.

"These certificates were supposed to be permanent certificates after work had been completed. In 10 years of Dikshit's rule and an entire year given to get these colonies developed, the Congress government could not complete the work. We will complete the work within months of our coming to power," said senior BJP leaders.

Sources said apart from the BJP, the BSP is also likely to get seats this time in these areas.

Heading: HC admits PIL seeking judicial inquiry on Jamia encounter - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi Police officers were on alert at Preet Vihar on Monday after they got a call from a private institution that had received an e-mail threatening that Preet Vihar market would be blown up. Police sources said they received the complaint about three to four days ago and had made all the necessary security arrangements.

"The e-mail says Preet Vihar A-block market will be blown up at 1.10 pm on October 20. We were there with a dog squad, security personnel and stood guard from noon to 3 pm," a senior police officer said.

The e-mail was sent in the name of 'Osama Bin Laden' said a senior police officer at the Preet Vihar police station said.

Preet Vihar police station officials said the e-mail was forwarded to them from the Delhi Police headquarters at ITO. "We were sent the e-mail by the police headquarters who had received it from the complainant," the police sources said.

A senior police officer said ever since they received the e-mail, they have been holding meetings with the market association to take all precautionary steps. "We had to share the information with them and we asked them to keep an eye on anyone they found suspicious and immediately inform the police," the senior police officer added. "Meetings with the local MLA and councillor were also held and we discussed the parking issue with them and asked them to decongest the parking areas of the market," said a senior police officer. Police sources added the e-mail was also forwarded to the Delhi Police's Special Cell, that is trying to trace the sender.

"We have approached Special Cell's for help in the matter and further investigations are on," the senior police officer said, adding, "the e-mail is not being taken lightly and the market will be given added security all through the festive season."

Heading: Judicial custody of Batla House caretaker extended by 14 days - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi High Court on Monday admitted a public interest litigation (PIL) seeking judicial inquiry into the September 19 Jamia Nagar police encounter in which two suspected militants were shot dead.

NGO 'Now for Harmony and Democracy' moved a Bench led by Justice Mukul Mudgal in a two-pronged attack on the police operation and a subsequent media report in the 'India Today' magazine which reportedly featured "confessions" of three arrested - Saquib Nissar, Zia-ur-Rahman and Shakeel - with regard to the serial blasts that rocked the Capital on September 13.

"We have sought a judicial probe into the encounter as a whole and also want action against the police officers who leaked the so-called confessions of the three accused to the media. We have prayed for contempt action against the magazine too," Prashant Bhushan, counsel for the NGO, said.

The Bench, however, refused to accede to a request by Bhushan to hear the petition on an urgent basis, and posted the case for hearing on November 7.

The petition voiced doubts about the police version that the persons killed at L-18 flat in Batla House were "militants" involved in the blasts.

"Some of the questions raised strike at the very root of the official version of the story regarding the said encounter. In light of the air of suspicion surrounding the police version, which itself seems ridden with discrepancies, an independent judicial probe into it is necessary to maintain people's faith in police," the petition said.

Bhushan sought the court's directions to both the police and the media against the publication of "defamatory material" related to the accused which might influence the trial.

"Leaking all kinds of stories to the media will only defame the accused and influence the upcoming trial," Bhushan said.

Heading: Delhi Police fail to submit encounter report, NHRC sends reminder - Indian Express
Content:
A Delhi court on Monday extended by 14 days, the judicial custody of Abdul Rehman, caretaker of L-18 Batla House in Jamia Nagar, where two suspected terrorists were killed in a shootout. Rehman was produced in Metropolitan Magistrate Praveen Singh's court today at the end of his remand period. On September 24, the court had dismissed his bail plea on the ground that the allegations were grave and the probe was at the initial stage. It had taken note of the fact that the tenants of Batla house flat, including Mohd Atif, who was killed in the encounter, were allegedly involved in the serial blasts that killed 26 persons in the Capital on September 13. M S Khan, counsel for the accused, had earlier alleged that police have failed to produce the original lease deed, a crucial piece of evidence, which was allegedly forged by Rehman.

Rehman, a stenographer with the UP Public Works Department, was arrested after flat owner Mohsin Nissar, told police he had forged his signature in the lease deed while giving away the flat to the two suspected terrorists on rent.

Heading: Accessorise - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi Police have failed to submit a detailed report in time on the Jamia Nagar encounter to the National Human Rights Commission, prompting the rights body to issue a reminder to the force.

The NHRC had issued a notice to Police Commissioner Y S Dadwal on September 23 asking him to submit a report within 15 days on the September 19 encounter in which two suspected Indian Mujahideen terrorists and a police inspector were killed.

Dadwal was to submit the report, which the NHRC sought by October 7, after an NGO raised questions about the encounter.

"The Commissioner of Police, Delhi, has not submitted the required report so far," the NHRC said today, adding that a reminder has been sent to Dadwal asking him to submit the report by October 31.

Heading: Causes on Reels - Indian Express
Content:
Ten new designers focus solely on accessories at the Delhi Fashion Week

As the city gears up for the clash of the fashion weeks, the Delhi Fashion Week and the Wills India Fashion Week that start barely a day apart, fashion watchers can be sure of one thing; to see more holistic work since the fallout of the FDCI has opened the platform to many new young designers, eager to showcase their work, some of it startling in its originality.

For the first time since the inception of Indian fashion, accessories, crucial elements in fashion will not be neglected. Ten accessory designers are showing for the first time at Delhi Fashion Week beginning on Tuesday. Bags, scarves, shawls, wrap dresses, jewellery stalls, even blankets dot the venue, Emporio Mall in Vasant Kunj. The look is defined by etching Kalidasa's poetry on silver, weaving sequins in hand weaves of Bengal and using Moroccan designs on a Cashmere shawl. "We received an overwhelming demand from buyers who attended the fashion week last time. Most of the designers showing here are currently exporters," says Geetanjali Kashyap of Fashion Foundation of India. Bangalore-based jewellery designer Deepti Sudhindra who has been in the circuit for nine years has found her niche by etching Henry David Thoreau's poetry on to silver, transforming a ubiquitous coconut shells into delicate beads, pendants and necklaces and contemporising the 200-year-old filigree craft of Karimnagar artists of Andhra Pradesh. "I take a coconut shells and embellish it with silver," explains Sudhindra, 32, who will be showcasing eight different collections. "My look is contemporary but the design element is essentially Indian," says Sudhindra who works on a commission basis.

Turning scarves, shawls and wraps into a heritage label is Kolkata based designer Bappaditya Biswas, 36, who founded Bai Lou in 2002. Closely working with weavers of Bengal, Biswas uses Jamdani and double cloth weaving techniques. "We don't believe in embellishments on top of the fabric. Everything is woven in and comes out as a finished product," says Biswas who works with 350 weavers. His collection has stoles in malta silk with geometrical patterns, scarves in a blend of silk and wool in an oyster pink and aqua blue. "Wearing scarves is a recent trend in India and the hand weaving craft of Bengal has got a boost," says Biswas.

But it is Nepal based fashion designer Yasmine Rana who has given the jaded crafts industry in the neighbouring country a lift, by incorporating traditional Nepalese designs into luxurious loungewear. Rana, of French origin, has been in the field for 25 years. Her collection—lounge wear, chic jackets in shining blue and jade green, cashmere shawls and blankets have a bourgeoisie elegance. "My designs are classy, multi-cultural and bold. I pick-up ideas from my travels, use local designs and natural material," she emphasises.

Among others, Peachy Bawa of Basta will show a range of leather bags, Delhi-based Shilu Kumar of Pashma will exhibit a collection of scarves and Jyotika Jhalani of the label Janavi will show a trendy line of beach garments, hand bags and high end wraps in silk and chiffon.

Heading: Folk Tales - Indian Express
Content:
A series of short films will try to bring up issues usually shoved under the carpet

As suicide bombings and child abuse become realities we come home to everyday, a series of short films to be screened in the city attempt to wake us from the slumber that we have resigned ourselves to. So Black and White, which will witness the screening of short films by five directors at the Weavers Studio Centre for Arts, will be addressing issues as varied as terrorism and poverty on one hand and alternative sexuality and destiny on the other hand.

The films to be screened are a mix of fiction, docu-drama and documentaries. While the longest film is squeezed into 30 minutes, the shortest is around 6 minutes long. "A short film is an effective medium to convey a social message. It can be pithy and hard-hitting," says director Abhishek Ganguli who will screen his docu-drama Bijoyini. The film traces the vicious nexus of traffickers and pimps which has trapped several girls from this side of the country in its net. "I shot the film at Swarupnagar, a village on the Bengal-Bangladesh border. It is based on the life of a girl who was trafficked to Bombay and ended up in the Kamathipura red light area," says Ganguli. The girl was eventually rescued and the film traces how she was rehabilitated.

Tathagata Bhattacharjee's Coloured explores a 'mindset which is the result of repeated terror attacks'. "It tells the story of a Pakistani citizen who comes to the city for treatment. However, soon people start suspecting him for extremist affiliations," says Bhattacharjee. A film like this throws up questions like what leads to criminalizing a whole national/religious identity, and can anybody be blamed for being scared and hence cynical?

The flair for contemporary issues extends to Arindam Basu's film called Aa Maatir Katha. Basu's film delves into the LGBT community's strife for rights and freedom of expression.

However, personal experiences expand into metaphors for life as Indrani Chakrabarty's film Destiny, traces how her robust, energetic great grandmother dwindles into a helpless, almost lifeless woman following a cerebral attack. "My great grandmother's life was the most poignant statement on the uncertainties of life," says Chakrabarty. The filmmaker got together footages of her great grandmother celebrating the former's wedding with shots of her as she slowly wasted away in the deathbed. "She suffered for 16 months and the agony was unbearable. It was then that I realised that this story was an eye-opener," says Chakrabarty.

Black and White will be on at the Weavers Studio Centre for Arts on October 24

Heading: Dempo to go out all guns blazing - Indian Express
Content:
In a new book, Arpana Caur pays tribute to folk art from the world over

"This is the Tithi bird. It has been cursed to live in fear of the sun," states artist Arpana Caur, as she looks at an ink and acrylic on canvas by Gond artist Rajendra Singh Shyam. She swiftly moves to the other side of the room to show us Jangarh Singh Shyam's bull with fine red dots painted on a black background on paper. The two works from her collection of folk art seem rather dissimilar, but the artist traces common elements as she points out that Rajendra was a disciple of Jangarh. She has been carefully studying every work in her Folk Art Museum for a long time, but during the last year the research has been more in-depth as she dedicated pages to each of them in the book titled The Magic Makers that will be released next month.

"With this we hope to reach people who may not be able to visit the museum. The aim is to popularise folk art," says Caur, as she sifts through the 300-page publication that has been neatly classified into different categories, in tandem with the display at the folk art museum. If the Midnapore patua portraying incidents from Ramayan finds place in the section on 'Folk Painting', then ceramic pots from Cambodia and Turkish teapots are under 'Images from Abroad'. Details about scrolls with tantric motifs are discussed by author PC Jain in a chapter on 'Tantra' and 'Sculptures' has several beaten metal artifacts from Bastar. "The classification puts the information in a streamlined manner," smiles Caur.

Amid the 500-odd objects of Folk art, Caur's canvases too find place in the publication in an article written by John H Bowles that narrates her collaboration with Mithila-based artist Sat Narayan Pandey for a show titled 'Between Dualities' that took place in 1997. While this had the duo work together on artwork, later Caur used motifs of folk art in several of her canvases. For instance, in 'Tears for Hiroshima' she paints godana motifs with the ruined Genbaku Dome to depict destruction caused by the bombing and 'Rites of Time' has Warli trees circling the canvas.

More contemporary themes, meanwhile, find place in work by folk artists. If Amrita Das portrays Tsunami in Sri Lanka in Mithal patterns, Bapi Chitrakar paints the Gujarat earthquake on a Bengali scroll and Gond artist Durga Bai has the Bhopal gas tragedy in an ink drawing.

As Caur checks the final proof of the book, also lined up are annual exhibitions on folk art. The beginning will be made with an exhibition on Bengal folk art featuring Roma Chatterji's collection that will take place on October 25 and up next are a series of curatorial shows that will feature work from Caur's museum. "Folk artists need to get their due," notes Caur. The book she says, has more tales related to folk art, bringing together the traditional and modern.

Heading: Mohun Bagan finally rope in Marcos - Indian Express
Content:
Beto's injury a concern, efforts are on to get him fit; coach calls for tight defending

History beckons Dempo. The Goan outfit and the defending I-League champions have already made the country proud by becoming the first Indian club to qualify for the AFC Cup semi-finals. A win tomorrow in the home match at Gachibowli Stadium in Hyderabad will take them on the threshold of an Asian elite status. The AFC Cup champions get a direct entry to the Asian Champions League.

Safa won the first-leg semi-final in Beirut, thanks to Hamze Aboud's 90th minute strike. Still the Indian football team coach Bob Houghton feels that Dempo has a very good chance to enter the final. "For last one year or so Dempo has been a success story as far as Indian football is concerned. The way they have been playing, they have a very good chance to go the distance," he said the other day.

The hosts have to win by a two-goal margin. A 1-0 victory will take the match into extra-time. They have to keep things tight to deny the visitors of an away goal. So, coach Armando Colaco, who is down with fever, has a job at hand. His deputy Mauricio Alfonso, who conducted the day's practice session, admitted that they were under pressure, but promised to go out with all guns blazing.

A lot, however, will depend on the availability of Roberto Silva Beto who appears a doubtful starter for tomorrow's game. The Brazilian striker is nursing a shoulder injury and didn't play for last one week. Good news is, he took part in today's training. Team physio and doctor are working overtime to ensure he takes the field.

Dempo midfielder Climax Lawrence sounded hopeful. "I won't be surprised if he plays. His mental strength is exemplary. He is very keen to play in this historic tie and our support staff are putting on extra efforts to get him fit," he told The Indian Express on match eve.

Midfielder Clifford Miranda and first-choice goalkeeper Abhijit Mondal too would be out for different reasons. While Miranada is suspended for this tie for picking up two yellow cards in last two matches, Mondal has a bad back.

Colaco seems unperturbed. "These things are pretty common in football. It shouldn't affect our performance.

"We have their replacements ready and they are in very good shape. I have put a lot of emphasis on defence organisation to avoid conceding goals. At the same time, we have to be aggressive" the coach said.

Safa too would be handicapped by the fact that they wouldn't be getting the service of Amer Khan, out suspended. But in Hamid Tarmina, they have a Moroccan midfielder who can play a pivotal role in the middle-third.

His incisive passing is a concern for any opposition defence and this is the precise reason why the Dempo boys want to mark him well. Striker Mohammad Kassas, whom Safa coach Samir Saad usually brings on as a substitute, too can pose a threat, especially when the defenders are tired.

So, a mouth-watering contest is on the cards. Referee Yuichi Nishimura from Japan will be the man in charge to control the show.

Heading: No smoke, nor fire, Trinamool’s Lalbazar march a damp squib - Indian Express
Content:
Mohun Bagan have finally managed to rope in Brazilian Marcos Pereira as his old club JCT gave the go-ahead today. The midfielder, who has been training with Bagan since the start of the I-League, couldn't play in any of the matches so far as he didn't get a clearance from the Punjab outfit. Today the player, accompanied by the Bagan officials had a meeting with the JCT management that sorted out the issue. Marcos' inclusion will be a morale boost for the beleaguered green-and-maroons who are currently placed 10th in the I-League standings with only two points to their credit. They will play their next match against East Bengal on Saturday.

Chelsea CEO meets Houghton

Chelsea chief executive officer Peter Kenyon arrived in Goa today and was received by the All India Football Federation (AIFF) secretary Alberto Colaco who said the visit would hopefully help cement a relationship with the English Premier League giants.

Colaco also said there's no agenda involved but talks will be held on the overall development of the game in the country.

"We are having a discussion right now. There will be an unofficial interaction with the media tomorrow," Colaco, who is in Goa now, said.

The world's highest paid CEO's visit is aimed at understanding Indian football and developing the relationship between Chelsea and the AIFF.

Senior national team coach Bob Houghton, who cut short his visit to Kolkata to be here for the meeting, met Kenyon along with the AIFF officials and those from the Bharti Group to chart out a comprehensive development programme.

Chelsea were the first major team to sign an agreement with the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) as official football development partner of AFC's Vision China project.

Heading: Prank call finds terrorists in flight to Agartala - Indian Express
Content:
The much-touted Lalbazar siege of Trinamool Congress on Monday failed to create tremors at the police headquarters. What it did instead, was to choke the city traffic and create a nuisance for the public.

Traffic in the central business district of BBD Bag was thrown out of gear for nearly three hours and many of the roads leading to Lalbazar were closed down.

Trinamool chief Mamata Banerjee was conspicuous by her absence. But 5000 party activists marched close to the headquarters to protest against police commissioner Gautam Mohan Chakraborti and the highhandedness of his troops in dealing with the public.

Still, the day — which according to the Trinamool bigwigs, was to reawaken memories of July 21, 1993, when 13 activists of the Youth Congress were killed in police firing — saw a rather routine protest.

In view of what came, the police preparedness appeared a security overkill — the multi-tier force deployment included contingents of the Special Action Force and Rapid Action Force, water cannons, rubber bullets and tear gas. Over 50 police pickets were set up across the city. And three police barricades, each comprising more than 200 policemen, were put up between Phears Lane Crossing and Lalbazar. Officers of the rank of assistant commissioners and deputy commissioners were deployed for monitoring security.

But the troops ensured that the TMC supporters stayed put at the barricade set up around 500 metres from Lalbazar.

Pouring in from different districts since morning, the Trinamool workers had gathered at Esplanade Metro channel. Around 2 pm, the march began, led by Partha Chatterjee, Madan Mitra, Saugata Roy and others. A huge contingent of policemen escorted them throughout. The mood was tense but the momentum was gone by the time the rally reached Lalbazar police headquarters.

The flashpoint was expectedly at B B Ganguly Street-C R Avenue crossing, where a blockade was put up. But the Trinamool men steered clear of confrontation and gathered near a small stage set up at Phears Lane, quite a distance from the police headquarters, which they had promised to storm.

In his speech, Leader of the Opposition Partho Chatterjee, who allegedly had a recent tiff with the police commissioner following the Charu market incident, said: "Some policemen have become servants of the CPM and the state government. Gautam Mohan Chakrabarti and his brother Ashok Mohan Chakrabarti are acting as agents of the CPM. The people of Bengal are being terrorised."

Barring the usual speeches and routine criticism, the TMC leaders asked their followers to show restraint. "We will return one day to Lalbazar after we are in the government and then wash it with 'Gangajal'. But not today," said Chatterjee, as the leaders directed the supporters to slowly disperse, much to the relief of the policemen thronging nearby.

Heading: Delhi Police team interrogates Ansari, associate for serial blasts - Indian Express
Content:
Three members of a city-based event management company turned into suspected terrorists — thanks to a couple of pranksters.

Ananya Dutta, Sudipto Dutta and Prithviraj Ghosh of Ananya Advertising had reached the Kolkata domestic terminal at 6 am on Monday along with a 16-member dance troupe. The team was to go to Agartala by an Indigo flight scheduled to depart at 7.55 am.

But one of the team members, Suranjana Guha, found that she had left her identity card at home.

When the airline officials refused to allow her to check in, other members of the team insisted that she went back to her home in Ultadanga and bring back the requisite papers.

Police officers suspect that after leaving the airport, she made distress calls to her mother and other friends.

Around 6:25 am, the airport manager and the airport police station received two phone calls claiming that three terrorists were to board the Indigo flight to Agartala. The callers named Ananya Dutta, Sudipto Dutta and Prithviraj Ghosh as the terrorists, said a police officer.

Immediately, the INT wing of the CISF located the passengers and handed them over to the airport police. During interrogation, police told them that the callers had identified themselves as Papiya Guha and Nilanjana — whom Suranjana happened to know. Later, the call was traced to the Hudco housing in Ultadanga.

After filing a diary in the airport police station, the detained passengers finally went to Agartala by an afternoon flight.

"They have to move court and only when the court directs it, we can arrest the people involved or submit a report, as this is a case pertaining to the CISF," said an officer at the airport police station.

Heading: GJM delegation to meet Gandhi in Darjeeling today - Indian Express
Content:
Aftab Ansari, the mastermind behind the attack on the American Centre and the abduction of Khadim chief, and one of his associates Happy Singh, were interrogated at Alipore Central Correctional Home on October 15 by a team of the Delhi Police.

They were interrogated in connection to the September 13 serial blasts in Delhi, in which 25 people were killed and over 70 injured.

They Delhi Police team suspected that the two inmates, who are serving jail terms, possess vital information about a few activists of the Indian Mujahideen (IM) and Student Islamic Movement of India (SIMI), said a senior officer who was on duty when the Delhi Police team visited the jail.

Two officers of the Delhi Police — Inspector Hriday Bhushan and Sub-Inspector Umesh Barthwal — had interrogated Ansari and Happy at the chamber of Jail Superintendent Kumaresh Roy. First the gangsters were interrogated separately for two hours in Roy's room and later, together for two hours, said an officer.

"Though the police didn't disclose much about the duo's association with IM and SIMI, the officers told us that the gangsters knew some of those who had set off the bomb at Karol Bagh," he added.

Earlier, the Delhi Police had moved a petition at the chief metropolitan magistrate's court in Delhi seeking an order to interrogate Ansari and Singh. The order was passed on October 10.

"The Delhi Police team came to Alipore Central Correctional Home on October 15 and produced the court order before the jail authorities. Accordingly, the interrogation was arranged at the jail superintendent's chamber," said the jail officer.

Recently, the Special Task Force of Kolkata police had interrogated Aftab and four of his fellow inmates in Alipore Jail regarding their connection with terror outfits and the underworld.

Heading: City’s top hospitals breeding grounds of mosquitoes - Indian Express
Content:
Less than two months after facilitating talks between the Trinamool Congress and the state government over the Singur issue, Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi seems headed for the hot seat again. This time, it is the Gorkha Janmukti Morcha (GJM), which has sought an audience with him during his bi-annual sojourn in Darjeeling.

A Raj Bhawan spokesperson confirmed to The Indian Express that GJM representatives will meet Gandhi on Wednesday at 4 pm.

GJM secretary Roshan Giri said: "We have requested a meeting since he is here and we feel it is our duty to meet him. During the meeting, we will highlight our demands regarding Gorkhaland.

We are not satisfied with the state government."

Wednesday's meeting will be held against the backdrop of the new phase of the GJM's non-cooperation movement, which seeks to convert all signboards bearing "West Bengal" — both official and private — to "Gorkhaland".

Since the Morcha began implementing its diktat on October 17, 16 cases of defacement of public property have been registered in the district, Darjeeling SP Rahul Srivastav said on Monday. "We have registered 15 cases in the Hills and one in the plains. Out of this, 12 to 13 are complaints by aggrieved parties. In the remaining instances, the police have filed cases suo motu," he added. Each case involves groups of eight to 10 persons defacing several signboards together, so we have clubbed them together. Our investigation is on, but no arrests have been made yet," he added.

In Kolkata, Home Secretary Ashok Mohan Chakrabarti said the Darjeeling district administration has already removed official signboards that were defaced by GJM supporters.

"Legal action has been initiated against the perpetrators. We will not allow any kind of disturbance to continue. Two Bengali organisations that had called a bandh in Darjeeling on Wednesday, have now deferred the same. We have also received information from the Centre that the next round of tripartite talks will be held at the end of November," he added.

Heading: JE, malaria continue unabated - Indian Express
Content:
More than 48 hours have passed since the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) served notices to four leading hospitals of the city after they were found to be breeding grounds for mosquitoes. But hospital authorities are yet to clean up the mess.

While three of the four hospitals — Lady Dufferin Hospital, BR Singh Hospital, NRS Medical College and Hospital and ESI Hospital in Kankurgachi — remained indifferent, NRS Medical College and

Hospital officials said that they were yet to receive the KMC notice.

"The civic body keeps sending such notices, so this is not a new development. We do not have stagnant water or garbage dump in our hospital premises," said Dr RK Mondol, Medical Superintendent of B R Singh Hospital.

However, when The Indian Express team visited B R Singh Hospital, it witnessed a different scene. Although the premises had been cleaned superficially, they were greeted by a leaking tap that had formed a puddle in the toilet.

At the NRS Medical College and Hospital, the team found filthy drains and unused construction materials lying around the campus.

Pobitro Rai, relative of a patient, who has been staying outside the centenary building of the NRS Hospital for the last eight days said, "I have not seen any cleaners since Saturday morning. Drains are brimming with filth and there are so many mosquitoes here."

A Group D employee of NRS Hospital said the hospital was seldom cleaned in spite of having enough number of sweepers.

"Hospital grounds are still overflowing with garbage. The area behind the staff quarters is the worse affected and it is not a surprise that people here are suffering from malaria," he commented.

Tanya Mondol, a senior official of The Lady Dufferin Hospital, said the KMC notice was not served to the hospital, but to the PWD team working within its premises.

"We routinely clean our hospital. The PWD has cleaned up its mess two days ago," she said.

The civic body, meanwhile, said it would take legal action against The Lady Duferrin Hospital authorites. Civic officials said the hospital was sent similar notices thrice before, but nothing was done to clean the premises.

Heading: No test kits around, dengue surges on - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Medical Health Officer of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC), Debdwaipayan Chattopadhaya asked the municipal surveillance department to trace all the reported cases of malaria, dengue and chikungunya and submit a detailed report of each patient.

Even as the civic body remains indifferent in controlling the vector-borne diseases, the diseases keep on spreading through out the state. A two-year-old girl, Sumina Khatun, in Joynagar South 24 paraganas was recently found to be affected by Japanese Encephalitis (JE). Although experts are skeptical about the JE report of Khatun, they strongly suggest conducting a research on the un-diagnosed fevers that are frequently being reported in the city. "The civic body must conduct active surveillance in each ward," said Dr Amiya Hati, former director of the School of Tropical Medicine (STM).

Despite being asked several times by the STM and the state health department, the civic body is yet to conduct an investigation to ascertain how Behala resident Pralay Choudhury was affected with JE, as the case could not be explained scientifically.

The KMC health officials also admitted that the dengue figure available with them might not be accurate as they cannot collect the exact data in absence of dengue clinics. "We have the exact data of malaria. From January to till date, 1496 persons have been detected positive with falciparum cases. But we do not have such figures for dengue as we do not have dengue clinics," said a KMC health official.

So far, 27 persons have been affected with chikungunya and 19 with dengue in the district. Two dengue deaths have been reported from these areas so far.

Heading: To curb cyber crimes, software to be certified - Indian Express
Content:
Even though dengue continues to plague the city every year, the KMC has neither procured dengue test kits nor taken any initiative to set up a public health laboratory for conducting dengue tests.

Interestingly, the civic body allocated Rs 72.59 crore in the ongoing financial year and Rs 57.21 crore in the last financial year for its health budget.

Subodh Dey, MMiC (health) said: "We realise now that we must have dengue test kits to conduct the tests. A few days ago, we asked the state health department for 15,000 dengue test kits." Ironically, the civic body is still waiting for the kits, when it can easily procure these by spending a few lakhs as one kit costs Rs 420-500 and can test at least 50 blood samples.

The KMC can also conduct the tests in its laboratories as it has nearly 110 trained lab-technicians. A private laboratory charges Rs 500-800 for conducting a dengue test, while private nursing homes charge nearly Rs 1,500, making it unaffordable for the poor.

A poor person can also get the test done at a low cost at the School of Tropical Medicine (STM) or Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) but for it the person has to be referred by the local councillor.

While dengue has kept on affecting the city-dwellers over the last four years, KMC is yet to set up an infrastructure to test the blood samples for dengue.

In 2005, dengue fever took the shape of an epidemic affecting 3,464 people and claiming 12 lives.

In 2006, 390 people were affected by the disease with one death and in 2007 the figure was 16 with no death. But, this year dengue-figures have crossed 55 with three deaths, though unofficial records claim more.

Health officials say if testing tools of dengue are made easily available; the dengue count can go high.

Mayor Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya, however, said: "Fifty-five cases cannot be considered as an outbreak of dengue. As of now, we do not think that we need to conduct dengue-tests and set up an infrastructure for that."

Heading: Wait gets longer, no special status in sight for BESU - Indian Express
Content:
To curb the growing menace of cyber crimes in the country, Union Ministry of Communications and Information Technology will set up the first ever Indian accreditation facility for software in Kolkata. B J Srinath, senior director of Indian Computer Emergency Response Team under the IT ministry, said: "The accreditation facility will be the first-of-its-kind in India and will accredit the security aspects of software developed by companies."

Cyber security issues have underlined the need for credible and secure software that cannot be misued. The proposed facility will accredit an IT product on its security related aspects. The pilot project facility will be set up within the premises of the Electronic Regional Test Laboratory (East) under the Central IT department, located in Kolkata. The Rs 8 crore project will help in certifying IT products and enhance their credibility in a world threatened by cyber crimes.

At present, India does not have any certification infrastructure for IT products because there are very few Indian software available in the market. The non-availability of certification facilities has forced Indian software companies to get certification from abroad.

The government accreditation centre will enable India to join countries like Korea, Taiwan, Japan and Australia which already have government accreditation facilities for software security. "The facility will help Indian software developers working on software security products to save the time and cost of getting certification from foreign countries," said Srinath.

The testing of IT products for security accreditation at the proposed centre will be open to all companies, which can get their products certified by the government. "Till now India received certified products from abroad. With the accreditation facility, we will also be able to certify IT products," said Srinath. The Indian certification will be admissible in all the 28 countries which have Common Criteria Recognition Arrangement (CCRA). The IT ministry is also considering to set up a full-fledged IT security product-testing and certification facility in the country.

Heading: IIT-K: Students’ arrest a rare incident, institute’s image intact - Indian Express
Content:
After the Central government agreed to confer the status of Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology (IIEST) to Bengal Engineering and Science University (BESU) in December 2007, the institute is unlikely to get the status for the second consecutive academic year.

The institute has decided to admit students for the 2009 batch through the West Bengal Joint Entrance Examination.

Last week, BESU Vice-Chancellor N R Banerjea and registrar Biman Bandopadhyay visited Delhi to meet Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD) officials, but they failed to get any assurance in this regard. "We met MHRD Secretary R K Agarwal among other officials, but they made no commitment, as to when the institute would get the IIEST status," Bandopadhyay said.

Earlier in August, BESU submitted a modification in the money allocation plan of the institute (as IIEST institute) and said the money will be used by the institute in 11th and 12th Plan period.

According to the teachers of the university, currently, MHRD is busy pumping money in the eight newly-planned IITs throughout the country. Under these circumstances, the IIEST status, which deserves a special Act to be passed by Parliament, has taken a back seat.

Meanwhile, teachers' association is also rallying hard for the IIEST status for BESU. The Bengal Engineering and Science University Teacher's Association ( BESUTA) has contacted the parliamentarians from the state to lobby for the IIEST status.

On September 4, Minister for Information and Broadcasting Priya Ranjan Dasmunsi wrote to the Centre to initiate an IIEST Bill in the Monsoon Session of Parliament. Earlier, Pranab Mukherjee had also written to the Central government to look into the issue.

The state government is, however, not very keen to expedite the process for the IIEST status for BESU. The state government has only agreed that 50 per cent of the students admitted to BESU after getting IIEST status will be from West Bengal. At present, there are 250 teachers and over 2,000 students at the institute.

"Two years ago it was declared that IIEST status will be conferred on BESU, but neither the state government nor the Centre is keen on conferring the status to the institute in time," said Manas Hira, general secretary of BESUTA.

Heading: ‘Client list of Biswas was long, included other students’ - Indian Express
Content:
Following the arrest of an Indian Institute of Technology-Kharagpur (IIT-K) student, Priyankar Biswas, allegedly with 94 grams of heroin, the oldest IIT of the country claimed the incident to be a rare one, which does not reflect on the environment of the institute's campus.

Biswas is a third year B.Tech student at the Department of Agricultural and Food Engineering of the institute. According to the institute's director, Damodar Acharya, he was admitted to IIT-K in 1997, but has not been able to complete his course even after a decade.

"In 2005, Biswas was asked to leave the institute, as IIT students are required to clear the B.Tech programme in eight years. He was, however, allowed to complete his course after he came with a Calcutta High Court order in 2007," Acharya said.

Biswas is an resident of the Nehru Hall hostel of the institute and belongs to Gaighata in North 24 Parganas, about 50 km from Kolkata. 

"Biswas hardly interacted with other students of the hostel. He had no roommate and his room was also at one corner. So, we had no clue about his activities," said Sourav Dutta, president of Nehru Hall.

"I don't think he had any friends at the institute, he mostly interacted with outsiders," Dutta added.

His professors also found his behaviour weird at the institute.

"Biswas approached us for a readmission after a gap of two years. He spoke very little, and that too, with his head down. He told us that he met with an accident and was mentally ill for a couple of years. He also produced a medical certificate for proof," said Prof B C Mal of the Department of Agricultural and Food Engineering.

"Since we keep changing the syllabus every three to four years, we always faced a problem in choosing the right syllabus for him," Prof Mal said.

"Although, IIT-K has decided to expel Biswas, but there are other procedural delays in the final decision. We are waiting for the final report of the police. We cannot take a decision without any evidence," said D K Tripathi, Dean (Students), IIT-K.

He said the police carried out a search in the hostel after Biswas' arrest but could not find anything.

On maintaining a regular vigil at the institute, M Chakraborty, deputy director of IIT-Kharagpur, said: "The students who enter IITs are considered matured and a strict vigil might prove counter-productive."

Heading: Govt claws through Sunderbans, comes up with watery data - Indian Express
Content:
For Priyankar Biswas, the journey from a village on the India-Bangladesh border at Gaighata, North 24 Parganas, to a promising future has come to a grinding halt. According to the police, Biswas — who is lodged in a prison cell along with two of his alleged associates for selling and possessing illegal drugs — had built up a clientele that included IIT students and outsiders close to the IIT campus.  

"Preliminary investigations have revealed that many students of IIT-K are addicted to drugs," a West Midnapore police officer said.

According to sources in the police, earlier, the accused used to procure narcotics from small eateries in and around the IIT campus. But in order to earn money, Biswas started procuring drugs from big dealers from a place near Kharagpur. He is suspected to have links in the border areas, the sources said.  

IIT authorities have, however, termed the incident as a stray one. "We already have adequate measures in place to check such incidents inside the campus," said DK Tripathy, Dean (Students). 

West Midnapore Superintendent of Police Rajesh Singh said that investigations were on to find out the procurement route for heroin. "We have got some leads and investigators are working on them," said Singh, refusing to divulge more details about the case. The other two persons arrested with Biswas are also from the India-Bangladesh border towns of Lalgola in Murshidabad distric — an area that the Narcotic Control Bureau Zonal Director K Shankar said is a hub for drug trafficking. "The police are also probing Biswas' links with drug dealers of Murshidabad," the police sources said.

"West Midnapore is not known for drug trafficking. Our efforts to curb illegal drug trade are concentrated mostly in Murshidabad and Nadia districts. While poppy, from which heroin is made, is grown in Nadia, drugs enter Murshidabad district from the Bangladesh border," Shankar said.

A senior police officer said that Biswas became a drug peddler when he returned to Gaighata after the IIT struck off his name in 2005.

Biswas, meanwhile, told a Midnapore court that he was being "framed" in the case. He said he was called out of his hostel room and someone forcibly put a heroin packet in his pocket to frame him.

Heading: Jute mill reopens after five years, no staff retrenched - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the tiger count has been declining in India, the government has only archaic data generated by unscientific methods for the most famous habitat of the Royal Bengal Tiger — the Sunderbans. The last data, though doubted and rejected by experts, for the big cats in the area dates back to 2004.

The National Tiger Conservation Authority's report released in

February had placed the number of tigers in India as 1,411. The survey, however, was forced to leave the Sunderbans out of the count.

"Conducting a survey in Sunderbans is extremely difficult because of its peculiar terrain. Due to large amount of water in the area, tiger trails cannot be found and pug marks are washed away every six hours," said Dr Jayla of the Wildlife Institute of India (WII), Dehradun. He is in-charge of the tiger census in West Bengal.

He added: "It will be another two years before a concrete data of Sunderban tigers based on scientific methods can be made available." The 2004 tiger census in the Sunderbans was mainly based on pugmark analysis and had put the number at 274, three up from the last census in 2001.

The figure was challenged by Debashish Sengupta, a professor at the Indian Statistical Institute. The institute had analysed the 2004 data under a project commissioned by the West Bengal government to develop software to process the data.

The study claimed that there are not more than 65 tigers left in the world's largest habitat of the wild cat— mangrove forests of the Sunderbans.

In 2006, the West Bengal forest department had come up with another set of data that put the number of the big cats in the Sunderbans at 279. "We were supposed to continue our study with the second set of data also. But the data was never made available to us," said Sengupta. The WII officials said that they had rejected the 2006 data as it was based on unscientific methods that could be easily manipulated.

At present, radio collaring and camera mapping methods are being used at many tiger reserves to ascertain the number of the predator. But the collaring has not been applied on Sunderban tigers. While the WII blames it on the allocation of funds, in the last two years, only one animal has been collared. "One tiger has been fitted with a radio collar, we need to apply similar instruments on at least eight animals," said Dr Jayla.

Heading: 12 CRPF men killed after Maoists trigger blast, then fire on injured - Indian Express
Content:
As a convoy of 13 trucks carrying fruits to Pakistan occupied Kashmir left Baramulla's mandi, hundreds of fruit growers turned up to see off the vehicles. The trucks will cross Kaman on Tuesday. However, for security reasons they had to reach Salamabad on Monday itself.

All Valley Fruit Growers Association, an amalgam of 14 organisations, had organised a consignment of 12 tonnes of fruits for PoK's market. A large number of drivers had offered their services for this historic trip, only 13 were selected through a draw of lots.

"I still can't believe my luck that I will be driving to Chikoti (PoK) with apples," said an elated Zahoor Ahmad Bhat. "My entire village is excited that I will drive on a route that had remained closed for 62 years," he added. The trucks were all decorated with banners saying "long live cross-LoC trade".

At Sopore's mandi, hundreds of fruit growers shouted pro-LoC trade slogans, as they assembled to see off four trucks. "Hopefully, full-fledged trade will start soon through Kaman," said Basher Beig, president of the fruit mandi. "This trip will bring two nations closer," said Mehboob Ahmad Magray, a driver from Kupwara.

Director of Horticulture Department, Showket Ahmad, who accompanied the trucks up to Salamabad, was jubilant too. "Kashmiri fruit growers will now have access to a big market," he said.

A new road has been laid outside the proposed truck terminal, where the vehicles will drive in on Tuesday. The workers are busy giving final touches to the Customs office and godowns that will store fruits.

At Lalpul, one can see ruins of a pre-partition market. There are only three kiosks selling eatables here. "For us, the LoC trade will serve a purpose only when trucks stop here," said Mohammad Qadeem, who sells vegetables.

Traders at the only Hindu dominated village, Lagama, are upbeat too. "This is the foundation of peace," said Vishwanath, a villager.

Heading: Jamia Nagar ‘excursion: 4 UP cops transferred - Indian Express
Content:
Striking in a big way after the announcement of two-phase Assembly elections in Chhattisgarh next month, Maoist rebels ambushed a team of Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) personnel this afternoon, killing 12 and leaving six others wounded near a forest village between Modupal and Kompalli in Bijapur district.

The Maoists first triggered an explosion and then opened fire on the injured CRPF personnel. They escaped with weapons of the securitymen, including an Ak-47 assault rifle, two SLRs, a light machine gun and INSAS rifles, police said. Security forces have been rushed to the area to flush out the Maoists.

Bijapur SP Ankit Garg said the incident took place around 1.30 pm when CRPF men were patrolling the area, moving towards the Modupal base camp. They were attacked by large number of Maoists who first set off an explosion and then opened fire.

Police sources said three security personnel were killed in the blast while nine others were killed in the firing that followed. A Maoist was killed when the CRPF personnel returned fire. All the injured were taken to the district hospital in Bijapur from where they were being airlifted by helicopter to the government medical college hospital in Raipur.

Police sources identified the dead CRPF personnel as S K Bharadwaj, Kailash kumar, Pappu Kumar, Akhilesh Kumar, S Singh, Motiyar Rehman, Neeraj Sharma, Dijeendra Teka, Arun Singh, E E Surya, V O Ram and P C Sethi . Among the injured were Vikram Reddy and I Pawan Kumar.

Heading: Maharashtra Building attacked in Kanpur - Indian Express
Content:
The Noida policemen who had crossed the Uttar Pradesh border and entered Delhi to arrest an alleged chain-snatcher at Jamia Nagar on Thursday were transferred on Monday.

According to sources, the four policemen have been transferred after the Uttar Pradesh government took note of the alleged use of a black Verna car to chase the alleged chain-snatchers and the violence that erupted in Jamia Nagar on October 16.

According to sources, Station House Officer Ramsen Singh has been transferred to the Police Lines. Sub-Inspector Ajay Pal and Constables Kulwinder singh and Vijayveer have been transferred to the Economics Offence Wing of Varanasi, sources said. "All four policemen were beaten up in Jamia Nagar after they tried to pick up two young boys, who they claim to have been chasing," a police source said. The Noida policemen had managed to escape.

Noida police claim one of the men the police team was chasing has five cases registered against him in Sahibabad (Ghaziabad) and Delhi. "Aamir Rehman, who was allegedly chased by the UP Police team, has been booked in cases under IPC Sections pertaining to attempt to murder and assault or criminal force in attempt to commit theft of property," the police source said.

Heading: Three sons murdered, she seeks protection for the rest - Indian Express
Content:
The repercussion of the recent attack on North Indians in Mumbai, allegedly by the Maharastra Navnirman Sena (MNS), was felt in Kanpur on Monday, as a group of 25 people pelted stones on the Maharashtra Bhawan in Khalasi Line.

The attack occurred in the evening, when only a few peons were present inside the building. No one was injured.

Constructed in 1928, the building is owned by the lone trust run by Marathis in Kanpur. Over the years, it has served as an important venue for prominent festivals, including Ganesh Utsav and Krishna Janmastami.

Bal Mandir, a school up to Class VIII, with student strength of over 200, operates from the building.

Arun Hardekar, the manager of the school and the building, told police that unidentified people — some of them women — shouting anti-Raj Thackeray slogans began brickbatting the building in the evening. "The window panes have been shattered and furniture has been damaged," he said. No one, however, entered the building.

Senior Superintendent of Police, Kanpur, Hari Ram Sharma told The Indian Express: "Prima facie, it appears that the people were provoked to attack the Maharastra Bhawan." A search for the culprits is on. 

"On charges of creating disturbance, disrupting law and order and damaging private property, a case has been registered under Sections 147, 336 and 427 of the IPC," he said.

Sources said the violence was carried out by members of Dalit Baudh Panther (DBP), though the police or Hardekar are yet to confirm it. Prior to the attack, the DBP members held a protest against the MNS and Raj Thackeray at Colonelganj crossing and burnt an effigy of Raj Thackeray.

President of the DBP, Dhanirao Baudh, said: "Though we are strongly against the act of Raj Thackeray and the MNS, we were not involved in the violence at Khalasi Line area." But he said the protests against the MNS will continue till justice is done to North Indians in Mumbai and Maharastra. "Raj Thackeray should be arrested and made to apologise in public for creating differences between people and promoting regionalism," he added.

Heading: Poll office ready to introduce Photo Electoral Roll in state - Indian Express
Content:
A Dalit woman from Allahabad, who has taken to arms to protect her family, visited the state capital on Monday to meet Director General of Police Vikram Singh.

Vidhyawati (45) from Allahabad, was seeking protection from the men accused of murdering her three sons. They were threatening to kill her and her family, she said.

Armed with a licensed gun, she, however, could not meet the police chief. The police took her application and assured her that it would be forwarded to Singh.

In her application, Vidhyawati named former village pradhan Manik Chand Patel, his son Doodhnath and cousin Rakesh Patel. She accused them of murdering her son and now forcing her not to give statement against them in court.

The men had been released on bail a week ago from the Allahabad District Jail.

The Deputy Inspector General, Allahabad Range, MK Prasad, said: "We provided an arms license to her after she complained about the threat to her family.

Security has been arranged for her when she visits the court for hearings."

Two of Vidhyawati's sons were allegedly poisoned in 2003 and 2004. A third was killed brutally in 2006 and his body was found on the railway tracks.

The murders took place after she staked claim on her father's land following his demise.

No FIR was lodged in this connection.

"My rivals were trying to capture my land and when I opposed it, they beat me up. Because of the threat I left the village but did not let them capture the land," said Vidhyawati, who is currently living in Soran with a physically-handicapped husband and two children.

Heading: Rae Bareli U-turn: Maya cites new reason - Indian Express
Content:
The Photo Electoral Roll (PER), if introduced, may put an effective check on the "impersonation of voters" in the forthcoming Parliamentary Elections. Of the 11.35 crore voters, the office of state's Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) has already prepared the PER of about 70 per cent.

The electoral office will also run the duplicate software on the existing rolls as an exercise termed "De-duplication of voters". As per the Sections 17 & 18 of the RP Act, no person is entitled to be registered in more than one constituency and for any constituency more than once. "Hence, the software should be run on the existing rolls and duplicate entries thoroughly investigated," said an official, quoting the recent directives of the Election Commission.

Chief Election Officer A K Bisnoi said the wrong entries can be seen under various categories with the help of the new software.

"If a person is dead, in case a girl marries and relocates, or voters migrate, it will register in the software. So will the appearance of same person at two booths," he said.

Sources in the CEO's office said 28 lakh names have already been deleted from the voters' list and around 51 lakh names have been added. "It means the net new addition to the list is about 23 lakh voters," the official added. This, he said, was normal as 2 per cent growth is expected.

The rate of addition and the deletion of names is high in urban areas of Meerut, Ghaziabad, Agra, Kanpur and Gorakhpur. But there, the migration of voters happens frequently and thus deletion of names from the PER is almost in same proportion as additions, he said.

In areas like Jyotiba Phule Nagar, Chitrakoot, Chandauli and Shrawasti, the addition or deletion figures do not exceed 20,000.

The ECI move to trace wrong entries is set to disturb the equations of political parties, which have already tasked their workers with ensuring that their equation stays "favourable" at the booths. But what has skewed the pitch further is the delimitation exercise, which has changed the map of various constituencies. "The political parties, particularly those with dedicated cadres, are going all out to ensure new voters' entry into the PER," the official said.

Sources said the states going to poll may confirm the use of the PER for the first time. "There is little chance that the poll commission will make PER mandatory. No person can be stopped from using his voting right in absence of his photograph on the PER. But the PER would certainly stop miscreants from trying to impersonate a voter at the booths," the official said.

How to get registered
To get registered for the Photo Electoral Roll, a person above 25 years in age will have to communicate to the Chief Electoral Officer's Office, mentioning the current and former addresses.

Heading: BJP calls Maya’s upper caste meet a ‘showoff’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Mayawati government came out with another reason why it restored the land meant for the proposed rail coach factory at Rai Bareli by a Cabinet order.

It claimed that the Railways had insisted that the land be allotted only after it is approved by the state Cabinet.

A government order, issued on October 18, but which became available on Monday, said the land was being given to the Railways on lease for 90 years after Cabinet approval as requested by the Railway Ministry.

The order states that the chief engineer of the northern railway had made such a request in a letter on November 15, 2007 and chief administrative officer of Railway Coach Factory, Kapurthala in another letter on March 4, 2008.

For the first time, the government has said that the Railways had requested for a Cabinet approval for land allotment.

Railway officials, however, were not available to explain why they had made the request and why they had accepted the land when it was allotted by an administrative order on July 30, 2008.

When the government cancelled the allotment on October 12, it had explained its action on the ground that there was resentment among villagers and a Singur-like situation might have developed.

Next, it said that the allotment was illegal because Cabinet approval was required. On October 18, the Cabinet met and put its stamp of approval.

Now the government neither mentions the farmers' anger nor the illegality of the allotment. A senior officer said, "If the Railways were aggrieved by the cancellation, they should have approached the government, instead of moving the High Court."

Interestingly, a petition filed by the railways in Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court against cancellation of the land allotment is still pending.

Heading: Polio spread unchecked, govt transfers CMO to save face - Indian Express
Content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has termed Chief Minister Mayawati's "new-found love for upper castes" as a mere showoff. Reacting to the upper caste convention held by the BSP on Sunday, state BJP president Ramapati Ram Tripathi maintained it will not benefit the upper castes.

Addressing the media, Tripathi said: "If Mayawati says 80 per cent of the members of the upper caste are poor, then why they were removed from the BPL list?" He further asked Mayawati that though she had announced a Persian-Arabic university for the Muslims, why hasn't she announced the formation of a Hindi or a Sanskrit university?

He also accused the BSP of shielding terrorists and continuing with its "Periyarvaadi Savarn Virodhi" agenda.

Heading: Recession hits ‘Dollar City’, artisans worst hit - Indian Express
Content:
State tops polio list with 243 cases, 47 cases of P1 infection

Following worldwide condemnation for its inability to control spread of polio virus, especially the most virulent Type 1 infection, the Uttar Pradesh government transferred Dr Rajendra Kumar Saxena, Chief Medical Officer of Badaun district today as a face-saving measure.

Transmission of Type 1 virus in the state began from Badaun this year.

Experts, including those from the World Health Organisation, had pointed out the lacunae in the routine immunisation drives in Badaun, which had led to the problem.

With 243 polio cases, Uttar Pradesh tops the list of polio-affected states in the country. To date, the state has reported 47 cases of P1 and 196 cases of P3 virus infection.

Bihar, which is in the second spot, has reported 226 cases. But Bihar has been able to control the spread of Type 1 virus and only two cases have been reported this year.

Ironically, the Type 1 virus circulating in high risk districts of western UP is of the Bihar strain.

Health Minister Anant Mishra confirmed that the Badaun CMO had been transferred following complaints regarding his negligent attitude from various agencies. "We hope that this would send a message among the officials and they would take the polio drive seriously," he said.

Senior officials say the government can do little besides transferring the CMO.

Of course, it has launched the mop-up rounds of vaccination.

Principal Secretary of Medical and Health department Neeta Chaudhary the Centre has ben asked to provide guidance in formulating the future strategy to fight the virus.

"The present strategy seems to be failing and the virus is spreading rapidly and is becoming a serious cause of concern," she said.

'No word on JE vaccine'
The state government is still waiting for 10 lakh doses of the Japanese Encephalitis vaccine. Around 4.6 lakh doses which the Centre had supplied last month were found unfit for use when these reached Lucknow from the cold storage in Karnal. The Centre had withdrawn the supply and promised fresh stocks. The JE vaccination drive has already been delayed by two months in the high-risk districts of eastern UP. "There is no word about the vaccine from the Centre yet," said Neeta Chaudhary.

Heading: Thokia’s brother, aides kill STF informants who ‘celebrated’ encounter - Indian Express
Content:
The prevalent economic depression has hit Uttar Pradesh's "Dollar City" too. The carpet industry in Bhadohi, rechristened the Dollar City owing to its exports worth billions to the US and Europe, is one of those worst-hit by the global meltdown.

The industry, which otherwise did significant business between September to February — both in the domestic and the international market — is fearing that this year, the five-month period may turn out to be the worst. While order cancellations from the US and Europe have started coming in already, the manufacturers claim they aren't even getting too many domestic orders.

A visit to the district, around 44 km from Varanasi, shows that the gloom has already set in. The worst-hit are the 2.5 million artisans, who contribute 55 per cent of the value addition to the $1 billion export industry.

According to exporters, this is the worst crisis they have seen in the recent times. Ravi Pataudia of Pataudia Exports — one of the biggest exporters — and the president of the All

India Carpet Manufacturer's Association (AICMA), said: "The slump is not just creating panic in the market but also among the consumers."

Sales in September were down by one per cent, which in terms of money means a huge amount. In October, it is worse. The figures will be available at month-end, he added.

Avinash Chandra Barnwal, a manufacturer and exporter of East West Trading Corporation, said: "We have been either asked to wait before we start executing the orders or they are being cancelled. In the past, these months used to be the busiest for us."

Secretary of AICMA Satyendra Kumar Sinha said: "We were already facing stiff competition from China which makes cheap stuff. Though sales for October are yet to be calculated, it is clear that exports have gone down."

The artisans, who work from their homes as weavers and workers, are the worst hit. Ramdayal, a carpet weaver of Ghamhapur village, said: "Since September, I have received only one order, and have two looms and eight people working. We used to get at least three to four orders at this time and used to work day and night to ensure timely delivery. Now, we hardly have any work."

Heading: PCS officer arrested on dowry charges - Indian Express
Content:
The jubilation of the state police over the elimination of dreaded gangster Ambika Patel alias Thokia, who was gunned down on August 4, is finally over in the badlands of Bundelkhand.

Thokia's brother Deepak Patel, who had taken over the gang since his death, has bounced back and killed two villagers on Friday night.

Patel and his associates had called upon Ramjee Pandey and his brother Ram Milan outside their residence in Lodhapurwa village in Chitrakoot — tied them to a tree, shot them and fled the spot.

According to reports, the Pandey brothers were found "guilty of celebrating" Thokia's death and had allegedly provided information to the Special Task Force in this connection.

When the police reached the village to verify the incident, the villagers, however, denied the whole incident. After an hour-long search, the police found the bodies tied to a tree. The Kotwali police, in the absence of any direct accusation against Patel, have lodged an FIR against unidentified criminals.

Chitrakoot Superintendent of Police D K Rai said: "I believe the Pandey brothers were murdered by Deepak Patel. Ram Milan Pandey was a brave man and used to fight against wrongdoings."

Three police teams have been formed to comb the jungle, he added.

On September 11, Patel and his associates had stopped construction of a road in the Bharatkoop area and demanded 10 per cent commission from Adersh Construction Company.

On being refused, the gang members had beat up the labourers. They have also pumped bullets into the tires of a JCB machine and water tankers, forcing the company to abandon the project.

Later, an FIR against Patel and his associates was lodged with the police.

Heading: Member of thieves’ gang in net, police say leader a folk singer - Indian Express
Content:
A Provincial Civil Service (PCS) officer of Uttar Pradesh, Manoj Kumar, serving as an Officer on Special Duty (OSD) with the Meerut Development Authority (MDA) was arrested on Monday in a case of dowry harassment.

The case was registered by Kumar's wife at the Sihanigate police station of Ghaziabad on Sunday. Renu had accused him of assaulting her for the past several weeks.

SP (City) Ghaziabad, Vijay Bhushan said: "A PCS officer of 1991 batch, Manoj Kumar had joined as OSD two months ago. His wife lodged the FIR yesterday and subsequently the arrest was made."

Homeguard dies in Rae Bareli cracker explosion
Home Guard Constable Rakesh, who was injured in a cracker explosion on Sunday, succumbed to his injuries in Rae Bareli on Monday. The constable was among the six injured in an explosion which occurred on the Oonchahar police station premises. The incident took place after about 35 kg of crackers the explosive substances seized from a manufacturing unit by the police exploded.

A request has been sent to the government seeking an ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh. Efforts were also being made to sanction widow pension to the constable's wife.

Heading: Sofats booked on forgery charges - Indian Express
Content:
In a typical case of real life imitating the reel life, a Punjabi folk singer has been found to be allegedly running a gang which steals loaded trucks at gunpoint. The police seized two trucks laden with goods worth Rs 60 lakh and rescued three persons from illegal confinement. One gang member has been arrested.

According to the police, the gang leader is a Punjabi folk singer Nishan Singh Gill, who has an audio cassette to his credit.

Giving the details, SP City II Gurmeet Singh Randhawa told mediapersons that following secret information, the police had set up a checkpoint near the Perfect Marriage Palace on the Chandigarh road on Sunday night.

The police intercepted a truck around 1 am. When the truck was stopped, two youths jumped out of the vehicle and fled under the cover of darkness. The police managed to arrest one person, who was later identified as Fateh Jang Singh.

On searching the truck, the police found two gagged youths in the cabin of the vehicle. They told the police that the gang members had held them hostage at gunpoint and were about to desert the duo at an isolated place.

SP Randhawa said that after a while, another truck was stopped at the same naka.

Four youths jumped from the vehicle and gave a slip to the police. The police rescued one Sunny Kumar, the driver of the truck. SP Randhawa said that both trucks were ferrying aluminum residue worth Rs 60 lakh in the market.

Randhawa said that the leader of the gang was posing as a singer and has also opened an office near Phillaur.

The SP said that the police had identified the six absconding members and they will be arrested soon.

Heading: Sangat Darshan fizzles out in city - Indian Express
Content:
Crime: Absconding doctors have been charged with committing a land fraud four years ago

The police have booked leading city doctors on charges of forgery. Dr J R Sofat and his son Dr Sumit Sofat have been booked by Division Number 5 police station under Sections 120, 420, 467, 468, 469 and 471.

The sections are non-bailable and according to the police, the father-son duo is on the run.

In the past too, Dr Sofat has been in the news for all the wrong reasons. The Sofats have been booked earlier for making a false case of a successful IVF pregnancy which the doctors claimed had been done on a woman in her sixties. In another case, the Medical Council of India had suspended the medical licence of Dr Sumit Sofat when the latter refused to acknowledge the MCIs letters over the issue of illegal advertising.

Division Number 5 SHO Shivinder Singh, "This case pertains to a land deal in 2000 where Dr Sofat was the buyer. However, the deal fell through after both parties registered a series of FIRs against each other. An inquiry revealed that the father-son duo had not only filed false complaints but also committed fraud in the case."

It has been learnt that Dr Sofat had purchased a 1,200-square yard plot on the Ferozepur Road in 2000. The deal for the plot was sealed for around Rs 70 lakh.

Dr Sofat had not got the registry of the plot done on the grounds that he was under the scanner of the Income Tax department.

Despite pressure from the seller, Dr Sofat refused to get the plot registered in his name.

The selling party cancelled the power of attorney which stood in Dr Sofat's name.

In 2004, a settlement was brokered between the two parties wherein Dr Sofat sold the plot back to the owner on higher rates. When Dr Sofat came to know that the owner of the plot had sold it to a third party at a handsome profit, he not only refused to give up the plot but also got it registered in his name using a fake power of attorney.

Dr Sofat had filed a complaint of kidnap and murder against the seller of the property alleging that they had killed his servant. The police traced the servant.

Heading: 49 more dengue cases pour in - Indian Express
Content:
