The second phase of Sangat Darshan, which was supposed to be held from October 23 to 27, has been postponed. Of these dates, Sangat Darshan will be held only on October 26 in the Ludhiana north constituency where Harish Bedi is the MLA. The remaining dates had been reserved for the Ludhiana rural constitency where Cabinet Minister Hira Singh Gabria is the MLA.

Owing to the ongoing festivities, residents and traders are more interested in focussing on their business. Moreover, the CM's visit may cause public inconvenience and hence can hamper the shopping of masses, revealed sources.

The Sangat Darshan may be organised after November 3 but the exact dates have not yet been finalised, sources added.

Heading: PU faces staff crunch, blames it on lack of funds - Indian Express
Content:
As many as 49 confirmed dengue cases were reported from the various hospitals across the city today.

With this, the total number of confirmed dengue cases has swollen up to 1,241. Besides, 284 suspected dengue cases were also reported.

According to the data procured from the different hospitals, 16 confirmed dengue cases were reported from the CMC Hospital, five from the Mohan Dai Oswal Hospital while four cases were reported from the SPS Apollo Hospital. The rest of the cases were reported from other hospitals.

Dayanand Medical College and Hospital (DMCH) has been admitting nearly 50 to 60 patients every day. The hospital has already registered about 1,300 patients so far. A few hospitals have reportedly stopped admitting symptomatic patients.

Of over 2,000 cases of dengue having been reported in the state, over 1,400 cases are claimed to be from the district alone. The Health department, however, had confirmed 1,144 cases till Saturday.

Three deaths reported in the last couple of days are suspected to be due to the dengue.

Heading: MC wakes up, buys 10 fogging machines - Indian Express
Content:
With almost a quarter of the academic session coming to an end, students at the UIET department of Panjab University are yet to be beneficiaries of basic facilities including faculty and infrastructure.

Around 165 seats were increased last year, but the department seems to be ailing owing to inadequate resources. Though the authorities maintain that the hiring process for faculty is on, there is still a long way to go for the department. Talking to Newsline, Prof B S Sohi, chairperson of the department said, "There is a shortage of faculty and other infrastructure facilities, however, the same is being taken care of. In all, the department is short of 35 readers and 15 lecturers. The hiring process for faculty is on."

The department has also been in the news a number of times after students complained of the lack of facilities. Two issues demanding immediate attention of the authorities seem to be the hiring of adequate faculty and the construction of lecture halls, according to students.

Meanwhile, it is not only the UIET department that is facing a faculty crunch. Other departments too seem to be struggling with having to make do with guest faculty in order to comply with the required work force.

Be it the University Business School, the Economics department or the Mass Communication department, the absence of faculty in all these departments is being compensated by the guest faculty. Sources maintain that at present the university is short of around 250 lecturers and readers.

The authorities at the university, meanwhile, owe the faculty shortage to the lack of funds and claim that the university is in urgent need of finances. According to a university official, "The first and foremost reason for the lack of faculty is because of the shortage of funds. For hiring a faculty member, we need to take into consideration the opinion of the Finance Board and most of the times, the board insists that we hire only in dire need." Further explaining and clarifying the university's stand, PU Registrar S S Bari said, "We have begun with the hiring process and faculty is being appointed in all departments wherever required."

Heading: To Dubai, to show how to crack crime from handwriting - Indian Express
Content:
After a decade, the authorities in the municipal corporation finally realised the need to replace the archaic fogging machines with the new ones. After spending Rs 1.20 crore, the MC has purchased 10 new fogging machines. Five old machines have also been mended to make them up and running with an additional expenditure of Rs 21 lakh.

The wisdom dawned upon the authorities in the municipal corporation after the dengue cases in the city crossed the 1,000 mark.

MC Commissioner G S Ghuman said, "Each machine carries the price tag of Rs 12 lakh. Five new machines with German technology have been delivered while the remaining five will be transported within a week.

Eleven machines are running on city roads. With the purchase of 10 new machines and by repairing five old machines, we will have a total of 26 machines now."

The Commissioner said," Nine machines were lying in the junkyard since 2000. We managed to get five German machines repaired. We could not get the spare parts of the remaining machines as they were of American technology."

MC authorities claim that fogging operations have been intensified with bi-weekly spraying in every ward. The residents rue that despite increasing number of cases, the authorities have not yet woken up and fogging in many wards is being carried out after a month or even more.

King fog: the new mantra

The MC has changed the medicine used for fogging purposes. Fore more than 20 years, melathin mixed with diesel was used for killing mosquitoes. However, 'King fog' is the new medicine. Doctors confirmed that mosquitoes had become used to the earlier drug and hence they have changed the drug.

Additional expenses

With the addition of 10 new and five repaired machines, the additional expenditure on fogging operations will increase by more than Rs 5 crore per annum, claimed an MC official. Last year's expenditure was around Rs 9 crore.

Heading: Back to life in one room: necessity, not choice - Indian Express
Content:
Two handwriting experts from Pune, who have helped the state police crack cases of robbery and even murder, are being wooed by Dubai. Manish Pande and Paresh Billimoria will fly to the emirate on October 23 to display their skills in analysing handwriting before the corporate and public sectors there.

Interested in analysing handwriting since their childhood, Pande, an employee of Poonawalla Group of Companies, and Billimoria, an architect, took a two-year course in graphology from the US. Now they are carrying out research in criminal graphology, which could be of great help for the police department, they say.

In the last six months the two have conducted three special sessions for recruits and officers at police training schools in Nashik and Khandala and more such sessions are scheduled next month.

Impressed with their skills, the Nashik police sought their help in solving a murder case in July. "The Nashik police had rounded up five suspects, one of whom was the killer. Police gave us handwriting samples of all five suspects. We pointed out a suspect after analysing the samples. Police followed up our analysis and the man we identified did turn out to be the killer," said Pande.

"Handwriting reflects the behavior of a person. The slants, points, spacing between two alphabets, words and lines and other aspects in handwriting show the mental, emotional other personality traits. A combination of certain traits can warn of possible criminal tendencies of a person," Pande explained.

"From a handwriting sample, we can guess the person's willingness to obey rules as also the levels of aggressiveness, anger and frustration. It may not be the final word in the involvement of a person in the crime, but it certainly can provide clues that can help solve the case," said Billimoria.

"Handwriting analysis is useful in various crimes like suicide, forgeries, tampering with documents, robberies, murders and even sexual harassment," he said.

Pande and Billimoria will be in Dubai for about a month. "Jayant Shitole, a businessman in Dubai of Pune origin, has arranged our discussions with various persons from the corporate and other sectors. He came to know of us from our website graphoanalytics.com," Pande said.

"After going through the website, I thought the graphologists could help solve some problems the corporate and public sectors in Dubai face," said Shitole, who was in Pune.

Heading: Mumbai effect: 200 MNS members detained in city - Indian Express
Content:
The real estate market is going through an uncertain phase, leading to desperate measures by builders. Freebies like BMWs, focus once again on one-room flats... it's all happening. Starting today, a 3-part series on a boom market that's going bust but one where the principals are trying to stay afloat

This is one mode of housing that almost went out of fashion. Making a strong comeback after almost five years of dormancy is the one-bedroom apartment that was once the most common kind of housing options across the city.

Called 'compact housing' in its reinvented format, the 1BHKs are set to storm the city as there are no less than 10,000 such units getting readied by Pune builders to come up in the next one year. The overriding reason behind the builders turning to 1BHKs is the unprecedented rise in realty rates over the last three years that has put 2 and 3BHKs out of the reach of many aspiring buyers.

It was only a couple of weeks ago that Promoters and Builders Association of Pune president Lalitkumar Jain sent a notice to all its 250 member builders to reintroduce 1BHKs in their projects. "With these 500-700 sq ft compact homes priced at Rs 15-Rs 25 lakh, they will be in demand," said Jain. At least 1,200 units that will come up immediately will cost below Rs 20 lakh, he said.

In some of the fringe areas like Undri and Wagholi, the rates on offer for 1BHKs are as low as Rs 7.5 to 9 lakh. And these are not 'economy' flats as they come with all the frills - swimming pool, health club, children's play park and generator back-up.

With interest rates going up to 11.75 per cent to 12.5 per cent as compared to the 7 to 7.5 per cent two years ago, the buying capacity of citizens has been compromised and hence the rise of this new segment, says Jain.

However, wannabe buyers of these 1BHKs are not willing to buy this argument and say the builders are doing themselves a favour and not the other way round.

"Many 2, 3 and 4BHK projects are languishing across the city with no takers. Earlier, buyers were forced to stretch their budgets to meet the demands of the builders. Now the situation is just the opposite. The builders are being pushed to tailor make apartments to suit our budgets," said Smita Yadav, a bank employee who had been scouting around for almost three years for an apartment to fit her budget.

According to Jain, builders are also trying to fill the void left open by the government. "Despite the state hype on economic housing, nothing has happened to that effect and so builders decided to cater to these demands," he said.

Satish Magar, the developer of Magarpatta township and who recently launched the Nanded township, said that under the township policy, it is mandatory to reserve 10 per cent of the total area for compact housing. "Besides, builders in the city are providing 1BHKs due to genuine demand," he said.

Magar said the demand for 1BHKs may prove to be temporary. "This will change with the CRR going down. Interest rates too will go down and there will be more affordability," said Magar.

With an economic housing policy nowhere in sight, and the current cash crunch faced by builders, compact housing projects are getting launched like never before, especially in the fringe areas of Phursungi, Katraj, Ambegaon, Akurdi, Nigdi, Talegaon Dabhade and Dehu Road.

Heading: Power cut plan soon, dark days in store - Indian Express
Content:
Around 200 Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) members were placed under preventive detention by the city police on Monday to thwart any untoward incident, following a non-bailable warrant issued against party chief Raj Thackeray by the Jamshedpur district court for allegedly making derogatory remarks about Chhat Pooja.

Joint Commissioner of Police Rajendra Sonawane said, "I am not sure how many activists have been detained as the drive is still on," he said.

The city president of MNS, Prakash Dhore said, "Around 200 of our members have been detained since morning. The festival of Diwali is near. If our party chief is arrested, we will give a fitting reply."

"Does the State government have the guts to arrest Raj saheb ? Let them arrest him and they will realise the blunder they have made," Dhore added.

He said that their major demand was that advertisements for recruitment to the Railways should be issued in major newspapers in Maharashtra and not just in newspapers in UP and Bihar, a devious plan that was preventing Maharashtrians from getting railway jobs.

The Jamshedpur court issued the warrant against Thackeray on Friday, which was received by the Mumbai police on Monday. "The police are nabbing MNS activists under pressure from the state government, which in turn is under pressure from the central government. It is Union Railway Minister Lalu Prasad who is pressuring the State government. If Raj is arrested, we will see how Lalu steps into Pune," he said.

On Sunday, job aspirants who had gone to Mumbai to appear for the Railway Board examination from north Indian states were beaten up and thrown out of the examination centres by MNS members.

Heading: The young and the educated throw poll challenge at political giants - Indian Express
Content:
With the Tata Power Company being able to procure only 70-80 MW against the expected 150 MW on a day- ahead basis, Puneites reeling under power cuts are waiting for the new loadshedding protocol being worked out by the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC).

But the picture does look grim, due to lack of availability of power in the state and the country.

According to Jayant Deo, managing director of the Indian Energy Exchange (IEX), on Sunday, against the demand of 49,400 MW hours in the country, the available energy sold in the market was just 18,600 MW hours.

Even as the Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL) officials were mum on how much power Pune really needs, activists were looking forward to the MERC order on the loadshedding protocol this week.

S P Nagtilak, MSEDCL Chief Engineer for Pune division, refused to comment on the quantum of loadshedding worked out for Pune. It is a policy matter, he said. While the MSEDCL has submitted its data to the MERC on the present loadshedding protocol, the order was being expected this week, Shantanu Dixit, coordinator of the Prayas Energy Group said.

With the demand around 304 MW, Tata Power Company has not met it in full. Supply has been varying day by day. Pradeep Bhargava, chairman of the Maharashtra cell of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), said the company had been told to procure 150 MW initially. Now, with the demand so high, it is unlikely the company can buy more power.

Heading: Pan, gutkha  spitters will have to pay through their nose at this society - Indian Express
Content:
Sporting a blue Gandhi cap and a jacket of the same colour, Sangharsh Apte is a picture of confidence as he prepares to contest the Lok Sabha election. The slightly built, 27-year-old research assistant with a media firm in Pune, armed with a Masters degree in social work (MSW), has chosen to contest from the stronghold of a political heavyweight —Baramati, a seat held by Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) chief and Union Agriculture Minister Sharad Pawar for 20 years.

Apte is one among the members of the Prabuddha Republican Party (PRP), which will field candidates against big names in all the Assembly and Lok Sabha seats in Maharashtra.

His wife is also getting ready for the polls, as an Assembly seat contestant. The candidates have already started campaigning door to door and raising funds from people to cover election costs.

The PRP believes only the youth can bring a positive change in the political system in the country. The party has vowed to follow the ideals of Gautama Buddha, Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar and Mahatma Jyotiba Phule, and aims at fighting for freedom, equality and fraternity and rooting out corruption.

On the name sounding similar to that of another party, PRP office-bearer Mahendra Nikalje said: "Our party has nothing to do with the Republican Party of India (RPI) or its factions, as all these, or any political party for that matter, are trapped in communal politics and are far away from the true philosophy of a republic. The PRP has taken a vow to turn the principles of 'freedom, equality and fraternity' into reality."

The PRP, established in 2002, contested Lok Sabha and Assembly polls in 2004. It did not win any seat. The party head office is at Ambajogai in Beed district and has about 500 members.

"We have finalised the candidates from Pune district for both the polls. Party offices in other districts are doing the same. As for me, I will contest from Baramati. The USP of our party is that we are all young and educated," Sangharsh said.

"Each candidate will raise at least Rs 25,000 through donations from people for the deposit amount and other resources. We will depend only on interaction with people and refrain from any poster-campaign."

His wife, Pallavi Harshe, who is also an MSW, said, "I will be the candidate from Kothrud for the Assembly polls and have started my groundwork. I have visited about 50 households, explaining our party's stand, asking people to vote for us and donate some money."

Even the women members wear the blue Gandhi cap and the jacket, the party trademark. Harshe, who is a call centre employee, said, "This attire establishes our identity and we believe it brings positive thoughts and social awareness."

Heading: Dengue on the rise, claims five this year - Indian Express
Content:
Rs 1,000 fine if anybody found dirtying the society premises

Till about ten days ago, Goyal Residency, a residential apartment in Kasarwadi area of Pimpri-Chinchwad, was like any other ageing building. But not anymore. The building, housing around 50 flats today sports a brand new look, gleaming in the sun and standing tall and wide. Gone are the paan and gutkha stains that spread starkly on almost all floors of the society.

Days ahead of Diwali, the residents have given the insides of the building a new coat of paint and have taken a vow. The 200-odd residents have decided to put spitters, especially those of paan, tobacco and gutkha kind, in their place. From now on, anybody dirtying the building premises with paan, gutkha or tobacco stains will be fined Rs 1000. That's not all. Those who catch the spitters red-handed and inform the society office-bearers will be given an award of Rs 500. The notice, which has been put up all over the society, warns spitters that the society will initiate a move to seize their flats if the fine is not paid.

Society chairman Sanjay Shah, the key architect behind the move, said that the red dirty stains had made the society an ugly place to live in. "It was a sight which could make anyone feel nauseous. No amount of pleadings with anyone was going to help. That is why we decided to initiate the strictest possible move," said Shah, who is a former Garware Nylons employee.

Stating that he has drawn support from all flat owners, Shah said they might not succeed entirely, but a beginning has been made. "Certain people will still spit deliberately. But such elements are there in every society and region. You have to put them in place for larger good of the community," said Shah, who is known in Kasarwadi area as a social-minded person. He wastes no time in rushing to the aid of those in distress.

A delighted Sunita Kandge, a housewife, said,"Mala jar kuni thooktana disla ter me tyachya kaana khali vaajav naar...(If I see anybody spitting after eating gutka or paan, I am going to give him a tight slap). Kandge vahini, as she is fondly addressed, said spitters don't think twice before making a mess of a decent place. "Ashya lokana barobar karayla pahije...(let's put such people in place). Every evening Sunita Kandge leads a bunch of faithfuls, young and the old alike, and sings bhajans and abhangs at a Ganesh temple constructed by joints efforts of the society residents. Priya Deshmukh, a young housewife, said, "Noosta notice lavun chalnar nahin, kadak karvahi karayla havi...(Only displaying notice won't do...stern action should be taken against spitters). Desmukh said the move has been liked by one and all in the society. Civic activists said such a move is unique in the industrial town of Pimpri-Chinchwad.

Heading: Konddeo statue: Sambhaji Brigade renews threat - Indian Express
Content:
While malaria cases are on the rise over the last three years, dengue cases have also been rising consistently every year.

This year alone, dengue has already claimed five — with the recent victim being 26-year-old Vaishali Bhosale from Wadgaonsheri who died at Sassoon General Hospital on October 16. Others who succumbed to the disease hailed from Gokhale Nagar, Bhavani Peth, Viman Nagar and Satara,

According to Dr S V Patil, district malaria officer, there were 108 positive cases of dengue from April to September in Pune district.

Patil said that according to the data from Pimpri-Chinchwad, there were 30 positive cases of dengue while the Pune Municipal Corporation had yet to provide their statistics.

Dr P S Pawar, medical superintendent at Sassoon, which treats patients from outside the district, said that this year, so far, they have registered a total of 47 dengue patients apart from the five deaths.

Dr Rajesh Gadia, chief intensivist at KEM Hospital, said that at least 25 patients are undergoing treatment for dengue at KEM and a chunk of them hail from Kondhwa, Wadgaonsheri, Bhavani Peth and Nana Peth.

Dengue, often known as breakbone fever, is transmitted by aedes aegypti mosquito and is manifested by a sudden onset of severe headache, muscle and joint pains. The classic dengue fever lasts for about six to seven days and clinically the platelet count will drop until the patient's temperature is normal.

According to Gadia, the peak of dengue is September and October when monsoon subsides. What usually happens is that mosquitoes breed in stagnant water.

Hence, after the onset of rain, water gets collected and stored in cement tanks at societies, discarded rubber tyres and others. The mosquitoes, however, cannot withstand cooler climates.

According to Sassoon officials, the number of malaria cases has increased over the years. From 138 cases registered at Sassoon and five deaths in 2005, it has climbed to 177 cases and 17 deaths. Last year saw 240 cases with 28 deaths.

According to the Sassoon data, there were 63 dengue patients in 2007 with two deaths, 99 patients in 2006 with two deaths and 43 patients in 2005 with three deaths.

Heading: Swedes visit PMC with their Princess, discuss development - Indian Express
Content:
"Dadoji Konddeo was not Shivaji's guru, but was only working for him, and there has been no mention in any historic text or relic found that he has been Shivaji's mentor," said Shantaram Kunjir, working president, Sambhaji Brigade.

Dadoji Konddeo, the veteran warrior who is said to have taught the war tactics of sword and 'dandpatta' to Shivaji when he was a young boy, is in the eye of the storm again with the Sambhaji Brigade threatening that, if the statue is not removed it will not stop short of adopting its "own methods."

In 2000, the Pune Municipal Corporation in its golden jubilee year renovated Lal Mahal, the palace where Shivaji and his mother Jijabai lived during his formative years. On a small plot near the entrance, it installed statues of Shivaji tilling the land with a golden plough with Jijabai and Dadoji Konddeo by his side. The tableau portrayed Konddeo as his guru. This had led to a furore in 2004 with the Sambhaji Brigade asking the civic authorities to remove the statue. This eventually led to the closure of the Lal Mahal as a major tourist destination. It was, however, reopened in 2006.

The Brigade had also ransacked the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (BORI) on January 5, 2004, after objecting to certain passages from the book Shivaji — Hindu King in Islamic India by James Laine.

Santosh Chitnis, general secretary, Sambhaji Brigade, Pune said, "Due to the standoff between certain historians and the Sambhaji Brigade members, we were portrayed as a terrorist organisation. We, however, would like to clarify that the Brigade is a law-abiding organisation and believes in fighting for what is true."

Kunjir also insisted that it was Shivaji's father Shahaji who was responsible for mentoring Shivaji.

He said, "Shivaji's initial formative days were spent in Bangalore where he was brought up under the guidance of his father. Then at the age of 13, he was sent to Pune to manage the city. Dadoji Konddeo was just an administrative officer and his tasks were those of taking care of the administration and development of the city. We had already raised the issue in 2004 and had got an assurance from the civic administration that the statue would be removed, in 2006. However, nothing materialised." He also said, "We want the statue of Shahaji Raje to be installed after removing that of Dadoji Konddeo. We have given the administration a period of one month to do so and are hopeful that the civic administration will comply with our demands."

Interestingly, the state government has also put on hold the Dadoji Konddeo award, Maharashtra's own version of the Dronacharya award given out at national level, owing to the controversy regarding whether he was actually Shivaji's guru or not.

The state government has formed a committee of historians to settle this controversy. Shrimant Kokate, A H Salunkhe, Gangadhar Banbare, and Chandrashekhar Shikhare are amongst the prominent members of the committee.

Heading: Comedy reloaded - Indian Express
Content:
A Swedish delegation, led by Crown Princess of Sweden Princess Victoria, visited the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) on Monday to understand the democratic and executive structure of the civic body and to discuss the development work being carried out by the civic administration. The Princess showed interest in understanding the growth of the city and the development planning being undertaken by the PMC with the Swedish Industrial Development Agency (SIDA).

Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi gave a brief presentation on the ongoing development work and the possible sectors where the Swedish Government can contribute.

Pardeshi said that Pune has seen a growth rate of about 12 per cent due to the strong presence of automobile and information technology sectors. The rise of construction industry has seen unexpected growth in the city, he said pointing out that the public transport system was a major cause of concern and that efforts are on with the Swedish agencies to better the situation. Goran Johnson of Ramboll highlighted the assistance being extended by the Sweedish agency for the planning of land use and transport. "Wise planning is needed for the city or else the situation might go out of hand," he said.

Earlier, Mayor Rajlaxmi Bhosale welcomed Princess Victoria

Heading: Ripples effect - Indian Express
Content:
Laughter Challenge winner Sunil Pal's performance left the old pals of COEP in fits of laughter, as they met at the alumni fest

The story of Ratan Noora, aka Sunil Pal is the quintessential rags to riches story except loaded with humour. "I found the character of Ratan Noora when I first came to Mumbai in 1995," says the comedian. "Noora was a regular customer who came in peeke tight, every night at an eatery where I worked as a waiter. I entertained my friends imitating him and they loved it! From that day to today, this character has helped me scale heights, I never imagined."

Pal was in town to perform during the Alumni Fest-08 of College of Engineering, Pune (COEP). His signature Ratan Noora act, got him applause even before he started.

The Pièce de résistance was the enactment of Madhuri Dixit being kidnapped by Veerappan where Pal imitated Bollywood actors like Sunil Shetty, Nana Patekar Naseeruddin Shah and so on.

Although having worked as a junior artist in films with Aamir Khan, Priety Zinta and Aishwarya Rai, it wasn't till he won the first Great Indian Laughter Challenge in 2005 that he finally arrived! Making time for films as well as stand up shows he talks about the challenges in both. "During a film shoot you have to focus on many things at once, camera angle, script, co-artists and many other things, so focus is divided. In stand up performance, your script has to be packed with punches, it's a live audience and one cannot afford to let the act drag anywhere, I usually choose common topics like saas-bahu and husband-wife quarrels that people identify with." Not content with waiting for grand offers to come his way, Pal has embarked on a new venture on a grand scale."Bhavnao ko Samjho, is a film written, directed and produced by me. For the first time 54 comedians will be shown together on the silver screen. It might even get us a mention in the Limca Book of Records," says Pal.

Speaking of the new crop of comedy films doing well at the box offices he feels that it is not just a phase, "Where there are tears there will be laughter, comedy has always been an integral part of cinema, be it Akbar-Birbal stories, Charlie Chaplin, slapstick or risqué. It is just the representational styles that keep changing."

One wonders what makes the King of Laughter laugh, "Almost anyone or anything can make me laugh. Everyday life can be turned into a humourous situation. I love watching Johnny Lever and Rajpal Yadav on screen though."

So what does this funny man do when not making people laugh? "I just sleep" is his rapid response. Getting ready to leave for a performance at the event, he leaves with a parting shot for youngsters, "In today's fast paced competitive lifestyle even fun has taken new meaning, mainly partying, drugs or alcohol. The term 'clean fun' is almost redundant. Don't take tension, the only person you should compete against is yourself. Bas haso aur hasate raho."

The fest was 60 minutes of pure entertainment. Also commendable was the performances by the students of COEP — classical dance and music, skits as well as dancing to popular numbers from Rock On, besides a hard-hitting message on the bomb blasts. Enjoying the evening thoroughly were R Vasudevan, president COEP Alumni, Anil Sahasrabuddhe, director, COEP, Prof Harish Shah from Stanford, Lila and Firoz Poonawalla, Narendra Kale, chairman, Kale Consultants, Sanjay Inamdar, managing director, Flucon, to name a few.

Heading: Swedish ties - Indian Express
Content:
It took just 21 days for Lila Poonawalla Foundation to transform 13 ordinary girls into Peace Ambassadors by taking them on a trip to UK

If you educate one woman, you educate a family," This was profound insight by Neelu Nanwani, one of the Lila Fellows chosen to attend a three-week training programme held at Gloucestershire, United Kingdom.

In collaboration with UK based Asha Foundation, started by human rights campaigner and author Zerbanoo Gifford, the Lila Poonawalla Foundation undertook an ambitious project of grooming young women into peace ambassadors. "This is the first batch that we sent and it has been a wonderful success. Many of these girls had never been out of Pune, let alone on an airplane to UK, they were neither familiar with poetry nor public speaking and had not got a chance to discover life beyond routine. Now they can confidentially act out sonnets from Shakespeare, skillfully manage time, assume leadership and respect other cultures," says Lila Poonawalla.

The project from August 10 to August 30, included trips to Oxford University, Tin Tern Abbey, Jane Austen Centre, Roman Bath and the Grange, a centre for people with learning disabilities. The girls attended a series of lectures on effective leadership, stress management, cultural appreciation and negotiation skills. They presented plays, dances, performed eurhythmy and cooked delicacies for an Indian tea party for the people at the Grange. "We had heard that foreign countries are clean and disciplined, but there we observed their social life, first hand. My English has improved I have become more punctual and learnt to listen, not just speak," says Madhuri Kad.

For Kasturi Paigude this trip was about discovery. "We have so many social norms and expectations bogging us down here, there we were free and empty and could absorb whatever we wanted to learn."

Swarada Angal says that she has returned a new person, "This has been the most enriching experience of my life, to observe the education system there and interact with professors who treated their students with respect was something I am not accustomed to here. I also learnt about dignity of labour — be it gardener, shop attendants or the disabled people weaving shawls, everyone enjoyed their work and did it with complete dedication."

"The change in these girls is phenomenal, we wish to send more batches of students and offer this opportunity to all the girls from Pune, but we need more people to help us with the funding," says Firoz Poonawalla.

Although inter-cultural programmes have been conducted before, the difference in this one was the skillful selection of the right candidates. One needs to have outstanding academic records and show real aptitude for hard work to be awarded a fellowship by the foundation anyway. "To choose the top 13 of these meant we were looking for that extra bit. These girls have passion, determination and the will to influence society, not just keep the learning to themselves," says Poonawalla.

Hence the girls who were chosen were the ones who with just a hint of opportunity would squeeze it to the last drop.

Within two months of being back they have been brain-storming regularly to come with effective grass root models to deal with global warming, education and conservation. If just one batch of peace ambassadors can start turning the wheels of society so soon, just imagine what a batch like this every year could do!

Heading: Manning moves - Indian Express
Content:
On a visit to Vikhe Patil School in city, crown Princess Victoria

of Sweden is impressed by the diverse culture of India

Be it music, literature or economy, the east and the west exchanging resources for the betterment of the society is not new. And this time, to strengthen the bond between Sweden and India, Her Royal Highness, crown Princess Victoria of Sweden visited Vikhe Patil School in Pune on Monday.

The princess was in the city to understand the overall functioning of the Indian school and at the same time learn about the development work being conducted at Loni by Swedish International Development Agency (Sida). "This is the first time that I have visited India. It has been a long awaited dream that has finally come true," says the princess.

Explaining the purpose of her visit, the princess says, "This was a relatively short visit given the fact that India is a diverse country. But yes, this was an effective crash course in understanding the culture and traditions of India."

The princess was welcomed by the students of Vikhe Patil School, who presented traditional Indian dances in front of the foreign delegates. An impressive presentation of folk dances on the famous track- Mile sur mera tumhara won the audiences' applause. Ashok Vikhe Patil, founder, Vikhe Patil School explained the rural development work being conducted by Pravara Medical Trust, Loni along with the activities conducted at the school.

Declaring the purpose of her visit to be extremely successful the princess further says, "I am very happy with the kind of work that is being conducted here. I understand that India is a developing country but it is satisfying to know that the education scene in India is changing and efforts are being taken to educate children from rural areas. I hope that this work continues and I get an opportunity to visit the country again."

Heading: Sport and spirits - Indian Express
Content:
Son of famous Bharatnatyam dancer Mallika Sarabhai, Revanta Sarabhai feels that art cannot be associated with sexual identity

At 24, this heir apparent of Sarabhai legacy defines his own existence with set lines of his ingenious skills. And the legacy of cadence is carried from two ladies to the man in the family where the man leaves no stone unturned in balancing the components of Lasaya and Tandava in his moves. Apart from basking in the glory of an impressive lineage, Revanta Sarabhai, grandson of Mrilani Sarabhai and son of famous bharatnatyam danseuse Mallika Sarabhai, has earned his own identity.

In the city this Sunday to give a bharatnatyam recital on the theme Celebrations, for the Poona Music Society, the prodigy shares his perspective for his passion.

At the age of eight when Revanta gave his first solo performance at the Lotus temple in Ahmedabad, the hope of man taking the centre stage in classical Indian dance soared high. And here he is living up to the expectations. With more than a hundred Bharatnatyam recital shows and solos scattered across the globe, Revanta strives to bring back the lost legacy of the role of a male dancer in Indian classical dance as he goes about elaborating on the components of Bharatnatyam. "Bharatnatayam is born out of the dance of the universe. Shiva and Paravati when they dance what originates is Bharatnatyam," says Revanta who also is a trained Kuchipudi dancer. The dancer who has completed a BFA from the University of Arts from Philadelphia further elaborates, "There are two very distinct components in the dance form, Tandava and Lasaya. Where Tandava explores vigour and energy Lasaya on the other hand explores grace and beauty. A dancer has to be the embodiment of both."

Revanta, who also is trained in contemporary dance forms and martial art feels dance cannot be associated with sexual identity. "I think of myself as a body driven by intricate rhythmic pattern, beats and above all passion for dance." According to him a true dancer balances both in his movements and expressions. A man and a woman they both complete each other and a dancer cannot do justice to dance if he does not balance both these attributes in him or her."

Today, when women completely dominate the traditional classical dance and the names of male classical dancers are hard to come by, Revanta's approach towards dance is refreshing. "I also want the youth to take notice of traditional classical dance. Where hip-hop and reggae is gaining ground, I want to shift the focus of youth to traditional Indian dance and that will only happen when men as well as women both will equally feel a sense of belonging to the dance form," says he.

Heading: Words Worth - Indian Express
Content:
CYG concluded on a colourful note as Nivedita Saboo embodied culture with a resplendent fashion show

All is well that ends well and the Commonwealth Youth Games were almost accurate here with a host of enchanting activities around to mark its concluding ceremony. The most shimmering of them was the evening at Ishanya that had the creme de la creme of the city enjoy a variety of cultural programmes, fashion shows, art displays and laser shows.

It was tussle of performances between Sudarshan Chakraborty's dance troupe Sapphire and Nivedita Saboo's fashion cherubs.

Designer Nivedita Saboo embodied couture and culture with the resplendent fashion show by the queens of ramp walking on a backdrop of water fountains and laser illumination ensembling various patterns. "The collection is a shift from the games to the festive season however I have kept the CYG colours in mind and created colourful couture. It has been breathtaking with a confluence of my show, dances and entertainment coming together to congratulate the gaming spirits," adds Nivedita Saboo

Sapphire presented vigorous shifts and fiery moves dancing on themes of fire and water. And the models paced and posed to the formations of choreographer Achla Sachdev.

The queens of ramp, including Aditi Govitrikar, Anupama Verma, Bunty Grewal, Pooja Chopra, Vidut Jamwal, Meghna Kawale and Rosie Nicholson looked stunning with traditional wears. They mesmerised the guests with sequences such as Resplendent Swayamvar, 80s revisited and Shimmer Forever.

The artistic evening was hosted by Shailesh Mehta and Parul Mehta and had many foreign delegates get the taste of India. Suresh Kalmadi, MP seemed in high spirits over the success as he added, "Pune has been a great host and it's been a energetic journey with dedicated teams. It's over to Delhi now with greater expectations for the 2010 games."

Heading: Across country, chorus for action against Raj and his men - Indian Express
Content:
Renowned Bengali writer Sunil Gangopadhyay feels that people need to be optimistic about globalisation and culture will survive on its own

Sobriety, humility and simplicity looked pleased as the living legend carried them along in his journey of success. Sunil Gangopadhyay, the doyen of Bengali literature with unassuming looks and pleasant countenance, is a man who has learnt to take success in his stride. Born in Faridpur, the 74-year-old Bengali writer, who also happens to be the president of Sahitya Academy, was felicitated by the Bangiya Sanskriti Samsad (BSS), in Pune recently. A prolific writer, Sunil Gangopadhyay has authored more than 200 books and experimented with different genres, which include travelogues, children's fictions, poems, features, essays and short stories. He is one of those distinguished writers whose stories- Aranyer Din Ratri and Arjun, Pratidwandi have been made into films by Satyajit Ray.

"I started writing in my youth because when you are young you are sensitive. You fall in love, you feel the pain and then you automatically start writing," smiles he. But at the same time, he expresses concern over the indifferent attitude of the younger generation towards Bengali literature, "Learning English is very good as well as very important in today's scenario. Even knowledge of Hindi is much required but at the same time mothertongue should not be neglected. In fact the responsibility lies with the parents to create an interest among the children towards the literature."

The audience at the felicitation ceremony sat enchanted as a famous play of the author Praner Prahari was enacted by some of the members of BSS. While the playwright watched the play in rapt attention quietly appreciating the effort, the audience marveled at his sensitivity towards human emotions and lucid expressions in writing. An institution in himself, the writer started his career with poetry, however, in a candid confession he shares, "I was flabbergasted when I was asked to pen down my first novel. I did not know from where to start. It was then that I met an American writer who suggested that writing a novel is very easy. Just remember a date of your life and all that you did on that day. You'll get the idea for your story.

Taking heed of his suggestion I have used this technique many times." The writer's first novel was Atmaprakash. Some of his famous works include Aranyer din- ratri(the days and nights of the forest), Sei Som oi, Prothom Alo( first light), Purush, Yubok Yubotira (The Youth), Kakababu series, Bondhubandhob(an unusual work on friendship) among others. Talking about his love for Pune, Gangopadhyay says, "I have been coming to Pune since many years. Earlier it was not as crowded as it is now. Pune has always been a cultural and educational hub but today it has progressed in terms of industry as well. These days we have ample number of people complaining about globalisation taking its toll on cultural identities. We should not be afraid of globalisation. Life goes on. If a culture dies with the pressure of globalisation, let it die. A culture exists on its intrinsic strength. Don't be pessimistic. Strong cultures will survive", concludes the legend.

Heading: No vertical limit: High-rises on tiny plots get OK - Indian Express
Content:
The violent attacks by Raj Thackeray's men against North Indians in the city and suburbs on Sunday sparked a volley of reactions from across the country on Monday. In Parliament, at press gatherings and through statements, voices from across the political spectrum demanded action against those who planned and supported the attack on "outsiders" gathered to take an exam being held by the Railway Recruitment Board.

Congress spokesperson Jayanti Natarajan told reporters that the party's government would take immediate steps to punish the guilty and bring them to justice. Replying to a question about action against the MNS chief, she said those who act against the Constitution and create strains in the social fabric should be dealt with sternly.

Here is what the others said:

Maharashtra state BJP chief Nitin Gadkari: "Whenever MNS is involved in such violent acts, both Chief Minister and the Deputy Chief Minister talk of teaching the culprits a lesson and not allowing such acts. However, they don't do what they say. This only goes to prove that the ruling coalition wants to allow the social peace in Mumbai to be disturbed so that they get political benefits. A political party deliberately takes law into its hands and the government looks the other way."

Bihar CM Nitish Kumar: "I will talk to the Prime Minister in this regard as the Maharashtra government has totally failed to check the spurt in violent activities of divisive forces in Maharashtra and the Centre should issue a directive to Maharashtra government."

BJP leader Shatrughan Sinha: "The insane elements have been targeting people from Bihar and Uttar Pradesh frequently and the Maharashtra government has failed to stop them... I appeal to the Prime Minister to intervene to sternly deal with the divisive elements posing a challenge to the unity of the country."

CPI party statement: "Any leniency shown to these divisive forces will have far-reaching consequences for the unity and integrity of the country."

Jharkhand Mukti Morcha leader Nasar Fidausi: "Such incidents have been taking place for past couple of years but no action was initiated by the Maharashtra government to arrest Raj Thackeray against whom a local court here had issued a non-bailable warrant last month for abusing the Bihari community and the Chhat festival."

Lok Janshakti Party leader Ram Chandra Paswan: "Congress-NCP government is not competent enough to protect the lives and belongings of North Indians living in the state. Moreover the state government appears to be encouraging MNS for electoral gains, while North Indians are being tortured. Otherwise how can somebody continue with violent campaigns against a particular community for so long."

CPI(M) Politburo in a statement: "That it (the government) has failed to do so and in fact is showing leniency to the leader of the outfit shows the utter bankruptcy of the politics of Congress and its coalition partner."

Heading: 7/11: BJP says cops not sure who did it, demands CBI, judicial probe - Indian Express
Content:
MHADA clears 24 proposals, 11 of them will have FSI of over 2.5

The worst nightmares of urban planners may just be coming true in Mumbai. Last week, the Mumbai board of the Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MHADA) cleared about 24 proposals that will allow the metamorphosis of two- to three-storey buildings on small plots into towering high-rises.

Of these, 11 proposals foresee consuming a Floor Space Index (total buildable area on a plot) of over 2.5.

In September, the Supreme Court removed the cap of 2.5 FSI imposed by the High Court on redevelopment of buildings built prior to 1940 and allowed an unlimited vertical growth for such structures even if they are not dilapidated. The SC order also does away with minimum open space required to be kept between two buildings.

These are the first set of proposals to be okayed following the SC order.

A classic example is that of Chunilal Baldev building in Bhuleshwar, one of the most crammed places in the island city. The three-storey building is on a tiny 60 sq mt plot. With a proposed FSI of 4.85, the new building will be at least 15 storeys high. A redevelopment project in Khetwadi has proposed a staggering 6.3 FSI on a narrow 260 sq mt plot, another one in heavily crowded area of Fort has asked for a 4.92 FSI on a narrow 104 sq mt plot.

"FSI of over six on a 260 sq mt plot would mean that the building would go as high as 30 storeys. Though legally this may be allowed, such tall structures with little open space around them will end up compromising on residents' safety as they will be highly unserviceable," said Pankaj Joshi from the Urban Design Research Institute.

MHADA officials, who are expecting an avalanche of such proposals, state that these 24 projects will now be issued a No-Objection Certificate after which they will be forwarded to the BMC for approval.

Meanwhile, the BMC too has received its share of proposals. These are amended plans for proposals that were approved as per restrictions on FSI imposed by the Bombay High Court two years ago. "As per the High Court ruling, these 160 proposals had a FSI cap of 4. Following the Supreme Court's ruling, some of the developers amended their plans and asked for an FSI between 4 and 8," said CV Saste, deputy chief engineer for the BMC's building proposal department.

"At this rate the city is going to get completely unlivable. Such constructions will be a fire hazard and lead to traffic congestion in already congested areas. The BMC is bound by rule to approve them. The lack of wide roads and similar infrastructure is not a criteria," said urban planner Shirish Patel, the petitioner in the Supreme Court case.

Heading: As MNS revives attacks, ‘vulnerable’ taxi men have unions busy fighting each other - Indian Express
Content:
de points out terror outfits named were different in two police versions

Who is behind the serial train blasts of July, 2006? With the Mumbai Police recently claiming that Indian Mujahideen, now blamed for the recent terror attacks across the country, executed the blasts, the state BJP on Monday demanded CBI as well as judicial inquiry into the July 11 explosions that killed 188 people.

Talking to mediapersons, BJP national general secretary Gopinath Munde said that after the blasts at seven places on July 11, 2006, the then Commissioner of Police A N Roy had announced on September 30, 2006, that Pakistan's ISI, Lashkar-e-Toiba and SIMI were behind the blasts. But, Munde said, on September 24, 2008, Commissioner of Police Hasan Gafoor declared that that blasts were executed by the Indian Mujahideen.

"How can this be possible?" Munde asked. "What is the truth?" He pointed out that the names of the accused persons and the terror outfits involved were different in the two police versions.

He said that if the same police commissionerate was telling two different stories about the same case, it was a serious lapse and the truth should come out. "If the Indian Mujahideen were involved in the train blasts and police officials had closed the inquiry against them, I feel that the blasts at Jaipur, Delhi and Malegaon could have been averted," Munde said. "If this is the seriousness with which the police is investigating the blasts, it will only help the accused persons get acquitted and the truth will never come out," he said.

He claimed that in the past two weeks, about 70 to 80 police officials had met him and pointed out the "lapses."

Reacting to the recent observation of NCP chief Sharad Pawar that terrorism in the country began after BJP's Rath Yatra and the demolition of Babri Masjid, Munde said that blasts and other violent activities were in existence in states like Jammu and Kashmir even before that. "His allegations are baseless," he added.

Heading: In the season of recession, city registers a rise: In its BPL numbers - Indian Express
Content:
dros of Mumbai Taximen's Union has filed defamation case against his rival Sharad Rao who had accused him of receiving bribe from taxi drivers

At a time when the Raj Thackeray-led Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) has revived its attacks against the north Indians, the taxi drivers in the city, a majority of whom are from north India, are faced with a piquant situation: Instead of holding out together, their unions have locked horns with each other.

Anthony Lawrence Quadros, general secretary of the Mumbai Taximen's Union, on Saturday filed a defamation case against rival unionist Sharad Rao, who had alleged in a press conference last week that Quadros had received a bribe from the taxi men.

In a petition filed against Sharad Rao and T Kurien, another union leader, at the Bandra Metropolitan Court, Quadros states that Rao had alleged he (Quadros) was earning Rs 15,000 per taxi in the process of buying new taxis for the taxi men. "This is insulting and has tarnished my reputation and has hurt me immensely," Quadros has said.

There are some 1.5 lakh taxi drivers who drive 50,000 taxis in the city. The Quadros-led taximen's union claims to have a following of over 47,000 taxi drivers. Also, there are three major taxi unions to which the city taxi men are affiliated to. But the unity among the taxi men is fractured. Agrees Quadros: "The taxi unions should unite, but there are egos that act as a hurdle here. The unions should show a united front on this."

Early this year, the MNS activists had targeted the north Indian taxi drivers and damaged their vehicles. The help from the unions did act as a healer to the taxi men. The unions had also made representation to the government against the rage faced by the taxi men.

"We know little about politics, but whichever union we are affiliated to should take up the cause of taxi men. We do face problems from the RTO, traffic police, the transport department and also the MNS. In this case, it would be better for us if the unions are united," said a taxi driver requesting anonymity.

Meanwhile, when contacted Kurien of the Mumbai autorickshaw union denied receiving any notice from the court. "I don't have any problem with Quadros¿ and the unions should unite," he said. Rao, however, was not available for comment in spite of repeated attempts. According to Rao's close aide Govind Kamtekar, the union leader was at Azamgarh to attend a meeting.

Heading: Fire at 27-year-old Kaskar Industrial Estate, no casualty - Indian Express
Content:
BMC survey says 12.17 lakh families have per capita income of less than Rs 591.75 per month

The global meltdown may be hitting the rich and well-to-do, but simultaneously the number of those Below Poverty Line (BPL) is rising in the country's financial capital, according to the statistics compiled by the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation.

Despite being labelled the world's seventh largest city in terms of billionaire population by Forbes, the city has an unusually high number of people — around 12.17 lakh families — who earn less than Rs 591.75 per month, do not own a house, fridge or television.

While, Mumbai's average net worth is pegged at $7.6 billion, the labour class remains neglected. In a survey carried out by the BMC, 12,02,355 families claimed to be BPL. After suggestions and objections over the last four months, the figure has increased by another 15,000 families.

"There is an addition of around 15,000 families and roughly 75,000 people. Now the state government will decide the poorest of the poor among them," said chief community development officer and project officer in charge of urban poverty eradication, Jyoti Panda. "We have checked the claims of the surveyed families and now we recognise them as BPL on various parameters."

In the coming months the state government is expected to declare the poorest of the poor. Usually this figure is 10 per cent of the total BPL families (10 per cent of 12 lakh families is 1.2 lakh families). "There will be then two priority lists and programmes will be undertaken in phases to improve their standard of living," she said.

The survey was carried out using a questionnaire comprising 54 socio-economic parameters, including housing, profession, education, infrastructure availability and family background. "Not everyone identified as BPL is economically weak. There are families which are educationally backward or do not have proper infrastructure like a house, but are well-off in other parameters," Panda said.

The city's population is estimated at 1.3 crore and around 60.75 lakh people have been mentioned that their expenditure per person per month is less than Rs 591.75 or that they do not have a telephone, refrigerator or a two-wheeler and that they find it difficult to have access to the basic services like toilet, school and house.

The survey carried out by the state's Urban Development Department in 225 towns and 18 big cities has revealed that the number of families living below the poverty line in cities has gone down by 9.03 per cent, but the figure has gone up by 12.52 per cent in smaller towns in the last decade. However, the figures for Mumbai are in sharp contrast to this.

* Total families surveyed: 16.07 lakh

BPL families: 12.17 lakh
* Maximum number of BPL families: Andheri - 1.8 lakh, Bhandup -1 lakh
* Least number of BPL families: Girgaon -1862, Kalbadevi - 2980

Heading: Hot October: BMC to seek more water from Bhatsa dam - Indian Express
Content:
A week after a major fire at Kalbadevi's Johri Mansion, another fire broke out on Monday morning at Kaskar Industrial Estate in Oshiwara. This 27-year-old industrial estate housed as many as 40 small galas, mostly of small scale industries, and a branch of the Union bank of India. Though there was no casualty reported, the owner of the industrial estate claimed that goods worth Rs 7 crore were damaged. Of the 40 galas, only four were not gutted in the fire and it took nearly three hours to douse the fire, said the sources.

According the eyewitnesses, the fire broke out at a gala that housed plastic and acrylic goods. "Everything happened suddenly. We immediately informed the Andheri fire brigade and Goregaon fire brigade. They rushed to the spot within minutes," said security guard of the estate and eyewitness Vinod Yadav.

As many as 16 fire engines, 11 water tankers, four ambulances and a hydraulic platform rushed to the spot. "We came here as soon as we got the tip-off. Though investigations are going on, prima facie we think that there was a short-circuit in the first floor," said Chief Fire Officer A V Sawant. Fire officials thanked for the timely tip-off as a big tragedy could be averted. "Right behind this estate is a slum area. If there was a delay, we would have faced a larger tragedy," said Sawant.

According to the fire officials, fire spread fast because of the presence of plastic and acrylic materials in the building. "Both plastic and acrylic are highly combustible materials. They catch fire very fast and emit highly toxic gases. This slowed down the cooling operation," said Sawant.

Local corporator and member of the BMC's standing committee Rajul Patel condemned the lack of fire hydrants near the area, which, according to him, could have reduced the damage. "Every day we hear about such fire accidents in the city. Some of these accidents can be prevented with hydrants. Most of the roads lack these hydrants. Hydrants on some of the streets don't work too. I will take up the matter in this week's standing committee meeting," said Patel. A fire hydrant is an active fire protection measure which helps fire fighters access municipal water supply to assist in extinguishing the fire.

Locals also alleged that the lack of mandatory water body inside the industrial estate also contributed in spreading the fire. "All industrial estates should have a small water body inside the compound which can help in these kind of cases. Such a water body is absent here. We'll submit a report to the BMC once the cooling operations are over," said Sawant.

Heading: Walkeshwar murder: Police nab another accused - Indian Express
Content:
Rise in mercury levels lead to increased water demand; Civic body to appoint contractors to look after leakage complaints

After a week of sustained arguments from corporators over an impending water crisis in the city and more drama over the issue on Monday in the BMC's general body meeting, the civic officials have promised to take stock and resolve the situation.

Civic officials admitted that the sudden rise in October heat has led to increased demand for water. At present, the city requires 4,250 million liters per day (MLD) of water, while the supply is only of 3,400 MLD, nearly 20% less. "To meet the rising demand, the administration will be meeting the state government this week and request them to supply us more water from the Bhatsa dam," Municipal Commissioner Jairaj Phatak said.

Last week, coporators had pointed that a lot of water is wasted due to leakages. As per civic officials, such leakages lead to wastage of around 18 to 20% of drinkable water, and so the BMC has decided to appoint contractors who will look after leakage complaints only. "Earlier we had separate posts in the hydraulic department to look after leakages, these posts have been closed for sometime now. We will fill up these posts immediately," said Phatak. Keeping in mind, the shortage of junior engineers in the hydraulic engineering department, the BMC will also start recruitment for around 1,500 vacant posts.

"The Middle Vaitarna and Gargai-Pinjar projects are underway. When they will be completed, the city will have more water. However, Middle Vaitarna will only get over by 2011 and Gargai-Pinjar will take longer. We will have to make do with current facilities to deal with the problem," Phatak stated.

According to sources, administrative wards of L and M are the worst affected. Civic body stated that such areas will be given water tankers and bore wells. They will also undertake a study of the water distribution patterns to check the problem of uneven water distribution. "Uneven water distribution is another problem. Sometimes civic body just diverts water channel from one ward to another, which is not really a solution for uneven distribution. We need concrete solution for this problem," said BJP corporator and member of the standing committee, Yogesh Sagar.

The civic body will also resume its efforts to popularise rain-water harvesting to deal with the situation.

Heading: 3 arrested for murder of youth in Nagpada - Indian Express
Content:
A day after the police claimed to have nabbed the prime accused in the murder of a 78-year-old woman, Indu Udeshi, another accused was picked up from Elphinstone Road on Monday. According to the police, the three men who had visited Udeshi, two days before her body was found, were the last ones to see her alive.

During the interrogations, the prime suspect, Sandeep Pawar, confessed to his crime and revealed the role of his uncle Sunil Narkar in the conspiracy, said the police.

According to Senior Police Inspector Iqbal Shaikh from the Malabar Hill police station, "After we interrogated Sandeep, he revealed the whereabouts of Narkar and admitted his role in the conspiracy. We also recovered a partial amount of Rs 8,500 of the stolen property from him."

When asked about the background of Narkar, Shaikh said that Narkar used to do odd jobs.

"We are still conducting enquiries to trace the identity of the third suspect who had accompanied the arrested accused. However, as of now we can not disclose any more details about the third person as it might hamper the investigation," added Shaikh.

Udeshi's body was discovered on Sunday at her plush apartment in Walkeshwar by her servant and her sister-in-law.

Heading: Man accused of killing HIV positive wife walks free - Indian Express
Content:
Tardeo police claim to have arrested the accused in the murder of a youth, Raffan Khan, whose body was found in pieces in bags near Willingdon Club on October 12. The accused, identified as Sarfaraz Khan (22), Taqir Khan (20) and Ram Bhawan Paswan (25), used to work in the same workshop as Raffan and had an argument with him on the day of the incident over some money matters, say the police.

The trio was arrested on Sunday and has been booked for murder.

Khan's body, which was cut into pieces and stuffed in bags, was spotted by a passerby who informed the police. "The body was cut with a chopper and there were injury marks on the head of the victim," said Police Inspector Mohan Waghmare from the Tardeo police station.

The police also found a piece of paper in the pocket of the victim's trousers with some phone numbers on it. On calling up on one of those numbers, police came across Talib Khan, victim's friend who stayed in the same village as Khan near Lucknow. Talib told the police that the victim along with six other youths had moved to Mumbai two years back and were working at a metal polishing workshop unit at Nagpada.

"We sent our teams to his village and collected information on the identities of those 6 youths and also brought Talib to Mumbai to identify Raffan's body," said Waghmare.

On being questioned, one of those six youths, Sarfaraz Khan broke down and confessed to have killed Raffan with the help of two others — Taqir and Ram. "The trio confessed that they used to stay together on the top floor of the workshop and Raffan used to send his earnings home regularly. Therefore, he could not lend money to the accused whenever they needed it. On the day of the incident, they got in an argument with Raffan in the workshop during which the three assaulted him with some equipment, leading to his death," said Waghmare.

According to the confession, the trio then chopped body and stuffed it in bags at the workshop and dumped the bags near Willingdon club on October 12 to avoid any suspicion. They three have been charged with murder, said Waghmare.

Heading: Cong man elected corporator after Shiv Sainik’s disqualification - Indian Express
Content:
The sessions court on Monday acquitted a man charged with killing his wife who was HIV positive.

Dayashankar Vishwakarma (27), was acquitted on Monday after the prosecution failed to prove its theory of supari killing (contract killing), and could not provide with circumstantial evidence to nail the accused.

According to the police, the victim was married to Vishwakarma's first cousin, and after his death got married to the accused.

The prosecution argued that it was during victim's first marriage that she got infected with HIV.

However, soon after Vishwakarma found out that his wife was HIV positive, he planned to kill her, said the prosecution. The police in the case had mentioned a person named Raju Kanya, who had taken a loan of Rs 15,000 from Vishwakarma. In lieu of the loan, Kanya agreed to kill Vishwakarma's wife, said the prosecution.

On June 17, 2007 while Kajal and her four-year-old son were at home, Kanya allegedly strangled her to death with a wire. The neighbours were alerted when the child started crying and immediately informed the police. Though Kanya fled the scene, Vishwakarma was arrested later. "Only seven witnesses were examined in the court. Prosecution did not summon the prime witness, who was believed to have overheard Vishwakarma's plan to kill his wife," said defence advocate Jayesh Vithlani.

Defence had earlier argued that Vishwakarma was not in Mumbai on the day of the murder. Judge R U Deshmukh thus acquitted Vishwakarma of all charges, while Kanya still is an absconding accused.

Heading: Man arrested in Dahisar for extortion threats - Indian Express
Content:
The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation on Monday announced that Jagdish Kutty of the Congress has been elected as a corporator in place of disqualified Shiv Sena corporator Subhash Kanta Sawant from Chakala, Sahar airport.

Kutty was the second highest candidate in terms of number votes polled in the elections held last year.

Sawant was disqualified after the caste scrutiny committee found discrepancies in the caste certificate following which Kutty,appealed to BMC to consider him for the post of corporator, as he had the maximum number of votes after Sawant. Accordingly, he was elected.

However, Shiv Sena opposed the move, branding it as a conspiracy on behalf of the state government of Congress- NCP, to bring down the majority of the saffron combine in the BMC. "Only Sena corporators were sidelined for the disqualification. No Congress corporator has come under the scanner. This has been done on purpose," said Sena leader, Ravindra Waikar. BJP leader Bhalchandra Shirsat moved a notice of motion in the General Body meeting, objecting to direct appointment of the second candidate as the corporator. "There has to be re-election and people should be given a chance to elect the candidate they want," he said.

While total of six corporators were disqualified, the re-election was kept on hold after the candidates moved the Bombay High Court and the Supreme Court. Only in the case of Simintini Nadkar, Sena's disqualified corporator, re-election was held, as the second winning candidate had failed to appeal to the BMC.

Heading: WR inaugurates its heritage gallery at Churchgate - Indian Express
Content:
Accused was inspired by a news programme on Javed Chikna

A news programme which profiled Javed Chikna, a "D Company extortionist", led Abu Talib Alauddin Khan (32) to become his imposter and make extortion calls.

Khan, a Dahisar resident, was on Monday picked up in the afternoon after Crime branch unit XII probe found him to be the voice behind threat calls that were made to two prominent builders from Mumbai, including one from Khar.

Khan, who was in dire need of money for some personal reasons, has told the Crime Branch that he figured the techniques of extortion through the news programme which showed how international phone cards are used and the manner in which extortion calls are made, which he then implemented by the script.

One of the builder assuming that it was the actual call from the underworld, was almost going to part with the extortion amount of Rs 50 lakh on Wednesday, before which the Crime Branch made the arrest, said sources at Crime branch.

Khan a driver by profession already has cases against him of assault and a 1992 case of extortion against him. "He would go to the many building projects where redevelopment is to take place and get details and information of the builders who he would later threaten," says Rakesh Maria, joint commissioner of police (crime).

The Crime Branch found two mobile phones and four SIM cards including an international phone card which he had not yet used for the threat calls. "He would call them up and say he is Javed Chikna and demand Rs 50 lakh to one crore," said Maria.

Heading: Advertising contract on various railway stations delayed again - Indian Express
Content:
A heritage gallery constructed by the Western Railway (WR) was inaugurated on Monday by A K Jhingron, general manager, Western Railway, at Railway headquaters building in Churchgate. According to the WR sources, the gallery has a collection of rare artifacts dating back to pre-Western Railway era.

"Giving a heritage look to the big hall — from conceptualisation to materialisation— took a year to complete. The work on the gallery would have been completed on August 15, but due to some reasons the work could not be completed. In Bhavnagar and Ahmedabad , Western Railway has it's heritage galleries. In headquarters of every division of the Western Railway, such galleries will be constructed, " said Jhingron. "It is just a beginning. We will add more rare photographs, greeting cards and books relating to the Railways to the gallery," he said.

According to the sources, many offices at the ground floor of the GM Building were shifted to other places to make way for the heritage gallery.

"The heritage gallery is an attempt to bring all the historical items spread across the divisions of the Western Railway under one roof. A 2184 sq ft hall has been specially designed for this purpose. Heritage items from various divisions such as Mumbai, Vadodara, Ratlam, Rajkot, Ahmedabad and Bhavnagar have been brought and displayed in a thematic manner. Around Rs 35 lakh has been spent to construct this heritage gallery," said Shyam Sunder Gupta, CPRO, Western Railway.

The heritage items displayed at the gallery include steam engine model, crockery and cutters of the Bombay-Baroda & Central India Railway (BB&CI) dating back to late 1800s, trophies such as Challengers trophy of 1894, various signalling equipment, communication equipment and Manglore tiles of 1865. These items were used in the early days of the Railways, WR sources said. Hand grenade that was used during Chinese aggression and a tablet-type single line block instrument which was used to pass messages to station masters— these instruments were given to the drivers— are also displayed at the gallery. Western Railway Additional General Manager R S Chugh and other senior officers were present at the inaugural function.

Heading: Diamond jewellery worth over Rs 25 lakh looted - Indian Express
Content:
Mega tender of high reserve price, exorbitant form cost scrapped;but company that won the tender has moved court now

It was a record of sorts when the Western Railway (WR) fixed the price of a tender form, for a contract for advertisement rights in station premises, at a whopping Rs 25,000 per form. As expected, the exorbitant pricing of the tender form turned counterproductive with not a single bidder showing up to purchase the form.

Moreover, advertising contractors were also wary of the tendering exercise owing to the WR's reserve price of Rs 52 crore, which was twice the advertising revenue of about Rs 26 crore recorded last year.

"The reason behind this exercise is simple — some WR officials don't want to give long term contacts for advertisement in stations between Churchgate and Dahanu Road as there is more personal gain in short term contracts that can be given without tendering. It is a way to mint money by doing favour to their favourites," said a WR official.

Even big advertising contractors are not willing to work with the Railways due to non-cooperation from the officials. "The Railway officials don't want to let contractors work. They do anything to harass us— from not providing electricity to starting civil work at stations. Eventually, the contractor suffers losses and runs away, and the purpose of these officials is served," an advertising contractor said without wanting to be identified.

Three years ago, a firm named Meena Advertisers was given advertisement rights between (1) Churchgate to Mumbai Central, (2) Mahalaxmi to Elphistone Road, (3) Dadar and (4) Andheri to Goregaon. However, soon the Railway Board showed interest in 'mega contracts' for advertising at all stations and the WR had invited tenders, after terminating small contracts like this one. "In March 2008, my two contracts from Churchgate to Mumbai Central and Mahalaxmi to Elphistone Road were terminated because of mega tender. Though mega tender was awarded, it did not work," said Bipin Raje, proprietor of Meena Advertisers.

Ashok Sharma and Associates, which won the mega contract for advertising for all stations from Churchgate to Dahanu Road, is now in court against the Railways. On why did the company leave, all Kalpana Kale, manager of Ashok Sharma and Associates, said was: "We cannot comment on it as the matter is before court."

Meanwhile, Shyam Sunder Gupta, chief public relation officer (CPRO) of WR, said, "This company never started work nor did it deposit the cost of the tender (Rs 55 crore). So naturally their contract was terminated." Gupta also disagrees with the fact that tender form price and reserve money was exorbitant.

"As the tender was of Rs 52 crores, accordingly price of the form was fixed. Also, reserve price of a contract depends on many factors. Definitely, it would have been fixed after analysing the potential."

Heading: Crime Branch opposes plea filed by Chhota Rajan’s wife - Indian Express
Content:
A jeweller's residence at Juhu was looted, and diamond jewellery worth Rs 25,75,000 and foriegn currencies amounting to Rs 26 lakh were stolen, said the police. According to Juhu police, the jewellery was believed to have been stolen between October 4 and October 18 from Ashish Aggarwal's house. A case of theft has been registered on Monday against the servants, who are supected to have stolen the jewellery, said the police.

The main suspect of the case is one Ramchandra who has been working as a servant with the Aggarwals, said the police. The police also suspect the involvement of more servants in this case. We are interrogating everybody who work for the Aggarwals and everyone who visited their residence as well, the police said.

"All these servants have been working with the Aggarwals for a long time," said Senior Police Inspector D Katakade of the Juhu Police Station. "We haven't arrested anyone so far and are inquiring into who could have done this. I do not wish to comment much on this case as we are still investigating and it would not be right to talk about the case now," he said.

However, a police source said that Ramchandra and two more persons had been detained by the police. The Aggarwals were not available for comment.

Heading: HC issues notice to Anna Hazare - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai Police Crime Branch on Monday opposed the plea filed by Sujata Nikhalje, wife of fugitive gangster Chhota Rajan, seeking permission to travel to Singapore with her elder daughter Anita. According to Nikhalje, she is travelling to Singapore to secure an admission for her daughter in a university. The Crime Branch stated in its reply that she would flee the country, if permission was granted.

The Crime Branch also said that Sujata was involved in the organised crime syndicate run by Rajan and indulged in converting the funds gathered through extortion by pumping it into the redevelopment business managed by her in the name of Khushi Developers.

Sujata had moved a plea before the Special MCOCA court last week stating that she wants to accompany Anita who might get an admission in the Singapore Management University or City University of Hong Kong.

Heading: Jeepmen on track after U-turn - Indian Express
Content:
Bombay High Court on Monday issued a notice to social activist Anna Hazare in a petition challenging a stay granted on the recruitment of Battiwalas in the Pune Municipal Corporation.

Petitioner Vikas Ekbote, an aspirant to the post, contends that the stay granted on the recruitment by Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh on August 13, 2008 has been challenged. The job profile of a Battiwala includes supervision and maintenance of street lights within the boundary of the corporation.

The Pune Municipal Corporation had started the recruitment process on August 22. However, a complaint written on the letter head of Hakka Nivara Samiti, making a reference to Hazare and alleging rampant corruption in the selection process was sent to the state government and the Bombay High Court.
