Assistant government pleader Pradeep Patil said that the Pune Municipal Corporation, as directed by the CM, decided to stay the recruitment process. Appearing for the state government, Patil and assistant government pleader Vinay Masurkar on Monday asked the court to grant them time to file their reply.

The CM and Hazare have been made respondents in the petition. The case will come up for hearing on November 20.

Heading: CCI not yet certain to host Champions League - Indian Express
Content:
er dismal start to season, first win charges Mahindra United

Losing three games on the trot to kick off a football season will make any coach start having bouts of insomnia. And if it is a team that started out with the extra baggage of being one of the top contenders for the title, the nightmare would seem just more frightening and never-ending.

After winning the Durand Cup in the build-up, Mahindra United and team coach Derrick Pereira would have definitely had plans of making a confident start to the second edition of the ONGC I-league. But with defeats against Churchill Brothers and newly promoted outfits, Chirag United and Mumbai FC, the city giants found themselves languishing at the bottom of the table after three rounds in the first leg.

Mahindra's 1-0 win thanks to Sukhwinder Singh's goal against Punjab powerhouse JCT at Ludhiana on Saturday may not have been an A-class performance and could be termed scrappy. But Pereira was pleased with his team finally opening their account in the I-league for the 2008-09 season.

"We actually dominated the game from the start, and could have easily finished with a bigger margin if we would have converted our chances. I was also impressed with the way we held on to our one-goal lead," said Pereira from Kolkata, where his team is preparing for their next encounter against another newly promoted side, Mohammedan Sporting on Friday. He said that Mohammedan had a number of experienced players in their setup and would definitely not be an easy opponent to contend with. "Throughout the season we are going to take it one match at a time, and playing in Kolkata is never an easy task," revealed Pereira.

The Jeepmen had taken an early lead in their home encounter at Cooperage against Chirag United before going down 3-1 in disappointing fashion. Pereira insisted that his team hadn't performed to their potential but had also missed a number of chances in each of their three defeats. "The difference has been that our opposing teams have converted their chances while we haven't. Even Mumbai FC missed one and scored of the other, while our boys miffed close to five chances," said Pereira.

The Mahindra veteran had blasted his midfield after his team's early losses, but insisted that the likes of Steven Dias and Pierre Djidjia Douhou were slowly but surely getting their form going. "I was surprised with their performance especially after watching them during our Durand Cup win. But it was satisfying seeing them blend well together against JCT," said Pereira.

Another player whose performance has been under the scanner is Nigerian striker Edeh Chidi, who has struggled to find his finishing touch this season so far and is still to open his account. But Pereira insisted that Chidi was an experienced finisher and would soon turn the corner. "He is still creating an impact upfront in spite of not scoring any goals. We will definitely continue with him in the side, and I am confident that he will come good soon," he said, dispelling any fears of Chidi losing his spot in the team.

Pereira revealed that despite making a horrible start to the season, his players were not too ruffled and were simply waiting for things to fall into place. "We are an experienced outfit and we know that in football any team can win on a given day," he said. Pereira was of the opinion that his team was now raring to go, especially after posting their first points of the season against JCT.

Heading: Kenkre FC enter Super 7 - Indian Express
Content:
The Cricket Club of India has not yet been earmarked to host Champions T20 League ties in December at the Brabourne Stadium which is also the venue of the second and final Test between India and England in the same month.

"Nothing has been finalised yet. They are talking to us, that's all for now," CCI's chief executive officer Kanwaljeet Rajpal said.

The CCI's response followed speculation that the Brabourne Stadium would host matches during the December 3-10 Champions League prior to hosting the December 19-23 England-India Platinum Jubilee Test.

As per BCCI's regulations, a Test match venue cannot hold any other ties for at least a month ahead of the match to prepare the ground, outfield as well as the central square, properly.

Champions League Commissioner and BCCI vice president Lalit Modi has already announced that matches in the USD six million prize money T20 event would be held at Bangalore, Chennai and Mumbai.

He had earlier said that with the non-availability of the regular international venue Wankhede Stadium, which is undergoing renovation to prepare it to host matches in the 2011 World Cup including the final, Brabourne and D Y Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai were shortlisted to host the ties.

The Champions T20 League programme is to be announced on October 23 by the organisers. Incidentally, Test cricket is set to return to Brabourne after three and a half decades, the last one having been held in February, 1974, between India and England.

Heading: Saurashtra draw with Mumbai, bag three points - Indian Express
Content:
A young Kenkre FC became the first team to qualify for the Super 7 play-off in the MFL Elite Division, by defeating Western Railway 3-1 in their final match of Group at the RCF Sports Complex on Monday. In another crucial Group B match, Central Railway and ONGC played out a goalless draw. Both the teams with 12 points each have thus practically qualified for the Super 7 playoff, with only Mumbai United having a remote chance of pushing their claim.

Ravikant Naidu put Western Railway ahead in the 38th minute, but a header by Mathew Odje five minutes later restored parity for Kenkre FC. Dara Adhikarimpyom, who came in as a substitute, scored the all important goal in the 84th minute for Kenkre FC with a long ranger from the left flank that beat A Majeed in goal all ends up.

In the ONGC-Central Railway match, the players were conscious of the fact that a draw would be sufficient for both the teams to go through. However, they fought hard and played for pride. The railmen played well in short bursts, with Kasif Jamal and Aziz Qureshi creating a few openings. For ONGC, though Jatin Bisht was off-colour, the forward line played well enough in the last 20 minutes to create problems for the Railway custodian, Raghu Khanolkar.

The Budweiser man-of-the-match for Kenkre FC was Adhikarimpyom and for ONGC, goalkeeper Rajat Ghosh Dastidar.

Heading: Suraj rides Maximise to victory in Deccan Chronicle Gold - Indian Express
Content:
Saurashtra today secured three points in the Col CK Nayudu Trophy Under-22 cricket tournament although their match against Mumbai ended in a draw here.

Replying to Saurashtra's imposing total of 754 in the first innings, Mumbai picked up from an overnight score of 351 for five only to get wrapped up for 473 runs on the fourth and final day.

Saurashtra's Bhavik Gor bagged four wickets for 82, while Saurya Sanandiya took three wickets for 104. The hosts preferred not to enforce the follow on to Mumbai and decided to bat again. At the close of the match, Saurashtra were 63 for 3 in 29 overs.

Earlier in the day, Bhavik and Saurya put up a creditable show with J Odedara (two for 79) and Balkrishna Jadeja (one for 113) playing supportive roles as the visitors kept losing wickets at regular intervals.

For Mumbai, Aditya Tare (53) and Sachin Wagh (65) tried to arrest the downfall but the other batsmen, barring Rohan Raje (27), failed to deliver.

In the second innings, Saurashtra managed to pile up 63 for three in 29 overs before the match ended. Mumbai's S Raje, R Singh and I Abdulla bagged one wicket each.

Saurashtra will play their remaining two matches against Baroda and Gujarat next month.

Brief Scores: Saurashtra 1st Innings: 754 for 4 & 63 for 3 in 29 overs (Sheldon Jackson: 22, Rahul Dave: 22; S. Raje: 1/20, R. Singh: 1/3 and I. Abdulla: 1/5) drew with Mumbai 473 (Aditya Tare: 53, Sachin Wagh: 65, Rohan Raje: 27, B.S. Sandhu: 24; Bhavik Gor: 4/82, Saurya Sanandiya: 3/104, J. Odedara: 2/79, Balkrishna Jadeja: 1/113).

Heading: Let there be hops - Indian Express
Content:
We uncork the best bubbly blends in town to celebrate the return of sunshine

Olive Bar & Kitchen Bandra
Ask head bartender Vincent to make you the Italian Beauty, Campari, with sparkling wine which starts off as bitter but ends with a tinge of sweetness. Mixing sparkling wine with Campari, known to evoke as strange a facial expression as that during the consumption of a chunk of wasabi, was pretty unusual and frankly innovative. On the downside, the Melon Spark (melon liqueur) is a tad too sweet and there is something wrong about the Passionate Spark (vodka and passion fruit).
Rating Good
Call 2605 8228

Dome Hotel Intercontinental, Marine Drive
A GREAT ambience injects enough fizz into sparkling cocktails. It certainly does not get much better than the fabulous view of sunset one gets at Dome. Or better, the cozy couches by the poolside at night. Although their menu has only one sparkling cocktail —Kir Royale (and an excellent one at that)—F&B head Karan Khiani encourages customers to ask for any cocktail off the menu, even if it means resorting to the ever-reliable Google. A winner that he recommends is the perfectly balanced Paan Bellini, made using a Paan Elaichi liqueur with cloves as garnish. The Limoncello Fizz (limoncello liqueur, lime juice, whole red grape) is inspiring, and certainly what any young lemonade should aspire to be.

Rating Excellent
Call 5639 9699

Indigo Golaba
INDIGO is a place where guests sparkle as much as the superlative sparkling cocktails. They have the best list in town. It isn't particularly innovative, but it has enough diversity and consistency to make up for that. My favourite is the Melon Cooler (melon liqueur), which has the perfect balance of flavour, sweetness and crispness. The Arise My Love (crème de menthe) is theoretically fantastic but some may find the mint a bit overwhelming. They have the best Bellini in town. A traditional long drink from Italy, it's an elegant blend of Prosecco and peach purée. Chic.

Rating Excellent
Call 6636 8999

Shiro Lower Parel
SHIRO, with its gorgeous décor

and awesome high ceilings, does good cocktails in general. All their sparkling cocktails are fortified with around 10 ml of vodka, an appropriate amount to make these cocktails have just the right sting. The blackcurrant and litchi cocktail are lovely, although not as light as desired. Their Mango and Ginger sparkling cocktail sounded nice but my liver begged for mercy by then. I also happen to know for a fact that if you ask nicely, head bartender Ashish or Sanjeev would be willing to make something off the menu like their fantastic passion fruit sparkling cocktail. However, I guess vodka-based cocktails are better here.

Rating Average

de

Heading: LAST BITE  with Sandhya Mridul - Indian Express
Content:
Two gents are determined to increase the reach of the world's favourite golden beverage

India is currently at the bottom of the pyramid of beer drinking countries, with the Czech Republic and Ireland topping the list. "Don't be fooled by these figures. A lot of alcohol is had in India, sadly it's not beer," says

Johan De Deyn, technical manager of Asia Pacific Breweries. "This leaves a huge potential for growth in the Indian market, which is slowly opening up to different kinds of beers, whether it's dark malt beer or fruity lager," he adds.

Based in Hyderabad, Deyn is in India to promote beer, its consumption and production in a market that currently forms only 0.8 per cent of the world's beer drinkers. Chief Executive Officer of South Asian Breweries, Ashwin Deo is behind Deyn's visit, since moving from promoting a sparkling wine like Moet to a product like beer has been, in Deo's words, "A shift from cheese to chalk. Moët, and for that matter most of the wines, are high-end products. Its niche and usually appeals to an older generation. The way I see beer is that it appeals to a generation that's young at heart." Deo adds that he would prefer wine for a formal occasion and beer for a night-out with the boys.

Deyn is giving us a crash-course on beer, its history and how it's made. It's a lazy afternoon of Tiger beer at Olive in Mahalaxmi, and Deyn busts a few myths about the golden brew. "Most people assume that light beers are not strong. Dark beers are seen more as the 'real thing'. However, one can brew a light beer and make it strong, just by increasing its alcohol content," says the expert who has been in the business for over 20 years.

While Indian soil is not ideal for growing barley— one of the key and most expensive ingredients of beer—Deyn and other serious players in the industry are hoping to introduce strains of barely that are more suitable for brewing to the farmers in Punjab

and Haryana, where most of the crop is grown. "We will, however, make the offer viable for the locals — it has to be economically viable," says the guru of hops, malt and yeast.

"Currently most of our malt and hops are imported," he adds, the idea is to get India at par with China which is currently producing and exporting a lot of beer. "India can because it has the resources and the labour?it's just a matter of time." Well

Deyn's words might ring true, but till then, it's time to clink pints.

Heading: Loose to Win - Indian Express
Content:
CPM state secretary and Left Front chairman Biman Bose said on Wednesday "unholy" powers are trying to destabilise West Bengal.

Referring to Trinamool Congress agitation in Cooch Behar, Maoist blast in West Midnapore and Gorkha Janamukti Morcha (GJM) agitation in Darjeeling, Bose asked people to fight unitedly against such powers.

"Unholy opposition forces are creating a dangerous situation in the state. Trinamool Congress in Cooch Behar, Maoists in West Midnapore and GJM in Darjeeling — all of them are trying to create anarchy in the state. There are attacks, intimidations and murders. The democratic environment in the state is being destroyed by their acts," Bose said.

"We have asked supporters of Left Front in Darjeeling to maintain calm and peace," he added.

Referring to Maoist blasts in West Midnapore, he said: "The Naxals are attacking doctors and nurses in medical camp meant for the poor. People should understand their motives."

Heading: Bollywood makes Indians look dumb - Indian Express
Content:
Look chic with bright colours, ruffled dresses & big sleeves this summer

Celeb of the day
The surprise entry on Day Two was Kabir Bedi, who looked as hot as a firecracker. He was accompanied by girlfriend Parveen Dusanj and daughter Pooja Bedi.

Chatting up with each other and posing for the shutterbugs, they looked like one big happy family.

Dadu showcased an amazing mix of woven dresses, draped racer back dresses and ruffles with quilting, pleating and tonal embroidery on smocks in pink, yellow and white — the colours seemed just right for the summer.

VOLUMINOUS sleeves ruled the roost on the second day. Crab and Dolman sleeves were present in Kallol Dutta's unstructured line.
Leg-of-mutton, batwing, bell and longish puff sleeves made a jarring presence in Drashta Sarvaiya, Arjun and Aastha Bahl line. High on style, these sleeves are well on their way to the top of the fashion poll.

Goss of the day
THOSE who say that they love fashion more than their lives are evidently lying. Most of them chose to stay indoors, watching Raj Thakeray on their television sets instead. As far as attendance goes, Day Two wore a desultory look.

Heading: Hermes is here - Indian Express
Content:
When Canadian comedian Russell Peters toured India last year he was very amused at how many men hold hands here. Come October 27 and Peters will once again be back on stage, at Shanmukhananda Hall, with his observational comedy about communities and culture around the world. "This time I'm hoping to be funny again," says Peters and immediately adds, "Being funny is a tough thing."

This is Peters' 20th anniversary tour, and his performance will feature his 'greatest hits' along with some new material since his visit last year.

Peters who writes his own acts is very popular for his in-your-face mockery of racial stereotypes and his cracks on the cultural divide between different ethnicities. "Ninety-five per cent my act is based on real-life experiences of meeting people. But it is the exaggeration of those experiences that make the act interesting," admits Peters, who says he lets spontaneity get the best out of him. "I don't think about the script once I get on stage. I just go with the flow," he says, whose humour even parodies his parents with the signature "Somebody gotta get hurt real bad".

Peters, who at present lives in Los Angeles, was born in Toronto and is of Indian descent with his father born in Mumbai and his mother in Kolkata. Speaking of which he says, "All of my mother's family, going back to my great-grandmother were born in Kolkata. Even my brother, Clayton, who's also my manager, was born in Kolkata. I have uncles, aunts and several cousins who still live in there."

Although he has travelled the globe belting out witty performances in countries including Australia, China, UAE and Vietnam among others, the one continent he has missed is South America and explains why. "They don't speak English so that's out of question," laughs Peters, who still refuses any Hollywood movie offer that asks him to play a dumb, nerdy NRI Indian. "I think Bollywood makes Indians look dumb enough so I certainly refuse to let anyone else make us look dumber," says Peters with a grin. While his latest release is a self-produced DVD titled Red, White and Brown, the compilation may not find a release in India but he plans to carry some for the fans.

Heading: Ahmedabad lab nodal centre for India’s maiden moon mission - Indian Express
Content:
The French luxury giant opens in India despite a western financial recession

Hermes, that French luxury label that we all hate to speak of about for fear of a mispronunciation (and yet dream of owning), is here. But going by the number of socialites flaunting their Rs 4 lakh-plus priced Birkin handbags, they've always been here.

Mumbai is not their agenda presently, as the fashion company opens its first Indian boutique in the plush arcade of the Oberoi Hotel, New Delhi, with Gucci, Louis Vuitton and Christian Dior, as neighbours. The next stores are likely to be opened in Bangalore and Kolkata.

Patrick Thomas, their charming CEO with an Irish name, came down to launch the Delhi boutique, gently assuring us that he is "very French". But like most of the world, Hermes especially, is having a huge India moment. Its chief designer Jean Paul Gaultier brought out a line last season (Spring-Summer) inspired by India's royalty and vivid colours, and even used the sultry Lakshmi Menon as their model in all their international campaigns.

"The objective is to become Indian in India. We are here to sell objects, not fashion," shares Thomas, 61, explaining why, despite two ongoing fashion weeks and a global recession there is no clash of interest with the timing of their launch.

The store is beautifully packaged with a representative presence of all that the brand is renowned for. There are items from JPG's Indo-phile Spring-Summer collection as well as pieces from their newer Autumn-Winter collection. Luxurious cashmere shawls, priced at Rs 72,000, rub shoulders with their famed Birkins, elegant Kelly bags (Rs 3 lakh), fine china, watches and perfumes and accessories like ties (Rs 8,800) and their collector-item silk scarves (approximately Rs 17,500). "Every scarf has its own story to tell and we have about 18 to 20 designers and four Indian designers who bring in a dash of Indian sensibility," smiles Thomas.

The global financial meltdown has become a cause of worry in the luxury industry, but Christian Blanckaert, Executive VP, International Affairs for the brand, assures that it will not affect their market in India.

Orders, however, have already started coming in, with a waitlist for the elusive Birkin already in place. Ten percent of the brand's sales worldwide come from specially commissioned items.

Heading: All 14 accused in minor tribal’s rape sentenced to life - Indian Express
Content:
As you read this, Chandrayaan-1 is getting ready for its journey to the moon, Earth's only natural satellite .

S Satish, Director (Public Relations), Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), said: "As of now, the spacecraft will be launched at 6.20 am on October 22. Today, at 5 am we started filling the second and fourth stage of the launch vehicle, PSLV-C11, which will use the liquid propulsion system weighing about 44 tonnes."

The filling process will take about 35 hours and is expected to finish by 4 pm tomorrow, said Satish.

Earlier in the day, Prof J N Goswami, director of the Physical Research Laboratory (PRL), Ahmedabad, who is also the principal scientist for the Chandrayaan-1 mission, spoke about the possibility of finding helium-3 on the lunar surface. "Although generating power through nuclear fusion of helium-3 is a distant dream, but the possibilities are immense," he said. The samples brought to Earth by the Apollo mission have indicated that Iron titanium oxide traps helium-3 molecules on the lunar surface, he said.

Goswami said he-3 content is very low. For every 100,000 helium-4 molecules, there is only one helium-3 molecule on the lunar surface. Besides, the scientific community is yet to simulate the conditions necessary for nuclear fusion. But, if Chandrayaan-1 is able to locate probable areas for finding helium-3, that in itself will be a very big achievement. It will help eliminate the two stages of producing deuterium from hydrogen and then producing helium-3 from deuterium, he added.

Goswami also elaborated PRL's contribution to India's first lunar mission. Along with realising the payload for the High Energy X-ray Spectrometer (HEX) designed and developed jointly by PRL and ISRO's Satellite Centre at Bangalore, PRL is also the nodal centre for ISRO's Planetary Science and Exploration (PLANEX) programme. PLANEX aims for technological advancement in planetary research and is formulating ISRO's future planetary exploration programmes by evaluating proposals for possible Chandrayaan-2 payloads.

Emphasising the aims and objectives of HEX, Goswami said: "The most futuristic dream of science is to set up a human-cum-robotic base on the lunar surface and HEX will pave the way for it." He said the polar region on the moon is the most plausible site for this because of the simultaneous presence of mountains receiving perennial solar energy, and permanently shadowed areas with temperature much below zero degree, which act like deep freezers for water-ice. So, HEX, along with NASA's Mini-SAR, will try to identify the polar regions covered with thick water-ice deposits, he said.

Another major contribution by PRL has been formulating and coordinating the activities of the Chandrayaan-1 Science Team, he said. The team comprising 11 science groups with representatives of all the payloads has formulated science and data analysis plans for the mission.

Heading: Inquiry against cops after women display banners at Modi programme - Indian Express
Content:
Public Prosecutor had contended that the accused had raped the girl after tying up her boyfriend

Bharuch Additional Sessions Judge N K Purani on Monday sentenced all 14 accused in the gang rape of a 15-year-old tribal girl at Divan Dhanjishah High School ground in Jhagadiya taluka of Bharuch district to life. The court has also levied a fine of Rs 10,000 each on the accused.

The accused have been identified as Brijesh alias Bhalo Keval, Mukesh alias Chilli Vasava, Prakash alias Abdul Vasava, Nitin alias Puni Vasava, Sanjay alias Praveen Vasava, Prakash alias Pako Vasava, Jayantibhai Bhikhabhai, Gangaram Vasava, Jitu Vasava, Pankaj alias Bobby Vasava, Ajay alias Ashwin Vasava, Yogesh alias Goli Vasava, Sailesh Vasava and Harish Patel.

The Bharuch district Fast Track Court passed the judgement eight months after the incident took place on February 2 this year. The victim was a student of Class X at the time of the incident.

Public prosecutor P N Parmar had contended that the accused had raped the girl by tying her boyfriend with rope that evening.

According to the victim's testimony the accused were riding three to four motorcycles.

The victim's father, a government servant, told Newsline: "My daughter is the eldest among my four children. I am satisfied with the court's verdict. The verdict will prevent such gruesome incidents in future. It has been a long drawn process, but justice, though delayed, has not been denied."

The matter was under the investigation of Inspector D D Damor and Deputy Superintendent of Police (DySP) N P Raizada.

According to the police, similar incidents of rape had occurred at the Divan Danjishah School earlier also.

Parmar said: "Several such rape cases have occurred in the tribal dominated Jhagadiya area. Of the 14 accused, 13 are from the Vasava community and are reported to be involved in several other cases where minors were raped. However, none came up to file an FIR. The recent Bharuch Fast track court verdict will at least create some deterrent before a person indulges in such an offence in this area."

Heading: Clash between Godmother’s kin disrupts court proceedings - Indian Express
Content:
Police Commissioner initiates inquiry against inspector, others for laxity in security

Surat Police Commissioner RMS Brar has initiated an inquiry against Udhna Inspector A K Qureshi and 12 others including the women police personnel after several women displayed banners at Chief Minister Narendra Modi's programme in Khatodara.

Modi was present at the inauguration of a new building of the Surat Raktdan Kendra at Khatodara, when a few women, who were sitting in the public, took out banner displaying "14 varsh Ni Chokri Ne Apharan Kartao thi Mukti Apavo (Rescue the 14 year-old-girl from the kidnappers)."

Fourteen people, including 13 women, were arrested under Section 188 of the Indian Penal Code. Brar later initiated an inquiry against the inspector in-charge and the women police staff over laxity in security measures.

According to sources, a 14-year-old girl from Bhestan was kidnapped by some unknown persons from near her house on October 11. The girl's father Balinarayan Mishra, an auto driver, had lodged a complaint with the Udhna police station in this regard, but to no avail. On October 15, the girl's parents also handed over a complaint to Brar. Later they decided to display banners during Modi's visit to Khatodara to draw his attention, but ended up being booked under violation of Prohibitory Orders.

Brar said: "We have initiated an inquiry against the police staff including Udhna Inspector A K Qureshi and others, who were on duty at the site to ascertain how women were allowed to enter the site with banners and why they were not properly checked by the women police personnel. Assistant Commissioner of Police F Division S G Gohil has taken the statements and he is preparing a report. Later we will take necessary steps."

Heading: Several in the fray for polls to elect milk federation chief - Indian Express
Content:
A sudden brawl between two family members of Santokben Jadeja, popularly known as Godmother, resulted in a commotion in the Porbandar district court premises on Monday morning.

The incident took place outside a designated TADA courtroom in the district court premises around 11 am on Monday. Santokben's brother-in-law, Ex-MLA and gang leader Bhura Munja (58) and her nephew, Ebha Arjan Munja (35) had gone to the court in connection with a TADA case. Bhura and Ebha were among a total of 40 persons the TADA court had summoned for deposition on Monday.

An altercation ensued between Bhura and Ebha reportedly because the former did not like Ebha staring at him. "Bhura slapped Ebha on his face and Ebha started beating Bhura in retaliation. The brawl between the two notorious gang leaders of Porbandar caused sudden commotion on the court premises. The court proceedings were also disrupted," said Kamlabuag Inspector M C Patel.

Apprehending problems because of the two rival gang leaders being summoned by the court around the same time on Monday, the Porbandar district authorities had already deployed extra police personnel on the court premises since Monday morning in order to avoid any untoward incident. The policemen on duty immediately sprung into action and the situation was put under control.

Bhura and Ebha also lodged cross-complaints against each other at the Kamlabuag police station in Porbanbar. The two were later taken to the TADA court that had summoned them.

The uncle-nephew duo has been booked by the Kamlabuag police on charges of voluntarily causing hurt, intentional breach of peace and criminal intimidation.

Superintendent of Porbandar police Dipankar Trivedi said Bhura and Ebha will be arrested by Monday evening, after their depositions before the TADA court gets over.

Heading: Junior doctors call off strike against assault on colleague - Indian Express
Content:
With the tenure of Parthibhai Bhatol as chairman of the Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation (GCMMF) coming to an end on October 17, the race has begun for the coveted post of the country's biggest milk food product marketing company in the cooperative sector.

Several names have started doing the rounds in the state dairy sector as the announcement for elections was made.

The strong contenders include: Vipul Chaudhary, chairman of Dhoodhsagar dairy and BJP MLA Madhu Srivastava, Chairman, Baroda Dairy.

Interestingly, Bhatol, who had replaced Dr Verghese Kurien, GCMMF founder and the father the White Revolution in an election preceded by high drama in April 2006, told Newsline that "he will not mind contesting the elections again."

Bhatol said: "I will consult my colleagues and friends at GCMMF and the 13 district cooperative milk unions for recontesting and will certainly contest if I get the green signal."

A former Congressman, Bhatol is now with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). Apart from the support of his party leaders, Bhatol will bank on his track record. During his tenure, the company's annual turnover increased from Rs 3,750 crore in 2005 to Rs 5,255 crore the last financial year, which is further expected to touch the Rs 6,500 crore mark this year.

Waghodia BJP legislator Madhu Srivastava, who got elected as chairman of the Baroda District Cooperative Milk Producers Union nearly a year ago, admitted he was not averse to contesting for the post.

Srivastava added, "I will contest only if I am assured of support by the party."

The most serious challenge to Bhatol, however, is expected to come from Vipul Chaudhary who has a long experience in the dairy sector.

A former minister in the Shankersinh Vaghela government and now with the BJP, Chaudhary commands significant influence in the cooperative dairy sector by virtue of heading the Doodhsagar Dairy, the biggest cooperative dairy in the state having the largest number of voters on the electoral rolls of GCMMF. Nearly one-fifth of the GCMMF electorates are reported to be from the Doodhsagar dairy.

"I would like to contest for the post. But before filing my nominations, I will consult the BJP parliamentarian from Godhra and Panchmahal Dairy chairman Bhupendrasinh Solanki and also Srivastava," said Chaudhary.

The Anand district administration, within whose jurisdiction the GCMMF headquarters are located, has begun the process for conducting the election. Anand District Collector R N Joshi said he had already appointed Sub-Divisional Magistrate R G Chaudhary as the Election Officer and has asked him to complete the polls at the earliest.

Chaudhary is likely to announce the nomination and election dates within a week. According to Chaudhary, Bhatol will continue on the post till a new chairman is elected.

Heading: Too few teachers for too many disabled children - Indian Express
Content:
The strike called by nearly 150 junior doctors of the Junior Doctors' Association (JDA), New Civil hospital (NCH), on Sunday, was called off on Monday evening as the hospital authorities assured the agitating doctors of meeting their demands. The strike was called after a junior doctor was allegedly beaten by a patient's relative on Sunday evening.

Dr Chintan Patel was allegedly "slapped" by one Rashid Mirza, elder brother of patient Ayub Mirza, at the E-1 ward of New Civil hospital (NCH), on Sunday evening.

According to hospital sources, Ayub (28) was admitted to the hospital on Wednesday afternoon with severe burn injuries. On Sunday afternoon, Dr Chintan called Ayub for a dressing to be done. With the patient reporting late, the doctor apparently rebuked him, following which he succumbed to his injuries.

When Rashid arrived at the hospital and learnt from his relatives that Dr Chintan Patel had allegedly "kicked" the patient, he went to Dr Chintan and apparently "slapped" him before the patients and other hospital staff. The security guards and other doctors arrived at the scene and controlled the situation.

The members of the Junior Doctors' Association (JDA), irked by the incident, declared a strike from Sunday evening. Dr Chintan later lodged a complaint against Rashid with the Umra police station.

New Civil hospital Superintendent M K Wadhel office met the agitating doctors today and assured them that security would be stepped up on the hospital premises. Following which, the doctors called off their strike.

JDA vice-president Dr Devendra Choudhary said, "We had earlier demanded the higher authorities to increase the security of doctors as a similar incident had taken place earlier. We also apprised him of the other problems like lack of drinking water, no reading room and high rates charged by the canteen."

Dr Choudhary added, "We called off the strike as our tutors and professors had already booked their tickets for Diwali vacations and if we continued with the strike, they would have to attend the patients."

Hospital superintendent Dr M K Wadhel said, "The relatives of the patient had alleged that Dr Chintan kicked the patient. After the incident, we have increased the security and there are 15 security persons deployed in the hospital area."

He added: "We had called extra staffers from all the community healthcare centres and they are on duty in the hospital. Work was not stopped as the tutors and professors were also asked to treat patients."

Heading: Scholarships for rural students haven’t increased in last 27 years - Indian Express
Content:
While the number of disabled students in Gujarat is 50,000, the total number of trained teachers is only around 12,000

While the number of disabled students in Gujarat, including those suffering from visual/hearing impairment, mental retardation and ortho-handicap and those who come under the Integrated Education for Disabled Children (IEDC) scheme, is almost 50,000, the number of trained teachers for each category is a mere 1200.

This is a clear indication of the appalling teacher-student ratio in the state.

Under the existing situation, 38,000 students are left unattended as per the prescribed 'one teacher per 10 students' rule. Under the IEDC scheme, children with mild to moderate disabilities are integrated in normal schools.

The state has a total of 65,558 disabled students enrolled in primary schools alone.

Out of the 50,000 disabled children, 35,000 students from 26 districts (220 talukas) covered under the scheme are from rural areas.

Accommodating disabled children from rural areas, however, remains a difficult task.

With 20-25 disabled children in each taluka and lack of adequate facilities, a teacher can attend to only one child every week.

With children suffering from cerebral palsy not being considered as part of the Mentally Challenged (MR) category in the IEDC scheme, there are no teachers for this category of students.

IEDC Director, K D Parikh said: "The number of disabled children, particularly in the mentally challenged category has been gradually increasing in remote areas of Dahod, Pachmahals, Valsad, Dangs, Kutch and Bhuj. We have around 30 special schools to take care of these children, but the total number of trained teachers is only around 12,000."

He added: "The major problem, however, remains the attitude towards the disabled and illiteracy of parents, who hesitate to send their kids to special schools. In certain areas, parents are so poor that they cannot afford to bear the educational needs of the disabled students.

Heading: Fuel station owners begin agitation against IOC, Essar Oil - Indian Express
Content:
The National Scholarships for Talented Children from Rural Areas for Secondary Stage Study were started in1971-72 (including +2 stage) with an objective to provide quality secondary stage education to school children from rural areas. Though the scholarships have been operational in Gujarat since then, the amount a student receives under this scheme is just Rs 30 to Rs100 per month, even after 27 years.

A senior official from the state Education Department said on condition of anonymity: "The aim of these scholarships is to help brilliant students from rural areas, who are not able study further because of financial problems. But how can we expect a student to sustain himself/herself with a mere Rs30-100 per month. This scheme is no more than a joke."

He added: "Several government officials have tried to revise this scheme, but nothing concrete has been done due to the lazy work culture."

When contacted, the state Education Department confirmed that this scheme has not been revised since its inception. "There are no doubts that the expenses of secondary and higher secondary studies are going up day by day and the scheme is not providing any help to students from rural areas," S M Gamik, Under Secretary (Secondary), Education Department, Gujarat.

He added: "If we really want to support talented children from rural areas for secondary stage study, then we should revise this scholarship as soon as possible, otherwise no student will be interested in applying for this scheme in future. The minimum amount in the revised scheme should at least be Rs 1000 per month."

Heading: State govt to provide free cycles to salt pan workers - Indian Express
Content:
More than 300 fuel station dealers in Rajkot, Porbandar, Junagadh and Jamnagar districts began their indefinite strike on Monday. The fuel station dealers did not lift fuel from various centres to protest against Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) and Essar Oil Limited.

Shivlala Bhanderi, president of the Rajkot Petrol & Diesel Dealers Association, said: "We have received a good response from the fuel station owners, as they did not lift fuel on Monday. Fuel was not lifted in the four districts either from the IOC, Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum dumps." He added: "Most of the fuel stations in these districts have stocks to last for a day or two, after which the end users will face crisis."'

Mansukh Barai, leader of the Fuel Station Dealers from Okha said: "Till evening, 'No Fuel' boards will be put up in most of the fuel stations. We are maintaining our unanimous decision of not lifting fuel as part of our agitation against Essar Oil."

In few parts of Jamnagar, however, district fuel station owners have not joined this ongoing strike, as majority of these stations are company-owned.

A state level body, the Gujarat Federation of Petrol and Diesel Dealers Association, is taking active part in resolving this issue at the earliest.

A meeting between IOC's Executive Director and the dealer leaders from Rajkot and Junagadh has been called on Tuesday at Ahmedabad.

"Our meeting has been fixed for Tuesday with the ED of IOC in Ahmedabad. We hope to do some positive negotiation. Otherwise we will intensify our strike and fuel station owners of the entire state will join in this agitation," said Bhanderi.

Heading: BRT service: Hectic activity on for completion of first phase - Indian Express
Content:
The government has decided to provide bicycles free of cost to the each of the 20,000 families engaged in salt pan work in the coastal districts of Gujarat.

A proposal mooted by the State Industries Department for this has been accepted by the Finance Department.

Sources in the Industries Department said on

Monday that the decision to give bicycles to each of the 'agariya' (salt pan workers) families was to save them from the drudgery of walking long distances from their villages to workplaces. The cost of this project is about Rs 4 crore.

"The government will soon initiate the process of purchasing bicycles for the 'agariya' families who live mainly in places like Surendranagar, Kutch, Rajkot, Jamnagar, Bhavnagar, Banaskantha and Valsad," a senior official said.

Heading: Brick prices shoot up as workers go on strike - Indian Express
Content:
If not by Christmas, then the first phase of the BRT service connecting Vasna with Naranpura will be operational by Uttarayan, it has been learnt. Hectic activity is now on at various levels, if work from Nehrunagar to Shivranjani cross and further toward IIM and Memnagar is anything to go by.

Bosses at the Ahmedabad Janmarg Ltd (AJL), the special purpose vehicle for the project, are running against time because the launch has to take place before the announcement of the Lok Sabha elections.

In fact, after a disappointing delay in completion of the Sabarmati Riverfront Development project, political bosses ruling the roost in Gandhinagar will depend heavily on two mascots of progress: the Nano and BRTS.

Incidentally, AJL has already finalised the bus design, though the colour is yet to be given a final go-through. But officials are not in a hurry on this front, and have said that other loose ends will have to be tied up prior to that.

Project in-charge D Thara said: "All the bus stops on the routes will have to be completed and drivers will have to be imparted special training to operate them to ensure that the time schedule is maintained and that they get a clear understanding of instructions from the Central communication unit."

She said the tenders will be finalised by mid-November for the development of this communication unit. Then a ticketing system will also have to be finalised along with the launch of the bus service. She said the sample bus will be procured next month.

Municipal commissioner I P Gautam said the launch will be "very soon." He, however, refrained from giving a fixed date for that.

The AMC administration has once already faced an embarrassing situation by announcing the launch date of the Kankaria Lake Front Development project, which went wide off the mark.

Gautam said the "operational nuances" of the project will have to be taken care of before the announcement of the launch date.

Apart from completing the bus stops, the training of bus drivers and the construction of bus stops and bridges will also have to be completed, he said.

According to him, the split flyover bridge at Memnagar across Drive-In Road will be completed by the end of December whereas the one near the AEC junction in Naranpura will be finished by January.

The first few days of the launch will be for trial runs, he said.

Heading: Cash, valuables worth Rs 6.57 lakh stolen in three separate incidents - Indian Express
Content:
State govt has made it mandatory for all brick kiln units to get clearance from the pollution control board

The brick manufacturing industry had up till now been among the unorganised sectors. But, the state government, with its mandatory pollution control board clearance policy, has firmly united the sector, so much so that about six lakh workers in the 1,200-odd kilns in the state have proceeded on an indefinite strike after Dusshera.

Result: Spiralling prices of bricks even as over 6 lakh workers have been rendered jobless.

As per the new state policy, kilns with mobile chimneys will not qualify for registration from the Gujarat Pollution Control Board. According to this, over 40 per cent of the existing units — small and medium — do not qualify for the registration. Till now, only two per cent of the units have applied for registration, while the rest are protesting.

Concerned over the fact that about six lakh workers have been rendered jobless, the Mazdoor Mahajan Sangh has requested the unit owners to start production.

State Industry Minister Saurabh Patel was not available for comments. The Gujarat Brick Manufacturing Association (GBMA) on Monday submitted a memorandum to Patel. "A small unit produces 20 to 30 lakh bricks per season, while a medium unit manufactures 40 to 60 lakh bricks per season. These function on moving chimneys. But, these do not qualify for registration under the new policy of the Gujarat Pollution Control Board," said GBMA president Devendra Prajapati.

The pollution control board certificate is now a mandatory document required along with VAT, Sales Tax, Balance Sheet and Annual Audit Report papers to get registration cleared from the Gujarat Mineral Development Cooperation, which grants access to lignite quota.

The non-registered units are now not likely to restart working soon with the state government, which is also imposing a ban on the free sale of lignite to stop the black-marketing of minerals.

"The association has made it clear to the state government that the kilns will not begin work for the season until their demands are met," Prajapati said.

SIDELIGHTS

The standoff between the brick kiln manufacturers and the state government began in April 2008 when the latter discontinued lignite supply from the Panandhro site in Kutch district to all the industries with an objective to keep this mineral site reserved for power generation. With this, a quota of eight trucks, each weighing 10.5 tonnes per fortnight per kiln, was given by the Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation to the brick manufactures. But all the kilns in Gujarat were also asked to re-register themselves to avail quota from other sites, including Mata Nau Madh Rajpardi and Tadkeshwar. Panandhro has been the sole lignite resource for industries for the past 20 years. Before that, manufactures used smoke coal procured from Bihar and Nagpur.

In a season that lasts six months, collective production of kilns across Gujarat accounts for 2,000 crore bricks. With inflation at its pick, the prices of bricks are likely to go up further, following a short supply. A brick that used to cost Re 1 per piece before the monsoon, now costs Rs 3.5 per piece. "The prices are likely to go up further as there has hardly been any production," said GBMA secretary Vasant Prajapati.

Heading: Traffic cops given training in first-aid treatment - Indian Express
Content:
Cash and valuables worth Rs 6.57 lakh were stolen from houses in three separate cases under the Ellisbridge police station on Sunday.

While two of the victims are city-based doctors, a labour court judge filed the third complaint, the police said.

Unidentified persons broke into the house of city-based doctor Anant Kanuga at bungalow number 8 in Preetam Nagar Society between 5.30 pm and 9 pm.

The thieves broke into the house when the family had gone out to attend a private function.

They decamped with cash and jewellery kept inside the safety vault of a cupboard in one of the bedrooms on the first floor, the police said.

Dr. Kanuga, who owns the Shahtanu Nursing Home in Ellisbridge, returned home with his family around 9.30 pm and found the place robbed. He informed the Ellisbridge police station. The police said prima facie it appears to be the handiwork of an insider. A complaint has been registered and forensic experts have also been roped in to help trace the miscreants.

Another city-based doctor Parul Desai filed a similar complaint, accusing some unidentified persons of breaking into her clinic at Bhramshatriya society in Paladi and decamping with a ceiling fan and television set estimated to cost about Rs 2,500.

In the third complaint, Harshal Acharya, a judge in the labour court has accused unidentified persons of breaking the lock of his main door, entering the house and decamping with Rs 3,000 cash.

His house is situated in Nivada Apartments near Jethabhai Park in Paladi.

Heading: 3 die in separate road accidents - Indian Express
Content:
A special programme was organised jointly by the Ahmedabad Traffic Police and the HCG Medi-Surge Hospital on Monday to train the city's traffic police personnel in providing first-aid care to accident victims. More than 40 traffic police personnel attended the programme, where they were also given first-aid kits.

The aim of the programme was to the train traffic police, who are the first ones to reach an accident site, in providing on-the-spot care to trauma victims.

The personnel were explained the use of different medicines and dressing material in the kits.

An eminent Orthopaedic surgeon, Dr Dipak Dave explained to them the importance of timely first-aid treatment and also how to prioritise the seriousness of the injuries.

Heading: DCB arrests Majid Patel in Akshardham attack case - Indian Express
Content:
Rash driving claimed the lives of three people in three separate accidents on Sunday. While two accidents took place on the outskirts of Makarpura police station area, in which trucks crushed a woman and a daily wage labourer, the third accident claimed the life of an 11-month-old infant at Alkapuri.

The first accident took place on National Highway No. 8 in Kapurai Bridge. Sooni Bangali was on way to Ankleshwar in an auto-rickshaw along with her two children when she suddenly from the vehicle. A truck coming from behind hit her, killing her on the spot.

"The truck driver could not apply brakes on time and ran over the woman killing her at the spot. It then hit the auto-rickshaw injuring her three children — seven-year-old Akash, five-year-old Rohit and two-year-old Prem — along with Sunil Bhalla, another passenger who was travelling with them," said Makarpura police sub-inspector S K Vasava.

Truck driver Ramesh Goswami, a resident of Nawali village in Anand district was arrested on Sunday evening and later released, as the police believed that the accident did not occur because of his fault.

In another incident that took place on the same day, a dumper truck (GJ-6 VV 5414) was reversing at a high speed around 10:30 pm, when it ran over Mathura Bhai (35), who was resting on a pavement in front of Mirza Complex in Manjalpur. He was crushed to death, Vasava said.

"The driver absconded along with the cleaner, while an eyewitness, Narod Bhagoda from Limkheda in Dahod, registered the complaint," said Vasava. Police have, meanwhile, seized the killer truck.

In a third incident, Kisha, an 11-month-old infant, daughter of Narvat Damor, a daily wage labourer from Limkheda in Dahod district, was crushed to death by a car. The accident took place when the car was reversing in Sterling Apartments in Alkapuri, where Damor was working. Sayajigunj police, who are investigating into the incident, said it could not be ascertained who committed the crime, as the car fled before anybody could notice.

Heading: ‘Temple attack financer collected money by showing CDs of 2002 riots’ - Indian Express
Content:
A day after being nabbed by the Bharuch district police, the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) on Monday arrested Majid Patel in connection with the Akshardham Temple attack.

Majid is the seventh person to be arrested in the case till date.

The Joint Commissioner of Police, DCB, Ashish Bhatia said: "Majid has been arrested and brought to Ahmedabad. He will be produced before a designated POTA court soon."

Majid is believed to have played a crucial role in arranging the money through the Hawala channel for carrying out the terrorist attack.

Majid, who fled to Dubai after the Akshardham case, is expected to provide the police with some crucial leads about the sources of money being pumped into India through the Hawala channel, given that more than 20 accused in the case are still at large.

Thirty-four people, including two National Security Guards commandos and two state commandos died when two Pakistan-based terrorists stormed the Akshardham temple at Gandhinagar on September 24, 2002 and opened indiscriminate fire and lobbed grenades.

In July 2006, a designated POTA court convicted three of the six accused arrested in the case to death. While one was sentenced to a lifetime in prison, the other two were respectively awarded ten and five years of imprisonment. The verdict was later challenged in the Gujarat High Court and the HC judgement is awaited.

Heading: MSU students start mapping of varsity after 60 years - Indian Express
Content:
Majid Patel, who was arrested in connection with the 2002 Akshardham Temple attack, collected money by showing CDs of attacks on minorities during the 2002 Gujarat riots, the police have said. Patel was arrested by the Bharuch Local Crime Branch (LCB) from Tankaria village on Sunday for financing and providing logistic support to the temple attackers.

"The money collection drive for the terrorist attack was undertaken by Majid alias Mohammed and two others from the same village in the district. They collected large sums of money by showing footages of riots and attacks on minorities during 2002," said Bharuch Superintendent of Police Subhash Trivedi. He added that people donated liberally as they thought the money was going for the welfare of the riot victims.

But Patel (53) and the others used the Hawala module to transfer money to the terrorists, which was later used to procure sophisticated arms and ammunition, the police said.

Incidentally, Patel, a businessman by profession, is settled in Saudi Arabia for the last 20 years. He had come to his village when the LCB was tipped off by sources. LCB officers said Patel had invested heavily into real estate and the shipping business.

LCB Inspector Dilip Aggarwal said Patel could be the key to the Lashkar-e-Toiba operatives, who allegedly executed the attack on the Akshardham Temple, which killed at least 30 people.

Aggarwal said the two others accused of financing and providing logistic support to the terrorists who attacked the temple in Gandhinagar on September 25, 2002 are Ghulam Leheri and Iqbal Patel.

"While we have handed Majid Patel to the Ahmedabad Crime Branch, who are probing into the attacks on the temple, the whereabouts of the other two accused would also be available very soon. All of them are from Tankeria village near Bharuch," said Aggarwal.

Heading: Students up ante against Science Faculty lecturer - Indian Express
Content:
While the Maharaja Sayajirao University (MSU) authorities failed to embark on the task of mapping the entire campus in the last 60 years, it has turned out to be a cakewalk for the students of the Geography department of the university.

They have been at the task for some time now and mapping is expected to be complete in the next two months.

This is for the first time in MSU that a complete map comprising minute details of the university including roads, buildings, hostels, open space, playgrounds, library and administrative block will be featured, said geography department officials.

The students are voluntarily preparing the map and will do the major groundwork during their Diwali vacations, while the university will help them fulfil the basic requirements.

Kanchan Rolee, Head of Department (HoD), Geography, MSU said: "There is no map in the MSU which has such minute details about the university, except for the few blueprints of the university campus, which is available with the engineers."

Interestingly, the students have taken the task to map the entire campus without any financial assistance from the university. This map will later be completed and put on AUTOCAD format.

Meanwhile, a group of students have completed the outlining of the entire science, arts, and commerce faculties as well as the boys' hotel, while the minute details are still pending.

"It is through the use of 100-feet chain and tape that we are measuring the minutest details, right from the entrance of each building in the university," said Gauri Vipra, one of the students working on the project.

"We have completed the work of contouring some faculties and the girls and boys hostels," she said.

Rolee said the aim behind creating this kind of map was to prepare a signboard to guide students to every location on the faculty premises. She added: "Once the map is taken in the AUTOCAD format, it will be updated as and when new structures come up in the university campus."

She said it had also become necessary to map the university as various changes had taken place here over the years, which had altered the geographical appearance of the campus. "The extensions have altered the shapes and sizes of the buildings. Besides, new ones have also been constructed," Rolee said.

A present, the students are doing a field-based map to create a sketch to identify the benchmarks, which will then be labelled and coloured. Later, overlapping mapping techniques will be applied. Only after the full compilation will the entire area of the MSU campus be known, said Rolee.

Heading: Style statement - Indian Express
Content:
M S UNIVERSITY (MSU) Physics Department students and Science Faculty General Secretary (FGS) Prajay Patel went on a dharna at the head-office of the university to protest against lecturer Deepak Rathod.

They alleged that Rathod is occupying an office, which is not allotted to him.

Patel said: "Rathod is not attending to the students properly. He is also not shifting his office, though he has been asked to do the same by the university authorities and the Physics Head of Department. Besides this, there are several allegations against him that he used to browse through pornographic sites."

He also said Vice-Chancellor Prof Ramesh Goyal has not taken any initiative to sort out the issue despite the fact that Science Faculty students submitted a memorandum to this effect two days ago.

Responding to queries by Newsline, Rathod refused to accept any of the charges.

He said: "The Science Faculty students are trying to settle scores with me because I refused to release funds for the Science Faculty garba two weeks ago. I am also the treasurer of M S University Union office." He also refuted allegations of surfing pornographic sites on the Internet.

Heading: Pleased as punch - Indian Express
Content:
Fashion gets an A certificate. Director Madhur Bhandarkar protests and tells us why this film is special

Corporate and Page 3 were movies that provided a realistic view into the trials and tribulations of the rich and famous. Madhur Bhandarkar says people in society, their lives and issues have always fascinated him, so, naturally, it was imperative that a film on fashion would soon follow. "All society parties have models and designers as guests. I wanted to highlight this fraternity through a film," says Bhandarkar in a telephonic interview.

Fashion is ready for release on October 29 but much to Bhandarkar's dismay has been given an A certificate, though he says he removed all possible objectionable content. "The censor board have their own opinions and one has to understand that," he states philosophically.

Bhandarkar's last film Traffic Signal, that narrates a depressing story of beggars and hawkers at red lights, didn't really work.

"Though the idea had been on my mind, I did not immediately start working on Fashion. Otherwise the audience would have labelled me as someone who only makes films on high society," he continues.

There's a lot of hype about Fashion, about how it exposes the dark side of the glamour industry but Bhandarkar rubbishes the trivia. "It views the fashion world from the perspective of the middle-class man who comes home after a nine-to-five job and turns on the TV set to see models walking on the ramp. His idea of the fashion industry ends there. I take that audience behind the ramp into the professional and personal lives of the models and designers," he explains.

Bhandarkar's style of cinema has coined a new phrase in Bollywood, 'middle cinema'. The film stars Priyanka Chopra (who plays Meghna Mathur) in the lead along with a host of real life models. It's Bhandarkar's most expensive venture yet, with budgets exceeding Rs 40 crore.

"I visited many fashion weeks in Delhi and Mumbai, spoke with choreographers, model coordinators, designers and buyers to give the film authenticity," says Bhandarkar. His next film, Jail, explores lives of inmates.

Heading: The Baron’s Back - Indian Express
Content:
Olympic pugilist Vijender Singh adds quick wit to his resume

Ques* From recently acquiring a secretary to being a showstopper for Rohit Bal to plans for a birthday bash in Delhi for your "new" friends, you also just inaugurated the Gold's Gym's Mulund branch. Life's changed after your Olympic win.

Not much, except that I receive too many party invitations. I have to oblige, for the sake of boxing. I want to promote the sport in India and bring it to the same level as cricket by being more visible. IPL-like tournaments will help too. The corporate world can change everything.

Ques* Mumbai's charm has touched you too.

Most successful cricketers are based out of Mumbai. I am merely here for some work and the event.

Ques* But are you not compromising on your training?

I am the same and I will prove it with results. If I don't, come back to me with the same question. I did take a break after my win but now I am back at my training camp in Patiala. I am already training for five hours a day.

Ques* What do you do in your spare time?

I sleep. And listen to music — I love Kailash Kher's songs.

Ques* Movie offers?

I love watching them, especially Akshay Kumar's films, but I don't have the time to act. Promotions are different; movies are full-time commitment and I don't think I can act. Besides, the actors may not like it if a boxer joins their fraternity.

Ques* Why do you say so?

All I can tell you is that an actor refused to shoot with me recently.

Ques* How about an item number?

That's Rakhi Sawant job, not mine.

Ques* How are things back home?

My family's extremely proud of me. But my real home is National Institute of Sports, my training camp in Patiala. It has such a lively sporty feel to it that if you come there, I promise you, you'll forget Mumbai.

Ques* You have a huge female fan following.

Don't even talk about it. I am fed-up. They write all kinds of letters to me and mail them to my home address and my parents end up reading them.

Ques* So you're still not used to all the limelight?

I am ,but my humble parents are not.

Ques* Do you have a girlfriend?

I have many friends and something or the other keeps coming up in the media.

Ques* You're neither accepting nor denying it.

So why not leave it at that?

Heading: Study Time - Indian Express
Content:
A R Rahman is a man of few words and says he gets bored easily, occasionally, even of his own compositions. He's clearly in the mood for reinvention. Rahman and Phat Phish, an entertainment company, have plunged into the reality-show brigade with

The Big Band and will soon tour 15 cities searching for that one magical group of musicians.

"Bands in our country are highly underestimated. And if there is one thing that reality shows have succeeded at, it's discovering great talent," says Rahman.

Formatted as a travelogue, the show will move to neighbouring countries including Sri Lanka, Pakistan and Nepal and is expected to go on air by December on Doordarshan. "It's about the content not the channel," insists Rahman.

On the personal music front, Rahman has two feature releases—Subhash Ghai's Yuvvraaj and Danny Boyle's Slum Dog Millionnaire. "Yuvvraaj's music is classical and if you enjoy Beethoven, you'll love this," he says about the Salman Khan-Katrina Kaif starrer. And Slum Dog? "It's about multi-culturalism, bridging gaps across the globe," says Rahman.

But if there's one project that Rahman gets animated about, it is the rap version of the English translation of Thirukkural, the classic Tamil work which he is creating. Rapper Blaaze will be singing it. "Akon has expressed interest in singing a Punjabi song and talks are on with his manager. But one has to understand that bhangra is not the only flavour of India," he signs off. Since it's Rahman, point well taken.

Heading: Break Point - Indian Express
Content:
Author Raksha Bharadia's book Roots and Wings is now on stands

"I was such a bad parent that I ended up writing this book," that's an honest confession by author Raksha Bharadia, whose book Roots and Wings was released in Ahmedabad on Sunday. Roots and Wings, published by Rupa & Co, is a handbook for parents and comes from the author of Me - An Handbook for Life and co-author of Chicken Soup for the Indian Soul. Released at the hands of eminent architect B V Doshi at the Crossword store, the audience at the function appeared more than curious to know the subtle nuances of parenting.

Roots and Wings, Raksha said, talks about how to provide roots to the children and at the same time giving them wings so that they can diversify on their own.

Apart from the topics like creativity, sports, understanding anger and fear concerning childhood, Raksha has interviewed people from different spheres of life who have made a mark in their respective fields.You find names like Javed Akhtar, Jaya Bachchan, Dr A P J Abdul Kalam, Shreya Ghoshal, Sachin Tendulkar, Kumar Mangalam Birla and the likes sharing insights about their childhood and parenting.

"I have included lots of real-life stories that would help the reader know about the upbringing of those children who have achieved something. For eg, what kind of freedom Javed Akhtar gave to his son Farhan or how Shreya Ghoshal was encouraged to follow her passion for music in a situation where everybody thought of mathematics or science to be the only ways leading to success," explains Raksha.

The book is dotted with tips that may come handy to parents and as well as the author's own experiences. "For me, it was a real-life laboratory. And the biggest lesson I have learnt is that my children are not extension of me, they are whole in themselves. Now, I respect them. We need to give them unconditional love and have the faith that they'll reach their own level," says Raksha, a mother of two.

After this handbook, she is ready with another 'chicken soup'. This time its Chicken Soup for the Indian Mothers' Soul and then she diversifies into fiction. Your readers are waiting.

Heading: Sarah Palin a hit in 'Saturday Night Live' - Indian Express
Content:
At the Fiama Di Wills Salon at the Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week, the buzz was about the makeover session of south Indian actor Ileana D'Cruz on Friday. The petite actor, who was first spotted in a Fair and Lovely ad with director Rakesh Roshan a few years ago, was rumoured to have had signed a movie opposite Shahrukh Khan. But when D'Cruz finally did make her appearance after the last show of the day, she was quick to dispel the rumours. "I don't know how it started but people have been asking me about it. There's not been any talk of any movie with Shahrukh. I wish there was though," sighs the 21-year old, who is a big name in south.

With a host of successful Telugu films to her credit since her debut in YVS Chowdhary's Devadasu in 2006, D'Cruz is now looking to break in to Bollywood. But the actor asserts she is in no hurry. "Obviously, it's something that I would like to explore, but I am a firm believer in the adage that there's a right time for everything. Tollywood has been very good to me. So I'm happy with the way things have shaped up so far," she says. But when Bollwood comes calling D'Cruz has her wish list ready. "The Mumbai film industry has some really good looking actors. I would love to work with Imran Khan or Harman Baweja," she grins.

Heading: Oops! McCain asks Russia's UN envoy for money - Indian Express
Content:
Actor Alec Baldwin on Monday called Sarah Palin "a good sport" for confronting her comedy double Tina Fey on "Saturday Night Live" - and the Republican vice-presidential candidate said she'd do it again "in a heartbeat."

After weeks of being lampooned by comedian Fey, Palin's appearance on the late night sketch show gave "Saturday Night Live" its best ratings in 14 years, drawing roughly 14 million viewers, according to early estimates by TV network NBC.

Baldwin, who pretended to mistake Palin for Fey in one sketch, defended the decision to invite her on the program.

"When you come on a show like that, you are prepared in advance to get worked over. Palin knew that. Palin came on to be a good sport. And she was. She was polite, gracious. (More so than some of the famous actors who come through there, believe me.)" Baldwin wrote in a blog on The Huffington Post.

Palin was a surprise running-mate pick by Republican presidential nominee John McCain and has been a big hit with conservative Christians for her no-nonsense folksy style.

But on "Saturday Night Live," Fey's parodies of Palin in the vice presidential debate and struggling in TV interviews have been a hit with the show's fans on TV and online.

In one of Saturday's sketches Palin, the governor of Alaska, participated in a mock press conference but wouldn't take questions from reporters, and she later pumped her arms to a rap song featuring a moose being shot.

Palin said afterward that she had a great time on the program and told WWOR-TV in New York on Sunday, "I would do that again in a heartbeat."

"It was the most welcoming and friendly environment that you could imagine. Everyone was so nice, and you know, you have to have a sense of humor through all of this. You have to have some levity through this. Otherwise, it would really, I think, grind on you and wear you out," she said.

Many critics and industry pundits also liked her.

"Ms. Palin's delightful performance on Saturday stood out from the efforts of other politicians who have made fun of themselves on the NBC late-night comedy show," wrote Alessandra Stanley in a New York Times column called The TV Watch.

Baldwin, who co-stars with Fey on the TV comedy "30 Rock", said several political commentators had riticized "Saturday Night Live" for giving Palin a spot on the show fearing it would sway voters on Election Day, Nov. 4.

"You're kidding, right? The woman is the vice presidential nominee of one of the two major parties in this country. Don't put her on SNL? With all of her exposure and the Tina Fey performance? What reality are you in?," Baldwin wrote.

Heading: Top Aus Catholic school suspends entire graduating class - Indian Express
Content:
John McCain's US Presidential election campaign has solicited a financial contribution from an unlikely source - Russia's UN envoy - but a McCain spokesman said on Monday it was a mistake.

In the letter, McCain urged Russia's UN Ambassador, Vitaly Churkin, to contribute anywhere from $35 to $5,000 to help ensure McCain's victory over Democratic rival Sen. Barack Obama, currently ahead in voter preference polls.

"If I have the honor of continuing to serve you, I make you this promise: We will always put America - her strength, her ideals, her future - before every other consideration," McCain assured Churkin.

Moscow's mission to the United Nations issued a terse statement on the Republican presidential candidate's letter, saying that the Russian government and its officials "do not finance political activity in foreign countries."

A spokesman for McCain, a long-time critic of Russia, had a simple explanation for the fundraising letter's arrival at the Russian mission in New York: "It was an error in the mailing list."

The letter was addressed to Churkin and sported a McCain signature near the bottom.

Earlier this month, both McCain and Obama harshly criticized Russia for invading Georgia two months ago, but neither was willing to say yes when asked if Russia under Prime Minister Vladimir Putin was the "evil empire".

It is illegal for U.S. presidential candidates to accept funds from foreign sources. The McCain campaign accused Obama earlier this month of not doing enough to screen for illegal contributors and asked U.S. election officials to investigate.

McCain has agreed to public financing for his campaign and therefore cannot accept funds from private donors.

Heading: Indonesia court rejects Bali bombers appeal - Indian Express
Content:
The entire graduating class at a top private school in Australia has been suspended after scores of teenage pranksters let off fireworks, disrupted traffic and dashed across campus semi-nude, the school and news reports said.

Many of the 250 students in year 12 caused "unacceptable" trouble at the Melbourne school during end-of-term pranks on Monday, said a statement from Xavier College, an independent Roman Catholic boys school.

Police said they received complaints of up to 100 students carousing through the neighbourhood Monday.

The school statement said one boy was hospitalized after being injured. The Melbourne Herald Sun newspaper said the 17-year-old student suffered multiple leg fractures.

The trouble erupted during "muck-up day," an unofficial tradition of graduating students taking part in pranks and other activities at the end of the school year.

"Unfortunately during lunchtime (Monday) a large number of Year 12 students exhibited unacceptable behaviour and as a consequence the decision was taken to cancel classes this afternoon, tomorrow and Wednesday," Xavier's director of development Graham Sharp said in the statement.

The statement did not refer to any off-campus behaviour and school officials could not be reached Tuesday.

Some students had run naked through school assembly wearing only their school ties as G-strings, and others let off fireworks at a railway station, said the 'Herald Sun' newspaper.

Security guards were posted outside the campus Tuesday after area residents complained of students harassing drivers and disrupting traffic on Monday night.

Acting Senior Sgt. Rod Philips, of the Victoria police department, said police had received numerous calls Monday complaining of up to 100 students causing trouble, and were investigating vehicle damage.

Heading: Japan PM Aso haunted by family's wartime past - Indian Express
Content:
An Indonesian court rejected on Tuesday an appeal by three Islamic militants on death row for the 2002 Bali bombings challenging the country's method of executing convicts by firing squad. The three men - Imam Samudra, Amrozi and Mukhlas, also known as Ali Ghufron - lodged the legal challenge in August, saying execution by firing squad was inhumane.

The head of the constitutional court in Jakarta rejected their appeal, saying there is no method of execution that is painless.

"The pain death convicts endure is a logical consequence inherent in a death process ... so it is not categorised as torture," said Constitutional Court chief Mohammad Mahfud. The lawyers of the bombers had argued that beheading, their clients' preferred way of execution, or lethal injection were less painful.

Attorney General Hendarman Supandji has said he will announce the execution time for the three on Friday, a move seen as breaking tradition because in the past the government has never announced dates of execution.

A Bali court initially sentenced the three men to death in 2003, but their lawyers have used a number of legal avenues that have delayed the executions.

Some critics say their execution would cause just a minor ripple in the most populous Muslim country, but others say there is a growing fear of a hardline backlash because of the execution.

Heading: Come and clarify humanitarian position, SL to Pranab - Indian Express
Content:
His hair turned-white, his aged eyes clouded-over, Roh Won-baek recalls the years during World War Two when he toiled in a coal mine owned by Japanese Prime Minister Taro Aso's family.

"Many died and got injured while working. I'm here alive and talking, but that's just because I was lucky enough to survive the close calls," said Roh, who was among more than 10,000 Koreans forced to work in the Aso family mine from 1939-1945.

Aso, who became Japan's Prime Minister in September, was only a child during World War Two when his family's mining company used Korean forced labourers rounded up by the Japanese army.

Nevertheless, despite the circumstances and the passage of time, many Koreans are galled by Aso's past.

This is especially so at a time when relations between the two countries have been uneasy due to a territorial dispute over a desolate set of islands that hark back to Japan's 1910-1945 occupation of the Korean peninsula, and a furore over textbooks that Koreans say gloss over Japan's militaristic past.

"Aso's family history might be hard to swallow for some, and could be brought up if other irritants in South Korea-Japan relations come to the surface," said Park Hong-young, a political science professor at Chungbuk University. Japan's actions in Korea, including its use of forced labour, making women work as prostitutes at frontline brothels for its troops, and property confiscations during its occupation of the Korean peninsula still weigh on Korea's relations with Japan more than 60 years after the war.

PROBLEMATIC FIGURE

Clouded by his family's wartime past, Aso, a staunch nationalist, is a problematic figure for Koreans, and analysts say his words and actions will be closely watched.

This may be especially so in light of comments he made in 2003 when he triggered a furore in the two Koreas with remarks seen as praising Japan's colonisation of the peninsula.

Analysts believe that as prime minister, Aso will try to avoid inflaming relations with South Korea, China and other countries that also suffered under the yoke of Japanese occupation.

"I do not expect the issue concerning Aso mines would be raised as a diplomatic agenda between South Korea and Japan," said Lee Moun-woo, an expert on Korean-Japanese relations.

Lee said that South Koreans would pay close attention to the way Aso addresses Japan's wartime legacy. Koreans often accuse Japanese leaders of failing to show sufficient contrition for Japan's actions during World War Two.

Shortly after taking office, Aso publicly stood by a landmark government apology made in 1995 for wartime actions. He has also hinted that he would avoid visits to Tokyo's Yasukuni shrine for war dead, seen in Beijing and Seoul as a symbol of Japan's past military aggression.

The scion of an elite political family involved in charting Japan's post-war recovery, Aso has distanced himself from his family's dark wartime past.

"I was five or six at the end of World War Two and as an individual, frankly, I have no recollection at all," Aso said in response to a question on Allied prisoners-of-war that were also forced to work in his family's mines.
