Heading: Six dud firms to transfer money to Virbhadra, family - Indian Express
Content:
The first of Arvind Kejriwal's planned daily janta durbars collapsed an hour after it started Saturday, after a heaving crowd of over 20,000 people threatened to physically swamp the chief minister and his cabinet colleagues, and the meeting teetered on the edge of disintegrating into complete chaos.

Kejriwal and Urban Development Minister Manish Sisodia were forced to retreat into the secretariat building about an hour after the durbar started at 9 am, leaving the other ministers attempting to hear the people's complaints.

The chief minister said he was in danger of being crushed by the crowd, and announced that the durbar was being suspended until the government was able to plan better and put proper arrangements in place.

Standing on the roof of the reception wing of the secretariat, Kejriwal told the crowd behind police barricades: "I accept that there were problems with the arrangements. I am deeply sorry that we could not listen to all your problems. People climbed on to the chair and table at which I was seated, and I could have been crushed if I had not left... We will come back to you with full arrangements and have another janta durbar in four to five days."

"When the crowd became unmanageable, there were two options before me, either to resort to a lathicharge or to talk to the people. I chose the second option. Next time we will have the janta durbar at a stadium," he said.

The chief minister had announced that the entire cabinet would sit outside the Delhi secretariat every Saturday to listen to the people's grievances, and would attempt to solve the urgent problems on the spot. Every weekday, a minister would receive grievances from the public.

A large proportion of the people who thronged the road outside the Delhi government headquarters were contract workers seeking permanent jobs.

Kejriwal said: "I realise that the maximum grievances are among contractual workers from BSES, Asha workers, teachers. I assure you that we have taken note of your complaints.

"On Monday I will ask all departments for data on the number of contractual staff, and why they cannot be made permanent. They will submit a report in a week, and I will try to take a decision in a month. You have waited for so many years, give me this much time."

He also requested them not to come back at the next janta durbar, so that other complaints could be heard.

The chief minister and six cabinet ministers sat in the open outside the secretariat along with senior officials, as people began handing in their complaints. Health Minister Satyendra Jain, whose mother passed away on Saturday morning, was not present.

Each person was given a slip to confirm the receipt of his complaint. Officials at the help desk said those who had supplied their mobile phone numbers would receive a confirmation SMS. \"All written complaints will be put up on our web site and the status of action taken on the complaint will be constantly updated," an official said.

Barely 15 minutes into the durbar, however, the crowd — Kejriwal said there were 5,000 people against an expected 500, while police sources said at least 20,000 people had turned up — turned unruly. Delhi Police and Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) personnel struggled to manage the crowd, which broke the barricades at some places. The entire stretch of road from ITO to Rajghat was closed, and barricades were erected on the divider so that people could occupy one carriageway.

Some 300-400 police personnel were present outside the secretariat. "There was seating arrangement for 1,000 people outside the secretariat, but a much larger crowd turned up, leading to the chaos," a police officer said.

Several people returned disappointed. "I had come here in the hope of getting relief from my problems. But I was pushed around, and I am leaving after having waited for five hours. I wanted to meet the CM to seek a job for my physically handicapped son. There is no one to look after his needs after I retire," said M S Kaushik.

The BJP accused the AAP of promoting anarchy. "This is definitely promoting anarchy. It is a sign of bad governance," senior BJP leader Harshvardhan said.

Heading: After telling Delhi to sting, AAP wants Lokpal to snoop - Indian Express
Content:
The web of financial transactions between Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Virbhadra Singh, members of his family and controversial businessman Vakamulla Chandrashekhar involve money transfers from him to the CM and his family via at least five companies that ceased to exist. And, in one case, money moved back and forth between the two sides.

This is revealed in an investigation by The Indian Express based on Registrar of Companies records and bank statements, including the one made public by Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Arun Jaitley.

As per that statement, on January 10, 2012, Chandrashekhar received Rs 49.99 lakh in his personal account from Maple Destinations, a company owned by the CM's son and daughter, Vikramaditya Singh and Aprajita Kumari, respectively. The very next day, this amount was transferred to Tarini International, a company of Chandrashekhar's Tarini group. As per RoC records, in the financial year 2011-12, Maple received Rs 49.99 lakh from Tarini Sugar and Distillaries Ltd, another company of the Tarini group.

No one from the CM's family responded to questions from The Indian Express on this transaction and others and involving companies that didn't exist. Chandrashekhar denied any wrongdoing and said he was "open for any investigation at any levels".

Between November 4 and November 21, 2011, Chandrashekhar, as per his bank statement, received inflows into his personal account amounting to Rs 1.6 crore from six companies. During the same period — November 4 to November 29 — a total of Rs 1.75 crore was transferred to the accounts of Chief Minister Virbhadra Singh, wife Pratibha Singh and son Vikramaditya Singh.

Consider the nature of these transactions:

* One of these six companies is Punjab Foods Private Ltd. On November 21, 2011, Punjab Foods deposited Rs 45.5 lakh into Chandrashekhar's account and four days later, Rs 40 lakh from here was transferred to Vikramaditya Singh's account.

Incidentally, six months earlier, on April 18, 2011, Punjab Foods had filed an application before RoC, Chandigarh, to wind up its operations.

That application stated, "Pritpal Singh (director of the company), informed the members the company is not having any business activity for the last 10 years. Further company is having neither any assets nor any liabilities, therefore Easy Exit Scheme 2011 is opted for the closure of the company".

The company was officially wound up on April 20, 2011. Yet, Chandrashekhar's account showed a deposit of Rs 21.50 lakh from Punjab Foods as late as July 24, 2012.

Speaking to The Indian Express on January 2, Chandrashekhar had said he received money from Punjab Foods against agricultural produce he sold.

* On November 4, 2011, Chandrashekhar had a balance of Rs 4.05 lakh in his account. Over the next five days, Rs 92.90 lakh came into it from Kesari Nandan and Co (Rs 17.99 lakh), Shiva Stores (Rs 15.01 lakh), Jai Durga Impex (Rs 12.25 lakh), Laxmi Enterprises (Rs 7.65 lakh), Siddharth International (Rs 26 lakh) and one Suraj Singh (Rs 14 lakh). On November 11, Chandrashekhar transferred Rs 65 lakh, in two transactions, to Virbhadhra Singh's account.

According to the RoC records, Jai Durga Impex, Shiva Stores, Kesari Nandan and Co and Siddharth International all had ceased to exist before any of these transactions.

From Chandrashekhar's account, a transaction of unknown value failed on November 15, due to "insufficient funds".

* Between November 17 and November 21, Chandrashekhar's account received Rs 45.5 lakh from Punjab Foods and Rs 53 lakh from from one "V Chandra Shekhar". Four days later, Rs 71.80 lakh in two instalments of Rs 40 lakh and Rs 31.8 lakh was transferred to CM's son Vikramaditya Singh from Chandrashekhar's account.

Subsequent to this transfer — and some minor transfers not related to the CM's family — Chandrashekhar's account balance became Rs 55.05 lakh on November 25, 2011. On November 29, 2011 two instalments of Rs 25 lakh each were transferred to Pratibha Singh and Virbhadhra Singh.

His balance after these transactions was Rs 4.73 lakh, marginally higher than what it was when the transactions began.

When asked about the transactions with the CM and his family, Chandrashekhar said: "These companies are vendor companies with whom we have had trade relationships. We have done all transactions legitimately through banks. Whether they are doing business still or not, I am not competent to answer as it is purely their business."

Despite telephone calls and text messages Vikramaditya Singh was not available for comment. Jaitley has accused Virbhadra of granting an extension to Venture Energy and Technology, promoted by Chandrashekhar, for executing a hydel project.

Asked about the money received from Maple, Chandrashekhar said: "I and VVikramaditya Singh together wanted to do a construction project in 2010-11. Accordingly, my part contribution of Rs 2 crore was made to Vikram. Since the project did not take off, he returned the money through Maple. Where is the illegality?" He added: "Shri Virbhadraji is a very noble person and worthy of friendship...I am open for any investigation at any levels."

Heading: Delhi businessman overtakes Vadra’s car, booked for rash driving - Indian Express
Content:
After urging citizens to sting corrupt government officials, the AAP government is pushing hard to pass its version of the Jan Lokpal Bill in Delhi. While the process to draft the bill is already underway, Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal has announced that the Bill will be passed in a special Assembly session by February.

"A committee has been formed to draft the law. The committee under the chief secretary will include secretaries of the departments of home, urban development, law, finance and advocate Rahul Mehra," Kejriwal said on Thursday.

"We will all meet at Ramlila Maidan either in the last week of January or first week of February," he said.

The Bill, he said, would be discussed with the "people of Delhi" at Ramlila Maidan for consent.

A Lokayukta will head the new body to combat graft with powers to conduct its own investigations, surveillance and even tap phones.

"As in the AAP's model Jan Lokpal Bill, the head of the body, in this case the Lokayukta, will have powers to tap phones, conduct independent investigations and surveillance against those who face corruption charges," Urban Development Minister Manish Sisodia said.

According to Kejriwal, the Lokayukta would function as an independent body. "Today if I am accused of corruption, there is no independent body which can investigate me but this will happen once the law is drafted," he said.

Heading: Does AP mean Ahmed Patel, asks prosecutor in Italy court; middleman says don’t know - Indian Express
Content:
A Delhi businessman was penalised by traffic police for "rash driving" after his car overtook the cavalcade of Robert Vadra, son-in-law of Congress president Sonia Gandhi.

A police officer, who did not wish to be named, said the car of Saurabh Rastogi, a businessman who lives in Paschim Vihar, was chased and intercepted by police after Vadra's securityman called the police control room and complained that a car had driven past "dangerously".

The officer said Rastogi was headed towards Lajpat Nagar from the Modi Mill flyover in Okhla at the time of the incident.

"Rastogi was in a Maruti Ritz and Vadra's cavalcade was ahead of him. We were told he had been honking continuously. In a bid to overtake the cavalcade, he accelerated and sped past Vadra's car. It was then that a securityman travelling with Vadra made a PCR call. The traffic police were also informed," the officer said.

Rastogi's car was chased by traffic policemen and intercepted near Amar Colony in south-east Delhi. "He was issued a challan for dangerous driving under Section 184 of the Motor Vehicles Act and let off," the officer said.

Heading: Day 1: Clash leaves dozens injured - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: Maya demands ban on MNS - Indian Express
Content:
The statewide agitation by Samajwadi Party (SP) against the "misrule" of the BSP government left over two dozen partyworkers, including an MP and a legislator, injured in a clash with the police on Tuesday.

All across the state, SP supporters courted arrest. They were, however, released in the evening.

In Lucknow and Banda, partyworkers marched to the collectorate offices and tried to stage a sit-in protest. When the police stopped them for entering the collectorate, they clashed with the police. SP spokesperson Rajendra Chaudhary said local MLA Bishambhar Yadav was critically injured in the police lathicharge in Banda. Banwari Lal Kanchhal, a Rajya Sabha MP, received injuries during the protests in Lucknow, he added.

Chaudhary said that incidents of police lathicharge also took place in Kanpur, Meerut and Ghaziabad. Senior party leaders, including Shivpal Singh Yadav and Akhilesh Yadav, led the agitation in other districts.

In Lucknow, nearly 2,000 workers, including women, took out a march from the Qaiserbagh district party office and reached the collectorate around 1 pm. SP (West) Paresh Pandey had an altercation with Kanchhal over entering the premises of the district magistrate's office.

As Pandey tried to prevent the MP, partymen lost their temper and indulged in a clash with the police. During the lathicharge that followed, one Mohammad Hanif suffered head injuries. Nearly 10 others were also hurt. They all courted arrest and were taken to the Heera Lal Degree College at Sarojininagar. They were later released.

The party will continue with their planned three-day "Ghera Dalo-Dera Dalo" protest across the state, Chaudhary added.

Heading: Coach factory: Railways likely to file another petition in HC - Indian Express
Content:
Terming the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) "a small regional outfit", Chief Minister Mayawati has demanded that the Centre should take stern action against it for " inflicting atrocities on north Indians".

Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, she also demanded that the Election Commission should ban the organisation with immediate effect. This comes after MNS chief Raj Thackeray was arrested earlier in the day.

"Several groups are angry and seeking retaliation against the unconstitutional activities of the MNS. It may cause a violent unrest at several places. This will be unfortunate for the country and the Congress will be held responsible for this," Mayawati said. The adverse impact of what north Indians are facing will not even spare Maharashtrians, she added.

The chief minister termed the action taken against MNS by the Congress government in Maharashtra as "mere formality". "North Indians, who have gone to Maharashtra to earn their livelihood, are being harassed by the MNS for last one year. But the Congress government remained in a slumber. Now, when the Lok Sabha elections are round the corner, the party woke up and in a jiffy arrested the MNS leader," said Mayawati.

She also accused the BJP for being silent on the issue. "Why the BJP has not demanded a strict action against MNS? This shows its dual policies," she said.

Heading: Congress MLA accuses police of being BSP leader’s agent - Indian Express
Content:
The Railway Ministry is likely to file a petition in the Allahabad High Court, questioning the Uttar Pradesh government's decision to provide land for the proposed rail coach factory on lease for 90 years.

The ministry believes that the lease will unnecessarily delay the project. Hence, it wants the land on outright purchase.

Following cancellation of land allotment by the state government on October 12, the Railway Ministry had filed a writ petition in the Lucknow Bench of Allahabad High Court against the government action. The court had ordered status quo and fixed the next hearing for October 22.

On October 18, the state Government had decided to return the land to Railways, but on lease. According to the ministry, it was another hurdle in executing the project, because finalising the terms and conditions of the lease could turn out to be a tricky business.

Explaining the need to file another petition, a railway official said: "Now, the situation is different from when we had filed the earlier petition. The government is returning the land, but with a new condition. We want an outright purchase. Lease will involve completion of new formalities, which will make various deadlines for the project irrelevant."

Heading: Community centre once, now office of Akhilesh Das - Indian Express
Content:
A day after the state police arrested the brother of Anugrah Narayan Singh, a Congress MLA from Allahabad, the legislator accused the police of being an "agent" of BSP leader Ashok Bajpai .

Singh's brother Narayan Pratap was arrested along with 13 others on charges of gambling. "My brother and the others are being falsely implicated on the behest of BSP leader Ashok Bajpai and his son Harshvardhan Bajpai," Singh alleged. "In his statement to media, Harshvardhan has admitted that he had told the police to arrest Narayan," the MLA added.

"I will meet Chief Minister Mayawati and demand a probe, besides an inquiry into my assets and that of Ashok Bajpai and his son," Singh said.

He said the police have started harassing prominent persons who are not linked with the BSP. "My brother is in property business and he was meeting some builders in his house, when police raided the house and arrested them," he alleged.

"The police action is aimed at tarnishing my image, as I had defeated Harshvardhan in the 2007 Assembly elections," Anugrah said, adding that he will reveal startling facts of police misdeeds on Wednesday.

The police, however, refuted the allegation saying that they had recovered Rs 9.50 lakh and playing cards from the spot. BSP leader Harshvardhan Bajpai denied his role in the arrests. "Narayan Singh and others were gambling at Civil Lines. It was an illegal act and I appreciate the police action."

Heading: Maya announces out-of-turn promotions at police meet - Indian Express
Content:
For the last 10 months, the community centre of the Lucknow Municipal Corporation (LMC) in the Purana Qila area has not hosted any wedding or private function. Reason: at present, the centre is virtually functioning as the election office of Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) national general secretary Dr Akhilesh Das.

While the hall and rooms accommodate BSP workers, the lawn is used as a parking slot.

A security personnal at centre said on Tuesday: "If you have to book the community centre for any function, contact Dasji's residence."

Locals claimed that the community centre has not been rented out to any private party since last year after BSP supporters occupied it. No one is allowed to enter its premises, where a banner of the BSP has been put up.

Local corporator P S Jaiswal, who is also a BSP member, said: "Booking of the community centre was closed last year because locals had complained against loud music and chaos during marriage functions."

He added, "The centre is now being used as a venue for meetings of BSP workers. As it was not in use for a long period, sometimes, party workers use it. A few months ago, Dr Das had renovated the centre with his MP fund. Then what is the problem if he uses it for some work?"

Das, however, denied the developments. "I have nothing to do with the community centre. Somebody is trying to defame me. It is possible that the authority who runs the centre has booked it for programmes to be held by the BSP."

According to Das, the community centre was built in 1994 when he was the mayor of Lucknow. The proposal was approved by the LMC House. "That centre belongs to the civic body and it is the responsibility of its officials to take care of it," he added.

When asked, LMC officials seemed unaware of the status of the community centre. "I have not received any application about the booking of a community centre in Purana Qila area. I am not sure whether the centre belongs to LMC," Additional Municipal Commissioner A C Sinha said.

Das further claimed: "You should ask LMC officials and the present BJP mayor why they are not removing the encroachers from the community centre premises."

When asked, Mayor Dinesh Sharma said: "I have received a complaint from locals that the community centre has been encroached upon. Two LMC officials have been directed to visit the spot to take stock of the situation."

Heading: Now, VHP takes on family planning - Indian Express
Content:
A six feet deep and three feet wide tunnel has been discovered from a barrack in Ambala jail where two condemned prisoners and two others serving life sentence have been lodged.

The inmates of the barrack, Sanjiv Kumar, son-in-law of slain MLA Relu Ram Punia, and Dharampal are facing death penalty. They share their barrack with Masood Akhtar and Mohammed Salim serving life for espionage.

The tunnel was dug with spades and covered with grass and weeds. The digging, which had been going on for some time, was traced after the cyber cell system of the police intercepted Masood and Salim's conversation with their conduits.

The police then brought it to the notice of the Central Jail authorities. Soon senior police officials visited the barrack along with the jail staff and unearthed the tunnel.

DGP (Jails) Dr John V George, however, chose to downplay the incident and called the tunnel as a mere 'pit'. He did not comment on how the tunnel was dug, how the prisoners could get access to spades and how the jail authorities remained oblivious of all this. Efforts to contact the jail superintendent proved futile.

Sanjiv Kumar was held guilty of murdering his father-in-law and seven family members in August 2001. He committed the murders in complicity with his wife, both of whom were sentenced to death by the Sessions court in Hissar. The death penalty was subsequently upheld by the High Court and the Supreme Court. A mercy petition is pending with the President.

Heading: Improved technology keeps power thieves in check, brings in more money - Indian Express
Content:
The Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) has decided to launch a campaign against family planning. It will use a book to urge Hindus to ensure that they produce at least four male children — "two for the family and two for the Hindu cause".

To spread its new strategy among the Hindu masses, the VHP will circulate a book Bharat mein Hindu Bahumat (Hindu majority in India). About 10,000 copies of this book have been collected in Karsewak Puram, the local headquarters of VHP here, said Rama Patnaik, a VHP full-timer.

Senior VHP leaders, however, are not ready to disclose much on the issue. "It is a good move by the VHP, as the family planning system introduced in India by the Congress is anti-religious," said Mahant Ram Kripal.

"Our religious books do not give permission to control births," he added.

Publised by an Ahmedabad-based publisher, the 100-page book says that at the given rate, the population of Muslims and Christians will outnumber that of Hindus in half a century. The book asks Hindus to ensure the birth of at least four male children and prepare two of them for the cause of Hindutva. It also directs parents to teach girls to prepare themselves for this.

The book claims family planning is a "Christian and Muslim strategy to make Hindus a minority in India".

In the present circumstances, it will be an anti-national act by the Hindus to adopt family planning system, says the book.

Speaking to The Indian Express, Ramanand Maheshwari, a VHP leader and member of the team that will circulate the book, said: "Within a few days we will take the book to the Hindu masses. We will also give it publicity through meetings, street plays and processions."

Heading: Gangster Anees surrenders before Barabanki court - Indian Express
Content:
A slew of measures, includproper training, computerisation of equipment and more authority to the Vigilance Wing of Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Ltd (UPPCL), has proved fruitful, as cases of power thefts have reduced significantly across the state.

In the last six months, enforcement squads have ensured an 18 per cent increase in revenue collection from power theft cases.

According to the government data, from April 1 to September 30, the UPPCL collected Rs 13.5 crore as penalty from 21,586 consumers who were accused of power thefts. Incidentally, in the same period, last year, the collection was a mere Rs 5.4 crore from 22,080 consumers.

"Well-trained staff and use of latest electronic equipment have helped to increase the collection," said Avneesh Awasthi, Managing Director, UPPCL.

Superintendent of Police (Enforcement) UPPCL, Vigilance Wing, Laxmi Singh said: "Checking of power thefts has become more effective in the state because of proper training given to the enforcement squads. Computerised equipment has also helped to improve the efficiency." The UPPCL has 33 enforcement squads — each having around ten enforcement officers, comprising police personnel and power engineers. Earlier, these squads used to depend solely on reports of assistant engineers and junior engineers, who inspect the electric metres, and the police personnel accompanying them remained clueless about ways to check power thefts.

Last year, the UPPCL Vigilance Wing conducted a workshop, specifically for police personnel in the enforcement squads. Along with training, the UPPCL also provided the squads with latest equipment for checking the metres.

Now, the squads have high-tech machines like MRI scanners and aqua checks, which are connected to laptops for checking any tampering of the metres. "Besides, the computer shows the pattern in which the metre has functioned in the last one year," Singh said.

Not only this, the whole process of metre checking is video-recorded so that it could be used as evidence in case any dispute arises in future.

The vigilance wing is also planning to conduct raids more strategically in future. "We procure the list of consumers from the UPPCL and after a detailed analysis of power consumption and load factor in different areas, we chalk out the action plan," Singh added.

"We normally focus on areas where load factor is less, which is because of only two factors — either there is no factory in the area or power theft is rampant there," said an officer of the squad.

Interestingly, the UPPCL has stopped filing cases against people and industries accused of power thefts. In the last six months, just one case has been filed in court whereas in the same period 230 cases had been filed last year.

Heading: Tourism department wishes to sell its sick hotels, finds few takers - Indian Express
Content:
Anees Radiowala, close aide of fugitive don Ejaz Lakdawala, surrendered before the Chief Judicial Magistrate court in Barabanki on Tuesday.

The police were on the hunt for Anees, a resident of Mumbai, since he had procured bail from a Barabanki court against fake sureties on April 14.

Acting on a tip-off from the Mumbai police, the Special Task Force of UP Police had arrested Anees and three others — Mohammed Rahim Khan, Ishrat Warsi and Namdeo — in Barabanki on July 25, 2007 while they were on their way to Nepal.

They were arrested for allegedly planning to kill singer Himesh Reshammiya and film producer-director Raj Kumar Santoshi over extortion demands. Later, the court granted him bail against sureties by four people and was released on April 14.

Superintendent of Police (Barabanki) Praveen Kumar said the four bail bonds in the name of Deo Narayan Verma, Hari Lal Verma, Ram Lal Verma and Kanhai Lal Verma that were submitted in favour of Anees were found to be fake. Following this, a fresh case against Anees and others was lodged with the Dewa police.

Kumar said: "We had raided Anees' Andheri residence several times and pasted the court notice declaring him a proclaimed absconder. The pressure built by the police has forced the accused to surrender before the court."

Heading: Couple thrown off train, husband dies - Indian Express
Content:
The much-hyped privatisation of hotels and other property owned by Uttar Pradesh Tourism has received a lukewarm response. While officials maintain that big players of tourism sector are interested in buying the property, the first bid opened on Monday had an altogether different story to tell.

The list of the bidders for the hotels and rest houses in Gorakhpur, Kaushambi, Kushinagar, Sankisa and Sarnath near Varanasi had no big names. For most of the property, there were either no takers or barely one or two bidders, who owned hotels in the nearby areas.

The only site for which there were three bidders was the hotel at Sarnath, which also happens to be the only property in proper condition.

Sources in the tourism department said poor infrastructure and decaying condition of these hotels and guesthouses are keeping many players away from bidding.

A senior official of the department said: "These hotels are in a bad shape and in such remote and inaccessible areas that no one would be keen to own them." The official added barely 40 of these properties are in a decent condition, while the rest are all in a bad shape. Moreover, the bid rules state that the basic structure of the properties could not be changed and this could also be responsible for few takers.

"Only properties on the Delhi route like those in Ghaziabad, Baghpat or Hindon have evoked a good response as they are huge properties. With the Commonwealth Games approaching, these hotels are being eyed by the buyers," the official added.

The department, however, maintains that they are waiting for the "right bidders" to strike a "good deal" before they finalise any names. "We are not hurrying up the process as we want a good deal," Sushil Kumar, principal secretary tourism, said.

The department had decided to sell around 70 of its hotels and rest houses to private players on the public-private partnership model, as most of these were suffering with heavy losses.

Heading: Accident or suicide? Mystery surrounds death of CA - Indian Express
Content:
Four unidentified men threw a couple out of a moving train near Malhaur station early on Tuesday morning, when the husband objected to making lewd remarks against his wife. While the husband, Pappu Sharma (34) died on the spot, his wife Abhilasha Sharma was undergoing medical treatment at the Civil Hospital. 

Pappu, a native of Bihar, and Abhilasha were on way from Naubasia in Bihar to Ambala, where Pappu worked as a plumber.

A railway guard spotted the couple lying near the track and arranged to send them to the hospital.

Abhilasha told the police that on Monday night, four youths boarded the train at Kalihari station in Bihar and started harassing them by passing obscene remarks against her. The couple changed the coach, but the miscreants stalked them and reached the new coach.

She added that on Tuesday morning, when her husband tried to reason with them, they beat him up. Near Malhaur Railway Station, they threw the couple out of the moving train.

According to the police, Abhilasha had married with Pappu just four days ago, much against the wishes of her family.

Inspector of Government Railway Police, Tripurari Pandey said: "We are trying to arrest the accused and a GRP team has been sent to Punjab and Delhi."

Heading: Gas leak lands factory workers in hospital - Indian Express
Content:
Mystery shrouds the death of a 25-year-old man, Harshad Fore, who reportedly jumped off Moolchand Flyover near Defence Colony area of South Delhi. Though the police suspect it to be an accident, circumstances in which his body was found out suggest he might have committed suicide.

Police said the incident occurred around 2 am on Tuesday. A senior police officer said the dead body has been sent for postmortem.

The police sources said the deceased was a native of Mumbai and was working as a chartered accountant in the Capital for the last few months.

His family in Mumbai, including his elder brother who is also a chartered accountant in Mumbai, has been informed about the incident. They are expected to reach Delhi tonight.

A case of accident has also been registered with the Defence Colony police station and further investigations are on.

Police officers said as his body was found at the Moolchand underpass, it was closed for the traffic for about an hour till it was taken to the hospital. Fore was declared dead on arrival. Though the police have registered a case of accident, they are still not sure about the sequence of events.

"As told by family members, Harshad left his house to go to Ladakh. No one knows why he was still in Delhi," said police sources.

Sources added they are probing the matter from all possible angles and police are not ruling out foul play.

Heading: ‘It is our duty to look after families of martyrs’ - Indian Express
Content:
Four people fainted after they reportedly inhaled ammonia gas in the Haryana Cold Storage in Ram Darbar, Phase II.

The incident occurred late on Tuesday evening when goods were being unloaded from a vehicle. The valve of a cylinder broke, releasing ammonia gas. The workers dispersed on detecting the leakage, but as the gas spread those working in the adjoining factory smelt it and fainted. Four of them were taken to the Government Medical College and Hospital in Sector 32. Their condition is state to be stable.

Officials of the fire department, meanwhile, reached the spot and plugged the leak. Sub-fire officer Baljinder Singh said it was due to timely intervention by the department that the leak could be plugged. Since the incident occurred late in the evening, most of the factories had closed down. This also prevented serious damage.

Heading: Colleagues, ministers, family members bid adieu to Chhatwal - Indian Express
Content:
"The Haryana Police personnel have left no stone unturned to put duty before themselves," said Haryana Governor Dr AR Kidwai, while speaking at the 49th Indian Police Commemoration Day in Panchkula on Tuesday. He said that 10 police personnel of the CRPF on border patrol had laid their lives in Ladakh, while protecting the Indian territory from Chinese intruders on October 21, 1959.

"It is since then that October 21 is observed as Police Commemoration Day, not only to commemorate the memory of those 10 brave souls, but also to remember those who lay their lives for the security of the country and its people every year," said a spokesperson of the department.

He added: "Of these martyrs, Havaldar Shailender Singh, Constable Krishan Kumar, Constable Suresh Kumar belonged to Haryana. We are also proud of the sacrifices made by the Haryana Police personnel, including ASI Narender Singh, Head Constable Sarjent Singh and Umar Mohmmad, who gave their lives while fighting against criminals."

Kidwai said: "Keeping in view the sacrifices made by them for the security and safety of the society, we are also duty bound to look after them and their families. It is a matter of great pride that the Government of Haryana has extended a number of facilities and concessions for the police personnel and their families."

Haryana DGP Ranjeev Dalal said that performing one's duty with dedication should be the priority of every officer. K K Sindhu, IG, Ambala Police Range, read out the names of the martyrs of the Indian police.

Two-minute silence observed

CHANDIGARH: Inspector General of Police S K Jain called upon the officers to dedicate their services for the cause of the state and country.

He was addressing a gathering at the Police Commemoration Day parade at the Sector-17 police station on Tuesday. They also observes a two-minute silence as a mark of respect for those who had laid their lives for the country. Jain read the names of all 683 personnel, who have laid down their lives in last one year across the country.

Martyrs' saluted

MOHALI: The Mohali police saluted the police officers who had lost their lives while serving the country since September 1, 2007 on the ocassion of Police Martyrs Memorial Day at a special memorial held at Mohali Police Lines in the Community Centre, Phase XI, on Tuesday. Mohali Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Jatinder Singh Aulakh, paid tributes to the departed souls.

Heading: ‘Family needs to identify suicidal tendencies’ - Indian Express
Content:
The cremation of Punjab cadre IAS officer AS Chhatwal, who had committed suicide by hanging himself on Monday, was attended by a large number of bureaucrats from both from Punjab and Haryana, besides a few politicians today.

Wreaths were laid on behalf of Punjab Governor General SF Rodrigues (Retd) and Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal. Among those present on the occasion were Information and Public Relations Minister Bikram Singh Majithia, Finance Minister Manpreet Singh Badal, Health Minister Laxmi Kanta Chawla, Chief Secretary Ramesh Inder Singh, President of Punjab State IAS Officers Association Tejinder Kaur, Principal Secretary to the Chief Minister DS Guru and DS Cheema, Advisor to the CM.

In a condolence message, Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal, expressed deep shock at the unfortunate death of Chhatwal. Describing him as "an honest, bright and effective officer", he said Punjab had lost one of its best civil servants.

Badal also visited Chhatwal's house in Sector 39 and met his wife and family members.

Information and Public Relations Minister Bikram Singh Majithia, remembered Chhatwal as "an outstanding and honest officer whom I had specially chosen to head the Science and Technology Department".

Sukhbir Singh Badal and MP Sukhdev Singh Dhindsa, also expressed grief at Chhatwal's demise and described it as a "personal loss".

Punjab Chief Secretary Ramesh Inder Singh said Chhatwal was "an amiable person and an outstanding officer".

The Punjab State IAS Officers Association held an emergency condolence meeting this afternoon to mourn the death of Chhatwal. Expressing "profound sorrow and shock" in a resolution passed in the meeting, Association President Tejinder Kaur described Chhatwal as "an outstanding officer, warm and spirited person and, a dear friend to all." He said: "His passing away is an irreparable loss to the cadre as well as to the state."

Former ministers Tota Singh and Jagmohan Singh Kang were also present.

Heading: ‘Outstanding and honest fireman’ given a farewell by MC - Indian Express
Content:
Taking the drastic step of ending one's life is not a spur of the moment decision. Suicide is a painful decision taken by an individual after much thought. The signs for the same can be recognised by the person's family. These are some views of city psychologists, after the shocking incident of suicide by Punjab IAS officer A S Chhatwal came to light.

Dr B S Chavan, Head of department, Psychiatry, GMCH, Sector 32, says he had conducted a study on 101 families in the city, in which, one member had committed suicide.

"The families when gave a thought to the events preceding the suicide, said the deceased did give some signs. Suicide bids are generally preceded by certain acts like avoiding interaction with people. The person becomes very quiet and avoids even routine activities. The depressive symptoms need to be recognised," he said.

"People having suicidal tendencies usually start planning for the future of their family members. They appear gloomy and avoid daily activities. They plan out the act very meticulously," he added.

Dr Adarsh Kohli, assistant professor, department of Psychology, PGI, says that if the person is close to his or her family, then the members would be able to recognise the signs. "The family members should be sensitive to the behavioural changes in an individual. In some cases, people cannot resolve their inner conflicts by themselves, the family needs to be supportive in such instances."

Heading: Travel agency to pay up for harassing UP election officer - Indian Express
Content:
The fireman, who succumbed to his injuries at the PGI on Monday, after having received nearly 40 per cent burns in a fire-fighting operation nearly a week ago, was cremated today evening in the presence Mayor Pardeep Chhabra and Municipal Commissioner Dr Roshan Sunkaria, among others. To Mayor Pardeep Chhabra, Mavi was an outstanding and honest fireman. He offered his condolences to the family in their moment of grief.

At Mavi's residence in Dhanas, it was a picture of grief and tragedy. Mavi is survived by his wife, mother and two sons who are studying in Class XII.

Amarjit Singh Mavi was engaged in a fire-fighting operation at a Sector 22 residence on October 14.

While the fire was brought under control, there was, reportedly, a leaking cylinder covered under a sack, which apparently burst as Mavi entered the room. Not wearing a safety gear, the fireman received face and chest injuries to which he succumbed on Monday night.

A meeting of the Emergency and Fire Services committee was, meanwhile, held to discuss the issue of providing insurance cover to firemen. The details of the proposal are, however, yet to be finalised.

Heading: ICICI Bank to cough up Rs 2 lakh for ‘theft of vehicle’ - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Forum has directed a travel agency to pay Rs 26,000 as compensation for deficiency in services. The booking agency, The Travel People in Sector 17, has also been directed to pay Rs 1,100 as costs of litigation after an election observer of the UP General Assembly Elections was harassed due to wrong bookings and miscalculation of timings.

The complainant, Harinder Kumar, availed the services of agency for booking air tickets from Chandigarh-Lucknow-Hardoi and back on four occasions. The tickets were booked for April 8, 2007, April 29, 2007, May 9, 2007 and May 13, 2007. Harinder, being the election observer for the UP State Assembly Elections, needed to travel between these places and eight air tickets were booked from Jet Airways for the same. He was assured that there is no chance of his flight being missed or delayed. He was also told that the baggage will be booked from Chandigarh to Lucknow and will be transferred from one flight to other by the staff.

On April 8, 2007, the flight from Chandigarh to Delhi was delayed by one-and-a-half hours and by the time he reached Delhi, the connecting Jet Airways flight for Lucknow had already departed. He also said that he was forced to carry his entire luggage himself and no service of automatic transfer of luggage to Sahara flight was provided to him.

On reaching Lucknow, the complainant decided to cancel all the remaining air tickets due to the short duration between the flights reaching Delhi and those leaving from Delhi.

He informed the office at Chandigarh to cancel all the air tickets and refund the amount. He, however, alleged that he was not refunded the full amount and deducted cancellation charges.

The Travel People, in their reply, said delay of flights was not in their control, so they cannot be held responsible for the chaos. They also denied that they were informed by the complainant's office in Chandigarh to cancel all the tickets and refund the amount.

The forum, headed by Jagroop Singh Mahal, said it is the fault of the travel agency in making the wrong bookings for which, they are liable to pay compensation to the complainant.

Heading: Firm to pay up for harassing student - Indian Express
Content:
Finding the ICICI Bank guilty of gross deficiency in services, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum today directed it to pay Rs 2 lakh as compensation for illegally and forcibly retaining a vehicle. The Forum also found the Bank guilty of 'theft of the vehicle'.

The Bank has also been directed to adjust the amount of Rs 1.85 lakh due as loan, from the complainant. In addition, GE Financial Services has also been directed to issue a no-objection certificate (NOC) to the complainant. Both the companies have also been directed to pay Rs 5,000 as litigation costs.

The complainant, Inderjit Diman, had got his second-hand Indica financed from GE Countrywide Consumer Financial Services for Rs 2.25 lakh. While he took Rs 1.65 lakh of the amount as loan, the remaining Rs 60,000 was paid in advance. He was to pay monthly instalments of Rs 4,750 for four years, between May 7, 2004 and March 7, 2008.

The complainant said that after he had paid 14 instalments, he was approached by the collection manager of ICICI Bank, who said they will clear his entire loan with GE Financial Capital by opening a Car Overdraft (OD) Account with their Bank for a sum of Rs 1,50,000. They also said he would not have to pay any further amount to GE Financial Company and they would clear his loan and would get an NOC, after which, he could start repaying them.

The complainant averred that he agreed to their offer and paid them Rs 1,500 as processing fee and also submitted the registration certificate of his car.

He was then given a Demand Draft of Rs 1,25,239, which was the amount due with the GE Financial. The complainant deposited the said draft of Rs 1,25,239 towards the loan account but was shocked when the GE Capital said they would not issue the final receipt till he deposited Rs 19,500 more. He said that he informed ICICI about the same and they told him to deposit the amount, which would be adjusted in his account, but was not done despite numerous letters and reminders. They instead, asked him to pay the instalment and also made him deposit Rs 10,000.

He alleged that the ICICI Bank recovery agents forcibly and illegally took away his car without his knowledge and consent, causing mental tension and harassment.

ICICI Bank, said it was the complainant who had approached them for availing the Car Over Draft Facility, under which, he availed a finance of Rs 1.5 lakh and subsequently got issued a demand draft of Rs 1,25,239 in favour of GE Countrywide, as this was the only amount which was required to be paid for the purpose of clearance of his loan account.

The bank admitted that they had taken his car, but denied that it was taken forcibly. It also stated that the Bank was willing to return the vehicle to the complainant provided all the dues were cleared, but when he refused to do so, they sold the vehicle on May 17, 2006, at Rs 1,05,000.

The forum found that before taking possession of the vehicle, the Bank did not serve any notice to the complainant. He was not informed about the date and place on which the vehicle should have been brought by him for the surrender.

Heading: Let students be innovative and do things their way - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed Artex Informatic Solutions in Sector 34 to pay Rs 30,000 as compensation for causing mental and physical harassment to a student by wasting her time and money after she got admission in the Sikkim Manipal University. They have also been directed to refund Rs 12,300 charged as the admission fee.

The complainant, Garima Mahantan, took admission in Sikkim Manipal University through their managing director at their office — Artex Informatic Solutions. The student wished to avail herself of the distance education course in MBA (Master of Business Administration in Health Care Services) and paid Rs 11,450 as the fee. It was alleged that when the complainant approached the office in Sector 34 to get her roll number for the first semester examination, which was to be held from January 29, 2008 to February 3, 2008, she was "rudely" told that her application form was not considered by the university and thus she could not take the examination.

Alleging gross unfair trade practice and deficiency in service, she moved the consumer forum.

In their reply, the Sikkim Manipal University admitted that the complainant applied for admission in their MBA course and deposited the fee in cash. It was pleaded that on the scrutiny of the application, it was found that she had applied for a course MBA HCS, which was not offered under the IT and Management Prospectus Fall 2007 purchased by her. The course of MBA HCS was offered under the Allied Health Sciences and Life Sciences Prospectus Fall 2007, which was never purchased by her. Thus, her application was rejected.

The second opposite party which was Artex Informatic Solutions said that she was given the IT and Management Prospectus, which relates to MBA and contains the relevant form. She filled up the application form and submitted the same along with the fee and other charges to the opposite party.

As the prospectus relating to the MBA HCS was titled "Allied Health Sciences and Life Sciences", which was entirely different from the IT and management prospectus, thus she was not eligible to sit for the examination.

The forum found that the complainant was misled and harassed by the university by accepting her admission form, which their office in Sector 34 was not competent to accept. "The complainant has have been put to monetary loss in the shape of the admission fee and had also to spend a good amount of money and their time in coming from Chamba (Himachal Pradesh) to Chandigarh to sit in the examination, besides wasting one precious year, which took place entirely due to the fault of the University."

Heading: Qualification bar raised for Physical Education lecturers at PU - Indian Express
Content:
It gives me immense joy when I see my pupils think out of the box and teachers only act as a base to propel their innovations beyond the skies.

When I started out as a teacher in the early 90s, I felt very awkward about the education system. A weak student was often suppressed by the virtual teaching methodology. But being the pope of a reputed institute now, I never let my priests rate any child weaker or stronger. Rather than leaving a tilted sapling to grow at an angle, we support it to grow straight so that it stands tall in this competitive world.

A teacher is the best substitute to a mother and if both do their roles to perfection, the dream of a clean and pure India will be no far. For this, a perfect blend of moral values and knowledge is required. In this process, we should not forget to give them ample time for leisure activities, which is an equally important aspect of proper education. I believe students should be given all the freedom to do a particular thing in their own innovative ways.

A teacher should act as a guide and must not force a student to do anything in a prescribed manner. Gone are the days when books were everything.

Now is the time of innovative thinking. In the West, students get the freedom to do things their way. The practical aspect of anything is very important and students should be given adequate exposure and acquainted with the practical aspect of any concept that is being taught to them.

This theory of practical aspect should not only be applied to the students during their school hours but parents should also help them in this regard. At home, the parents should trust their children and give them responsibility. A task can be done in many ways and by giving students freedom to choose their own ways we not only boost their morale but also help in their personal and mental development.

Heading: HDFC ties up with educational institute for study loans - Indian Express
Content:
Going a step ahead of the guidelines laid down by the National Council for Teachers Education (NCTE), a committee formed to review the educational qualifications of Physical Educational lecturers at the Panjab University have decided to raise the bar. The decision, it is said, has been taken with an aim to improve the quality of education on the campus.

As per the NCTE guidelines, an individual is eligible to be appointed as a lecturer if he or she holds a masters degree in physical education and there is no particular requirement for him or her to have an MPhil degree or to have cleared the NET exam. The university officials, however, have decided to give preference to the ones who have cleared the NET or have an MPhil degree. It would be only in the absence of such individuals that a lecturer with a MA in Physical Education will be hired.

Talking to Newsline, G K Chatrath, a PU Fellow and a member of the committee said, "The decision has been taken by the committee keeping in mind the quality of education. We have gone a step ahead of the NCTE in defining the educational qualifications for Physical Education lecturers for the benefit of students."

An official at the varsity said, "Teachers with masters degree in Physical Education were hired only on temporary basis to fill the vacancies. We do not want the students to suffer, so we have kept this relaxation."

The decision, however, has come as a surprise for individuals seeking jobs in the university. A candidate, with an MA degree in Physical Education, said, "The decision is not fair at all. What is the need to go ahead of the guidelines of the NCTE? The decision, if implemented, is bound to rouse criticism."

Heading: Vivek School students on a high as they share experiences of conference in Canada - Indian Express
Content:
The Institute of Computer and Finance Executives (ICFe), a training provider in the financial sector, has tied-up with the HDFC bank for providing a study loan facility. This facility is available for meritorious but economically weak students who wish to undertake courses offered by the institute. This education loan facility is available at all ICFe centers across India.

A student of the institute will be eligible for the education loan ranging from Rs 50,000 to Rs 1, 00,000 from HDFC Bank. The loan is available in easy payback installments of 12, 24, 36 and equal monthly installments, after the completion of the course. ICFe imparts training in fields of Accounting, Banking, Insurance and Financial Services.

Heading: Speeding? UT Admn to put up speed limit boards on city roads - Indian Express
Content:
The Students of Vivek High School, who are just back from Canada where they had gone to attend the Round Square International Conference, shared their experiences at a media conference today. The weeklong programme was held at the Glenylon Norfolk School in Victoria from October 3 to 9. The students were accompanied by school chairman H S Mamik, principal Daman Dugal and the Round Square School representative Rajbir Sandhu.

The visiting group included Udhay Singh, Viraaj Pannu, Natasha Sekhon, Akshay Vashistha, Aslesha and Saba Sodhi. The theme of the conference this year was 'Creating sustainable communities' and was attended by all permanent members and observer schools from USA, Australia, South Africa, India, Canada, Oman, Dubai, Bangladesh, Jordon, UK, Germany, France, Columbia and Peru. King Constantine of Greece, who is the chief patron of Round Square, presided over the opening and closing ceremony.

Sharing their experiences, students said that the conference provided a great platform to them to interact with students from different backgrounds. School principal Daman Duggal said, "In my opinion, every school must arrange for such educational tours for the students. Students get first-hand experience and learn a lot by meeting children from different regions and cultures.

The barazza, as it is known, or the student group discussed the significance of carbon imprint and each country's contribution to the same. The conference included an adventure day and the students were also taken on a tour of the Vancouver Islands where they saw killer whales, dolphins, sea lions and seals in their natural surroundings. Keynote speakers at the conference included Brian Keating, a anthropology professor and nature enthusiast, Tad Homer Dixon, an environmentalist, Sharon Wood, the first American woman to climb the Mount Everest and Craig Kielburger, an international human rights activist and founder of the 'Free the Children movement'.

The Round Square Conference of Schools is a worldwide association of more than 60 schools, based on the philosophy of German educationist Kurt Hahn, that allows students to travel between schools and travel foreign shores.

Heading: Work on solid waste plant in Mohali begins - Indian Express
Content:
New site will give respite to residents and industrialists in the Industrial Focal Point area

The work on the new solid waste treatment plant in Mohali has finally started. A notification has been issued to acquire 76 acres in Sector 102-A for the project, which will give respite to hundreds of residents and industrialists from the present site in the Industrial Focal Point at Phase VIII-B.

Till now, garbage of the entire city was dumped in a densely-populated area surrounded by industrial units, mega projects and residential areas like, IT major Quark Media, Dell Computers and Punjab's most-touted special economic zone QuarkCity. The Residential Welfare Society of the PSIEC Housing Complex in the Industrial Focal Point claimed that the garbage was dumped against the national dumping rules.

The foul smell of the garbage and the smoke from the burning of the garbage had been causing health problems like breathing, skin and eye complications.

The Residential Welfare Society had been fighting a legal battle seeking shifting of the dumping ground from the present site.

As a short-term arrangement, the Mohali District Administration had last year requested the Chandigarh Administration to allow the dumping of garbage for processing at Chandigarh's waste processing unit but the Chandigarh Municipal Corporation (MC) had categorically refused to accept the offer.

The Mohali District Administration had proposed that since the MC was setting up a new unit of a capacity of 600 MT and presently Chandigarh's total garbage generation was much less than that, Mohali Municipal Council may be allowed to dump its garbage in that unit till a separate unit comes up in the city.

Now, with no other option in hand and even the Punjab and Haryana High Court directing the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (SHUD), Punjab, to file a status report on the steps being taken to set up the solid waste treatment plant in Mohali, the department of Housing and Urban Development has stepped up its efforts to set up the facility as per the site earmarked in the Master Plan in Sector 102-A by initiating the land acquisition proceedings despite opposition by the residents of Chaomajra, Dairi and Dharali villages.

As per the acquisition notice under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, 34.29 acres in Dharali, 30.14 acres in Chaomajra and 11.57 acres land was being acquired in Dairi village for dumping and burning garbage and waste material of Mohali, said officials in the department of Housing and Urban Development.

Officials said, as per the directions of the High Court, the issues regarding the setting up of a solid waste treatment plant in Mohali were being discussed and sorted out between the Mohali Municipal Council and the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority under the overall supervision of SHUD Arun Goel.

Sources said initially the new site will be used as a scientific garbage dumping and burning centre before setting up of the solid waste treatment plant under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM).

Heading: Criminal contempt petition filed against Haryana advocate general - Indian Express
Content:
The statements of the original owner of the property in Solan, now co-owned by Justice Nirmal Yadav and others, were recorded by the Gokhale Committee on Tuesday. The committee is in Chandigarh for the second time to investigate the cash-at-judge's-door case.

The three-judge committee reached the city in the morning and started its work at 11.30 am. It also recorded the statements of Solan naib tehsildar and deputy commissioner. The statements of Ravinder Singh, prime accused in the case, and Justice Nirmal Yadav, for whom the former had allegedly sent Rs 15 lakh from Delhi, are yet to be recorded.

The committee comprises Allahabad High Court Chief Justice Hemant Laxman Gokhale, J&K High Court Chief Justice K S Radhakrishnan and Delhi High Court Justice Madan B Lokur.

In a resolution passed by the General House of the Punjab and Haryana High Court Bar Association, meanwhile, it has been decided that the president and secretary of the Bar, along with Advocate Anupam Gupta, will meet the three-judge committee.

"The committee should meet those people who have important pieces of evidence in the case. But if the evidence is found to be false, action should be taken against them," said Advocate Rajiv Godara.

The Bar expressed resentment over the fact that it had not received any response from the Chief Justice of India, whose office was contacted 20 days ago for a meeting. "A delegation of the Bar will meet the CJI in his office in Delhi," said Advocate Rupinder S Khosla, president of the Bar association.

The Bar has also decided to meet the Union Law Minister in this regard.

Heading: Two convicted for possession of RDX - Indian Express
Content:
A criminal contempt petition has been filed by the District Bar Association, Panchkula, against Haryana Advocate General, Deputy Commissioner, Superintendent of Police, Panchkula, and other office-bearers of the Advocate General office and the Panchkula Administration.

The petition is yet to come up for hearing as the High Court will decide the fate of the petition on the administrative side. The Panchkula District Bar Association has demanded initiation of criminal contempt proceedings against the Advocate General, an additional Advocate General of Haryana, DC, SP and SDO (Civil), Panchkula, accusing them of disobeying the High Court orders and demolishing sheds of Panchkula lawyers without any legal order.

The matter pertains to a dispute, which had arisen last year after a member of the District Bar, Panchkula had moved the High Court demanding demolition of a few sheds terming them as encroachments in the Panchkula District Bar. After the matter had come up for hearing before the High Court, the Panchkula Administration had demolished certain sheds after a letter was issued by the office of Advocate General, Haryana.

Terming the issuance of letter as "completely false", the Bar Association had raised hue and cry in the court.

The Bar Association, last year, had also demanded strict action against the office-bearers of the Advocate General and Panchkula authorities. "There were no orders by the High Court for demolition of sheds. A letter was got issued by the office of Advocate General by itself. This is criminal contempt of Court," said Advocate S K S Bedi, counsel representing the Panchkula Bar Association.

Surprisingly, after an application demanding action against the office bearers was filed in the High Court, the Bar member who had filed the petition withdrew it.

Suspecting foul play, the Bar Association had claimed that the member (an advocate) had withdrew his petition because he was allured by the Haryana AG office and promised that he will be made Additional Advocate General.

Subsequently, the petitioner was made the Haryana Additional Advocate General. Now, the Bar Association has filed the contempt petition demanding action against all of them including the petitioner (advocate) who had filed the petition.

Heading: Getting Personal - Indian Express
Content:
Police say accused were suspected Babbar Khalsa terrorists, but the court did not find any evidence in the submission

A local court today convicted two persons for possessing large amount of explosives under various sections of the Explosive Substances Act and the Arms Act in Chandigarh.

The two accused, Kamaljeet Singh and Paramjeet Singh, were arrested by the Chandigarh police from Kisan Bhawan in 2005. They were suspected to have been trained by Jagtar Singh Hawara, head of the Babbar Khalsa International Terrorist Group, and were allegedly preparing to be 'human bombs' to kill VIPs in Chandigarh.

The court, however, found no evidence to substantiate the allegations and they were hence acquitted under Section 121 (waging war against country).

Sources said that their arrested in 2005, the Chandigh police had recovered 450 grams of RDX, two human bomb belts, a .25 bore pistol, five cartridges and two detonators.

The police had booked them under sections 121, 121-A, 153 of the Indian Penal Code, Section 4 and 5 of the Explosive Substance Act and Section 25 of the Arms Act.

While Paramjeet was convicted under Section 4 B (II) and 5 B of Explosive Substance Act and Section 25 of the Arms Act, Kamaljeet was found guilty under Section 4 B (II) and 5 B of the Explosive Substance Act.

They were acquitted in the rest of the charges framed against them. The quantum of punishment will be announced on October 23.

Based on the statements of the security guard of Kisan Bhawan, the defence counsel said the two were not arrested from Kisan Bhawan at that time as shown by the police. The public prosecutor said the two were arrested in the early hours, so no person was present at the spot.

Both the accused belong to different villages and are not related to each other.

Heading: Cheers to good health! - Indian Express
Content:
This Diwali, you can choose to present with a personal touch

As much as we all know that a simple greeting (read SMS) would suffice, Diwali these days does come with commercial trappings. While the debate to give (or not) and receive (or not) goes on, we take a side step. Despite the gloomy economy, festivities are still in the air, the stores are decked up and so are you! Along with all of that come shopping sprees that bring in gifts for the family, friends and the corporate world too. The gifts have gone from sweets to silver, candies to champagne, juices to jewellery! While it is really easy to flit from one store to another, picking up neatly packaged hampers and Diwali 'specials', you can be a tad different this year. How's that? "By choosing to personalise a gift," shares Anaheeta Mehra, boutique manager at Mont Blanc. Inundated with corporate orders, here you can get anything from a belt to a card holder, a pen to a bracelet to even a wallet tagged with a personal note. "We personalise products like pens, card holders, bracelets by engraving initials or the first name while all the leather items are embossed. It's a huge hit," adds Mehra.

Speaking of all things personal, here's an option that will have your five-year-old thrilled. Imagine reading her a Little Mermaid story where she features in herself! "These are personalised story books. For example in the Little Mermaid your child's name is printed as part of the title and he or she features as one of the characters in the story," explains Manoj C Dayal who was in the city recently to introduce 'My Personalized Mall'. "We work through our website www.mypersonalizedmall.com and offer a gamut of personalised products like story books, key chains, pens, gift sets, photo mugs, plates, mouse pads, T-shirts, magnets et al," Dayal informs. Another new addition here are the DVD comic movies that can actually have your child star as the hero. "All we need is a photograph and your child can be Spiderman," smiles Dayal. And how much does the special something cost? "The story tale book for instance is yours for as little as Rs 349."

Given the fact that you are making efforts to keep the Diwali gift special, you can try and work out a list depending upon people's interests. "And if you know their colours, it's even better," smiles Kamal Grewal, one of the city's best "linen-designers" (if we can call her that!). This Diwali, Grewal has a new addition to her specialised linen collection. "It's about coordinated dining sets," mentions Kamal as we eye four arrangements. So if you know your friend has a dinner set in blue and green with no linen to match, Grewal comes to the rescue. "Using the colours of the plate, I design matching table mats, tissue napkins complete with holders and even tablecloths if the budget is magnanimous," says Kamal who works out of her studio in Sector 8.

Speaking of specials, one of the safest bets is chocolates. With everyone around shedding the kilos, skip the mithai for customised chocolates and there are plenty of options. Mohali's Rameet Bakshi who has been dishing out chocolates under her label 'Crown Chocolates' and has a delicious lineup. "You can choose your flavours and the look, we'll personalise it to the T," mentions Bakshi. If you are looking for corporate specials, head to the Taj where you can choose from three box sizes varying from 12 pieces to 32 pieces. Prices start at Rs 200 (excluding taxes) for 12 pieces. Go on, take your pick.

Heading: The natural way - Indian Express
Content:
People choosing to drink must realize that there will always be some risk to their health & social well-being, warns DR DEEPINDER SINGH

Due to the different ways that alcohol can affect people, there is no amount of alcohol that can be said to be safe for everyone. For instance, no amount can be safe while driving. People choosing to drink must realize that there will always be some risk to their health and social well-being. The more alcohol consumed, the higher the risk. Alcoholism is a state of dependency upon alcohol in which drinking is out of control. WHO defines alcoholics as excessive drinkers whose dependency on alcohol has attained such a degree that it shows a notable mental disturbance or interference with physical and mental health, their interpersonal relationships and smooth social and economical functioning. It is not that all heavy social drinkers suffer from the disease called alcoholism, but a large number of such habitual drinkers suffer physically, mentally, emotionally and socially at any time of their life.

Affects of Alcohol

Alcohol affects frontal lobes of the brain, the seat of inhibition, reasoning powers, memory and judgment. It affects cerebellum, the seat of motor muscle control and five senses. And finally it affects the spinal cord and medulla, the seat of involuntary functions such as breathing, heart beat and body temperature control.

How to be safe?

* Drink plenty of water, especially when you're drinking. This will ensure your body doesn't dry out too badly.

* Eat something before you drink and your body will be better equipped to soak up the stuff. Go for food that takes a long time to digest, such as bread, cheese, potato and pasta, as this will line your stomach.

* Try not to mix your drinks, because you're only adding to the number of toxins that your body has to deal with.

* Try turning to the bar or party later than usual, to minimize your drinking time, or kick off with a soft drink so that you stop feeling thirsty.

* You should have at least, two drink-free days a week.

* Binge drinking is dangerous, as your body can only process one unit of alcohol per hour.

If you find yourself drifting towards alcohol dependence, three legs of tripod on which you have to work are insight, motivation and abstinence. All you need to have is a change in philosophy, firm commitment and take the first step. Lao-tse said, "the journey of thousand miles begins with one step." Why wait for a non-starter like NEW YEAR RESOLUTIONS. It can take place only NOW.

The writer is a lifestyle counsellor, Fortis Hospital, Mohali
