Heading: Chill! - Indian Express
Content:
Australian experts suggest regular exercise to prevent osteoporosis

In a bid to help osteoporosis patients to improve their bone and muscle strength, Australian experts have suggested brisk walking, jogging and weight training as the most effective forms of exercise. Experts on World Osteoporosis Day said regular exercise can reduce osteoporosis related fracture risk by up to 50 per cent. It is estimated that one in two women and one in three men over the age of 60 in Australia will suffer a fracture related to osteoporosis.

"Osteoporosis places a huge burden, both physically and financially, on the individual and the general community, and research shows that the rate of osteoporotic fractures is significantly increasing, particularly with our ageing population," head of Osteoporosis Australia Judy Stenmark said. "Exercises should target the main muscle groups, such as the arm muscles (biceps and triceps), upper torso muscles, lower abdomen muscles, muscles around the hip, thigh muscles (quadriceps and hamstrings) and calf muscles," guide co-author Maria Fiatarone Singh said.

"The most effective activities progress in difficulty and always challenge different muscle groups. The best activities for great bone health are those done in rapid, short bursts of high intensity such as brisk walking, jogging and weight training," Maria added.

Heading: Disadvantage India ! - Indian Express
Content:
Scientists create 'the world's most relaxing room'

Scientists have created "the world's most relaxing room", a large-scale multi-media space they claim aims to calm even the most stressed out of minds. According to them, the room will help motivate different groups of people to combat stress, including, for example, students facing exams and businesses wishing to lower their employees' stress-related absenteeism. Prof Richard Wiseman, who led the team at University of Hertfordshire, said: "The pace of modern-day life, credit crunch, and financial crisis is making many people feel very stressed and so we have created this space to help them relax. "Research suggests that the subdued green light enhances the production of dopamine in the brain and provide a calming sensation. "And, in addition, the artificial blue sky helps create a mild form of sensory deprivation that will help them turn their attention inward and distract them away from daily stress." In each 15-minute session, people will be bathed in a calming glade-like green light, listen to a specially composed soothing sound track, and look at a completely clear artificial blue sky, the 'ScienceDaily' reported. The music that will be played features a solo soprano voice, chosen for the soothing properties of the human voice, together with a Tibetan singing bowl, used in meditation and a string ensemble.

Heading: Live Wire - Indian Express
Content:
DR ARUN KOCHAR finds that heart disease has a racial discriminatory bias, geographically

Heart disease is number one killer of mankind across the globe, albeit with geographical and racial inconsistency. It has been noticed that race and ethnicity do play a role in heart disease prevalence and some groups of people are at increased risk for heart disease and many do not respond well to certain treatments. Ppeople of Indian ethnicity have the highest rates of heart disease in the world, despite coming from a culture that shuns smoking, encourages a vegetarian diet and lacks many of the classic risk factors for the disease. According to new research, India could account for 60 per cent of heart disease cases worldwide in coming years and this will signify a huge burden on national healthcare amenities.

MECHANISM OF DISPARITY

Racial disparity of heart disease prevalence has been noticed in Indians living elsewhere also. The rate of heart disease is 40 per cent higher in Indians than that among the rest of Britain's population. In Trinidad, Indians have double the national average for heart disease, and in Singapore the risk for Indians is nearly four times than that of natives. In fact, scientific observation had been that certain races are more disposed to heart disease, obesity and diabetes than others. As a group, death rates of heart disease in African-Americans are 40 per cent higher than those of Caucasians. A low incidence of heart disease has been noticed among Mediterranean countries. Thus heart disease does have a racial discriminatory bias geographically.

Reasons for this Indian incongruence are uncertain, but scientists do believe that genetically our genes had probably over the years become programmed to be energy miser and thrifty so as to enhance metabolic efficiency and fat storage. Known as "thrifty gene hypothesis" this assumption attempts to explain our evolutionary development as a possible reason. Indians for a long time during the prehistoric times were subjected to extended periods of famine and starvations. These modified thrifty genes helped the body overcome the fasting times by using stored food deposited during feasting times, same as camel uses energy in his hump to cross the desert. But with modern times when food is always and easily available, thrifty genes are still operational and poor Indians are still storing fats around their waist for probable, prospective never-to-occur famine.

Another school of thought blames low foetal birth weight as possible mechanism for unusually high incidence of heart disease. The followers of this supposition believe that seeds of unhealthiness are sowed in the mother's womb itself leading to development heart disease in adulthood.

LIVING WITH FLAWED GENES

It is difficult to cope with preordained future, but the least we could do is to look after modifiable risk factors. Abstaining from smoking and alcohol, exercising regularly, looking after our blood pressure and diabetes, visiting our cardiologist periodically, eating sensibly, avoiding excess calories and avoid becoming overweight are some of the wiles to overcome this peril.

The writer is an interventional senior consultant cardiologist working at Fortis hospital, Mohali

Heading: Fear Factor - Indian Express
Content:
Actress Rituparna Sengupta is eyeing the stars in Bollywood

Bollywood might be warming up to her, but back home, in Bengal, Rituparna Sengupta is a superstar, which also translates into the lady being a critically acclaimed actress. Active in the field of arts - she's a painter, dancer, dabbles in handicrafts and writes occasionally, Rituparna, in the Hindi world, is best known as the beautiful wife of Rajpal Yadav in Main, Meri Patni Aur Woh. When she's not acting, the actress is busy with the world of sports and children suffering from thalassaemia. Here's a quick Q&A with her.

Ques* Do you still take yourself as an outsider in this industry?

No. There were teething problems, but I've settled in...I guess it took me time to understand the difference between Kolkata and Mumbai industries. I am a brand over there and I want the same status here too.

Ques* A brand name in Mumbai too?

Absolutely. People in Kolkata know me well for both commercial and art cinema. I want to attain the same status here and I believe I can get it by a combination of my approach towards both commercial films as well as art films. I am trying my best.

Ques* You did your first film in Hindi 'Main Meri Patni Aur Woh' almost four years back and still you are struggling for your recognition. What do you think is the reason?

I chose the right film, but it's not my fault that it didn't work at the box office. Similarly, take for example, Gauri The Unborn, which is based on the contemporary topic of abortion or Sirf Life is Greener on the Other Side. Both the films had stars like Atul Kulkarni, Manisha Koirala, Kay Kay Menon, Nauhid Cyrusi, Ranvir Shorey, Sonali Kulkarni, Parvin Dabas, still these didn't appeal to the audience, so it's just luck. I think I have to be doubly cautious in choosing films!

Ques* Don't you ever think that despite being a National Award winner, you are wasting your energy in striving for a good role in Bollywood!

No, I don't think that I am wasting my energy but I surely feel bad. Again, such thoughts are temporary, I understand that success is the aftermath of struggle and it becomes ephemeral for people who get it easily.

Ques* Most of your films show the problems with women. Is it merely a co-incident?

Even I don't know it! Maybe my directors feel that I can portray such characters better. It's not the case with Mumbai, this Bengali film, Trishna that I'm doing now has me portraying several shades.

Ques* Item songs are quite an easy way to get a place in Bollywood. Why didn't you try for any such number yet?

Because no one has yet offered me one! If offered, I'll definitely do an item number. I don't think there is anything wrong in it.

Ques* Have you marked any limit beyond which you won't go for any character?

There are always lines which are never meant to be crossed. I accept only those characters that appeal to me the most and can satisfy the actor in me. I am not like other heroines who throw tantrums or make a fuss about the kissing or bikini act.

Ques* It's very natural phenomena that audiences take actresses like goddesses. Don't you think that showing skin can hurt their feelings?

I am open to any kind of criticism if they feel like. Criticism is good because it helps finding the faults in me.

Ques* Which will be the recent release among your films?

It's Warner Brothers' SRK which is directed by Ajay Verma. It's an emotional comedy. I am playing my best ever character in this film named Vidya. There's Vinay Pathak with me, Illaya Raja has given the music and Gulzar has penned the lyrics.

Ques* What does SRK stand for?

That's a secret.

Ques* Tell us about your forthcoming films.

There's Karan Razdan's 'Mittal Versus Mittal' based on marital rape, Anjan Dutta's political thriller 'BBD', 'Main Osama' where I play an air hostess, 'Saab Chai Pani', 'Paroksh' has me as an ambitious corporate woman, 'Love Khichdi' and 'Dard-E-Disco' are comedies, and besides this, there are Bengali films including Suman Mukherjee's 'Chaturango'. It's based on a novel by Rabindranath Tagore.

Heading: On song - Indian Express
Content: Now this is something which a Bond Girl is not expected to reveal, but Ukrainian born actress, former model and now the Bond Girl in upcoming 007 film, Olga Kurylenko, confesses that she is afraid of heights. Olga is the new Bond girl who casts opposite Daniel Craig, the James Bond in Quantum of Solace (QOS), which releases this November, 7. "Yes, I don't like heights and I am an acrophobic" she admits. Olga embarked on an epic adventure which took her to far flung parts of the globe including Panama and Chile for the shoot of QOS. "I was scared, but I did it, and that's one of the great things about this job, in particular working on a Bond movie. You get to do so many different things. Where else are you going to get the chance to work through your fear like that? You have to do it, you have to jump off the roof and there's no choice. I was so proud of myself when I did it. It was a big thing for me and thereafter it was like 'wow, I did it!' You feel such a sense of achievement," she smiles. Her character, Camille, "is very strong and very determined," says Olga. "Independent and very feisty, she's almost like a female version of Bond. She's vengeful and was really a great character to play," she's learnt how to fight, how to shoot, how to fly and how to strip a gun.

Heading: Speed Zeal! - Indian Express
Content:
Television king Gajendrra Singh moves on to movies

The journey for Saibaba Telefilms started in 2006. Since then they have produced hit music reality shows and now the man behind it all, director Gajendrra Singh has announced his company's venture into Bollywood. With several plans to grow, it has stepped forward with an aim to reach the regional audience with its expertise in music reality shows and fiction series for the masses. Along with spreading its wings the company has unveiled its new logo and website. A dream project of the firm has finally been outlined with its first movie, Yaari Motor Company (YMC). The movie will be directed by very well known Shivaji Satam's son, Abhijeet Satam. The music being the soul of a movie and an ace music director duo are being roped in for the same. YMC is a story about four final year students, their geniuses, friendship, aspirations and the motorcycle. The second movie project Gulnar, to be directed by Gajendrra Siingh, talks about the Indo-Pak relationship and will take off by end of next year. "For many years I've wanted to make a romantic film on Indo- Pak ties. Our films have gone into Indo-Pak relations but none has taken a detached view of the matter. With Gulnar, I hope to change that. Movies are the big leap for us and we hope to reach audience's expectations by creating remarkable cinema," spoke Singh.

Heading: Admn makes ample parking space mandatory in buildings - Indian Express
Content:
Chitkara students are all set to vrroom into SAE-A in Australia

They love the road and will do anything for the thrill that set their pulses racing...anything, even if it means designing an all new car! But then it's all for the love of the road. If you know the feel of that then you will identify with the urge that drew these students of Chitkara Institute of Engineering and Information Technology to spend more than a year to put together TAZZ- a formula student car.

Christened after 'torque accelerated zoom', the vehicle is almost ready for a take off once the body is mounted. "We have designed the car to compete at Formula SAE-A in Australia next month," shares Raghav Thapar, a team member adding that only four other teams from the country are participating in the competition that will judge the vehicles on the static and dynamic basis. The team, led by Gurpinder Singh Virk, also comprises Ankur Kataria, Akhil Goyal, Akhil Mahajan, Mohit Bhola, Bharat Bhushan Kansal, Manik Jain, Sanmeet Singh Thapar and Aditya Sharma. The faculty advisor of the team is Ravinder Pal Singh and they got technical assistance from Ranjit Singh Randhawa, an automotive expert in Kharar and Ashish Bhatia of Grace Automotives, Chandigarh.

Capable of running at a speed of 200 km per hour the car has a modified V4 592cc engine. Team leader, Gurpinder Virk informs, "We have modified the engine as per rules supplied by the competition organizers. The frame of the car has been developed by using stainless steel pipes. It has hydraulic disc brakes and double wishbone suspension system. The body work of the car is under process and before going to Australia, we are going have a nation wide media launch in beginning of November." The car is presently sponsored by Bridgestone, while technical sponsorships have come from Grace Automotives and Cheema Boilers Limited. Chitkara Director, Madhu Chitkara has funded the team with about six lakhs. The total cost of the project is around 20 lakhs. Amidst the knowledge that Australian and older teams will have an edge, their hopes are high. "We are giving it our best shot and hope to race to victory!"

Heading: First in state: Model police station opens in Shahkot - Indian Express
Content:
Issues orders pertaining to parking norms for several categories of plots and sites, exempts multi-level parking from FAR, allows parking in basement of school sites

Making it mandatory to have a provision for ample parking space, UT Chief Administrator Sanjay Kumar has issued orders pertaining to the parking norms for commercial and residential areas, malls, multiplexes and other categories of plots and sites. The Administration has allowed multi-level parking above the ground level, which will be

free from the floor-area-ratio (FAR) norms. 

The footprint (ground floor) of a separate parking block on the same premises, however, will be counted up to 50 per cent of the ground coverage permissible. The block won't be allowed for purposes other than parking, driver's rest room with toilet, a toll centre and any other facility that is essential for parking, with a condition that these facilities will not exceed 150 square metres per 1,000 ECS (equivalent car space) of parking space or in multiples of that.

Other parameters, such as ground coverage and height for such parking lots, will be governed by the existing rules for any other multi-level building. Norms for multi-level mechanical parking will be decided on case-to-case basis.

There are more than 7.7 lakh motor vehicles, including four-wheelers and two-wheelers, registered in Chandigarh. According to the statistics maintained by the UT Registering and Licensing Authority, on an average 37 four-wheelers and 50-odd two-wheelers are registered in Chandigarh every day.

Roads in the city remain clogged throughout the day and have even started succumbing to the pressure of traffic. While residents find no place to park their vehicles at any market, mall and shopping area, particularly during the peak hours, it is nothing short of a challenge for the Administration to carve out new parking lots. Recently, four lots were identified in Sector 17 and constructions started for accommodating around 200 to 300

vehicles.

According to the orders issued on Tuesday, all residential buildings on a one-kanal site or above will have parking facilities equivalent to one ECS per floor and further subject to the condition that adequate parking is planned to ensure no vehicle is parked outside the premises.

Heading: Moga village takes shine to CFL, shows the way - Indian Express
Content:
Director General of Punjab Police NPS Aulakh today inaugurated state's first model police station.

Announcing that more such police stations would be opened, the DGP said these would increase accountability of officials, while the quick response system would help in checking the crime rate.

He ruled out the possibility of revival of terrorism in the state. While commenting on the recent diamond robbery case, he said efforts were on to arrest the accused and nobody would be spared. The station would have many new features, including effective beat system, reception-cum-single-window information system, on-the-spot registration, computerised complaint filing system, status of complaints, and passport and arms licence verifications.

The station would be eco-friendly with rain harvesting system.

Meanwhile, the station received two complaints on the first day from Chakchela and Rame villages and immediate directions were given to solve them.

Tributes paid to police martyrs

AMRITSAR: The district police held a commemoration day parade to pay homage to police personnel who laid down their lives at Hot Spring in Ladakh while patrolling during an attack by the Chinese Army on October 21, 1959, and also those who died in harness. A two-minute silence was observed and policemen reversed their arms in the memory of martyrs. Health Minister Laxmi Kanta Chawla, who presided over the event, inaugurated the Martyrs Memorial at Police Lines and laid a wreath. Chawla assured full co-operation to the families of martyrs. Heading: Badal visits ADC Kirpal’s family, assures help - Indian Express
Content:
This is called an electrifying makeover. After a seminar on energy conservation organised by the PSEB last week, out of 177 houses in this village, 150 have switched over to compact fluorescent lamps (CFLs). The rest will change to the energy saving option this week.

Surjit Singh, a villager, says, "I have got all the 13 bulbs in my house changed, they were of average 80-100 watts and have been replaced with 15-watt CFLs. PSEB team has assured me that my bill will reduce drastically, besides I will be doing my bit in energy conservation."

Manjit Kaur, a housewife, says, "I changed five bulbs in my house. But I will be convinced only after seeing the power bill."

Lakhbir Singh, an electrician of this village who seems to be the opinion leader, says, "I had changed a few 200-watt bulbs in my house six months ago and my bill reduced to half. Now, I have changed another nine bulbs and am expecting more reduction in the bill."

Rajbir Singh Deol of Arpan Electricals, who is providing CFLs to villagers, says, "We are selling lamps at a subsidised rate; for three lights, we charge Rs 230, while SC families get them in Rs 150. A normal bulb costs between Rs 10 and Rs 15 as against Rs 77 of CFL, but people have become farsighted."

Rajbir claims that this week he will be going to Chandigarh to change all the bulbs at the residence of Power Secretary Suresh Kumar and PSEB Chairman YS Ratra, and then at the Power Colony in Patiala.

SDO Bakshish Singh says, "If on an average every house uses 80-watt bulb in whole village for eight hours, the energy consumed in two months is 23,040 KWs, while with 15-watt CFLs, only 4,320 KW will be consumed, thus 81.25 per cent of the energy is saved. After houses, we will change bulbs of tubewell motors as well."

Charatsinghwala has been chosen out of total 12,188 villages of Punjab for this project, say officials.

Pawan Kumar Bansal, Director, Energy Conservation, PSEB, says, "We have 45 lakh consumers in Punjab and if all change at least five bulbs to CFL, we can save 600 MWs of power. Besides, Punjab has 10 lakh tubewells and if two CFLs are replaced on each tubewell, 150 MWs can be saved."

The PSEB authorities have appealed to consumers to gift CFLs on this Diwali.

Heading: Sampla is head of Khadi Board - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal today visited the bereaved family of PCS officer and ADC of Tarn Taran Kirpal Singh, who died of kidney failure on Sunday.

The CM, who spent about half an hour with the family, promised all possible help in getting a suitable government job for his child or wife. Harvinderpal Kaur, wife of the deceased, blamed some top functionaries of the government for playing a partisan role during the kidney donation controversy, leading to the death of her husband.

She also blamed the media for sensationalising the controversy. She said she has apprised the CM of the circumstances that led to the death of the officer and the bureaucratic and legal hassles. Badal said, "Any of the two children of the ADC, on becoming eligible, will be given a job and even if officer's wife wants, we can help her in getting a job."

Heading: Punjab to float Rs 500-cr loan - Indian Express
Content:
Vice-President of the Punjab BJP Vijay Sampla took over as the new chairman of the Punjab Khadi and Village Industry Board here this afternoon. BJP cabinet ministers, parliamentary secretaries and MLAs among other party colleagues attended the installation ceremony.

A Dalit face of the party who rose to prominence owing to his role during Talhan agitation in Doaba, Sampla has remained the general secretary of the BJP twice and had held the charge of president of the SC Cell of the state unit. Cabinet ministers, Manoranjan Kalia, Chaudhary Swarna Ram and Tikshan Sud, were present on the occasion. Chief Parliamentary Secretaries Jagdish Sawhney, Sukhpal Singh Nannu, chairman of Punjab Infotech Harjit Singh Grewal and member of the national youth executive of the party, Vineet Joshi, also attended the ceremony.

Heading: Lakhowal meets Union agri secy - Indian Express
Content: As part of fiscal management to run the state grappling with resource crunch, the Punjab government today floated a Rs 500-crore loan to partially finance the capital expenditure incurred on plan schemes and other such development initiatives. The state government has already mounted its debt by over Rs 2,500 crore ever since it came to power. According to an official spokesperson, the state government has notified the sale of Punjab Government Stock (Securities) of 10-year tenure for an aggregate amount of Rs 500 crore. The Centre has accorded its consent to the plan. The government stock would be auctioned from the RBI's Mumbai office tomorrow.

Heading: Badal worried over days of Raj in Maharashtra - Indian Express
Content: Punjab Mandi Board chairman Ajmer Singh Lakhowal met Union Agriculture Secretary T. Nanadkumar to apprise him of the problems of paddy and cotton in Punjab. He said CCI has not entered 14 markets and farmers were selling their produce below the MSP to private purchasers. He said late sowing of paddy and inclement weather had led to high moisture content and discolouration of the grain. The government should look into the problem.

Heading: Major breach inundates over 100 acres - Indian Express
Content:
Guruta Gaddi Diwas: Flags-off NRIs' nagar kirtan

Expressing concerns over the rising incidents of regionalism in the wake Raj Thackeray's Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) unleashing violence on "outsiders", Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal today said this trend was dangerous for national integrity.

He said both the state and Central governments were responsible for such acts of violence, as they had given a free hand to Raj and his men.

Badal flagged-off a nagar kirtan of NRIs to Nanded in Maharashtra to take part in the Guruta Diwas celebrations to be held on October 30 as per the Bikrami Calendar. The procession, comprising dozens of buses, will reach Nanded on October 28 and 29.

"I can only request Raj to restrain from violence as it will serve no purpose. Any grudge that he has can be peacefully redressed," said Badal.

Earlier, he arrived at the Akal Takht and addressed a gathering, where Jathedar Giani Gurbachan Singh and jathedars of other Takhts and Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee head Avtar Singh Makkar were also present. Damdami Taksal chief Harnam Singh Khalsa had invited NRIs to take part in the celebrations.

Badal said Guru Granth Sahib was most relevant today, when individualism was ruling the nation. "The Guru Granth Sahib is not just the Guru of Sikhs, but of the whole mankind," he said, adding that there was nothing wrong if Sachkhand Hazoor Sahib was celebrating the event 10 days later.

On the preparedness for the parliamentary polls, Badal said the Congress-led UPA would be routed.

Heading: Paddy procurement not up to the mark, says Khangura - Indian Express
Content:
Days before work was to begin on the Raunta distributary to increase its capacity by 20 per cent, a major breach of 145 feet on one side and 110 feet on the other occurred near Bajakhana in the wee hours today, affecting more than 100 acres.

While at some places, the paddy has been harvested, at others standing crop was inundated.

On August 14 last, SAD (B) president and MP Sukhbir Badal had laid the foundation stone for increasing the capacity of the distributary to 300 cusecs from the current maximum level of 243 cusecs at a cost of about Rs 7 crore.

Interestingly, the foundation stone laid by Sukhbir stands at a stone's throw from the breach.

When the breach occurred, only 100 cusecs of water was flowing in the distributary, said an official of the Irrigation Department, who was at the spot today, when efforts were being made to plug the breach that occurred towards the tail side. According to department's Junior Engineer Baldev Singh, the project envisaged raising the distributary banks to a height of one foot on each side. He added that repair works, wherever needed, were also part of the project.

"The foundation stone might have highlighted the capacity part only, but the project also includes rehabilitation and strengthening of the distributary," said Irrigation Department Executive Engineer HS Cheema, adding that the work, which had been allotted to contractors early this month, would commence in 10 days.

Heading: Mann raps attack on minorities - Indian Express
Content:
Congress MLA from Qila Raipur Jasbir Singh Khangura lamented that farmers in Punjab had to wait for nearly eight days for their harvest to be procured in mandis. Khangura said he visited mandis in his constituency only to notice lacunae in the procurement process.

In a letter to Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal, he said, "It is regrettable that the government has failed to plan effectively for the procurement. Deputing principal secretaries to the districts to resolve issues shows that the administration has failed to get its act together."

Khangura alleged, "Not even the best of public relations can gloss over the gaping holes in the working of the administration."

Heading: Decade after murder, banker’s family still awaits justice - Indian Express
Content:
Seeking the intervention of the Akal Takht on the issue of attacks on minorities in the country, SAD (A) president Simranjit Singh Mann on Tuesday held a protest march along with the representatives of the Anglican Church of India and Diocese of Amritsar to condemn violence against Christians. Mann lambasted the SAD (B) for an alliance with the BJP which was behind attacks.

"It is high time that the Akal Takht Jathedar intervened, as Sikhs too are a minority community," he said. Mann also sent a memorandum to the Prime Minister through the Deputy Commissioner, in which he charged BJP Lok Sabha MP Navjot Singh Sidhu with leading an attack on Khairdin Mosque in Hall Bazaar in August. He has demanded a ban on BJP, Bajrang Dal, Shiv Sena, RSS and VHP.

Heading: Time is not ripe to step up campaign against govt: Capt - Indian Express
Content:
A decade has passed since the murder of Naresh Mahajan, a bank manager with Oriental Bank of Commerce who was killed under mysterious circumstances on October 22, 1998, but his family still awaits justice. Unhappy with the functioning of the CBI, which is investigating the case, Mahajan's family has sought its transfer from the Chandigarh to some other unit.

In a letter to the Joint Director of CBI, Puneet Mahajan, a relative of Naresh, seeking re-investigation, said after the initial zeal, the Chandigarh unit lost interest in the case and the investigation was very "casual". "Within a short span of 10 months, the Chandigarh unit filed the closure report twice in the CBI special court in Patiala," Puneet said.

S C Mahajan, brother of the deceased, accused the Chandigarh unit of CBI of not following the directions of the Punjab and Haryana High Court. "As per the directions, investigations have to be conducted by an official not below the rank of SP, but the second closure report was filed on the basis of the probe by an inspector-rank official," he said. The body of Naresh was found in his car, abandoned in Ranjit Avenue. Though initially the police reported it to be a case of suicide, Mahajan's family had suspected it to be a case of murder, following which the police registered a case of murder. As per investigations, involvement of certain persons working in close liaison with Mahajan in the running of a 'parallel banking operation' was suspected. The family had also named some persons, including Mahajan's colleagues, as suspects. Meanwhile, none of the CBI officials could be contacted despite repeated attempts.

Heading: Una SEZ: NGO to submit report to CM - Indian Express
Content:
Former CM Capt Amarinder Singh today termed the one-and-a-half-year tenure of SAD-BJP government as "zero credibility period" and said that the time was not right to step up the campaign against the state government.

"There are enough loopholes of the government which we will be exposed one by one, but the peak time for election campaigning has not come," he said. Amarinder, who was here to conduct a meeting of party workers, said he expected that the Lok Sabha elections would be held after March next, once the elections to some state assemblies were over.

He claimed the Congress would make a clean sweep in CM Parkash Singh Badal's Bathinda belt and indicated that his son, Raninder, was also likely to throw in his hat from the region.

Ironically, he swiped at Sukhbir Badal, saying that the state administration was confused about who the real leader was. "It's a family show at the moment with record-breaking corruption at all levels," he alleged. He termed the government's policies as anti-investment and because of bad management by the Badals, investment worth Rs 1,67,000 crore brought in by the previous government had come to a naught. "A number of units are moving out of the state because of the anti-industry policies of the government, at a time when neighbouring states are providing lucrative tax benefits," he added.

Officials at every level, from IAS officers to constables, were under pressure, which was hampering the quality of work, he alleged.

'Politician-agency nexus causing delay in procurement'

Captain Amarinder Singh also visited Khanna and Doraha mandis to witness the process of paddy procurement. He said the bonus of Rs 50 was not enough and the matter had already been taken up with Sonia Gandhi. For the reported delay in procurement, he cited a nexus between former SAD MLAs and the government agencies as the reason. He said the same had happened in the past when these leaders, who were professional arhtiyas, did not allow agencies to pick up paddy from mandis and later purchased the same at lesser rates from farmers and sold it at high rates to the agencies. According to him, moisture was not such a major problem in mandis of the region but the food supply inspectors were harassing farmers.

Heading: VB registers FIR in bitumen supply scam - Indian Express
Content:
People's opposition against the proposed SEZ at Gagret in Una district has received the backing of NGOs, who have initiated a debate over the good and bad affects of the SEZ. In this line, Himalaya Neeti Abhiyan is preparing a detailed report on the factors that would affect the people's livelihood in the rich agricultural belt of the district. The report would be submitted to Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal.

Guman Singh of Himalaya Neeti Abhiyan says the protest has to be backed by solid logic, for which a detailed survey of people who are likely to be affected and those who back the idea of setting up the SEZ was done.

Discussing the preliminary findings, Singh said, "As per a survey of the area, measuring 32 square kilometres, the land of 23 of the 26 villages of Gagret block would be used up, displacing a population of 60,000 people." Another question is that the people would lose rights over the common land that is used as grazing ground for cattle, as even that would be acquired. He questioned that even if the people are rehabilitated nearby, would they be able to carry on with their agriculture and animal husbandry activities in the same manner.

"Since it does not seem possible, will the state be able to get them employment in industries, given the fact that under the SEZ Act, the state government cannot enforce the condition of 70 per cent employment to locals," he said.

Meanwhile, the Una district administration has agreed to fulfill the people's demand of demarcation of the SEZ area once again in public view. Una Deputy Commissioner Padam Singh Chauhan said, "I have ordered the District Revenue Officer to address the apprehensions of people about misrepresentation of the actual area to be covered under the proposed SEZ in Gagret. He would soon carry out demarcation of the area in presence of the public."

Heading: Workers’ strike hits work at Solan, Barotiwala units - Indian Express
Content:
The state Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau today registered a case in the bitumen supply scam of 2007-08, which is expected to run into several crores. The FIR in the scam has been registered against officials of the Public Works Department (PWD) and Chandigarh-based transporter company M.K. Enterprises, who have come under the scanner for their involvement in the scam.

Though the scam pertains to the entire state, the first case has been registered for Una district, where a supply order of about 900 bitumen drums worth Rs 35 lakh went missing on the way to their destination.

DIG (Vigilance) Ashok Sharma confirmed that the case has been registered for cheating, forgery and criminal conspiracy. "No PWD official has been named in the FIR so far as further investigations would pinpoint the ones involved in the scam at various levels," he said. He added that the inquiries in the scam for other districts were also in process and soon a chain of separate FIRs would follow.

Him Agro Industries Corporation, which was the nodal agency for procuring supplies, had also made an aborted attempt to register an FIR against the transporter company here at Shimla East Police Station. Sharma said since the scam was already under investigation with the Vigilance, there was no need for a separate case, so it was turned down.

Sources say that later stages of investigation would involve questioning of several officials from the level of junior engineers to engineer-in-chief.

The scam pertains to supply of thousands of litres of bitumen from Panipat refineries that was inordinately delayed and in some cases went missing, whereas payment for the stock was released by the PWD before receiving the supply.

As per the tender, all supplies were to be transported within five days after which a fine of Rs 10 per day was to be imposed on transporters, but Him Agro Industries, did not take any action for the delay, though in many cases the delay was of over six months. The role of Him Agro would also be investigated.

Heading: ‘Emphasise on food quality to compete internationally’ - Indian Express
Content:
Following the indefinite strike of workers against the expulsion of some of their fellow workers and alleged violations of labour laws, production and related operations remained suspended at GMP Technical Solutions factory at Mandhala village near Barotiwala on the fifth consecutive day.

Meanwhile, the indefinite strike of employees of Himachal Futuristic Company Limited (HFCL) also entered its second day today.

The protesting workers today again staged a dharna outside the main gate of the HFCL at Chambaghat, urging the government to intervene in the issue without any further delay. The employees had gone on indefinite strike to protest against the decision of the management of the company to transfer a worker to Delhi. The management had put locks on the main gates of the factory on Monday, forcing the employees to go on strike.

Similarly, protesting workers of GMP Technical Solutions factory near Barotiwala today again staged a dharna outside the factory gate and held a rally in protest against the suspension of 11 workers and non-acceptance of their long-pending demands.

The workers of the unit had gone on indefinite strike on Friday after the management of the factory had allegedly terminated 11 workers on various charges last week. After this, the workers had pleaded the case of their fellow workers before the management. But after getting no response, the workers decided to go on strike. Besides, the workers are also demanding abolition of contract labour system in the factory.

The agitating workers alleged that despite orders of the state government, the management of the factory still employing the workers on contract basis. Even, the ESI facility was also not providing to the workers and provident fund scheme has also not been introduced to the workers by the management despite repeated assurances.

Addressing workers, leader of Indian National Trade Union Congress Shyam Thakur said that exploitation of workers will not be tolerated at any cost and the agitation would be intensified if the legitimate demands are no conceded.

He also demanded unconditional revocation of the 11 workers.

Heading: ‘Emphasise on food quality to ‘Emphasise on food quality to compete internationally’ - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to achieve growth of 15 to 20 per cent in the food processing industry in the country, experts today called upon farmers, industrialists, academicians and national agencies to work together to bring about a revolution in the industry.

Speaking on the concluding day of the two-day national seminar on Food Safety and Quality, vice-chancellor of Guru Jambheshwar University, Lt Gen D D S Sandhu (retd) said, "India has potential to become world's largest food factory and is likely to grow further. We are already ranked first in the world in terms of milk, fruits and vegetable production and rank second in the world in terms of wheat production."

Although India is one of the largest producers of many raw food materials in the world, he expressed concern over the relative under-development of Indian food industry.

Prof B S Khatkar, seminar convener and chairman, department of food technology, GJU, said Indian food industry is "a sleeping giant".

Advisor, Quality Council of India, Anil Johri said Indian food industry would have to emphasise on quality and safety to compete at the international level.

Heading: CST relief for Maruti; tax cut by 1 pc - Indian Express
Content:
Rs 2.5 lakh for kin of those who were found eligible for adjustment, but expired before they joined

The Haryana Cabinet, which met here today under the chairmanship of Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda, decided to revise its policy regarding re-employment of those employees of boards, corporations and public sector undertakings who were retrenched between March 1, 2000, and March 1, 2005.

The Cabinet decided that now Rs 2.5 lakh would also be provided to the families of those retrenched employees who were found eligible for adjustment as per the policy and were issued appointment letters, but expired before they could join.

The Cabinet also approved the proposal to amend Haryana Civil Service (Executive Branch) Rules, 2008, to make recruitment to the Haryana Civil Service (Executive Branch) and Allied Services through a common or combined examination.

The Cabinet also decided to amend the Haryana Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Backward Classes Department (Group A) Service Rules, 1998, to fill up the post of joint director from amongst the deputy directors on the basis of joint seniority.

The Cabinet gave ex-post facto approval to the announcement made by the CM on August 24 and 26 for allotment of free 100 square yard residential plots to families belonging to Backward Classes (category A) at par with the Scheduled Castes families. However, it was decided that the family should fall in the Backward Class (category A) as notified by the government, but should not be in the creamy layer.

The Cabinet decided to enhance the limit of discretionary grant of the Governor from Rs 1 crore to Rs 1.5 crore per annum from the current financial year. The proposal of development and panchayats department to amend the Business of the Haryana Government (Allocation) Rules, 1974, to provide discretionary grant of Rs 25 lakh per year to each of the chief parliamentary secretaries and parliamentary secretaries was also approved.

It was decided to enhance the house rent of chairman, Haryana Staff Selection Commission, from Rs 10,000 to Rs 15,000 per month in the event of non-allotment of a government house, thus bringing it at par with the chairmen or advisors of boards, corporations, public undertakings. The balance Rs 3,000 would be paid by the chairman.

The proposal of the Finance Department to operationalise from January 1, 2009, the New Defined Contributory Pension Scheme for the state government employees appointed in service on or after January 2006 was also approved. Similarly, the proposal of the Finance Department to amend Family Pension Scheme, 1964, was also okayed.

The policy for preferential allotment of residential plots to those domiciles of Haryana who have distinguished themselves in the fields of art, culture, social service, science and technology, judiciary, defence or sports was approved by the Cabinet.

The Cabinet approved the proposal of the gram panchayat to lease its shamlat land at Silani Kesho village measuring 23 acres and 13 marlas at a concessional rate of Rs 3 lakh per year, with a provision of 5 per cent annual increase, to Krishna Drishti Educational Society, being headed by cricketer Virender Sehwag, to set up a sports academy and a school.

OTHER CABINET DECISIONS

* Approval for inclusion of BCs in free 100 sq yard plan for SCs

* Discretionary grant of Governor enhanced. Grant for CPS/PS

* New policy for contributory pension of staff

* Amendment in VAT for interest-free loan under industrial policy

* Lease of shamlat land for Sehwag's sports academy, school

Heading: ‘2 judges were present at house where cash was delivered, why was the fact concealed?’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana Cabinet today decided to reduce rate of Central sales tax on inter-state sales of Maruti vehicles from 2 per cent to 1 per cent to provide them a level playing field in the market. Maruti Suzuki India Limited had represented that in view of general reduction in rate of Central sales tax from 3 per cent to 2 per cent with effect from April 1, 2007, the rate of Central sales tax on interstate sales be reduced. This reduction in tax in the state would be effective from November 1.

With this reduction in tax, the buyers of Maruti vehicles would benefit to the tune of Rs 140 crore for the remaining period of the current financial year. This benefit would be Rs 200 crore per annum for the subsequent years.

The Cabinet also decided to reduce rate of tax on barley sprout from 12.5 per cent to 4 per cent on the recommendation of the state-level consultative committee. The decision to reduce tax would benefit consumers to the tune of Rs 4 lakh per annum. The Cabinet also decided to reduce the rate of VAT on sale of earth-moving equipment sold to state and Central government departments and union territories, public sector undertakings and municipal bodies from 12.5 per cent to 4 per cent. With this reduction, the state exchequer would bear a burden of Rs 1 crore on the current projected sales.

Heading: No restriction on number of storeys if specified height is maintained: UT - Indian Express
Content:
CASH AT JUDGE'S DOOR:Senior Bar member says one of the judges made a 'sustained, conscious and wilful' effort to influence investigation, claims Bansal was in touch with the other judge's son

Adding new dimensions to the cash-at-judge's-door case, Advocate Anupam Gupta, who is also the senior standing counsel for the UT Administration, made certain startling revelations at the General House of the Punjab and Haryana High Court Bar Association on Tuesday.  

Gupta, who is known for being vocal on various issues, claimed that there were two judges — one a Supreme Court judge and the other a senior HC judge — present at the Sector 11 residence of the judge where a packet containing Rs 15 lakh in cash was "wrongly" delivered on August 13.

Gupta declared that Sanjeev Bansal, former Haryana additional advocate general and an accused in the case, was in constant touch with the same SC judge's son between August 14 and 16, the day the FIR in the case was registered. "As many as five calls and an SMS were exchanged between Bansal and the judge's son," he said.

"I am convinced that the packet was mistakenly delivered at the HC judge's residence in Sector 11, but why has the presence of two judges at her residence been concealed," Gupta questioned.

He alleged that the senior HC judge present there had made a "sustained, conscious and wilful" effort to obstruct and influence the investigation.

"This senior judge even made a call to the SHO concerned. No HC judge ever calls up an SHO directly. After the incident took place, records show, this judge went towards the northern sectors in Chandigarh and made a call to Bansal. He was in a state of total panic," claimed Gupta.

The advocate also accepted the demand made by an NGO that he should be examined by the CBI to find out his "interest" in the case. "I accept the challenge to be examined by the CBI. Let me state publicly that I will only be too happy to be examined. Place me in your custody, conduct lie-detector and narco-analysis tests. I assure it will be all the worse for you, not for me."

Gupta informed the General House that Jai Parkash, senior munshi of Sanjeev Bansal, was well known to Ravinder Singh, the Delhi-based businessman and alleged kingpin in the case. "This fact stands corroborated by the 222 calls made between the two in the last six and a half months," said Gupta.

Following his revelations, the Bar Association has passed a resolution, demanding that the scope of the CBI probe should be expanded.

In another resolution, the Bar criticised the "lopsided reporting" being done in the case by an English newspaper published from Chandigarh.

The association requested the editor of the daily to look into the matter. The speakers ridiculed a report published by the daily on October 19, in which the accusations levelled by an NGO against an advocate for having "vested interest" in the case was published without naming of the NGO and the advocate.

"Had this newspaper mentioned the name of the NGO, readers would have come to know about the credibility of this self-styled NGO," said Advocate Rajiv Godara.

"We also deprecate the so-called NGO which is acting at the behest of the vested interests in the judicial system and interfering in the proceedings of the High Court Bar," said Rupinder S Khosla, president of the High Court Bar Association.

Calls made between Bansal and son of SC judge, according to Gupta

August 14:4.56 pm Bansal called judge's son (127 secs)

August 14:6.39 pm Bansal to judge's son (33 seconds)

August 15:7.38 pm Judge's son to Bansal (8 seconds)

Heading: DMCH takes school initiative for safer Diwali this year - Indian Express
Content:
There will be no restriction now on the number of storeys in all buildings that have volumetric controls — already restricted height, floor-area-ratio (FAR) and ground coverage — in Chandigarh, provided a clear height is maintained as per rules. The decision was taken by UT Chief Administrator Sanjay Kumar on Tuesday.

Kumar issued detailed orders pertaining to the FAR and ground coverage guidelines for the sites that have volumetric controls. Such relaxation shall be implemented only in sectors beyond 31, as Sectors 1 to 31 are covered under the architectural control.

Talking to Newsline, Kumar said: "Such relaxations had been due for a long time now. Time had come to let people avail these, provided they do not tamper with the rules." The UT Administration also announced ground coverage, height and FAR norms for integrated projects like Medicity and Educity.

For the Rajiv Gandhi Chandigarh Technology Park (RGCTP), the Administration has allowed 40 per cent of the site coverage, allowing the built-to-suit, main campus and small campus sites to go vertical up to 74 feet and 3 inches. The floor-space-index for such sites in RGCTP has been kept at 1:50.

The existing allottees who have already raised their buildings in the RGCTP will be allowed extra space or additional volumetric control, provided they upgrade the parking facility according to the new parameters for the entire built-up area, including the existing and what has been proposed.

For all integrated residential housing schemes — a campus with a population of 6,250 (approximately 4-5 people per dwelling unit) — outside the sectoral grid of Chandigarh, the minimum area has been fixed at 25 acres, with 40 per cent of ground coverage, 2:0 FAR and 62 feet and 3 inches of height up to the parapet level. Up to 2.5 per cent of the entire area can be allowed for commercial use to meet day-to-day requirements of the residents. For commercial area, permissible ground coverage will be 30 per cent, FAR 2:0 and height 62 feet and 3 inches.

Heading: Dr Brar deposes before standing committee - Indian Express
Content:
An interactive session and hands-on workshop organised in various schools

Dayanand Medical College and Hospital (DMCH) in collaboration with Burns Association of India (Ludhiana chapter) has taken a step forward to make school children aware of fire safety during Diwali, as there is an increased risk of fire mishaps during Diwali festival, which features the use of candles, diyas and fireworks.

Diwali is thoroughly enjoyed by people of all age groups, as they love the splendor and sparkle of fireworks. All accidents due to fireworks occur as a result of carelessness, negligence and ignorance. But these can certainly be avoided by observing some very simple precautions.

A small negligence on the part of kids can turn the celebration into a mishap or personal damage. All of us enjoy the pleasure of light and sound but when disaster strikes, the injured has to bear the cross. With each passing year, incidents of fire burning during Diwali season have been accelerating at an alarming rate. During Diwali, parents need to be more cautious about children and should take necessary safety measures to avoid any accident.

An interactive session and hands-on workshop on burn-prevention during Diwali was organised in various schools like St Thomas School, Delhi Public School, BCM School and R.S Model Senior Secondary School.

Dr Sanjeev Uppal, Professor of Plastic Surgery, Department of DMCH, spoke to the students and gave tips to the students about how they should burst crackers to avoid accident. Children, usually, like to burst crackers many days before Diwali. Anaars and rockets are very dangerous and children should ignite these crackers with safety. He opined that crackers should be bursted in open space only in the presence of elders and clothing should be tight fitting preferably made of cotton.

He advised some steps to avert mishaps: a bucket full of water should be kept ready nearby which may help in dousing flames if somebody catches fire; buy fireworks from reputed manufacturers only; keep the fireworks to be used at a safer place; always use a long candle/'phooljhari' for igniting fire crackers; and keep elbow joint straight to increase the distance between the body and the crackers. In case of burns, pour a large quantity of water on the burnt area and the patient should be taken to a burns specialist or a major hospital .The students participated in the session and also asked the queries, which were answered by the doctor.

Dr Uppal also advised students to educate maximum number of people after the session. Fire is a good master when it is in our control but it becomes bad master when goes out of control, it does not identify people who come in its contact that whether he/she is a celebrity, a politician, a student, a teacher, and so on. Fire damages everything which comes in its contact. Last year, 42 cases were reported at DMC emergency on the day of Diwali. Most of them were boys and young males.

Many such sessions will be organised in coming days in different schools of Ludhiana like Kundan Vidya Mandir, DAV Public School and Sacred Heart Convent School, BRS Nagar, so that this Diwali people of Ludhiana remain safe from any accidents.

Heading: Delay in scrapping of safai workers’ panels resented - Indian Express
Content:
The Director, Students Welfare, Punjab Agricultural University, Dr Dulcha Singh Brar deposed before the standing committee inquiring into the charges of sexual harassment levelled against him by a female employee of the university.

Dr Brar, accompanied by his son, appeared before the committee on Tuesday morning. While Dr Brar did not comment on the meeting, his son, Gaurav informed, "We have asked the committee to give us some documents regarding the complaint for we have no information about what we are being inquired into. All we have is a letter asking us to come and depose before the committee." When asked if Dr Brar recorded his statement with the committee today, Gaurav said, "No, for we never knew about the complaint. So we had nothing to say on the issue."

All along the inquiry, which began around mid-September, Dr Brar has been maintaining that he has never been informed about the matter. He has been claiming that apart from this one letter asking him to meet the committee he has never received any official communication from the university on this issue.

Dr Neelam Grewal, Dean, College of Home Science, who is inquiring into the matter refused to comment on Gaurav's contention. She however remarked, "The committee is almost through with its work. Another meeting or so, and we will wind up the matter." The Dean further clarified, "One should understand the difference between a standing committee and an inquiry committee."

Notable here is that in this case, Dr Brar was the only one who was yet to be called for inquiry. The complainant and her witnesses in the case have already deposed before the committee.

However putting aside all speculations that he would not appear before the committee today, Dr Brar met the committee today morning. Dr Brar is currently on a long leave till December 31.

Heading: New dengue cases reported - Indian Express
Content:
Meeting of Safai Labour Union and Disposal Workers' Union was held in which the workers said that though the Chief Minister has made a number of announcements about dissolving Mohalla sanitation committees, but nothing concrete has been done so far.

No paper work is being done on this issue, lamented the employees. However it needs to be mentioned that a number of councillors were not in favour of dissolving these committees and hence workers were apprehending that they were causing the delay.

They also said that till now, the pending demands of jobs to the family members of dead employees, new appointments, more facilities for employees, especially the sewermen, were pending.

The employees also complained that sewermen working in zone D in wards 57, 59 and 69 have been working for more than two months but till date nine employees have not got their salaries. Employees have asked for an inquiry into this case.

Sham Lal, Ashok Kumar, Gurinder Singh, Surinder Chanalia were among those present on the occassion.

Heading: Workshop on digital production held - Indian Express
Content:
With 66 new confirmed dengue cases reported from various city hospitals, the number of confirmed dengue patients has swelled to 1,307 till now this season. Besides, as many as 319 suspected dengue cases have been reported from the city.

According to the health department, till now as many as 573 confirmed dengue cases have been reported from outside the district at the city hospitals. Of over 2,000 patients of dengue reported in the state, over 1,500 cases are claimed to be from the district.

The Health Department however, has confirmed 1,307 cases till now.

Heading: PU faces faculty crunch, blames it on lack of funds - Indian Express
Content:
Sarvaakar vision infinit (Mumbai) organised a two-day workshop on "Understanding audio-visual communication and digital production" at Desh Bhagat Institute of Management and Computer Sciences, Mandi Gobindgarh, on Monday. This event is a part of the on-going northern-India wide Media Knowledge Event Punjab Chapter.

On this occasion a journalist, writer-director from Mumbai, Utpal Amerandra Chowdhury, was the main speaker. The first day of the media workshop focussed on topics like digital technology, film and television production, and radio production etc, and the discussion was on direction, script-writing, etc. Students from media, management, information and technology, and people with a creative urge took part in the workshop.The main aim of this workshop is to create media awareness and media literacy among the people. In this workshop, convener of the workshop, Utpal Amerandra Chowdhury presented his paper on "How films are made and different skills of acting."

Heading: Guruta Gaddi Diwas celebrated - Indian Express
Content:
With almost a quarter of the academic session coming to an end, students at the UIET department of Panjab University are yet to be beneficiaries of basic facilities including faculty and infrastructure.

Around 165 seats were increased last year, but the department seems to be ailing owing to inadequate resources. Though the authorities maintain that the hiring process of faculty is on, there is still a long way to go for the department. Talking to Newsline, Prof B S Sohi, chairperson of the department said, "There is a shortage of faculty and other infrastructure facilities, however, the same is being taken care of. In all, the department is short of 35 readers and 15 lecturers. The hiring process of faculty is going on."

The department has also been in the news a number of times after students complained of the lack of facilities. Two issues demanding immediate attention of the authorities is the hiring of adequate faculty and the construction of lecture halls, according to students.

Meanwhile, it is not only the UIET department that is facing a faculty crunch. Other departments too seem to be struggling with having to make do with guest faculty in order to comply with the required work force. Be it the University Business School, the Economics department or the Mass Communication department, the absence of faculty in all these departments is being compensated by the guest faculty. Sources maintain that at present the university is short of around 250 lecturers and readers.

The authorities at the university, meanwhile, owe the faculty shortage to the lack of funds and claim that the university is in urgent need of finances. According to a university official, "The first and foremost reason for the lack of faculty is due to the shortage of funds. For hiring a faculty member, we need to take into consideration the opinion of the Finance Board and most of the times, the board insists that we hire only in dire need."

Further explaining and clarifying the university's stand, PU Registrar S S Bari said, "We have begun with the hiring process and faculty is being appointed in all departments wherever required."

Heading: CM’s media advisor hears out grievances - Indian Express
Content:
Everest Public Senior Secondary School celebrated 300 years of `Guruta Gaddi Diwas' on Tuesday. On this occasion, shabads and bhajans were recited by the students. At one point the whole school resounded with the slogans "300 sal guru de nal and waheguru ji ka khalsa, waheguru ji fateh" raised by the students.

The principal, Asha Sharma told the children about ancient Indian culture. She said that Guru Grnath Sahib Ji was an eternal guru of Sikhs. She also urged the students to follow the principles of Guru even as she distributed sweets and fruits among children and parents.

Heading: Slain cops remembered - Indian Express
Content:
Dr Daljit Singh Cheema, media advisor to CM, on Tuesday visited Ludhiana in connection with the Sangat Darshan complaints. A meeting was conducted at the Circuit House, in which all MLAs, MC officials, SDM (East and West) and area councillors took part.

In the meeting, Deputy Speaker Satpal Gosain, and SDM (East) also exchanged heated arguments on the issue of ration cards and later both were passified by Cheema. Meanwhile, Cheema drew the list of important projects and complaints which needed to be sorted out on urgent basis.

These complaints would be discussed in the October 25 meeting at Chandigarh and thereafter the new projects will start, said sources.

Heading: PU raises bar for physical education lecturers - Indian Express
Content:
To pay tributes to the policemen who had laid down their lives for the country, "Police Commemoration Day" was observed at the Police Lines here on Tuesday. SP (D) Gurmeet Singh was the chief guest on the occasion. Floral tributes were paid to the policemen of Khanna police district who were killed during the days of terrorism. The police team led by DSP (H) Raminder Singh saluted the departed souls. DSP of Payal, Ratan Singh Brar, and DSP (D) Balwinder Singh read the names of those policemen who got martyred during last year in different parts of the country. SP (D) Gurmeet Singh gave away blankets to the family members of deceased policemen. Gurmeet Singh also heard the problems being faced by the family members after the function.

Death anniversary meet of Basant Khalsa

KHANNA: Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal and president of SAD (B) Sukhbir Singh Badal will be present at the function to be organised here on Friday to pay tributes to former MP and Akali leader, late Basant Singh Khalsa on his 12th death anniversary. Besides, other cabinet ministers and leaders of SAD (B) and BJP will also attend the function, according to a release. Basant Singh Khalsa was elected MP in 1996 from Ropar constituency. His son, Bikramjeet Singh Khalsa is MLA from Khanna at present.

Heading: NSS volunteers undertake cleanliness drive on PAU campus - Indian Express
Content:
Going a step ahead authority from Panjab University has raised the bar of qualification for the lecturers for Physical education. The step has been taken by PU authorities with an aim to improve the quality of education in the campus. The authorities at the campus have gone a step ahead of National Council for Teachers Training in defining the educational qualifications for the posts of Phydsical educational lecturers.

As per National Council for Teachers Training (NCTE) an individual is eligible to be appointed as a lecturer if he/she is MA in Physical education and there is no requirement for him/her to have M.Phill degree or to have cleared NET. However the authorities at PU have decided to give first preference to the ones who have cleared NET or have an M.Phill degree. It would be only in absence of such individuals that the MA in physical education would be hired.

A committee to fix the educational qualifications for the post of Physical lecturers was formed and the decision has been the outcome of their discussion. Talking to Newsline G K Chatrath PU Fellow and a member of the committee said, "The decision has been taken by the committee keeping in mind the quality. We have gone a step ahead of NCTE in defining the educational qualifications for Physical education lecturers so that students at the campus would get quality teachers".

The relaxation of hiring MA in Physical education on temperoary basis has been made only to fill up the gap. Explaining one of the officials from the varsity said, "We donot want the students to suffer and that is why we have kept this relaxation. Though individuals with MA Physical Educatuion degree would be hired but that would be only on temporary basis".

However the decision has come as a surprise for the individuals seeking jobs in the varsity. Showing concern one of the MA physical candidate seeking job said, "The decision is not fair at all and what is the need to go ahead the decision of NCTE. If the decision is implemented it is bound to arouse criticism".

Heading: Alour college hogs limelight at PU youth festival - Indian Express
Content:
As part of the campus beautification drive, over 200 NSS volunteers from College of Agriculture and Home Science of the Punjab Agricultural University cleaned sides of the roads on the campus during their two-day regular activity camps.

According to Dr K.S. Verma, Programme Coordinator, NSS, PAU, the volunteers, both boy and girls, took keen interest and worked together in small groups with spades and khurpas and uprooted and removed the undesired growth of grass along the roads from near Kairon Kisan Ghar, Dr M.S. Randhawa Library, Student's Home and the main road leading to the Thapar Hall.

PAU Vice-Chancellor, Dr Manjit Singh Kang also joined the volunteers and worked with a spade stacking grass into small heaps. He interacted with the participating boys and girls individually and appreciated the volunteers for the noble cause they have undertaken. Programme officers, Dr T.K. Gill, Dr Sarita Saini and Sandeep Singh were also hailed for their supervision and guidance.

He said that as per the motto of NSS, the students get an opportunity to do something useful for the society. Dr Verma said that PAU NSS unit had earlier participated in several programmes of the UNO such as "Eighth millennium development goal by UNO" and 'Wake up and speak' to eliminate poverty.

Heading: Neha takes DAV-8 into the finals - Indian Express
Content:
Gobindgarh Public College, Alour (Khanna) dominated the events held during the Panjab University zonal youth festival, Ludhiana Zone-A, held at Guru Nanak National College, Doraha. The college bagged 21 positions in various competitions.

More than 12 colleges of Ludhiana, Khanna, Samrala, Doraha and Sidhsar participated in the festival.

Three items - quiz, group song and skit — of the college have been selected for participation at Inter-Zonal youth festival, which is going to be held at G.N.N. College, Doraha, from November 16 to 19, informed the principal, Dr Suresh Tandon even as he congratulated the faculty members and students on their impressive performance in the festival. He further added that this achievement of the college would inspire other students to participate in such activities.

Piara Singh Kalsi, president, GESWT, N.K. Khanna, Secretary, GESWT and Vimal Vinod Bansal, Chairman, GPC congratulated the principal, staff members and students.

The college got first positions in group song, quiz and skit. In geet, collage-making, classical dance, creative writing (poetry), histrionics, mime, knitting and mehandi, the college got second positions and in group shabad, classical vocal, clay-modelling, poster-making, rangoli, short-story writing, phulkari, cross-stitch, pakhi-making and kavishri (individual), the college got third positions.

Heading: CHA to lock horns with PSB in finals - Indian Express
Content:
DAV Senior Secondary School, Sector 8 qualified for the final by topping their three-team group A with two successive victories in the Chandigarh Senior Women Football Championship for Deepak Kapania Memorial Trophy being organised by the Chandigarh Football Association at the Sector 17 Football Stadium here today.

In their last league fixture, bolstered by a fine brace from Neha Pandey, DAV Senior Secondary School defeated Saupin School, Sector 32 by 2-0. Both goals came in the first half. DAVSSS-8 shot into the lead in the opening minute. Straight from the kick off, Neha Pandey got possession of the ball and dribbled her way into the box before stunning Saupin School defence with a fine placement.

With good speed and ball control, Neha Pandey got her second goal in the 25th minute as she capitalised on a pass received from the right flank. DAVSSS-8 were also awarded a penalty as a Saupin defender handled the ball inside the box. However, Saupin goalkeeper Osheen made a brilliant save to stop the penalty taken by Gurpreet Kaur. St Stephen's Football Club just managed to eke out a narrow 1-0 win against equally balanced Chandigarh Football Academy Coaching Centre, Sector 45.

The all important goal was scored by Shikha Sharma in the 39th minute. Maintaining their pressure, Stephen's FC were awarded a spot kick but Sikha Sharma's penalty was saved by CFA Coaching Centre custodian Jaskiran Kaur. It was St Stephen's second successive win and have brightened their chances to qualify for final as they were leading with six points.

Heading: Mahal group sweeps PAUTA elections - Indian Express
Content:
Bolstered by a fine brace from Damandeep Singh, Chandigarh Hockey Academy edged out Lucknow Hockey Academy by 2-1 in an evenly contested semi-final match to reach the final of the first Administrator's Challenge Cup Hockey Tournament for Under-17 being organised by the Chandigarh Sports Department at Sector 42 Hockey Stadium on Tuesday.

Damandeep scored in the seventh and 31st minute for CHA while Deepak Yadav pulled back one for Lucknow in the 58th minute. Meanwhile, Punjab and Sind Bank Academy scored an emphatic 5-4 victory over Surjit Hockey Academy after both the teams were locked at 1-1 till the regulation period. Chandigarh Hockey Academy will lock horns with Punjab and Sind Bank Academy for the title.

Heading: Police ask residents to become informers, keep tab on illegal activities - Indian Express
Content:
It was a battle of nerves and slim margins at the Punjab Agricultural University Teachers' Association (PAUTA) elections that ended around 8 pm today-three hours behind schedule.

After three rounds of checking and rechecking, the team led by Dr M S Mahal was declared the winner. Dr Mahal defeated his rival Dr M L Sharma by a slim margin of 45 votes. Of the 814 voters, 714 made use of their adult franchise. Dr Mahal was polled 372 votes while Dr M L Sharma got 332 votes in his favour.

Dr Baldev Singh Sohal of the Mahal group defeated Dr Harmeet Singh Khingra of the rival group by a margin of 39 votes. Dr K S Sangha was defeated by Dr Mukesh Siag by a margin of 57 votes while Dr Gurbachan Singh Saroa of the Mahal group defeated Dr Jagjit Singh Sarabha by 23 votes. Dr Romesh Chand Sharma is the new treasurer. He won by a margin of 82 votes.

Post the results, Dr M L Sharma called upon all the teachers to work together for common interests.

"The elections are over and one team had to win but now we are all one and will stand united."

Echoing the same feeling, Dr Mahal who will now head PAUTA for a year said, "We may have fought these elections as adversaries but now we are one as the main aim of both groups is the interest of the teachers."

The others elected from Mahal group includes Harpreet Singh, Kuldip Singh, Navprem Singh, M Javed, Rakesh Sharda and Inderjit Kaur all for the post of councillors.

The post of extension north has been bagged by Vipin Kumar Rampal, extension south by Mukhtiar Singh Gill, extension north by Harpal Singh Randhawa and Research South by Jitender Singh Brar.

All these are outstation posts.

Heading: Kingfog fails to catch MC’s fancy, new drug to fight dengue - Indian Express
Content:
To keep a check on gambling and illegally stocking of crackers in the densely populated areas of the city, the Ludhiana police have sought help from residents and asked them to inform about any such activity. The police have promised not to disclose the name of the informer.

"Our appeal has already started paying dividends," said SP (Detective) Gurpreet Singh Toor.

"On Tuesday, we seized over Rs 80,000 on the Jail Road. Our team from the Crime Investigation Agency (CIA) arrested nine persons who were indulging in gambling while playing cards. A resident had given us a tip-off," Toor said.

The SP Detective said that the police had resorted to such a practice as the police cannot be omnipresent.

"A neighbour is the best person to know what is going on in his adjoining house. As an ideal citizen, it is his duty also to inform the police if any illegal practice is going on in his neighbourhood," the police officer said.

Toor said that District Police Chief SSP R K Jaiswal had instructed all police officers to keep a check on the crimes like gambling and illegal manufacturing and storage of fire crackers as such crimes spiral during the festive season. "To seek public support in keeping these crimes under check, we appeal to the residents of Ludhiana to inform us about any such illegal practice going on in their area. And we promise to keep their names a top secret," he added.

The police appeal has come in the view of the recent incident when a major fire had broken out in Field Ganj on October 14. Two persons were injured in the incident.

Heading: IAS officer’s suicide shocks Khanna, the town where he grew up - Indian Express
Content:
With dengue mosquitoes gaining immunity to mosquito repellents, the Ludhiana Municipal Corporation has decided to replace Kingfog medicine with a new drug called pyrethrum.

Ludhiana Municipal Corporation Medical Officer (Health) Dr Charanjit Singh Uppal said, "We have been instructed by the Health department to replace Kingfog with pyrethrum for door-to-door spray. We have placed the orders for the new drug."

The MC has also intensified fogging operations in the city. Now, spraying is carried out bi-weekly instead of a weekly basis. Dr Uppal said,"Our daily expenditure of fogging is now around Rs 1.5 lakh, which includes cost of medicine and the cost of running it."

This will continue till the time dengue patients are pouring in the city hospitals, he claimed.

Meanwhile the monthly expenditure of 16 fogging machines is around Rs 45 lakh as against Rs 30 lakh in the previous month when MC was going slow on the fogging operations.

Despite challan, no revenue for MC

Though over 215 challans have been issued to the city residents for not following precautionary measures to control dengue, not a single person has paid the fine. Dr Uppal said, "We have started sending them court notices."

The councillors in various wards are trying to muscle in and force the MC authorities to quash these challans.

Heading: Special Olympics promise to give unique experience to special kids - Indian Express
Content:
A shock wave spread in Khanna as news of the sudden demise of senior IAS officer Avinash Singh Chhatwal poured in the city. Chhatwal belongs to Khanna and his parental house is situated at Preet Nagar where his parents and retired school teachers reside.

Chhatwal reportedly committed suicide at his official residence at Chandigarh on Monday. A 1986-batch IAS officer, he joined as SDM of Talwandi Sabo in 1988.

A product of AS Senior Secondary School in Khanna, Chatwal topped in his pre-medical exam at AS College for Boys in 1977 and joined the Government Medical College in Patiala from where he did MBBS and MS (Surgery). He served at senior posts including deputy commissioner of Gurdaspur and Sangrur, apart from being a PUDA administrator. His wife Manpreet Kaur is also a doctor and is posted at senior level in the Health department. His only daughter is also a doctor.

People from all walks of life have expressed grief over the sudden demise of Chhatwal. Khanna MLA and Parliamentary Secretary Bikramjeet Singh Khalsa said, "We have lost a true friend and an honest officer." Khalsa added, "I talked to him many times to discuss various development works in the city and he had always responded positively."

Municipal Council President Iqbal Singh Channi said, "Chhatwal was an honest officer who worked with sincerity." A family friend of Chhatwal, Dr D D Verma said, "The town has lost its real son."

Heading: Protests against MNS reaches Kolkata - Indian Express
Content:
40 mentally challenged children, who have never been to school, will get a chance to display their talent

Under the initiative of the Sarv Shiksha Abhiyan, special children who have never ever been to school will get an opportunity to participate in the Punjab State Special Olympics. The Punjab chapter of the Special Olympics Bharat (SOB) will host the 11th Punjab State Special Olympics from November 7 to 9 at Guru Nanak Public School in Sarabha Nagar.

Inclusive Education for Disabled District Coordinator Anil Sharma said, "Mentally challenged children from across the state will participate in the event. Two children (who never been to school) have been selected from each district. This way, 40 mentally challenged children from all over the state have been identified under the Sarv Shiksha Abhiyan."

Dr Ravi Bhushan, area director, SOB Punjab said, "Less than 1 per cent of special children get an opportunity to attend a school. Considering this, Special Olympics Punjab has initiated the step to train the IERTs (Inclusive Education Resource Teachers) of the Sarv Shiksha Abhiyan. The teachers are being trained under Community Coaching Training Programme. We will train the teachers as how to motivate parents of these special kids to send them to participate in the special Olympics."
