Dr Bhushan further said, "About 400 children will participate in different events including athletics and Bocci (a game meant of special children in a ground 60"X12"). This is the second time when a group of 36 special children from Pakistan will also participate. They are being accompanied by 15 coaches, 10 parents and six officers."

Heading: Buddha calls for peace as plains match hill heat - Indian Express
Content:
Trinamool Youth Congress (TMYC) activists burnt an effigy of Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray at Ganesh Talkies on Tuesday to protest against his party's anti-north Indian agitation in Mumbai.

Thackeray has been remanded in judicial custody till November 4 for his alleged involvement in the attacks on north Indian candidates appearing for the Railway Recruitment Board entrance exam for the Western region on Sunday.

The TMYC activists blocked the Ganesh Talkies crossing around 4.30 pm and raised slogans against Thackeray. Ashok Jha, general secretary of TMYC, said: "We condemn the violence against north Indian candidates. Although, Thackeray has been arrested, it is unlikely to deter the MNS and chances are that Thackeray will be released soon."

Heading: Rungta in CBI net for taking Rs 1-crore bribe - Indian Express
Content:
A bandh called by the Amra Bangalee forum in the plains added fuel to the already simmering tension in the Darjeeling Hills on Tuesday, prompting Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee to issue a statement in which he requested the people to maintain peace.

Bhattacharjee said the situation in the upper regions of the state had turned grave as the Gorkha Janmukti Morcha's (GJM) agitation for autonomy was violently being countered in the plains by different groups working out of Siliguri.

The chief minister has asked the district administration to be alert, requested the people not to be provoked and has also said the tripartite talks can skid off the track because of the escalating violence. Bhattacharjee said: "Defacing signboards of the state government, forcibly changing numberplates of vehicles in the Hills and forcing locals to wear the traditional Nepali dress have damaged the democratic environment."

On Monday, the police arrested a conflict in Siliguri when people began to crowd a vehicle that flaunted 'GL' on its numberplate. Superintendent of Police, Darjeeling, Rahul Srivastav said on Tuesday: "The vehicle's driver had stopped to ask for directions. Local youths spotted the numberplate and were about to torch the vehicle when we intervened."

The CPM, however, is not encouraging bandhs in Siliguri, having put the blame squarely on the Congress for fuelling the anti-Gorkhaland agitation. Urban Development minister Asoke Bhattacharjee said in Kolkata on Tuesday that the people of Siliguri and the Dooars would not support bandhs. The district secretary of 'Amra Bangalee', Shambu Shatrudhar, said the administration had not heeded their deadline to put right defaced signboards in the hills. "We had given them time till Monday to remove 'Gorkhaland' and put back 'West Bengal' on them," he said.

Meanwhile, GJM secretary Roshan Giri said: "We have heard the CPM's trade union body is trying to engineer an economic blockade in the hills. They are trying to create a rift between the Bengalis and the Gorkhas. We want development of all communities. Organisations like 'Amra Bangalee' largely have Bangladeshis as members."

Heading: ‘We will lie down before trucks, but not let Tatas leave’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested two persons — industrialist Kisen Kumar Rungta and advocate P Saraf — from Camac Street on Tuesday when they were allegedly taking bribe of Rs 1 crore.

The duo had allegedly promised K P Dalmia that they would get the bail of his son, Kolkata-based businessman Dinesh Dalmia, from the Supreme Court.

Dinesh, a Director of a software company M/s. DSQ Software Ltd, was arrested by the CBI on February 12, 2006 in connection with Rs 595 crore scam. A spokesperson of the Central Bureau of Investigation said: "We are interrogating the accused duo. This is probably the biggest trap we had laid in our history."

To secure the bail, Rungta and Saraf had demanded Rs 7 crore from K P Dalmia to the latter agreed to. Rungta allegedly told him that Rs 5 crore would be spent on fixing CBI officers and Rs 2 crores was his fees. Rungta demanded Rs 1 crore as his first installment.

But on Tuesday, K P Dalmia informed the anti-corruption wing of the CBI about the matter and lodged a formal complaint.

The CBI officers told Dalmia to arrange for meeting with Rungta at his office of Surya Alloy Steel Industries Private Limited on the Camac Street. As per the plan, when the duo arrived, Dalmia handed them the amount. Subsequently, plain-clothed CBI sleuths arrested Rungta and Saraf, while receiving the money.

Later, the central agency conducted raids at five other places in Kolkata, including Rungta's New Alipore residence and offices.

Heading: Bill not paid, hospital shows encephalitis-hit child the door - Indian Express
Content:
The Save Nano Committee has reacted strongly to the reports of a letter sent by Tata Motors to the West Bengal government asking it to facilitate the relocation of the Singur project.

The committee members have been holding a dharna at the gate of the Tata factory in Singur and preventing trucks laden with equipment from leaving the site.

Rajkumar Mal, joint coordinator of the committee, said, "If Tatas try to shift the machinery with the help of police, our members will lie down in front of the trucks."

Principal Secretary (Industry) Sabyasachi Sen, however, said the letter did not specifically ask for police protection for shifting the equipment. "Nearly two weeks ago, we received a letter from Tatas, in which they informed the government and the police that they were planning to move equipment from the project site," he said.

Regarding the issue of land lease in Singur to Tatas, Sen said: "The company has not specified a timeframe for shifting and both parties (state government and Tatas) haven't yet decided about the land lease. We'll come to the issue at the right time." Sources say the issue of land lease may attract controversy in future because while Tatas are now shifting the Nano plant to Gujarat, the land on which the factory was located still lies with the company.

The state government, which had earlier tried its best to keep the Nano project in the state, is now ready to provide help to the company in dismantling and relocating the factory. The Tatas, however, are facing tough resistance from pro-industry Singur locals in dismantling the small car factory.

Raj Kanojia, IG (Law & Order), said the police had not received any order from the government to provide security to the company during the transfer of equipment.

"We already have a standing force of nearly 700 policemen around the Singur plant. We have been providing security to the project since it got underway. If there is any disturbance, we will take strict action," Kanojia said.

Tata Motors spokesperson Debashis Ray refused to comment on the issue.

Heading: Transport dept to review Metro rehabilitation project - Indian Express
Content:
Bystanders, doctors help him get readmitted

It took hours and intervention from bystanders to get eight-year old Shahjehan Sheikh, suffering from encephalitis, readmitted at the NRS Medical College and Hospital after the child's mother was forced to take him out due to monetary problems.

On Tuesday afternoon, Shahjehan's mother, Sufiyan, was forced get his son discharged from the hospital, as she was unable to bear medical bills.

Shahjehan, a resident of village Chanabaj in Murshidabad district, was admitted to the hospital nine days ago. His father, a farmer, had collected money from the village to meet the medical expenses. But three days ago, he had to return to his village leaving his wife and brother, Jabbah Sheikh, behind, as the cost of the family's stay in Kolkata became unbearable.

"Shahjehan had been ill from before the Pujas but he soon recovered. When he fell ill again, he was admitted to a hospital in Behrampore for three days but the doctors advised us to move him to Kolkata," Sheikh said.

On Tuesday afternoon, they were forced to get Shahjehan discharged from the hospital, as they were unable to foot the hospital expenses.

As Shahjehan lay on the grounds within the premises of the hospital, locals and other families of patients gathered around them. On intervention by the people and other doctors who had gathered there, the medical superintendent of the hospital, Prof Lakhmi Kanta Ghosh, re-admitted the child.

"There was nothing we could have done, we had no money to meet the mounting medical expenses as my husband is a farmer and we do not have any money left," Sufiyan said. Ghosh said that he would approach the Indian Medical Association to help Shahjehan. He added that the hospital would take care of his medical bills.

Heading: Denmark group comes up with brewery unit near Nano site - Indian Express
Content:
A team from the state transport department is likely to visit B B Ganguly Street next week to assess the situation and rehabilitate the business establishments, which would be displaced by the East-West Metro rail project, transport minister Subhas Chakraborty said.

Representatives of local business organisation also urged Chakraborty to rehabilitate them so that they could run their businesses.

About 20 buildings on the B B Ganguly Street are likely to be acquired for the project. Authorities of the East-West Metro have planned to construct a station at street, which would necessitate demolition of some buildings.

The Metro authorities have decided to rehabilitate the business establishment in other parts of the city. A total of 52 shops, 85 office establishments and two godowns will be demolished. The businessmen are keen to get new shops in the same locality.

Heading: Day after hoax call, family tenders apology - Indian Express
Content:
Not far from the Tata small car factory site in Singur, a brewery with 100 per cent foreign direct investment is coming up without much hue and cry.

The Carlsberg Group of Denmark — also known as South Asia Breweries in India — has invested nearly Rs 70-80 crore in the manufacturing unit.

"At present, the distribution of beer in Kolkata is done from our Himachal Pradesh brewery. Our West Bengal unit will be ready in about six months," said Pradeep Gidwani, managing director of Carlsberg and South Asia Breweries, at the launch of the premium beer brand in Kolkata.

The Singur brewery is a joint venture of South Asia Breweries and Sri Lanka's Lion Brewery Ceylon Ltd.

The company has been marketing the product as a premium all-malt beer, which is free from adjuncts like rice or sugar, which are normally found in other brands. The company had ventured into the city about a month ago and got a good response.

"We aim to create a new brand of super-premium beer in India. Carlsberg will mainly focus on its target consumers — urban Indian males, aged 25-35 years," Gidwani said.

He added that the beer industry has become extremely competitive in India and they hope to acquire 10 per cent of the market share for mild beer in the country in the next one year.

The company already has three breweries, one each in Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh.

The next venture of the company will be to market and launch its products in north-eastern states, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Orissa.

Heading: Five from state die in Sikkim accident - Indian Express
Content:
Realising the gravity of the implication of the hoax call made to the Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose international airport on Monday, family members of Suranjana Guha apologised to the police and the members of the event management company for the harassment caused to them.

On Monday Guha's mother, Papia Guha, had allegedly made a hoax call to the domestic airport, saying the three event managers booked on the Indigo flight bound for Agartala were terrorists.

She did this after Guha was not allowed to check in with other members of a dance troupe being taken to Agartala by the event management company.

Defending Papia's act, family members of Guha said the company was responsible for her harassment, as they had not informed her that she needed to carry her identity proof.

"She reached the airport without her identity card, she was scolded and insulted, while the representatives of the event management company walked away towards the security check-in area," her family alleged.

According to them, the company could have told her to go home and fetch her identity card. They admitted that the phone call was made in the heat of the moment.

The company, however, claimed that Guha knew she had to bring her ID card and was even told to get it from home as there was ample time left for the flight to take off.

Police, in the meantime, swung into action. "This is a non-cognisable offence and as we were harassed, we have decided to move court on the basis of the general diary filed by the three members of the event management company," said a source at the airport police station.

Even the three employees of the company could move court, they said.

Heading: CID claims poaching kingpin will be arrested soon - Indian Express
Content:
Five members of two families from West Bengal, who had gone on a trip to Tsongmo lake near Gangtok in Sikkim, died in a road accident on Monday.

According to sources, the deceased were coming back to Gangtok after visiting the lake in a Tata Sumo along with six others when the driver lost control and the vehicle fell into a nearly 200-feet deep ravine.

Incidentally, six persons of another family who were travelling with the deceased had a miraculous escape. They, however, could not be contacted for comments. Sources said the five dead were seated on the back seat of the vehicle.

The Dhar family, which belongs to Madhyamgram in North 24 Parganas and the Biswas family from Haltu on the southern fringes of Kolkata, had toured many places together in the past.

On Monday, when the trip was planned to Tsongmo lake, Dipali Dhar and Shefali Mitra preferred to stay back at their hotel in Gangtok, as they had visited the lake on an earlier occasion.

"I wish I had either gone with them or stopped them from going to the lake," were the only words that a sobbing Dipali could manage to say over the phone from Gangtok.

A relative of the Dhar family said that Dipali's mother was not in a position to speak, as she is devastated by the accident.

"She is inconsolable. Her family was wiped away in the accident," said Sandip Thakur, Dipali's uncle.

Both the families had decided to visit Gangtok after Darjeeling.

"My father-in-law and mother-in-law had been planning to visit Gangtok and Darjeeling for the last 20 years. But it proved to be their last trip," said Partha Sarbadhikari, a relative of the Biswas family.

The bodies of the deceased were brought back to the city on Monday. "The Sikkim government arranged for a vehicle to bring the bodies to Kolkata," Sarbadhikari said.

The five persons who died in the accident included Asim Dhar (45), his daughter Debkanya Dhar (20), Asim's father, Satyendranath Biswas (75) and Puspa Biswas (65).

Heading: Pollution board conducts study for rainwater harvesting in city - Indian Express
Content:
The CID on Tuesday claimed that they were close to nabbing the kingpin of the gang that killed a Royal Bengal tiger in the first week of October.

The cid along with the state police has launched a manhunt to nab him.

"We have launched a manhunt for the eluding man who had a major role to play in the killing of the tiger," said Sanjay Mukherjee, Special IG, (CID).

He said the investigating officers have found leads in the case and expressed confidence that the man would be nabbed very soon. Two other men arrested in the case are in police custody.

The state police, meanwhile, claimed to be keeping a close watch on the known criminals of the Sunderbans. "We are keeping a close watch on the criminals of the area, who deal in illicit trade of wildlife products," said a senior officer of the South 24 Parganas police.

Police stations in Gosaba, Canning, Namkhana and Basanti have been alerted to keep a tab on anyone trying to deal in illicit animal trade, the officer said.

The CID had arrested two persons — Paritosh Mondal and Panchanan Giri — of Kumirmari island in Sunderbans in connection with the killing of the tiger. While these two persons have been arrested, the alleged kingpin of the racket is still at large.

Heading: Armed robber attacks bank agents in Sealdah - Indian Express
Content:
In an effort to provide a detailed database to explore the possibilities of rainwater harvesting in various parts of the city, the West Bengal Pollution Control Board (WBPCB) has come up with a scientific study.

The WBPCB has assigned the Centre for Ground Water Studies to undertake a scientific study on the issue, covering 141 wards under the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) in relation to the existing geo-hydrological situations.

"The main objective of the report is to evaluate area specific rainwater harvesting possibilities covering 141 wards of the KMC and identify priority areas where such harvesting structures could profitably develop," said T K Gupta, chief engineer, WBPCB.

"Our purpose also includes area specific identification of appropriate types of rain harvesting structures that will be sustainable," he added.

While there are water investigation authorities both at the Central and the state level working on statistics pegging the situation of the ground water level in different areas of the city, the current completed study has been developed to act as a guide for industries, suggesting depth for recharge of aquifers.

Those who conducted the Rs 1.5-lakh funded project included experts and former members of State Water Investigation Directorate along with Central Ground Water Board among others.

The project divided the KMC area into five sectors —- northern, western, southern, eastern and central —- from the point of view of hydrogeology as related to feasibility of rainwater harvesting structures.

The study revealed that the central zone, with a depth of water level varying between 10 to 18 metres, has the fastest recession of ground water. The report suggested that rooftop rainwater harvesting and ground water recharging through 80 to 100 metres deep recharge wells is essential to stop further recession of ground water level in this zone. Moreover, the presence of aquifers at multiple levels below the ground will make ground water recharging possible through recharge pits and recharge shaft.

The western sector, on the other hand, reported two aquifer systems with a water depth level varying between 10 to 18 metres below ground. Harvesting through recharge well at the depth of 160 to 180 metres was suggested by experts.

According to the researchers, the eastern sector, with a ground water depth of 9 to 16 metres, has the option of going for recharge wells of 80 to 120 metres depth. The northern sector has a single aquifer system with a water level varying between 14 to 17 metres and recharge of aquifer through recharge wells of depth varying between 60 to 80 metres.

As a beginning of the initiative, WBPCB has already given a copy of the report to CREDAI Bengal (Confederation of Real Estate Developers Associations of Bengal) as guide to their future efforts of rain water harvesting and putting up recharge wells.

"We have received such a report from the government. This kind of a database is essential as it guides us about what we need to do regarding ground water recharging. Such initiatives and in-depth studies are useful for us to recharge at the correct depth," said P Sureka, president CREDAI Bengal.

Heading: JCT pin hopes on ‘new kid’ Balwant - Indian Express
Content:
Two persons were hacked by an armed robber, while they were on their way to deposit cash in a bank in Sealdah on Tuesday morning. One of the depositors injured in the attack has been admitted to NRS Hospital. No arrests have been made in this connection.

Forty-year-old Nirmal Bhattacharya and his nephew Sunny — both agents for a money collection scheme of the bank — were climbing up the stairs of the Sealdah branch of Canara Bank at 14, Acharya Prafulla Chandra Road, when an armed man attacked them with a sharp-edged weapon and hacked Sunny.

Sunny had collected money from the traders of the area on Monday and was about to deposit it in the bank. Following the attack, the money, mostly in small currency notes, fell on the ground, and the robber tried to snatch it away. But Sunny and his uncle raised an alarm and the attacker fled, leaving the two injured.

"We did not understand what had happened in the beginning. Then Nirmal Bhattacharya came down injured. He told us what had happened," said Kamal Das a local pan shop owner. Sunny received several chopper blows and was admitted to NRS Hospital by locals.

The police later arrived at the spot with a sniffer dog but they did not get any breakthrough.

Deputy Commissioner of police, North, Damayanti Sen said the investigations were on to identify and nab the attacker. Locals are, however, alarmed after the incident. "We feel insecure after the incident," said a local shop owner.

Heading: Poor defence cost Dempo dear - Indian Express
Content:
He admitted that Sunil Chhetri's absence has affected his team. But JCT coach Sukhwinder Singh said in young Balwant Singh, they had the back-up ready.

"As a coach you should be prepared for everything. Balwant, who is a product of our football school, is the new kid on the block," Sukhwinder told The Indian Express as JCT started their preparations for their upcoming I-League tie against Chirag United on Thursday.

His assistant Parminder Singh agreed. "He is a real talent. He will mature with experience. We are working on to have a perfect understanding between him and the Brazilian striker Eduwardu like Chhetri and Edu had," he said. Balwant has started his maiden I-League campaign in a spectacular fashion, scoring an excellent goal against Dempo.

Sukhwinder, however, is not at all happy with Brazilian Marcos Pereira who left the Punjab club to play for Mohun Bagan. A Nigerian midfielder is likely to replace him as the third foreigner in the side.

Meanwhile, the JCT top brass has started to toe the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) line and has set up JCT Sports Private Ltd .

Sailen Manna undergoes prostate surgery
Former Olympian and India football captain Sailen Manna today underwent a prostate gland operation at a nursing home in Salt Lake here. The former defender, who turned 84 recently, is suffering from complications in prostrate gland and was admitted to the nursing home last month.

"He was operated upon this evening and is now under observation. According to the doctors, he is doing fine and will take around a week to recover," a family source said.

Manna, who is a former Mohan Bagan player, led India to the Asian Games football gold in 1951.

Heading: Hurt Couture - Indian Express
Content:
Safa FC of Lebanon win 5-1 on aggregate, move into AFC Cup finals

Indian hopes died young in the AFC Cup. Ever since Dempo had qualified for the semi-finals, there was an air of expectation that they might go the distance. They were just two matches away from joining the Asian elites in the AFC Champions League.

That they lost the first-leg semi-final 1-0 in Beirut wasn't too big a concern considering the fact that they had the home advantage in the second-leg.

In the end, it turned out to be an anticlimax — a 4-1 hiding at the Gachibowli Stadium in Hyderabad today. The scoreline, however, didn't tell the entire story. Dempo fought, and fought well. But Safa FC of Lebanon converted their chances and moved into the finals.

Striker Mohammad Kassas and substitute Hussain Tahan did it for the Lebanese side with two goals each. Kassas scored his first goal in the ninth minute and sealed the issue with his second, eight minutes later.

Though Mboyo Iyomi pulled one back for the hosts on the hour mark, by then it was all but over.

"The early goals really upset our plans," Dempo assistant coach Mauricio Afonso said after the match. "At 1-0, we still had a chance but after conceding two goals within first 20 minutes, it was very difficult to come back," he added.

He lauded Safa's performance saying: "Safa forced us into making mistakes and based on their performance today, they deserved to be in the final."

At the same time, he lashed out at his defenders. "Our defenders made some bad errors and they have to take some responsibilities for this defeat."

Ahead of this tie, Dempo coach Armando Colaco put a lot of emphasis on the defensive organisation. In reality, the rearguard let him down.

Dempo went on the attack mode right from the outset leaving lots of gaps in the defensive-third. Anthony Pereira had a clear sight of the goal in the seventh minute but his volley went wide. Then on, things started to go south for the hosts.

Kassas broke the deadlock heading home a Rony Azar's free-kick. In the 17th minute, he went past three defenders to double the advantage.

The situation called for desperation and Colaco brought on Joaquim Santan for Nicolau Borges at the half time. The move paid off as it helped raise the tempo and Iyomi reduced the margin with a delightful strike.

He received a long ball from the back, chested it down perfectly, dropped a couple of defenders and fired past Safa goalkeeper Nazih Tay. The very next move saw Ranty Martins almost level the score. His powerful strike was stopped by Tay at full stretch.

Then Iyomi scored in the dying moments only to see the goal was disallowed for off-side.

Tahan scored his first goal from the counter attack, with nobody to mark him. He made it 4-1 deep into the added-on time.

Safa coach Samir Saad was naturally delighted after this win. He also agreed that the early goals made the difference. "The early goals made all the difference for us today. Our plan was to keep the game tight and to hit them on the counters and it worked out perfectly," he said.

Safa would be the first Lebanese club to play in the AFC Cup since Al Nejmeh got there in 2005.

Saad is looking forward to the possibility of facing Al Nahda of Oman who had a 1-0 victory over Muharraq in Baharain a couple of weeks ago.

"We can now look forward to the final and I hope that we face Al Nahda who are a strong side," Saad concluded.

Heading: Belle of the  Fashion Week - Indian Express
Content:
While multiple fashion weeks is good news for the style pack, designers hope too many cooks don't spoil the broth

Before egos and interests trailed high heels and crazy silhouettes onto the Lakme India Fashion Week runway, Delhi was the mecca for aspiring designers. From the choicest social butterflies and the most prestigious buyers to jostling shutterbugs and curious scribes, India's only fashion week promised all the works for a fledgling designer with promise. However, now, with four fashion weeks already in sway and another in the offing, the excitement seems to be diluted by some nagging questions. Will debutantes get the generous slice of attention and adulation in the crowd of new faces?

While the Lakme Fashion Week this year launched 75 new designers, the Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week presented around 55 newcomers while the Delhi Fashion Week flaunted about 22 new faces. "When we launched LFW three years back, our aim was to define the future of fashion and the future obviously lies with new designers," says Anil Chopra, advisor, Lakme. Chopra maintains that the sudden mushrooming of fashion weeks have not affected the brand value associated with LFW, but at the same time, he is unable to say the same for newcomers elsewhere. A feeling echoed by designer Abhishekh Dutta. "What is very important for a designer, new or veteran, is reviews in the media. However, with consecutive fashion weeks, people don't get time to breathe and reflect. Naturally, the reviews suffer in quality and quantity, that is of no help to a designer," says Dutta who had showcased his collections in WLIFW.

Kolkata-based designers Rumi and Bappaditya Biswas, whose label Bailou specializes in hand-woven scarves, dupattas and sarees, debuted in the Delhi Fashion Week this year organized by Sumeet Nair's Fashion Foundation of India. "We have been in business for six years now but never considered a fashion week before. We thought a breakthrough, with our rather wearable and simple collection, was not possible until Sumeet Nair's wife suggested we took part in Delhi Fashion Week," says Bappaditya Biswas. Biswas, who feels that multiple fashion weeks mean more exposure for aspiring designers. Small firms, like Bailou, would probably find it difficult to break even in the industry with a lone fashion week around, but business, say designers, doesn't support visibility always.

"It's true that so many fashion weeks make it easier for new designers to showcase their talents. But visibility often doesn't translate into business," says Dev, of designer duo Dev r Nil who debuted in LFW 2006. There's no denying the fact that establishment as a designer comes with business, and foreign buyers who play an important role in recognizing a designer's potential, are confused about the credibility of a fashion week and its participants. "Our fashion industry is not at par with those abroad. There can be several fashion weeks in countries in the West, but over the years they have established their significance in the world fashion calendar," says Dutta who feels that the country needs one well-rounded fashion week to establish itself as a fashion major for international buyers.

Amrita Hans, who showcased her line of handcrafted semi-precious jewellery for the first time at the Delhi Fashion Week, finds the idea of so many fashion weeks a little intimidating. "The important buyers are mostly divided between the several fashion weeks now. For better business, it makes more sense to participate in as many fashion weeks possible. However, that would mean that both the exclusivity and the quality of the collections suffer," says Hans. Vouches Kolkata designer Preeti Jhawar who made her fashion week debut in WIFW 2006. "Whichever be the week, established designers naturally hog the limelight because the fashion weeks here do not revolve around different styles mastered by groups of designers," says Jhawar. The multiple fashion weeks would make more sense if they concentrated on different types of clothing feels Jhawar. "It would be better if we had fashion weeks exclusively for bridal wear, prêt etc. That way, they would be more focused," echoes Dev. Are the fashion fathers listening?

With inputs from Premankur Biswas

Heading: Now, state wants Raj’s earlier bail cancelled - Indian Express
Content:
Success sits easy on Deepika Padukone. Relaxing in her make up van outside the Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week venue, the lissome model-turned-actor talks animatedly about her smashing debut and her relationship with actor Ranbir Kapoor.Padukone is still basking in the

success of her second release, Sidharth Anand's Bachna Ae Haseeno. The conversation veers towards Kapoor as her co-star and Padukone acknowledges, "I am more relaxed when I am acting with him and it shows on screen," she smiles.Soon, we'll see the 22-year-old in Nikhil Advani's Chandni Chowk to China opposite Akshay Kumar, where she again has a double role after Om Shanti Om. "I am very fond of the movie because it's the first time I have attempted action in a film.," says Padukone. The actor is also busy with director Imtiaz Ali's untitled film, opposite Saif Ali Khan.

Heading: Six hours of mayhem at Bandra court as police struggled - Indian Express
Content:
The application, claims that "there have been many cases where the party supporters have breached law and caused damage to public and private property"

Following the arrest of Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray on Tuesday, the state also promptly moved an application seeking cancellation of his bail granted by the 31st magistrate's court at Vikhroli, on February 13 this year. The prosecution sought the cancellation of the bail stating that Thackeray had, in several instances, created law and order problems in the city.

On February 13, Magistrate S J Sharma in his order had stated that Raj Thackeray should never in his political career, in capacity of a political leader, breach peace and tranquility in Maharashtra state. The bail would stand cancelled if he ever broke the law of the land, the order stated.

This application was moved following Sunday's violence by MNS supporters who attacked North Indian men who had come to the city to take an exam conducted by the Railway Board. The prosecution, in the application, claims that "there have been many cases where the party supporters have breached law and caused damage to public and private property". The magistrate has now issued a showcause notice against Thackeray, summoning him to be present before the court on or before October 23 in order to file his say.

Meanwhile, eight months since the case was registered at Vikhroli, no chargesheet has been filed in the case against Thackeray. "We're still in the process of investigation," said Amit Ansari, senior police inspector and investigating officer.

Earlier, The Indian Express had reported that since February 13, there have been over a dozen violent activities involving MNS activists reported from Mumbai and Pune.

For instance, days after Thackeray was gagged in September (the third time he was gagged this year) after the controversy over shop signboards in Marathi, MNS workers were booked in two incidents, in connection with the trouble over Jaya Bachchan's supposedly "anti-Marathi" comments at a press conference. The arrested activists were charged under Sections 120(B) and 336 of the Indian Penal Code for "conspiracy" and "endangering life or personal safety of others", and for unlawful assembly, respectively.

On August 15, MNS activists broke into and ransacked the Mercedes Benz school in Pune for allegedly not hoisting the Indian flag on Independence Day. All miscreants named in the complaint were MNS activists.

In July, MNS workers broke into the Maharashtra Institute of Technology (MIT) College in Pune and damaged property as they demanded more seats for Maharashtrians. Two days later, they attacked two more educational institutions as well as the local income tax office for what they said was discrimination against Maharashtrians and preference for outsiders.

Heading: Arch rivals speak in one voice against Raj - Indian Express
Content:
For six excruciating hours outside the Bandra Metropolitan Court, hundreds of activists of the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena mocked the Mumbai Police's law and order machinery as stone pelting and sloganeering became the order of the day.

The Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) also mobilized hundreds of its women activists to participate in the protest outside the court while the Mumbai Police had simply not posted enough women constables to tackle such an eventuality.

Even as MNS chief Raj Thackeray was being escorted into the city, the first shouts of protest went up around 11 am, by a woman who was requested by a police constable to make space around the court gates. What ensued was a well-planned demonstration and show of strength, sloganeering and name-calling. First, about 30 women escorted by male party workers drowned the calls for order with their shouting. In the next 10 minutes, the entire access area to the court was blocked by a huge mob.

A cane-charge by the police was met with heavy stone pelting, the crowd easily outnumbering the police constables wielding lathis. Arguments with mediapersons also ensued, and the court area was eventually cordoned off not only for MNS men, but also for the media. "He is a special man, it's a special case," is all that Deputy Commissioner of Police (Zone 8) Nisar Tamboli would say.

One woman officer, Assistant Commissioner of Police Harvinder Varisht, attempted to take charge, with very limited support. While the mob kept attacking with stones, and as an increasing number of protestors blocked the entire width of the Western Express Highway nearby, it was another four hours until the Rapid Action Force appeared.

Even as slogans laced with abuses against North Indian leaders — Lalu Prasad Yadav was a special target — rent the air, a little after noon, Additional Commissioner of Police Archana Tyagi called for a second lathi charge, driving the crowd towards the highway.

But the women protestors could not be persuaded to leave the road.

When one constable with a badge that said 'Marathe' was told by a woman MNS activist a Marathi policeman should not arrest Marathi protestors, he replied: "I am ready to remove my name badge to arrest you."

Two platoons of the State Reserve Police Force (SRPF) deployed outside the court proved to be inadequate with one platoon busy controlling a mob of Samajwadi Party supporters who had also turned up at the court.

After 12.55, when the first vehicle arrived with special public prosecutor Majeed Memon, the situation went completely out of control. BEST bus stops on the highway were vandalized, a Maruti van was burnt, and the areas around Bandra came to a complete standstill.

Finally, 10 minutes before the police convoy with Thackeray arrived at 2.45 pm, Rapid Action Force men arrived on the spot. Using tear gas and regular drills, the crowd was finally moved out of the court's access road — a good six hours after law and order first broke down.

Later on Tuesday night, police said 900 arrests for violence and arson were reported in Mumbai, along with 2,085 similar arrests across the state.

At the end of the day, faced with reports of what occurred at Bandra and across the state, Director General of Police A N Roy said: "We firmly want to assure people that situation is under control. Security forces are deployed across the state. It is not like this one organization is closing the city. Mumbai is not burning."

Heading: Finance ‘melting down’ on B-school favourite list - Indian Express
Content:
MNS chief Raj Thackeray has managed to make two eminent members of Mumbai's legal fraternity — who have had a track record of taking opposite sides in several high-profile cases— speak in one voice in his case.

On Tuesday, Rohini Salian and Majeed Memon, who represented the state at the Bandra Metropolitan Court after they were appointed special public prosecutors, sought 14-day police custody of the MNS chief.

Salian has appeared in several cases including the Ghatkopar blast case and represents the state in the recent theatre blasts case. Memon, a senior defence lawyer and the General Secretary of NCP has also fought high-profile cases like the Gulshan Kumar murder case and the 1993 serial bomb blast case as a defence lawyer to several accused.

Both have got into heated arguments in courtrooms innumerable times.

On Tuesday, both sought judicial custody of Thackeray on the grounds that his acts were unconstitutional and aimed at threatening innocent students who had come to appear an exam.

Memon said "We both appeared together on the state's request and our aim was to get maximum custody for the accused". Salian said: "The joint effort has nothing to do with our relations in court. We argued cases on merit and were professionals in court."

After Tuesday's proceedings, Memon watched the reports on the case on TV in the Bar of the Bandra metropolitan court from where he started his career, Salian immediately left the court and rushed to South Mumbai.

Heading: MNS leaves its sign on city - Indian Express
Content:
With world markets tumbling, finance and banking may lose their tag as the most sought-after subjects in B schools. These subjects, considered the gateway to the best paying jobs, could be soon replaced with options like marketing and manufacturing.

"For the last four years, finance has been the favourite. The brightest of the lot opted for it. In light of the present uncertainty, marketing is likely to overtake it in the next academic year," says Professor Kanu Doshi, dean, Finance, at Welingkar Institute of Management, Matunga.

Professor Dr V Bapat at Shailesh J Mehta School of Management, Powai, feels that so far, finance ruled the roost, but after the meltdown, manufacturing will be the next major attraction.

The impact on placements will be seen soon. Bapat says, "Intake in summer was less. Companies taking 20 students reduced it to 5. The major impact will be seen during December placements."

Dr Gulnar Sharma of Jankidevi Bajaj Institute of Management Studies, Juhu said, "The booming sector is pharma. Marketing, insurance, securities, retail sector have also not suffered a major setback. We have around 33 students enrolled in finance. They are quite concerned."

Hemlata Naik, a finance student at Alkesh Dinesh Mody Institute for Financial and Management Studies, Santacruz said, "I am worried. With banks employing former Lehman Brothers employees at low salaries, I cannot expect a good placement."

Purnima Subbiah, second year student of the Jamnalal Bajaj Institute of Management Studies, Fort, says, "There are always slack periods. I think it ultimately depends on how talented students are."

MBA aspirant Aayush Ahuja says, "The US financial crisis may reverberate in India after one or two years. Anybody becoming employable after two years will think twice."

Heading: Meanwhile, North Indians hope to use loudspeakers for Chhat puja - Indian Express
Content:
MNS rampage costs state 460 buses

On one hand where the chief of the Maharahstra Navnirman Sena (MNS) speaks strongly about the development of the state, his party workers, on the other hand, ransacked 460 public transport vehicles costing the state over Rs 30 lakh. The figure does not include the damage done to the taxis, auto drivers and the private vehicles.

This is only the estimated cost with the public transport units like the Municipal transport and the Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC) yet to calculate losses incurred due to cutting down on the trips.

According to the figures obtained from the municipal transport offices and the MSRTC, over 460 buses were damaged across the state, which is estimated to cost the state over Rs 30 lakh with the MSRTC bearing the maximum burnt.

Around 201 MSRTC buses were damaged by the angry MNS activists on Tuesday. In Jalna, an MSRTC bus was set ablaze by the angry mob. However, in majority of the cases the windowpanes of the buses were damaged.

The Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST) was also targeted by the MNS activists with some 115 buses being damaged. "We suspended the services of the BEST in Mulund and Kajupada in Borivali for some time. We are yet to calculate our losses, but roughly it could be around Rs 1.5 lakh excluding the losses incurred due to the suspension of services," said A S Tamboli, spokesperson for the BEST.

As many as 60 Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal (PMPML) buses were damaged and 8 people were injured in the MNS fury. In Navi Mumbai, 12 NMMT buses were damaged by the MNS activists, leading to 50 per cent loss in the revenue. "The MNS is not doing anything good for the state if they claim to be doing so. They are only damaging the state's property," said a senior IAS officer looking after one of the public transport units.

Heading: Exams postponed in city colleges - Indian Express
Content:
North Indians in the city are hoping to get an exemption from the Bombay High Court's order and use microphones for crowd management for the upcoming 'Chhat' puja.

The Supreme Court on Monday agreed to hear a petition seeking a direction to Maharashtra government to allow use of microphones and sound systems during the 'Chatt' festival in Mumbai on Friday.

A petition in this regard was mentioned before a Bench led by Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan which agreed to give it an urgent hearing as the festival is scheduled for November 4. Senior advocate Arun Jaitley, appearing for an organisation, Bihari Front, said use of microphones and loudspeaker was necessary for crowd management.

Congress leader Sanjay Nirupam, last year had filed a Special Leave Petition in the SC, against the Bombay HC judgement. "While the Central government's law has put a ban on loud speakers after 10.00 pm, the 'Chaat' puja function at Juhu beach was not allowed to use the microphones," he said.

"We hope that the SC gives positive response by Friday. It's a clear discrimination against the North Indian's by the state government by not allowing use of microphones for the 'Chaat' festival."

Last year also the organisation had filed the petition and the apex court had permitted the use of sound systems.

The organisation said that in Mumbai the festival is celebrated on the Juhu Beach and use of sound system on the day of the festival would not cause any inconvenience but rather help in security arrangement.

An apex court judgement prohibits use of sound system after 10 pm. However, the state government can relax the restrictions during festivals by notifying the relaxation 15 days in advance.

What they think of Raj's arrest

Sanjay Nirupam, Congress leader:

What Raj was doing is illegal; he was promoting crime and violence. The action against him is justified. At least now, MNS will understand that they are not above the law. North Indians in Mumbai are scared that the MNS activists would attack them. Raj could not have survived like this for a long time; this had to happen. The government was following the procedure to arrest him and finally the action has been taken.

NCP chief Spokesperson Narendra Verma:

The law has acted against him as he was trying to take it in his hand. We welcome Raj's arrest and demand that he should be implicated in all the cases across the state where MNS activists have attacked people who had come to take the Railway Recruitment Board examination. Raj is responsible for instigating the workers.

Heading: Shopkeeper in Vile Parle stands up to  MNS threat, refuses to shut shop - Indian Express
Content:
In Kirti College at Dadar, where the residence of Thackeray is situated, examination of all the streams in first year junior college were postponed. Principal of the college MB Kekare said, "The exam was supposed to start at 2.30 pm. As soon as we learnt the arrest of Raj Thackeray, we decided to postpone exams as we thought that students and staff members would find it difficult to travel in such circumstances."

Similarly, practical exams at Manik Vidyamandir at Bandra, scheduled for Tuesday, were also postponed, informed Principal Shubhda Vinaykar. However, scholarship exams were conducted as per the schedule. At Balmohan Vidyamandir, which is in close proximity to Thackeray's residence at Shivaji Park, Tuesday was the last working day before Diwali vacation. Bapusaheb Rege, trustee of the school said that the work experience exam that was to be held on Tuesday would be conducted after the vacation.

"After hearing Raj's arrest, several anxious parents called us in the morning. Many students come from far off places and we thought it appropriate to cancel the exam. " Mithibai College, Vile Parle conducted all the exams including the third year Bachelor of Science university exams as per schedule at late afternoon on Tuesday. "There was no disturbance in this area. Our exams went on smoothly."

Heading: Thackeray arrest: city witnesses minor incidents of violence - Indian Express
Content:
After the MNS and the Sena went on a rampage against north Indians on Monday a Bihari shop keeper in Vile Parle (west) finally stood up to them, rebelling against an unofficial diktat to shopkeepers in the area to remain shut. One Shahid Singh (26), from Bihar, the owner a gift shop, refused to pull his shutters down despite assault by some 20 men allegedly from the MNS.

According to Shahid, now recuperating at a private hospital, the men — he says they claimed to be from the MNS — came up to his shop at 10:30 am and demanded that he shut the shop. When Singh did not comply, the enraged men started pelting stones at his shop and then attacked him and two of his staff, Subhash Singh (31) and Rajesh Sharma (18) with bamboo sticks. According to Shahid the men fled after that. While Subash and Rajesh were only superficially hurt Shahid was hurt on his head and had to get stitches. Shahid has not filed any police complaint or NC and when asked for his reasons he simply stated, "What's the point? I don't think I can gain anything from this." Shahids's shop was the only shop in the entire station road that remained open for the first half of the day.

All the shopkeepers in Vile Parle (west) near the station say they were confronted by a group of men at around 9:30 am in the morning just as they were opening their shops and were told not to work. "These men came to me and said that I shouldn't open my shop today and said the same with every shopkeeper in the lane," said Tushal Vohra the owner of a shop on the Vile Parle station road. " Even though its not right we closed our shutters as one stone could have cost a lot if it hit our shop's glass."

"I told them that they had no authority to tell me to close my shop," said Shahid. He added, "It is my right to work and sell my wares and they are nobody to tell me not." When asked if he was afraid he said, "I was not afraid of them, somebody has to stand up to them and I am very proud I did. I haven't done anything wrong so I felt that I shouldn't be afraid," he said. "Why should we close the shop," said an infuriated Subash. "We work hard for our money and through hard work I have got myself this job. How can you treat anyone like this? Just because we are working class people are trying to bully us," he added.

Subhash further said, "If these people just want to divide the country why don't they take a piece of land and keep it to themselves and make it their own country, then they will realize their folly." Shahid added, "Even after the men left and I was grievously injured I still stayed in my shop since if they came back I wanted to face them. When they didn't come back for an hour I finally went to Cooper hospital and told my friend to take care of my shop."

Heading: Society members move HC against felling of trees - Indian Express
Content:
Following the arrest of MNS chief Raj Thackeray in the wee hours of Tuesday, sporadic acts of vandalism were reported from across the city with MNS party workers targeting BEST buses, autorickshaws and taxis.

* A group of party workers burnt a toll booth in Anandnagar on the Eastern Express Highway at around 3.15 am. They threw bottles containing petrol at the booth and set it on fire. Those present inside the booth stumbled out unscathed and saw the men running away. The Navghar police have registered a case under Section 144 against four unidentified youths but are yet to make any arrests.  

* In Ghatkopar party workers broke the windshields of 19 autorickshaws and 16 taxis, a tempo and two cars and burnt the hood of a rickshaw. On the complaint of an autorickshaw driver four people were arrested.

* Two BEST buses were burnt at Chembur's Suman Nagar at around 6.30 am on Tuesday. Senior Police Inspector, Chembur police station, Balasaheb Pachundkar was injured while trying to control a mob pelting stones. At around 11.30 when the police were patrolling the area to ensure that no untoward incident took place they encountered a group indulging in stone throwing. "Seeing the police approaching they started pelting stones at the van and while attempting to stop them Pachundkar was slightly injured. We nabbed Vijay Bhaskar Garje, a MNS shakha pramukh while he was trying to escape via Sion-Trombay road and have booked him under Indian Penal Code Sections 143, 147, 149 and 332 related to rioting and deterring a public servant from duty," said police inspector Dilip Raut.

* Over 40 persons were rushed to K B Bhabha hospital in Bandra after MNS activists who were present in full strength outside Bandra court where Thackeary was to be produced started pelting stones. "Four policemen, one fire brigade official and 35 others were brought to the hospital. All are treated on OPD basis," said Sulbha Chirmule, acting medical superintendent, Bhabha Hospital.

* Three taxi drivers and one bus driver were rushed to civic hospitals in the city. MNS activists assaulted Laxman Dagdu Landge, a BEST bus driver and Sheikh Mohamad Sharif a taxi driver, on duty on Tuesday afternoon. Both were taken to Sion based Lokmanya Tilak Municipal General (LTMG) hospital. "Both the patients came in the morning with minor injuries and were treated on out patient department basis," said Dr Sandhiya Kamat, dean LTMG hospital. Another taxi driver was rushed to King Edward Memorial hospital in Parel after he was attacked. He was treated on OPD basis as well.

Heading: Activists unite in support of those affected by infrastructural projects - Indian Express
Content:
Members of a housing society in Wadala have moved the Bombay High Court challenging the destruction of trees on their premises for a redevelopment project.

About 170 members of the Azad Nagar Cooperative Housing Society have moved the court against the BMC, East West Builders and office bearers of Azad Nagar Bhadut Mandal, Azad Nagar CHS seeking to stop the mass destruction of century old trees and other developmental activities carried out by the developers.

The petitioners allege that trees were being cut by the developers along with the help of police and BMC officials even though the matter is before the High Court and is sub-judice. However, following protests by the opposing members, the pace of activities had slowed down, the petitioners claim.

The members had in 2007 gone to court challenging the BMC's decision to hand over the land for redevelopment. The petitioners claim that the land having a market value of Rs 1,500 crore was handed over for a meagre Rs 24 crore. The petition alleges that the bidding process was not transparent and the deal was the handiwork between the officials of BMC and the office bearers of the society.

The original petition had sought the withdrawal of the Letter of Intent given to the developer, Intimation of Disapproval (IOD) as well as Commencement Certificate. The court had then directed the BMC to give a hearing to the petitioners before demolishing the premises and kept the matter for final hearing. 

The BMC heard the petitioners and passed an order in February 2008 approving the redevelopment contending that there was no interim protection granted to the petitioners by the court. One of the petitioners, Pankaj Thakker, alleged that trees were being destroyed even after a stay on demolition on the premises.

They also claim that the destruction is on even though a written request on the issue is pending before the Tree Authority. The petitioners say that the prime piece of residential plot measuring around eight acres and housing 32 chawls (320 tenants) was handed over to East West Builders.

They also claim that the property is unique as it was built during the pre-independent era and has 1000 big trees giving fresh oxygen to thousands of residents and pedestrians. The case will come up for hearing this week.

When contacted, President of the housing society Ravikant Dhanvade stated that there is no order staying the cutting of trees. "BMC had passed order to demolish the chawls stage wise. We have also got permission from the tree authority to cut trees," Dhanvade said. Dhanvade states that they have got permission from the Environmental Control Board and BMC to cut 33 trees.

MD of East West Builders Anil Agarwal confirmed that the redevelopment project is going on as the court refused to grant an injunction to the petitioners.

"We have got the necessary permission for redevelopment and cutting of trees," Agarwal said. The case will come up for final hearing next month.

Heading: Hearing of Susairaj’s bail plea adjourned - Indian Express
Content:
Activists from varied fields have come together to form a people's enquiry commission in order to look into the issues related to people affected by infrastructural projects across the state.

The commission will tour the state to conduct public hearings on issues of compensation, rehabilitation and land acquisition for various infrastructural projects. It is expected to come out with its report two months later. The people's commission has RTI activist and Magsasay awardee Arvind Kejriwal, former inspector general of police SM Mushir, Dhule based senior advocate Nirmal Suryavanshi and former IPS official and advocate YP Singh as members. On Tuesday Medha Patkar, leader of the National Alliance of People's Movement (NAPM) sat on the second day of her fast at the Azad Maidan to protest against the state government's failure to look into the issue of rehabilitation and land grab across the state.

From Kavita Desai who is still fighting for compensation after her forefathers' land was taken away several decades ago for a dam in Walvan to Tunabai Walekar, an adivasi who claims her land was bought in return of a measly compensation for the Lavasa city township project in Pune, those affected by projects across the state have come together to demand official action.

In Mumbai, the demand is for expediting a proposal submitted by the NAPM for redevelopment of slum community in Mandala under the Basic Services for Urban Poor (BSUP) programme of the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM). "The proposal has already received in-principle approval of the central ministry for urban poverty alleviation. About 3,500 residents in the slums will bear 12% of the cost of the project as per rules ," said Simpreet Singh from the NAPM.

Heading: Cancer awareness: tobacco-chewers on oncologists’ radar - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court on Tuesday adjourned the hearing of the bail application moved by Kannada actress Maria Monica Susairaj for a day. Maria is an accused in the murder of television executive Neeraj Grover.

The hearing got adjourned after the state government sought time till Wednesday. Maria had moved the court for bail pleading not guilty in the murder case.

According to her application there is nothing to prove her motive behind the murder and there is no evidence to sustain the murder charges against her. According to her lawyer, G S Kannur, she has all reasons to be granted bail.

The application also states that there is no possibility of tampering with the evidence.

The Sessions court on September 16 had rejected her bail plea for the second time on grounds that prima facie evidence available in the case pointed fingers at Maria along with her naval officer fiancé and co-accused, Emile Jerome Mathew.

The court had rejected the defence's plea of making Maria an accused only with respect to destruction of evidence and its claim that the murder was not pre-mediated as Susairaj had called Mathew 20 times from her mobile on May 6, the night of the incident asking him to come to Mumbai.

Despite Susairaj's statement that she was party only to the destruction of evidence, the police in June named her as the main accused in the case.

Heading: Films to look out for at the Asian Film Festival - Indian Express
Content:
Supporting the ban imposed on smoking in public and workplaces, oncologists propose to impose a ban on chewing of tobacco

A team of six internationally acclaimed oncologists, associated with the International Federation of Head and Neck Oncologic Societies (IFHNOS), is on a world tour to create awareness about Head and Neck cancer.

The team has already visited London, Barcelona, Rome, Athens, Warsaw, and Moscow and is now in Mumbai to discuss the growing threat of this type of cancer which originates from the chewing of tobacco and accounts for nearly four lakh victims ever year. The team comprises of four surgeons, one chemotherapist and one radiologist from USA, Canada, Hong Kong and Germany respectively.

Head and Neck cancer -a group of biologically similar cancers originating from the upper aero-digestive tract, including the lip, oral cavity (mouth), nasal cavity, paranasal sinuses, pharynx and larynx- are strongly associated with certain lifestyle practices such as tobacco chewing and smoking, alcohol consumption and certain strains of the sexually transmitted human papillomavirus.

Strongly supporting the recently imposed ban on smoking in public and work places, oncologists proposed to impose a ban on chewing of tobacco. "As compared to other countries we visited, cancer patients in India suffering from typical Head and Neck cancer affecting the cheek pouch in the lower jaw at the back of the tongue. This is because of chewing of pan and tobacco," said Dr Jatin Shah, professor of surgery E W Strong Chair in Head and Neck Oncology chief, Head and Neck Services, USA.

Comparing the situation in India to the rest of the world, Dr Shah said, "In United States tongue and floor of mouth are the most commonly affected areas. Also oral sex, linked to Head and Neck cancer, is increasing in US and it accounts for 20 per cent of head and neck cancers."

More than 500 oncologists and medical students from across the country and from neighbouring countries participated in this conference. "The main idea of this conference is to share the new developments in treatment modalities and apply it in a regional context. India is falling short of doctors. Also the tobacco chewing population is high," said Dr A K D'cruz, professor and surgeon, chief head and neck services, Tata Memorial hospital.

In the last 25 years over 150 surgeons from India have been trained in the US. "Although the method of treatment differs from country to country, there are certain golden standards for every therapy. India as opposed to many other countries we visited has tremendous knowledge regarding head and neck cancer. We were really impressed by the concepts and the treatments used in India regarding head and neck cancer and they are in the category of the golden standards," said Dr Jochen A Warner, professor and chairman of the Department of Otolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery, Philipps University of Marburg, Germany.

Citing the successful implementation of the ban on smoking in public places in countries like Russia, USA and UK, Dr Shah exuded confidence about achieving similar success in India.

Heading: Ankita stars in MDSC’s win - Indian Express
Content:
Opener Rahil Shaikh missed a chance to notch a century in the 23rd Sportstar Trophy MCA Under-19 selection trial tournament at Fort Vijay, Azad Maidan here on Tuesday.

The right hander would have become the first batsman in two years to reach the three-figure mark in the competition, but Shaikh fell short by eleven runs.

Shaikh held the Vijay Manjrekar XI innings together after the loss of Saurabh Randive for 18 and Ameya Dandekar for 0. Fortunately Shaikh found an ideal foil in captain Nikhil Patil who joined him at 70 for 2.

The two raised 97 for the third wicket before Dattu Phadkar XI staged a remarkable comeback picking six vital wickets, the downfall happening after Shaikh fell leg before to seamer Nadeem Mehndi.

Shaikh made a fluent 89 with seven hits to the fence and two sixes while Patil showed some aggression in his bright display, hitting eight fours.

The second match between Vijay Merchant XI and Khandu Rangnekar XI did not begin at the Elf-Vengsarkar CA ground, Oval because the authorities had not prepared the wicket. The match will be played from Wednesday to Saturday.

Chandrakant Pandit, Director MCA Academy inaugurated the tournament at the ELF-Vengsarkar CA Ground. He presented caps and shirts and goaded the players to bat and bowl well and make it tough for the opponent to win the match. "It's in a four-day match you will learn to play the game. It presents a true test to the players. Any cricketer can play a 50 and 20 over game. You should play the match like a one-innings game.

The pitch conditions change over a period of four days and this tournament will help you prepare for the BCCI's Cooch Behar Trophy.This tournament has given many cricketers to Mumbai. All of you should play a big role in the development of Mumbai cricket,'' he said.

Heading: King Challenge proves too hot for Winning Chick - Indian Express
Content:
ONGC registered their fourth straight win in the Mumbai Hockey Association (MHA) 2008-09 Super League at the MHA-Mahindra stadium in Churchgate on Tuesday. They thrashed a hapless Mumbai Port Trust (MPT) outfit 8-1, and have already garnered 12 points in the league.

ONGC started the carnage early on in the day, as Sandeep Antil fired in from close quarters in the 5th minute. MPT then enjoyed a brief period of dominance but failed to convert their chances as ONGC's Olympian Harpal Singh and company kept their strikers at bay. But a twin strike by Amir Bhardwaj in the 26th minute stretched the lead for ONGC. MPT though then got some respite as Mohd Ather Khan banged in from an acute-angle cross unleashed by Mohd Nadeem. The teams went into the break with ONGC leading 3-1.

The second half though completely belonged to ONGC, as they pumped in five goals at regular intervals.

Jayanta Mebei converted a penalty corner in the 42nd minute, and two minutes later S Singh made it 5-1 for ONGC. H Singh then deflected in a cross pass from the axis in the 48th minute to make it 6-1.

Captain Arun Rawat then pushed in a rebound pass, before reserve goalkeeper Kamaldeep Singh, who was fielded as a player, scored a diving goal in the final minute of regulation time to complete the 8-1 rout for ONGC.

Heading: Bubblegum kiss - Indian Express
Content:
Can a once-popular nightspot cling on to existence after a run-in with the law?

It's hardly a surprise that the mood at Bombay 72 Degrees East in Juhu was low on Saturday night. After a rave party bust, the ambience at the erstwhile popular lounge bar was on the wrong side of sombre. We weren't expecting huge crowds and we were right. The place was emptier than a wind-swept prairie. This is where, on October 4, around 200 people were detained for trafficking and using illegal substances like LSD, Ecstasy and hashish. Untill that fateful day, Bombay 72 Degrees East was a fairly popular, hence, crowded place. Could all its patrons have abandoned it so completely after that one debacle?

Inside the lounge, we had the pick of seats, since we seemed to be among the few people who decided to pay it a visit. It would also make placing our orders easy, we felt. As it turned out, it wasn't. We ordered two Caprioskas, a Rum Experience and a scotch. The waiter came back in five minutes and told us that the Rum Experience was not available. So we ordered Sangria instead but that was not to be had either. And when they came and told us that nothing on the scotch list, except Royal Challenge was available, we'd had enough. Upon enquiring, the waiter, in hushed voice, informed us, "You know, after what happened that day, they took away most of our stock." We cluck-clucked in sympathy and ordered for what was available.

It isn't easy to have rollicking fun in a near-empty lounge bar and we didn't. The drinks were reasonably well-made, although we couldn't taste the difference between the Mojito and the Caprioska. The music was a little too pseudo-Arabic and didn't help raise our spirits. We know that the place didn't have a license to hire a DJ, but some cheerful tunes would've helped to lighten the mood. The décor and the general layout of the place were comfortable, but depressingly low-key. A despondent air seemed to cling to the place as the depressed-looking waiters hung around, with hardly anyone to cater to.

As closing time approached, we were puzzled by the complete non-appearance of any patrons at all. Notoriety might have worked wonders for the careers of Rakhi Sawant and Rahul Mahajan, but it obviously doesn't work the same way with restaurants and pubs.

We caught up with one of the few customers there, Gautam Pal, who told us, "I hadn't heard of this place until the rave party incident. After that, I got curious and decided to check it out." That sounded good. Maybe a bad reputation might still help. "But," Pal continued, "It's quite likely that I might not return. It's empty."

This might sound premature but it seems, to us, that the final nail in Bombay 72 Degrees East's coffin might have been struck.

Heading: Speaking volumes - Indian Express
Content:
Wavtal, that was premiered at the Asian film festival, is a sensitive take on terrorism and its aftermath

Wavtal means a twister and true to its name, the film tries to portray the myriad coils and complications that occur in a woman's life post the tumultous Mumbai riots of 1992. Premiered at the Asian Film Festival, Wavtal is based on Anant Samant's marathi novel K-Five and traces the dark journey of a victim of terrorism.

Director Shivaji Lotan Patil's first film it also has many fresh talents including Puneite Tejaswini Pandit who plays the protagonist. Speaking on her experience Pandit says, "When I first read the novel it was a very shocking narrative for me to absorb. And when I was told I have to play the central character, it took some accepting. This is my first project with a major role and for me it has been a very intrepid step working in the film. I have invested a lot of effort for the performance and the viewers so far have appreciated the role."

The character of K-five is played by Ashok Samarth. Although a Muslim in the novel, his identity is only revealed through his personality in the film. Revealing his role Samarth says, "I remain reserved and reticent in the film and that makes it one of the most challenging roles. I am shown to be insensitive and arrogant. However it is about the person that he is, irrespective of the religion or community he belongs to." Patil finds the story extremely appealing as he adds, "The book has been written so well that the visuals are automatically created while reading it. It might be a fiction but in the current times, the events are strong possibilities in anyone's life."

The film will be released in Marathi as well as Hindi. Well-known producer and director Aditi Deshpande aims to present the film to maximum audiences. "As a filmmaker I feel it is my responsibility to promote good films. The film has been wonderfully executed and must be watched by maximum people. The best part is that most of them are new talents and they have wonderfully utilised the opportunity. Such good films will bridge the gap and get the viewers closer to Marathi cinema," adds Deshpande.

Heading: Capital city - Indian Express
Content:
Look chic with bright colours, ruffled dresses and big sleeves this summer

Show of the day

Effortless chic and a burst of yellows and purples made Narendra Kumar's Nari Nari the show that you shouldn't have missed. The outfits were hair-style co-ordinated, and Fashion triplets Priyanka Chopra, Kangana Ranaut and Mugdha Godse set the runway ablaze. The show also had excellent footwear with such beautifully irreverent detailing. Sexy.

Celeb of the day

The surprise entry on Day Two was Kabir Bedi, who looked as hot as a firecracker. He was accompanied by girlfriend Parveen Dusanj and daughter Pooja Bedi. They were there to cheer little Aliya (Pooja's adorable daughter), who walked the ramp for Pallavi Jaipur. Chatting up with each other and posing for the shutterbugs, they looked like one big happy family.

Trend of the day

Voluminous sleeves ruled the roost on the second day. Crab and Dolman sleeves were present in Kallol Dutta's unstructured line. Leg-of-mutton, batwing, bell and longish puff sleeves made a jarring presence in Drashta Sarvaiya, Arjun and Aastha Bahl line. High on style, these sleeves are well on their way to the top of the fashion poll.

Ensemble of the day

Rimzim Dadu may have called her line

'My Village', but her collection was far from rustic. Dadu showcased an amazing mix of woven dresses, draped racer back dresses and ruffles with quilting, pleating and tonal embroidery on smocks in pink, yellow and white — the colours seemed just right for the summer. What we loved the most was a pink-corded dress, an example of fine tailoring.

Goss of the day

Those who say that they love fashion more than their lives are evidently lying. Most of them chose to stay indoors, watching Raj Thakeray on their television sets instead. As far as attendance goes, Day Two wore a desultory look.

Heading: Bond with the best - Indian Express
Content:
In the midst of three fashion weeks taking place in two cities, the Delhi-Mumbai debate is hard to resist. Even so when the Booker winner Aravind Adiga dedicates his debut novel to Delhi, the capital city's charms are incomparable to Mumbai's mish-mash.

My only visits to Delhi take place during the various fashion weeks there. And in eight years as a rank outsider, I've sensed immense changes taking over. When less than a decade ago, the image of Delhi was one of pompous politicians and brash boys in their papa's BMWs, it's quickly debunked stereotypes and emerged as a stylish international city. Yes, it has overthrown that other self-appointed numero uno metro: Mumbai.

If Mumbai has the financial clout of its once-sexy Sensex, Delhi (once an exclusive public sector town) has quickly caught on as one of the richest cities in the world. If Mumbai has Bollywood and its forced stardust, Delhi, courtesy the National Institute of Fashion Design, is home to the most brilliant fashion creators in the country. If Mumbai has cricket, Delhi (or the North at least) provides the cricketers.

More importantly, since

Mumbai struggles for space, showing off the beautiful Arabian Sea on both sides, Delhi has expanded its girth to include the mall-filled Gurgaon and Noida, happily feeding and feeding off a new class of people for whom money is not to be concealed but to be shown off in good taste.

Louis Vuitton opened in Delhi five years ago, in the plush Oberoi Hotel, a whole two years before it found a country-cousin counterpart in Mumbai's Taj Mahal Palace & Tower. The uber-popular logo luggage maker was an instant success in Delhi; it took its bottom lines in Mumbai to show profit after over one year. Christian Dior and Valentino are already here, rivalling Mumbai's year-old Gucci and Burberry. Two of India's most famous designers —Tarun Tahiliani and Manish Arora—moved here from Mumbai.

Delhi has some hot spots that rival the finest one will find in

New York, London, Hong Kong or Paris. Three-sixty Degrees, also at The Oberoi, is one of the buzziest restaurants in the country. The Park Hotel, at Connaught Place, boasts of modern architecture by Sir Terence Conran, with its pink-blue lobby divided by beaded walls.

Another agreeable consequence is the mushrooming of independent restaurants. While, until a few years ago, one would have to go to a five-star to get good food, a 'Delhi Belly' now means an expanding waistline. There's Diva, by Ritu Dalmia, who learned her cooking in Sicily. In Greater Kailash, the suburb-turned-city centre, is Shalom, where you can get Lebanese as good as in Beirut. Then there are Tabula Rasa, a chic terrace eatery, and the newly opened Indochine, from the London-based chain. And my favourite — Khan Market — is Delhi's version of Covent Garden.

Renewal is in Delhi's air, buses and rickshaws are making way for CNG vehicles and the Delhi Metro has its swishiest denizens swelling with pride. The Commonwealth Games, taking place here in 2010, promise to show off an even more vibrant and infrastructure-strong capital of a new India.

As the erstwhile Mumbaikar, now Delhiite, Tahiliani puts it: "This is a new millennium city that's steeped in Indian culture. Where else can you find monuments coexist with modernity?"

This definitely should have our regional political parties mighty worried.

(namrata.sharma@expressindia.com)

Heading: Chatterati - Indian Express
Content:
Master tailor Angelo Petrucci reveals the secrets behind 007's sharp suits

When Italian tailor

Angelo Petrucci, 36, was asked to design suits for Pierce Brosnan for the Bond film, Golden Eye in 1995 he worked on creating illusions for Brosnan's lean frame. "He's great as Bond but we were used to the more strapping Sean Connery," says Petrucci, who was in Delhi recently to custom make suits for select customers there. Petrucci represents Brioni, the menswear label from Italy. He's been designing for Bond films till the last release starring Daniel Craig, Casino Royale.

Dressed in a crisp blue suit at Brioni's store at The Oberoi, Petrucci talks fondly of his first Bond experience. "The character James Bond has immaculate style. We selected the best fabrics, Prince of Galles-Glencheck, Grisaglia-Sharkskin and pinstripes which were in vogue that time," he says. Petrucci designed 70 suits for Golden Eye, each costing 3,000 euros. "All suits for James Bond were designed as per the scene. So I would study each Bond film, scene by scene and design a suit accordingly," he explains. He met Brosnan just thrice, off the set.

The prolific tailor has also designed clothes for 24 heads of state like Gerhard Schroeder, Nelson Mandela and Azlan Shah, the former Sultan of Malaysia. "The thought process involved in designing suits for presidents is very different from Bond. They're not jumping off buildings," he smiles. This is Petrucci's first experience designing for Indian men. More than 24 prominent Delhiites, from politicians to businessmen, visited Brioni to check out Petrucci's suits, each of which retails for over Rs 2 lakh.

Petrucci is all excited about the upcoming Bond flick, Quantum of Solace, though he has nothing to do with Bond's attire in this flick. "I'm not sure who's done the clothes," he says and adds a tad forlornly, "But I hope they ask me again."

Heading: The force be with you - Indian Express
Content:
Under wraps

Keeping with the trend of appearing on TV reality shows as special guests before a film release, Tusshar Kapoor and Celina Jaitley visited the sets of Voice of India Challenge to promote Golmaal Returns. To please the saas-bahu audience, Celina ditched her cleavage-revealing outfits for a sober sari and huge Parvati-style bindi. With her unimpressive career she may just be trying to impress her co-star's sis Ekta Kapoor for a role.

Bummer Tusshar decided to sport a suede jacket even in this Mumbai heat.

Heading: Haute Face - Indian Express
Content:
Ajay Choudhury's abstract paintings create a storm in a tea cup

He picked up a brush when four. By the time he was seven, he had his first solo show. But unlike some child artists—who make it big riding on the novelty of being so young but vanish with time—Ajay Choudhury has sustained his passion. "My exposure to painting happened because of my relatives, who taught at Patna Art Collage. However, I have been painting seriously only for the last 10 years," says the 33-year-old, who has a day job as a police officer.

His current solo is a deft mix of maturity and child-like spontaneity. Showcased at Anupa Mehta's Loft, a residency gallery space in Lower Parel, the exhibition consists of drawings of charcoal on paper and acrylics on canvas.
