"Currently, I am working on 4X4 feet canvases but I see myself moving to larger canvases where I can unleash to my energy and brush strokes," says the artist who ranges between abstract expressionism and minimalism.

Born in Palaman, Bihar, the artist now lives and works in Ahmedabad and is dedicating much of his time to art. "People can be dismissive about my art when they learn I have another job,

especially when they know it's with the police force. However, I see them as two completely exclusive parts of my life. Besides, I have had really positive responses from an artist as prominent as M F Husain," says Choudhury. His energetic line and confidence had impressed the veteran painter, currently in exile in London. After an appraisal like that, Choudhury does not allow petty criticism to affect his love for art.

The Mumbai show, which opened

on Tuesday despite the political protests, is a suite dedicated to black and white. It celebrates minimalist

purity. "What I am trying to communicate in this show is that though the paintings look really playful almost childlike in their freedom, a lot of thought have gone into their composition," says the artist. He spends at least half an hour thinking before giving colour to his thoughts on canvas.

"Sometimes I can take up to six months to complete a painting, sometimes it gets over in a week," says Chourdhury, who has created two works at Loft. "It's a dialogue between the canvas and me. When I go away for some time and the painting will tell me if I need to work on it more," says the artist on the mystery of creating the mesh of crisscrossing lines that play out their energetic dance on the white

surface of the canvas. "Creativity is an accident and when it happens I am thrilled." So are we.

Heading: Screen for safety - Indian Express
Content:
The fashion week threw up two new stunners

When newbie Malavika Rane walked down the runway for the Delhi Fashion Week, most designers took her to be a seasoned model. The 21-year-old was adjudged the "New Face" by Tikka Shatrujit Singh, adviser, Louis Vuitton and bagged a gift voucher for Rs 2.5 lakh. "I had been doing fashion shows off and on through college but took it up seriously only after my graduation," she said. The Mumbai-based model walked the ramp for seven designers including Malini Ramani, James Ferriera, Gaurav Gupta and Rahul Reddy. "She is different and has an interesting face. In fact, I did not know that she was walking the ramp for the first time," says designer Gaurav Gupta.

Another big find was Tanzanian model Millen Megsi who was judged the "Face of the Week" among 22 models in the finale and took home a gift voucher from LV.

The contest was floated on the second day of the fashion week and Megsi was every designer's choice. "Black models are gorgeous and you will see more of them in the next fashion week," said designer Tarun Tahiliani in whose show Megsi cut a decadent figure in a sterile white jersey gown. So, are black models an inclusive gesture in the multi cultural city? "As far as I know, it's not the first time black models are walking the ramp in India. In fact, they add more diversity and reflect the global world we live in," said Gupta.

Heading: Families of Godhra accused welcome SC ruling, but say they will believe it only when their dear ones walk free - Indian Express
Content:
Breast cancer is the second leading cause of cancer-related deaths in women, making it a significant health concern, says DR NIRJA CHAWLA

Any woman can get breast cancer, but there are some women who are more likely to develop it than others. Age is a major identifiable risk factor and more than 80 per cent of breast cancers occur in women more than 50 years of age. It does occur in younger age groups, but is rare in women less than 30 years. The chances of developing breast cancer at age 40 are one in 217, at age 50 they are one in 50 and at age 85 they are one in eight. The other risk factors on your check-list should be: any family member with breast or ovarian cancer, male family member with breast cancer, no full-term pregnancy, or having first child after 30 years of age and menopause after 55 years.

Irrespective of your risk status, remember that all women, low and high risk, should be screened for early detection of breast cancer and the best way to do this is to perform mammography (a special X-ray of the breast) every one to two years from age 50, according to the latest recommendations of the American College of Physicians(2007). Mammography between ages 40 and 50 years will depend upon an individual woman's concerns and risks. In cases where there is a strong family history of breast cancer, screening should begin at least, 10 years before the age breast cancer appeared in the family member.

Scientific evidence-based medicine suggests that breast self-examination (BSE) and clinical breast examination by your doctor (CBE) have not shown to decrease the death rate from breast cancer, sometimes cause undue alarm, anxiety and unnecessary investigations. Mammography alone or combined with ultrasound/MRI have shown to be extremely effective for early pick-up of breast cancer and thus improving cure rates. Most often the first clues to breast cancer is a lump in the breast. But do remain alert to changes in the size, shape of the breast, dimpling or puckering of the overlying skin, discharge from the nipple or inverted nipple. Not all lumps in the breast are cancer. But if a lump or nipple discharge does not seem to go away it should be checked. Cancerous lumps are usually painless. Painful breasts, on the other hand, are common and should not cause alarm unless they last more than a few days.

Breast cancer can be prevented by use of certain medicines in high risk cases. Based on scientific evidence, the risks can be lowered by moderate exercise, limiting alcohol intake and by avoiding obesity after menopause. Certain foodstuffs have also shown beneficial effects: those containing isothiocyanates like broccoli, cabbage, cauliflower, mustard greens and turnips, Polyphenol containg foods like apples, onions, green tea, lycopene found in tomatoes, folic acid rich foods like avocado, bananas, orange juice, asparagus, green leafy vegetables, dried peas and beans, Vitamin C rich foods like citrus fruits, guava, and Vitamin D obtained from sunlight and fortified milk.

The author is a Chandigarh based infertility specialist & gynae hysteroscopic laparoscopic surgeon. You can visit her website www.endoscopy.co.in, www.nirjachawla.com for more information. Her e-mail is drnirja@gmail.com

Heading: Govt backs petitions in HC against findings of POTA review committee - Indian Express
Content:
Lingering suspicion clouds hope

At ground zero, Godhra, it was time for some wary relief tinged with lingering suspicion on Tuesday, after the Supreme Court upheld the POTA Review Committee's recommendation to lift the stringent Act from those accused in the 2002 train burning incident.

Newsline caught up with two of the families coping with their loved ones being locked up under POTA, for the last six years.

For Mohammed Abdul Sattar Majmu, 70, the news that his blind son, Ishaq Mohammed Majmu is likely to get off POTA's stringent provisions, is like an unfulfilled election promise.

"Journalists from all over had trooped into my house, discussing our plight. My son is a blind man. How could he have been guilty? Yet, has anything happened that will spare him?" asked Abdul Sattar in his two room tenement in Godhra town.

Between the frequent power-cuts, the septuagenarian rued over the failure of the state to protect his 35-year-old son who was blind since birth. "I won't believe in any judgments till my son walks free. It seems all the courts are owned by the Gujarat government," said Sattar, who lost his wife, Kulsum Biwi, on December 7, 2002.

According to Sattar, his wife would weep every night till the day she died of a heart attack thinking about Ishaq, her blind unmarried son, who was picked up by a 'dabba' or a police van from their shop in April 2002 on allegations that he was one of the perpetrators who burnt the S-6 coach of the Sabarmati Express in February 2002.

Ishaq's younger brother, Shabbir, said that over the past seven years since his arrest, the family has been able to meet Ishaq just thrice. "From my scrap business I can manage just Rs 60-80 a day and it takes Rs 200 to go to Ahmedabad," says Shabbir, adding that his brother met the family twice on police parole, when some neighbours and friends pitched in with Rs 10,000. "The four policemen, who come with him, also need to be fed. Else they make haste and don't let Ishaq free even for the allotted time," added Shabbir, one of the four brothers of Ishaq. His other family members are laari-owners.

On the other hand, Abdul Sattar recalls the night when the police picked up Ishaq from the shop. "When we went to the police inspector at the Godhra Town Police Station with the doctor's certificate saying that he is blind, they realised that they cannot book him for killing anyone. Next thing we knew was, he was booked for inciting the mob," said Sattar.

Signal Faliya, where the incident occurred, is about three kilometres from Abdul Sattar's house. Sattar, who is himself partially blind, said: "We didn't even let him go to the chowkdi alone, and these policemen say that Ishaq walked all the way to Signal Faliya and shouted slogans from the railway tracks ."

Elsewhere, at Ruhul Amin Hathila's residence at Chabildas nee Chali, his wife, Najma, could not help beaming over an old photograph of her husband, who had prepared about 50 bail applications of those who have been arrested right after the train carnage by the Godhra police. "We have been married for the last 16 years, but for the last seven years it became unbearable when I had to re-assure the children and his old mother that he will soon be released," says Najma.

For the two children, Razzaq and Zeenab, studying in the Zakir Hussain High School, the daily routine has remained unchanged. "Rezzaq would ask me many questions everyday, while Zeenab was too young to understand what was going on. All I did was to keep saying that he was innocent and will be released soon," said Najma.

"He was sleeping when around 11 PM in April they came and picked him up. The police officers kept turning us away," said Najma, who lost her father-in-law, Haji Hussain Hathila, a former Godhra Railway Station employee, while Ruhul was lodged in jail.

Heading: Supreme Court judgment will put bail petitions on fast track - Indian Express
Content:
We had always opposed the formation of this panel, says state home minister

Gujarat Minister of State for Home Amit Shah has said that the state government has always opposed the setting up of the Central POTA Review Committee. He said the government also backs the petitions filed in the High Court by aggrieved parties challenging the merits of the Committee's findings that offences against those accused in the Godhra train carnage cannot be made under the anti-terror law.

The minister was reacting to the Supreme Court verdict that had held that a trial under POTA cannot proceed once the Review Committee gives the finding that the offences cannot be made out under POTA.

Shah told Newsline that the state government opposed the Central POTA Review Committee, as it was set up by administrative orders, and not under any law. The merits of the Committee's recommendations can be challenged in the High Court, he said.

He declined to comment further on the issue, saying that the HC would hear the case on Thursday.

About the Tuesday verdict given by the SC, he said: "We have not yet received a copy of the verdict. The government has asked its lawyer to dispatch a copy of the verdict given by the apex court. We'll study the SC order after receiving the copy."

Heading: Young blast survivor happy to be back home - Indian Express
Content:
Tuesday's Supreme Court order has rekindled the hopes of securing bail for close to 100 men lodged in Gujarat's jails in connection with the Godhra train burning incident of February 27, 2002.

The Supreme Court's decision where it upheld the constitutionality of the POTA Repeal Act and held the recommendations of the Central Review Committee on POTA to be valid, is also a setback to the Gujarat government in several important cases, most notably the Godhra train burning case.

With this Supreme Court order, the bail petitions of the Godhra accused that are pending in the Supreme Court will get a fresh lease of life. The procedure for bail is very stringent under POTA and the repeal has given vast powers to the public prosecutor to oppose a bail application.

The Supreme Court's decision came in the case filed by Mohammad Hussain Kalota, one of the Godhra accused, who had challenged the decisions of the Gujarat High Court that had upheld the validity of the POTA Repeal Act and the Central Review Committee formed under it.

However, the division bench of the Gujarat High Court, while upholding the Repeal law, had placed a rider by insisting that the Committee's decision would be subject to Section 321 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, which bestows upon the public prosecution a right to withdraw prosecution with the consent of the court.

This rider was challenged by Kalota in the Supreme Court which overruled it.

Eighty-two accused out of the 133 originally booked under POTA for committing acts of terrorism and being a part of the conspiracy to set on fire the Sabarmati Express carrying karsevaks from Ayodhaya, are lodged in jail.

Kalota's advocate Mukul Sinha said: "It is an important judgment for all the accused still in jail in spite of the order of the Central Review Committee. The Committee had clearly said that there was no scope of any terrorist conspiracy in the Godhra case and all proceedings under POTA be dropped. The Supreme Court has upheld the validity of the POTA Review Committee's powers to pass such an order and as of now it is totally binding on all courts of the land."

However, the POTA Review Committee's decision can be challenged before the High Court. In fact, a challenge of the committee's orders on merits is pending before the Gujarat High Court but no stay has been granted by the High Court on the implementation of the Review Committee's decision.

The POTA Review Committee had in its decision of May 16, 2005 concluded that there was not even a 'prima facie case' to show that the events that took place on February 27, 2002 that led to the burning of the S-6 coach of the Sabarmati Express were part of the terrorist conspiracy as defined under POTA.

The POTA Review Committee had also come to the conclusion that the Godhra case was a "simple case of unlawful assembly committing various offences under the Indian Penal Code and other Special Acts, but certainly not POTA."

Heading: Petro dealers end strike on positive assurance - Indian Express
Content:
Neighbours welcome eight-year-old Yash with a burst of crackers

It has been a long wait for the residents of Greencity Housing Society near Civil hospital, Asarwa. Eight-year-old Yash Vyas, the lone survivor among the father and sons trio, caught amid one of the 17 blasts that rocked the city on July 26, was discharged from Apollo Hospital on Monday.

His father Dushyant Vyas and brother Rohan (11) could not survive the blast. Praying for Yash's recovery, his classmates at the Sharda School had performed the 'mahamrityunjay jaap.'

On Monday, his classmates and society members gathered to celebrate his homecoming with crackers and sweets. But that would have to wait for another 20 days, as he was not brought home immediately for fear of infection. At present, he is at his aunt's place in Sola.

Yash is, however, happy to be back and is looking forward to joining school.

Heading: Medicos’ Munna Bhai act:Gandhigiri at Civil Hospital - Indian Express
Content:
They were protesting againt IOC's decision of giving contract of transporting fuel to a private transporter

The indefinite strike by fuel station dealers in Rajkot, Junagadh, Jamnagar and Porbandar on Monday was called off on Tuesday, following a meeting between the state Coordinator of Oil Companies and the agitating fuel station dealers in Ahmedabad.

The dealers began their strike against the Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) and Essar Oil Limited on Monday by not lifting petrol and diesel stocks from the dumps. In Rajkot and Junagadh, the dealers protested against the IOC after the company gave the contract of transporting the fuel to a private transporter, who quoted a lower price than the fuel station dealers. In Jamnagar and Porbandar, fuel station dealers protested against Essar Oil Limited after the latter started supplying fuel of a very high temperature from its Vadinar refinery.

When contacted, Satish Meshram, Executive Director of IOC and Gujarat State coordinator of oil companies, said that when the tendering process started, IOC held several meetings with the fuel station dealers in order to make them understand the process of quoting and tendering.

However, 38 pumps of Junagadh failed to quote prices through the method suggested by IOC and were thus not awarded the contract.

Meshram said: "We discussed all the points with fuel station dealers in today's meeting. Regarding the transport vehicle issue, we have asked for three months time from the dealers and assured them that we will try our best to resolve the matter. As far as the hot fuel loading issue is concerned, we have told the dealers that we will sort out the problem in the next 20 days after discussing it with Essar Oil Limited."

The fuel station dealers said they are satisfied with the solutions promised in the meeting. Shivlala Bhanderi, President of Rajkot City and District Petrol/Diesel Dealers Association, said: "We have been assured that 40 dealers of IOC in Rajkot and Junagadh will get the contract of transportation in the next three months. Regarding the hot fuel loading issue of Essar Oil Limited, the coordinator has promised us that if they are not able to arrive at any solution till November 11, all the three oil companies - IOC, Hindustan Petroleum and Bharat Petroleum - will supply fuel to some 150 dealers of Porbandar and Jamnagar from their own dumps instead of Essar's Vadinar refinery dump. As the authorities have assured that our demands will be fulfilled, we have officially called off our strike."

Heading: Bihari diaspora celebrates arrest of Raj Thackeray - Indian Express
Content:
Protest against vacancies not being filled, work for 12 hours despite being on leave

Overburdened with work, 13 medical officers of the Rajkot Dindayal Upadhyaya Civil Hospital registered their protest by applying for mass leave and yet working for 12 hours continuously on Monday.

There are 10 posts of medical officers lying vacant, but they have not been filled up for the past 18 months.

Resident Medical Officer (RMO) of the hospital G S Makwana said: "There are 32 posts of medical officers in the Rajkot Civil Hospital, but only 22 have been filled up. Of these 22, four medical officers have given their resignation, which have not been accepted as yet. Therefore, they have proceeded on long leave. No step has been taken to fill these four posts either. Furthermore, four doctors are deputed elsewhere, while one has been on medical leave since a long time. So, only 13 doctors are actually working."

He said work in the entire hospital includes attending emergency cases, check-ups of the 2,500-3,000 patients who visit the OPD everyday, indoor duty, surgical OPD, mobile van dispensary, night duty and post-mortem. "The entire work is being performed by just 13 doctors," he added.

They have not been given leave for the past 18 months. M C Chavda, one of the 13 doctors, told Newsline that the problem needs to be addressed on an urgent basis otherwise it may affect their mental stability.

"During Diwali, all the private doctors and hospitals will keep their doors closed and the entire rush will be diverted to the Civil Hospital. We just want that the doctors who have been sent to other centres are returned. We made this request to the medical superintendent, but he paid no heed to our demand. He said that since 22 posts are occupied, work is being done by 22, and not 13 doctors," Chavda said.

He added: "On Monday, we worked continuously from 8 am to 8 pm to show our protest. We did not allow work to get hampered. So, neither did our protest affect the patients, nor did the mass leave put our seniors in trouble."

Medical Superintendent of Rajkot Civil Hospital R Deshmukh said: "The appointments are made by the Health Commissioner so I cannot say anything on the issue. Deputation is a government process and has to be done whenever required."

Heading: Police crackdown on illegal hookah bars - Indian Express
Content:
Members of Bihar Vikas Mandal burst crackers, distribute sweets

The Bihar Vikas Mandal (BVM) celebrated the arrest of Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray, on Tuesday.

The members burst crackers and hugged each other, besides distributing sweets among themselves.

The interesting thing was that not a single policeman from the Pandol police chowky, which is situated just 50 metres from the site of the celebration at Katargram, turned up to inquire about the ongoings.

More than five lakh people from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar are settled in Surat and work in the textile, diamond and others industries in the city.

Several youths gathered at the Pandol industrial area in Katargam under the banner of Bihar Vikas Mandal to celebrate Raj Thackeray's arrest as the news was telecast on television channels.

The youths burst fire crackers and chanted slogans against Raj Thackeray for his vitriolic speeches against the Uttar Bharatiyas and the assault on the youths in Mumbai by MNS activists.

Bihar Vikas Mandal Surat city president Prabhunath Yadav said: "We strictly condemn the attacks on Uttar Bharatiya students who came to appear at the Railway Board exams in Mumbai. Even the attacks on innocent Uttar Bharatiyas staying in Mumbai are increasing each day.

He said the MNS activists are arrested and later released on bail.

He added: "We believe that the attacks on innocent people by the MNS activists are more dangerous than the bomb blasts. We wish that Raj Thackeray is charged under MCOCA."

He said they are happy that the Maharashtra government became active and dared to arrest the MNS chief.

"We have relatives in Mumbai and we are worried about them." Yadav said.

Heading: Bangladeshi girl arrested for supplying fake notes - Indian Express
Content:
Arrest 28 people, including staff and school-going boys and girls

The police registered a case against two illegally-run Hookah Bars in Umra on Tuesday evening. In the first-of-its-kind case in Surat, the police arrested 28 people, including school-going boys and girls. All have been booked under the Prohibition Act.

Acting on a tip-off, the Umra police conducted raids at two Hookah bars, Moon Light at L B Shopping Complex and Kashan in the City Light area, in the evening. During the raid, the police officials were shocked to see school-going boys enjoying Hookah parties at both bars. The raids led to the arrest of 28 people, including the staff and four minor girls, who were also present at the bars.

Later, the police also raided the recently opened Hookah Bar in the Ghod Dod Road area, but found it empty. Officials suspect that the bar owner might have received information about the raids at the other two bars and alerted his staff and customers.

Umra Inspector R S Patel said: "We discovered that several Hookah bars have been functioning illegally in the Umra area. These bars attract a huge number of school and college going students. After receiving information, we conducted raids at the two bars. The bar owners were not able to produce any license and thus strict action will be taken against them."

Heading: Gujarat ‘vats’ for 12.5% tax on tobacco products - Indian Express
Content:
The Special Operations Group (SOG) arrested a 26-year-old Bangladeshi girl wanted in connection with supplying fake currency notes, in the Adajan area on Monday.

Salma Habibur Shaikh started trafficking counterfeit notes after the Surat police arrested her husband Habibur Shaikh with fake notes worth Rs 98,000.

A bar dancer by profession, she was continuing her husband's "business" after the Maharashtra government banned dance bars. She brought fake notes from Mumbai and circulated them in Surat.

On August 16, the Surat SOG had arrested three Bangladeshis with fake currency notes to the face value of Rs 1.94 lakh. Hafizur Sikander, Mohammed Jamil and Mohammed Zakir Mulla —all residents of Nadail district in West Bengal — disclosed that Salma had given them the fake notes for circulation in the local market.

SOG Inspector B K Ayar said: "Habibur and Salma frequently visited Mumbai to bring the fake currency notes. She was aware of the links in the racket. After Habibur's arrest, she started running the racket with the help of local Bangladeshi youths. It was easy for her to operate as she was aware of the people behind the racket."

He added: "With Salma's arrest, many more links in Surat and Mumbai will come up."

Heading: Next D-day for Chandrayaan-1: Nov 8 - Indian Express
Content:
Urges the Centre to allow for the same to make up for the loss following the abolition of CST

The Gujarat government has urged the Centre to allow it to impose 12.5 per cent Value-Added Tax (VAT) on tobacco to make up for the revenue losses following the abolition of Central Sales Tax (CST) from the state in a phased manner.

Sources in the Sachivalaya said on Monday that Gujarat Minister of State for Finance Saurabh Patel will raise the issue at an Empowered Committee meeting of state finance ministers called by Union Finance Minister P Chidambaram in Chandigarh on November 3.

The Centre has started abolishing four per cent CST from those states where VAT has been introduced in place of Sales-Tax. Accordingly, the CST has been abolished by one per cent from Gujarat since April 2007. It will be completely done away with from the state by 2010.

Sources said Gujarat mopped up revenues of Rs 3,000 crore annually in the CST scheme. The government has now decided to make a strong representation to Chidambaram at the impending Chandigarh meet to permit the state government to levy at least 12.5 per cent VAT on tobacco to offset the CST revenue losses.

Incidentally, the Centre has compensated the states with adequate funds as it has started abolishing the four per cent CST in a phased manner.

Gujarat has been paid Rs 338.14 crore of the total Rs 764 crore due since April 2007 in lieu of one per cent CST abolished that year. Patel will now request Chidambaram at the Chandigarh meeting to pay the remaining dues to the state, a senior official said.

Heading: City’s DCB makes huge recoveries from high security jail - Indian Express
Content:
On that day, the spacecraft will enter the Captured Lunar Orbit

If the weather god permits then by the time you read this report, India's first lunar mission would have taken off from Sriharikota and scientists at ISRO's Space Applications Centre (SAC), Ahmedabad would be already looking at the next most important date of the mission — November 8.

"On this day, the Chandrayaan-1 Spacecraft will enter the Captured Lunar Orbit with perigee as 500 km and apogee as 7,500 km," said A S Kirankumar, Deputy Director, Sensors Development Area, SAC. From this, it will be slowly lowered to the intended orbit of 100 km when all the scientific instruments on Chandrayaan-1 will start functioning.

Kirankumar, who also heads the team at SAC responsible for all the electro-optical payloads of the Terrain Mapping Camera (TMC) and the Hyperspectral Imager (HySI) being carried by the Spacecraft, elaborated on the role played by SAC in Chandrayaan-1. "Along with TMC and HySI, we also developed the hardware for the High Energy X-ray Spectrometer built by Physical Research Laboratory Ahmedabad," he said.

Ram Rattan, Associate Director of SAC informed: "Even the Moon Impact Probe built by Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre Thiruvananthapuram has an optical camera built by SAC." In addition to this, SAC will perform a major role along with ISRO's Telemetry, Tracking and Command Network (ISTRAC) by radio metrical corrections of data products received from various payloads.

Ram Rattan also emphasised on the unprecedented 3-D topography of the lunar surface which will be done by SAC's very own TMC at a spatial resolution of five metres with height information of three metres. When asked about the difference between SAC's HySI and NASA's Moon Mineral Mapper (M3), as both intend to investigate the mineralogical composition of the lunar surface, he explained, "M3 can analyse wave lengths in the range of 0.4-0.3 microns, while HySI can analyse wave lengths from visible to near infrared spectrum. The values are from 0.43 microns to 0.96 microns."

SAC has also established two control centres for TMC and HySI which will coordinate with the Ground Segment of Chandrayaan-1. With Chandrayaan-2 already approved by the government, Rattan said that SAC is planning to build all the imagers, sensors and cameras in-house, with major addition being surface level measuring instruments.

Heading: Two crude bombs found in Mehsana district - Indian Express
Content:
Mobiles phones, cell phone batteries and chargers, audio and video CDs, DVD players, knives, electric wires, cash and transistors were seized from the high security Sabarmati Central Jail premises in one of the biggest surprise raids carried out in the jail on Tuesday evening.

A total of 110 personnel were involved in the operation carried out jointly by the city police's Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) and the jail authorities. Five mobile phones, three cell phone batteries, two mobile chargers, one DVD player, two transistors, two knives, nine audio and video CDs, electric wires and Rs 1,900 cash were seized from the inmates in extensive searches that lasted till late on Tuesday.

Deputy Commissioner of Police, DCB, Abhay Chudasma said the raids were conducted following some leads given by jail clerk Ashok Zapadia and his accomplice Mehmood Khan Pathan during interrogation. They were arrested on charge of smuggling mobile phone into the jail. At present, they are DCB's custody. "A complaint was later filed in the Sabarmati police station. Investigation into the case is being done by the DCB," he added.

Heading: Out of ‘site’: Education dept website has stale links - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly a month after 17 crude bombs were found in Kalupur in the Walled City area, two more explosives of similar make were found in Ambaliyasan town in Mehsana district on Tuesday morning.

The Mehsana district police were on their toes on Tuesday after being informed about a 'bomb' that a six-year-old boy had brought to his house thinking it to be a ball.

The boy's father opened the pan-masala tin box, which was tightly tied with jute strings and found gunpowder, ball bearings and nails inside.

Langanaj Sub-Inspector V V Desai said: "In order to confirm that it was gunpowder, the man took a pinch of it and threw it on fire. A flash appeared. He immediately intimated us about it."

A team of Langanaj police rushed to the spot. Mehsana Superintendent of Police Raju Bhargav also came along with the Bomb Disposal Squad and the Dog Squad. Based on the boy's statement, the police later found another bomb lying in a deserted place in the Old Marker area in Ambaliyasan.

Heading: Foetuses sent to BJ Medical College for further probe - Indian Express
Content:
Despite instructions for daily update, several sites carry old information

It comes as a shock when several websites linked to the website of the Education Department of the Gujarat government are not updated on time; and that too when the Gujarat Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board (GSHSEB) has instructed all granted and self-financed schools of the state, which have secondary and higher secondary, to make their websites and update them daily.

The website of the Gujarat Council of Elementary Education was last updated on September 9, a fact clearly mentioned on the website as well. Asif Mansuri, Assistant Manager, Information System, Gujarat Council of Elementary Education, said: "I joined only a month ago, so I will not be able to comment on the issue. But one thing

is there the process of updating the website is going on and in the near future, the work will be done."

He added: "From our side, the data and information to be updated on the website is ready, but in September, the Education Department got a new private company for operating the website and since then the website has not been updated."

The technical officials of the Commissionerate of Schools and Mid-day Meal Programme said it has been quite a long time since their website has been updated.

The old private company which used to update our website was removed by the Education Department and a new private company was appointed, which has not started work of updating the website yet.

"The work from our side is all done and we have already given our content and material required for the website to the Education Department. Now it is in their hands when to update and how to update as we have no role to play in updating the website," said a senior official from the Commissionerate of Higher Education.

These apart, the websites of the Director of Technical Education, Directorate of Literacy are also not updated on a regular basis along with the website of the Education Department, Gujarat government.

A senior official from the Education Department, Gujarat said on condition of anonymity: "Several things on the website of the Education Department are not updated on a regular basis, then how can you ask and expect the schools to make their own websites and update them on regular intervals?"

Heading: City roads not good enough for ViTCOS’ brand new buses - Indian Express
Content:
Probe into the case of four foetuses found in a canal in Palanpur came to a standstill after investigation officers sent the samples to the BJ Medical College. Its report will come in 20-25 days.

"We have to wait for the B J Medical College to give its report. It is difficult to take any action before the report comes out," said investigating officer N K Chauhan.

"The findings of further examination is important for the investigations to proceed. As the place where the foetuses were found is far from the village, people hardly visit the area and have therefore, been of little help," he said.

The four foetuses were found at Rasana village wrapped in a plastic cover. The post-mortem examination report, submitted by the Deesa Civil hospital, stated that all the foetuses were of girls. While there is strong possibility that it was bio-medical waste, police sent the sample for forensic test on Tuesday saying that female foeticide could not be ruled out.

Heading: Public Accounts Committee pays a visit to SSG Hospital - Indian Express
Content:
Narrow roads, increasing number of vehicles and multiplying number of hawkers on the roadside, make it difficult to ply buses in the city

Though the Vallabhipur Transportation Cooperative Society Pvt Ltd (ViTCOS) has added five more buses to its fleet in order to facilitate public transport, the city roads still remain incompetent to welcome and encompass the new buses. The narrow roads, coupled with increasing number of vehicles and several roadside hawkers, have not only led to heavy congestion, but actual verbal and physical tussles between the bus drivers and the vehicle owners.

With such a situation, the ViTCOS buses are finding it difficult to move about in the city roads. "We do face serious traffic problems in crowded areas and have requested the municipal authorities, but nothing much has been incorporated to facilitate the movement of the buses," said Haren Dodhiya, Chairman, ViTCOS.

Narendra Rana, ViTCOS manager, Vadodara chapter, added: "We have been allotted certain spots to make halts, but they are intentionally occupied by the auto drivers. This leaves no space for the buses to halt and causes traffic disruption, besides discomfort to the passengers as well as to the public on the roads. There have been several incidents where our drivers have got into arguments and physical tussles with the auto drivers, especially in Mandvi, Panigate and other crowded areas."

The Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) had started a drive to remove roadside vendors from crowded market areas and relocate them to a hawking zone 100 metres from the main road. The endeavour, however, did not prove successful, as within days of relocating the hawkers, the areas resumed their earlier look.

"The main motive behind relocating roadside vendors was easing the traffic. But the whole process needs regular monitoring. We do not have the manpower to conduct regular checks. Besides, this process needs cooperation from the traffic department as well," said C M Makwana, Deputy Commissioner, VMC.

Though the VMC had laid down a long-term plan for easing the traffic and widening the roads, no measures seem effective for the recent traffic commotion.

"We are studying Rajkot's model, where over 5,000 trees were scientifically relocated in order to clear the main road. We are also planning wall-to-wall widening of the roads, but all this will take a year's time," said VMC Mayor Balkrishna Shukla.

Heading: Seminar on global slowdown in MSUExpress News Service - Indian Express
Content:
The Public Accounts Committee appointed by the state government paid a visit to the Sir Sayajirao General (SSG) Hospital on Tuesday. A team of over 14 members, including MLAs and party workers from the ruling party as well as the Opposition, visited the hospital to review the grant demanded by the medical college and the hospital for infrastructure development.

The team was headed by Kuvanji Bavariya, Rajkot MLA from Jasdal and the chairman of the Public Accounts Committee. During their visit, which started around 9 am on Tuesday, the members visited various wards and departments of the hospital and the medical college.

"The dean of the college and the medical superintendent of the hospital have been asked to submit a report to the committee, requesting the grant for infrastructure development," said A T Leuva, dean of Baroda Medical College.

He added: "The team not only visited all the wards, but also interacted with the patients and class IV workers in the hospital to understand the problems being faced by them."

Bhupendra Lakhawala, BJP president, Vadodara, who accompanied the committee, said: "The basic purpose of the visit was to identify the areas which need to be improved. During our visit, we found that 90 per cent of the system was in place. There are certain recommendations like more purchase of medicines and installation of instruments and machineries."

The 16-day state wide visit started from Rajkot and covered central Gujarat on Tuesday.

The team will now proceed to south Gujarat and visit medical colleges and hospitals in Bharuch, Surat, Vyara, Rajpipla and other places.

Heading: Doctor arrested for being negligent - Indian Express
Content:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) endowment unit of the Maharaja Sayajirao University (MSU) has announced to organise a seminar on India's macroeconomic management in the context of 'global slowdown' on December 6.

MSU's RBI endowment unit is the only research unit instituted to a university in Gujarat.

The seminar will invite discussions on several issues such as global slowdown and its impact on the financial market, and issues faced by the Indian stock market with the Indian industrial and retail sectors in the face of recession.

RBI endowment unit officials said the event is a timely endeavour to focus on the challenges and strengths of the Indian economy in the backdrop of the global economic meltdown.

The last date to register as a participating expert is November 29.

Heading: ‘Untreated disposal into Vishwamitri river needs to be checked’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Nanod police on Tuesday arrested an orthopaedic, Naishad Parmar on charge of being negligent while operating upon one Daulatsinh Gohil, which led to his death some four months ago. Dr Parmar was later released in the day.

Inspector T K Patel of the Nanod police station said: "Gohil was driving a motorcycle at Rajpipla when an accident occurred and he fractured his foot."

He added: "He was taken to Parmar's hospital, who operated upon him without consulting any physician and without administering anesthesia."

A patient can be operated upon only after a physician gives a health certificate giving details of his blood pressure and blood sugar level. However, no such precaution was taken in Gohil's case, which eventually led to his death.

Heading: MSU, Health dept to help UK cater to diaspora’s mental health problems - Indian Express
Content:
The Vadodara Municipal Corporation's (VMC's) project to clean the Vishwamitri has taken a head start. But its perennial problem of continuous disposal of untreated city sewage into the river also needs to be addressed.

As the city's daily water consumption amounts to 300 million litres per day, over 80 per cent of the water goes to the sewage and only 60 per cent of the sewage is disposed of with treatment. With a major amount of the direct disposal coming from the 4,000 slum pockets by the riverside, the disruption of the drainage lines in many areas has resulted in direct disposal of the sewage.

In many areas when the drainage line is disrupted, domestic sewage is directly diverted to three main drainage lines — Ruparel, Masiya and Bhukhi. "During breakdown of the lines, there is no option but to direct domestic disposal to the drainage line to prevent overflowing. Drainage is directly connected to the river, which disposes untreated sewage," said a VMC official on condition of anonymity.

There are also cases of illegal drainage connection in many areas. VMC's work in the Manjalpur area has been in progress for the last one year and the municipal corporation has provided direct drainage disposal to the area," said VMC opposition leader Chirag Zaveri.

Admitting the fact, city mayor Balkrishna Shukla said: "Some of the lines had to be given by the municipal corporation because of certain circumstances, and not by choice. But with the new sewage treatment plant, we hope to treat 100 per cent of the city's sewage before disposing it."

Heading: Between him and him - Indian Express
Content:
In Association with the UK National Health Services (NHS) Trust and Huddersfield University, the Gujarat Health Department and MSU Faculty of Social Work is exploring possibilities of catering to the mental health problems of 30 per cent adult Gujarati NRIs settled in South West Yorkshire for the last two generations.

Most of the Gujarati NRIs settled in Dewsbury and Batley areas of SW Yorkshire belong to the Muslim community from the Alipore area of Navsari district.

A group of six mental health experts from Ahmedabad, Navsari along with Prof. Aruna Khasgiwala, MSU Dean FSW, visited SW Yorkshire around 10 days ago to discuss the various mental issues of the adult Gujarati population.

Prof Khasgiwala told Newsline: "It is probably for the first time that the NHS and Huddersfield University has given the green signal to FSW students to undertake field work in SW Yorkshire in those areas which have more NRI population."

Social workers serve as the trainers to solve the mental health issues. According to said Prof. Khasgiwala, this will be a different kind of approach where the students will be acquainted with different kind of methods in tackling community mental health services in the UK.

She said: "We are yet to materialise this effort on paper."

During their visit, the experts also met elderly Gujarati NRIs, who had dementia problem, at a Day Care Centre in the UK.

Meanwhile, MSU Vice-Chancellor Prof Ramesh Goyal said, "The University will meet the FSW and discuss the steps on how to formalise this effort as soon as possible."

Incidentally, it was last year that the Director of NW Yorkshire NHS Trust, Mike Young, visited Navasari district to know about the multicultural, spiritual and family roots in Alipore which are leading to problems of dementia among the adult Gujarati population.

That time, Young had interacted with the FSW teachers and the experts at the SSG Hospital and had expressed the need for Gujarat based mental health experts to collaborate with the NHS Trust to help solve the mental health issues among the Gujarati NRI population.

Heading: Wok the Talk - Indian Express
Content:
Ace photographer Swapan Parekh gets personal in his first solo show

A frame stuns in the very beginning with a silent yet striking homage to his mother — two pairs of feet that are a world apart from each other, a synthesis of structure and symmetry against the background of a deathly grey butterfly. Commercial photographer and World Press Photo jury member Swapan Parekh's exhibition "Between Me and I" at Photo Ink gallery is a much-awaited solo show from the reputed artist after almost 25 years of journeys with the camera.

"Colour is very tough as a narrative," exclaimed a cheerful Parekh who has put up this exhibition after two years of work. Having studied at the International Center for Photography in New York, Parekh won the first prize at the World Press Photo in 1994 for a spot news photograph. Back in India, he moved into advertising and commercial photography and established a very successful career.

"Between Me and I" is his most personal and in-depth work into the theatre of his mind. "I would call it collective wisdom and nothing has been more pleasurable than doing this," he says. As one closely studies the photographs, it is not just the content but the peace and clarity in composition that amazes. Each photograph is as detailed in depth as it is casual in character. For instance, even though the exhibition is not obviously a series, on closer inspection, there is coherence in recurring themes such as alphabets, animal forms, symbolic elements and colour. Images kept getting added to the exhibition even two weeks ago as Parekh kept shooting what his mind allowed.

"'Between Me and I' is exactly what it sounds like. It is that tangential space, that parallel aesthetic that I realised while on a commercial shoot, in the middle of a holiday or simply at a gathering of friends at home," explains Parekh.

Parekh's images fuse several contemporary issues in his frames. For instance, India's nuclear policy flashing in the news is juxtaposed with a pigeon in one photograph. Another frame shows a statue of Dr Ambedkar in a monsoon-drenched town of South India.

The display in the gallery was chosen carefully. Spaces were painted white to fuse into the simple, white frames and the size of the prints was deliberately kept medium. "The whole experience was liberating and brought me immense peace. I deliberately kept the images a little short of being obvious and smart using only conventional dark room techniques of correction," said Parekh.

A record turnout from the photographic fraternity included Raghu Rai and close friend Mahendra Sinh. Their presence was testimony to the fact that Parekh's work has become a landmark in contemporary colour work in India.

The exhibition travels to the prestigious Foam Foto Museum in Amsterdam in a slightly larger format and also to Chatterjee and Lal in Mumbai next month. To sum up the experience, Parekh says, "This photographic process is still happening as a life-time project and the control is in my hands finally." Perfectly concluded for something only between him and him.

The show is on till November 20.

Contact Photoink at 28755940

Heading: First Romance Hero - Indian Express
Content:
Keeping with the trend of appearing on TV reality shows as special guests before a film release, Tusshar Kapoor and Celina Jaitley visited the sets of Voice of India Challenge to promote Golmaal Returns.

To please the saas-bahu audience, Celina ditched her cleavage-revealing outfits for a sober sari and huge Parvati-style bindi.

With her unimpressive career she may just be trying to impress her co-star's sis Ekta Kapoor for a role.

Bummer Tusshar decided to sport a suede jacket even in this Mumbai heat.

Heading: Coaching amid friendly fire - Indian Express
Content:
He made an impact as Ash's loyal brother in Jodhaa Akbar. Now catch Sonu Sood as the romantic lead

Sonu Sood, best remembered as Sujamal in Jodhaa Akbar, is finally playing the romantic lead. He will be seen serenading khallas girl Eesha Koppikhar in Ek Vivah— Aisa Bhi releasing this November. With this film, the 33-year-old actor has two reasons to smile. "I will finally be doing something other than action and I'll get to play the guitar," smiles Sood, who recently visited his family, based in Delhi. Shooting is complete for the Kaushik Ghatak directed film who's previously directed Kyunki saas bhi kabhi bahu thi and Sanjivni. Sood insist the film will be completely different from Ghatak's specialty, of saas bahu dramas. But cheesy family dramas are Rajshri Productions' forte, remember? "I play Prem an aspiring singer from Bhopal who meets Esha and falls in love with her voice. He has to wait for 12 years until he can marry her," says Sood, sounding optimistic about the screen play. Typically, Koppikar's character is simple and blemish free, a pretty girl who plays the harmonium and worships a tulsi plant in her courtyard.

Clichéd though the plot may sound, playing a romantic lead in a Rajshri Production is a big step for a bit actor like Sood. His last outing with romance was with the dud Aashiq Banaya Aapne (2005). And then, he's following in the illustrious footsteps of Salman Khan who also played Prem, in Maine Pyaar Kiya, one of the biggest blockbusters of Indian cinema. "This film has more depth. It traces my character's journey growing up, from college to becoming a man of the world. The movie treats relationships with sensitivity," says Sood. "I'm praying that 10 years down, people count me among the romantic actors in Bollywood," says Sood, with a touch of apprehension. In case Ek Vivah.. doesn't work out, Sood has Dhoondte Reh Jaoge, in which he plays a superstar balancing 11 roles. Some character artist, this.

Heading: No home run  as yet at half marathon - Indian Express
Content:
Athletics in Action's coach Rangam Pamei lost to a team made up of his own students

Zeliangrong FC made their debut in competitive football at the RN Tamchon Memorial Trophy here this year and, on Tuesday, reached the last four beating Athletics in Action (AIA) 4-3 on penalties at the Ambedkar Stadium. But beyond the turf, the match took 'friendly rivalry' to a new meaning.

And AIA coach Rangam Pamei — who also doubles up as their playmaker — was not upset at losing out. Not surprising, since the opposition was also made up of his own students, players who, till last year, had been his team mates. "More than half of their players are my students. In fact, all of them played for AIA last year in this tournament. This year they decided to play under the banner of a students' union, with my permission. Obed (Kamei), Akhon Mei and Adam (Gangmei) still come to my institution for practice," Pamei said after the match.

Pamei, a former Hansraj College skipper (1997-98) and Goans Club player (1995-98), instead said that having a 'breakaway' group was actually a blessing in disguise, since it gave "other students an opportunity to play in this tournament. And as first-timers, I think, we have done a remarkable job," he added.

True, given that they had managed to hold their own against an opposition that had as many as six professionals -- DJ Kabui (City Football Club), G Kamei (Garhwal Heroes), Obed Kamei (Shimla Youngs) and Jacky (City Football Club). And the fact that the 33-year old Pamei, despite his age, was on field for the entire duration, keeping a check on the substitutions.

"Taking the field with your students is fun. Of course, I don't keep running like them. But while going for every move they (the players) follow my instructions. For example I may not be involved in the attacking line, but I keep directing them on the passes," he said.

With a stake in both teams that took to the field on Tuesday, and having proved that there is no dearth of talent in either team, the midfielder-cum-coach wants recognition for his club (Athletes in Action). "We need to get recognised by the state body. We approached them earlier, but they said there are already too many clubs playing under various categories of the DSA (Delhi Soccer Association) League and we have to wait," he said.

NK Bhatia, secretary of the DSA, admitted that there was a long waiting list for approval. "There are already so many teams waiting. Not all of them have proper papers or experience fitting our requirements. There are many fake clubs who apply just for the sake of getting recognised. We will conduct some sessions for all such clubs in the coming weeks after modifying a few criteria for recognition," says Bhatia.

Heading: Solanki in cruise mode - Indian Express
Content:
With just a little over a fortnight to go for the Airtel Delhi Half Marathon, the organisers are yet to get the list of Indian participants even as they seem to have, more or less, finalised on the names of foreign participants.

Confirming this, the organisers said since it was the prerogative of the Athletics Federation of India (AFI) they could do nothing but to wait for the AFI to release the list of names in the men and women's categories for the prestigious event scheduled to be held on November 9.

Unlike in the case of Indian participants, the organisers need not look up to the individual federations or, for that matter, the IAAF, though it is the golden label event approved and recognised by the world body. All the foreign participants, particularly the Kenyans, the Tanzanians or the Ethiopians, are handled by a single agent or a group of agencies that process the list of available marathon runners and fix them up on behalf of the organisers.

Vivek Singh of the Procam, the organisers of the event, said that there are over 18,000 participants who have registered for the event while a few thousand more will be representing various corporates. "Forty-three teams from 36 corporates have already registered to swell the number and we are still counting as we have not closed entries for the corporates," he said.

The list of foreign athletes that he released on Tuesday has fewer top names as most of them seemed to be either pace-makers or, at best, second or third string runners from the poor African nations. Nevertheless, last year's winners in both sections will return, he said.

But, as has been customary, the organsiers have roped in two legendary athletes--one of them is Sir Richard Hadle — to add glamour to the event. If it was Javier Sotomayor last year, it will be Jackie-Joyner Kersee this year. The Cuban high jumper was the biggest draw last year and, hopefully, the US track queen will fill the void to give the extra push to the Delhi event this time.

The prize pool, upped to $210,000, is attractive and even if the Indians don't come anywhere near the second or third-string foreign participants, the former can still hit a pay dirt as there is a separate prize money category for the top-10 finishers among Indians.

Heading: Diwali melas lose sparkle due to security concerns - Indian Express
Content:
Sweta Solanki continued her good run in the women's National tennis championship, scoring an easy win against Tamil Nadu's Kesika Jayapalan 6-1, 6-1 in the second round at the DLTA Complex on Tuesday.

The second seed Delhi girl had no problems getting past Jayapalan with her impressive court coverage, making her opponent work hard and run all around. Jayapalan had no answers to Solanki's agility, struggling to hold her own serves and managing to win just two games in the match that was over in less than an hour.

Up next for Solanki, though, is C Shweta Rana, who has been hitting good form this week. Having come through the qualifiers, Rana continued her winning streak with an impressive 7-5, 6-4 upset win over eighth seed Treta Bhattacharya.

This was Rana's fifth match in a row this week, but the gritty girl made sure there were no hiccups in her way to advancing to the next round. Rana attacked from the start, going a break up in the second game itself. But that was before Bhattacharya decided to not let things run away and broke back in the fifth game, then levelled scores at 5-5.

Rana finally capitalised on her strong baseline play and accurate forehands to win the first set, then Bhattacharya's edgy serve and two double faults to eventually wrap up the match in one hour 25 minutes.

In other singles matches, seventh seed Geeta Manohar got past wild card Gopika Kapoor 7-6 (7), 6-1 while Sayali Bhilare of Maharashtra upset third seed Abhilasha Ahuja of Haryana 6-0, 7-5.

Other results (doubles, second round): Sagarika Phadke/Sonal Phadke bye; Sowjanya Bavisetti/Sindhu NIla Partheepan bt Shilpi Jaiswal/Shruti Jaiswal 6-0, 6-1; Prarthana Prathap/Anushree Thammanna bt Baljinder Kaur/Renuka Keshwani 6-1, 6-3; Arantxa Andrady/Sayali Bhilare bt Sadhana Athreya/Likitha Shetty 6-2, 6-1; Ratnika Batra/Sweta Solanki bt Kesika Jayapalan/Dipti Srivastava 6-2, 6-4; Treta Bhattacharya/Shalini Sahoo bt Shweta Rana/Arushi Sharma 6-1, 6-4; Tanvi Gupta/Richa Valecha bt Vishika Chhetri/geeta Manohar 2-6, 6-2, 10-8; Jilke Nelord/Harshini reddy/ bt Abhilasha Ahuja/Rani Smita Jain 1-6, 6-1, 10-8.

Heading: With fewer melas this time, Gurgaon officials play safe - Indian Express
Content:
Security concerns are forcing Delhi Police to clamp down on Diwali melas and bazaars this festive season. Most organisers are finding it difficult to meet the stringent regulations drawn up by the police, keeping in mind the recent blasts. Due to the mandatory security guidelines this year, several Diwali melas in South and Central Delhi have been cancelled.

These include the famous melas of Sundar Nagar, GK-II, Vasant Vihar, Karol Bagh and Defence Colony. The police have drawn up a list of musts for Diwali melas, which include adequate and secure parking space, a fence around pandals of a height set by the police, CCTV surveillance, metal detectors at entry and exit points, the use of non-inflammable material at the melas and adequate deployment of security. In addition, only a fixed number of stalls would be allowed, as per the availability of space.

"Security arrangements are necessary and mela organisers will have to adhere to them," said Delhi Police spokesman Rajan Bhagat.

A number of RWAs have called off the event deterred by the list of prerequisites.

"It is better to take necessary precautions rather than taking a risk. In addition, since the response of customers in other markets and melas seems to be lukewarm, we have decided to cancel the mela this year," said Atul Bhargava of the Sunder Nagar Resident Welfare Association.(RWA).

The mela organised by the Defence Colony RWA has met a similar fate, with permission to hold the mela being denied to the organisers this year. "While the mela has become increasingly popular over the last few years, the security parameters this year could not be met by us," said Harjeet Singh, president of the A-Block RWA.

The fate of the Vasant Vihar mela still hangs in a balance. Vasant Club, the organising body of the mela, to be held on the October 26, has sent in an application to the Delhi Police, and is waiting for permission.

Others have decided to go ahead with their plans. The Blind Relief Association (BRA) has gone ahead with its annual Diwali Bazaar next to Oberoi Hotel. The event, commonly known as Blind School Diwali Bazaar, is known to attract people from all over Delhi.

The BRA is run by a managing committee headed by Justice (Retd) A S Anand, former Chief Justice of the Supreme Court. "We earn about Rs 35 to 40 lakh," said K C Pandey, executive secretary of the association. While security provisions has meant additional expenditure, the association has decided to give a go-ahead.

"The number of stalls this year has been decreased to allow for more space, and emergency exits have been increased," said Pandey.

Heading: Councillors missing from duty as they line up for Assembly tickets - Indian Express
Content:
This Diwali, be prepared to have the option of visiting just a handful of melas in your neighbourhood, Gurgaon officials have warned.

Citing the recent blasts in the Capital and several mishaps that are a regular occurrence at such events, specially at stalls selling firecrackers, the Gurgaon police, the Municipal Corporation of Gurgaon (MCG) and the Deputy Commissioner's office have earmarked just seven spots for this year's event from October 26 to 28.

Authorities will be keeping a close watch at these venues to ensure that rules are adhered to, with adequate firefighting equipment kept at hand, NOCs from the police and the fire department, non-inflammable tent material as well as emergency exits at the venues.

District Magistrate Deepti Umashankar has issued orders under Section 144 of the CrPC regarding the sale of crackers on the occasion, said officials. "Sales of crackers would be allowed only at certain spots with temporary licences issued to them. Anybody found selling crackers (and other explosive material) without obtaining the necessary licence, or at the places other than specified by the DM would be punished under provisions of Section 188 of the IPC," said Vatsal Vashisht, City Magistrate, Gurgaon. Each stall would be allowed to keep upto 25 kg of firecrackers, he added.

"We have asked the license issuing authorities to make sure that the areas are large and open grounds and each stall has firefighting equipment. Fire tenders and police personnel would be deployed to ensure of the safety of people," said Joint Commissioner of Police, Manjit Singh Ahlawat.

The MCG has proposed three additional venues — namely Sukhrali village, Jharsa village and New Colony, which are awaiting approval. The city magistrate and the two SDM offices would be issuing licences from October 25 to 28.

Heading: Year after airline engineer’s death, finally a suspect - Indian Express
Content:
With Assembly elections just weeks away, the number of councillors attending meetings at the MCD is has seen a huge dip. The priority of municipal councillors has shifted from the Town Hall to their respective party offices.

Several MCD councillors are hoping to get a ticket to contest the elections and are busy going that extra mile to ensure that their names make it to the final list.

"Many councillors are vying for the ticket. I myself could not make it to the House meeting last week. The focus has now shifted to the party office," said Congress councillor from the Mehrauli ward Satbir Singh who hopes to get a green signal to fight for the Mehrauli Assembly seat.

Leader of Opposition Jai Kishan Sharma reiterated Singh's point: "It is true. Everyone wants to move to the next level. Some councillors may not be eyeing the Assembly ticket. But everyone wants to attend party meetings, as a lot of field work needs to be done at the this point of time. Hence a lot of councillors are missing the proceedings at the Town Hall."

Some councillors, however, say low attendance is nothing new for the Town Hall, come poll season. The story is the same during every elections. "Assembly elections may be one reason. But because of the Election Code of Conduct, no major decisions takes place this time either. That is also another reason why a lot of councillors do not show up. It is assumed that a lot of things will be left pending till the elections are over," said Congress councillor and ex-mayor Farhad Suri, another ticket hopeful.

At any given meeting of the House, more than 80 percent of the councillors are in attendence. After election dates were announced, the attendance fell by fifty percent. "About fifty percent of the councillors were missing from the House last week. The situation is the same every time before the elections," said a senior MCD official.

MCD Standing Committee Chairman Vijender Gupta also agrees that there has been a massive fall in the attendance count. "The effect was clearly seen in the very first meeting after poll dates were announced. Only nine councillors attended the meeting of the Standing Committee. It is, however, a matter of just a month. Assembly elections would not stop the working of the MCD. House meetings will go on as usual," said Gupta.

Heading: Students battle it out at Innovision - Indian Express
Content:
Exactly a year after Sanskriti Sinha, 26, aeronautical engineer with a private airline was found run over on the tarmac of domestic terminal at IGI Airport, the police have found a suspect: the driver of a 'follow-me' vehicle of the Delhi International Airport Limited (DIAL).

According to sources, the driver was rounded up after investigating officials found discrepancies in report of the first polygraph test conducted on him. But since the police do not have any concrete scientific or forensic evidence in Sinha's death, they have sought the nod for a second polygraph test on the suspect, sources said. The second lie-detector test would be conducted soon, they said.

Sinha worked with Air Deccan, now merged with Kingfisher. She had died on October 22 last year.

She was crushed by a blunt object, suspected to be the bumper of a heavy vehicle. The police suspected heavy vehicles running inside the airport — luggage trolleys, ground-handling vehicles, ladders, flight catering or 'Follow-Me' vehicles was involved in the incident. All such vehicles underwent technical inspection.

Now, the police have established it was a 'Follow-Me' vehicle.

After shortlisting several suspects, the police recently chanced upon three — all of them drivers. Polygraph tests have been done on all of them. "All vehicles under suspicion were inspected by teams from the Central Forensic Science Laboratory (CFSL) but we did not get any clues. We questioned several drivers thoroughly, as it has to be the driver of a vehicle at the airport responsible for the accident," said Amulya Patnaik, Joint Commissioner of Police (Operations). Some 15 vehicles were checked by the police.

According to officers, nothing concrete has emerged against the suspected driver yet; there is also no evidence against any of the vehicles inspected.

Officials also confirmed they had not come across any motive behind Sinha's death. "There is no clear scientific evidence in the case but we are working on various aspects," Patnaik said. "We have reviewed the case and questioned many people again. I am hopeful that the case would lead to a logical conclusion within a few months."

Sinha was found dead, with her head crushed and neck dislocated; she was to get engaged the same week.

It was earlier learnt that some vehicle moving on the IGI airside hit her. Police registered a case under IPC Section 304 (culpable homicide) against an unknown driver as it was found that the driver's negligence caused Sinha's death.

The technician, it was found, had complied with all safety regulations and was wearing a high-visibility jacket to be easily picked up by drivers of vehicles on the tarmac.

The police began their investigation by questioning several employees of the DIAL, Air Deccan, the drivers of vehicles that run on taxiways — such as luggage trolleys, ground-handling vehicles, ladders, flight catering and 'Follow Me' vehicles. Around 200 people were questioned but they could not crack the case. Forensic reports did not show bloodstains on tyres of any vehicle inspected.

Heading: Malhotra attacks Congress leaders over support to Jamia encounter-accused - Indian Express
Content:
At Innovision '08, held at the Netaji Subhash Institute of Technology (NSIT), challenging competitions kept the budding engineers on their toes. Events such as 'B-Plan' had future planners and corporate leaders presenting proposals for startups in fields as varied as machine technology and agricultural development.

'Black Pearl', the motorboat designing competition tested the mechanical skills of competitors. Teams used plastic bottles, lunch boxes, tin cans among other material to prepare their boats.

'Robowars', a competition between battery-powered robots created by the students was another highly popular contest. 'Junkyard Wars' challenged the participants' ability to create a functioning model out of scrap. 'Admaker' tested wacky ways of creating an ad campaign on products like rolling pins, mosquito repellants, toilet cleaners, among others.

The competitions were not limited only to college-goers, 'School Bag', a quiz and technical paper presentation saw senior school students from a number of Delhi schools participate.

Another event was the Auto Expo held on the second day. G O D S (Group Of Delhi Superbikers) burned the tracks with their Hayabusas, Yamahas and YZFs.

Heading: Delhi Police, DIAL to join hands, increase security outside airport - Indian Express
Content:
A day after Shiv Sena mouthpiece Saamna raked up the Jamia Nagar encounter in an editorial, the Bharatiya Janata Party on Tuesday mounted an attack on the Congress over its "politicians supporting terrorists" in Delhi.

With just over a month left for the Assembly elections, Vijay Kumar Malhotra, the party's chief ministerial candidate, termed the serial blasts in Delhi a failure of the Congress government and attacked Delhi Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit and senior Congress leaders for going soft on the alleged terrorists arrested the encounter.

"The Congress aims to woo jehadis for a win in the coming elections," Malhotra said. Criticising senior leaders like Kapil Sibal, Shakeel Ahmed, Mohsina Kidwai, and Sheila Dikshit for supporting terrorists, Malhotra said, "The government in Delhi has failed to act on the issue of terror. Support to terrorists has demoralised the police force and the family of Inspector Mohan Chand Sharma killed in the encounter."

The Saamna editorial demanded a ban on the Samajwadi Party for extending overt support to extremist organisations like SIMI that is allegedly supporting the residents of Jamia Nagar in Delhi. The piece said Jamia Nagar "has developed into a mini Pakistan".

Toeing a similar line, Malhotra charged, "Senior leaders of the Congress and some other parties have spoken in support of terrorists who have already confessed to their crimes. This is only for political mileage." Malhotra said the silence of Congress chief Sonia Gandhi and Delhi CM Sheila Dikshit's support to Jamia Nagar residents "exposes their vote bank politics". He also criticised the government on the education front and made pre-poll promises. "The Delhi government has failed to establish colleges in the Capital in the past decade."

He said his party would open two new medical colleges and at least 50 other colleges in the Capital. "Students need to have access to quality institutions apart from the ones already there in Delhi University and the party will work towards that," he said.

Heading: IGI in the grip of a network of touts - Indian Express
Content:
All taxi drivers to be registered, DIAL to install CCTV cameras at departure and arrival halls

Following the latest incident of abduction and murder of a Saudi Arabia-based businessman by two cabbies outside Delhi airport, Delhi Police have at last woken up to need of increasing security outside the airport.

While the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) provides security inside the terminals, Delhi Police, together with DIAL, will make stringent security arrangements outside the airport. In the second meeting in a week on Tuesday, senior DIAL officials and Delhi Police planned several measures to rectify the poor security arrangements.

Newsline gets a preview of the new arrangements:
* DIAL will install CCTV cameras outside airport terminals at the departure and arrival halls which are within the range of parking lots, prepaid taxi booths and the main road in front of the halls. Surveillance cameras function only in the airport at the moment. Though the number of CCTV cameras to be installed has not been decided yet, officials say around 15 such cameras would be installed at the domestic terminal.
* The Delhi Police have asked DIAL to keep repeating announcements related to security at terminals so that passengers remain aware about what to do after coming out of the terminal. Delhi Police officials would also attend to the passengers.
* DIAL has also been asked to display precautionary boards so that passengers are not lured by unauthorised persons or touts.
* All taxis would be registered at police stations and their owners would have to submit proper documents.
* Delhi Police have also asked taxi operators to register themselves in the booths at the airport and provide details of the number of drivers on each taxi. Details of private taxi owners and drivers would also be kept with the traffic police.
* Delhi traffic police have been asked not to allow any taxi driver, private or prepaid, to park their vehicles on the road or call passengers themselves.
* Palam and IGI Police officials have been asked to intensify checks outside terminals. The number of officers on duty will be increased. The presence of cops at peak hour would be nearly doubled.
* The police have already started making a list of people who have a criminal background or are suspicious by nature. Delhi Police are also working on providing identity cards to all drivers and maintaining route records of all of them. Any unauthorised vehicle would not be allowed to operate.
* DIAL will also provide volunteers at the terminals. "These arrangements would be in place very soon. Meetings are being held with the officials concerned and taxi operators. We're trying to make sure that when a passenger comes out of the airport, he knows what to do next," said Amulya Patnaik, Joint Commissioner of Police (Operations).

Heading: After film, One Night rings in again: title in Hindi - Indian Express
Content:
Ensuring safe transport for passengers has become an issue of major concern for the Delhi Police and the Delhi International Airport Limited (DIAL) after the latest incident of kidnap and killing of a Saudi-based NRI businessman by two cabbies on October 10.

At a security meeting on Tuesday, Delhi Police have asked DIAL to display precautionary boards so that passengers are not misled by touts.

Prepaid taxi drivers outside the domestic wing of Indira Gandhi International Airport say passengers don't trust them anymore.

"The man who was killed took a private taxi. Even as the police keep denying their presence, touts move around openly here. The murder is blemish on all the other taxi drivers who go only through the prepaid procedure," said a prepaid taxi driver, lined up on number 17 as he awaited his turn in the queue which had almost 500 taxis. These are all commercial taxis recognised by the Delhi Government. Each of them has to pay Rs 10 per round to the traffic police every day.

The system looks simple. While getting out of Terminal 1B of the airport, passengers need to get a prepaid slip from Counter no. 4 of the terminal. A group 4 guard checks the slip, and takes the passenger to the next waiting taxi.

While getting out of the airport area, the taxi driver needs to produce the prepaid slip and take a clearance from the traffic police kiosk that is supposed to check the presence of touts. The policeman on duty takes down the journey details and allows the driver to go.

"We are working on providing identity cards to all the drivers and keeping driving records of all of them. Any unauthorised vehicle would not be allowed to operate near the airport," said Amulya Patnaik, Joint Commissioner of Police (Operations).

The police have also asked taxi operators to attend to passengers as per slips, register themselves in the booths and provide details of the number of drivers on each taxi.

"Private taxi owners and drivers would be registered with the traffic police, Palam Airport and International Airport police stations," said Patnaik.

"Most touts works in connivance with the local police, traffic police and even the airport officials. But it is sad the passengers have started feeling insecure in taxis due to the presence of criminals who pose as private taxi drivers," said Major Singh, former president of the Delhi Airport Taxi Drivers' Union.

Sagar M, a passenger from Mumbai, had a different tale to tell. "I need to come to Delhi often and prefer prepaid taxis to avoid touts. But last week when I came, the security person at the airport took me to a taxi with a private number, though I had a prepaid slip," he said.

Nine days after Gurgaon police found an unidentified body on National Highway-8 and later learnt it was that of an NRI businessman, the Delhi Police arrested two private taxi drivers for the abduction, robbery and murder of K T Shameer.

The 39-year-old cloth merchant from Riyadh was abducted from outside IGI Airport by private cabbies on October 10 evening. He was robbed and the body thrown in the bushes on Delhi-Jaipur highway near Manesar.

Heading: At St Stephen’s, asking questions was not good: Rahul Gandhi - Indian Express
Content:
Chetan Bhagat did not consider himself an Indian author, cutting across masses, in the true sense of the term all this time. With the launch of the Hindi translation of his best-selling book One Night @ the Call Centre, he feels he will now be more widely read.

"My books are originally in English but now that they've been translated and published in Hindi, I feel I'm finally being able to communicate to the youth across all of India," said Bhagat who spoke Hinglish a little self-consciously at the launch at the Constitution Club last evening. He also mentioned Hello!, the film based on the second book while all eyes were actually on the chief guest for the evening, senior BJP leader L K Advani.

Sharing the stage with Advani was actress Gul Panag who stars in the film, and director Atul Agnihotri.

There was little talk of the book, the focus of the evening for Bhagat was the "politics of difference". "What is taking place in Mumbai right now is not right. I've been told that as an author, I have my finger of the pulse of today's youth. But they need opportunities, otherwise they get frustrated and then they don't think of the country. When Advaniji was in office, one knew that things were being taken care of," said Bhagat who further stressed on the requirement of a "middle path" and a "moderate voice" in the political circles.

Panag voiced the importance of the upcoming elections and how it was the duty of the youth to cast their votes. Agnihotri spoke sparingly but not before adding that he had received a lot of love from Advaniji.

"Rupa publishes both Chetan's books and mine. I'm here, thanks to them. It is a different matter that my books are not as popular as his and lend themselves to serious conversations and not popular cinema," said Advani. He went on to recount how he still remembered Dale Carnegie's How to Win Friends and Influence People that he read at 15.
