Content:
Chelsea have another chance to show off their new expansive style on Wednesday when AS Roma visit Stamford Bridge in the Champions League.

In the short time that Luiz Felipe Scolari has been in charge, the Brazilian has gone a long way to doing what both his predecessors failed at — which is to win over the neutrals. Gone is the siege mentality adopted by Jose Mourinho during his incredibly successful time in charge of the club while the dour and brief Avram Grant era is a fast fading memory.

Scolari has been charm personified since taking one of the toughest jobs in British football and his side, flying at the top of the Premier League, are playing with a smile rather than ruthless efficiency.

The 5-0 victory at Middlesbrough on Saturday, completed with a long list of absentees, was a master class in passing and movement that sent alarm bells ringing around the country.

Skipper John Terry spoke of the different philosophy that Scolari has brought to west London. "In the first two years after Jose Mourinho took over we had a strong mentality where we'd go to places and shut up shop to get the three points," Terry said in the Daily Telegraph.

"Now we're eager to really push on and get that second goal and kill the game. It's very enjoyable to play under him."

The one blip so far this season for Chelsea was a difficult night in Romania in their last Group A clash when they could only draw 0-0 with newcomers CFR Cluj. However, with Roma having already lost to Cluj, Chelsea can take command of their destiny with victory against the Italians who are smarting from a 4-0 thumping by Inter Milan at the weekend and who have bad memories of recent trips to England.

Chelsea could have Petr Cech back in goal after he missed the Middlesbrough match with a leg injury while midfielder Joe Cole may also return.

Liverpool confident

In another fixture on Wednesday, Liverpool take on Atletico Madrid who are struggling after three consecutive defeats in La Liga. The Reds, in contrast, arrive full of confidence despite the absence of injured striker Fernando Torres, who misses the chance to return to his former home where he is still idolised by the fans.

On Saturday, Liverpool twice trailed at home to Wigan Athletic before winning 3-2 thanks to a late goal from Dutch workhorse Dirk Kuyt who will lead the line on Wednesday. Kuyt lacks the finesse and speed of Torres but whenever asked to play a more central role he rarely disappoints.

Heading: Dempo’s AFC dream ends with 4-1 loss - Indian Express
Content:
After years of inspiring football fans around the world, FC Barcelona will on Wednesday face the lesser-known Swiss club which claims to have been the inspiration behind the creation of the Spanish giants.

Swiss champions FC Basel have organised an exhibition at their stadium museum ahead of the Champions League Group C encounter, showing how businessman and former player Hans Gamper migrated to Spain before founding FC Barcelona in 1899.

According to legend, Gamper may even have based Barcelona's striking half red, half blue team strip on Basel's near identical colours which had been in use since the Swiss club's own founding six years earlier. "Sadly there is no historical document proving that Barca's shirts were based on FC Basel's, but the circumstantial evidence is quite compelling," Swiss Sport Museum collection leader Hans-Dieter Gerber said. "The fact that Gamper went to Spain and set up FC Barcelona who started playing with the same distinctive colours he had played in suggests the story is at least credible."

Heading: Bad weather cuts short Siachen trek - Indian Express
Content:
On at least three occasions in the run-up to the Railway Recruitment Board's examination on October 19, where candidates from North India were attacked by Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) activists, the Railway Protection Force (RPF) Headquarters in New Delhi had informed the Maharashtra Police that it was anticipating trouble at many of the examination centres and wanted the local police to beef-up security.

In one of its communications to Navi Mumbai Police Commissioner Ramrao Wagh, the RPF had expressed concern over "certain local political activists and hoodlums" who could target applicants from outside Maharashtra and had demanded that sufficient police strength be made available to guard the exam centres.

The October 19 written exam was conducted to fill up 518 posts in the categories of enquiry-cum-reservation clerks, goods guards and assistant station masters. Out of the 2.29 lakh applicants, only 26,000-odd could appear for the exam following the violence perpetrated by MNS workers. The first missive was sent on October 3 wherein the RPF informed the state police about the examination giving out a list of all the examination centres. "We told the Maharashtra Police that a similar problem had taken place during railway exams in 2006 and that ample force was to be deployed at the 144 exam centres in Mumbai," a top RPF official told The Indian Express. This communication was then followed up with two more letters, the first one sent on October 9 and the second on October 16 when RPF officials, both at the headquarter and state level underlined the "possibility of a disruption".

RPF officials also said that the stone-pelting on applicants in Thane on October 19 were recorded on camera by the MNS workers who later sent the video footage to all the news channels.

Heading: Less time at hand, J-K parties feel poll jitters - Indian Express
Content:
After a gruelling 70-km trek up the world's highest battlefield, braving temperatures as low as -25 degrees Celsius, members of the second civilian expedition to the Siachen Glacier returned to the base camp on Sunday.

With bad weather and heavy snow hitting the region over the past week, the expedition had to stop 18 km short of the designated target of Kumar Post, which marks the half-way point on the glacier.

It took members of the expedition, which started from base camp on October 12, eight days to trek up to Camp III —one camp short of Kumar Post—and return to base.

While the expedition started on a good note from base camp, the weather turned bad after the third day. With heavy snowfall and a low cloud cover reducing visibility to nil on the glacier, the expedition got stuck at Camp II for two days.

While most expedition members suffered from only minor side effects, a student from the Chail Military School, Amit Kumar, had to be evacuated by helicopter after he collapsed due to the extreme temperatures at Camp I. For the remaining members, the five-day training at the Siachen base camp paid off with no one suffering any major injuries.

The trek, organised by the Army Mountaineering Institute, involved a 70-km climb to the glacier and back. The expedition, which for the first time included five female participants, reached heights of over 15,000 feet and followed the traditional route used by the Army to induct soldiers on the Saltoro Ridge.

Heading: MUMBAI MENACE - Indian Express
Content:
The women's wing of a Sangh Parivar outfit has demanded that the Catholic nun who was allegedly raped in Kandhamal be arrested for making frivolous accusations if she does not come forward to assist the police investigation.

The 29-year-old nun, an administrator with a pastoral training centre in Kandhamal, was allegedly raped and paraded semi-naked on August 25 during the riots in Kandhamal. She fled the state thereafter and has refused to assist the investigators in identifying the accused, claiming that she has "lost faith" in the state police.

On Tuesday, the Rashtriya Sevika Samiti, the women's wing of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, questioned the authenticity of the nun's claims. "Why is she not showing up despite pleas from the CID? If her allegations are true then the rapist should be given capital punishment. But if she refuses to cooperate she should be immediately arrested. This kind of behaviour lowers the image of women in society," said Swati Suchitra Mohapatra, zonal organising secretary of the Samiti at a dharna here.

Mohapatra also compared the Kandhamal incident with the unverified rape allegations made by nun Jacqueline Mary in Baripada in 1999. "Subsequent police investigations revealed that what Sister Mary said in the FIR was not true, and was a made up story," she said.

The Samiti leaders also demanded the arrest of those involved in the murder of Mata Bhaktimaye, who was gunned down with Swami Laxmanananda Saraswati and three others in Jalespeta on August 23.

Meanwhile, senior VHP leader Swami Jeevan Chaitanya's hunger strike entered its second day on Tuesday. Swami Chaitanya and 70 other Hindu godmen also held a yajna amid wishes that the conspirators behind Saraswati's killers be brought to book. The seers have been protesting here with a charter of five demands. According to them, shortly before his death Saraswati had named two men, claiming they were out to murder him. Senior BJP leaders, including national vice president Jual Oram and state president Suresh Pujari, went to the venue of the protest and extended their support to Jeevan Chaitanya.

Heading: parties play politics but under rules, anyone can apply for any post anywhere - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai is no stranger to the violence that has been unleashed in the metropolis the last few days by Raj Thackeray's Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) against migrant jobseekers from other states. Looking back, it all started with the brand of agitational politics that his uncle and Shiv Sena chief, Bal Thackeray, patented in his early years as a politician.

Thackeray Sr left his job as a cartoonist with The Free Press Journal in 1960 and started a Marathi cartoon weekly called Marmik. The situation was ripe for regional and linguistic polarisation as the erstwhile Bombay Presidency had been divided into two linguistic states — Maharashtra and Gujarat. There was a battle for the then Bombay city, with Marathis uniting to demand that the city should remain in Maharashtra. In the ensuing agitations, 105 people lost their lives.

Marathis in the city mostly worked in textile mills, engineering industries and the port. A majority belonged to the working class and were lower-rung white collar employees. The top jobs were largely occupied by non-Marathis.

Bal Thackeray began organising Marathis on the sons-of-the-soil issue. Subsequently, Marmik started an anti-south Indian campaign as people from the southern states thronged the city for jobs and also opened shops and restaurants. Marmik started publishing lists of officials employed by the corporates in an attempt to prove that Marathis were being marginalised and south Indians favoured. Circulation jumped and Thackeray Sr gained.

The Congress was accused of using Thackeray Sr to combat the growing influence of the communists in the trade unions in textile mills; and encouraging him to float the Shiv Sena on June 19, 1966.

The first campaign forcefully taken up by the party was against south Indians. Shiv Sainiks would attack shops and restaurants of south Indians, the so-called "lungiwallahs". Since the party in power apparently wanted to pamper Thackeray Sr, the government was soft on him and seen to be so.

Four decades later, Raj — who walks and talks like his uncle — is playing the same card. The Congress and NCP want to weaken the Shiv Sena, which is the main opposition party. Raj broke away from the Sena to form the MNS in 2006 ostensibly because Thackeray Sr promoted his son, Uddhav, as heir. In a city where the average Marathi family is not able to afford a house, Raj's rhetoric attracts youngsters.

Raj is targeting north Indians because they are the most visible migrants in Mumbai and its outskirts. Besides, after delimitation, the assembly seats in the expanding Mumbai metropolitan area (Mumbai and Thane) has gone up from 47 to 60 — with some dominated by north Indian migrants. The MNS worries that leaders like Mayawati, Lalu Prasad Yadav and Amar Singh may be trying to claw their way in.

Heading: PM in Japan, high hopes for n-ties - Indian Express
Content:
The attack on North Indian candidates appearing for a Railway Recruitment Board exam in Mumbai by Raj Thackeray-led Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) activists, followed by his arrest, has again put the spotlight on the Railway recruitment policy. It isn't the first time that an RRB exam has prompted such attacks; perhaps the deadliest incident was in November 2003 when Biharis were attacked at exam centres in Assam. In the cycle of violence that followed, there were attacks on Assam-bound trains passing through Bihar, followed by targeting of Biharis in Assam. Many lost lives and the Army had to be called out to restore peace. Around the same time, there were attacks on RRB centres in Mumbai. Of course, since there was no MNS then, it was the Shiv Sena and Bal Thackeray spearheading the "sons-of-the-soil" plank. RAGHVENDRA RAO looks at the Railway Recruitment Board exam process and explains that while it is a fertile ground for emotive politics, there is nothing in its guidelines to prevent candidates belonging to a state from applying for jobs advertised anywhere in the country:

What is the history of Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs) in India?

As early as July 1942, a Service Commission with a Chairman and two members was established for recruitment of Subordinate Staff to the then North West Railway. Following a review in 1945, Service Commissions were set up under Railway Board at Mumbai, Calcutta, Madras and Lucknow with the twin function of recruiting Class III staff and also advising General Managers on issues relating to appeals from subordinate staff on disciplinary matters.

In 1948, the Indian Railway Enquiry Committee recommended that they should deal exclusively with recruitments and not appeals. In 1949, a ban was imposed on recruitment in Indian Railways due to financial constraints and the number of commissions got reduced to a single one in Bombay. In 1953-54 when the economic condition of Railway improved, four service commissions were again set up at Bombay, Madras, Allahabad and Calcutta. This was followed by setting up of more Commissions in other parts.

It was in 1983 that seven more commissions were set up at Ahmedabad, Ajmer, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Chandigarh, Jammu and Srinagar (with sitting at Leh) and Trivandrum, to cater to the needs of neglected areas. In 1984 two more service commissions were set up at Malda and Gorakhpur while a full-fledged commission came up in Ranchi to cater to Scheduled Tribes of the area.

In January 1985, Railway Service Commissions were renamed Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs). Currently, 19 RRBs function all over the country, located at Ahmedabad, Ajmer, Allahabad, Bangalore, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Chandigarh, Chennai, Gorakhpur, Guwahati, Jammu and Srinagar, Kolkata, Malda, Mumbai, Muzaffarpur, Patna, Ranchi, Secunderabad and Thiruvananthapuram.

What categories of posts are recruited through RRBs?

Mostly Group C posts are filled up through recruitments made by RRBs. Group D recruitments are made by zonal railways. Most of the 14 lakh railway employees belong to Group C and Group D categories. In fact, 60-70 per cent of posts in each Railway division —there are 67 — fall under Group C.

The Group C posts include posts of Station Master, Assistant Station Master and Assistant Driver. Non Technical Popular Categories include under-graduate categories like Junior Clerk, Account Clerk, Ticket Collector and Commercial Clerk. Graduate Categories include posts of Senior Clerks, Junior Accounts Assistants, Commercial Apprentices, Traffic Apprentices and Enquiry cum Reservation Clerks.

Other posts include those of Apprentice Mechanic, Assistant Shop Superintendent, Junior Engineer, Selection Engineer, Permanent Way Mistriedds (PWM), Draftsman, Chief Draftsman, Staff Nurse, Health/Malaria inspector, Pharmacists, Radiographer, Lab Assistants and Superintendents, Dietician, Catering Supervisors, Finger Print examiner, Artisans, Law Assistant, Teacher, Physiotherapist, Telephone Operator and Stenographer.

Who all can apply?

A person residing anywhere in the country can apply for a job advertised by any of the RRBs, provided he meets the eligibility criteria. Applicants residing in the area catered by a particular RRB do not get any preference. Also, nothing prevents an applicant belonging to one state to apply for a job advertised by an RRB located in another state. The selection process includes job reservation for SCs, STs, OBCs and ex-servicemen.

On the day the MNS attacked North Indians in Mumbai, there were 2.29 lakh applicants giving the RRB exam.

What is the selection process?

Indian Railways is divided into 16 zones, further divided into 67 divisions. As and when job vacancies come up in a division, it places an indent upon its zonal RRB, which then advertises.

The RRBs get employment notifications, calling for applications from eligible candidates, published in national newspapers, Employment News/Rozgaar Samachar. RRBs are bound to get indicative advertisements published in local newspapers too. The time period given to apply in response to notifications is not less than 30 days. The applications received in the time period prescribed are scrutinised with reference to criteria published in the notification.

Following this, the schedule of the written or online examination is published in newspapers and Employment News and the eligible candidates are informed of their date and centre of their examination by call letters.

After the examination, the list of successful candidates is published and successful candidates are also informed by post. Candidates declared successful in Written or Online examination are then called for aptitude test and documents verification. Interviews were eliminated in most RRB examinations since March 18, 1999, reportedly to check nepotism and manipulation.

Heading: POTA repealed, so Gujarat can’t try Godhra accused under that law, rules SC - Indian Express
Content:
For Japan, the only nation to have suffered the wrath of an atom bomb, supporting India at the Nuclear Suppliers Group in Vienna early last month was not an easy decision. But then, it did, underscoring the strategic view Tokyo has of New Delhi. It is in this background that Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's three-day bilateral visit to Tokyo beginning on Tuesday assumes importance with expectations of making significant headway in a civilian nuclear cooperation agreement.

According to sources in the Indian Government, Japan, unlike Russia and the United States, does not have a domestic law that bars nuclear energy cooperation with countries that are non-signatories to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty. "In fact, Japanese export controls, even in high-technology areas, are based more on administrative controls and convention, rather than any domestic legislation," said a source who is part of the PM's official delegation. Singh will discuss these issues with his Japanese counterpart Taro Aso over the next two days.

In the last couple of years, Japan has been busy expanding the list of entities for other countries to facilitate higher imports of sensitive technology. "Our list too has come down by seven," said the source. So, even if no concrete agreement materialises between the two countries, expectations are running high. Nevertheless, a separate agreement between the two countries will help Japanese businesses sell reactors and dual-use technologies for nuclear power plants in India.

It is from a position of strength — having successfully concluded a civilian nuclear deal with the US and emerging largely unscathed from the financial turmoil still unfolding in the US and Europe — that India's high-powered business delegation led by Mukesh Ambani of Reliance Industries Ltd, hopes to push for greater market access to Indian products in Japan. Besides Ambani, ICICI Bank CEO and Confederation of Indian Industry President K V Kamath are also part of the business delegation.

India Inc and the Government will also highlight the $30 billion business opportunity in the civil nuclear energy space to Japanese companies such as Toshiba and Japan Atomic Power Co. Besides the state-owned Nuclear Power Corporation of India Ltd, several other giants such as Larsen & Toubro and Reliance itself intend to foray into nuclear energy through joint ventures with global majors.

However, India is not likely to push Japan too hard to firm up such decisions, since it understands the "emotional issues" that grip Japan in letting any country access sensitive technology.

"Given Japan's unique situation (it has seen five prime ministers in a relatively short time and there is a group that opposes even Japan's own fast-breeder programme), we will let them take their own time. Nevertheless, if Japan wants, it will find a way to be more forthcoming," the source said.

Heading: Rajapaksa brothers head for India, Pak - Indian Express
Content:
In a setback to the Gujarat Government in the Godhra train deaths case, the Supreme Court today held that the POTA review committee's decision to drop charges against the accused under the repealed anti-terror law would be binding on the government and the designated court.

"We hold that since the review committee under Section 2 (3) of the Repealing Act expresses the opinion that there is no prime facie case for proceeding against the accused, in cases in which cognizance has been taken by the court, such cases shall be deemed to have been withdrawn," said the three-member bench headed by Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan.

The decision came on a batch of petitions filed by the accused, challenging the decision to prosecute them under POTA even after the State POTA review committee had held that offence under the anti-terror law could not be made out against them.

Earlier, the Gujarat High Court had dismissed their petition, and their bail applications too were not entertained.

Upholding the constitutionality of the 2004 Act brought for repealing POTA, the Supreme Court today ruled that courts would not adjudicate the opinion given by the POTA review committee. However, the court underlined that the decision was always open for judicial review.

"We make it clear that if the opinion of the review committee is challenged by any aggrieved party in writ proceedings and is set aside, the court where the proceedings were pending will continue with the case as if there had been no such opinion," said the

Bench which also comprised Justices R V Raveendran and Dalveer Bhandari. The trial court has been directed to resume proceedings in the case.

The apex court held that wherever the review commitee holds that the charges under the anti-terror law must be dropped, the case stands withdrawn under POTA. "Once the law made by Parliament specifically states that wherever the review committee is of the opinion that there is no prime facie (case) for proceeding against the accused, the cases shall be deemed to have been withdrawn," it said.

"If the Parliament wanted to make the provisions of Section 2(3) of the Repealing Act subject to Section 321 (withdrawal of prosecution) of the CrPC, it would have been done so by making appropriate provisions thereof. As that has not been done, the plain meaning of words of the legislation has to be given effect to," it said.

Heading: BJP slams Manmohan on economy - Indian Express
Content:
As the UPA government faces the heat on Sri Lanka from its Tamil Nadu allies, Sri Lankan President Mahinda Rajapaksa is sending his two brothers on specific missions to India and Pakistan: while one will talk diplomacy with New Delhi, the other will talk defence in Islamabad.

Officials sources said Rajapaksa's brother, Basil, designated as Senior Advisor to the President, will be visiting Delhi next week. However, the dates are yet to be finalised.

The other brother, Gotabhaya, who is the Lankan Defence Secretary, reached Islamabad today

for a five-day visit. Gotabhaya is scheduled to meet Pakistan Defence Secretary Kamran Rasool, Defence Production Secretary Lieutenant General Shahid Siddiq Tirmizey and other senior defence officials.

In the past couple of years, Colombo has turned to Islamabad for supply of weapons of all kinds, ranging from tanks to small weapons and even ammunitions.

Meanwhile, New Delhi too is considering sending External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee for crucial diplomatic engagement to Lanka. Foreign Secretary Shivshanker Menon has said Mukherjee's trip is "a possibility", although the dates are yet to be finalised.

Heading: SP rules out alliance with Congress in MP - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP on Tuesday launched a scathing attack on Dr Manmohan Singh's financial management, saying the Prime Minister, "who has been pre-occupied with the Indo-US nuclear deal, has, in fact, imported the crisis in America's financial system".

The party, during a discussion in Parliament, reiterated its demand for reducing the CRR to five per cent, a point originally made by BJP leaders Arun Shourie, Jaswant Singh and Yashwant Sinha at a press conference on October 14.

"We may have not imported any nuclear reactors from America, but India has certainly imported the crisis in America's financial system," said BJP general secretary Ananth Kumar. Asking the Treasury benches to figure out the "plight of the aam aadmi," he warned that the construction industry was facing "one of the biggest slumps" in recent years.

"The Index of Industrial Production released this month shows that India's industrial growth has plummeted to 1.3 per cent in August from 10.9 per cent in the same month in 2007. In the months to come it is likely to turn negative. A large number of people in manufacturing will lose their jobs," he said.

Holding the Prime Minister, Finance Minister and the Planning Commission Deputy Chairman responsible for "inflation and recession, the true hallmarks of the UPA government," he said that India has felt not just the "ripple effect" of the global financial crisis, but its "tidal wave effect" and that there was a real danger of the meltdown of the Indian economy.

Heading: 13 killed in Imphal blast - Indian Express
Content:
The Samajwadi Party on Tuesday launched a broadside against the Congress and ruled out any tie-up with the party in the Assembly elections in Madhya Pradesh next month.

The announcement was made by party general secretary Amar Singh at a 'Vikalp Rally' organised by SP in the state capital. Instead, the party announced that it had joined hands with the Samanta Dal and the Prajatantrik Samadhan Party, two smaller parties having negligible presence.

"We kept trying for an alliance though they called me 'mad' and 'blackmailer'," said Singh, referring to comments made by Congress leaders Satyavrat Chaturvedi and Ahmed Patel. Singh, in his long speech, directed his criticism more at the Congress than at the BJP or the Opposition leader L K Advani.

Singh said though his party had saved the Congress-led UPA government and supported the nuclear deal in national interest, the oldest national party betrayed it by poaching four MLAs in Madhya Pradesh. The relations between the SP and the Congress had soured after the defection and the strong possibility that they would contest on Congress symbols.

Singh claimed that Congress leaders like Digvijay Singh, Kamal Nath and Jyotiraditya Scindia had assured him that they wouldn't attempt to break the SP but had gone back on their promise. "They later tried to justify it saying all the four MLAs originally belonged to the Congress," he said, and asked sarcastically, "Even I was a Congressman, will they accept me now?"

Heading: Bihar boy went for RRB exam, died on Mumbai railway track - Indian Express
Content:
At least 13 persons were killed and more than 30 others injured when a powerful explosion rocked Imphal on Tuesday night. The blast occurred at Ragailong area in the capital city at around 7.30 pm.

Colonel Rajesh Mishra, defence spokesman at Imphal, said over the telephone that the explosion went off with a defeaning sound near a camp of the Assam Rifles which also had a barrack close by. The locality also has a training centre of the Manipur State Police Commando Force.

Meanwhile, sources said 11 persons were killed on the spot, while two others succumbed to injuries on way to the hospital. There was, however, no confirmation of death of any security personnel. The toll is likely to go up.

The bomb was suspected to have been kept in a two-wheeler. Some security personnel might be among the injured. The identities of those killed were yet to be ascertained. Some of the bodies were mutilated beyond recognition, sources said.

Most of the injured were rushed to the Regional Institute of Medical Sciences in Imphal. The Government has announced a red alert in Imphal and neighbouring areas after the explosion. It was only two days ago that suspected militants had lobed a bomb at Chief Minister Okram Ibobi Singh's residence at Babupara in the heart of the city.

Though no group has so far claimed responsibility for the blast, the needle of suspicion was pointed towards Prepak militants, the Army official said.

Heading: Ansari for shifting Question Hour to 4 pm - Indian Express
Content:
Last Thursday, Jagdish Mahto wished his son, Pawan Kumar, luck as he left for Mumbai to try his luck in the Railway Recruitment Board exam. Today, Mahto could not get himself to bid a final farewell to Pawan, 25, whose body arrived in his village of Barakhurd here.

Mumbai Police said the youth died after falling on the railway tracks while trying to catch a train for Bhayender from Andheri for his RRB exam on Sunday. But Pawan's relatives alleged that he was attacked by MNS activists.

For the last six years, ever since he completed his BA (first class) from the Sardar Patel Memorial College in Biharsharif, Pawan had been preparing for competetive exams. His father sold a plot of land to provide financial support.

"I had to take loans at huge interest rates to support Pawan. I knew he would get a job someday and relieve me of my responsibilities," said Mahto. His three elder daughters are all married.

The family was very happy when Pawan recently cleared the written test for a clerical grade examination. He also sat for the assistant station masters' exam. In Mumbai, Pawan was staying with his friends, Shailendra Kumar and Manoj. It was the latter who called up Mahto on Sunday to inform him of his son's death.

The entire village is in mourning. Villagers pointed out that they have no option but to send their children out to look for jobs.

"It is not about how our Pawan died, it is about the sad end of a journey of a struggling Bihar boy," said Brijnandan Prasad, a villager.

Heading: 3 advisories sent to Maharashtra: Patil - Indian Express
Content:
The elders may not be inclined to change, but Rajya Sabha chairman Mohammad Hamid Ansari has hit upon a new idea to save Question Hour — he has mooted a proposal to shift it from 11 am to 4 pm.

Invariably, the first item on the agenda, Question Hour has become the usual casualty of the verbal battles, protest dharnas and walkouts with which members start their Parliamentary work. The calculation is that members would have exhausted their lungpower either at the outset or during Zero Hour, but certainly by the time Question Hour would be taken up later in the day. The House would be also through with items like oath-taking of new members, introduction of fresh ministers and obituary references, which consume a lot of time during Question Hour these days.

The Congress and Left parties are reportedly open to the idea. Sources said Ansari has convened a meeting of the Rules Committee of the House for Thursday to consider the proposal. Ansari heads the 16-member committee. The members include Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman Rahman Khan, E M Sudarsana Natchiappan and K Keshava Rao of the Congress, Ram Jethmalani (nominated), Najma Heptulla and Bal Apte of the BJP, Tariq Anwar from NCP, D Raja from CPI and Chandan Mitra (nominated).

The Chairman's move can be sourced to the alarming details, which are forthcoming with regard to Question Hour, the most vital instrument with Parliament to ensure the accountability of the executive. The sources said during the current year, a total of 580 questions were listed for oral answers. However, answers to only 98 could be obtained in the 20 hours devoted to Question Hour. Replies to the rest were placed on the table. According to Rule 38 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Rajya Sabha (and Rule 32 in the Lok Sabha), the first hour of every sitting—11 am to 12 noon—shall be available for asking and answering questions. Though the presiding officer of either House is empowered to shift Question Hour to another time, no one has ever used this discretion.

Ministers are required to give oral answers to questions put by members. To facilitate this, ministries are bunched together in five groupings with days marked for every group. When ministers are hard up for information, they can ask for time to do so. Such assurances are monitored by the Committee on Government Assurances. A total of 20 questions are listed each day. Members have to send their questions to the House Secretariat at least 15 days in advance. Their admissibility is decided by the Chairman. Members can also ask short-duration questions on a matter of urgent public importance at a shorter notice.

The first sitting of Rajya Sabha was held on May 13, 1952. However, till May 26, 1952, there was no Question Hour in the House. The first half-an-hour was made available for asking and answering questions on May 27 and 28, 1952. Questions were thus put in the Rajya Sabha for the first time on May 27, 1952. On July 14, 1952, the Chairman made an announcement regarding amendment in the Rules thereby making the first hour of the sitting on every Monday to Thursday available for asking questions. The new procedure was followed in the House from July 21, 1952. This procedure continued till July 1964 when it was further revised to include Friday also.

Heading: Afzal Guru: Rahul says even Rajiv case hanging - Indian Express
Content:
Under attack from the Left and NDA MPs for inaction over attacks on north Indians by MNS activists, Home Minister Shivraj Patil on Tuesday said at least three advisories have been sent to the state Government in the wake of the attacks.

Patil, while responding to the Zero Hour mention on MNS attacks, said, "We have issued three advisories to the state Government, we have expressed our anguish and anger and I have also personally talked to the Chief Minister on the issue."

"When we issue advisories to the states, we do not specify that it is under Article 355 or any other article. The advisories ask the Government to take appropriate action failing which the Centre would be forced to use further provisions under the law," Patil said, adding that "the letters issued are dated October 19, 20 and 21."

During the Zero Hour discussion, Shiv Sena MP and former Lok Sabha Speaker Manohar Joshi warned of a "bigger movement" in Maharshtra if the Government did not give preference to the locals in railway employment.

As Railway Minister Lalu Yadav, accompanied by JD(U)'s Sharad Yadav and Digvivay Singh, objected to such remarks, Joshi said, "Your people want to snatch jobs from the people of Maharashtra... this cannot go on. You haven't been able to develop your state, so they come to Maharashtra and other parts of the country. The PM should intervene, the Railway Minister should do something, otherwise there will be a bigger movement."

Lalu, rubbishing the allegations of selection of north Indians by the Railway Recruitment Board, said that "completely transparent procedures were followed".

Sharad Yadav, in a reference to Raj Thackeray but without naming him, said, "This man has broken all laws... this has been going on for the last two years... the state Government should either govern or get out."

Brinda Karat from the CPI(M), who moved the Zero Hour mention leading to an impromptu discussion in the Rajya Sabha, said, "The Maharashtra Government is supporting such activities, this is opportunistic politics by Congress and NCP." Congress' Jayanthi Natrajan objected to aspersions being cast on the state Government even as Brinda asked the Home Minister on the action taken on violence against north Indians by the MNS activists in the last six months.

BJP's Yashwant Sinha also sought answers from the Home Minister on the advisories issued by the Centre under Article 355 of the Constitution. Digvijay Singh said Patil did not have the right to the remain in the post.

Concluding the debate, the Home Minister said, "Anyone from any part of the country can work and live anywhere. No one can stop them. What has happened, should not happen in Maharashtra or anywhere."

The Opposition, comprising of the Left as well as NDA MPs, however, staged a walkout as they were not satisfied with the reply. Soon after, Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman K Rehman Khan adjourned the House for an hour.

Heading: Sena wants law to reserve 80 pc jobs for locals - Indian Express
Content:
Seeking to justify the delay in hanging Parliament attack convict Afzal Guru, scion of the Nehru-Gandhi family Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday said he himself had not got justice in the assassination case of his father Rajiv Gandhi as yet but he believes in the justice system.

In an interaction with HN Bahuguna University students here on Tuesday, when Rahul was asked about the reason for the delay in Afzal Guru case, he cited his own case saying he was 14 years old when his grandmother late Indira Gandhi was killed with 32 bullets. There were 150 witnesses. Two persons were hanged but the case took seven years.

In Rajiv's assassination case, 40 people were involved. It has been 17 years but "nobody has been punished". "The issue is not that Afzal Guru has not been hanged; the issue is that our legal system works very slowly. My father was the Prime Minister. My grandmother was the Prime Minister. I was a son, a grandson. I have not got justice. But I believe in our justice system; you do get justice in India," said Rahul.

During the interaction which lasted over an hour, the Amethi MP faced a volley of questions seeking to draw a comparison between him and his father. Rahul said he was only following in the footsteps of his father who was striving to involve even village youth in the political system.

"I do what my father used to do. Times are different now, so issues are also different. My father talked of computer. It is already there today. We are talking about nuclear energy, education. Our thinking is the same — how to take the youth along," said the AICC general secretary.

Unlike his father who was forced by circumstances to enter politics, Rahul suggested that he never had any other career in mind. Asked if he would still be in politics if his father were alive, Rahul remembered how he saw his father working tirelessly for people. "I would ask him 'Papa, why are you doing it, why are you mingling with the crowd?' But he did not stop. As long as he was in politics, he worked for you (youth)."

The Amethi MP reminisced how Rajiv was attacked by people, who are "big leaders in the opposition" now, when his father talked about computer. "I saw how his entire efforts were sought to be negated. It had a deep influence on me. Were my father alive, I wouldn't have taken some other path," he said.

Heading: Two MPs resign, Katara expelled - Indian Express
Content:
Finding itself in a piquant situation with Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) hijacking its Marathi agenda; the Shiv Sena now wants a countrywide legislation to reserve 80 per cent of the jobs for local residents.

A delegation of Sena MPs met Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on the issue and urged him to move a Bill to protect the interests of the sons of the soil in all states. "Our stand is that 80 per cent of the jobs should be reserved for local people. We met the PM and he said he'll think about it," Rajya Sabha MP and Sena's spokesperson Sanjay Raut said. "It is very necessary to protect the interests of local people in all states, otherwise there will be chaos and the country may head for fragmentation."

He further said the Sena had been fighting for the interests of local people for the last four decades and had sacrificed a lot. He said if any other party—even the Muslim League—would take up the Sena's issues, it would be welcomed. "It (Marathi) is our agenda and nobody can hijack it from us," he said.

Heading: ‘Zero-tolerance’ towards Sena brand of politics - Indian Express
Content:
The Lok Sabha strength has been reduced by three. While the House expelled Babubhai Katara (Dohad-ST) by a voice vote, Speaker Somnath Chatterjee announced the resignations of two others, Manorama Madhvaraj (Udupi) and Kunnur Manjunath Chanappa (Dharwad South) on Tuesday.

All three were elected on BJP tickets. They had voted for the UPA Government during the July 22 vote of confidence in defiance of party whip. They have since been expelled from the party.

Though the BJP had also petitioned the Speaker for Katara's disqualification on the ground of defection, the House expelled him due to his involvement in a case of human trafficking. A House committee, which is mandated to look in to misconduct of members, had made a strong recommendation for his expulsion. The panel, headed by V Kishore Chandra S Deo, indicted him and recommended "the severest of punishments".

The House exclaimed with "ayes" as the Speaker put the resolution, moved by Leader of the House Pranab Mukherjee, to vote. The resolution said Katara "has committed an act of grave misconduct which has brought disrepute to and maligned the image of the entire fraternity of legislators". Mukherjee said that though it was an "unpleasant job", he had to discharge it. He said members "should be extra-careful" in protecting the image of "this great institution".

The Speaker informed the House that he had received the resignations of Madhvaraj and Chanappa on Monday and that he has accepted them.

Heading: House panel against ban on acquiring farm land - Indian Express
Content:
AICC general secretary Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday termed the anti-North Indian campaign launched by the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena as "wrong" and called for "zero tolerance" approach towards this kind of politics. He also chastised those looking at the entire issue in the context of parochial north and west India divide.

"You cannot do politics of divisions. Either have zero tolerance towards this, or be ready for divisive politics. What Raj Thackeray is doing is wrong; I am very clear about it," said Gandhi while interacting with students of H N Bahuguna Gadhwal University here.

"The problem is with your thinking as well. When you think in terms of Uttar Bharat and Paschim Bharat, you are thinking like them. I say there is either India or no India." In response to another question, he said terrorism and communalism were "similar" because of the "divisive mentality".

Heading: Chief accused turns chief guest - Indian Express
Content:
With land acquisition for industry running into trouble across the country, from Singur in West Bengal to Rae Bareli in Uttar Pradesh, the Parliamentary Standing Committee looking into the Land Acquisition Act has rejected the demands for a ban on acquisition of agricultural land for industrial purposes. Instead, it has suggested enacting a separate legislation on the lines of the Forest Conservation Act to control the diversion of agricultural land.

"The Committee is of the view that to put a complete ban on the acquisition of agricultural land would not be a practical solution," said the Standing Committee on Rural Development, which looked into the Land Acquisition (Amendment) Bill, 2007. The Committee has, thus, rejected the suggestions that "good agricultural land should not be acquired at any cost". The panel has instead suggested that an equal amount of wasteland should be developed in case agricultural land is acquired for the projects. It has asked the government to insert a provision to this effect in the legislation itself.

In fact, the Committee headed by senior BJP MP Kalyan Singh has also rejected suggestions to impose ceiling on land acquired under the Act, citing reservations cited by ministries of Environment and Forests, Tribal Affairs and Urban Development, which feared that it may create problems for some major projects of public interest. However, given the requirement of agricultural land to maintain food security in the country, the Committee has recommended bringing separate legislation on the lines of the Forest Conservation Act, 1980 to protect the diversion of prime agricultural land for non-agricultural purposes.

Significantly, the panel has also rejected the proposal to fix some percentage of land to be purchased by the private party (70 per cent of project land) before the government acquires the remaining land for any project citing it as "contradictory and impractical". It has recommended complete acquisition by either a private party or by government.

The committee has suggested an improvement in the compensation proposed by the government. "The committee has recommended that the highest price of sale deed as indicated in the sale deeds of the last three years plus 50 per cent of the said highest price should be the criteria for assessing and determining the market value of the land," Singh added.

Heading: Tunnel detected in Ambala jail, escape plans thwarted - Indian Express
Content:
In a somewhat bizarre development, the chief accused in the infamous chinkara hunting case — former state transport minister Dharmarao Baba Atram — has been invited by the Forest Department to be the chief guest at the concluding function of the 14th Forest Department Sports Competition at Chandrapur on October 24.

The invites, which clearly state Atram's name as chief guest, have been sent by Conservator of Forest (CF), South Chandrapur, Mahip Gupta and CF, North Chandrapur, R S Yadav, who are vice-president and president of the organising committee respectively. A K Joshi, Additional Principal Chief Conservator of Forest (Production and Management), whom the invites mentions as chief organiser, however, claimed ignorance, "I have been on leave since October 6 and am currently in Bangalore. I have no idea about the invitation."

When contacted, Principal Secretary J P Dange told The Indian Express, "Please contact the Principal Chief Conservator of Forest (PCCF). He has printed the invites."

However, PCCF Jwala Prasad claimed that he was not aware of who had invited Atram or printed out the invites. "I was invited for the inaugural function, which I attended. Rest I don't know," he said. When asked for his views about the 'honour' given to a person who has been accused of a crime against wildlife, Prasad said, "I will inquire about it."

Principal Chief Conservator of Forest (Wildlife) B Majumdar did not shed any light on the issue either. "I am in Andhra Pradesh now. But I am surprised," he said.

Meanwhile, R S Yadav, chairman of the organising committee, was more forthcoming. "He is the local MLA. As per protocol, we have to invite him." Regarding the charges against Atram, Yadav said, "According to the Indian Penal Code, nobody is guilty unless so proved. And there are so many such MLAs and MPs. So, should they be barred from all such functions? You people should not take things that far."

Interestingly, the printed invites clearly state that Atram will be sharing this 'honour' with Atul Deshkar, the BJP MLA from Brahmapuri. The BJP, especially its state president Nitin Gadkari, had been particularly strident in condemning Atram's alleged involvement in the case. Atram, who is the NCP MLA from Sironcha in Gadchiroli district, was sent to jail after his bail plea was rejected by Bombay High Court in August this year. He is currently out on bail.

Heading: India ranks 70 on world prosperity index - Indian Express
Content:
The Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) has decided to launch a campaign against family planning and will use a book to urge Hindus to ensure that they produce at least four male children —"two for the family and two for the Hindu cause".

To spread its new strategy among the Hindu masses, the VHP will circulate a book Bharat mein Hindu Bahumat (Hindu majority in India). About 10,000 copies of this book have been collected in Karsewak Puram, the local headquarters of VHP here, said Rama Patnaik, a VHP full-timer.

However, senior VHP leaders are not ready to disclose much on the issue. "It is a good move by the VHP, as the family planning system introduced in India by the Congress is anti-religious," said Mahant Ram Kripal. "Our religious books do not give permission to control births," he added.

Publised by an Ahmedabad-based publisher, the 100-page book says that at the given rate, the population of Muslims and Christians will outnumber that of Hindus in half a century. The book asks Hindus to ensure the birth of at least four male children and prepare two of them for the cause of Hindutva. It also directs parents to teach girls to prepare themselves for this. The book claims family planning is a "Christian and Muslim strategy to make Hindus a minority in India". In the present circumstances it will be an anti-national act by the Hindus to adopt family planning system, says the book.

Ramanand Maheshwari, a VHP leader and member of the team that will circulate the book, said: "Within a few days we will take the book to the Hindu masses. We will also give it publicity through meetings, street plays and processions."

Heading: BSP members stage walkout in Lok Sabha - Indian Express
Content:
India has ranked 70th among 104 nations on the World Prosperity Index (WPI) 2008 and quality of secondary education, cost of starting a business and the lack of government effectiveness are among the reasons why India is so low on the index.

"India has a relatively entrepreneurial culture. It requires government effectiveness and tackling corruption," Alan McCormick, Managing Director of Legatum Institute, that brought out the Index, said.

Increase in capital and education contribute directly to the value of physical and human capital and thus directly increase economic output. Poor governance and excessive bureaucracy impose costs on business and thus restrain growth, the report released last week said.

The Institute also ranks India at 10th place on its 'Who's Going Places' list, with China on number six. "These countries have the best context right now within which to create wealth," McCormick said. Both economies have recently grown faster than almost any country in the rich world. Because these two giant nations are home to more than two billion people, these improvements in competitiveness are bringing about a dramatic lessening of the global wealth gap and are very good news for global prosperity, the report said.

"India outstrips many South Asian nations in various aspects of wealth creation. It ranks stronger with reference to other Asian countries in terms of avoiding dependence on commodity exports and foreign aid," McCormick said.

This is the second year that the Institute has come up with the Prosperity Index. In 2007, only 50 countries were analysed as compared to 104 this year. "India was featured in last years Index and was ranked 46 th of 50 countries analysed. Although comparisons between 2007 and 2008 rankings are nor valid due to changes in methodology of survey, but the drivers and restrainers of India's prosperity are quite similar to last year," Legatum Corporate Communications Hamish Banks said.

Heading: ‘SC, HC judges were present when cash-in-bag was delivered’ - Indian Express
Content:
BSP members caused a ruckus and staged a walkout from the Lok Sabha in protest of the Speaker's ruling on an allegation made by a fellow party member.

The BSP's Brajesh Pathak had alleged that he had been threatened by a man purporting to be CBI official to vote in favour of the UPA Government on July 22. According to Pathak, the man had warned him that unless he complied, BSP chief Mayawati would be implicated in criminal cases. The 'CBI official' had also produced documents to back this threat.

In his ruling, Chatterjee said he had sent copies of the documents handed over by Pathak to the Ministry of Personnel, which had forwarded the factual report of the CBI on the matter. The CBI had maintained that a comparison of the documents handed over by Pathak with the original ones has "revealed that contents of documents have been modified with obliterations, interpolations and fabrication".

The Speaker ruled that the "matter be treated as closed" in view of the CBI report and because the documents in question related to cases pending in different courts, including the Supreme Court. Pathak demanded that Chatterjee review his decision and refer it to the Privileges Committee. Chatterjee said that by questioning the Speaker, the BSP member was "setting a very bad precedent".

Chatterjee called upon Basudeb Acharia of the CPI(M) to speak. When Mohammad Salim started speaking in favour of Pathak, the Speaker told Acharia, "You are not being allowed to speak by your deputy leader. What can I do?" Thereafter, BJP members created a ruckus over the issue of the Railway Police Force lathicharge on their colleague at Bina. The Speaker adjourned the House till 2 pm.

Heading: AMU plans five new centres, alumni body says too far away - Indian Express
Content:
In a new twist to the cash-in-bag case, advocate Anupam Gupta, who is also the senior standing counsel for the UT Administration, said today that there were two other judges — one from the Supreme Court and the other from the High Court — at the Sector 11 residence of Justice Nirmaljit Kaur where a packet containing Rs 15 lakh was delivered on August 13.

Gupta claimed that former Haryana additional advocate general Sanjeev Bansal, an accused in the case, was in touch with the same SC judge's son from August 14-16, when the FIR in the case was registered. As many as five calls and an SMS were exchanged between Bansal and the judge's son, he said.

"I am convinced that the packet was mistakenly delivered at the HC judge's residence in Sector 11, but why has the presence of the two other judges been concealed," asked Gupta. He alleged that a senior HC judge present there had made a "sustained, conscious and wilful" effort to obstruct and influence the investigation.

"This senior judge even made a call to the SHO concerned. Records show this judge went towards the northern sectors in Chandigarh and made a call to Bansal," he claimed.

Gupta also accepted the demand made by an NGO that he should be examined by the CBI.

Following his revelations today, the Bar Association passed a resolution demanding that the scope of the CBI probe be expanded.

Heading: Panel to propose uniform law for all marriages - Indian Express
Content:
The Aligarh Muslim University's decision to have five centres in Malappuram (Kerala), Katihar (Bihar), Pune (Maharashtra), Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh), and Murshidabad (West Bengal) hasn't been welcomed by the university's alumni association. At the Sir Syed Day function, held at Pragati Maidan on Monday, the AMU Old Boy's Association said such a plan should have taken into consideration the opinions of AMU's students, staff and alumni.

Safdar H Khan, the association's president, said, "They have selected distant places." The association will meet the vice-chancellor this week to discuss the issue.

The university's proposal to open five centres at Rs 2,000 crore has been accepted by the Ministry of Human Resource Development. AMU spokesperson Rahat Abrar said the executive council was involved in the decision-making process and students' feedback wasn't required for expansion plans. He said the locations of the centres were finalised keeping the demographics in mind. These areas have large concentration of Muslims, he said.

But the association, one of the oldest in the country with 7,000 members, said instead of Pune and Malappuram, centres should have been established in Punjab or Haryana where there are no minority institutions.

The meeting was attended by 1,500 former students who urged that students' union — dismissed last year after campus violence — be reinstated and elections to the students' body be organised soon.

Heading: Parties want info on caste in census - Indian Express
Content:
While a uniform civil code remains a dream, the Law Commission is ready with a proposal to bring all inter-religious marriages under a uniform law.

Having realised that existing marriage laws are inconsistent, the Commission has come up with a proposal to amend the Special Marriage Act, 1954. According to sources, the proposal suggests that all inter-religious marriages should be brought under the Special Marriage Act. All the provisions under this statute can be made applicable to all marriages, even if they have been held under specific religious marriage laws.

The proposal is expected to be submitted shortly to the Union Law Minister. In addition, the Commission may also submit a report strongly recommending compulsory registration of marriages as well as a proposal amending certain sections of the Foreign Marriage Act, 1969.

Suggesting a commonly enforceable set of laws governing marriage, the Commission's proposal seems in tune with Article 44 relating to the uniform civil code. However, Hindus, Buddhists and a few other religious sects have a choice between their personal law and the Special Marriage Act.

The Commission is also set to propose an important amendment in a penal provision in case of suicide attempts. The Law Commission is believed to be of the view that suicide attempts must be de-criminalised.

Heading: Flouting rules, ACC reappoints officer nearing retirement age - Indian Express
Content:
With an eye on the upcoming elections, political parties, including some prominent UPA allies like Samajwadi Party and Rashtriya Janata Dal, on Monday urged the Government to include caste information in the next census exercise in 2011.

Speaking at a seminar organized by PMK, another UPA ally, leaders from these political parties said collecting caste information would bring in clarity on the issue whether the so-called creamy layer needed to be kept out of the reservation quota or not. PMK founder S Ramadoss said even the Supreme Court had observed that in the absence of reliable scientific data, the Government would not be able to make significant changes in the reservation laws.

He said that in order to collect this information the Government needs to introduce a new column in the census form asking for the caste of the people.

"Such data will help us in forming an idea about the level of development, backwardness and poverty levels of different castes," he said, adding that as of now there were conflicting figures based on estimates by different institutions.

Heading: Earth to Moon: India’s on its way - Indian Express
Content:
Disregarding the stipulation which bars reappointing or extending the service of an official beyond the age of retirement (60), the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) reappointed T K Viswanathan, as Secretary, Department of Legal Affairs. Viswanathan, who is due to retire at the end of this month, has also been given the additional charge of Secretary, Legislative Department. This, say sources, was done at the request of Union Law and Justice Minister Hans Raj Bhardwaj.

However being wary of the consequences that might follow the step, the Cabinet Committee has carefully worded the decision, trying its best to ward off all possible challenge to it by pushing for the secretary's extension on a contractual basis.

The Union Ministry of Personnel has time and again ordered that no proposal for employing a government servant beyond the age of superannuation can be considered. It also frowns upon any move to reappoint a retired officer on a contractual basis, as was the case with Viswanathan.

As per Fundamental Rule 56, the Union Government can — and that too only in public interest — give an extension in service to the Cabinet Secretary, Defence Secretary, Home Secretary, Director, Intelligence Bureau, Secretary, Research and Analysis Wing and Director, Central Bureau of Investigation.

Incidentally, the Law Minister had admitted at a function at the Indian Law Institute last month to having pleaded the officer's case with Prime Minister Manmohan Singh since Viswanathan's services were needed for some more time. "Does the minister think that there is no other officer capable of doing the job? And, what will the government do after one year?" asked a senior functionary.

In a similar incident, Bhardwaj, in July, ordered the reappointment of Indian Legal Service Officer S K Sharma, who retired as Director (Prosecution), Central Bureau of Investigation, for a period of one year.

Heading: Raj gets one night in a lock-up, can sleep easy - Indian Express
Content:
So Why is this unique?

• Will try to map high-resolution 3-D topography of entire moon, get mineral composition of surface,investigate presence/absence of water. Such detailed analysis, if successful, will be a first.

• At Rs 386 crore, cheapest moon mission so far.

• With 11 payloads, one of the most heavily loaded lunar missions.

• At two years in space, amongst the longer duration missions.

What's The journey to the moon like?

• After lift-off, first milestone is separation of spacecraft from launch vehicle PSLV-C11. Expected 19 minutes after lift-off.

• Then Chandrayaan-I will be powered by its own engine.

• Will circle the earth in elliptical orbit. Will fire rockets at scheduled stages to go into progressively higher orbits until it reaches 386,000 km from the earth. Will take 11 days to go around the earth in this orbit.

• In the 2nd revolution in this elliptical orbit, spacecraft will slow down to get sucked into moon's gravitational field after which it will start orbiting.

• Then begins stepwise lowering into lower and lower orbits until it reaches the targeted orbit of 100 km from the moon.

• In this orbit, Chandrayaan will fire the Moon Impacter Probe (MIP), designed to hit the lunar surface at a designated area. MIP not supposed to survive after that but will demonstrate technologies for a future soft-landing mission.

• Once MIP released, all scientific instruments on Chandrayaan will be turned on and will begin their observations.

What's it carrying?

• 11 payloads, five Indian. Six foreign payloads: three from theEuropean Space Agency (to map minerals), two from NASA (to detect water-ice) and one from Bulgaria (to monitor radiation levels).

What next?

• Chandrayaan 2, which will involve landing on moon. Expected date: 2011-2012

Heading: Govt orders regulator war-room meetings with RBI, Sebi chiefs - Indian Express
Content:
The Maharashtra government displayed uncharacteristic alacrity and arrested Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray in a pre-dawn move today in Ratnagiri district and brought him to Mumbai for the attacks on north Indians taking railway job exams in the city. But considering the state was pushed by the Centre to finally act, and going by the prosecution record of authorities in a similar incident involving Thackeray's supporters, few were betting on the outcome.

Thackeray was picked up from a circuit house in Ratnagiri district around 3.40 am by a Mumbai Police team and produced in a Bandra court in the city this afternoon. News of his arrest sparked sporadic violence across the city and elsewhere around the state. MNS supporters, including scores of women, pelted stones and clashed with police outside the court. Activists attacked taxis, set fire to a toll booth, tried to burn buses and businesses in Mumbai, Thane, Kalyan as well as Nashik and Pune. By the end of the day, nearly 4,000 had been arrested across the state since Monday.

Thackeray was charged with rioting, criminal intimidation and endangering the life and personal safety of others, remanded to judicial custody and granted bail. However, he could not make it in time to the court in Kalyan in Thane where he is booked in a similar case and will spend the night in a local police station in Manpada. While he was gagged by the police for the fourth time this year and is expected to secure bail and walk free tomorrow, the record of authorities in pursuing a similar case involving his supporters has raised doubts over whether the victims of Sunday's attack can harbour hope for justice.

In November 2003, activists of the Bharatiya Vidyarthi Sena (BVS), the students' wing of the Shiv Sena which Thackeray then headed, had threatened and chased away north Indians who had come to Kalyan to appear in the same Railway job tests. The notorious attack at the Kalyan railway station had similarly made headlines then and 14 BVS activists were booked for unlawful assembly and rioting.

Five years on, the trial in the case is yet to begin. That attack was seen as part of a campaign Raj launched against north Indians to counter the influence of cousin Uddhav's "Mee Mumbaikar" campaign that aimed to develop a pan-Mumbai identity for residents of the financial capital and expand the narrow, Marathi identity of the Shiv Sena. Even then, Raj had argued that Maharashtrians were being discriminated against by the Railways.

While Raj was not named in the case then, the 14 BVS activists were all booked for bailable offences. "The trial has not begun yet and the matter is adjourned every time," said Ravindra Kapote, one of the 14 accused. During the incident, Kapote was the Shiv Sena's Kalyan shaharpramukh or city unit chief. Today, he is in charge of the party in the Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation area.

Arvind More, another accused in the case, is alleged to have led the attack. He is at present the Shiv Sena co-ordinator for the Kalyan assembly seat and says he has not received any warrant from the court. "I usually don't hire any lawyer as I have 22 cases registered against me.We do it for the party and for the cause," he told The Indian Express.

With the victims of the attack having fled Kalyan, the complaint in the case was filed by a policeman who is now an inspector but is no longer with the Railway Police. The investigating officer has retired. A K Sharma, Mumbai's Railway Police Commissioner, said that "unlike in sessions courts and fast track courts, it takes time for trials to start in rail courts".

(With inputs from Mustafa Plumber and Sukanya Shetty)

Heading: Aussies very down under in Mohali, India’s perfect end to perfect Test - Indian Express
Content:
Stepping up crisis-management measures to cushion the anticipated economic downturn precipitated by the global financial turmoil, the government has ordered the High-Level Coordination Committee on Financial Markets to meet at least once a month as an emergency measure to take stock of the situation and identify timely responses.

The committee, headed by RBI governor Duvvuri Subbarao, is essentially a panel of regulators comprising heads of IRDA, PFRDA and SEBI besides top Finance Ministry officials.

The committee convened an emergency meeting in the first week of October to assess preparedness of regulators to tackle the impact of the financial crisis.

The decision comes after repeated suggestions to evolve a mechanism that can provide timely and coordinated response to a situation that is unpredictable, requiring effective regulation.

As of now, sources said, efforts are on to ensure that steps taken by the government to improve the liquidity situation are taken further by banks which are now extremely cautious about their lending profile.

Despite the fact that over $10 billion have been withdrawn from Indian markets in the form of FII withdrawals, sources said, the RBI is not setting any exchange rate targets. However, it continues to keep a close tab in case there is unexpected movement on the currency front. Further, indications are that more rate cuts are in the offing as the RBI works on the credit policy to be announced on Friday.

On the global front, India is willing to play a constructive role in trying to put in place more effective regulation. However, sources said, New Delhi wants to first ensure that it is made a purposeful participant and not pushed to stamp a blueprint devised by developed countries. To this end, the BRIC (Brazil, Russia, India and China) countries along with other major developing economies like Mexico and South Africa are in close touch to present a coordinated response on the global stage.

Heading: Line of Control becomes Line of Commerce - Indian Express
Content:
"Stand-in skipper, stand-in blazer," Mahendra Singh Dhoni beamed at the post-match press conference, on a charm offensive after an aggressive India had completed a whopping 320-run win to take a 1-0 win in the Test series against Australia.

The fact that Dhoni walked out for the toss in an oversized jacket, after Anil Kumble had to pull out on the morning of the match, was the only blip over five days in Mohali where everything else fit just right. Needing five wickets to wrap up the game on the last day, Dhoni threw the ball to Zaheer Khan first thing in the morning. He could well have been throwing the left-arm pacer a pair of boxing gloves.

Brad Haddin saw the first five deliveries of the day pitch on middle and leave him, but he quite clearly didn't see the one that pitched on middle and hit middle. His bat hung limp in his hands, searching for contact at least six inches off target. Next over, Zaheer threw one right up outside off-stump, cutting away, the old sucker punch. Drawn into the drive, White turned back to see Dhoni dive to his right and pick up a low catch.

Brett Lee bounded into the centre, all intensity. One ball later, he trudged out, head shaking in disbelief. Zaheer had pitched one outside leg-stump and hit the top of off. Lee, all things considered, might as well have not been standing in between. Three blows in the space of four deliveries, Australia were on the mat.

This was the perfect start as far as India were concerned. Apt, considering this was pretty much the perfect Test as far as India were concerned.

"We weren't good enough in any aspect of this game — fast bowling, spin bowling, batting and, at times, our fielding was a bit sloppy, so we've been out-played," Ricky Ponting said. "Sometimes as a captain and player you have to accept that they were better than us." This 320-run margin — apart from being India's biggest outside of innings victories — was also their biggest over Australia, beating the 222-run win in Melbourne back in December 1977.

Dhoni rubbed it in. "When the Australians batted in the first innings, they were 22 in 13 overs. I pointed that out to Rahul (Dravid) — you don't see that very often." Dhoni won the Man of the Match award for his two aggressive half-centuries, but this was a team effort if ever there was one. Virender Sehwag made up for throwing away his wicket in the first innings by blasting 92 in the second. Gautam Gambhir failed to convert a start on Day One, but got to three figures in the next time around.

Sachin Tendulkar played probably the best knock of the series so far, his 88 taking him to the top of the run-scoring charts and past the 12,000-run mark. Sourav Ganguly, who will retire after the fourth Test, got a century in the first — true to form, he looks intent on squeezing in as much drama as possible into his farewell series.

The bowling attack provided even more cheer. On a pitch where the Australian attack looked positively pedestrian, all four of India's front-liners left their mark. If it was Amit Mishra who stole the show in the first innings (apart from finishing things off on the final morning), Harbhajan Singh broke Australia's back early in the second with a three-wicket burst.

Ishant Sharma continued to torment Ponting, picking him up twice with deliveries that were close to unplayable, while Zaheer Khan sparked the party on Tuesday morning. Apart from a brief session of play on the first afternoon, when Dravid, Gambhir and VVS Laxman fell in quick succession, India looked miles ahead of the Aussies.

Greg Chappell lined up along with the Australian side as the teams shook hands at the end of the no-contest. Two men sent into exile during his regime — Ganguly and Zaheer — had thrown their names in the hat for the Man of the Match award. He had turning tracks specially prepared during an unscheduled week-long preparation camp in Jaipur — and the Indian pacers came to the party. In fact, there was even a small but extremely un-Aussie on-field altercation between skipper Ponting and Lee on Day Four. It's not just hard being India coach, it must be hard being coach in India as well.

After a week's break, the next Test begins in Delhi — where India haven't lost a match since 1987. Australia, on a three-day recovery break, really need the glorious uncertainties of cricket to kick into action.

Heading: 2 migrants, 1 MNS man killed in Kalyan violence - Indian Express
Content:
Barely weeks ago, a demand for opening the Srinagar-Muzaffarabad trade route and attempts to march to the Line of Control had led to violent clashes across the Valley. But it was very different today at the Peace Bridge. The moment the first truck carrying goods from Muzaffarabad rolled in, there was applause all around and slogans rent the air. Because this bridge on the Line of Control, which divides and connects the two parts of Kashmir, was now the Line of Commerce, kickstarting trade on the Srinagar-Muzaffarabad road after a gap of six decades.

Similar scenes were witnessed at Chakan-da-Bagh crossing when three trucks from Poonch hit the road to Rawalakot, scripting a new chapter in Indo-Pak ties.

"Ever since my childhood, I have been waiting for this moment," said Mazhar Naqvi, a trader from Muzaffarabad who drove the first truck carrying rice and spices. "It is impossible to express the happiness". As Kashmiri traders surrounded his truck and tried to shake his hand, Naqvi was overcome with emotion: "Everyone in our part of Kashmir is happy to see the beginning of trade, we wish this continues always. It is trade between two brothers, two parts of one Kashmir."

Mubeen Shah, president of the Kashmir Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI) who led a delegation to the Peace Bridge, said: "Today, it is a symbolic beginning. But I am sure we will manage to break all impediments and make this trade a reality for future generations."

Khalid Mohammad, who drove a truck carrying onions from Muzaffarabad, was sure trade was going to benefit people on both sides. "It will also help bring peace in the region. I wish trucks from the Valley arrive in Muzaffarabad everyday."

J&K and PoK sent 13 truckloads of goods each. Kashmiri traders dispatched 12 trucks of three varieties of apples — Delicious, Golden and American besides pears. A pick-up van carried spices, saffron and honey to Muzaffarabad. The PoK traders sent onions, basmati rice, corn, spices and moong dal.

Unlike April, 7, 2005 when the Peace Bridge was first opened for people on either side, the function today was relatively low-key with no senior J&K official present at the Peace Bridge. Earlier, at the Salamabad trade facility in Uri (17 km from the Peace Bridge), Governor N N Vohra had flagged off the convoy for Muzaffarabad.

Sardar Ateeq Khan, Prime Minister of PoK, walked up to the middle of the Peace Bridge to receive the trucks from the Valley. "We won't let this trade become hostage to circumstances. We will make it a success. It is just a beginning today, I am sure this trade will gain momentum soon," he said.

Governor Vohra too expressed the same hope. Addressing a gathering of Kashmiri traders, he said: "Today is the beginning. I am hopeful that in the coming days this trade will gain much more importance. This day is important for the traders on both sides."

In Poonch, three trucks carrying fruits and vegetables were flagged off by H H Tyabji, Advisor to the Governor, from Chakan-da-Bagh crossing. As the convoy rolled into Rawalakot, people on both sides of the Zero Line cheered. "The cross-LoC trade will bring down animosity between India and Pakistan and will greatly help in improving relations," said Tyabji.

He said that both sides have agreed, for the present, on 21 items for trade. But these will be subject to review every three months and the items could increase or decrease, depending what the two governments decide in consultation with traders.

Rawalakot Deputy Commissioner Zafar Mehmood, who was leading the PoK team, said: "On our side, people are quite excited about this new relationship. The traders are quite eager to engage in cross-LoC trade. This trade will boost relations."

Heading: Too Late? McCain Emphasises Distance From Bush - Indian Express
Content:
Barack Obama will suspend his campaigning for more than 36 hours this week to visit his grandmother Madelyn Dunham, who is gravely ill in Hawaii.

Dunham, 85, all but raised Obama during his teenage years in Hawaii, and he has spoken of her often on the campaign trail. A campaign spokesman, Robert Gibbs, declined to specify the nature of her illness, other than to say it was quite serious. Dunham lives in Honolulu.

"I think everyone understands that the decision that Senator Obama is making to go to Hawaii underscores the seriousness of the situation," Gibbs said. "As he has said, she poured everything she had into him."

The Obama campaign has canceled scheduled appearances by Obama in Des Moines and Madison, Wisconsin. But the senator will make an unexpected stop in Indianapolis on Thursday, Gibbs said, since that aligns more easily with his plan to depart for Hawaii.

Obama will fly to Hawaii on Thursday afternoon, and likely depart back to the mainland Friday evening. Gibbs said he is expected to return to the campaign trail on Saturday.

To leave the trail at this juncture, when the bell lap is upon both Obama and his Republican rival John McCain carries an element of risk. Obama is running ahead in every national poll, but his lead in some recent polls is not large.

But Obama has little family left. His father and mother are dead, along with his grandfather, Stanley Dunham. His grandmother raised him for many years, while his mother lived in Indonesia.

Heading: Swing voters bothered by McCain’s temperament - Indian Express
Content:
Battling George W Bush for the GOP presidential nomination in 2000, John McCain lashed out at the Texas governor, denouncing his proposed tax cuts as a giveaway to the rich. Eight years later, this time running as the Republican presidential nominee, the senator from Arizona is again criticising Bush and his financial policies, as he renews his efforts to demonstrate that he would represent a departure from the current administration.

At virtually every campaign stop, McCain is reprising a line he used last Wednesday in his final debate with Barack Obama: "I am not George Bush." And in a television ad introduced last week, McCain looks into the camera and says, "The last eight years haven't worked very well, have they?"

As he struggles to pull his campaign out from beneath the shadow of a president whose approval ratings have reached historic lows, McCain is offering some of his toughest criticism of the Bush White House.
