Banerjee also said since the Tatas had announced the pullout from Singur, they should immediately return Rs 200 crore loan that was given to them. "It is the money of the common man. We want it back in our state," she said.

Trinamool leaders of Singur hinted that the party could start a fresh protest in the town demanding return of land to farmers.

Heading: Dengue cases spiral north, cleanliness in Mohali still a distant dream - Indian Express
Content:
West Bengal is the most peaceful state in the country, still the state police need to be more people-friendly. This was Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's advice to the force at the 'Investiture Ceremony of Bengal Police 2008' at the Science City Auditorium in Kolkata on Wednesday.

Taking a dig at the recent occurences in Maharashtra, Bhattacharjee said: "Observe other states. In one state, people from other states are considered unwanted and cannot go there for jobs. This is unthinkable in Bengal."

He also highlighted communal clashes breaking out in different parts of the country. "People are fighting over religion in other states. West Bengal is safe and peaceful," he said.

Bhattacharjee, however, said there is no cause for complacency because terrorism, especially ultra-Left terrorism, is posing a real threat to the state.

He exhorted policemen to act as a friend of the people. "The police, from the level of superintendent of police to the officers of a police station, must gain confidence of the people. No discrimination should be made between the rich and the poor while addressing their complaints," he said.

The chief minister also said: "The government is trying to increase the number of police housing estates and police hospitals. We will provide treatment to all injured policemen on duty."

Bhattacharjee conferred four Sourya Padak, seven Nistha Padak, 42 Prasansha Padak and 57 Sewa Padaks to the policemen.

Three Sourya Padak awards were given posthumously. Police medal for meritorious service and President's police medal for distinguished services were also awarded.

Heading: Nokia to compensate for faulty handset - Indian Express
Content:
With garbage heaps piling up by the day and stagnant water harbouring an increasing population of mosquitoes and flies, the woes of the Mohali residents knows no end.

Even after the recent spurt in dengue cases, the level of cleanliness at the district headquarters leaves a lot to be desired. The civic body has come under sharp criticism from its own councillors for this neglect. While the MC officials prefer to be tight-lipped on the issue, most of the permanent safai karamcharis are reportedly catering to the bureaucrats.

Of the total budgetary provisions of Rs 32.75 crore for 2008-09, the MC had earmarked Rs 23.65 crore for development projects. While Rs 1.5 crore was earmarked for the collection and removal of solid waste, the sanitation expenditure was covered under the development fund.

Despite the huge allocation, the sanitary conditions remain deplorable. Most of the areas have become virtual dumping grounds owing to the absence of proper garbage disposal dumps. This has led to the breeding of mosquitoes and flies.

For a population of nearly 1.22 lakh people spread over an area of almost 23.86 square km, two private contractors have been given the charge to maintain sanitation in the residential areas, which were divided into four zones. These MC safai karamcharis, however, also look after sanitation work in the Industrial Area.

The present system appears grossly inadequate to provide satisfactory sanitation to the entire township and MC officials prescribe an addition of at least 500 more safai karamcharis. Interestingly, there is a ban on new recruitments.

Despite having 100 safai karamcharis, the sanitation work in the residential areas has been outsourced on an annual contract of Rs 1.4 crore, said Executive Officer, Mohali Municipal Council, Amena Kumar Goel.

Claiming that all was well on the sanitation front, the EO said, "We are paying special attention to keeping the city clean and green."

While admitting that Mataur village was the dirtiest place within the MC limits, Goel asserted that no case of dengue has been reported from that area.

"Phase 3-B 1, from where maximum dengue cases were reported, is among the cleanest places and it is the breeding of dengue mosquito in stagnant water within houses, had led to the outbreak," claimed the EO.

Responding to the allegations of municipal councillors regarding unsatisfactory cleanliness arrangements, Goel said the municipal councillors have been empowered to check the contractors' work in their respective areas and report any lapse. Former MC vice-president Harman Preet Singh Prince, accused MC president Rajinder Singh Rana of "failing miserably" in keeping the city clean even after over two years of rule.

In the last MC meeting, municipal councillor Mohanbeer Singh Shergill had also raised a strong voice against the poor cleanliness arrangements. Municipal Councillor Kuljit Singh Bedi, who represents the dengue-affected Phase 3-B 1, warned that if special steps were not taken forthwith, the present unsanitary conditions could lead to an epidemic in the coming days.

Heading: Foreigner booked for disrespecting Tricolour - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed the Nokia Care Centre in Sector 22 to pay Rs 1,100 compensation for causing harassment to a customer after they demanded Rs 4,500 for the repair of a handset, while it was in the warranty period. They have also been directed to get the defective handset repaired. They have also been directed to pay Rs 550 as litigation costs.

The complainant, Rangi Ram, a resident of Panchkula, purchased Nokia N-70 mobile handset for Rs 16,230 in 2006. It was alleged that after some time of the purchase, the screen of his mobile went totally blank. He then visited the Nokia Care Centre, where the officials prepared a job sheet and informed him that the set had a manufacturing defect and thus cannot be repaired.

He was told that the set will be replaced and asked him to visit the centre after a few days. He then deposited the set with them after he was assured of the replacement but, he was asked to deposit Rs 4,500 for the same.

Nokia Care Center, in its reply, said that the handset of the complainant was water/liquid logged when he handed over the same to them and it was for this that an estimate of Rs 4,500 was given to him.

It was pleaded that thereafter, he never approached it to receive the handset in question. It was asserted that in the event of any handset being liquid damaged, waterlogged, tampered or physically damaged, the same is no longer covered by and under the limited warranty benefit offered by the Nokia Corporation/Nokia India and as such, they are under no obligation to repair the handset under the limited warranty benefits.

The forum said that the act and conduct of Nokia Care in not honouring the warranty and consequently not repairing the defective mobile set during the warranty period without any cost amount to deficiency in service.

Heading: Book school director for misappropriation of funds, says Patiala Divisional Commissioner - Indian Express
Content:
The Mohali police on Wednesday booked a foreign national on charges of disrespecting the Tricolour on the last day of the second cricket test match between India and Australia at the Punjab Cricket Association (PCA) Stadium.

A case under Section 2(L) of the Prevention of Insult to National Honour Act, 1971, was registered against the yet-to-be-identified accused at Phase VIII police station, Deputy Superintendent of Police (City-II) Swarndeep Singh told Newsline.

Singh said the action was taken on the basis of a news report, which appeared in English daily, showing the foreign national walking about with the national flag wrapped below his waist.

"We have yet to identify the accused through his details being procured from a Chandigarh hotel, where the foreign national had reportedly stayed during his Mohali visit," said DSP (City-II).

This was the second case of disrespect to the Tricolour registered in Mohali during the test match. During the inauguration of the match on October 17, the officials of PCA were booked under same charges for hoisting the Tricolour upside down on top of the north pavilion block.

The law provides imprisonment up to three years or fine or both for those found guilty of dishonouring the Tricolour in any manner at a public place.

Heading: ‘No religion negates values of peace, equality and justice’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Patiala Divisional Commissioner S K Ahluwalia today directed the principal a local private school to register an FIR against its director for misappropriation of school money running into lakhs of rupees.

After an inquiry initiated into the management of Modern School, the commissioner has held its president Ravi Singh, guilty of misappropriation of the school funds.

The school principal has also been directed by the divisional commissioner to file a complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act against the president, with regard to the dishonour of cheques.

He has also directed him to file a civil suit for the recovery of the misappropriated amount and other defaulting members of the managing committee.

The commissioner had initiated an inquiry against the management of Modern School after complaints were made by the parents and other public persons regarding the misappropriation of funds.

Heading: Software engineer held for torturing doctor wife - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly 800 students participated in an inter-faith dialogue held at Moti Ram Arya Senior Secondary Public School, as part of the Moral Week celebrations on Wednesday.

Various persons from religious and social organisations including Ex-Mayor Harjinder Kaur, Jama Masjid Imam Mulana Ajmal Khan, Administrator of the Simla-Chandigarh Diocese Father Thomas, Brahmrishi College of Education principal Dr Manisha and former secretary general, National Assembly of Bahai's in India, Professor Anil Sarwal, expressed their views on the topic.

Harjinder Kaur said, "There is no religion in the world which negates values of peace, equality, justice, truth, compassion, human dignity and love."

Quoting Mahatama Gandhi, Father Thomas explained the many facets of love for humanity propagated by Christianity, which Mahatama Gandhi used to tell his followers about after reading the Bible. 

Mulana Ajmal Khan, said human beings can be saved of many evils and acts of violence if they remember that some supreme power is keeping an account of all our activities.

Dr Manisha talked about inculcating virtues of love for not only human beings, but also for all the living and non-living beings on earth.

Heading: City schools flout fire safety norms - Indian Express
Content:
A Senior software engineer working with a multi-national company at Mohali, was arrested by the Punjab police here for allegedly torturing his doctor wife for dowry.

The police said the accused, Vikram Khorana, was wanted after his wife got a case registered at the Mohali police station for allegedly torturing her.

The FIR, registered under Section 498-A and 406 of the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), also listed Vikram's mother Renu Khorana and father Ram Singh Khorana as accused.

Following the rejection of his anticipatory bail, Vikram, who was working in Quark Media House at Mohali, had come to Jammu to evade arrest. His father Ram Singh and mother Renu had, however, got anticipatory bail from the court.

The police, after receiving specific information, raided his father's house at Sector 5 of the Channi Himmat area and arrested him.

Vikram had married Dr Upasana (name changed) in November 2007 and according to reports, her greedy husband, along with the in-laws, started harassing her from day one demanding cash and gift items.

Things went overboard when Renu's in-laws asked her to go to her parents' house and arrange money for buying a flat for Vikram in Chandigarh. As she refused, Renu was badly beaten and was thrown out of the house. She spent the night while sitting outside the house and later went to the police.

The police tried to sort out differences, but as all efforts failed, an FIR was registered against the accused.

Heading: 1 dead, 138 confirmed cases in Mohali, dengue on the rise - Indian Express
Content:
The schools in the city have shown gross neglect for the basic fire safety measures. While government schools do not have even the basic equipment, private schools are also guilty of violating the norms.

The sorry state of affairs can be gauged from the fact that most government schools lack even fire extinguishers.

Schools like Government Model High School, Sector 12, Sector 26, Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 10 and Government High School, Daria, Sector 47 are at a loss of fire equipment.

"We understand that it is a basic necessity. But we do not have the funds to buy them on our own. It should be the responsibility of the department to be concerned about such things but nobody has ever bothered," says a principal of a government school on condition of anonymity.

While some schools do have fire extinguishers, they are either expired or defunct.

"The authorities take the safety of children for granted. I am not sure if we will be able to deal with an emergency involving fire," says a teacher at Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 16.

S K Setia, former director public instructions (Schools), had, earlier, decided to upgrade schools by providing them with the latest fire extinguishers. He had also directed that adherence to fire safety norms should be made compulsory for all schools, while warning that schools found violating the prescribed guidelines would be dealt with strictly.

The auditorium in Bhavan Vidyalaya is a glaring example of how most schools are flouting the basic fire-safety norms. Constructed in the basement (which is against the local building bylaws), the auditorium has only one entrance with no proper outlet for ventilation. The hall in St Stephen's School also has only one exit and a few fire extinguishers.

Director Public Instructions (Schools) Samwartak Singh was not available for comments.

Heading: CBI probe demanded into dera manager’s ‘murder’ - Indian Express
Content:
The dreaded dengue fever has taken its toll in Mohali. A resident of Phase I, Kulwant Kaur, in her early 30s, died on late Tuesday night after a drastic fall in her platelet count at the Fortis Hospital.

Kulwant was suffering from acute fever since October 14, and had initially taken medication from a private practitioner in Phase VI, who then referred her to the PGI, Chandigarh, or Fortis Hospital on October 16, said area municipal councillor Rajinder Prasad Sharma while speaking to Newsline.

He added that Kulwant was admitted in the Fortis Hospital since October 16. During her hospitalisation, she underwent blood transfusion several times to boost her platelet count.

"At one stage, her platelet count had dipped to 30,000 but then recovered to 75,000, giving hope for her discharge," he added.

"All of a sudden, however, the doctors declared her dead last night," said Kulwant's family members.

In a contrasting statement, Fortis Hospital Medical Director Dr Ashok V Chordiya, claimed the patient was brought to the hospital only on Tuesday and that had died within 8 hours of hospitalisation. "She came with acute fever and her platelet count was very low, which is believed to be cause of death," revealed Dr Chordiya.

The DHO revealed that on coming to know about the dengue death from Civil Surgeon Dr Avtar Singh, he sent a team of officials, led by Epidemiologist Dr Sunita Paul, to visit the area.

"Our team was stunned to find the larvae of the dengue mosquito in stagnant water at the victim's house," said Dr Surila.

"We also carried out fogging in the house besides undertaking fever survey in the area," said the DHO. He added that no other member of the victim's family was found suffering from fever.

Though officially, it was the first dengue death in Mohali, a young woman had also died, due to

suspected dengue, nearly a fortnight ago at the PGI.

No confirmation was received from the PGI on a query posed by the Mohali district health department, said District Health Officer (DHO) Dr S P Surila.

The official count of confirmed dengue patients,

reported from Mohali, has touched 138, confirmed the DHO. A number of suspected dengue patients, however, continue to pour in private and government hospitals.

MC, Health dept responsible?

Area councillor Rajinder Prasad Sharma squarely held the Mohali Municipal Council and Health

department responsible for the death.

"Nothing has being done to check the spread of dengue in the city, which will be difficult to control

if it turns into an epidemic," said Sharma.

Heading: State still far from target of institutional deliveries - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court today issued notices to Director, Central Bureau of Investigation, Delhi and State of Haryana, on a petition filed by Ram Kumar Bishnoi, who had sought directions to the Central agency to investigate the alleged murder of Faquir Chand, a former manager of Dera Sacha Sauda, Sirsa.

The probe has been sought on the basis of the confession (see box) of one of the accused in the case before the media. The petitioner read out the confession made by Gobind Singh, former driver of Dera Sacha Sauda Chief, recorded in a video CD, in which he has named the persons who have allegedly eliminated Faquir Chand. The video CD was also placed on record.

It has been alleged that on September 23, 1990, Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh became the head of the dera, following which, Faquir Chand, who was the manager of the dera for more than 20 years, went missing. Faquir has missing since 1991. Complaints were submitted to the SP, Sirsa, regarding his sudden disappearencein 1992 and then another complaint was submitted on January 11, 1993 to Haryana police to trace him, says the petition.

The petitioner says that Haryana Police has done nothing till date as the persons accused belong to Dera Sacha Sauda and are "very influential". "The Haryana police had earlier given a clean chit to the dera chief in a case of rape and murder and it was only after the intervention of the High Court that the case was handed over to the CBI," argued the counsel for the petitioner.

It has been further stated that the petitioner even approached the CBI office personally at Chandigarh and his statement was recorded by the CBI. "Nothing has been done till date by the CBI as the officers said that without direction of the High Court in this case, they cannot investigate or arrest the accused," said the counsel.

Heading: HCS pass marks reduced for SC candidates - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the state government has established 491 delivery-huts in various parts of Haryana, the state is far from achieving the ambitious target of cent per cent institutionalised deliveries in the state.

The government launched the ambitious project to institutionalise deliveries and to provide the best possible medical care to pregnant mothers in the state almost half-a-decade ago, but

in spite of having improved the figure, a lot more needs to be done to take its benefits to rural areas.

Though the figure of institutional deliveries has jumped to 43 per cent from the 23 per cent-mark in 2004-05, when only 23 per cent deliveries were carried out in proper institutionalised manner and the remaining 77 per cent were conducted by midwives in highly unhygienic conditions; the fact remains that still more than 50 per cent of deliveries are conducted in the same traditional way.

"It is not easy to achieve cent per cent result in any field and our focus is on minimising the number of traditional deliveries," admits an official, adding,"The main aims were to reduce maternal mortality rates (MMR) and infant mortality rates (IMR) and ensure safe deliveries, which we have achieved with the setting up of delivery huts in the state."

Under the scheme, maternal mortality rate was to be reduced from 300 to 100 per lakh live births and infant mortality rate from 58 to 30 per thousand live births. Other aims were to ensure 100 per cent antenatal registration, to detect high-risk pregnancies and ensure timely referrals and ensure administration of polio dose and BCG vaccine to the newborn.

The institutional delivery rate in government health institutions was merely 15 per cent and only limited deliveries were conducted by the ANM concerned, who is responsible for providing health services to a population of approximately 5,000 to 7,000 persons.

However, to some extent, the new concept has broken the belief that the institutional deliveries are expensive. "In rural areas, where institutional deliveries were the prerogative of only the elite or the literate class, the setting up of delivery huts has received a very good response," said an official.

But, the goal of every single woman delivering her child in an institutionalised manner looks far.

Heading: ‘Sugarcane price would be highest’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana Chief Minister, Bhupinder Singh Hooda today announced five per cent decrease in the minimum pass marks required by SC candidates for recruitment to the posts of HCS (executive and judicial branches). candidates from this category would now be declared pass even if they get 45 per cent marks, five per cent less than the earlier minimum pass marks. He also announced increase in the amount of financial assistance being given to advocates belonging to the Scheduled Castes (SCs) for purchasing library books from Rs one lakh to Rs 1.5 lakh

Hooda, who was here to attend a seminar on 'Uplift of lawyers from weaker sections', organised by the Dr Ambedkar SC/ST Association of Advocates here today, said the state government was committed to the uplift of the weaker sections of society.

Terming Congress and the people of scheduled castes and backward classes as complementary to each other, he said that whenever people of these communities got annoyed with the party, it had lost power and whenever Congress lost power, a number of atrocities were committed on the people of these communities.

Hooda said he was highly sensitive to the problems of poor people of the society because he belongs to a family which always fought against social injustice. Giving details of the steps taken by his government for the uplift of the poor, he said that a seven-time increase in the budget meant for the development of SCs had been effected. HPCC president Phool Chand Mullana. Babu Ram Dahiya, president, Dr Ambedkar, SC/ST Association of Advocates, gave a memento to the Chief Minister. Former Chief Justice of Punjab and Haryana HC, Vijender Jain, was also present.

Heading: Ahluwalia granted bail by HC - Indian Express
Content:
The state government will soon declare new sugarcane price for the farmers, which would be the highest in the country, said Haryana Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda.

The CM said that sugarcane growers in the state were presently getting Rs 138 per quintal for sugarcane. Efforts were also being made to get export duty on basmati Rice reduced for the benefit of the farmers. The annual budget of the agriculture department had been raised from Rs 142 crore in the year 2004-05 to Rs 298 crore, Hooda said, adding the state government was also giving subsidy of Rs 500 per quintal on wheat seeds and Rs 1,200 per quintal on the seeds of pulses and oil seeds.

Heading: Row over central varsity: 3 Cong MPs meet Arjun Singh - Indian Express
Content:
The Himachal Pradesh High Court today granted bail to IAS officer Subhash Ahluwalia. While announcing the order, the court, however, imposed some conditions, saying that the accused will not tamper with evidence and not threaten witnesses in the case.

As per another condition imposed by the court, the accused would not be given his passport till investigation in the case is completed. Moreover, till the case against him for possessing disproportionate assets and income continues, he will not leave the station without permission.

Ahluwalia's bail application came up for hearing in the court of Justice Surender Singh Thakur, who ordered that bail be granted to Ahluwalia on bonds and surety of Rs 20,000. The sureties would be presented in the court of Special Judge J.L. Gupta, before whom the case was put up after Ahluwalia's arrest on October 8.

Pleading for Ahluwalia's bail, his counsel argued that ever since the case was registered by the Vigilance Bureau against him under Sections 13(1)E and 13 (2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, the accused had been cooperating in the police interrogation and had remained available for preliminary interrogation over 12 times.

The prosecution opposed his bail application and stated that the accused was an influential person and could influence witnesses and can escape from within the jurisdiction of the court. The prosecution also said that so far, information about the bank lockers of the accused at Panchkula was still eluding the police.

Justice Thakur observed that though corruption has deep roots in our country, it is not a common crime. In view of all the facts presented in the case and since the accused has been sent into judicial custody, he should be released on conditional bail.

Though Ahluwalia was remanded in judicial custody by Special Judge J.L. Gupta two days back, since then he has been admitted to a private hospital in Shimla and could not be moved to Kaithu Jail as per the court order. It is learnt that yesterday evening, Ahluwalia had reported improvement in his health, but remained admitted to the hospital till today.

Heading: Four Himachalis get awards for bravery - Indian Express
Content:
The proposed Central university in Kangra district has generated further controversy. First, it was a war of words between the ruling BJP and the state Congress leaders and now, three Lok Sabha members have met Union Human Resource Development Minister Arjun Singh, urging him to open the proposed university in or around Dharamshala and not at the site proposed by the present state government.

The three Congress MPs who met the Union HRD Minister are Chander Kumar from Kangra parliamentary constituency, Pratibha Singh from Mandi and Dhani Ram Shandil from Shimla segment.

Interestingly, the row over the university is not between the BJP and the Congress alone, but within the Congress as well. While some leaders have been supporting setting up of the university at Dehra, others want it at Dharamshala.

Chander Kumar told The Indian Express over phone that all of them met the HRD Minister today and explained to him the entire "politics" behind the proposal to open the university at Dehra. He said they had told Arjun Singh that the previous Congress government had suggested to open the university in and around Dharamshala and land was also identified for it.

"We told the Union Minister that while Dehra falls in Kangra district, it is close to the home district of Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal. Besides, Dehra Vidhan Sabha constituency is part of Hamirpur parliamentary segment represented by Anurag Thakur, Dhumal's son," said Chander Kumar.

He added that they had even given a letter to the Union Minister in this regard, stating that the Central university could not be opened at the proposed site in Dehra as the land suggested by the state government belongs to the forest department.

Apart from this, the proposed site is lacking infrastructure, transport and other facilities, said the Congress MP, who represents Kangra parliamentary segment. Chander Kumar said there is sufficient infrastructure which could be used to run classes at Dharamshala.

Even for constructing residential accommodation for the staff of the university and other offices, enough government land is available in and around Dharamshala, he said, adding that government land is available at Indru Nag and Sakoh localities near Dharamshala. The Congress leader said government land is also available at Shahpur, which is merely 25 kilometres away from Dharamshala. Besides, Kangra airport at Gaggal is only 14 kilometres away from Dharamshala.

Chander Kumar claimed that the Union Minister gave them a positive response and instructed the HRD Ministry officials to look into the matter.

A team from the Union HRD Ministry had paid a visit to the proposed site and inspected the entire area a few days ago. The HRD Ministry has to take a decision soon in this regard as Lok Sabha polls are not far away.

Heading: 3 from Punjab, 2 Haryanvis also awarded - Indian Express
Content:
Twelve years back, when Saroj realised how social restrictions among women in the Gaddi community result in illiteracy, long-term financial dependence and misery for the family once the husband is dead, she set up a self-help society to impart vocational skills to tribal women.

As she brought to life the idea given by a French woman, Isabelle Pompignat Mahendroo, the concept of self-reliance initially seemed too hard to click among the women of the tribal community in villages in the vicinity of Dharamshala. However, she initiated a food processing business from her home in Bhagsunag with the help of three girls and funding from donors for Gaddi Women Self-Help Society.

Over 12 years, the society has helped nearly 50 Gaddi women of Dharamkot, Bhagsu, Naddi and Baal villages to learn food processing, computers and stitching skills, which help them earn nearly Rs 700 as salary from the society and additional income from independent work.

Being a tourist destination, Dharamshala attracts several foreigners and the peanut butter, tofu and jams made by the women of the society is a hit among the restaurants and local stores. Saroj was today awarded the Gold Medal of the Godfrey Phillips Bravery Award for her perseverance in changing the mindset of Gaddi women, who never considered themselves important outside the home. "I saw the society's first success within first five years when six unmarried girls who had joined us had collected enough money to take care of their marriage expenses. This is where many others realised the importance of financial independence," says Saroj. The society has lately devised new training programmes for women in production, selling, maintaining accounts and writing bills.

The others to receive bravery awards from Himachal Pradesh include Virendra Dutt Sharma, a customs inspector, who was awarded the silver medal for saving lives of 20 passengers on board a bus that got stuck in Sirsa river near Nalagarh as the bridge across the river was damaged.

Kripal Thakur of Una district saved the lives of five persons who were washed away in Swan river. He was awarded a bronze medal by Godfrey Phillips for a social act of courage. Abdul Ghani (53 ) of Chamba was also awarded a bronze medal for donating blood 156 times and helping poor TB and leprosy patients and orphans.

Heading: Acid attack on sisters - Indian Express
Content:
When Sangeeta Deol of Punjab looks back at her 58 years of life, most of it was a struggle after she was afflicted with polio. However, today she is the owner of one of Punjab's top bee-keeping and mushroom cultivation farms at Dhanad village in Jalandhar. Deol was awarded the Godfrey Phillips Bravery Award in the topmost category of "Mind of Steel" by Governor Prabha Rau at a ceremony held in Shimla today.

Sangeeta contracted polio when she was just nine months old. Sangeeta was married into an agrarian family, where despite her physical challenge she drove a tractor in fields. "When I was married, all the land belonging to my husband's family was under mortgage. All that we had was a new tractor. I asked them to sell it and buy a second-hand one. From the balance amount, we got back some of the land. Later, one by one

we got back about eight acres," recalls Sangeeta.

However, she wanted to become independent and make a mark for herself. She began travelling to Delhi daily to market her mushrooms. "I tried setting up a poultry shop with over 8,000 birds after starting with just 20 chicks, but finally I settled for mushroom cultivation and bee keeping, for which I also did a formal course," she told ENS. Along with her husband, Inderpreet Singh, Sangeeta also invented an auto-honey extracting device.

Ramesh Kumar Nayak, a shopkeeper from Haryana, was awarded the gold medal for saving the life of a man who got stuck in a clogged sewer tank while cleaning it. Though the man died later, Nayak succeeded in rescuing another man who had gone into the sewer tank to save the first one.

Rajnish Pathania from Punjab was given a special bravery award for saving lives of eight of the 12 people aboard a Sumo, which fell into Kandi canal in Hoshiarpur district.

Vinod Kumar Kanathia from Haryana was awarded the silver medal for educating Muslim women in Mewat region of the state. He set up an Adi Gram Samiti that has started a education campaign for Muslim girls with 12 new exclusive centres for girls between six and 20 years of age. Today, the samiti runs 95 such education campaign centres in Mewat, where 5,000 girls have been educated.

A special award was given to Manmeet from non-profit voluntary organisation "Agaz", which works in Punjab for the uplift of women. Agaz has also adopted Aitiana village in an effort to make women self-reliant.

Heading: Panels for rural education dissolved at MLA’s behest - Indian Express
Content:
IN FEROZEPUR :Two motorcyclists booked for attempt to murder

Two motorcycle-borne youths today morning allegedly threw acid on two sisters who were going to work on a two-wheeler.

Twenty-six-year-old Nidhi Nanda, a practicing lawyer, and her 20-year-old sister Jyoti Nanda, a B.Sc student, who works with an insurance company, sustained injuries on face and back.

Both have been admitted to the local Civil Hospital. Senior Medical Officer (SMO) Dr MS Deena said injuries were not grave, but the patients were under observation.

Police have registered a case of attempt to murder against two unidentified persons. Narrating the sequence of events, Nidhi claimed that the accused slowed down their motorcycle near their two-wheeler and threw acid on them from a jug. "It was a big jug of 2.5-litre capacity. I was wearing my black coat, due to which I sustained only minor injuries. My sister, who was riding pillion, sustained more injuries," Nidhi said.

She said she had no clue about the accused and their motive. "I noted down the number of their motorcycle. Their motive could be known only after their arrest," said Nidhi. "Armymen, who were travelling in a vehicle behind us, took us to the hospital," Nidhi said.

Ferozepur SSP Dinesh Partap Singh said the number provided by victims appears "inaccurate". "We are verifying the near-possible numbers. The victims have not specified any motive. But there is always a reason behind such attacks," said the SSP.

Heading: Eyes transplant scam: 3 weeks on, cops yet to arrest accused - Indian Express
Content:
In a clear violation of rules, Rural Education Development Committees (REDC), also called Pendu Sikhya Vikas Committees (PSVC), are being dissolved in Adampur much before the completion of their three-year term.

This is allegedly being done on the directions of SAD MLA from Adampur Sarabjit Singh Makkar, who has not only directed the dissolution, but is also giving list of the persons to be taken in the new committees. The recommendations have been written on his letter-head and bear his signature.

Five PSVCs have been dissolved so far. In one such letter dated October 13, 2008, Makkar has recommended disbanding of Government Elementary School, Kadiana, PSVC to the school head and the BDPO concerned, saying that he has received "complaints regarding committee's functioning". He has also included a list of members to be taken in the new PSVC.

Notably, these committees are being formed under the Sarv Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), a Central government scheme under which grants are given for development of the schools in rural areas.

The funds are utilised by PSVC members, who include two panchayat members, one retired government teacher, an ex-serviceman, two PTA members, school head and a social worker.

As per norms, committees cannot be dissolved before three years, but its members can be changed in case new panchayats are elected or a member dies.

SSA state Project Director Krishan Kumar said, "PSVCs cannot be dissolved before the completion of their tenure, and the DEO concerned should be held responsible for any violation."

However, Makkar denied having recommended the dissolution and writing any such letter.

However, he said the school heads might have got his signatures on the list of proposed members after the decision to form a new PSVC was taken. Interestingly, the headmaster of Kadiana school, in a resolution, has said that the new committee was being formed on recommendation of MLA Sarabjit Singh Makkar.

Authorities at various other schools also said that they were under pressure to dissolve the committees.

Heading: Routed candidates running the show, Cong tells Speaker - Indian Express
Content:
Almost three weeks after the registration of a case against two doctors for illegal eye transplantations, the police have failed both to arrest the absconding accused and seize her passport.

Senior police officials said they were conducting raids to nab Neelima Sodhi, who is absconding ever since an FIR was registered against her at Rajpura police station. "We have warrants against Neelima till November 12," they said.

The seriousness of the detective wing of the city police can be gauged from the fact that officers investigating the matter are still trying to reach the accused on her mobile phone. "Her mobile phone is switched off and we do not have her passport. How can we know her whereabouts?" said DSP (D) Ashish Kapoor, adding, "We have, however, issued a red-corner notice."

Kapoor said they have written to the CBI's forensic laboratory to conduct a polygraph test of the accused, after a local court granted permission. "A reply from the CBI is awaited. The test will help in ascertaining how many illegal transplantations were carried out," he added.

Notably, three accused are behind bars. The investigating officer in the case, CIA Rajpura in-charge S S Cheema, said they have conducted raids at Chandigarh and Patiala, and Neelima would be arrested soon.

Accused Sunil, an employee at Government Hospital, Ambala, used to deliver bodies to the relatives after post-mortem.

Manjit Verma, driver of Dr JPS Sodhi and Neelima Sodhi, used to come to Ambala and buy a pair of eyes for Rs 1,500 from Sunil.

Heading: 12 lakh MTs of paddy yet to be lifted from mandis - Indian Express
Content:
A group of 16 Congress MLAs, led by leader of Opposition Rajinder Kaur Bhattal, today met Punjab Vidhan Sabha Speaker Nirmal Singh Kahlon and sought action against alleged breach of privilege and infringement of the rights of elected members of the Vidhan Sabha.

They said defeated candidates of the ruling party were bypassing elected representatives in disbursing funds and inaugurating schemes. This, they alleged, had the active support of the government.

The delegation alleged that Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal has abdicated his authority to his son Sukhbir Singh Badal, who has being laying foundation stones throughout the state.

The Congress has demanded that the Speaker should refer this issue to the privilege committee of the Vidhan Sabha and summon the Chief Secretary. "Laying of foundation stones, inauguration of important projects, distribution of cheques for development works and recommendations for transfers of employees are being undertaken by the defeated candidates," they alleged. Sukhpal Singh Khaira, Jeet Mohinder Singh Sidhu, Ajitinder Singh Mofar, Avtar Singh Brar, Darshan Singh Brar were part of the delegation.

Heading: Short Take - Indian Express
Content:
The state government may boast of buying 81 lakh metric tonnes of paddy, out of the total arrival of 82 lakh metric tonnes, but the truth is that 12 lakh metric tonnes are yet to be lifted from the mandis.

The complaints are same as last season: less number of trucks and shortage of labour. Long queues of trucks can be seen outside the shellers, where paddy bags are stored, as there is no labour to unload them. As per reports from different parts of the state, trucks have to wait for more than two days before they can head back to mandis to lift more stock.

About 1.6 lakh MTs of paddy is lying in Ferozepur, 1.14 lakh MTs in Bathinda, 1.14 lakh MTs in Moga and 9,100 tonnes in Muktsar.

Chairman of the Punjab Mandi Board Ajmer Singh Lakhowal said, "Farmers are not facing any problem as their harvest has already been bought, but the state government is finding it difficult to lift it. We have asked our secretaries to start fining the agencies if there is a delay in lifting the produce. We can impose a fine of 25 paisa per bag per day."

Harbans Singh Risha, who trades in Khanna mandi, said, "There are no hiccups here, as we are in a big mandi. But we have got reports that lifting is being delayed by three days."

It was learnt that before the start of procurement season, it was mooted that arhtiyas be handed over the charge of transporting grains, for which they would be paid extra. However, political preferences allegedly prevailed and the plan was thwarted.

Heading: We’re in the ‘army’ now! - Indian Express
Content:
The film circuit's abuzz with one-minute captures and contests

Everyone wants to cut a long story short, skip the sob and leapfrog to the end. That's the way life is, in a super fast track, so fast that even three-hour features have zipped it down to two, sometimes even an hour-and-a-half to keep the fidgety, short-on-time viewer in his chair. Short, now that's the keyword here. In a world that has too much to say, but too little time, short films come to the rescue. To the point, these witty pieces of imagination and captures say it all in nano seconds. Call them the two-minute maggie noodle films or micro-wave popcorn entertainment, the increasing number of short film contests and festivals doing the circuit are making sure that the shorties get to stand tall.

Surf this: There's the Get Shorty short film contest for amateur filmmakers on Zee Studio, Filmaka India always has one going on on its website, Buzz18 too has announced an Indian short film contest in association with the production house Pritish Nandy Communications called Shortcut, Passion for Cinema's out with the second one-minute film contest, Short Film Festival of India is always open to entries, Indyarocks too has a short film festival to its credit, YouTube has already become the centre of short takes..."It is very important that one starts with short films, it's like testing the waters first," feels Aamir's director Rajkumar Gupta. There is no dearth of stories, the universe is made up of them, and Gupta's of the view that sometimes, a short take justifies the piece more. "The short film contest is a very encouraging platform, one which acts as a stepping stone to bigger features, and here, aspiring filmmakers can experiment with their art and tell very compelling and moving stories in just a minute!" he adds. Road to the big screen, the short film with its big ideas and shoe-string budget proves just the right push for an amateur. "But please, do not confuse it with home videos," pleads a very skeptical Onir. The My Brother Nikhil director feels that it's too early to club this genre with cinema. "Because we don't have a very big market for this, and we are just beginners as of now," he refers to the difference in use of language, form, technology and content here. "No doubt it's a growing industry in India and there is talent appreciation, but the unfortunately, there's no money here, the filmmaker has to dish out every penny. Even the festivals don't pay! So you have to be sure and not treat it as a hobby," he opines.

Unlimited internet access, websites mushrooming all over the virtual space, accessible cheap technology, all aid the short filmmaker. "But till your content is not strong, nothing will work," says city's Dr Gaurav Chhabra. Brevity lies in the soul of wit, and after dabbling in short films, the doc's realized it's the right platform and push only when you succeed in saying something real big in few words. "Chhota mooh, badi baat," he reminds us of his local fest. "It's a boost, but avoid using mobiles, use only DV cams or high definition cameras to shoot, and make it picture worthy. It has to look like a complete piece of art with a thought, it has to have an impact," Onir sums it up with words of caution and advise. Good things always come in small packages!.

Contest call
* Zee Studio's Get Shorty where participants can send in their short film of about five minutes on a DVD to Zee Studio and the five best films received will be played on national television.
* The Wild Card Contest on Filmaka. Submissions close November 25th, 2008. No specific subjects, but duration limit is one to three minutes. www.filmaka.in
* Buzz18's out with Shortcut. The entries cannot be more than 10 minutes long.
* You can log on to shortfilmfestivalofindia.com for info.
* Check out passionforcinema.com and try the PFCOne contest
* For the environmentalists, BBC's Wildscreen is an option and so is India's CMS Vatavaran films.
* If you are interested in telling in a short poetry format, log on to www.sadho.com

Heading: Belle of the Fashion Week - Indian Express
Content:
The Theatre Army is acting to create a brand-new audience in the city

They hope to create a movement, one that will involve a large audience not only in the city, but villages too. The Theatre Army is on a roll and wants to reach out to various sections, with socially relevant plays in both Hindi and Punjabi. A pass-out of the Indian Theatre Department, Gaurav Sharma believes in keeping it simple, yet make the process effective. "Nukkad nataks are tough to do, but they have far-reaching effects,'' Gaurav adds they use their third eye while planning and performing plays. Recently the theatre group presented two plays titled, Mainu Tagore Bana De Maa and Idgah, both chosen to sensitize the audience towards values and human relationships. "Mainu Tagore...was a solo play and depicts the story of unfulfilled dreams of a daily wager, while Idgah was based on Munshi Premchand' story and childern of Khudda Alisher did a wonderful job of the performance,'' shares Gaurav, who directed the plays. The group also performs on a regular basis in government schools for they feel youngsters need to be involved in theatre to add meaning to their life and chisel their personality. What's best, the plays are chosen to get students interested in their syllabus as well. "We are focusing on Punjabi plays as of now, for we felt that not much is being done in the language and we need to promote it, theatre being one of the best mediums and also create a sincere following,'' Gaurav says they depend on the audience for support, improvement and encouragement. As for finances, it's always tough to manage that, as their shows are not ticketed. "Precisely why we have to look towards television or films to earn a living and have no regrets doing that, for we have the privilege to follow our heart and continue living our dream,'' Gaurav and his group are all set to launch a Hindi magazine, which will focus on the latest in the world of theatre and also the personalities influencing the the art. "We are working towards making it both informative and entertaining,'' promises Sharma.

Heading: Creative touch - Indian Express
Content:
Deepika Padukone on working with boyfriend Ranbir Kapoor and her forthcoming releases

Success sits easy on Deepika Padukone. Relaxing in her make up van outside the Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week venue, the lissome model-turned-actor talks animatedly about her smashing debut and her relationship with actor Ranbir Kapoor. "I am only two films old in Bollywood, so I find it a little premature when people call me successful. When I approach a shot, I give it my best. It's great if the film clicks. If it doesn't, I don't brood over it," she grins, in between getting ready for a turn on the ramp for designers Shantanu and Nikhil's Fiama di Wills show.

Padukone is still basking in the success of her second release, Sidharth Anand's Bachna Ae Haseeno. The conversation veers towards Kapoor as her co-star and Padukone acknowledges, "I am more relaxed when I am acting with him and it shows on screen," she smiles. In fact, ever since their romance became public, there have been many offers for them as a lead pair. But the actor is quick to point out in the same breath that they are not looking to cash in on their romance. "We don't approach offers thinking it will give us more time with each other. We have been signing projects only if they are appropriate for our careers. With that kind of money involved, nobody takes a risk unless they are confident it will pay off," she says.

Soon, we'll see the 22-year-old in Nikhil Advani's Chandni Chowk to China opposite Akshay Kumar, where she again has a double role after Om Shanti Om. "I am very fond of the movie because it's the first time I have attempted action in a film. I had been training in jijitsu most of last year that involves hanging from cables and wires," says Padukone, with some bruises from her action sequences clearly visible.

"There's this particular fight sequence that I have with Akshay in the movie which I was quite nervous about. He taught me action should be like a dance, smooth and graceful," she recalls. Even as she waits for the release of the film during Diwali, the actor is busy shooting for director Imtiaz Ali's yet to be titled film, opposite Saif Ali Khan. "It's a simple romance, quite contemporary, something which Imtiaz is so good at creating," she says.

Heading: Celeb watch - Indian Express
Content:
Yathee Kasaragod and Shalini Soni find their life's answers and expressions in colours

Life's happening around them and within their souls. Sensitivity to it all is what makes them artists, and also the urge to express it with the blend of style and freedom. Jodhpur based artists Yathee Kasaragod and Shalini Soni bring to the city their expressions through creative strokes. While for Shalini it's all about a personal journey, Yathee uses the palette to comment on life as well.

Showcasing 26 of his works, Yathee makes recurrent use of motifs like the birds, web and ropes. His characters are often groping for freedom, they find themselves caught in a net, looking for answers and struggling to make sense of life and the world. He titles his collection 'Behind the Window', "since these are emotions nobody expresses in open." So it's through the window that one sees the true expressions in the eyes — those of fear, doubt and hopelessness. The naked truths are all bared 'behind the window'. There is geometric division of the frames and detailing of the subjects through lines. Yathee uses graphics to portray the tragic Jodhpur temple accident.

In Shalini's works one sees glimpses of herself — in dreams, finding spirituality and fantasies. Her work is a very personal expression since it openly reveals her core. You find her dealing with the fact of elapsing time, relationships that may be, a sense of 'yet to bloom' depicted through the cocoons. In various frames she uses butterflies, flowers, shells, clouds et al. The thread, statues and the pomegranate remain her favourites," pomegranate symbolises fertility and spirituality, while the thread is a connection between ourselves and our higher selves. The forms of the ancient statues appeal to me, may be I connect with the past more," she smiles.

The exhibition is on at Government Museum and Art Gallery- Sector 10 till October 26, from 10 am to 7 pm.

Heading: Foot loose - Indian Express
Content:
Colour me wild!
The much awaited film 'Rang Rasiya', internationally known as the Colours of Passion, has been selected to be screened at two prestigious international film festivals. The film will be screened at the BFI's 52nd London Film Festival on October 26 and 30 followed by two screenings at the MIAAC Film Festival in New York, on November 6 (Museum of Arts and Design) and 8 (Tribeca Cinemas). The London film festival is UK's largest public film event, screening films from 60 countries. It focused on screening a selection of strong titles from other European film festivals, including Cannes and Venice. The MIAAC film festival in New York on the other hand show cases the finest films of Indian independent and diaspora cinema to New York for seven years. Directed by Ketan Mehta and produced by Deepa Sahi and Aanand Mahendroo, the film casts Randeep Hooda, Nandna Sen and Paresh Rawal, and Jim Boeven. Both strikingly beautiful and path breaking, Rang Rasiya charts the life of the great Indian artist Raja Ravi Varma. Often celebrated as a reformer, Raja Ravi Varma wanted his art to be seen by the common man. Through his imagery he brought Gods outside the confines of temples and places. The film also captures a love story of Shakespearean proportions…an intense tale of love betrayal and passion between the artist and his muse. Mehta's homage offers not only a spectacular insight into a turning point in Indian history, but also questions the freedom of the artist in contemporary society, exploring questions of moral policing, censorship and religious intolerance.

Made of Honour
FIRST, it was the Swiss, then the French, and now, it's the Americans. The world just can't get enough of Yash Chopra. The legendary filmmaker was honoured by a renowned American magazine, Hollywood Reporter in Mumbai. Chopra was felicitated for his invaluable contribution to the Indian cinema and the impact created by Yash Raj Films in business in the US. This reception was also held to celebrate The Nielsen Impact Awards, an international recognition of individuals who have significantly influenced the global media landscape. Katherine Oliver, the Commissioner of the New York City Mayor's Office of Film, Theatre & Broadcasting was also present to honour this event, along with leading luminaries from the Indian film fraternity. In 2004, Hollywood Reporter had carried a survey on the "Biggest Film Distribution Houses" in the world in which Yash Raj Films was listed as the 27th in the world, making it thereby, the Number 1 film distribution house in India. Founded in 1930, The Hollywood Reporter, now part of The Nielsen Company, was Hollywood's first daily entertainment trade paper and is relied by entertainment executives around the world for the most comprehensive and up-to-the-minute analysis of the entertainment business.

Heading: The English Knot - Indian Express
Content:
Talk On
Sparkle up your festivities with Vodafone's new schemes this season. The cellular service provider has announced 'Special plan 226' with full talk time worth Rs 201 and ISD bonus card 44 offering cheaper call rates for its prepaid customers in Punjab. Service taxes are applicable on the plans. The special prepaid 226 comes with a denomination of Rs 226. Apart from getting a full talk time customers will also get free 200 local SMS. This full talk time offer is valid till October 31. Priced at Rs 44, Vodafone ISD bonus card 44 offers cheaper ISD call rates to US, UK, Canada and Gulf countries. Both Vodafone plan 226 and bonus card 44 come with a validity of 30 days from the day of activation.

Get lucky
NOKIA India has rolled out a special offer for its consumers across the country. Nokia consumers can now take home an assured gift with every purchase. This includes Nokia branded leatherite pouches, exquisite Nokia mobile jewellery, Kolkata Knight Riders T-shirts, and 2-in-1 DVD packs, all redeemable over the counter. In addition to this, 500 lucky winners could also win Tanishq Gold gift vouchers worth Rs 5000, while four lucky consumers could win travel vouchers worth Rs 2,00,000 each. All one needs to do is walk into a Nokia outlet and purchase any Nokia handset worth Rs 5,500 or more. Consumers could also avail the scheme by exchanging their old Nokia handsets for new handsets worth Rs 5,500 or more.

It's a treat!
IN an endeavour to enhance the delight of their customers this Diwali, Godrej Appliances has announced the 'Godrej ke saath, Diwali bane aur bhi khas' scheme. The scheme offers any customer who purchases Godrej products an assured gift for Diwali. There are three levels of offers which are based on the product they purchase. On the purchase of high end products, the customer is eligible for 22 pieces premium Matt finished stainless steel dinner set worth Rs 2,995. In the mass premium segment, on offer is 3 pieces non-stick cookware set worth Rs 1,495 and for the mass segments the offer is 2 pieces non-stick cookware set worth Rs 995. The offer is valid till October 31.

Classic comeback
OCTOBER generally marks the end of the dull summer months and the beginning of much-awaited cultural activity. And this also the time for the much-awaited Chandigarh Sangeet Sammelan, which for the last three decades has been giving Chandigarh a musical treat. The credit for this venture goes to Kanta Saroop Krishen, who together with some like-minded people thought of the Indian National Theatre, the society that brings this cultural feast to the people of the city. This year's sammelan, which begins on October 24, features bright new faces like Ranjani Ramachandran, Arshad Ali, sitarist Deba Prosad Chakravorty from Kolkata and vocalist Raja Kale from Mumbai. The final day of the sammelan (October 26), will showcase flutist Prof Ravinder Singh and Ashwini Bhide Deshpande. Admission to the sessions is free and Indian National Theatre urges patrons to introduce their children to our heritage and culture.

Heading: History Repeated - Indian Express
Content:
We normally have certain concepts in mind that transform into a mindset. For example, when we think of a hedge, the picture that comes to our mind is a three to four feet high wall of green. But there are places where we do not need privacy and are looking for something that acts as barriers and beautifies the place. See the accompanying picture. The Duranta has been used as an indication for no access area and also for beautification. Such edges or 'hedges' are also used while making 'English Knot' gardens.

* I am interested in growing tulips and freesia. When should I start?

Raminder Singh, Chandigarh

You will have to wait for tulips till mid November. However, for Freesia you can go ahead.

* The seedlings of winter annuals are ready with me. Can I start transplanting?

Satinder Singh, Mohali

Yes, you can go ahead with planting of winter annuals. The advantage with early planting is that the plants will have better growth before winter sets in. you will have better flowering.

* I pruned my roses early i.e during September third week. Will it affect the flowering in any adverse way? My gardner says one should do pruning only in October.

Anup kumar, Chandigarh

Do not always listen to your gardner. You have done absolutely right by pruning early, as the first flush of blooms will appear before even the severe winter sets in and your blooms will escape winter injury.

* Can I plant palak now? Till when can I do it? I want to plant it in a staggered way to get more crop over a longer period of time.

Manisha, Chandigarh

Yes, you can plant palak now for winter and for spring season/summer crop you can grow it in February-March.

For gardening queries ask Dr Green at satishnarula@yahoo.co.in

Heading: Factions clash at PU, once again - Indian Express
Content:
Alliance Francaise recaptures some of the magnificent moments that made Europe

A dream, a vision, an idea and there was Europe. From the end of the Second World War, Franco-German reconciliation, the Hague European Congress and Eurovision to the post-war euphoria, creation of the Common Market whereby Europe became the Europe of six, to the great Europe Bridge, interminable negotiations with Great Britain which gave way to the Europe of nine, from democracy and artistic liberty, Beatles and Stones, Picasso and Dali, to the grand entries of Greece, Spain and Portugal making Europe of 10 then 12, from artistic expression of realism and violence, the fall of the Berlin wall to the democratisation of East European countries to the Europe of today, it surely is a world of change. And presenting it in a documentary is Hughes Nancy, narrating the whole story in an impressionistic way. On the occasion of World Day for Audiovisual Heritage, the Alliance Française and L'Institut National de l'Audiovisuel in association with The Indian Express are showcasing these movies from October 24 to 27, from 3:30 pm to and 5:30 pm. Apart from this, there'll be portrait of European artists, flashback of the construction of Europe, a montage of archives and music from L'Institut National de l'Audiovisuel, which present the moments of Europe, debate and discussion.

The special projection of the movie will take place on October 25 at 11am followed by discussion and brunch. Be there.

Heading: Building bylaws: Solar water systems a must everywhere - Indian Express
Content:
An old animosity between factions of Student Organisation of Panjab University (SOPU) and Haryana Student Association (HSA) turned ugly right outside the Botany department at the Panjab University campus today.

Two persons reportedly sustained injuries in the group clash and were identified as Sanjay Kumar and Surinder, former students of GSSD College in Sector 32 and HSA supporters. Police arrested former SOPU president, Uday Bhan, and Ankush, a student of Law department, from the spot.

Sources said Sanjay and one Sumit were involved in a tiff with SOPU supporters during the college elections last month. University Police Post in-charge Uday Pal Singh said Sanjay had come to the university on Wednesday to seek admission in the Physical Education department. "The members of SOPU saw him and decided to take revenge," he added.

Sources, however, said the groups had prefixed the clash and designated a time and venue for it. "About 30 HSA supporters reached the students' centre at 3 pm armed with swords and other weapons. When SOPU supporters reached the spot, the HSA supporters attacked them. The SOPU supporters ran towards the Botany department where their other members were waiting," sources added.

Eyewitnesses said the clash lasted 15 minutes until the police intervened. The gates of the university were immediately closed.

The members, however, managed to flee after scaling the wall of the campus opposite PGI. The police immediately rushed the two injured to Government Multi-Specialty Hospital in Sector 16. Doctors attending to them stated their condition was stable.

Prof Naval Kishore, Dean Students Welfare, said: "The students who are involved in the incident are outsiders and I am still to enquire about the matter and get details."

Police have registered a case against SOPU party president Barinder Singh Dhillon, president of campus from SOPU Sahil Nanda, Uday Bhan and Ankush, under Sections 147,148,149,323 and 506 of the IPC. Besides the two arrested, the others are still at large.

Over a crore spent, where is the security?
Security at PU came under the scanner once again following today's incident. The brawl outside the Botany department involved the university students who entered into a clash with a few outsiders. When the security intervened, the brawl had already taken place and students seriously injured. While the authorities generally maintain that it is not physically possible to check every outsider, those involved in today's brawl were students carrying weapons.
Security has been an issue of concern for quite some time now but nothing has been done to ensure it as yet.
After the hired private security failed to maintain discipline on the campus, the authorities decided to do away with the same and the hiring process for trained professionals is on.
The 40 trained professionals, who have already been hired, man all the university gates. On private security, meanwhile, the university has spent over a crore after paying Rs 5 lakh per month.

Heading: Trying to overtake, girl dies under truck - Indian Express
Content:
All commercial, institutional and hotel buildings, which use hot water, will have to install a solar water heating system of adequate capacity. The existing buildings which do not have this facility will provide it within one year from the date the orders are notified in the official gazette.

UT Chief Administrator Sanjay Kumar had issued orders regarding amendments in its building bylaws for commercial and residential units on Tuesday. As per rules, the orders will be notified by December 22, 60 days after being issued.

The orders are mandatory for residential buildings as well, constructed on a site of one kanal and above.

While a one kanal house will have to make provision for a solar water heating system with capacity of at least 100 litres, houses constructed on an area of two kanal or above will have to install the same with a minimum capacity of 200 litres. The existing houses are required to provide these facilities within two years from the date the orders are notified in the official gazette, that is December 22.

Talking to Newsline, Sanjay Kumar said: "The issue was under consideration for long and had to be implemented. We have given a timeframe of one year or two years, depending on the category of the premises, keeping in view that in certain houses, senior citizens stay alone. Such people might not be that swift in implementing the provisions. The timeframe will ensure all houses have such systems gradually."

Meanwhile, in all buildings with toilets or washrooms, dual flushing system of not more than seven liters per western commode (WC) will be mandatory to ensure water conservation. All commercial institutions and non-residential buildings will install the requisite flushing system within two years from the date of issuance of the notification.

According to the new fire safety norms, a minimum of two staircases are to be ensured in buildings above 15 metres of height. In buildings already constructed with one staircase as per the approved plan and architectural control, it will be mandatory to have more staircases as fire safety staircases. If the fire staircase cannot be provided within the existing building, it can be allowed beyond the architectural control of the building and the zoned area. In such cases, the staircases will be open to the sky and hence will not be counted towards the Floor-Area-Ratio (FAR). While providing the extra staircase, uniformity will have to be maintained.

In buildings, including residential, commercial and institutional, which are or will be located on plot measuring one kanal and above, will be required to have a rainwater harvesting system as per the specifications given by the Administration. This is to be installed within two years from the date of issuance of the notification.

The owner or lessee of any existing building, willing to avail the benefit(s) of additional volumetric control being granted through the orders issued yesterday, will only be granted the same after upgrading the parking facilities as per the new norms, wherever applicable, setting up solar water heating system, dual flushing system and rainwater harvesting system to recharge ground water in the respective buildings.

All new public buildings, which will be approved from now onwards, will have to conform to the requirements of Persons with Disabilities Act, 1995, and rules made there-under. The owners or lessee or occupier of existing buildings will make their houses as friendly as possible for persons with disabilities.

Norms for silent gensets
There will be no objection to install a silent generating set of capacity beyond 25 KVA in the basement or ground floor of the premises of commercial, industrial, public and apartment buildings in Chandigarh within the covered area norms subject to clearance by the Chandigarh Pollution Control Committee and the Electricity department. A silent generating set up to 25 KVA will be allowed on the lowest level of the residential building in compliance with air pollution norms and structure-borne noise levels being as approved by the Chandigarh Pollution Control Committee and the Electricity Department of Chandigarh Administration.

A silent generating set of any capacity and Dry Type Transformer or sub-station equipment will be allowed on the terrace or rooftop within service zone subject to the following conditions
i) That the structural stability is certified by a structural engineer
ii) That the Chief Fire Officer of the MC issues a No-Objection Certificate for the purpose
iii) That consent or clearance is obtained from the Chandigarh Pollution Control Committee
iv) The applicant will apply to the Electricity department for clearance and electricity connection

Heading: Foreign students to take PU’s own language test - Indian Express
Content:
Driving without helmet proved costly for a 21-year-old commerce student who was crushed under the front wheel of a truck today. Navjot Kaur, a resident of Mohali Phase VII, was on her way to college — Government College in Sector 46 — when the accident took place near the Mataur village roundabout .

"The victim, on her scooter (PB 65F 5082), tried to overtake the truck (PB 65G 5796) but did not notice another vehicle coming from the opposite side. Though she tried to turn left to avert the accident, she collided with the truck's bumper and lost balance. Thereafter she fell on the road and was crushed under the front wheel of the truck," a police officer said.

The truck driver did not stop and fled away from the spot. Passersby informed the police about the accident and noted down the registration number of the truck. Police later intercepted the vehicle near Colony Number 5 and arrested its driver, identified as Bharpur Singh of Mohali.

The father of the victim, meanwhile, lost consciousness upon identifying his daughter. Balvinder Singh, an assistant with Yadavindra Public School, Mohali, had to be rushed to hospital.

"Navjot had told her mother that she would return soon. They had planned to go shopping in the evening," Baljeet Singh, a relative of the victim's family said. Her brother is in Australia and has been informed about the accident.

The victim's body has been kept at the mortuary in Government Multi-Specialty Hospital in Sector 16 and would be handed over to the family after postmortem. Police have registered a case of rash driving and causing death due to negligence against the driver. The driver was later released on bail.

Heading: It’s early Diwali for family with Raj back home - Indian Express
Content:
Indian students applying to foreign universities are usually made to take English proficiency tests, mainly International English Language Testing System (IELTS) and Test For English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL).

The Panjab University has now decided to return the favour. Foreign students enrolling themselves here would now have to pass the university's own English proficiency test. The test would be compulsory and if a student fails, the degree would not be given.

This is probably one of the first instances where an Indian university has introduced a mandatory English proficiency test.

Professor Shelley Walia, Dean Foreign Students, explained the purpose: "We often find that foreign students, who have completed their degrees, have no clue of the language. The mode of instruction here is primarily English so it is appropriate that the student has a basic understanding and skill in the language."

Whether the test would have minimum passing marks or a grading system of evaluation is yet to be determined. All students, who are not the citizens of India and are studying in the Panjab University, would have to take this test whether they come from English-speaking countries or not.

Every year, around 300 foreign students apply to the Panjab University. Several of them are from the Middle East, Bhutan and Africa. Of late, a lot of students have come from Afghanistan. This is mainly attributed to reinstation of a liberal government in Kabul and the Centre's proactive policies to foster friendly ties with the Hamid Karzai Government.

The university has, meanwhile, made entry into the Ph d. course strictly on the basis of merit. An exemption, however, has been allowed to the foreign teaching professionals seeking admission in higher education.

Prof Walia said: "The teaching professionals, in a way, are mature enough and have experience. We have, therefore, exempted them from the entrance exam. They can directly enroll with us on the basis of their experience and educational qualifications."

Heading: Raj arrest: 1 lakh spent on security in single day - Indian Express
Content:
In a significant move ahead of Assembly elections in five states, CPM General Secretary Prakash Karat met Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mayawati at her official residence in Lucknow on Wednesday evening.

Karat, who was with Mayawati's for two hours, discussed the political scenario in view of the upcoming Assembly elections. BSP's National General Secretary Satish Chandra Mishra was also present during the meeting.

The meet has gained political significance in the wake of CPM's decision to support BSP candidates in those constituencies of the five states, where the former has not fielded its own candidates. "This has signaled the formation of an alliance between the BSP and Left parties at the national level ahead of the Lok Sabha elections," a source in the BSP said.

"Wednesday's meeting was an important step in the way of formation of the Third Front. CPM has already welcomed the idea by asking its supporters to vote for BSP in those constituencies, where its candidates are not contesting, a source in the state unit of CPM said. He, however, could not confirm whether both the parties would undertake joint campaign in the elections. Though what transpired between the two leaders at the meeting was not made public, a source said BSP may pass a similar resolution to support CPM candidates where its candidates are not contesting.

In an apparent bid to keep the Left in good humor, Mayawati had reportedly started maintaining distance from the BJP. The Left parties plan to work out a concrete strategy with the help of BSP to counter both the Congress and the BJP at the national level. Earlier, both BSP and CPM had joined hands to oppose the Indo-US nuclear deal during the trust vote in the Parliament.

Subsequently, Mayawati was projected as the leader of the possible Third Front.

Heading: Slain MNS man’s kin accuse Sena leader - Indian Express
Content:
The Railway police heaved a sigh of relief on Wednesday as it did not have to keep Thackeray in its custody. However, officials said they were prepared for any eventuality. Rs 1 lakh was spent in a single day on extra security that was deployed at stations and at the Kalyan railway court.

According to AK Sharma, Commissioner of the Government Railway Police, "Extra police force was called from Pune, Nagpur etc to cope up with the situation. Also, our man power - 3000 policemen- were deputed only for this purpose. In this exercise, Rs one lakh has been spent."

Earlier in the day, MNS workers stopped two trains on the Central railway's suburban section, one which was coming from Badlapur and the other that was coming from Kasara at 12.30 pm. S Mudgerikar, Chief Public Relations Officer of Central railway said, "But after 17 minutes, at 12.53 pm, train services were restored."

All outstation trains from Delhi to Bihar were also cancelled after a train was burnt by agitators in Bihar. Central Railway cancelled two outstation trains to Bihar. These trains are 3202- LTT- Patna express which leaves LTT at 10.10 pm and 2322 Howrah Mail which leaves CST for Kolkata through Bihar. Also, the 2141- Rajendra Nagar Express, which leaves CST at 11.25 pm was rescheduled for Thursday, 7.30 am.

"But this cancellation has been done only for today," added Mudgerikar.

The Railway Recruitment Board, which conducted Sunday's examinations (the day the entire episode erupted), refused to comment on the matter. Chairman Nand Kishore did not answer his phone and his office remained inaccessible to visitors.

Heading: Skull and bones in IIT-Kanpur could be of Mira Rd man - Indian Express
Content:
PISAVLI MURDER Day after, victim's uncle holds local corporator responsible for attack

The clash between MNS activists and North Indians in Pisavli village that left two North Indians and one MNS worker dead seems to have another angle to it. A day after tension gripped this village, located on the outskirts of Kalyan, Pandharinath, uncle of the slain MNS activist, Gurunath Bhoir, has alleged that Kailas Shinde, a local Shiv Sena corporator, was responsible for the attack and the MNS-North Indian clash was used as tool to exploit the situation and get Gurunath killed. In fact, barely a week ago, Gurunath had complained to the Manpada police that he was anticipating an attack from Shinde.

Shinde was, however, not available for comments and is absconding. "There were no clashes between the MNS and the North Indians till now and we have had cordial relations with the North Indians in our village," said Gurunath's uncle.

"It would be difficult to comment on it as probe is on. If we find Shinde's involvement in this case, we will nab him," said C S Ughade, Additional Commissioner (East Region) of the Thane police.

The two North Indians killed — Omprakash Dubey (34) and Mayur Dubey (30) — were both homeopathic doctors.

Bhoir, a builder, has an eight-month-old son. Mayur has a 15-day-old daughter and Omprakash is survived by his three children.

The incident occurred at the time when MNS chief Raj Thackeray was arrested and kept at the Manpada police station, not far from the village. Pisavli's population is estimated to be 30,000 and around 60 per cent of the residents are North Indians, a majority of whom stay in houses rented by the locals. Moreshwar Bhoir, MNS Kalyan taluka unit chief, stays in the same village.

According to Datta Karale, DCP (Zone III), on Tuesday morning, while MNS activists were forcing people to shut down shops in protest of Raj's arrest, Jaiprakash Dubey, a prominent North Indians of the village and a BJP worker, refused to shut his shop and attacked the MNS activists. The matter worsened in the evening when MNS activists, led by Moreshwar's younger brother Gurunath, clashed with the North Indians.

"In the evening Jaiprakash Dubey came near Bhoir's residence and challenged him," said Shoba Bhoir, the sarpanch of the village. "In retaliation, Gurunath and 10 others attacked the Dubey family. In the clash that followed, Gurunath was stabbed to death," added Karale. The MNS activists, in retaliation attacked the Dubeys and Omprakash and Mayur were lynched to death.

"It was a pre-planned attack," alleged S S Dubey, elder brother of Omprakash and Mayur. The bodies were taken to their hometown, Varanasi, on Wednesday evening. The cops have still not arrested anyone in the case.

Heading: AC train designing starts - Indian Express
Content:
