The Kanpur police now believe that the human skull and 16 bones recovered from the Indian Institute of Technology-Kanpur (IIT-K) on August 23 could be of Mumbai-based fashion designer Aadesh Bajpai, who went missing from the city on August 10.

Investigation in the case now heavily banks on a DNA report that is awaited.

Kanpur police found that Bajpai had become friends with an IIT-K student, Rahul Verma, through a social networking website. They questioned Verma, a B Tech student, but he denied having met or spoken to Bajpai on the phone.

Verma said his name had been unnecessarily dragged into the controversy. "It wasn't possible for me to be present with Bajpai on the evening of August 10, as I was attending a function organized by Art of Living in the Lecture room 7 of IIT-K," he said.

Verma claimed that the function started around 8 pm and lasted nearly two hours. "After attending the function, I went to the canteen of Hall 4 to have dinner, and after 10:30 pm, I went to my hostel room," he added.

A resident of Mira Road on Mumbai's outskirts, Bajpai came to Lucknow on August 3 on a business trip. After completing his business assignment, he came to Kanpur on August 10 to meet his cousin Vivek Trivedi in the Moolganj area. Trivedi has reportedly told the police that after meeting him, Bajpai left for IIT-K with Verma.

Trivedi further stated that Verma came to Moolganj and took Bajpai to IIT-K.

When Bajpai did not return the next day, Trivedi and other relatives started a search for him. On August 13, Bajpai's father Suryakant came to Kanpur and lodged a complaint with the Moolganj police station that his son had gone missing. The recovery of a skull and bones at IIT-K campus on August 23 gave a new twist to the case.

From Bajpai's mobile record, the police found that he had visited IIT-K on August 10. The case was then converted into one of kidnapping and the investigation transferred to Kalyanpur police station.

With investigations heading virtually nowhere, the police decided to go in for a DNA test of the recovered skull and bones. The report from the Forensic Science Laboratory, Hyderabad, is expected next week.

Circle Officer, Kalyanpur, Subhash Chandra Shakya said that they were working on every aspect of the case, but the position is still unclear.

IIT-K authorities said they were extending all cooperation to the police. Registrar Sanjeev Kashalkar said, "Neither has Verma run away from the institute, nor has he refused to face the police."

Dean of Students' Affair Partho Chakravorthy said that there had been references from the state security agencies about Bajpai having visited IIT-K. "We cannot keep an eye on all 4,000 students, but all required help is being given to the investigating team," he added.

Heading: Bail orders stress silence - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai commuter's dream of a comfortable train journey is inching towards reality with work on designing a prototype of an air-conditioned coach having begun at Research Design and Standards Organisation (RDSO) Lucknow. According to railway authorities, a train with air-conditioned coaches will glide on Mumbai's suburban railway tracks in two years.

R. K Rao of the Railway Board in New Delhi said: "Around two months ago, the designing began for an AC coach, at RDSO. Then they will prepare a prototype of the coach. Following trials, it will be ready for manufacture." He said the Integral Coach Factory, Perambur, would manufacture the coaches. "It will take at least two years from design to manufacture," he said.

Also, air-conditioned coaches can be attached to rakes running on AC/DC. Western Railway and Central Railway both have sufficient AC/ DC rakes now. In any case, sources said, WR and CR officials have been clear in their feasibility report that an entire train should be air-conditioned.

The move began about a year ago when Railway Minister Lalu Prasad asked WR and CR officials to work out a feasibility report. Earlier, about five years ago, the Western and Central Railways had submitted proposals to run air-conditioned coaches and a fully AC train respectively on the suburban section.

As far back as 2001 too, CR had shown interest in running a local train with only AC coaches from Kalyan to CST. The coaches for this train were to be fashioned from spare coaches of the Shatabdi Express.

"The fare was decided at Rs 220 for a one-time travel from Kalyan to CST or vice versa, as was applicable for the AC chair car of outstation trains," said a senior CR official. "Now, however, fare has not been discussed while designing has started," he added.

WR went one step further in 2002, when it converted a luggage coach into an air-conditioned one at the cost of Rs 11 lakh. A proposal was then dispatched to the Railway Board for approval to attach the coach, a half-coach with a capacity for 17 commuters, to a local train The proposal was rejected.

The coach continues to languish at the Mahalaxmi railway workshop, its wheels and some other parts removed. The new proposal for air-conditioned trains, however, will meet with a better fate, promise officials.

Heading: Former stock firm employee kills pregnant wife, hangs self - Indian Express
Content:
The three bail orders that Raj Thackeray has procured since Monday all include a rider prohibiting him from making inflammatory speeches or provoking sentiments, in which case the orders could be revoked. This condition is similar to the bail order issued to Raj after his arrest in February this year.

The MNS legal team is simultaneously attempting to get all his cases clubbed together for hearing at one court. However, the action is yet to be initiated. According to the bail conditions, Raj is expected to appear before the police at Kherwadi as well as before the Kalyan railway police on Thursday. At the Thane GRP, the cases him involve bailable sections.

Besides these, the hearing for the MNS application for a stay on the non-bailable warrant issued at Jamshedpur on October 17 is scheduled for Saturday.

Heading: State has right to turn green zone industrial: HC - Indian Express
Content:
After four members of the Nair family committed suicide due to financial crisis a few weeks ago, comes another similar incident where an unemployed man allegedly killed his nine-month pregnant wife before hanging himself at his residence in Kandivli on Tuesday night.

Parag Tanna (34) killed his wife, Neha alias Neeru (34), by smothering her with a pillow and later hung himself from the ceiling of his bedroom, allegedly due to depression over his unemployment and lack of finances. He had been staying in the flat with his wife and mother Induben, who discovered the bodies after she cam back from a temple visit.

Senior Police Inspector Surendra Kumar Jaiswal from the Kandivli police station said, "We received the information on Tuesday night about the murder and suicide from the residents of the building in Sairaj Nagar in Iraniwadi. When we reached, we found Parag's body hanging from a hook in the ceiling of the bedroom, while the body of his pregnant wife was lying on the floor there with a pillow lying nearby. We believe she had been smothered to death with the pillow by Parag before he hung himself."

As per the statement given by Parag's mother, she had left for her regular temple visit at 4 pm on Tuesday and had been at the temple till 9 in the night. When she returned home, she found the front door ajar and on venturing inside, discovered the bodies of her son and daughter-in-law.

"At the spot, we also found a 3-page-long suicide note in Gujarati in which he had written in detail about how he was unemployed and had no means to sustain himself and his family. Besides, he was depressed about the fact that after her wife delivers the child; he would be in no position to provide for the upbringing of the infant. In the note, he also requested his four sisters, who are married and stay with their husbands, to take care of his old mother. He also gave details about his insurance policies and all his other investment details in the note. He had invested some money in the stock market also," said Jaiswal. From the information gathered from Parag's mother and relatives, he worked with a stock market firm for some time but he quit his job due to some differences with his employer. He had been unemployed for about a month since then.

Parag had been staying in the flat on a leave-and-license basis since the past three months after the family sold their own house at Mathuradas Road.

"As Neha was pregnant by nine months, she had been staying with her family at Gorai for her first delivery as often is the custom. However, on Tuesday evening, Parag called her up and told her to come home, after which Neha requested her sister to drop her to their Iraniwadi residence," Jaiswal said.

The bodies, meanwhile, have been sent to Bhagwati Hospital for post-mortem. The family of Neha and Parag's mother were grief-struck and could not be reached for comment.

Heading: 3 years on, key accused held for murder, theft - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court on Wednesday observed that the state government is competent to change a zone from Green to Industrial.

The court was hearing a public interest litigation filed by Shetkari Sangarsh Samiti from Pezari village in Alibaug. The state government is acquiring 2500 acre of land in Shahapur village for Maharashtra Energy Generation Limited (MEGL), a subsidiary of Anil Ambani's Reliance Energy Limited which is proposing a 4000 MW natural gas and coal based plant there.

The locals had strongly opposed the proposal citing CRZ violation and other environmental issues.

The court had earlier directed the state government not to take possession of the 2500 acre land till further orders. Today the petitioners contended that the state government has no power for conversion of land use from green zone II to industrial zone. The land happens to be in G II zone.

Assistant government pleader Pradip Patil, however, submitted that under section 20 (2) of the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, the state government can change the zoning and in the instant case in the month of August the state government had issued notification in the official gazette inviting objections and suggestions from the interested parties.

"The court accepted the contentions and stated that the earlier order restraining the state from taking possession of land will continue. The state can however go ahead with the acquisition proceedings," Patil said.

According to Patil, MEGL had obtained the requisite clearance certificate from the Ministry of Environment and Forests. Thereafter, notification was issued in local newspapers under section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act.

Subsequently, the Additional Commissioner, Konkan Division, A D Kale issued notification on November 15 invoking the urgency clause under section 17 (4) of LAA whereby right of public hearing is deprived.

This was followed by numerous protests and morchas by the locals.

The case has been adjourned till November 26. The court had earlier stated that it will not interfere with the process of land acquisition by state authorities.

Heading: Cluster redevelop proposal to be finalised after Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
Three years after a gang of robbers murdered the father of two bar girls at their residence before absconding with cash and valuables amounting to Rs 3.5 lakh, the RCF police have arrested the alleged mastermind who planned the attack.

On Tuesday, while patrolling the Chembur Camp area Police Inspector (Crime) from the RCF police station nabbed Sunil Sisodiya alias Banda (23) who had orchestrated the robbery and murder of Subash Chari in January 2005. He had involved Vishal Kamalkishor Chari (18), Shripal Gulabsingh Sisodiya (40), Genuva Sisodiya and Sanjay Sisodiya in the plan, say the police.

"The accused and Chari hailed from the same village in Madhya Pradesh and therefore Banda was a frequent visitor at Chari's residence in Chembur Camp. Chari, during his visits, learnt of a peculiar arrangement between the father and the daughters whereby he would come to Mumbai every six months to take away a part of his daughters' earnings back home. His daughters worked as bar dancers and preferred to keep their savings at home rather than in a bank and the accused were aware of this," said RCF's Police Inspector (Crime) Shailesh Pasalwar.

Chari had arrived in Mumbai in December 2004 and had stayed on till the next month. A few minutes after midnight on January 10, when both the girls had gone to work, the five accused stealthily entered Chari's house. "Sunil Sisodiya had been planning the crime from five months before and he knew the girls' schedules. They had come prepared with the intention of killing Chari. They switched on the television at a high pitch to block out Chari's screams. While two of them strangulated him with a dupatta, the other slashed his throat with a knife and the remaining put an iron chain around his neck and tightened it till he died. Then they opened the cupboards and fled with 13 tolas of gold and Rs 2.15 lakh cash," said Assistant Police Inspector Rajesh Kewale who is a part of the investigation.

Chari's daughters had found his blood-soaked body under a mattress when they returned and filed a complaint at the RCF police station who issued an immediate alert. Their vigil led to the arrests of Vishal and Shripal who revealed that Sisodiya, who had made the plan, also amassed most of the stolen booty. They were acquitted by the court.

"We sold the gold and spent all the money in bars. Now I am in jail while the other four are back in Kanchanpur, our village in Madhya Pradesh. When I came to Mumbai, I worked in the kitchen of Congress house at Grant Road but then learnt how to commit thefts. But the others had an enmity with Chari and plotted the murder. I admit that I committed robberies but not the murder," said Sisodiya, who is presently lodged at the RCF police lockup.

"Sisodiya had committed four robberies in Malad and was in jail for over 10 months. After his release, he came to Chembur Camp to meet his aunt, when we arrested him," said Kewale.

Heading: Indian, foreign authors come together for literature fest in city - Indian Express
Content:
The much-delayed cluster re-development proposal will now be finalised after Diwali. Four months after the draft policy was introduced, public hearing on the proposal was completed recently. An overwhelming 400 suggestions and objections have been filed so far.

The draft notification for the cluster re-development approach was issued by the state urban development department in June this year. The date for finalising the proposal had to be extended because a large number of tenants, developers and various other groups wanted to give their opinion on the proposal.

Under the scheme, a cluster of buildings spread over a minimum area of 4000 sq meter will be granted a Floor Space Index (FSI) of 4 or FSI required for rehabilitation of existing tenants plus incentive, whichever is higher. The incentive FSI, the saleable component of the project, would be in the range of 50% to 75% of the rehabilitation FSI.

The deputy director of town planning who conducted the hearings, will submit report to the urban development department next month. "More than 50% of those who wrote in to us were present during the hearings. All these opinions have been recorded. The Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MHADA) too will be sending its suggestions separately," said an official from the Urban Development department.

MHADA will receive 5% of the total built up area free of cost every time the Floor Space Index (FSI) for rehabilitating the existing residents/ tenants exceeds 2.50.

"We are hoping to finalise the rule next month after taking all the opinions into account," the official added. UD officials state that once the scheme comes into force, the state government will also be able to select one of the nine developers who have shown interest in being a part of the pilot cluster redevelopment project in the island city.

Heading: HC order to flush out prisoners unable to pay bail bonds - Indian Express
Content:
With the idea of giving a boost to the literature of different Indian languages, a number of acclaimed writers and poets will come together on a common platform in the city as the second World Literature Festival begins on Thursday.

The festival, which is being organised by the Shahir Amar Sheikh Loknatya Kala Prabodhini, will be held at the P L Deshpande Maharashtra Kala Academy and will have authors from all over the world, including Germany, Norway, America, Greece and Scotland, among other international and Indian authors.

"Our aim is to discuss Indian literature at an international level. We will also be discussing literature in all Indian languages," said poet and social activist Namdeo Dhasal, one of the directors of the festival. "We will aim to make a forum that will involve the writers, publishers, translators and critics to make the work of good authors famous worldwide," he added.

The festival, which will be held in different parts of India each year, will also feature famous Indian names like Ashok Vajpai, Kanimozhi Karunanidhi, Keki N Daruwala, Malika Amar Sheikh and Gulzar among others. "Writers can help in analysing a number of social issues to overcome various conflicts," said B L Mungekar, former vice chancellor of Mumbai University and a present member of the Planning Commission. "Works of Indian writers get translated into so many languages. In India itself there are over 30 nationally recognised languages but still books are not given the respect they deserve," said Rajvinder Singh, a multi-lingual poet and one of the organisers of the festival, adding that India has the second largest English book production in the world, but lacks a tradition that makes books an important part of daily life.

"The exhibition is titled Wor(l)d Voices because we are essentially listening to what writers from around the world have to say about not only their books, but also their literary worlds and other issues they face," said Singh.

Heading: Univ senate meeting: VC says no delay in re-evaluation results - Indian Express
Content:
In a significant relief for thousands of undertrials languishing in jails due to their incapacity to pay their bail bonds, the Bombay High Court has held that the authorities should strictly go by laws under the Criminal Procedure Code wherein such persons can be declared indigent (poor or needy).

The order came on a bail application moved by an undertrial Shivaji Gavade Patil whose bail was rejected.

However, during the hearing of the application the issue regarding prisoners who were granted bail in bailable offences but could not furnish the bail bond was raised.

A division bench of Justice F I Rebello and Justice Ashutosh Kumbhakoni has now decided to monitor the situation for a year and has directed all the sessions judges in the state as well as Goa and Daman and Diu to call for periodical records from the Magistrates and jail superintendents to apprise them of the situation.

Through an amendment to section 436 of CrPC in 2005 it was decided that if a person is granted bail and he is unable to furnish the bail bond within seven days then he should be declared indigent and be released from jail. The judges had also visited jails in Ratnagiri and Yerawada after which amicus curie was appointed to assist the court in the issue.

The court observed that the state government and jail authorities cannot ignore the law and should not allow such persons to stay inside jail.

Amicus Curie in the case Yug Mohit Chaudhry had pointed out that there thousands of such cases in various jails across the state.

The matter will come up for hearing in November.

Heading: Train brings the smile back on the faces of millions - Indian Express
Content:
The senate meeting of the Mumbai University held on Wednesday saw a debate on major student issues, including the controversy regarding the re evaluation results. More than half the answer papers in all the streams sent for re evaluation to the University in the first half of October this year have 'drastic' changes in them. Out of 894 re evaluation applications completed by the university for third year commerce students, 541 papers have changes in them. Expressing concern over these changes, Pro vice chancellor Dr AD Sawant said, "Usually, after re evaluation, marks differ by plus or minus 5-10 per cent. But the changes were drastic this time"

The issue came to light after senate member Parag Vedak pointed out the delay in declaration of re evaluation results. The main reason for the delay is being attributed to the lack of examiners and their laxity while correcting papers. However, Dr Sawant refused to accept the charge that there was a delay and added that very few re evaluation forms are pending. "In Third Year Bachelor of Commerce. Only 21 out of 3879 applications in the first half of 2008 are pending. Similarly, only 1 out of 1388 and 7 out of 433 applications in LLM and Arts are pending." He attributed this decline in the number of pending cases to the recent streamlining of the photocopying procedure. Also, earlier students had to go the university to submit their applications but according to new rules, applications can be submitted in the respective colleges.

Regarding the setting up of sub centres at the University in Thane and Kalyan-Dombivali area, senate member B Salve said that it was the prerogative of the university to set up such sub centres in remote tribal areas instead of the urban part of the suburbs to ensure that tribal students who wish to study further and find travel difficult would be able to benefit. Vice chancellor, Dr Vijay Khole responding to the suggestions of Senate members to speed up the process of setting up sub centers said that the suggestion would be taken to the academic council and then the management council of the university. Once passed, a committee would be formed to survey tribal areas for the establishment of such centres. Senate members also elaborated on the lack of facilities at the Ratnagiri sub centre.

In light of the ongoing controversy surrounding the Marathi Manoos issue raised by the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena, senate member Prakash Darekar who belongs to the MNS said that the website of the university should have the option of Marathi, along with English."If IIT websites have the language option of Hindi, the Mumbai university website should also have the option of Marathi." Dr Khole responded by saying that the process of making the website in Marathi has already been initiated. Dr Khole responded by saying that the process of making the website in Marathi has already been initiated. Regarding the introduction of the one-year Masters programme, Parag Vedak said that the decision to introduce the course was being taken in a hurry without following the regulations of the University Grants Commission and All India Council for Technical Education.

Content:
Smile Train treats kids born with cleft lip and palate

More than a lakh children born with with cleft lip and palate in India may soon get back their smiles. Smile Train—an international program covering cleft lip surgeries in 50 countries across the world —is planning to reach out to more children than before.

With an average of 50,000 surgeries every year, Smile Train is planning to fan out to those rural areas that are presently not covered. Working exclusively on babies suffering with cleft lip, Smile Train corrects 50,000 children every year in India. Satish Karla, South Asian regional director, Smile Train says, "It is not a train. Initially we had plans to launch this programme on train but things didn't work so we are working in hospitals."

 According to Mullaney Brian, co-founder and president of Smile Train, the largest charity in US, cleft lip cases are ethnic specific and are found more commonly in Asians and black Africans. "The incidence of cleft lip in Asians is 1 in 1500 and in blacks 1 in 1200 where as in Caucasians it is 1 in 700. A million children are needlessly suffering due to ignorance. Surgery can change their lives." Brian adds, "The surgery is simple and costs just Rs 8000. It takes 45 minutes to return a smile on children's faces, a smile that will last forever. But even today thousands of children are deprived of the surgery. It not just affects their schooling but also their quality of life as they are tormented."

Hundred and fifty five hospitals and over 200 plastic surgeons in India conduct cleft lip surgeries sponsored by Smile Train.

"The uniqueness in this programme is that there are no mission doctors or hospitals from abroad conducting surgeries. Indian doctors are being trained and they take the procedure further in rural areas," says Brian.

"Even though there is awareness and such cases are picked up fast. India has a huge backlog of children with cleft lip. Over 10 lakh children require surgeries in India. Currently there is a mismatch of resources available and the patients. We are in constant look out for new hospitals to start cleft lip surgery especially in rural areas," says Karla.

Heading: Bihar-bound passengers stranded at CST due to protests in their state - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) on Wednesday handed over cheques towards maintenance of the 16 buildings in Tunga village at Powai where 3,000 households have been rehabilitated following the widening and developments of the Mithi river.

According to Dilip Kawathkar, Joint Project Director (public relations), MMRDA, all 16 buildings have been covered in Phase-I where amount derived out of interest were given to the respective buildings and the process commenced on Wednesday.

"Each building would get Rs 20,000 which is deposited in the bank by the developer for the period of 10 years and the interest derived every six months would be used for repair and maintenance of the buildings," said Kawathkar adding, "The total interest for all the 16 buildings is Rs 50.55 lakh for which the disbursal of cheques commenced on Wednesday."

The 3000 families were earlier residents of Parikhkhadi, Bailbazar, Sainath Nagar, which are under the widening of the Mithi River, they have since been relocated at Tunga village.

Kawathkar added, "MMRDA has ensured that post rehabilitation activities do not take a back seat. It would further ensure that registration of houses allotted to project affected persons gets expedited and that the maintenance work goes on at a regular basis."

Heading: MNS activists continue to vandalise shops, vehicles - Indian Express
Content:
The Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (CST) here was teeming with perplexed Bihar-bound passengers on Wednesday after their train Howrah Express was cancelled following some violent protests in Bihar where local students torched five bogies of the Vikramshila Express at Barh station in the north-eastern state.

After the Howrah Express (via Allahabad) was cancelled, the station was full of passengers huddled in groups, lounging and lying about while waiting for news about the train's new departure time on Thursday morning. While some of the people from Bihar at the station said they were leaving the city for personal reasons, some admitted that they wanted to flee the city due to the unrest that has been plaguing it after the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) workers took to the streets.

"We are worried that this time too, like the previous time, we will be targeted and beaten up," said one native of Bihar, who did not wish to be named.

He added, "We heard about the incident that took place in Bihar and we have decided that we don't want to take the same route, so we took this train."

This passenger and his friends, all construction workers at a site in Vikhroli, have decided that they will return to Mumbai only when there is a semblance of peace once more. "We will go there for two or three months and then come back once everything is okay," said another passenger. "Everywhere people are being beaten up. We have heard about the violence in Bandra and Worli and Kalyan," he added.

"Na he hum idhar ke rahe, na he hum udhar ke. (We are on no man's land right now)," said Mohammad Babaralo (25), a courier boy at Kalbadevi.  He was scheduled to go to Jharkhand via Hawra Mail on Wednesday. "I am not feeling well. The medicines here are not suiting me so am going back," said a pale looking Babaralo.

This group's main grouse is the fact that they are being targeted despite being in the city that offers everyone a good livelihood. "What these people are doing is very wrong. The money we earn here helps us feed our families back home. Now for the time we go back, we will have no income. Mumbai is as much ours and we are proud to say 'amchi Mumbai'," said another passenger in the group.

Meanwhile, A K Singh, senior PRO, the Central Railway said: "Two trains were cancelled today — 3202 Lokmanya Tilak-Patna Express that leave Kurla Terminus at 10.20 pm and 3222 Mumbai-Howarh Mail that leaves Mumbai CST at 9.25 at night. Another train Rajendra Nagar Patna train that was supposed to leave on Wednesday evening is rescheduled to Thursday morning."

Anxious passengers had queued up at the enquiry counter even as repeated announcements were made at the CST station. Many of them wanting to go home desperately like this 20-year-old Ravindra Kumar, who was restlessly waiting for a news on his train's departure. When asked about the MNS attacks in the city, Kumar said: "They say natives of Bihar should go back home. But if we go back 90 per cent of work in Mumbai will come to a standstill. Taxi drivers, factory workers, vegetable vendors, construction workers, motormen are all from Bihar. You cannot get all of them out," said Kumar, who works at steel shop at Bhayander.

Umesh Prasad and Dwarik Mahato, both farmers from Gaya in Bihar who were here for a 10-day visit, are tensed as they will have to wait spend the night at the railway station.

"We have no relatives here in Mumbai. We just came here to see Gateway of India, Elephanta caves and other prominent places. We have heard about the tension prevailing in the city," said Prasad with his one bag in tow.

Heading: Male-o-drama - Indian Express
Content:
Boman Irani gives suspense a shot with Maharathi,but agrees, comedy is his forte

Actor Boman Irani, 46, is a very busy man these days. With close to seven films (99, Maharathi, Three Idiots, Banda Yeh Bindaas Hai, Teen Patti, Yuvraaj, Little Zizou) lined up for release in the coming months, he has absolutely no time in between shooting schedules and post-production work. "I should slow down. After all I am still young to the film industry and I have taken on so much work. But I am happy that I have been trusted with vital roles in movie projects. I call it destiny," he states philosophically.

In between 'walking off the ramp' at fashion designer Anita Dongre's show at Wills India Fashion week last Saturday and filming, Irani has little time for anything else. But he will soon be seen on screen in a small cameo in Karan Johar's Dostana, alongside John Abraham and Abhishek Bachchan. "I am not too fond of cameos but sometimes its part of being in this industry," says Irani, who was recently in town for the promotion of his film Sorry Bhai. But ask Irani to choose from his line up of movies and he quickly comes up with Maharathi, the Paresh Rawal and Naseeruddin Shah starrer based on a popular Gujarati play by the same name. It's a murder mystery revolving around a wife's attempt to kill her husband by hiring a hit man. The shooting of the film is complete. "To be cast opposite Naseeruddin Shah is exciting in itself. I have watched his films when I was younger. And I miss the conversations we would share over lunch on the sets of the film," he reminisces.

This thriller is a one-off, says Irani, declaring that comedy will remain his forte. "I don't like slap stick comedy. I feel there is much more to a situation that just the gag," he says. These days Irani is busy winding up shooting for 99, based on the secret world of gambling, in which he plays a recovery agent with Kunal Khemu. Ask him what he misses most from his pre-acting days and Irani responds, "Photography. I carry my camera every where but hardly find time to use it."

Heading: Pretty in pink - Indian Express
Content:
Restaurateur Nelson Wang is back at the CCI Club, his "temple", after a nine-year hiatus

Nine years after being ousted, chef and restaurateur Nelson Wang of China Garden is back at the Cricket Club of India (CCI). Wang, who is credited for introducing Chinese to Indian masses, had had an unceremonious exit from the famed South Mumbai club in 1997.

The restaurateur, who was handling the catering for the Chinese cuisine at the club, is said to have been forced to withdraw his catering and refused his dues after a misunderstanding between the then management, headed by Raj Singh Dungarpur. "There was a problem between the two parties but I have put it all behind me. As for the money due to me, I am sure I will be compensated. CCI is a respectable institution and I have faith in all they do," says the chef who invented the Manchurian.

Wang returned to the club in August this year after the new management approached him. "CCI is my temple - this is the place that first gave me a career break. I feel fortunate to be back," raves Wang.

Current CEO and secretary Kamaljeet Rajpal chooses to call it "the return of the prodigal" and says that CCI is glad to have Wang back. "CCI has over 8,000 members and it's our duty to provide them with food at par in quality with what they enjoy outside. For a few years now there had been a demand to improvise on the same. Since we were in constant touch with Nelson, we proposed that he return and he accepted the offer after we ironed out the differences," smiles Rajpal.

Wang and the CCI committee have also reinstated Wang's affable manager Sam Chang from his retirement. "He is as young as energetic as he was a decade ago and an asset to the club as he shares a wonderful equation with many members,"

adds the CEO. The members too are supportive of the decision and sales seem to have doubled.

Wang, who also introduced Mumbai to the mouth-watering flavours of Schezwan and Hunan, has another innovation up his sleeve. The restaurateur has introduced veg meat, or mock meat dishes, in China Garden's outlets at Kemp's Corner and Khar. With the vegetarian guests in mind, dishes like veg lamb, veg prawns and veg chicken are meant to give them a flavour of the meats through 100 per cent vegetarian ingredients.

Heading: Fashion’s crowd - Indian Express
Content:
Pandit Shivkumar Sharma on an ideal audience

Few people know that Pandit Shivkumar Sharma is a trained tabla artiste and vocalist. The maestro is better known for bringing the santoor —a Kashmiri instrument traditionally used in Sufi music of the region and renowned for the subtlety of its music— on to the sanctified platform of Indian classical music. Ask Panditji about it and he enthusiastically launches into the history behind his association with the instrument. "My father had originally thought of introducing it into classical music. I took on the mantle after him and modified the santoor to fit the tonal range required for classical music," he says.

The renowned musician will be playing at the upcoming Raga Rasa Rang concert at the NCPA on Friday, October 26. What does the theme of the concert, Raga and Rasa, have to do with music? "In Indian classical music theory, each raga is accompanied by a certain mood, or rasa. When the raga changes, the mood changes. In fact, many people don't know it, but melody and rhythm work together to create a certain mood, so the tala is important too."

In a country with a long and rich tradition of classical music, the audience for this genre is shockingly limited. The Padmashri winner admits that classical music does have only a niche audience. "But," he says, "The number of fans is growing, not just in big cities like Mumbai, but also in smaller towns like Dehradun and Kota." He adds that he loves performing for an audience which is receptive and attentive. "Many people think that to understand classical music, you need special training. That's not true. If you're a regular and disciplined listener, you understand the music very easily."

Another interesting and little-known fact about the musician is that he partnered with celebrated flautist Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia to create music for five major movies - Silsila, Chandni, Lamhe, Parampara and Darr. How is creating music for a movie different from doing so for a live audience? "Very different," he says, "In a live performance, you get an instant reaction and you're in total control of the music. In a film, the music has to be situational and you have to keep in mind the concept, the script, the location, the characters and other factors. It requires a different kind of mindset."

Heading: Mayavanshi wins thriller - Indian Express
Content:
The Railways had a great day at the Mumbai Hockey Association (MHA)-Mahindra stadium in Churchgate on Wednesday as Western Railway and counterparts Central registered impressive wins in the MHA 2008-09 Super League. Western clinched a 4-3 thriller against Indian Navy, while Central won a hard fought battle against RCF 1-0.

The clash between Western Railway and the Navy outfit was a battle of two halves. Navy, who had taken the lead in each of their previous two defeats, ran into a 1-0 lead with Sajit Lakra converting their first penalty corner indirectly in the 20th minute. Western won four penalty corners on the trot in the first-half, but the equalizer continued to elude them.

Gursev Singh though fired Western right back into the game early in the second-half, as he converted a penalty corner with a drag-flick. Five minutes later, Jayesh Jadhav fired a brace to put Western right on top with a 3-1 lead. But the Navy-men came roaring back, as Bittu Shirgoka cashed in on a defensive lapse to fire in a loose ball in the 58th minute. Ajay Kumar then tapped a rebound pass from a Western defender in the 66th minute to level the game at 3-3. But two minutes from the final hooter, Hardeep Singh fed a bisecting pass to striker Chandrakesh Kumar, who guided the ball into the back of the wooden cage to deliver Navy a cruel third straight defeat. Ajaz Qureshi scored the solitary goal for Central Railway in their first win in the league.

Heading: With eye on polls, Karat meets Mayawati - Indian Express
Content:
Describing India and Japan as "major powers" and "two major pillars of new Asia," Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on Thursday said the two strategic partners are ready to play a "commensurate global role" in world affairs.

"On the strength of our strong bilateral partnership, we stand today as two major powers ready to play a commensurate global role," Singh said a day after inking a landmark security cooperation agreement with his Japanese counterpart Taro Aso here.

"India believes that a strong and dynamic Japan is a powerful factor of peace and stability in Asia and the world at large," Singh said at a welcome lunch reception held in his honour by the Japan-India Association and Japan-India Parliamentary Friendship League.

"We look to the wise counsel and leadership of Japan" to meet the challenges facing the globe, he said, adding that New Delhi wished to draw upon Tokyo's vast developmental experience and her traditional emphasis on "consensus, harmony and balance in solving formidable problems that now threaten global peace and prosperity".

Significantly, the function was also attended by former Japanese Premier Yoshiro Mori, who was instrumental in transforming the bilateral ties with a landmark visit in 2000, besides ex-premier Yasuo Fukuda.

Describing himself as a "frequent visitor" to Japan, Singh said: "it has been my earnest desire for past several decades, to see this relationship prosper and grow. I am very happy to witness today the transformation of India-Japan relations. It is truly developing into a global and strategic partnership as envisaged when Prime Minister Mori visited India in 2000".

"In the past 60 years, we have broadened and deepened the relationship into a durable and productive partnership," he said at the event, attended by prominent members of the growing Indian community in Japan.

In the next phase of the growing bilateral ties the two sides plan to exploit opportunities offered by globalisation, he said.

"In the next phase of our relationship, we seek to exploit the opportunities offered by globalisation and by the synergies in our economies to expand flows of trade, technology, investment and people-to-people contacts," the Prime Minister said.

Singh also thanked Japan for the developmental assistance it has been offering to India, especially for industrial modernisation. He also touched upon the raging global economic meltdown, referring to it as "multiple challenges" facing the world.

"The world is now facing multiple challenges. The spectre of recession in the global economy, coming as it does in the wake of steep rise in energy and food prices, threatens to disrupt the rhythm of economic development in many developing countries," he said.

Referring to other significant issues on the world scene, the prime minister said while terrorism is a "danger to our peace-loving societies, climate change and environmental degradation also threaten our beautiful planet".

Commending the immense contributions made by the Indian community in Japan, Singh said they have "built bridges of friendship and understanding between our two people. Their achievement have made India proud".

"I am confident that all of us gathered here today will redouble our efforts to strengthen our bilateral relationship, which is very important for our two countries, for Asia and indeed for the world at large," Singh said.

Heading: ‘Silting, not pollution, chocking Ganga’ - Indian Express
Content:
In a significant move ahead of Assembly elections in five states, CPM General Secretary Prakash Karat met Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mayawati at her official residence in Lucknow on Wednesday evening.

Karat, who was with Mayawati's for two hours, discussed the political scenario in view of the upcoming Assembly elections. BSP's National General Secretary Satish Chandra Mishra was also present during the meeting.

The meet has gained political significance in the wake of CPM's decision to support BSP candidates in those constituencies of the five states, where the former has not fielded its own candidates. "This has signaled the formation of an alliance between the BSP and Left parties at the national level ahead of the Lok Sabha elections," a source in the BSP said.

"Wednesday's meeting was an important step in the way of formation of the Third Front. CPM has already welcomed the idea by asking its supporters to vote for BSP in those constituencies, where its candidates are not contesting, a source in the state unit of CPM said. He, however, could not confirm whether both the parties would undertake joint campaign in the elections. Though what transpired between the two leaders at the meeting was not made public, a source said BSP may pass a similar resolution to support CPM candidates where its candidates are not contesting.

In an apparent bid to keep the Left in good humor, Mayawati had reportedly started maintaining distance from the BJP. The Left parties plan to work out a concrete strategy with the help of BSP to counter both the Congress and the BJP at the national level. Earlier, both BSP and CPM had joined hands to oppose the Indo-US nuclear deal during the trust vote in the Parliament.

Subsequently, Mayawati was projected as the leader of the possible Third Front.

Heading: Noida cops arrest 5 from Mumbai in internet hacking case - Indian Express
Content:
Sedimentation in river Ganga is the main cause of increasing pollution in the river, says a study carried out by the Geography department of Allahabad University and funded by the Union Grant Commission(UGC).

The recently submitted report to the UGC says 4 mm sedimentation per year is reported in Allahabad and Kanpur stretch of the river.

The survey was conducted by a team led by Dr S S Ojha, a reader in Geography department, in Phaphamau, Jhunsi and Naini in Allahabad and two places in Fatehpur and Kanpur. He said: " Till now, it was considered that industrial and human wastes had been polluting Ganga but the study revealed that had the river flown at its natural velocity, the pollutants would have been washed away." He added: "Silting affected the flow of the water and also caused expansion of Ganga bank that led to frequent changing of its course, causing floods in eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar."

In the absence of desilting operations, the river has become shallow over the decades, which hampered the its self purification mechanism, says the report.

Besides silting, throwing of polythene, flowers and immersion of idols have blocked the river bed, causing heavy obstruction in groundwater recharging. Ojha said: "While the sand along the banks of Yamuna is used for construction work, sand of the Ganga banks cannot be used due to its clayey nature and hence remains in the river for years."

Taking stock of government schemes, Ojha said: " Officials of Ganga Action Plan have not undertaken any dredging and the sedimentation has increased several times. Twenty mm sand was deposited in Ganga in just five years from 2002 to 2007."

He also said: "Yamuna is a tributary of Ganga and the main river is always deeper than its tributaries but in Allahabad, Yamuna is deeper than Ganga due to less siltation."

Elements containig arsenic released by industries have also posed a serious threat to the self purification mechanism of Ganga from Balia to Kanpur, says the report. After going through the findings, the UGC is reportedly planning a bigger study on the issue.

Heading: BSP leader, aides point pistol at cops - Indian Express
Content:
NOIDA police claimed to have cracked the case involving an internet hacker gang siphoning off Rs 1.66 crore from the account of an international electronic automotive goods supplier firm.

The people accused of being involved in the alleged internet hacking racket are all graduates — one of them, who had transferred the withdrawn money in his account is a civil engineer and an MBA.

The five arrested by the police are Mitul Trivedi, resident of Pune, Savio

Derochlobo, resident of Goa, Bharatbhai Patel, Uday Kapadia and Yogi Anjani Bhandari, all residents of Mumbai.

Police said the money transfer chain was broken after interrogating persons in Goa and Mumbai. "There are dozens of people who have received the money transferred from the account of P K Aggarwal. We have yet to trace the mastermind. The team sent to Mumbai will hopefully be able to crack the case soon," said R K Chaturvedi, SSP, Gautam Budh Nagar.

On October 11, P K Aggarwal had lodged a complaint saying Rs 1.66 crore had been siphoned off his bank account.

The first transaction took place on September 29, in which Rs 21.5 lakh was transferred to a Mumbai branch of the Punjab National Bank. The second transaction took place on October 1, in which Rs 81 lakh was siphoned off.

The Noida police have tracked down a long chain of money transfer to various local bank accounts in Goa, Mumbai and Mysore after they were alerted of a certain transaction to a bank account in Goa.

"The police were alerted of the fact that on October 2, Rs 80 lakh was transferred from the account of one Savio Derochlobo, resident of Panjim, Goa, who owns a firm called Panjim Asiatic State Development, to an ICICI Mumbai branch account. The money was then distributed among four, who have also been arrested. Savio had incurred a loan of Rs 5 crore and was in dire need of money," said Chaturvedi.

He also added that Rs 12.47 lakh have been recovered, apart from Rs 20 lakh that has been recovered from the bank account of N Venkatesh of Goa, after the police was informed of the money transferred in his account. "A total of Rs 52 lakh has been recovered and has been transferred back to the account of P K Aggarwal," said Chaturvedi.

According to circle officer Rajiv K Mishra, a team of the Noida police is investigating the accounts in Mumbai. "We will trace the complete chain and the mastermind involved in the crime soon," said Mishra.

Heading: Human remains found in IIT-K may be of missing Mumbai designer, say police - Indian Express
Content:
Three men, one of them a nominated corporator of the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), allegedly pulled a gun at policemen on checking drive near Kundan guest house under George Town police station late on Wednesday evening.

Sources said Krishna Mahajan, the nominated corporator of BSP, his friends Yogesh Kumar and Vijay were going on a bike, when Circle Officer (Traffic) O P Singh stopped them and asked for registration papers and helmet. An inebriated Mahajan allegedly took out his licenced pistol and pointed at Singh.

Superintendent of Police (Traffic) U S Jaiswal reached the spot but the miscreants misbehaved with him and threatened the policemen of dire consequences.

The policemen then dragged the trio, who were in a drunken state, to the George Town police station. Senior police officers soon reached the police station. Jaiswal said, "The accused pointed pistol at Singh and when I intervened, they misbehaved with me."

Initially, the policemen were demanding stern action against the accused. The police, however, reportedly buckled under pressure from senior BSP leaders. Sources said the matter was diffused after hours of negotiations between the police and the BSP.

Superintendent of Police Awdhesh Singh Vijeta denied the entire incident and said, "Only heated discussion had taken place between the policemen and the corporator."

Although the policemen did not lodge an FIR, they seized the bike and the pistol of the accused.

Heading: Needle of suspicion points to bride’s brothers - Indian Express
Content:
The DNA report, to be released next week, holds the key to the investigation into the recovered human skull and 16 bones from Indian Institute of Technology-Kanpur (IIT-K) on August 23.

The police suspect the remains could be of Mumbai-based fashion designer, Aadesh Bajpai, who went missing from the city on August 10. The Kanpur police have found that Bajpai had become friends with IIT-K student Rahul Verma, through the social networking website Orkut.

When questioned by the police, Verma, a BTech student, denied having any meeting or telephonic conversation with Bajpai. He said his name had been dragged unnecessarily into the controversy. "It wasn't possible for me to be with Bajpai on the evening of August 10, as I was attending a function organised by Art of Living in the Lecture room 7 of IIT-K," he said.

The function, he said, had started around 8 pm and lasted for nearly two hours. "Later, I went to the canteen of Hall 4 to have dinner, and after 10.30 pm, went to my hostel room," he added.

A resident of Mumbai's Meera Road, Bajpai came to Lucknow on August 3 on a business trip. After completing his assignment, he came to Kanpur on August 10 to meet his cousin Vivek Trivedi in Moolganj. Trivedi told police that after meeting him, Bajpai left for IIT-K with alongwith Verma. He said Verma came to Moolganj and took Bajpai to IIT-K. When Bajpai did not return the next day, Trivedi and his relatives began a search for him. On August 13, Bajpai's father Suryakant came to Kanpur and lodged a complaint with the Moolganj police, stating that his son had gone missing.

The recovery of a skull and bones at IIT-K campus on August 23 gave a fresh twist to the case. From Bajpai's cellphone records, the police found that he had visited IIT-K on August 10. The case was converted into one of kidnapping and the investigation was transferred to the Kalyanpur police station.

With investigations heading virtually nowhere, the police decided to go in for a DNA test of the recovered skull and bones. The report from the Forensic Science Laboratory, Hyderabad, is expected next week. Circle Officer, Kalyanpur, Subhash Chandra Shakya said they were working on every aspect of the case, but the situation is still unclear.

The IIT-K authorities said they were extending all cooperation to the police. Registrar Sanjeev Kashalkar said: "Neither has Verma run away from the institute, nor has he refused to face the police." The police spoke to Verma on October 3, and a team was expected on October 16 for a detailed inquiry. "A team of IIT-K authorities kept waiting alongwith Verma for the police team, but they did not come," he added.

The Dean of Students' Affair, Partho Chakravorthy, said there had been references from the state security agencies about Bajpai visiting the IIT-K. "We cannot keep an eye on all 4,000 students, but all help is being extended to the investigating team," he added. Asked about the status of the case, Kanpur SSP Hari Ram Sharma said: "It is too early to make a comment, but the case will be solved soon."

Heading: Govt to HC: Dismiss Railways writ petition on coach factory - Indian Express
Content:
Hours after a newlywed couple were thrown out of a moving train near Malhaur station by four unidentified men, the bride, Abhilasha Sharma, has said that she suspects her brothers' involvement in the incident, as they had disapproved her marriage with Pappu Sharma.

Pappu (34), who had objected to making lewd remarks against his wife by the four men, died on the spot. Abhilasha (20), survived and is undergoing treatment at the Civil Hospital. 

The Government Railway Police (GRP) also suspect that the family members of the victims are involved, as all the four men had been misbehavibg with the couple since they boarded the Amrapali Express from Naubasia station in Bihar.

"We do not rule out the involvement of Abhilasa's family in the incident," said Inspector General (IG) GRP Vishwajeet Kumar.

Abhilasha told the police that she married her childhood friend on October 17 against her brothers' wishes. Fearing that her brothers would not allow them to settle in their village — Madhavpur in Bihar's Purnia district — the couple decided to go to Punjab.

"Before boarding the train, the couple had spent one day at the home of their friend Manoj, who is also a close friend of Abhilasha's brother Bum Bum," said a senior GRP officer.

"The involvement of Manoj cannot be ruled out," he added.

"Bum Bum said that the inevitable has happened. Now, I don't need to tell anything to the police or anybody else," said Abhilasha. He had spoken to her on cellphone from Bihar.

The GRP have registered a case against four unknown men under Sections 308, 304, and 354 of the IPC and are hopeful of solving it.

The case may be transferred to the Bihar Police because the sequence of the events leading to the crime began in Bihar.

Heading: Security in Secretariat to soon go the Parliament way - Indian Express
Content:
The state government submitted an application to the Allahabad High Court on Wednesday asking it to dismiss a writ petition filed by the Union Railway Ministry in connection with the government's decision to take back land meant for the construction of a coach factory in Rae Bareli.

The government submitted that following its decision to return the land, the petition now stands "infructuous".The ministry, on the other hand, opposed the application on the ground that the new order is different from the previous one, as it talks about providing the land on lease.

In the previous order, land was registered in the ministry's name as an outright purchase.

The Lucknow Bench of the High Court comprising Justices Pradeep Kant and Ved Pal asked the ministry to submit a rejoinder as a reply to the counter-affidavit filed by the state. The next hearing will be held on November 11.

Dr Ashok Nigam, Additional Solicitor General and also the counsel of the ministry, said: "The counter-affidavit by the state government came around 4 pm on Tuesday. It hardly gave us time to prepare a reply. We have thus asked for more time to submit our rejoinder."

If necessary, we may amend the petition to challenge the fresh order of the state government, he added.

Heading: Soon, parents will be stakeholders in schools - Indian Express
Content:
Soon, the important buildings housing the state Secretariat offices in Lucknow will be refurbished with high-tech security gadgets. The security will be akin to the measures and gadgets installed at the Parliament House.

The state Cabinet has already sanctioned Rs 5.4 crore for installation of security measures like Video Surveillance System and the Smart Cards.

The surveillance cameras have been already installed in the Assembly building.

The Sachivalaya Administration Department - Administration (SADA) will hire Hyderabad-based M/s Electronics Corporation of India Limited (ECIL) to complete the new security installations for the secretariat buildings, including main building, Bapu Bhavan, Yojana Bhavan and Scahivalaya Annexe.

"As the Assembly is also on the premises of secretariat's main building, it will also be covered under the high-tech security scheme," a source in SADA said.

According to sources in the Assembly Secretariat, the important feature of the new security scheme is the use of Smart Cards. This card would keep a track on the movement of visitors and the employees.

"The movement of the cardholder will be recorded. It will help keep a record of the person's visits to different parts of the Secretariat building," the source said.

According to him, the holder of this card can move only in that parts where he is authorised to go. Moreover, he can exit from only the prescribed gates.

The best aspect of the Smart Card and the video surveillance system is that the employees' timing of arrival and departure could be recorded.

A control room will also be set up to monitor security. "The location of the control room will be decided by the authorities of the ECIL," the source said.

Besides, there is a possibility of the creation of separate control rooms on the premises of each building of the state Secretariat.

There is also a proposal to convert the existing gates into electronic gates.

Regarding the Video Surveillance system, sources in the SADA said there would be over 80 cameras to record the movement of cardholders and new visitors.

"These cameras will be very powerful. They will function like X-ray machines. It will not be possible to conceal any contraband objects on anyone's person. They will be installed at all the important points," the source said.

Besides, there is also an arrangement for the deployment of guards in plainclothes.

Heading: Narcotics officers under CBI scanner for link with drug dealers - Indian Express
Content:
To give voice to the parents of 1,081 primary schools students in the state, United Nation's International Children Emergency Fund (UNICEF) is all set to introduce an experimental model of the Parent-Teachers Association (PTA) in seven districts of the state.

In the new model, the parents will be the stakeholders in the project. The model aims to empower even illiterate parents to have a say in the functioning of the school.

As many as 8,652 parents and teachers will be trained for three days where they will analyse issues relating to the school, community participation and discuss problem areas. The training will be held in batches of 50.

Each school will have an eight-member committee, consisting of seven parents and the headmaster, who will serve as the member-secretary. The villagers will nominate the parents. Among the group, one parent will be selected as the president.

The PTA model will be introduced in districts like Rae Bareli, Lakhimpur Kheri, Lucknow, Barabanki, Baduan, Balrampur and Sonbhadra. A survey in this connection has already been conducted. At present, an awareness drive is in progress. Nehru Yuva Kendra (NYK), an autonomous body of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, will assist UNICEF to implement the model.

The new model will replace the earlier model of School Management Committee (SMC), which was initiated in four blocks — Barabanki, Lalitpur, Mithaura and Sitapur. "The model did not alllow the parents to have a voice, as the committee was then dominated by members like the gram pradhaan and teachers," said Binova Gautam, education specialist in UNICEF.

Sarva Shiksha Abhiyaan (SSA) State Project Director Beena said, "The PTA model initiated by the UNICEF is a good effort. Though it is mandatory to have PTA, they are hardly active in the state. So, we will adopt it if it is effective." The SSA was working towards making the PTAs active by the end of this year.

"With parents as stakeholders, the management of the schools will function in a better manner, as issues like attendance of teachers, distribution of books, mid-day meals will be properly looked into," said Gautam.

We are also exploring the option of bestowing financial powers on the PTA. At present, financial assistance is being provided to the gram pradhan, who in turn makes the necessary expenditure, he added.

Heading: Mother jumps before train with 3 children - Indian Express
Content:
Some of the inspectors and sub-inspectors of the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) posted at Lucknow have come under the Central Bureau of Investigation's (CBI) scanner for their alleged involvement with drug dealers.

A team of the Lucknow unit of the CBI has begun a preliminary inquiry into the issue. The move came after the CBI headquarters in New Delhi had received several complaints, naming the officers who were allowing drug dealers to operate in exchange for money, sources said. Most of the drug dealers are active in Lucknow, Barabanki and districts bordering Nepal and Uttarakhand, sources in the CBI said.

A case of alleged extortion against some NCB officials, which was registered with the Lucknow police in April, is still pending.

The FIR was lodged following a complaint filed by one Shiv Kumar, a brick kiln owner in Unnao district, at the Thakurganj police station. Kumar had to seek court's intervention to get the case registered, as the senior police officers had refused to lodge his complaint.

On April 9, the case was registered after court's order. Kumar alleged that a NCB team had picked him up from Ring Road in Thakurganj while he was buying petrol at a pump on December 4, 2006. The NCB officials detained him at their Mahanagar office and demanded money. They threatened to book him in a drug trafficking case if he failed to pay them the money.

The FIR alleged that only after his family members gave them Rs 17 lakh, the NCB team released him. Superintendent of Police (West) Paresh Pandey, however, said that he was unaware of the case.

Heading: Allahabad University V-C wants stern action against MNS - Indian Express
Content:
A woman committed suicide with her three children by jumping before a train on Wednesday morning in Kanpur.

Residents of Chakeri Gaon, the deceased were Rekha (34), Annu (13), Komal (10) and Shubham (8). Relatives of Rekha alleged that strained relations with her husband, Pramod Dixit, prompted her to take the extreme step.

Her brother Chandra Shekhar registered a complaint of harassment and abetment to suicide against Dixit at the Government Railway Police (GRP) station in Kanpur. Dixit was arrested later.

Locals claimed that Dixit was unemployed and an alcoholic, which had pushed the family into a financial crisis leading to frequent tussles between the couple. To manage the expenses, Rekha worked as a domestic help. On Tuesday night, the couple had a heated argument.

Locals said on Wednesday morning, Dixit thrashed Rekha when she asked him to look for a job. Subsequently, she called her brother Chandra Shekhar, who lived in Meuan village of Fatehpur district.

He later told the media: "She sounded disappointed on the phone and expressed the desire to end her life. Even after 15 years of marriage, Pramod was unwilling to start earning." He, however, said, "We did not imagine that Rekha would take the extreme step."

Inspector G R P Bhagwan Das Maurya said: "Both Chandra Shekar and locals claimed that the couple did not share a healthy relation. Prima facie it appears that family dispute prompted her to commit suicide."

He added, "Investigation is on and only when it is over, we can say anything conclusive on the issue."

Dixit, however, said, "Though we had differences, I did not prompt her to end her life with children." He claimed that the suicides had shocked him.

Heading: Under wraps - Indian Express
Content:
Vice-Chancellor of Allahabad Central University Professor Rajen G Harse, a Maharashtrian, has condemned the actions of Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) targeting north Indians.

Terming MNS chief Raj Thackeray's brand of politics "cheap", Harse said: "I am deeply pained to see youths of Maharastra indulging in arson and rioting and assaulting innocent people who are very much a part of the country."

Speaking to The Indian Express, he said these subversive forces should be dealt with an iron hand since they are attempting to divide the country.

Born in a Maharashtrian family, Harse hails from Kothrud — a small town in Pune. He spent his childhood in Mumbai and Pune, and completed his schooling and college education from there.

Recalling the resilient nature of Mumbai in particular and Maharashtra in general, he said: "Maharashtra is a cosmopolitan state, which welcomes people from across the country. I really do not want to live in Mumbai if this continues there."

With protests against Raj Thackeray growing louder in states like Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, Harse said that he does not feel threatened by students and people of Allahabad. "Being the V-C of an university in the Hindi heartland, where people have been protesting Raj Thackeray's misdeed, I do not feel threatened at all. Rather I feel safer here," he said.

Professors and students of the university also have no grudge against Maharashtrians settled in north India.

Student leader Sudhir Singh said: "No, we are not cowards that we will assault a Maharashtrian V-C in order to avenge what is happening in Maharashtra. It is our duty to protect the V-C here and we will thwart any move by anyone to harm him."

Heading: Trip to India at 3,750 Pak rupees only! - Indian Express
Content:
Stand-up comic Russell Peters returns bringing his provocation with a pinch

When Canadian comedian Russell Peters toured India last year he was very amused at how many men hold hands here. Come October 27 and Peters will once again be back on stage in Mumbai with his observational comedy about communities and culture around the world. "This time I'm hoping to be funny again," says Peters and immediately adds, "Being funny is a tough thing."

This is Peters' 20th anniversary tour, and his performance will feature his 'greatest hits' along with some new material since his visit last year.

Peters who writes his own acts is very popular for his in-your-face mockery of racial stereotypes and his cracks on the cultural divide between different ethnicities.

"Ninety-five per cent my act is based on real-life experiences of meeting people. But it is the exaggeration of those experiences that make the act interesting," admits Peters, who says he lets spontaneity get the best out of him. "I don't think about the script once I get on stage. I just go with the flow," he says, whose humour even parodies his parents with the signature "Somebody gotta get hurt real bad".

Peters, who at present lives in Los Angeles, was born in Toronto and is of Indian descent with his father born in Mumbai and his mother in Kolkata. Speaking of which he says, "All of my mother's family, going back to my great-grandmother were born in Kolkata. Even my brother, Clayton, who's also my manager, was born in Kolkata. I have uncles, aunts and several cousins who still live in there."

Although he has travelled the globe belting out witty performances in countries including Australia, China, UAE and Vietnam among others, the one continent he has missed is South America and explains why.

"They don't speak English so that's out of question," laughs Peters, who still refuses any Hollywood movie offer that asks him to play a dumb, nerdy NRI Indian.

"I think Bollywood makes Indians look dumb enough so I certainly refuse to let anyone else make us look dumber," says Peters with a grin.

While his latest release is a self-produced DVD titled Red, White and Brown, the compilation may not find a release in India but he plans to carry some for the fans.

Heading: Freight corridor can be Singur II, warn farmers - Indian Express
Content:
Eight Pakistanis, detained for illegally sneaking into India, had paid Rs 30,000 to a Karachi-based agent

A trip from Pakistan to India via sea route without proper documents can be as cheap as 3,750 Pakistani rupees. No kidding this, but a startling revelation made by eight Pakistani nationals, who were apprehended by the Indian Coast Guard (ICG) near Nalia in Bhuj on Sunday morning.

A Pakistani motorboat had dropped them on an uninhabited island opposite Jakhau, from where the ICG personnel apprehended and later handed them over to the Kutch police.

In what seems to be an organised racket, Kutch police officials interrogating the eight accused of sneaking into India illegally, said on Wednesday that an agent in Karachi had mediated the deal in the first week of October for 30,000 Pakistani rupees.

"The eight boarded a specified boat at Hyaderi, about 40 kms from Karachi, on October 17, and were dropped on the

island around 1 am on October 19," said Girish Pandya, Deputy Superintendent of Police, Nakhatrana division.

According to the police, the boat left Hyadari around mid-noon on Friday and reached Ketibandar in Pakistani waters by late that night. They resumed their journey around 6 am on Saturday after spending a night in a lodge there. Enroute their destination, they halted at a place called Savla Pir in Indian waters for about half-an-hour and continued after paying obeisance at a famous saint's dargah there, the police added.

"It seems that the four-member crew was familiar with the particular sea route they chose. This route has almost no security deployment. The accused also told us that they were assured security on the grounds that the 'expert' crew had safely ferried several people in the same way

before," Pandya said.

The police have seized 15,000 Indian rupees from the accused. "The Karachi-based accused had facilitated the currency transfer before putting these people on boards. The payment made to the boat owners was done in Pakistani currency," he added.

While fencing on the Indo-Pak land border across Gujarat is nearing its completion, the coastal and creek areas continue to remain porous and the security troops are not able to reach there because of rough and marshy terrains. Amid increased perception of terror attacks in Gujarat, the state intelligence has already alerted the BSF and the ICG against creek and coastal areas now being more vulnerable to illegal infiltration and smuggling

"We cannot rule out the possibility of terrorists and anti-social elements using the same mode to sneak into India," Pandya said.

"Coastal area of over 60 kms between Medi in Kutch and Jakhau in Bhuj is completely unguarded. In at least three cases of detected or foiled infiltration bids, including one with counterfeit Indian currency, intrusion took place from this stretch," said an officer of the Gujarat frontier, BSF.

Sources in the ICG said the boat used in this case was a twin-engine one. "This is because only a twin-engine boat can sail through this kind of terrain, which is full of shifting bars," said an officer.

A day before apprehending the eight – Mohammed Hussain Chavada (46), Mohammed Salim Hussain (21), Mohammed Aslam Hussain (19), Amina Hussain (35), Savra (16), Suhra (14), Suleman Hussain (12) and Mohammed Srif Hussain (10) – the ICG had on October 18 unearthed a liquor smuggling racket through the sea route. The ICG had caught 12 foreign liquor laden fishing boats some 20 miles off the Jakhau coast.

Meanwhile, the Kutch police have found addresses of the people staying in Anjar in Kutch, whom the eight Pakistanis intended to meet during their visit. The accused had migrated to Pakistan in 1990 and have been staying in Hajri near Karachi since then. They had come to India through land routes on at least two earlier occasions, the police sad.

Heading: With no more Pota trials, where does Nanavati-Mehta report stand? - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian Railways' Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC) has run into trouble in Vadodara, Anand and Kheda, with at least 1,333 farmers in Vadodara taluka alone opposing the move.

In a meeting held on Tuesday with Railways officials, the farmers threatened to begin an agitation on the lines of the one held in Singur. The meeting was held near Bil, one of the 16 villages in Vadodara which lie on the route of the corridor.

The discussion was initiated by the Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC) — in cooperation with a Delhi-based private engineering firm — which is providing the Centre a Rs 2,500-crore loan for the 50-metre wide Vadodara-Rewari Dedicated Freight Corridor.

The farmers were represented by the Baroda District Kheva Samaj chairman, Hasmukh Bhatt, who said that the Vadodara Urban Development Authority (VUDA) has already acquired some of their land for the Mega City project.

"Now, with the Railways asking us more land, we will have nothing left," said Bhatt, who refused to partake of the lunch provided by the railway officials.

If the Railways sticks to its plan for the DFC, the farmers from Varnama, Kalali, Bin, Sayli, Etola, Varsad, Pokarpur, Sindhrot, Kotna, Madhepur, Sevasi, Samyali and Patod will be directly affected, he added.

The leader of the engineering group, Tirthanker Banerjee, confirmed the names of the villages in Vadodara.

The director from JBIC, Suseke Mirato, said the bank officials, in cooperation with a Japanese environmental and social impact assessment group -- Japanese International Cooperation Agency (JICA) — are trying to estimate the sociological impact of the project.

The study encompasses farmers across Vadodara-Rewari, starting from Bahadurgarh in Uttar Pradesh to Vadodara and Mehsana districts.

"In Gujarat, we have faced opposition from the farmers in Anand, Kheda and Vadodara," said Mirato. "We are discussing the issues with the communities here and will submit a report to the Indian Railways suggesting the kind of compensation that could be given to the farmers."

The Railways officials, though, had a different story to tell, particularly in case of Vadodara.

"This is the builder lobby, which is asking farmers not to give the land for the DFC," said P K Rai, Senior Manager for Appellate Authority, who attended the meeting. "With growing realty value, some villages in and around the city have become hotspots."

The Railways has already constructed underpasses and drainage systems along the route of the corridor, he added.

Heading: Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor gets government nod - Indian Express
Content:
Was the burning of S-6 coach of Sabarmati Express at the Godhra railway station on February 27, 2002 a 'pre planned act' and 'a part of a larger conspiracy' as concluded by the Nanavati-Mehta Commission in part one of its report? Or was it just a 'simple case of unlawful assembly' as held by the Central Review Committee on Pota on May 16, 2005?

The order of the Supreme Court on Wednesday, upholding the constitutionality of the Pota Repeal Act and reaffirming that the decisions of the Pota review committee are valid, has again raised serious questions about the conclusions reached by the Justice Nanavati headed Commission of Inquiry.

The Commission's conclusions are

primarily based on the police chargesheet and confessions of the accused arrested under Pota, all which have no legal sanctity now.

"It means two things. First that the Pota charges be dropped, and secondly, all the evidence collected under Pota is now of no use. The whole conspiracy case has been built on the evidence collected under Pota. Now, all of that no longer stand," said Mukul Sinha, advocate representing the Jan Sangharsh Manch (JSM).

Furthermore, the decisions of the Pota review committee, which is binding on all subordinate courts where Pota cases are going on, was completely overlooked by the Nanvati Commission.

In fact, the order of the Central Review Committee on Pota was placed before the Nanavati Commission as an exhibit by the JSM, one of the parties appearing before it, and is part of the record. For reasons not disclosed, the Commission did not even once mention the order of the review committee in its 168-page report.

The review committee's decision had categorically not accepted the police case where it was said the conspiracy was planned the night before the attack on the train at a guest house near the Godhra railway station.

It had said, "Regarding the conspiracy alleged to have been hatched during the night of February 26, 2002 at the Aman Guest House, this theory does not seem to be probable on the case of prosecution itself."

While the Godhra accused can still be tried for criminal conspiracy under Section 120-B of the Indian Penal Code, under which they were booked in the first chargesheet filed on May 22, 2002, all the evidence collected in support of the conspiracy theory has been done under Pota.

The police case of conspiracy is primarily based on the confessions of one Jabir Behra recorded under the provisions of Pota.

However, Behra retracted his confession later, a fact noted by the Commission but not given any credence.

The Nanavati Commission, on the other hand, had completely bypassed this binding conclusion of a statutory body, and had on the line of the police investigation decided that the conspiracy was plotted at the Aman Guest House.

Heading: Union ministry refuses Rs 200-cr grant to Gujarat - Indian Express
Content:
The Central government has accorded 'in-principle' approval to the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC) project outline in August last year, the Rajya Sabha was informed on Thursday.

The project would be developed through Public-Private-Partnership with world-class infrastructure in the region, including road transport connectivity, Minister of State for Industry Ashwani Kumar stated in a written reply.

A central special purpose vehicle — DMIC Development Corporation (DMICDC) — was incorporated in January and the corporation has appointed an international consultant, he said.

A detailed perspective plan for the overall DMIC region with pre-feasibility studies, which includes road linkages to be developed in the region, would be prepared by the consultant, he added.

The Gujarat Infrastructure Development Board (GIDB), a state government-owned entity, has forwarded a proposal for the augmentation of roads in the state in the DMIC.

DMICDC has also entered into a memorandum of understanding with the GIDB in July to facilitate development of select 'early bird' projects.

The SPV has since then appointed an international consultant for preparation of development plan for the identified investment region in Gujarat.
