According to estimates, the 1,500-km project with manufacturing and trading hubs between New Delhi and Mumbai involves an investment of 100 billion dollars.

The project would be developed along side the Delhi-Mumbai dedicated rail freight route and is expected to be ready by 2013.

It would cover six states — Delhi and NCR, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Maharashtra.

Heading: SU cracks down on unauthorised study centres, franchises in Rajkot - Indian Express
Content:
State government has been charged with failing to meet guidelines set under BRGF scheme

The Union Panchayati Raj Ministry has refused to release the grant money to the Gujarat government for undertaking

developmental activities in the backward districts of the state. For, the government has failed to meet certain guidelines set by the ministry to avail funds under its Backward Regions Grant Fund (BRGF) scheme.

The Union Ministry has refused to release the grant money of over Rs 200 crore for the last two years. This apparently belies the ruling BJP's often-repeated claim that the Modi regime was development oriented.

Under the national-level BRGF scheme, the Panchayati Raj Ministry has earmarked

Rs 506.55 crore for Gujarat to undertake developmental works in five years (2007-2012) for the uplift of the rural poor. The scheme is designed to redress

regional imbalances in development.

Among other guidelines, each of the beneficiary states has been mandated to set up District Planning Committees (DPCs) in the backward districts identified by the Centre to avail funds under the scheme. The Gujarat government has, however, not yet constituted DPCs in the six tribal-dominated districts — Banaskantha, Sabarkantha, Dahod, Panchmahals, Narmada and Dangs — selected by the Centre.

Taking serious note of this "lapse", Chief Minister Narendra Modi convened an emergency meeting of ministers and senior officials immediately after the weekly Cabinet meeting here on Wednesday, where he reportedly directed officials to form DPCs without further delay. Modi also sought to know from them as to why DPCs had not been constituted as mandated under the BRGF's guidelines, sources said.

Gujarat Panchayat Minister Narottam Patel refused to comment on the issue, saying, "I cannot divulge anything that has been discussed at the meeting. Mediapersons should approach government spokesman Jay Narayan Vyas for this."

A senior official who attended the meeting, however, conceded that despite Union Panchayati Raj Minister Mani Shankar Aiyar having written to the state government, the DPCs were yet to be set up in the six districts. "The laxity has forced the Union ministry to block the funds," he said.

The official added that the grant of over Rs 200 crore was earmarked for Gujarat for 2007-08 and 2008-09 under the central-aided programme. But barring an initial one-time release of Rs 60 lakh, the union ministry has refused to provide the remaining grant money, he said.

"We already have district planning boards (DPBs) in all the districts. It is suggested that these DPBs could be converted into DPCs to fulfill the Central guidelines. But we never know if this will be acceptable to the Centre," said an official.

Heading: NFIR bats for ‘son of the soil’ theory - Indian Express
Content:
Team comprising SU Syndicate Members raided and locked four centres in the last two days

The Saurashtra University (SU) swung into action on Tuesday against unauthorised study centres and franchises of various other state universities running in Rajkot without the approval or No Objection Certificate (NOC) of SU. A team consisting of SU Syndicate Members raided four centres in the last two days in Rajkot.

On Tuesday, the study centre of the Institute of Chartered Financial Analysts (ICFAI), situated on Yagnik Road and the National Institute of Management situated on Raiya Road were locked down by the SU team. On Wednesday, the team raided and locked down the National Institute of Fashion Design (NIFD) on Yagnik Road and Bharti Resources Learning Centre on Akshar Marg.

The raids were led by Syndicate Member and SU Law Faculty Dean, Nehal Shukla. Shukla said the team conducted the raids on the directions of SU Vice-Chancellor (V-C) and Pro-Vice Chancellor (PVC). The drive is against those study centres and franchises of various other state varsities which are operating in SU's territory without taking prior permission of the university or the All India Technical Council of Education (AICTE).

Shukla said: "Every year, a large number of students are cheated by these fraud centres which give degrees that hold no academic value. We started a similar drive two years ago, but due to the lack of constant vigil, these centres cropped up again in new areas. We believe that legal police action is the only solution to this problem. We are going to register police complaints against all these centres after collecting all required proofs. At present, we have forced them to lock down their centres and ordered them not to open it again without permission."

When contacted, the branch head of ICFAI, Bhagirath Sisodiya, said their centre is not a franchise, but a Hydrabad-based university's centre. The university offers 'Distant Education Learning' (DEL) courses of MBA and MCA and for that they do not require any separate NOC or AICTE approval.

He said: "We just have our branch-office here and do not require any other NOC from SU as we do not teach students here, but counsel them. We are registered with the UGC and DEL and our name appears on the websites of both these bodies. Besides, these websites have a separate column which mentions the names of fake universities. If, according to SU, we are fraud, our name should be included in the list of fake universities. But that is not the case.

However, SU dismissed the versions of these centres. Kalpak Trivedi, PVC of SU, said: "As per UGC Act, no other recognised or unrecognised university can run its centre in the territory of any other university without NOC or approval. We have been conducting such drives from time to time. For the benefit of students, we give advertisements in newspapers at the beginning of every academic year. In these ads, we tell students not to join any of these fraudulent centres without conducting proper investigation. These centres charge huge fees for courses such as MBA and MCA, but surprisingly their certificates hold no value in the market. We will lodge police complaints against these centres in the next few days. Rajkot police commissioner has assured us that he will take concrete steps against these centres once we provide proper facts and proofs."

The students, however, believe that such drives are conducted once in a few years by the SU authorities, who have failed to keep constant watch on these centres despite several bad experiences. Students said that SU should conduct more awareness drives for them so that they are not misguided by the campaigns carried out by these fraud centers.

Heading: Scholars turn to Gandhian principles to check terrorism - Indian Express
Content:
The National Federation of Indian Railwaymen (NFIR) has advocated for the 'son of the soil' theory in railway recruitments in Group D category.

NFIR general secretary M Raghavaiah has said that filling of Group D vacancies in various railway zones should be solely for local candidates.

Raghavaiah, who is also a staff side leader in the Joint Consultative Machinery (JCM) National Council, said this will avert repeats of Mumbai-like attacks on the candidates. He was in the city ahead of the 28th biennial conference of Western Railway Mazdoor Sangh (WRMS), which began at Rajkot on Wednesday.

He said there is no need to fill the Group D posts on an all-India basis, because it does not require any high-end technical qualifications warranting national level competitive exams.

"Instead, they should authorise zonal general managers and divisional managers to recruit local candidates. The exam should be held simultaneously across the country, so that there is no scope for the candidates taking multiple exams," he said.

This, Raghavaiah said, is possible without violating the right to equal opportunity as enshrined in the Constitution of India.

He said so far, the government would hide behind the Constitutional stipulation to justify all India tests at different places and on different dates.

He was lavish in his praise for Prime Minister Manmohan Singh for prevailing over Finance Minister P Chidambaram on quantum of bonus to the railway employees and in improving provisions of the Sixth Pay Commission.

However, he said there are certain anomalies left in the Commission report and that those anomalies meant gross neglect and injustice to certain categories of railway employees.

These categories included assistant loco pilots (42,000), station masters (72,000), train controllers (3,200), senior section engineers (96,000) and technicians (1,60,000). "From recruitment till retirement, employees in these categories undergo the toil of remaining on foot plate but still not paid in accordance with their performance and productivity," he said.

WRMS general secretary and NFIR office-bearer J G Mahurkar said that such treatment has left them restive and because of that, the NFIR will take up their cause in its forthcoming meets at Rajkot and later at Bhopal, where future course of action would be worked out. He said that over 9,000 employees in these categories have succumbed to mishaps. Not only that, he said, it was unfortunate that even though 80 per cent of technicians were engineering diploma holders, they were kept in Group D.

Heading: Praful Thakar joins BJP with 150 Congmen - Indian Express
Content:
Day-I of the 83rd session of Indian Philosophical Congress at Gujarat Vidyapeeth

The need for emulating Gandhian principles amid concerns on growing violence and acts of terror dominated the first day of the 83rd session of the Indian Philosophical Congress (IPC) at Gujarat Vidyapeeth here on Wednesday.

In the inaugural session, Gujarat Vidyapeeth Chancellor Sudarshan Iyengar pointed out that while the growth of consumerism is eating into the fabric of social ethics, "the social values are also greatly threatened by the rising greed of individuals, which is one of the basic causes of conflicts".

Dr Iyengar inter-related the principles of anasakti (non-attachment) as explained in the Gita with the Gandhian ideology. He said the values like satya (truth), ahimsa (non-violence), brahmacharya (celibacy) can still provide a healing touch to the ailing humanity.

IPC general president Prof I N Sinha, in his address, stressed on the importance of ethics and values in countering the problems of terrorism and corruption. He also emphasised on the fact that the process of inculcating ethical values has to be initiated at the individual level and only then can it effectively reflect as a social way of life.

Sessions were divided into five broad categories, including history of philosophy, logic and scientific methods, metaphysics and epistemology, ethics and social philosophy and religion. Papers were presented on subjects as diverse as carvaka and materialism to memory consolidation research in cognitive neuroscience, to Kundalini Yoga and Hasya Yoga to more contemporary subjects like ethical scepticism.

Reflecting social concerns, philosophers also discussed subjects such as untouchability and corruption. M Prasada Rao ICPR/ JRF Research Scholar, Department of Philosophy and Religious Studies, Andhra University, Visakhapatnam, elaborated how the present caste system in India is different from the Varna System of ancient India. Bindu K L, Research Scholar Department of Philosophy, Karyavattom Campus, Thiruvanathapuram, outlined how the term Dalit, which basically stands for the poor or oppressed, has come to signify socio-economic exploitation of a certain section cutting across religious lines across South Asia.

The concluding session of the day had a colloquium on Gandhi and Peace. Panellists maintained that Gandhi and his experiments still remain valid at the backdrop of growing social conflicts and unrest.

"While human beings as a biological existence have myriad conflicts inherent in them, can a law of non-violence be an answer to man's problems?" asked Professor R C Pradhan from University of Hyderabad.

"Gandhi, unlike the cynics viewed history as victory of non-violence and truth, when others saw onslaught of violence in pages of history," Pradhan said. "It is this optimism of Gandhi, which still keeps him relevant in the modern time of growing conflicts," he added.

"While there have been tremendous developments in all spheres of humanity over the years, conflicts and violence have, however, continued to grow exponentially," observed Prof Manjulika Ghosh. "To address the crisis, one has to resort to ahimsa as talked about by Mahatma Gandhi, who turned the concept from a means of personal salvation to a tool of conflict resolution at the socio-economic sphere," she added.

Heading: State moots proposal to set up eight new medical colleges - Indian Express
Content:
Says the move is to protest autocratic and arrogant conduct of GPCC leaders

In A major blow to the Congress ahead of the next general elections, its city unit's general secretary Dr Praful Thakar on Wednesday joined the Bharatiya Janata Party along with 150 office-bearers in protest against alleged neglect and injustice to them.

They joined the saffron party at a public meeting in Modasa in the presence of BJP state president Purshottam Rupala and NRI C K Patel who was expelled from the Congress a day ago.

Thakar, who had lost one eye several years ago during a Congress demonstration, said he was pained at the neglect of the good work he and his colleagues had done so far for the party.

"Six vice-presidents, 17 secretaries, 19 general secretaries, 21 Mahila Congress office-bearers and a number of youth wing leaders have quit the Congress to cross over to the BJP," he said.

Incidentally, his wife Dr Krishna Thakar, who is a Congress councillor from Saijpur-Bogha ward, had been removed from the post of Ahmedabad City Mahila Congress. "We will discuss about Krishna Thakar, Deepak Makwana and Dr Ganpat Parmar once they are suspended from the party," he said.

Thakar said the Congress was eager to take action against his wife, but looked the other way when a party MP worked for the defeat of C K Patel, the official Congress candidate for Himmatnagar Assembly constituency in 2007.

He quoted Patel as saying in Modasa that the Congress was threatening to take action against indiscipline in the party, but at the same time, appointed those seniors on the core committee who themselves were facing charges of gross indiscipline during the last assembly election.

According to Thakar, those who joined the BJP include Raviraj Thakur, Satish Kanjharia, Bijalbhai Bharvad, KamleshTahiliani, Shobhana Kadam, Artiben Parihar, Anjana Christian and Dr Jitendra Joshi among others.

"We have faxed our resignation letters to the AICC president in protest against the autocratic and arrogance conduct of GPCC leaders," Thakar said when asked if they had resigned from the Congress before joining the BJP. City Congress president Pankaj Shah said he was unaware of the development.

Heading: Surat company develops aid for hearing impairment - Indian Express
Content:
In its bid to meet the ever increasing demand for medical education in Gujarat, the government has mooted a proposal to set up eight new medical colleges across the state. It will send the proposal to the Centre after Diwali.

State Health Minister Jay Narayan Vyas told reporters here on Tuesday that the proposal, which will be forwarded to the Union Health Ministry, has envisaged 1,200 seats in eight colleges.

Over a month ago, the government had sent a similar proposal to the Union Health Ministry seeking its approval for setting up another five medical colleges in the state — two in Ahmedabad and one each in Bhuj, Patan and Bhavnagar — with 750 seats.

The Centre has already forwarded this proposal to the Medical Council of India (MCI) for its consideration.

Vyas said an MCI team was expected to visit Gujarat shortly to explore the possibility of setting up five colleges in response to the proposal. If the Centre accepts both the proposals, the number of medical seats in Gujarat will swell to 3,450.

At present, there are 1,500 seats in 11 medical colleges — seven being run by the government and four self-financed — in the state.

Sources in the Health Department said the government has set a target of increasing medical seats to 4,500 in the next four years.

"We have plans to augment seats for not only MBBS courses, but also for post-graduate courses in medical colleges across the state," a senior official said.

Heading: Chain-snatchers make hay as policemen shift blame on women - Indian Express
Content:
After a research and development of seven years, Surat-based Auxin Life Science company has come up with Titanium middle ear prosthesis. Till now, this product was imported from different companies in South America and Germany.

Auxin Life Science is the first Asian company to develop the titanium middle ear prosthesis. The company has got the patent certificate from the Government of India. Auxin managing director Jai Diwan said their product is priced at Rs 5,000, which is Rs 7,000 less than the imported ones.

"Hearing impairment has become a matter of concern in India. As per statistics, 10 per cent of the total population suffer from this. Among the newborns, three per cent suffer from this disorder due to several reasons. And, over 60 per cent cases can be attributed to the disorders in the middle ear," he said.

He further said the company has distributed the product to the government hospitals in Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Delhi and Mumbai for those who had experienced hearing disorders due bomb blasts.

"The factory is at present set up in Roorkee. We have trained the ear specialists in all major cities across the country and explained to them the procedure to be followed during its implantation," Diwan said.

Heading: Indian team not allowed to meet fishermen in Pak jail - Indian Express
Content:
As many as eight incidents of chain-snatching were reported in Umra and Rander areas in Surat on Monday. But the police immediately put all the blame on women saying that they should not venture into lonely areas.

In a city that has 40 lakh popul-ation, eight incidents of chain-snatching in a day is nothing strange, said police officials.

The first incident took place at 10.30 am in the City Light area when Savitri Lipa was on her way to vegetable market in the nearby area. Two youths on a motorcycle snatched her gold chain and escaped. Two similar incidents occurred in the neigbhouring Bhatar area.

Separate incidents of chain-snatching also occurred in different areas of Rander. The victims — Pushma Gandhi, Champa Patel, Lalita Jain and Nirmala Mistry — lodged their complaint with the Rander police station.

In the City Light area, a woman lost her mobile phone and some cash from her car dashboard, when a motorcycle slowed down near her car and its pillion rider quickly picked up the booty. The two sped away before she got time to react.

Ironically, Additional Police Commissioner Range II Vikas Sahay has claimed that they have increased police patrolling in areas where such incidents take place regularly.

Blaming women for such incidents, Rander police inspector R H Hadiya said they should defend themselves and shout for help. They must also contact on the police toll-free number for help, so that miscreants are caught immediately.

Heading: Babus prepare for week-long ‘mini vacation’ - Indian Express
Content:
A seven-member delegation from the country that had gone to Pakistan to seek the release of 434 fishermen in custody, has decided to return after the authorities there refused them permission to meet the fishermen, a delegation member said on Thursday.

"Despite making clear our intention of the visit to seek the release of 434 fishermen and 379 seized boats from Pakistani custody, we have not been granted permission to meet them since the day we arrived on October 12," said Indian Fishermen Association president Veljibhai Masani from Karachi.

Masani alleged that although he had sought the Union Ministry's intervention in the matter six days ago, the Centre had not acted.

The delegation comprising State government official and several fishermen had been granted a 15-day visa to visit Karachi and Islamabad.

Heading: ‘Professional engagements’ force ASE head to quit - Indian Express
Content:
Offices in the New and Old Secretariat complexes in Gandhinagar will wear a deserted look with the ministers and babus appearing all set to enjoy a "mini vacation" of over a week during Diwali.

As per the government holiday list, there are four declared holidays in a row beginning from October 28 for the government employees. While Diwali is on October 28, there will be holidays on the Hindu New Year day on October 29 and Bhai Bij the next day. There will be yet another holiday on October 31 being Sardar Vallabhbhai's birth anniversary.

Though Diwali is on October 28 (Tuesday), most of the government employees have decided to leave on October 27 (Monday) — the working day — to have two more off days on October 25 (the fourth Saturday) and October 26 (Sunday). Thus, there will be a virtual "mini vacation" from October 25.

"Only those sachivalaya employees staying in Gandhinagar or Ahmedabad may prefer to report to duty on October 27, the working day. But, those hailing from distant parts of the State would certainly claim a CL that day so as to enjoy a week-long vacation and Diwali festivities with their relatives in their native places," said a senior office-bearer of the Gujarat State Employees' Federation. The federation leader, however, told Newsline on Monday that though government employees were entitled to take CL, the administrative bosses of certain key departments in the Sachivalaya may ask them to report on duty on the working day (October 27).

A senior official in the general administration department says the government usually declares a holiday even on a working day under the Negotiable Instruments Act, if that day intervenes a coupe of officially declared holidays. But, in view of prolonged holidays due to the Diwali festivities this month end, the government will not allow this facility to its employees, he said.

Besides, preparations being underway for the coming Vibrant Gujarat Global Investors' Summit may compel the babus in certain key departments such as Industries, Urban Development, Revenue, Finance and Science and Technology to work in their respective offices even during the Diwali break, said a senior Industries official.

Heading: Huge crowd at ICL surprises one and all - Indian Express
Content:
Ahmedabad Stock Exchange (ASE) chairman Mukesh M Patel has resigned from his post citing "pressing professional engagements" as the reason. Patel, a noted tax consultant, submitted his resignation letter to the ASE governing board on Tuesday.

Patel, who has completed one year as chairman, said he could have continued for another one year, but due to his professional engagements, he was unable to

devote the required time to the ASE.

"My one year at the ASE was good enough and during that time, I had no differences with any one. On the contrary, colleagues at the ASE are pressing me to continue and the board of directors had not yet accepted the resignation," he said.

Asked if he would not like to get a chance to further enhance ASE progress under his leadership, former GCCI president Patel said he would love to, but his professional commitments would not allow him that.

The ASE had former bureaucrat P K Ghosh as its chairman before Patel joined. In a recent board meeting, Patel had expressed his unwillingness to continue as chairman.

ASE executive director K K Mishra said Patel's tenure marked good tidings at the bourse. Mishra said it was also a matter of prestige for the ASE to have Patel at the helm at a time when it was in dire need of a competent and committed person.

Now that the Securities and Exchange Board of India has relaxed restrictions on investment on bourses, things at the ASE should improve for better.

Heading: Hanuman langur menace forces RIL to turn to Mumbai-based experts - Indian Express
Content:
The 30,000-odd cricket fans, who gathered at the Sardar Patel Stadium at Navrangpura in Ahmedabad to watch the 20-20 matches of Indian Cricket League (ICL) Season 2, surprised one and all.

Amazed to see such a huge audience for the match between the Ahmedabad Rockets and the Lahore Badshahs on October 19, Executive Board Member of ICL Kiran More, said: "We are happy to see that the players as well as the crowd are enjoying it. Everyone can clearly see the efforts that has been put for the tournament".

Speaking to mediapersons, he said that the huge crowd shows the increasing popularity of ICL in the country.

The stadium management expressed satisfaction that the Rs 10 crore spent to upgrade the stadium, which includes Rs 4 crore for floodlights, had not gone waste.

"I have never seen so many foreign cricketers playing together in the city in my entire life. The ICL is attracting lots of youngsters to the city," said Dinesh Shah, a spectator.

Another spectator Rohit Patel said: "I would feel deprived each time I watched the Indian Premier League (IPL) on television, as such matches never took place in Ahmedabad. But now, I can enjoy watching the ICL matches".

Heading: GSRTC employees hold dharna over leave encashment issue - Indian Express
Content:
Three wildlife experts invited after Vadodara Social Forestry Department fails to deal with the problem

After the Vadodara Social Forestry Department failed to offer its expertise in tackling the 200-strong army of Hanuman Langurs (Semnopithecus Antilus) at the Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) petrochemical complex in the city, RIL has turned to three wildlife experts from Mumbai to solve the problem.

On September 18, Newsline had carried a report which said that the RIL authorities had written to Vadodara Social Forestry officials, demanding action against the simian menace.

They had explained how the langurs might damage the elevated pipelines, which carry highly explosive sensitive petrochemical products like benzene and acrylonitrile. This, they said, could lead to a major mishap.

Nayan Desai, Deputy Conservator of Forest (DDF), Social Forestry, Vadodara Circle, said: "We do not have enough staff to tackle the issue. However, we have permitted the Mumbai-based wildlife experts to release the Hanuman Langurs in Jambhughoda Sanctuary. Social forestry's foresters and beat guards will accompany the wildlife experts when the langurs will be released."

Dwelling in the 1,263-acre RIL petrochemical complex, Hanuman Langurs had sent RIL safety officials into a tizzy after attacking a few RIL employees.

R K Desai, RIL Safety department head, said: "RIL invited three Mumbai-based wildlife experts four days ago to tackle the menace."

Heading: VMC cracks down on sweet shops to check adulteration - Indian Express
Content:
Over 1,000 employees of the Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation (GSRTC), Vadodara division, staged a dharna at GSRTC head office on Wednesday after its authorities failed to encash working employees' leave since 2005.

Later, they submitted a memorandum to the GSRTC authorities, which will be forwarded to Corporation's Managing Director G R Aloria. It is not only the Vadodara division, employees in other districts are also facing the problem.

Manoj Joshi, general secretary, Indian National Trade Union Congress (INTUC) and GSRTC employees union, told Newsline: "A tribunal case on leave encashment issue was going in Ahmedabad from 2003. While the GSRTC agreed to encash leave of retired employees, it has refused to do so in case of working employees."

The leave encashment of retired employees has a ceiling of Rs 10,000. If it exceeds, the payment will not be made, said Joshi, adding that discrepancies in furnishing payments of medical allowances have also been observed.

Heading: City-based company bags water pump contract worth Rs 541 crore - Indian Express
Content:
With Diwali round the corner, the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) has launched a drive to inspect sweets and confectionary shops and ensure that there is no case of adulteration in food items.

Food inspectors in all the zones of the city are in their last leg of sample collection, which would be followed by sample inspection. At least 49 samples have been collected from the suspected areas. "Food inspections were planned soon after Dusshera when preparations for Diwali started. We had roped in our food inspectors in all the four zones of the city," said C M Makwana, deputy commissioner VMC.

The inspection is aimed at detecting the quality of the sweets, mukhwas (mouth fresheners) and other food items. "We have noted that the quality of food colours used in the sweets are ISI marked. But with untrained people at work, the quantity of food colour used is much above the prescribed limit as per the food guidelines," said G R Gohil, public analyst, Public Health Laboratory.

As per the analysts, 10-15 per cent of the sweets and other food items are below the quality criteria during festivals. "Since sweets mark the major amount of consumption during festive season, we are inspecting both the raw material (khoya) as well as the final product (sweets)," said Gohil. Close tab is being kept not just on the food colour used but also on the silver foils, quality of sugar, milk and other ingredients used.

"This time, we are not just targeting small shops, but also the big shops. Strict action will be taken against offenders," said Makwana.

VMC had earlier undertaken the food inspection drive in May to take action against the heavy usage of artificial colours in mango pulp sold across the city.

Heading: Chandrayaan-1: Modi congratulates SAC scientists - Indian Express
Content:
City-based Jyoti Limited has bagged a contract worth Rs 541 crore from Karnataka Neeravari Nigam Limited (KNNL) for 28 pumps, which the company says is the largest ever contract for pumps bagged by an Indian company.

The pumping stations will cater to farmers in northern and eastern Karnataka with a catchment area of about 1,07,000 hectares.

Jyoti Limited's chairman Rahul Amin said that 90 per cent of the pumps would be manufactured in the city by various vendors. "KNNL officials said they want to follow the Gujarat model of irrigation. We faced stiff competition from the Kirloskar group, but because of the technical know-how we bagged the contract," said Amin.

The Upper Bhadra Lift Irrigation (UBLI) project under the KNNL would pump water from Bhadra reservoir to two separate reservoirs in northern Karnataka, 35 kms from the original spot.

"The water will reach the tanks and the small towns in the catchment area, often marred by droughts during the dry season," said Amin, adding they would install pumps for the package I and II of the UBLI project.

The 28 pumps, each as big as modern-day apartment, would be indigenously manufactured except for some of the ball bearings, which would be imported.

Heading: New traffic signal to ease traffic movement on R C Dutt Road - Indian Express
Content:
The launch termed a major milestone in Indian space programme

Chief Minister Narendra Modi visited the Space Applications Centre (SAC) here on Wednesday and congratulated scientists for the successful launch of the country's first lunar mission — Chandrayaan-1.

Mentioning Gujarat's contribution to the Indian space programmes right from Vikram Sarabhai's era, Modi said, "The benefits of India's space programme for the common man are immense, especially the data recorded by remote sensing. The catch identification for fishermen is a classic example."

SAC associate director Ram Rattan termed the launch as a major milestone in the Indian space programme. He said that each of the four-stage propulsion system of the spacecraft was perfectly ignited.

Gujarat Governor Naval Kishore Sharma and Gujarat Pradesh Congress Committee also congratulated the scientists at SAC for their continuous dedication, commitment and zeal in ensuring Chandrayaan-1's success.

Heading: Lahkar packs a punch above his weight - Indian Express
Content:
Considered one of the most important roads in the city, the R C Dutt Road connecting two business zones, Sayajigunj and Alkapuri, has got a new traffic signal to ease the traffic in the area.

Vadodara Joint Commissioner of Police Pravin Sinha said, "The signal would be working soon which will streamline the traffic." The signal will also cater to the pedestrians crossing the road.

However, on Wednesday, commuters faced difficulty as the crossing before the Alkapuri Police Chowki stalled many vehicles wanting to move across the road.

"If I have to go to my bank, which is across the road in the Concord building, I will have to go all the way to the Ambedkar statue, wait for at least 15 minutes for the traffic to clear, and then take a u-turn. Why would someone who is coming from Sayajigunj would take a detour of three kms to get to the other side of the road?" asked Vinay Parikh, a businessman from Sayajigunj stranded on the R C Dutt Road.

Heading: Shades of NBA in college league - Indian Express
Content:
Trinayan Lahkar's fondest memories at the Pramod Mahajan Memorial Badminton Tournament are those of 2006 when he lifted the u-13 title. Since then and as a grown-up, he's been twirling in and around mediocrity, keeping to a spot within the top five in the u-16.

On Wednesday though, at the AIIMS badminton arena, Trinayan added another high to his inconsistent career, rising for once above his age as he thrashed Akash Narang 21-13, 21-11 in the first round of the u-19 category.

Narang is a u-19 regular who missed all the tricks that Trinayan had in his kitty — gameplan of exploiting his opponent's weakness at the net with a deep service followed by a drop shot, attacking his forehand and making him cover the court. "I kept attacking his forehand. Besides, I kept on making him move a lot," Trinayan said.

As the scoreline suggested, he didn't sweat a lot while Akash Narang's wet face had more pains than just losing to a junior player. "It's not about losing to a u-16 player. It's not like that at all. My hands weren't moving fluently and I was also feeling a bit stiff while covering the court. Physically, I wasn't prepared for the game. And the u-16 players are doing well in the senior categories too," Narang summed up, pointing to Bhaskar Chakravarty who skipped the regular u-16 category in this tournament after winning the u-19 Delhi state open at Punjabi Bagh.

Malvinder Dhillon, vice president of the Delhi Badminton Association, portrays a different picture of the boy. "The first quality that you would notice in him (Trinayan) is the way he conducts himself. He is one of the best-behaved of the current lot. As a player he is very brainy. The only thing he lacks is fitness and that's why the inconsistency. If he gains a bit on the fitness front, he will match the top players in quality too," said Dhillon.

Unlike Bhaskar, Trinayan isn't dying to chew the tougher nut as yet, but he wouldn't mind the crest of the upset at the AIIMS badminton courts on Wednesday.

Other results (Boys first round)

U-10: Harsh Gupta bt Anmol Khosla 22-20, 20-17, Dhurov Rishi bt. Jayant Srivastava 20-22, 21-16, 21-12, Abhay Thakur bt. Suraj Negi 21-14, 21-18, Malhar bt Govind Mutreja 18-21, 21-12, 21-16. U-13: Arinjay Bist bt. Dipanshu Bisht 21-16, 21-14, Vineet Pathania bt. Anmol Khosla 21-10, 21-19, Robin bt. Raghav Bansal 21-17, 18-21, 21-13, Shivam Luthara bt Ankit Mahajan (22-20, 20-18). U-16: Shikhar Aggarwal bt Amanpreet Singh 21-17, 21-13, Shivam Tyagi bt. Karan Singh 19-21, 21-12, 21-09, Sumit Choudhary bt Shaleen Thakur 22-20, 21-10. U-19: Surender Rathi bt. Yesh Nain 21-19, 24-22, Abhishek Ahlawat bt Lalit Kumar 21-13, 21-9, Amanpreet Singh bt. Shiv Dhawan 21-15, 21-17.

Heading: Ratnika in quarters - Indian Express
Content:
Ever since the Basketball Federation of India (BFI) stitched a patnership with NBA last year, the federation is bent on introducing some of the latter's formats into its game plans. With the professional League lurking around the corner, the BFI has already begun its College Basketball League by adopting some of NBA programmes.

In the ongoing College League, the BFI has introduced a format whereby the teams play against each other in their respective groups before making the grade into super league. This seems to be paying rich dividends as the students are relishing the idea of playing more games than in a knockout situation.

The super league gets underway from Thursday at the Jesus and Mary College with top two teams from each group having qualified. The finals will be held at St Stephen's College.

In the last league match played on Wednesday in the boys' section, Hindu College defeated St Stephen's 54-49 in a seesaw battle. With the pendulum of fortune swinging from one extreme to another by the minute, Hindu sealed the fate of St Stepehn's in the last four minutes to emerge winners.

In the girls' group, St Stephen's, Gargi, Lady Shri Ram and Jesus and Mary Colleges have all qualified while in the boys' section SRCC, Hansraj, Zakir Husein and Ramjas Colleges made it to the super league.

Added attraction to this year's format are dunking competition among the boys and three- point shooting competition among the girls, besides a competition in free-throws for both boys and girls. Another novelty is the half-court game for the spectators.

Side by side, the BFI has also imparting lessons to players on avoidable injuries and sports psychology besides a coaching session for those interested. The league began on October 17 with 224 players participating in it.

Heading: TANDOORI KNIGHTS - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi wild card Ratnika Batra continued to march ahead in the women's National tennis championship on Wednesday, upsetting fourth seed Anushree Thamanna from Karnataka 6-0, 6-3 at the DLTA Complex to enter the quarter-finals.

Batra broke Thamanna in the second game itself and never allowed her opponent to settle down. The match saw Batra reeling repeated forehands to which her higher-ranked opponent had no answer.

With every game, Thamanna became more erratic and her usually reliable serve let her down with six double faults in the second set.

In another match, Tamil Nadu's P Sindhu Nila beat Mokshada Jain 6-2, 6-0. Once again, the winner took control of the match right in the second game then broke her thrice to take the set.

In the other second round matches, qualifier Sowjamya Bavishetti beat Likitha Shetty 6-0, 6-1, while top seed Shalini Sahoo defeated qualifier Arantxa Andrady 6-0, 6-1.

Results (singles): Sowjanya Bavishetti bt Likitha Shetty 6-0, 6-1; Ratnika Batra beat Anushree Thamanna 6-0, 6-3; P Sindhu Nila bt Mokshada Jain 6-2, 6-0, Shalini Sahoo beat Arantxa Andrady 6-0, 6-1.

Heading: Comic Capers - Indian Express
Content:
Radisson re-opens The Great Kabab Factory, giving kebabs and curries a modern twist

For the last three years, the Radisson Hotel has been virtually inaccessible, being right in the midst of construction of the Delhi-Gurgaon Highway. No wonder then, this hotel had fallen off the map for foodies. However, now that one can zip through the perfect highway road and the wedding and partying season is in tow, Radisson reopens The Great Kabab Factory, at just the right time. The popular restaurant chain that began its 8-year stint with Radisson was shut for almost a year and has now come back with an interesting new menu, giving the mundane tikkas and kebabs a contemporary twist. Also, a new wine list is on offer with pairing suggestions.

"The menu had become predictable and we felt it was time for a change," says Master Chef Meraj-ul Haque. Apart from their signature diner, the hotel will soon re-launch their coffee shop New York Café and even the rooms have now been dressed in smart colours and sleek furniture.

At The Great Kabab Factory, it took over six months for Haque to come up with 450 recipes of kebabs that will take turns to be listed on the daily set menu at the restaurant. Going with their popular format, six vegetarian and non-vegetarian kebabs are on offer everyday along with a portion of biryani and curry for the main course. "A lot of people prefer vegetarian meals and it is important to look beyond paneer-tikka and tandoori-aloo fare. I've tried to conjure a feast with vegetables available in the market," adds Haque. For instance, Haque — who comes from the legendary Qureshi family and holds fort in Mughlai cooking — has a wonderful new recipe for the vegetable galauti kebab. "I am using a combination of yam, bottle gourd and raw bananas to spin off a vegetable version of mutton galauti," he says. The ingredients might not sound appetising but the result on the table is divine. A must try for the vegetarians, the galauti breaks the monotony of the insipid paneer tikka. There are also options of corn and spinach seekh and a sumptuous matter tikki, that Haque has penned in the menu.

Haque's experiments do not end with the galautis. For his other recipes he has brought in ingredients like asparagus, which is converted into a delicious tikki with a bright green, soft texture. He is also experimenting with balsamic vinegar, wine sauce and fruit marinades to bring out a variety of textures and flavours in the kebabs. "We have a lot of expats coming to this restaurant. It was important to introduce some international ingredients which they can identify with," he says.

The menu also ventures beyond the common dal-makhni fare and Haque has stirred some refreshing lentil recipes with Benarasi panchmel dal, Hyderabadi dalcha and Lucknowi dum ki dal. Hopefully, this will just bring Radisson's old patrons hurrying back.

Heading: Pretty in Pink - Indian Express
Content:
Most menswear designers want to keep it simple; so what's a fashion hack to do?

Show of the day
Moroccan-inspired weaves with bursts of cool mints, liquid azures and flaming oranges set apart Vineet Bahl's collection. It would be unfair to label him just consistent for his clothes get more beautiful with each show. Indulge your calves and knees in his dresses and stay cool in his feather-light georgettes. Let's hope summer's here soon enough.

Celeb of the day
The presence of some glittering faces in the front row for Dev R Nil's show added some glitter into the otherwise slow-paced proceedings. There was Shatrughan Sinha, Poonam Sinha, Arbaaz Khan, Rohit Roy and Kiron Juneja who came to cheer the sweet Sonakshi who sashayed down the ramp. But the applause was the loudest from a back bencher, a certain Jackie Shroff (in the picture), who was the showstopper of the day, literally. Posing for photographs, joking around, talking in typical Bambaiyya Hindi and whistling for Sonakshi, Jaggu Dada was in a cheery mood. Indeed.

Trend of the day
Single-button jackets were probably the biggest sellout on the Menswear Day at LFW. They look utterly urbane, sophisticated and best suited for the hot season. From single-breasted cotton jackets presented by Zubair Kirmani to stylish printed bomber jackets and embroidered jackets by Dev R Nil, sequined denim jacket by Tarun Tahiliani and formal blazers by Troy Costa, these single-button jackets will definitely cool your torso on a mercilessly hot afternoon.

Goss of the day
It was a blink-and-miss appearance by ex-Australian skipper Steve Waugh. Seated in between Sabyasachi and Ravi Krishnan, nobody saw him enter or leave the venue. What happened to the forever intruding Indian paparazzi?

Ensemble of the day
Trust Narendra Kumar to breathe life into the dull; his menswear line had all the makings of a trendy toy-boy. A black silk jacket with flat sequins on it was teamed with cotton skinny pants—all the rage in the west—and a brown chiffon shirt. We like.

Heading: Day after Rahul comment, Stephen’s says college encourages questioning - Indian Express
Content:
Elizabeth Hurley will unfurl pink for a cause

Elizabeth Hurley, who is the spokes-model for Estée Lauder and The Estée Lauder Companies' Breast Cancer Awareness Campaign, is scheduled to be in Mumbai today for the campaign's Global Landmarks Illumination Initiative, where a historic landmark is symbolically covered in pink lights. This year the Taj Palace Hotel & Tower will be illuminated by Hurley in a pink glow. The event will also travel to London where the Tower of London will be covered in the same pink tones.

Fashion magazine L'Officiel's October issue also features the lissome Hurley on the cover. Sporting clothes from Dior's Autumn-Winter and Cruise collections, Hurley can be seen in various hues of pink and purple in support of Breast Cancer Awareness Month. The cover was shot in London, with well-known New York-based photographer and filmmaker Daniela Federici.

Says L'Officiel's fashion coordinator Ami Patel: "These colours are hugely fashionable." The lovely Hurley has been given an ultra glam look because, as Patel says, "Big hair and smoky eyes are big this season."

Heading: Asked for cop verification, help attacks housewife with hammer - Indian Express
Content:
A day after Rahul Gandhi said that St Stephen's College in the Capital did not encourage its students to ask questions in classrooms, the college, its teachers, students and alumni questioned the veracity of the comment.

Most students — both present and former — and teachers said on Wednesday that Stephen's has had a history of prodding its pupils to be involved in classroom by asking more questions.

The comment led the usually quiet Vijay Tankha, a faculty in the Department of Philosophy and Dean (Academics), to take a dig at the AICC general secretary. He said the Amethi MP might have asked too many questions in the wrong class. "A history class is quite crowded, so he may have been asked to bring his questions to the tutorial or talk to the teacher after class instead of asking them during the lecture.

"We should probably check to see how many tutorials he attended in his brief stint in college."

Rahul was a student of History at St Stephen's College for less than a year.

Adnan Nayeem Azmi, a student and president of the college student's union, said, "I have never been stopped from asking questions." But Adnan, and a few other teachers, added that the Lok Sabha MP's personal views "could have their own validity".

Mani Shankar Aiyar, Union minister and a St Stephen's alumnus, said he graduated from the college in 1961 and then spent the next three years, till 1963, at Cambridge University. For him, the years at St Stephen's were "far more intellectually stimulating than Cambridge — this is not just because of the teachers but also due to my peers".

But Aiyar added that there is a "huge generation gap between my and Rahul's time" at the college. "From my experience, I had a very easy relationship with our teachers; the teachers were also our mentors and we used to hold long debates and discussions with them."

Nandita Narain, Head of the Department, Mathematics, said Rahul was making a general point about higher education in India and not much should be read into the statement.

"It is my opinion, and that of the students I know, that at St Stephen's we always encourage questions and answers. But people have their own individual experiences, which have their own validity.

"What is important is that participation in class has to reach institutes outside our own."

Commenting on the state of higher education in India, Rahul Gandhi, in an interaction with students at HN Bahuguna Garhwal University in Srinagar (Uttarakhand) had said on Tuesday, "We don't ask people (students) to ask questions. When I was in St Stephen's College, asking question was not (perceived to be) good in our class."

Heading: Copter flies over Parliament, pilot ‘grounded’ - Indian Express
Content:
The middle-aged wife of a businessman was cruelly beaten up at her home last Saturday by a recently-appointed help with a hammer, the police have said.

The minor was angry the family had asked him to complete formalities for a police verification, an officer said.

The victim Begum Jahan was home in Lajpat Nagar on October 18 when she was attacked by the help who the family had hired early last week. Luckily, Jahan's husband Mohammed Azeem and son Muddasar came back on time to prevent any grievous injury.

Police sources said the help had been hired at the recommendation of a vehicle driver known to Azeem. Muddasar had asked the help to produce a photograph for the verification on October 17, but he had been reluctant to do so.

Next morning, soon after Azeem and his son left for their family business, the boy pulled out a hammer from a room and began to beat up Jahan, the police said.

Fortunately, the husband hurried back because he had forgotten something — and walked onto the scene.

A senior police officer said Jahan might have lost her life if the blows had continued. The police was called in immediately and she was rushed to the Moolchand Hospital with head injuries. She was discharged on Wednesday and is out of danger.

The investigating officer said the boy was stopped from escaping by neighbours. He is from Kamrup district in Assam and is now at the Prayag Observation Home. A case of attempt to murder has been registered against him.

Azeem runs a business of supplying meat and other non-vegetarian food to the Army. In his statement to the police, Azeem said the help had been hunting for a job

for long before the family hired him.

Heading: Noida BPO man, kin held for foeticide, wife’s death - Indian Express
Content:
A helicopter violated the no-fly zone code and flew over the high-security Parliament area for over 10 seconds on Wednesday afternoon, sending Parliament security and Civil Aviation officials into a tizzy.

According to airport and Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) officials, the helicopter pilot reportedly had to land at Safdarjung Airport and instead strayed over the Parliament and its annexe. The reason for this lapse, whether a miscommunication between the Air Traffic Controller (ATC) and pilot or the pilot voluntarily entering the no-fly zone, is not yet known. The DGCA has ordered an inquiry into the incident. Officials said a reprimand is likely to be issued to the pilot.

According to officials, a Pawan Hans helicopter entered the no-fly zone around 2.15 pm. Officials said the helicopter was on a scheduled flight from Dehradun to Delhi. The DGCA was informed about the lapse, as was the ATC.

"The Pawan Hans helicopter did fly into the no-fly zone and the DGCA is investigating the matter," a Ministry of Civil Aviation spokesperson said.

A senior DGCA official said: "We have grounded the pilot and a team has been formed to inquire into the matter. It will be immature to say anything at this point of time." Air space over Parliament, Rashtrapati Bhavan, North and South Block, PM's residence, the Taj Mahal, Maurya Sheraton and Taj Palace hotels is a restricted area.

Earlier violations


* A small plane violated airspace over the Prime Minister's official residence. The scare was caused by Punjab Chief Minister Amarinder Singh's aircraft steering off course, just before landing at Safdarjung. DGCA suspended the licenses of the two pilots.
* Last year, a Lufthansa cargo plane flew over the Prime Minister's residence. The pilot of the aircraft was banned permanently from flying in India.

Heading: Face music for unwanted calls, HC tells ICICI - Indian Express
Content:
A call centre employee from Noida was arrested on Wednesday for forcibly aborting his wife's female foetus and for further harassment that finally led to her death yesterday.

Besides Prem Singh, a resident of Noida's Sector-15, his mother Govindi Devi, father Dugar Singh and sister Bhagwati Devi have also been arrested for allegedly harassing Nirmala Devi to a "limit where she succumbed to their torture and died," Sector-20 police station SHO Vijay Singh said.

According to an FIR lodged by the victim's brother, Surender Singh, the family had been harassing her for long for a male child and forced her to undergo an ultrasound test to detect the sex of the three-month-old foetus recently. Prem Singh has two daughters, and after coming to know that the next child would also be a girl the family beat her up and forced her to abort it, the FIR registered at Sector-20 police station says.

The victim's brother, a Faridabad resident, said in his complaint that Prem Singh and his family also continuously pestered and often beat her up for dowry ever since their wedding, in 2003.

The police have lodged a complaint under various sections relating to dowry, murder and for pressuring a woman to kill her female foetus.

Accused Prem Singh told Newsline that his wife did not want a third child and had "forced" him to take her to a clinic for abortion. "We didn't force her to abort," he said, adding that she underwent abortion at a Noida hospital on Tuesday after several hospitals and clinics refused to do it since the foetus was at an advanced stage. Post-abortion, he said, doctors gave their go-ahead to take Nirmala home. She never regained consciousness, he added.

Heading: Seal deal: civic body messenger to SC’s de-seal order - Indian Express
Content:
Unsolicited telemarketing calls trouble everyone — even judges. During a hearing on Wednesday, a senior judge of Delhi High Court gave vent to his ire on ICICI Bank for making "unsolicited marketing calls" to him.

"I receive calls at all time of the day from ICICI Bank," Justice Vikramjit Sen said. "I do not know what business you get out of such calls.... You are a nuisance and have to face the music for making these unsolicited calls."

The division bench was hearing an application moved by ICICI Bank for a stay on revival of contempt of court proceedings before the Delhi State Consumer Commission on the basis of a petition by advocate Nivedita Sharma. Sharma had filed her appeal in response to the "menace of unsolicited commercial telemarketing calls" and divulging "private and confidential information".

On December 26, 2006 the consumer commission had levied a Rs 12.5-lakh penalty on the bank for making nuisance calls. Though the High Court subsequently stayed the Commission's decision on September 11, 2007, the court had warned the bank against making "unsolicited marketing calls".

The court had also warned the bank that the stay order should not be misinterpreted as "a licence to continue making unsolicited calls to customers". The High Court had also given customers liberty to move the consumer commission if they continued to receive unwanted marketing calls from ICICI Bank.

"I moved the Commission because I still got calls from the bank despite registering with the 'Do Not Call' registry," Sharma told Newsline. "The calls were in clear violation of the consumer commission's order."

The bank contended before the High Court bench today that Sharma was merely misusing the "liberty granted to her by the court" to seek relief with the consumer commission if still pestered by unsolicited calls. Terming her current litigation before the Commission as "misconceived", the bank argued that it was impossible for Sharma to receive any unsolicited call as her name had been "updated" on the 'Do Not Call' registry.

At this point Justice Sen sought to prove the bank wrong by citing his personal example. "Do you think you are above the law?" the judge asked. "Who is your highest ranking officer in northern India... bring him here; let him explain these calls."

The bench then kept aside the case for a while to give the counsel time to summon the concerned bank official. Later, the court gave some reprieve to the bank to file a suitable response by the next date of hearing.

Heading: Hauz Khas a dip in Delhi's past - Indian Express
Content:
MCD off the block to take off seals

More than 3,000 traders can take a sigh of relief as the MCD has issued an order to its zonal office to immediately start de-sealing of commercial units on roads notified in Masterplan 2021, following a Supreme Court order.

Commercial units on 1,500 notified roads, and on roads more than 20 meters wide, can now apply for de-sealing.

The traders have to submit an affidavit at the MCD office and get their premises de-sealed. The relief comes after the MCD had moved an application to inform the apex court that the monitoring committee was not carrying out any de-sealing.

"The court passed its order in August but the monitoring committee refused to follow it," MCD Standing Committee chairman Vijendar Gupta said. As a result, the civic body had to move an application again; "the court has now issued an order to de-seal the properties on notified roads".

MCD Leader of the House Subhash Arya said, "If need be we will set up camps and deploy additional staff to begin de-sealing of properties without further delay."

Blaming the monitoring committee for the inordinate delay, Gupta explained the "long process" of files moving from one table to the next: "We had approached the committee to deal directly with the Deputy Commissioners. But they want files to come from Town Hall. After their approval, the committee sends them back to Town Hall — from there, the files go to the zonal office."

The civic body is hopeful that all 3,000 sealed units would be operational within a month.

Meenu Bhatia
The 60-year-old's 'Yellow Bottle Café' in Old Rajinder Nagar market was sealed in March. Despite repeated affidavits, which release MCD from all claims of equity and paying her convergence charges, it remains sealed. "Now that the Supreme Court has told MCD that our premises can be de-sealed, I really hope they permit us to reopen before Diwali."

Vipin malhotra
Four months after Malhotra, 57, bought his small grocery shop in Old Rajinder Nagar market, it was sealed. The stress has been telling: he recently underwent a bypass surgery. "I am functioning from a makeshift structure for the last eight months because my shop is sealed." And that costs: he pays a monthly challan "between Rs 1,000 and 2,000" to MCD.

LALIT BHAWAN PATNI
At 72, Patni saw his stationery shop sealed this March. It's been a run since then — from pillar to post. "I am just fed up now. I can't afford to run around so much at this age; I just hope MCD has the decency to follow the Supreme Court's order." Patni says many traders in the market have been unable to pay their children's school fees since the sealings.

Heading: RAIL TRAIL - Indian Express
Content:
Students of Vidya Niketan School, Saket, take part in the heritage walk at the ruins in Hauz Khas conducted by The Indian Express in association with INTACH and ASI

A Schools' initiative from The Express Group
Quest is a project conducted by The Indian Express in schools in and around Delhi. It covers more than 50 schools in Delhi and NCR.

Quest aims at stirring awareness and opinions. Today, when all that children see are shopping malls and cineplexes, we at The Indian Express want to show a completely different picture of this city to them. Delhi has changed beyond nostalgia and recognition since Independence. How many of these kids know of the 'Seven Cities' of Delhi or the stories of the pigeon fliers of Old Delhi? The idea behind such an activity is to create awareness about the various structures and monuments that the students do not know about. This is a specially designed programme, which will help the students appreciate the rich culture and background of this city. In association with INTACH and ASI, this is a small effort on our behalf to depict a phase of our national life and the decay of a whole culture, a particular mode of thought and living. The visit is followed by the students sending in articles, pictures, poems, paintings, and collages to express their experiences about the heritage walk.

Irreplaceable monument
Madrasa e Hauz Khas is a beautiful example of Islamic architecture, built by Alauddin Khalji. I was greatly fascinated by the domes, arches, and the slightly inclined walls among other featutres. I was impressed by the Islamic calligraphy, flower and leaf carvings on the walls; and rock paintings. The corridors, jharokhas, tombs etc here have been beautifully built. The two-storied classrooms and restrooms, where the shishayas used to stay fascinated me a lot. I also noticed that some 'messages' etc were written on the walls. It should be realised that these monuments can't be replicated. They are very precious and we should preserve them.
— Anchal saini, XII

The heritage walk
I was pleased by the huge entrance and the greenery around Hauz Khas. It was once a madrasa, and is a beautiful piece of architecture, built by Allauddin Khalji. There is a huge and beautiful tank besides the building. The building itself was constructed around the 13th Century. In spite of its beauty, not many people come here. The whole monument is deserted.
— Prashant Singh, XII

Reliving the past
We saw a beautiful lake and different monuments during our heritage walk to Hauz Khas. We also saw different structures made of different geometric shapes. We got to know that in the late 13th Century, the rulers of Delhi had high walls constructed all around the city to protect it from attacks from Central Asia. Later on, they had a huge reservoir built within the boundaries of the city, which was a very important source of clean water.

We saw the madrasa complex and were also shown the assembly halls and the rooms of students and teachers. Then we came upon the graves of Firoz Shah Tughlaq and some others. The carvings on the graves and the tomb were really very beautiful and remarkable. We were told that there is not much documentation available about these monuments. I was totally engrossed and the walk really felt like I was reliving the past of my city.
— Manish Gupta, Xii

Away from bustle
An early morning, a walk in a cool and calm garden, away from the hustle and bustle of the city, strolling amid the remains of beautiful monuments; each depicting a different story — what can be better than a heritage walk?

I was fortunate enough to be a part of one such walk. A group of class XI and XII students were taken for a heritage walk to see and observe the architectural wonders of the Hauz Khas area, developed by the ruler of the Khalji dynasty, Allauddin Khalji, in 13th Century AD. The word hauz means a huge water tank and the word khas means "important". Apart from the water tank, we saw the ruins of a madrasa. The monuments are engraved with beautiful calligraphy; verses from the Quran are engraved on the walls of the madrasa.

I also saw some graffiti drawn on the walls of the monument, which is really sad, as some people are unable to cherish the importance of these monuments. They must think twice before they deface a monument like this.
— ANINDITA DAS, Teacher

Calm and peaceful
The Hauz Khas Madrasa area is very calm and peaceful. Our walk started from the water tank. Our guide explained to us the meaning of the words Hauz Khas. Hauz means water tank and khas means "important". The monument got its name from the tank. It was built between 1296 and 1316 AD. The tank was meant for the city of Siri. It was later covered with silt for use in cultivation. The madrasa was a residential school and its structure is very beautiful. The stone used in this structure, Quartzite, was different from those used to build other structures of that period. In those days, it was commonly found in the city of Delhi. Sandstone was also used for decorative purposes.

One notable feature was that it had slanting walls and even the windows projected outside the building. We also saw many secret paths. After that we moved on to Firoz Shah Tughlaq's grave. The tomb has beautiful calligraphy on the walls unlike Hindu temples or monuments, which represent nature. It is prohibited in Islam to represent living beings. Calligraphy was very dominant in those days. The pleasant walk made me realise that Delhi has a long and eventful history, which is reflected in its ruins and monuments.
— Radhika Gupta, Xii

We invite schools to be a part of this Express Group initiative. For queries mail to heritagewalks@expressindia.com

Heading: Noida police arrest five from Mumbai in internet hacking case - Indian Express
Content:
Nilgiri Mountain Railway: A Century and counting
Although the Nilgiri Mountain Railway completes hundred years in October 2008, a railway line to Ooty (Udagamandalam) was first proposed in 1854. Due to the challenges posed by the steep mountainous terrain that lay in between, work only started in full earnest in 1891. When built, the 46-km long metre gauge line connected the town of Mettupalayam in the plains with the hill station of Ooty in the Nilgiris, in the process ascending almost two thousand metres. Apart from climbing to great heights through some spectacular scenery, the Nilgiri Railway is unique and is the only railway in India to feature rack and pinion operation. Between Kallar (the first station out of Mettupalayam) and Coonoor, the average gradient on the line is 1 in 24.5 (one foot rise every 24.5 feet forward) with a maximum of 1 in 12. The Alternate Biting System or ABT entails a special toothed-rack rail mounted on the sleepers between the running rails. The train is fitted with cog wheels that mesh with the rack rail.The operation involves a locomotive pushing the train rather than pulling it up the steep incline. As a result, the best seats in the house are to be found in the first class coach up front. 208 curves, 16 tunnels and 250 bridges ensure that one is glued to the window at all times. The section between Coonoor and Ooty is no less beautiful, only less severe in terms of incline and hence, the rack system does not exist there. Today, diesel locomotives operate this section of the line but the rack and pinion portion is still used for the 'X' class steam locomotives, some dating back to 1914, all built at the Swiss Locomotive Works, Winterthur. The Nilgiri Railway was made famous through cinema first in 1984 with David Lean's A Passage to India and more recently in 1998 in the movie Dil Se, where a complete song (Chaiyya Chaiyya) was shot on the train. In 2005, UNESCO awarded the railway World Heritage status. The National Rail Museum in New Delhi has, among its vast collection, two exhibits from the Nilgiri Mountain Railway — a vintage third class carriage and an X class steam locomotive.
— Bharat vohra, Rail enthusiast

Lord Dalhousie and the introduction of Railways in India
Imperialist, expansionist, the epitome of British rule in India. These are perhaps the most apt adjectives for Lord Dalhousie, appointed Governor General of India in 1848. In his eight years at the helm, James Andrew Broun-Ramsay, 1st Marquess of Dalhousie, better known as Lord Dalhousie, was all that and more. He expanded Britain's empire in India by fair means and foul and held total sway over the vast realm. He was known for his overbearing self-confidence, centralising activity and reckless annexations.

However, history has also attributed far-reaching reforms to Dalhousie. Among his major reforms were those in the fields of education, public works, post and telegraph. Above all, he will always be remembered for introducing the railways in India. It was during his tenure as Governor General that on April 16, 1853, at 3.35pm, the first train in India left Bombay for Thane. Trains were started the next year in the Calcutta area and work began on the Madras-Arcot line in the South. Lord Dalhousie's famous Railway Minute of April 20, 1853 laid down the policy that private enterprise would be allowed to build railways in India but that their operation would be closely supervised by the government. He was also responsible for introducing the 5' 6" gauge for railways in India and the initial lines all used this gauge. Lord Dalhousie favoured 6' and 5'-6' was the compromise agreed to. It was only after the departure of Lord Dalhousie that other gauges were also introduced in the country.
— J L Singh, retired railway official

Did you know?
* Dapoorie viaduct is India's first railway bridge
* The Naini bridge on river Yamuna near Allahabad was opened for traffic on August 15, 1865
* The only steel arch railway bridge in India is the Reond bridge near Kangra
* The longest railway bridge at the time of Independence, with a total length of 10,052 feet, was Upper Sone bridge. It was opened by Lord Elgin in 1863
* The Rajghat Narora bridge is the oldest bridge on the Ganga
* The first bridge on the Brahmapurta is Saraighat bridge
* Northern Railway has the largest number of bridges
— Vikas Singh, rail enthusiast

Heading: JNU poll panel gets notice on Lyngdoh guidelines, varsity says spirit intact - Indian Express
Content:
NOIDA police claimed to have cracked the case involving an internet hacker gang siphoning off Rs 1.66 crore from the account of an international electronic automotive goods supplier firm.

The people accused of being involved in the alleged internet hacking racket are all graduates — one of them, who had transferred the withdrawn money in his account is a civil engineer and an MBA.

The five arrested by the police are Mitul Trivedi, resident of Pune, Savio

Derochlobo, resident of Goa, Bharatbhai Patel, Uday Kapadia and Yogi Anjani Bhandari, all residents of Mumbai.

Police said the money transfer chain was broken after interrogating persons in Goa and Mumbai. "There are dozens of people who have received the money transferred from the account of P K Aggarwal. We have yet to trace the mastermind. The team sent to Mumbai will hopefully be able to crack the case soon," said R K Chaturvedi, SSP, Gautam Budh Nagar.

On October 11, P K Aggarwal had lodged a complaint saying Rs 1.66 crore had been siphoned off his bank account. The first transaction took place on September 29, in which Rs 21.5 lakh was transferred to a Mumbai branch of the Punjab National Bank. The second transaction took place on October 1, in which Rs 81 lakh was siphoned off.

The Noida police have tracked down a long chain of money transfer to various local bank accounts in Goa, Mumbai and Mysore after they were alerted of a certain transaction to a bank account in Goa.

"The police were alerted of the fact that on October 2, Rs 80 lakh was transferred from the account of one Savio Derochlobo, resident of Panjim, Goa, who owns a firm called Panjim Asiatic State Development, to an ICICI Mumbai branch account. The money was then distributed among four, who have also been arrested. Savio had incurred a loan of Rs 5 crore and was in dire need of money," said Chaturvedi.

He also added that Rs 12.47 lakh have been recovered, apart from Rs 20 lakh that has been recovered from the bank account of N Venkatesh of Goa, after the police was informed of the money transferred in his account. "A total of Rs 52 lakh has been recovered and has been transferred back to the account of P K Aggarwal," said Chaturvedi.

According to circle officer Rajiv K Mishra, a team of the Noida police is investigating the accounts in Mumbai. "We will trace the complete chain and the mastermind involved in the crime soon," said Mishra.

Heading: Reprieve for airline that served beef to vegetarian couple - Indian Express
Content:
A day into campaigning for the JNU student union elections slated for November 3, On Tuesday, the Supreme Court sent a notice on Tuesday to the Election Commission (EC) of JNU asking for elaboration on the guidelines governing its elections.

JNU follows its own constitution while conducting elections and this year the Lyngdoh Committee guidelines were not being followed, the reason for which the notice was sent. The hearing of the case will be held on Thursday.

Sarada Prasanna Das, Chairperson of the Election Commission told Newsline that details on whether they would be asked to implement Lyngdoh Committee recommendations for their elections will only be clear after the hearing. "The letter does not specify any Lyngdoh guidelines violation, but has called for details of the elections held for the last three years," he said.

This year, the code of conduct of the JNUSU elections clash with the Lyngdoh Committee guidelines on three grounds — age limit set at 25, a qualifying criteria of 75 per cent attendance and allowing candidates to contest for the same post again. A few days before the Supreme Court sent the notice, Sandeep Singh, president of JNUSU had told Newsline that with most students being research students, maintaining an age limit of 25 was impossible in JNU.

The JNU Election Commission held a meeting on Wednesday with representatives of all student bodies. Sources said an answer to the apex court notice is being drafted. "We will file a reply to the court that meeting technicalities do not matter, as long as the spirit of the guidelines—to ensure a free and fair election is being followed. And JNU is already doing that," he said.

On its part, the JNU administration says that though they have no direct involvement with the election process of the university, they have been sending letters to JNUSU telling them to comply with the Lyngdoh Committee guidelines. Recto II R Kumar told Newsline, "Elections have become a legal matter now. We hope the EC will be able to convince the court, otherwise they might have to start the process all over again."

Incidentally, Lyngdoh Committee guidelines had openly been flouted during the Delhi University Student Union elections despite being accepted on paper. However, no such notice was sent to DU.

Heading: Apex court throws out Vikas plea, says Katara case to be heard in Delhi - Indian Express
Content:
If you are a vegetarian, make sure you fill in your meal preference request with utmost care the next time you book an air ticket. For, in case the airlines serve you non-vegetarian food, you cannot drag them to a consumer court and ask for a hefty compensation for "hurting religious sentiments".

According to the Delhi Consumer Commission, an instance of "deficiency in service" is different from deliberately "hurting the religious sentiments" of customers. Hence, if there was confusion regarding the nature of the meal, an airliner cannot be held responsible if a vegetarian ends up eating non-vegetarian fare.

This observation by Justice J D Kapoor has come as reprieve to Japan Airlines, which had earlier been asked to pay Rs 55,000 as compensation to G L Aggarwal and his wife Raj Rani Aggarwal for serving beef to them on their flight to San Francisco in September 2004.

Aggarwal, a resident of Palam Colony, had booked the tickets through a travel agent, requesting the option of Asian vegetarian meal or fare for diabetics be served to him and his wife. However, when dinner was served to them on board the flight, Aggarwal found that the food tasted unusual. Upon enquiry, he realised he and his wife had been served beef.

When the matter was brought to the notice of the airline staff, they failed to replace the food, saying vegetarian meals were over.

An irate Aggarwal lodged a formal complaint with the consumer forum, which slapped a compensation of Rs 55,000 on Japan Airlines. The carrier then approached the commission and argued the available computer records pointed out that the travel agent had not specified any meal preference.

Later, the complainant had simply requested for the meal option for diabetics, which, as served by the airlines, comprised non-vegetarian ingredients as well for their high-protein content.

The commission found favour with the airline's argument. "In our view, a deficiency in service is different from hurting religious feelings. Religious feelings are hurt with malicious intention. Negligence in serving non-vegetarian instead of vegetarian meals, particularly when the perception of diabetic and vegetarian meals differs among international airlines, can not be regarded as hurting religious sentiments," said Justice Kapoor. The commission then lowered the damages to Rs 10,000 for deficiency in service to be paid to the complainant.

Heading: HC seeks police response in plea against remand of blast suspects - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday underlined that any appeal in the Nitish Katara murder case would be heard only in Delhi and no where else.

Issuing a directive to this effect, the Bench, comprising Justices Dalveer Bhandari and H S Bedi dismissed Vikas Yadav's plea for transferring the proceedings of the case to a High Court outside Delhi.

Vikas, son of D P Yadav, was sentenced to life imprisonment in the Katara murder case on May 28 this year. Arguing for Yadav, senior advocate Ashok Desai submitted that his appeal proceedings against the sentence passed by a Sessions Court in Delhi would be vitiated if conducted in the Delhi High Court in view of the adverse publicity his client has received in the case.

He urged that the appeal proceedings be held either in the Allahabad High Court, or any other HC in the country except the Delhi High Court. Desai submitted that technically and legally the appeal should be heard only in the Allahabad High Court, as the original offence was committed under its jurisdiction on February 17, 2002. The counsel argued that the transfer of the trial to Delhi did not extinguish the accused's right to file an appeal in the Allahabad High Court.

The argument, however, failed to evoke a favourable response from the Bench, which finally dismissed the counsel's petition after hearing the argument for two hours.

Following an application from Neelam Katara, mother of Nitish Katara, the apex court had transferred the trial from the Sessions Court in Ghaziabad to Delhi in 2002.

Heading: Trust announces awards for young talent in arts, media - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi High Court on Wednesday sought a response from the police on a plea by the family of suspected militants, allegedly involved in the September 13 blasts, seeking to quash a trial court order extending their police remand till October 27.

Advocate Prashant Bhushan, appearing for the family members of the accused, said an accused can be detained for a maximum period of 15 days but the lower court erred by extending their police custody beyond that. Justice Kailash Gambhir issued a notice to the Centre and the police and posted the hearing for October 30. The petitioner challenged the trail court's order of October 16, through which the five suspected terrorists were remanded to another 12 days' police custody. "The investigating agency is required to collect evidence and find out the truth of different dimension in the matter. Keeping in view the dynamics of the case and factual matrix, police custody remand is absolutely necessary," Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Sanjeev Jain had said while passing the order.

Heading: Not good enough for squad of 16, but a perfect fit into the XI - Indian Express
Content:
Either the selectors are not doing their job properly, or it's just that they don't count at all at the Delhi & Districts Cricket Association (DDCA). Continuing with the trend of mysterious and questionable selection procedures, the Delhi under-19 team fielded a player in the XI who wasn't even part of the original squad.
