Delhi team management, "acting under instructions from the DDCA", drafted in left-arm spinner Darshan Kumar for the first match against Punjab in Patiala on Wednesday, at the expense of Varun Sood, who was originally in the squad and was available for the game. Incidentally, Darshan wasn't even in the team bus when the under-19 boys traveled to Patiala on October 19, and arrived at the ground on the match day.

Chairman of the Delhi under-19 selection committee Sanjeev Sharma washed his hands of the incident. "Well his name was not there on the team list that we (committee) had picked," Sharma told Sportline over the phone from Chandigarh. As an afterthought, and trying to defend the DDCA, Sharma did add that coach Mahesh Bhatti and Junior state coach Tarik Sinha could call up players, if needed. "It's not our job to select the playing eleven. It's in hands of the manger and the coach to call up players, if any emergencies arise. In this case, I think, Varun Sood didn't take the field, so they played Darshan — it's a like-for-like replacement," he added. But this 'like for like replacement' theory doesn't hold any water because there are no injury worries to the team and Delhi were playing their first league match since their selection. Adding more intrigue to the arbitrary call-up, Sharma admitted that "Darshan bowled well. He only went for 17 runs in his eight overs"

Darshan's figures can't stand as an alibi to the sequences of events leading to his selection, but as it unfolds further, it's classic case of selectors goofing up big time.

Heading: Sacred Heart bags second prize in quiz contest - Indian Express
Content:
Hosts Chandigarh Hockey Academy, a venture of the Chandigarh Administration scored an authentic 3-1 verdict against Punjab and Sind Bank, Jalandhar in the final of the first Administrator's Challenge Cup Hockey Tournament for Under-17 boys' at the Sector 42 Hockey Stadium on Thursday.

Playing before the home crowd, the Chandigarh Hockey Academy boys played an inspired game. The highlight of the well-deserved victory for the hosts was a three-in-a-row feat by speedy Gagandeep Singh.

Egged on by the trainees of the football, hockey and cricket academies run by the Chandigarh Administration, the fast moving Chandigarh Hockey Academy boys made a whirlwind start as they struck in the very first minute through Gagandeep, who was later shown green card in the 34th minute. Hardly had the cheers of the home crowd had died down, the Chandigarh Hockey Academy struck again in the eighth minute through Gagandeep who scored another field goal.

Maintaining their relentless pressure, the hosts forced their first penalty corner in the 12th minute. The dashing Gagandeep, wearing jersy number 10, converted the penalty corner to complete his three-in-a-row feat.

The Punjab and Sind Bank tried their best and started asserting themselves. In a counter move the bank men were able to reduce the margin by converting a penalty corner in the 46th minute when Gagandeep Singh rolled the ball in after capitalising on the rebound off the Chandigarh Hockey Academy goalkeeper Sukhjeet's pads. The bank men forced penalty corners in the 15th, 30th, 46th, 48th and 64th minutes. They could convert only one.

Pradip Mehra, adviser to the Chandigarh Administrator distributed the prizes. The jubilant Chandigarh Hockey Academy boys were presented a glittering trophy and a cheque of Rs 50,000. The Punjab and Sind Bank team received the runners-up trophy and a cash incentive of Rs 25,000.

Heading: Baldeep appointed Malwa College director - Indian Express
Content:
Students of the Sacred Heart Convent Senior Secondary School, Khanna, bagged second prize in the quiz competition, 'Vedanta 08' held at Thapar University, Patiala, on Saturday.

The compition was organised by "Lakshya Institute" Patiala under "Aranya Mega Tech Festival — 2008'. Students of more than 100 schools from Punjab Haryana and Chandigarh participated in the competition.

The school team comprising Neha of 12th calss, Harkirat Singh of 11th class, Neelshiva of matric and Ishaan Batta of ninth class bagged a cash prize of Rs 4,000. The quiz was based on basic IQ, mental ability, aptitude and logical reasoning.

The quiz comprised of three rounds. The first round was selection round which led to selection of four students from each school while the second round was of written test on mental ability and logical reasoning held at Thapar University. Heading: Seminar held on effective teaching of science - Indian Express
Content:
Senior orthopedic surgeon of Guru Teg Bahadur Sahib (C) Hospital here, Dr Jagdip Madaan attended a six-day workshop on fracture fixation by latest techniques and two-day workshop on cadaveric extensile exposure technique organised by Bombay Orthopaedic Society, Bombay, from October 11 to 18. Dr Madaan was one of the seven candidates selected for this course from India.

Detailing about training, Dr Madaan said all the doctors had got a chance to observe and assist latest surgeries in operation theaters equipped with all the latest gadgets at Nanavati Hospital, Hinduja hospital, KEM hospital, Grant Medical College etc.

Internationally-renowned surgeons like Dr Sanjay Aggarwala, chief of Hinduja hospital, Dr Lehari, who is better known as father of spine surgery in India and chief KEM hospital, Dr Harish Shinde of Laud Clinic, Dr Ram Prabhoo, an Dr Hemant Patnakar gave them tips on latest techniques of fracture fixation. It was interesting to see that most of orthopedic surgeons used space suits so that chances of infection were almost nill.

During the course, latest methods of fracture fixation by mini hole techniques, joint replacements by mini holes spine fixation and shoulder fixation were demonstrated.

Best part of course was cadaveric training. All delegates were given cadavers and all latest equipment and were trained to do surgery by different methods. All the delegates were given certificates at the end of the meet.

Heading: Diwali mela organised at KCW - Indian Express
Content:
BCM Arya Model Senior Secondary School Shastri Nagar organised a seminar on effective science teaching on Wednesday. Shiren M. Doshi, principal of Guru Nanak Public School, Delhi, was the resourceperson.

He talked at length about effective teaching of science and making it an interesting subject. Doshi, who has a vast experience of 29 years of teaching science, said, "Teachers should adopt an activity-based guided discovery approach to make the subject more intersting, effective and meaningful. The teachers should also stimulate creative spark in children."

Doshi, who is also author of "Living Science series of books for class VI and VII" made the seminar meaningful with group and individual activities and through power point presentation. Nearly 60 school teachers from various city schools participated in it.

Paramjit Kaur, the school principal, said, "The seminar was mainly based on experience sharing in science education and also to lay emphasis on developing science concepts, science skills and scientific attitude among learners.

Heading: ‘Make people aware of importance of blood donation’ - Indian Express
Content:
Students of Khalsa College for Women, Civil Lines, organised a Diwali mela on Wednesday. The mela depicted the vibrance of this festival.

Decorated stalls dotted the mela which was inaugurated by Dr Ajit Kang, a well-know gynaeologist, who is also the member of the Khalsa Diwan, along with Dr Varinder Thind, principal of the college.

Students sold items like decorative candles, diyas, gift wrappings, paper bags, pained kurtis and oil paintings. Special children from Ek Prayas and Aashirwaad school also exhibited their works at the mela.

Heading: Welfare of special kids  govt’s priority: Upinderjit - Indian Express
Content:
"The main reason why people do not donate blood is because no one has asked them to do so. If you motivate people, they will come forward. Don't hesitate. Tell them that through this noble act, they could potentially save precious lives." These observations were made by Satpal Bansal, a social worker, while delivering a lecture to the participants of an on-going training course for NSS programme officers in the auditorium of Dr M.S. Randhawa library on the PAU campus. He remarked that any healthy individual could donate blood.

Dr K.S. Verma, programme officer of NSS at PAU, said that Bansal was a retired manager of the State Bank of Patiala and was involved in motivating people for blood donation to save human lives. He added that Bansal had donated blood 143 times for which he has been honoured on number of occasions.

Bansal is life member of All India Blood Transfusion Society and has addressed people in hundred of camps organized by NSS, NCC, SGPC and various youth fora, said Dr Verma. An exhibition on the theme of blood donation to save lives was organized in the portico of the library and literature, badges and other motivational material was distributed.

The training course for NSS programme officers is being organised by training and orientation centre (NSS), Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Punjabi University, Patiala. Dr Balwant Singh is the coordinator of Training and Orientation Centre (NSS).

Dr K.S. Verma, the course director, said that the course has four daily sessions wherein experts deliver lectures to the participants on important topics like environment conservation, finances and accounts, animal welfare, community work, project planning, disaster management, landscaping and tree plantation, etc.

He said that the participating NSS programme officers would also be provided training on education system and need of NSS, historical and philosophical aspects of NSS, administrative set-up of NSS and enrolment of volunteers, etc.

Heading: Consumer forum turns the heat on soft drink firm - Indian Express
Content:
"The state government is doing a lot for the special and handicapped children in schools under Sarv Shiksha Abhiyan. We are also planning to help them out in higher studies. For this, we are thinking to tie up with Punjabi University, Patiala", said Dr Upinderjit Kaur, Education Minister, Punjab. She was in the city to attend the concluding day function of the Diamond Jubilee Youth Festival of Punjab University Zone-A at GMT College of Education.

Repeating her old announcement, she said, "Before Diwali, 14,000 posts of teachers will be filled in government schools."

While Heera Singh Gabria, Jail and Tourism Minister, said that through Youth Festival, youngsters get a chance to learn about their rich culture.

In this youth festival, 1,158 students from 17 colleges participated and performed through 43 items. Also present on the occasion were Kashmir Singh Thind, Amarjit Singh Bhatia, Sukhwinderpal Singh Garcha, Baljinder Singh Panesar etc.

Heading: Doctors make a case for higher compensation before pay panel - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Dispute Redressal Forum, while accepting a complaint lodged by N.K. Singla of Kitchlu Nagar here has directed the Ludhiana Beverages Pvt Ltd and Ludhiana Bottling Company, Focal Point, to pay a compensation of Rs 25,000 to the complainant for mental agony and harassment on account of deficiency in services of the company and also pay Rs 2,000 for litigation expenses.

After hearing the arguments of both side, Forum President and its members, D.S.Bakshi and Puja Diwan, held that N.K. Singla had successfully proved his case. The forum held that the company was certainly guilty of misconduct by resorting to unfair trade practice by selling beverage of soft drink, which was unfit for human consumption, as it was past its expiry date.

A crate of bottles was sold after six months of manufacturing and contents were to be used best within six months of the manufacturing. The forum also held that after six months of the manufacturing, that crate of bottles was sold by a big company for the sake of a few rupees risking the health of general public.

Singla, through the complaint, had submitted that he purchased a crate of Maaza soft drink from the Ludhiana Bottling Company, Focal Point, Ludhiana, selling agent of manufacturer Ludhiana Beverages Pvt Ltd, franchise of Coca Cola company vide bill dated March 10, 2007. The crate was purchased from a delivery van of the company. He alleged that when he was on the verge of opening one Maaza bottle, he found some foreign element therein. On close scrutiny, the foreign element appeared to be an insect. Concentrated portion of the drink had settled down while the water portion was on the top. A legal notice also sent to both the parties, which was received by them but they had failed to reply

During the arguments, the lawyer of company stated that the complaint was false and frivolous.They alleged that bottles were bottled by franchise of Coca Cola company with most sophisticated automatic plant ensuring high standard of hygiene and cleanliness with strict quality checks.

Heading: Rhapsody rolls out at Sacred Heart - Indian Express
Content:
The PCMS doctors have apprised the fifth Punjab Pay Commission about resentment among PCMS because of the pay disparity with the central doctors, stagnation in promotions and downgraded administrative status. In a meeting with the commission, the representatives of the PCMS association led by Dr Hardeep Singh, the state president, also discussed the issue of more and more doctors leaving their jobs.

Besides pay disparity, the doctors were frustrated over non-implementations of all the recommendations of previous fourth Punjab Pay Commission, stagnation in service and downgraded administrative status.

The control of all the national health programmes has been shifted to the deputy commissioners, SDM and at state level also, number of posts of bureaucrats have been increased which has curbed the administrative status of PCMS officers, said Dr Hardeep Singh.

The commission was apprised about stagnation in promotions, as 98.6% doctors were retiring on entry designation of service, without any promotion. This injustice was forcing more and more doctors to leave their jobs, he said.

Dr Hardeep Singh said that PCMS doctors were the only category getting less than their counterparts at the Centre, whereas all employees of Punjab were getting either more or equal pay to their counterparts at the Centre. The PCMS Association has demanded 4, 9, 13, 18, 27 year time-scales along with Central parity to the specialists. The PCMSA demanded conveyance allowance to all the doctors a la central pattern and equal to 75 litre petrol every month as recommended by fourth Punjab Pay Commission and compensatory allowance for hiring own driver also. Higher qualification increments to all specialists, risk health allowance, ESI allowance, children education allowance were also demanded.

Heading: MC fails to exploit Bhattian plant - Indian Express
Content:
The four-day annual function of Sacred Heart Convent Senior Secondary School began today with a scintillating performance by primary school kids. "To encourage mass participation, the school held a separate function for each class", said Sister Chantal, the school principal.

The chief guest of the morning function was Dr A.G. Abraham, director of Christian Medical College and Hospital. He was welcomed by a song "Jee aayan nu". While a medley of three languages reflected the children's love for parents and mesmerized them.

An English skit "The star child" depicted as how precious are children. "East rocks the West" was a good fusion of folk and classical dances. "Bacchon ki adalat," a Hindi skit, made parents realise that children observe each and every thing and adopt their parents as role models. Through "Keep fit and healthy," children showed their karate skills. While the foot-tapping Bhangra and Giddha was a befitting salute to the Punjabi culture.

The chief guest congratulated the children, teachers and staff for their efforts and asked the parents not to pressurize children and let them bloom.

He said, "Do not punish children, correct them. And never discriminate with a child if he does anything wrong." While Jose Paul, a resourceperson from Delhi, also urged parents to spend quality time with their wards.

In the evening, the students of class IX presented colourful programme. They invoked Gods' blessings through a prayer dance "Feel his presence" and welcomed Mandeep Singh Rai, chief commissioner, Income Tax.

A play "Dear Departed" symbolized today's scenario of materialism where greed for money has surpassed all family ties and duties. "Haamari Virasat - Dehshat', depicting the threat of terrorism was a dance drama which kept everyone spell bound.

It depicted as to how the youngsters were influenced by this menace, which was posing threat to humanity. The students also performed "Dance for fitness". The colourful costumes and synchronized actions of students with the light-and-sound effects were appreciated by all.

The chief guest said that each child was unique and parents should not indulge in comparisons.

Heading: Draw for cracker stalls postponed, traders cry foul - Indian Express
Content:
* With choked sewer lines in city, sewer treatment plant not receiving full supplies
* MC says it needs Rs 2.25 cr to clean clogged pipes

Though it has been more than a year that the Bhattian sewerage treatment plant (STP) got operational, it is not receiving full supplies of sewer water for treatment. Reason: choked sewer lines in the city.

The Punjab Water Supply and Sewerage Board has asked the Ludhiana Municipal Corporation to intensify the sewer cleaning process in the city. Meanwhile, the MC authorities have categorically stated that it will take them at least a year to clean sewer lines. The MC will have to shell out Rs 2.25 crore for this purpose. Till then, untreated sewer water will continue to pollute the Sutlej river.

Bhattian plant, which has been built with a total capacity to treat 111 million litres of sewer water per day (MLD), got less than 50 per cent of waste water for treatment just a couple of months ago. Even now, the total supply is around 95 per cent.

D S Malhotra, superintending engineer (SE), operation and maintenance cell, Municipal Corporation, said, "A number of sewer lines have been cleared and hence the capacity has increased to 95 per cent. Still a lot more needs to be done. We have floated tenders to clean the main sewer lines in the city. It will take at least a year to clean the lines. It can't be done overnight."

The sewer lines in Focal Point, Transport Nagar and Gill Road are in a bad shape.

The Bhattian plant had been constructed under the Sutlej Action Plan so as to treat MC sewer water before it flows into the river. It took more than a decade to build the project but the MC failed to clean sewer lines in all these years.

Heading: Telecom meeting goes awry, employees protest against general manager - Indian Express
Content:
Shopkeepers allege favouritism by district administration

Every year, the allocation of cracker stalls put up for Diwali is mired in controversy of alleged favouritism. Keeping in the tradition, this festive season is no different. Shopkeepers on the Pakhowal Road and BRS Nagar protested during a lucky draw, which led to the postponement of the event.

When the lucky draw began this morning, the shopkeepers started raising slogans against the district administration for alleged irregularities in the allocation of sites. The shopkeepers alleged that the administration has been continuously favouring the VIPs of the city in allocating the sites.

As soon as General Assistant to Deputy Commissioner J K Jain announced that for the Pakhowal Road and Orient Cinema locality, the shopkeepers gathered at the centre of the hall where the draw was taking place and tore away the slips of the lucky draw.

The traders alleged that the new allottees are the kin of VIPs in the city. For the Pakhowal Road, the district administration had received 291 applications for 20 shops out of which 13 shops have been already allocated while for the Orient Cinema locality, 200 applications were received for 30 sites. Of these, 17 sites have been allocated on a similar pattern.

The shopkeepers led by Youth Congress leader Komal Khanna and Youth BJP leader Sanjay Kapoor staged protest at the venue and demanded the cancellation of the lucky draw.

The cracker sellers are allocated shops in more than half a dozen places across the city including on Pakhowal Road, Tajpur Road, Sector 39, Dugri Phase 1, Sector 39, Rishi Nagar, Model Town Extension and Grain Market.

Heading: Lalu promises CYG train will stay: Kalmadi - Indian Express
Content:
A crucial meeting of Ludhiana General Manager Telecom S K Aggarwal with executive officers of Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited took a dramatic turn today when the officers walked out of his office and started raising slogans against him.

According to sources, "The general manager had called the meeting to discuss the implementation of the guidelines of the Delhi Sanchar Nigam regarding shunting of some security personnel deployed at telephone exchanges in the district. During the course of discussion, the general manager allegedly spoke rudely to a few officers. Following this, the officers walked out of the meeting."

The executive officers continued their protest for more than an hour.

It was around 2:30 pm when the general manager called the representatives for another round of meeting. Jasbir Singh, a Divisional Engineer from Mullanpur, said, "There was some misunderstanding in the previous meeting about a departmental issue. We spoke to the general manager not to lay off security personnel from telephone exchanges. He has agreed to this." There are 350 security personnel deployed at 125 telephone exchanages in the district. According to an officer: "Around Rs 22 lakh per month is spent on giving salaries to the 350 security personnel. The plan is to increase their salaries by 2.5 times in the near future, which will burn a big hole in the pocket of the Delhi Sanchar Nigam. The Delhi Sanchar Nigam wrote letters to all general managers to opt for cost-cutting methods. It was finally decided in the meeting that decreasing the number of security staff will increase chances of theft. The general manager has decided to convey the decision to the Chandigarh circle authorities."

Heading: No sale: Deserted offices tell the real story - Indian Express
Content:
Congress MP Suresh Kalmadi said today that Union Railway Minister Lalu Prasad has assured him the special train introduced for the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG) will become a permanent fixture.

"I spoke to the minister on Tuesday and he gave me an assurance that it will be made permanent. Now, all I have to do is follow it up till it is done," Kalmadi told The Indian Express from New Delhi.

In September, Kalmadi had gone on record to say, "Once the train comes in, I won't allow it to stop. It has been announced in the Union budget for only 12 days but we will ensure that it continues after the Games."

However, as of now, both special trains have been stopped. At present, they are being used as Patna specials to clear the Diwali rush. These are among the special trains that Central Railway introduces during Diwali each year.

During their brief stint as CYG specials, the trains had attracted many commuters. Senior divisional commercial manager Ashok Malhotra said both trains ran to full capacity after an initial lull. "The first two days saw few passengers travelling on these trains. Later the occupancy increased to 75-80 per cent; the last four trips saw full occupancy," Malhotra said.

Both trains left in the afternoon; one was fully air-conditioned and took only about 21 hours against the usual 25-26 hours to reach Delhi - almost like a Rajdhani or a Shatabdi.

Railway commuter forums have been lobbying to make the trains permanent. "We don't have to wait till the railway budget. In the past, several trains have been introduced and routes changed outside the railway budget," said Manik Birla, president of the Rail Travellers Service Agents Association, Pune. He cites several examples.

The Prime Minister had promised during his trip to Pune before the rail budget that the Pune-Delhi CYG train would be a permanent one, Birla added.

At present, trains from Delhi for Pune either run at odd hours or infrequently, or are known for their tardiness (See box).

RUNNING TO DELHI
Daily: Goa Express (arrival 4am, inconvenient); Jhelum Express (departure 5.20 pm, often late)
Weekly: Two, neither from Pune — Mysore-Nizamuddin Swarna Jayanti Express and Kolhapur-Nizamuddin Express
Biweekly: Sampark Kranti, from Yashwantpur (Karnataka) via Pune

Heading: PDS rice deficit: Minister sets week’s deadline - Indian Express
Content:
The district registration office at Sinhagad Road wears a deserted look these days. A year ago it was so crowded during the day that it took three to four hours for a property deal to get registered.

Even the miniscule number of citizens who visited the office had mostly come for the registration of leave-and-licence agreements and not registration of property.

"The registration of new properties is drastically down compared to last year," says A B Panmand, joint sub-registrar.

He is unwilling to put a figure to the drop. "It is well below 50 per cent. We had no breathing space last year as the office used to be crowded and the public had to wait for hours to get the documents of new properties registered," he said.

However, this slump has not made a negative impact on the revenue collection for the government due to increase in valuation charges, Panmand said.

As this comes at a time when city developers are offering a clutch of freebies to those who are willing to sign up new property, the writing is pretty much on the wall. The indirect discounts offered by builders, amounting to 10 per cent of the mark-up price of city apartments, have not brought home the gravy.

The scene is no different at the registration office at Paud Road. In fact, there is not much variation in any of the city's 20 registration offices.

The joint sub-registrar at the Paud Road registration office, V H Kulkarni, said she took charge of the office three months ago and so could not compare the present situation to that of last year. "Registration of properties do take place, but most are for leave and licences," she said.

Real estate agent Major (retd) Mathew Oommen, who focuses on the NIBM-Undri region, said developers are maintaining prices despite the slowdown, but the balloon will soon burst as not many have the sustaining capacity.

"Developers are somehow expecting business in the festive season by offering incentives as a desperate measure to continue the ongoing business. This is unlikely to be taken up by customers and the real-estate industry will have to give up and reduce the prices," he said. Buying of property has almost come to a standstill, he added.

According to Kothrud-based real estate agent Anthony Rajan, developers who used to directly deal with customers are now wooing agents in a bid to get customers. "Despite the incentives being offered by developers, customers are not ready to do business. This means all is not well with the industry," said Rajan. However, the rental business is doing well as an entire category of genuine buyers is keeping away from the property market, he said. M Kankadri of Ashiyana Services said developers are trying hard to sustain the current rates, but it seems they will have to reduce the rates by at least by 15 per cent.

"Developers were earlier unwilling to budge an inch on rates. Now they are open to negotiations. They have pumped in a lot of money in recent projects and hence cannot afford to keep the business stagnant for long," he said.

MAILBOX
IT techies used to buy a lot of properties but have now checked the trend. Some advisory emails in circulation between them tell us why:
* Don't take any loans; buy homes, properties with loans, or even cash
* Pay off as much of personal loans, private loans, as debt collection will be hastened
* If you are selling homes/ properties/ cars, do it now, when you can get good prices; they are going to fall

Heading: Raj’s name runs across police files, city and district - Indian Express
Content:
Tired of complaints of inadequate supply of rice in the state to above poverty line (APL) ration cardholders, food and civil supplies minister Sunil Tatkare has set a deadline to the Maharashtra State Cooperative Marketing Federation on Tuesday asking it to sort out the shortage issue by October 30.

"If they do not, the federation will be blacklisted and will stand to lose the contract with us," Tatkare said.

The city has 8 lakh APL ration card holders and with just over a week to go for Diwali, things are not looking bright as Pune got only 50 per cent supply in August and September.

"We have not received the quota for October at all," said Pradeep Patil, FDO, Pune. He has already written to the government, he said. "Pune needs 4,000 tonnes of rice and the last two months the department has received only 2,000 tonnes. The shortfall continues."

The scheme was launched in June to tackle rising prices of essential commodities for APL consumers. However, three months after issuing a Government Resolution (GR) the state is yet to implement the scheme. The scheme focuses on disbursing 5 kg of rice at Rs 12 per kg, one litre of palm oil for Rs 42 and one kg of tur dal for Rs 30.

A senior official of the Public Distribution System (PDS) said the shortage had occurred because the Andhra Pradesh government that supplies rice to the state faced some shortage. "The issue has not changed since the time the scheme was launched," he said.

The flip side is that against the Rs 42-per-litre APL price, palm oil is available in the open market at Rs 37. "We have enough palm oil supply but it has not been lifted by the 271 ration shops in the city with people not willing to take it at that price," said Patil.

On Monday, Janwadi Mahila Sanghtana representative Kiran Moghe had met divisional commissioner Nitin Kareer. "If the government comes out with a resolution it should adhere to it. What is the use of issuing a GR and there being no stock in the ration shops?" said Moghe.

The government is yet to clear the issue of tur dal for APL cardholders. The minister said that the issue is pending in the High Court and that too will be taken up soon. With the minister laying down October 30 as the deadline for the federation to sort out the issue, APL cardholders will have to look for other options this Diwali.

Heading: City stars dazzle at global Astronomy Olympiad - Indian Express
Content:
The Pune city and rural police have booked MNS chief Raj Thackeray under Section 109 of the IPC on charges of inciting violence in parts of the city and district.

The city police have booked Thackeray and four unidentified persons for setting on fire a Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mandal Limited (PMPML) bus at Kothurd on Tuesday. The rural cops have booked him in 10 violence cases.

Asked about the possibility of Thackeray's arrest, superintendent of rural police Ravindra Kadam said, "We may not arrest him soon; Kalyan court has released him on bail. We have, however, arrested several MNS workers and detained many others as a preventive."

Joint Commissioner of city police Rajendra Sonawane said, "We have booked Raj Thackeray in the Kothrud case and arrested 43 persons for 62 offences in the city." He did not comment on the possibility of Thackeray's arrest.

Meanwhile, sporadic violence continued on Wednesday before Thackeray was released on bail. Seven PMPML buses were pelted with stones and two torched in Pimpri-Chinchwad, said Deepak Pardeshi, PMPML spokesman. The MNS has caused PMPML an estimated loss of Rs 40 lakh . While repairs would cost Rs 15 lakh, the loss of revenue is Rs 25 lakh in the past two days. "We have not yet included the cost of the burnt buses," Pardeshi said. A bus was torched in Bhosari on Wednesday morning.

Many MNS workers of various parts of the city and the district have been told to stay off the district limits for 15 days. The police have passed prohibitory orders on rallies and gatherings of five or more up to 100m from government offices in the city till November 5.

Heading: Hold your nose, you are on highway in PCMC limits - Indian Express
Content:
Six Indian students, four of them from Pune, are on their way home with a rich cache of medals from the International Astronomy Olympiad in Italy, winning between them a gold, four silver and a bronze medals.

Abhishek Oswal of St Mary's School, Sarthak Chandra of Bishop's School and Jayant Thatte of SP College each won a silver at the Olympiad held between October 13 and 20. Anirudh Bapat of Army Public School won the bronze. Of the two students from other cities, Shantanu Agarwal of Patna bagged the lone gold while Nitish Kumar Singh of Mumbai took another silver.

The students' proud parents reached Mumbai international airport on Wednesday to welcome them home. "It was Sarthak's first trip abroad. We have been in touch and it has been a wonderful experience for him, as the competition was nothing like the usual exams in India," said Vandana Chandra.

For Anirudh Bapat, this was a second innings, having already won gold at the previous 2007 Olympiad held in Simeiz, Crimea. He participated in the senior category this time. "Anirudh particularly enjoyed the theory round. He is a little disappointed that he got only a bronze, but it is an achievement nevertheless," said his mother Swatee Bapat.

The National Astronomy Olympiad first screened the top six students from aspirants from all over India, and then sent them to Triste, Italy, for the Astronomy Olympiad. This was one of the six international science Olympiads held annually. Teams from 18 countries participated in the event. at Trieste Observatory of International Centre for Theoretical Physics.

The competition is open to junior high school students in two age groups: 14-15 and 16-17. India sent three students in each category. The team was led by Parag Mahajani, Pune, and Kedar Soni, Abhinav Vidyalaya, Dombivali.

The students participated in three rounds: observational, theoretical and practical. The observational round involves recognition of stars and constellations and estimation of star magnitude and angular distance. The practical round consists of questions based on data results of observation while the theoretical round involves questions on hypothetical situations.

Heading: NTPC to generate 300 MW for state by 2012 - Indian Express
Content:
The Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation, which has spent as many as Rs 300 crore for widening and giving a complete new look to the 13-kilometre stretch of the Pune-Mumbai highway under its jurisdiction, is yet to get its act together when it comes to keeping the highway neat, clean and tidy. If you travel from Nigdi to Pune, the highway comes across as a stinking mess what with overflowing garbage containers, clogged toilet blocks, ubiquitous plastic bags, broken concrete pieces, maze of tiles, mounds of sand a common sight throughout the PCMC limits of the highway.

At the chaotic Nashik Phata chowk, two garbage containers are placed at a blind corner right on the highway proving a major impediment to the speeding traffic and throwing up the possibility of an accident. Scores of officers, employees and corporators of the PCMC pass through this stretch practically everyday, yet none finds it worth complaining to the concerned officials. Similarly at Kundanagar, two garbage containers have been placed on the highway surrounded by mounds of garbage.

At the same Nashik Phata chowk, an open drainage chamber was lying dangerous for more than three months. After Newsline highlighted the point, the PCMC quickly repaired it. But now the concrete broken pieces are lying near the drainage chamber, posing threat to pedestrians. Besides, the chamber has not been aligned to the road surface, thereby creating the possibility of an accident if a speeding two-wheeler rider runs into it. Similarly, the paver blocks near Kasarwadi have sunk tossing the unsuspecting vehicles in the air. "I have seen at least 20 accidents at this spot," says Javed Shaikh, a local shopkeeper.

"PCMC has an office at Kasarwadi where nearly 100 employees and officers could be found, but not one of them is ready to take any initiative," says activist Raju Jawalkar. The situation is no different in Nigdi, Chinchwad, Pimpri and Phugewadi. At Pimpri chowk, a toilet block along the highway is perennially clogged and stinking. "This toilet block is rarely cleaned which makes it unusable for citizens," says D Shetty, a local resident. If you travel from Pune to Nigdi, the highway is in no better shape. At short distances, you will find grime and garbage along the road. On the entire stretch, bus stop sheds have disappeared, making commuters sweat it out in the blazing sun.

But the PCMC administration is unfazed. City engineer Eknath Ugile said the entire highway stretch will be beautified soon. "The paver blocks are temporary. They will be removed and the road surfaced tarred. Plantation of trees will be taken up on a big scale," he said. Municipal Commissioner Asheesh Sharma said his administration was alive to the problems of the highway. "Some work remains to be done on the highway. We are in the process of completing it. I will look into all the problems along the highway," he promised.

Heading: SIMI suspects’ bail plea: Court decision today - Indian Express
Content:
Even as Maharashtra has asked for 800 MW power from the National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC), the latter has agreed to generate 300 MW for the state by the year 2012 at its generating stations at Madhya Pradesh.

An official statement issued here stated that Ajay Bhushan Pandey, Managing Director of Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (Mahavitaran) signed an agreement with S N Goel of NTPC at a function held in Mumbai.

In a welcome move, the management of Mahavitaran, Mahagenco and Mahatransco has decided to give Rs 5000 as ex-gratia to all its employees. This payment will be released before Diwali. Meanwhile the petition of Prayas (energy group) and Sajag Nagrik Manch filed in the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission for indiscriminate increase in loadshedding hours by MSEDCL will be heard on November 4. The hearing willbe held on November 4, an official statement from MERC has been issued to the petititoners who have demanded the MERC direct the Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited to avoid loadshedding in Thane, Navi Mumbai and Pune till the state wide demand supply gap is below 4,500 MW.

Heading: Corporators lament civic body’s lack of care for environment - Indian Express
Content:
Hearing on the bail application of three SIMI suspects from Pune took place in the special court for terrorism cases on Wednesday. The suspects -- Feroz Mehboob Pathan of Ghorpade Peth, Ayaz Khan and Imtiyaz Baba Miyan Sheikh of Bhimpura Camp, -- had moved bail applications at the Pune court. Defence lawyer M M Syed pleaded for their bail. Syed argued that state Anti Terrorism Squad arrested the suspects with possession of Urdu literature, but the investigative agency never specified the content.

The Pune ATS unit had arrested Pathan near a hotel on Shankarsheth Road on August 21 with possession of 40 Urdu book claming that it was Jehadi literature. An Urdu document and four CDs were recovered from Imtiyaz.

The ATS then booked Ayaz Khan in the case. The ATS had arrested Ayaz was earlier arrested in a fake currency racket in Pune. The suspects were booked under unlawful activities prevention act and the complaint was lodged at Thane. "The ATS has not produced any details like the author, the publication or the meaning of the content in these books," said Syed.

"Investigative agencies have levelled allegations that Ayaz Khan and Imtiyaz Sheikh were associated with Pathan. But the way by which they were associated with Pathan is not mentioned," he added. Syed sought bail for the suspects pointing out the discrepancies in investigations.

Assistant public prosecutor S M Jagtap told the court that ATS have verified the content in the Urdu books and CDs recovered from the suspects.

"Books contain Jehadi literature. Pathan was circulating the books among others, creating unrest in the society. The CDs and document seized from Imtiyaz's possession also carries Jehadi content. Ayaz helped them in circulating the Jehadi material. The suspects are associated to Mohammed Bilal Rasool Kagzi, who was arrested in an extortion case by Mumbai police," said Jagtap. "There is sufficient prima-facie evidence against the suspects. It would be dangerous to release the accused on bail," he argued while opposing the bail application. Judge S J Kale would be passing an order in this case on Thursday.

Heading: Coming up, course in embedded systems - Indian Express
Content:
Expressing concern over the deteriorating environment scenario of Pune, majority of the corporators in the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) on Wednesday demanded to stop the farce of publishing Environment Status Report (ESR) every year, if nothing concrete was going to happen to really save the environment. The ESR-2007-08 came for discussion before the general body meeting. The corporators also brought the absence of civic officials and municipal commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi during the meeting.

BJP corporator Anil Shirole said, "The status report on environment is published every year, but there is hardly anything that comes out of it. The civic body hardly cares to implement the suggestions given in it."

He added, "Under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM), the union government has started assisting the cities to help themselves renovate. However, as far as the removal of the slums, there should have been a master plan and a time-bound programme."

Criticising, among other things, the garbage disposal situation in the city, Ujjwal Keskar said, "It has been found that even after segregating the dry and wet garbage in some select localities in the city, this collected garbage again dumped together. It only shows that the civic administration is not serious about the issue."

Avinash Bagwe and Avinash Salve, both of Congress said that despite being an important issue, the topic of environment comes for discussion only for one day in the whole year. "Therefore, this farce of publishing the ESRs should be stopped immediately," they said.

Arvind Shinde said, "The bulging population is the root cause of all the troubles. Therefore, the civic body should initiate steps for controlling the population."

He said, "The environment is also getting affected due to inordinate construction activity in the city. Every year, permission is given for carrying out construction on 8-lakh sq ft of land and most of the builders are violating the construction norms, thereby posing a threat to the environment."

Shankar Kemse said, "The report comes out every year, but there is no basic infrastructure in our wards, which should be provided on a priority basis."

Heading: Diwali bonus for PMPML employees - Indian Express
Content:
The Modern College of Arts, Science and Commerce is starting a three-month evening course in embedded systems. "This is the first course of its kind in Pune, which will give hands on training on ARM processor embedded systems to the students," said Rajendra Zunjarrao, principal of the College. This will be a weekend course that will include lectures, demonstrations and training.

"We shall start issuing the admission forms within a week. However, the date of the course will be decided only after we get at least 10 registrations per batch," Zunjarrao said, adding that the course will be conducted thrice a year. The fees for the course will be Rs 2000 and the certificates, on completion of the course, will be issued by Progressive Education Society (PES). Presently, training in embedded system is mostly given only by the industries, said Prof D B Gaikwad of the Department of Electronic Science. Speaking about the need to have a course on embedded systems for undergraduate and postgraduate students, Dr K S Chari, scientist, Information Technology and Communication Ministry, Government of India said, "By 2015, Indian is expected to import electronic hardware worth Rs 320 billion dollars, of which 80 percent will be embedded systems. This import can be reduced only when the country has its own skilled manpower and experienced faculty." He said that there is a wide scope for career opportunities for embedded system designers and testers as these systems are used in almost every field -telecommunication, health, biotechnology, defence, environment monitoring, agriculture and infrastructure development. Chari was in the college to inaugurate the three-day national workshop on 'Embedded System Development with hands on training, using ARM processor' on Monday. "For instance, voting machines, medical implants, close circuit TV cameras, automobile systems, wildlife monitors, chemical and biological sensors all have an embedded system as its core technology," Chari explained. Other than this course, the college has also applied for a postgraduate research centre in electronics with the University of Pune, which is expected to start within a year. "The importance of this centre is that teachers from Modern College and nearby colleges can come here for research excluding their work hours, which is not always possible while researching in the University of Pune," Zunjarrrao said. The research centre will accommodate up to 16 students, 8 for the PhD degree and 8 forM.Phil degree. The centre is expected to start within a year, he said. This is the sixth research centre in the college after botany, zoology, microbiology, life sciences and commerce.

Heading: ‘Direct flight to Kerala needed’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal Limited (PMPML) has announced Dowali bonus worth Rs 11 crore for its employees.

The 7,000 employees of the erstwhile PMT would be getting Rs 8.17 crore, while the 1,900 erstwhile employees of PCMT would be getting Rs 2.83 crore. This is the first bonus announced by PMPML after its merger, official said. Both PMC and PCMC corporations have contributed to the PMPML's bonus kitty. PMT employees would get 8.33 per cent of their annual income plus an additional Rs 4,260 as bonus while PCMT employees would be getting an 8.33 per cent of their annual income plus Rs 7,000. "We are going to give them the bonus on October 24 and October 25," said Deepak Unnavane, PMPML accounts manager.

Heading: NDA wins KP Jadhav football tournament - Indian Express
Content:
The United Kerala Foundation has demanded starting of a direct flight to one of the cities in Kerala from Pune. The foundation submitted a memorandum in this regard to Air India station manager Dhairyasheel Vandekar on Wednesday.

"There are around five lakh Keralites residing in Pune. There is a lack of convenient travel facilities to Kerala. If someone wants to catch a flight to Kerala, one has to go all the way to Mumbai," said K S Ravi, general secretary of United Kerala Foundation. Most of the Keralites here would prefer to travel by flight, he said.Ravi said flights from Pune should connect destinations such as Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram and Kozhikode. "Other than Keralites, there are also a number of tourists who go to various places in Kerala. " he said. Dhairyasheel Vandekar, station manager, Air India assured the delegation of the foundation that the matter would be taken up with the competent authorities.

"There is scope to start a Kerala flight from Pune. We will try to push the demand as soon as possible," he said.

Heading: T20 cricket  for corporates - Indian Express
Content:
NDA cadets won the final of the KP Jadhav memorial football tournament here on Wednesday, beating the much-fancied Pune FC under-19 team by a solitary goal at the St. Vincent's ground.

The game got off to an exciting start with Pune FC having their first chance to score in the opening move of the game.

The striker found himself one-to-one with the keeper but missed the target altogether.

Soon, at the other end, NDA drew first blood. Pradeep Singh put in a good through ball to Pravesh Thakur whose volley finish delighted the crowd. NDA then exerted a lot of pressure on the opposing goal. Their game was fast paced and they took shot after shot and tried to extend their lead. Pune FC on the other hand were looking to slow the game down by passing the ball around and keeping possession. NDA were a physically superior team and were winning headers with ease.

Pune FC found it tough to deal with their opponents and were looking to keep the score down to 1-0 going into halftime.

The second half saw the professional outfit come out all guns blazing. They played with much more intensity and looked likely to score. In the opening minute, a good cross put in by the left winger resulted in a goalmouth melee, but NDA managed to clear their lines. They then won two consecutive free kicks, both of which narrowly missed the target. Then in the 50th minute, their player tried an acrobatic bicycle kick but could not beat the keeper.

Pune FC huffed and puffed but could not manage to get past the NDA garrison. NDA sat back for most of the half and made their moves on the counter attack. Pradeep Singh nearly sealed the game for his team when he cut past a defender and found himself in on goal but failed to beat the keeper. Then in the last minute of the game, Pune FC almost scored an equaliser when the corner found an open man on the far post. But the player's header sailed over the bar and their hopes were dashed.

Heading: The right strokes - Indian Express
Content:
Corporate cricket is now coming in the most popular form: the Twenty20 variety, which has taken the nation by storm. The Avinash Bhosale Group on Wednesday announced the launch of 'ABIL Corporate Cricket Champions Cup 08', which will have 16 teams from the corporate world battling it out for the ABIL Cup. The championship, with prize money of Rs 5.5 lakh at stake, will kick off at Deccan Gymkhana ground on November 1. The matches will be played on Saturdays and Sundays and the competition will last eight weeks.

Addressing a press conference here, ABIL Group chief executive officer Sudhanshu Purohit said the ABIL championship matches would be played in the T20 (league-cum-knock-out) format, adhering to ICC rules and regulations. Sixteen teams from various sectors like automobiles, IT, manufacturing, telecom, finance and pharmaceuticals will be divided into four groups.

"Each team will play with all the teams in their respective groups, implying at least three games per side, followed by the quarter-finals, semi-finals and finals," said Sudanshu Lele, one of the associates for the championship.

"The championships is all about good, healthy cricket for amateurs," said Lele. Corporate giants such as Bajaj Auto, Cognizant Technologies, Cybage Software, HDFC, HSBC, IBM Corporation, Idea Cellular, Infosys Technologies, Kirloskar Oil Engineers, Mather and Plat, News Makers, Sakaal, Serum Institute, Sujanil Chemicals, Tata Motors and Venkateshwara Hatcheries will be the teams to watch in the championship. The winners and runner up will be awarded a cash prize of Rs one lakh and Rs 75,000 respectively. The best batsman, bowler, fielder and man of the series will bag a cash prize of Rs 25,000 each and a trophy. The man of the match declared for each of the matches played will receive a trophy and a cash prize of Rs 2,000. " Our main objective behind launching ABIL champion is to identify cricketing talent from Pune and encourage them to participate in national and international tournaments," he said. The highlight of the launch was the unveiling of the ABIL championship trophy by ace commentator Harsha Bhogle.

Heading: Animated indeed - Indian Express
Content:
Tamali Dagsupta's uncomplicated yet thought-provoking subject brings out the myriad aspects of feminine introspection

Be it any hour of the day, her mind is always at work thinking of various moods and emotions that can be given a shape on canvas. Little wonder then that Tamali Dasgupta, a Kolkata-based painter, who will be exhibiting in Pune says, "Painting is like a passion for me. The paint brush and art book have been my best friends since childhood." This artist was into landscape painting till recently when she took up figurative art particularly womanhood.

An exhibition of Dasgupta's work has been organised at Omkrishna gallery Anjan Bhattacharya and Sudip Bannerjee are two other well-known painters from Kolkata whose works can be appreciated at the exhibition.

Dasgupta has her own world of paintings. "I consider a painting to be worthy when it creates an interest in human minds. The painting does not need to have some hidden meaning but it should let the audience think," feels Dasgupta. Being a woman of the Internet world, she has a modern approach towards her works. She paints women with modern gadgets like cell phones, headphones and so on in different frames of mind. "I have a free vision.I consider blue a mysterious colour. It has a lot of depth and passion filled in it. I also use a lot of metaphors in my paintings," she shares. Being a Bengali, she considers the different moods that her paintings create as different rasas.

Dasgupta feels that Bengalis and Maharashtrians have a similar approach towards art. "Marathis love theatre and stage plays and art is also much emphasised in Bengal," says the artist who is expecting a good platform for her upcoming exhibition. She feels that her journey has just begun. She will keep on experimenting and believes that creativity should be continued in order to keep herself as well as her audience interested. She uses acrylic paint to transform her imagination into a figure. An active member of International Forum of Art and Culture (INFAC), Dasgupta has attended many workshops and her works have been exhibited at many places including Kolkata, Delhi and Hyderabad. Now it's Pune's turn giving art lovers one more reason to smile this festive season.

(Works of Tamali Dasgupta, Anjan Bhattacharya and Sudip Bannerjee will be exhibited at Omkrishna Gallery on October 28 from 11 am to 6 pm. )

Heading: Fine tunes - Indian Express
Content:
Ameesha Patel feels that while animated characters may not be able to replace real-life actors, their popularity cannot be discounted

While most actors come to inaugurate a place just to add the celeb quotient, Ameesha Patel's presence at SeamEdu, a state-of-the-art education academy that plans to offer courses in animation seemed a little more justified, given her added qualificationsof a high profile educational background and love of animation. "I have a great interest in animation and I happy to be a part of something so educational. I feel someday we are going to have state-of-the-art technology better than Hollywood," says Patel.

The runaway bride of the bridal issue of Verve magazine is very positive about the latest range of animation movies that have caught the directors' eyes in Bollywood. In fact Patel was extremely pleased when a special two-minute animation film featuring her, prepared by experts at SeamEdu was shown to her. "Animation is a great and interesting format. In fact I learnt my Amar Chitra Katha series through its animated version," says Patel. Giving her views on the no- star factor of animated films, the actress strongly opines, "You don't always need a star to make the film work. We don't make the films. It is films that make us." However the actor who enjoys watching animated films and names Bal Ganesh and Bal Hanuman as her favourites, feels that cartoons can never replace real life characters although they may enjoy as much importance.

Patel, who has also tried her hands at Tamil and Telugu films seemed very upbeat about her forthcoming releases, Chatur Singh Two Staar opposite Sanjay Dutt and Run Bhola Run, in which she teams up with Govinda. Talking about Chatur Singh Two Staar, she says, "This film is a laugh riot where I play the lady love of Sanjay Dutt. If Munnabhai MBBS made Sanjay popular as Munnabhai, then this film will make him popular as Chatur Singh." After playing the typical mainstream roles and some cameo roles, the glamorous actress now wants to be a part of historic films and also do negative roles. Ask the Kaho Na Pyaar Hai girl about her Diwali plans and instantly comes the expected reply, "I was so caught up with my shootings that I didn't get any time to plan something special for Diwali. Once I get back to Mumbai may be I'll plan something special."

Expressing the special relationship she has with Pune she adds,"Pune has a very special place in my heart because my grandmother lives here. I love coming to Pune. I have spent many Diwalis and Christmas eves in this city."

Heading: Twist in the tale - Indian Express
Content:
Music will always bind India and Pakistan, says Pakistani singer Shafqat Ali Khan

He feels Sufi music is both enduring and mollifying with the tunes originating from a rich and cultural history, but above all celebrated ghazal singer and son of Ustaad Salamat Ali Khan, Shafqat Ali Khan, feels music is something that goes beyond barriers, cultures and religions. In the city, for a performance, Khan says, "This is the first time I am performing in Pune. It is the home of stalwarts like Pandit Bhimsen Joshi. I am very honoured to perform here."

Khan, who is known for both his ghazals and crossover fusion, says that music is an art and can find its audience in any part of the world. "Music involves emotions and humanity. It is the knot that binds two cultures," feels he. Affirming the like-wise cultural backdrop between the two nations, Khan comments, "I feel, even after partition, music has been a very important element in binding the ties between India and Pakistan, and it will continue to do so."

Talking of doyens like Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, he says, "They were the ambassadors of Sufi music, so their identites should not be distinguished on the basis of their country only. Their compositions are very pure and captivate audiences irrespective of any region and religion."

"Music has been a medium to disseminate a message of humanity and peace. The love for music got respect to my father. I am following in his footsteps," says Khan, adding, "Pakistan has been my motherland and has made me what I am, but I also find a very fine audience here, as India, being a larger and a cultural country has more listeners for the classical genre of music."

With Sufi music getting a lot of acclaim globally and in India, Pakistani singers are getting great opportunities in Indian music industry and in Bollywood. "This is a good change for the musicians and the audience. This will help us get better musicians and good tunes too," he says.

Khan makes it a point to add, "I want to say that terrorism will take us no where. I wish to spread the word of love and peace and I am taking back fond memories of this concert in the city."

Heading: LinkedIn connects with investors for $22.7 mn - Indian Express
Content:
Look chic with bright colours, ruffled dresses and big sleeves this summer

Show of the day
Effortless chic and a burst of yellows and purples made Narendra Kumar's Nari Nari the show that you shouldn't have missed. The outfits were hair-style co-ordinated, and Fashion triplets Priyanka Chopra, Kangana Ranaut and Mugdha Godse set the runway ablaze. The show also had excellent footwear with such beautifully irreverent detailing. Sexy.

Celeb of the day
The surprise entry on Day Two was Kabir Bedi, who looked as hot as a firecracker. He was accompanied by girlfriend Parveen Dusanj and daughter Pooja Bedi. They were there to cheer little Aliya (Pooja's adorable daughter), who walked the ramp for Pallavi Jaipur. Chatting up with each other and posing for the shutterbugs, they looked like one big happy family.

Trend of the day
Voluminous sleeves ruled the roost on the second day. Crab and Dolman sleeves were present in Kallol Dutta's unstructured line. Leg-of-mutton, batwing, bell and longish puff sleeves made a jarring presence in Drashta Sarvaiya, Arjun and Aastha Bahl line. High on style, these sleeves are well on their way to the top of the fashion poll.

Ensemble of the day
Rimzim Dadu may have called her line 'My Village', but her collection was far from rustic. Dadu showcased an amazing mix of woven dresses, draped racer back dresses and ruffles with quilting, pleating and tonal embroidery on smocks in pink, yellow and white — the colours seemed just right for the summer. What we loved the most was a pink-corded dress, an example of fine tailoring.

Goss of the day
Those who say that they love fashion more than their lives are evidently lying. Most of them chose to stay indoors, watching Raj Thakeray on their television sets instead. As far as attendance goes, Day Two wore a desultory look.

Heading: Oil rebounds to near $68 a barrel - Indian Express
Content:
LinkedIn Corp. has raised an additional $22.7 million to help insulate the steadily growing online business network from the economic storm and provide more financial flexibility.

The investment announced Thursday was made by one of LinkedIn's long-time backers, Bessemer Venture Partners, and three newcomers - business software maker SAP Ventures, banker Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and The McGraw-Hill Companies Inc., which publishes 'Business Week'.

The deal values privately held LinkedIn at slightly more than $1 billion, the same appraisal assigned the Mountain View-based company when it raised $53 million in June.

LinkedIn hasn't drawn on any of that money yet, but still thought it was prudent to have more money in the bank as the economy slumps amid a credit crunch, said Dan Nye, LinkedIn's chief executive officer. He also said LinkedIn wanted the extra cash in case an enticing acquisition opportunity crops up.

The new investors in LinkedIn are all intrigued with how they might be able to use information picked up from the Web site's 30 million members to drum more sales in their own businesses, Nye said.

Goldman Sachs' investment won't give it the inside track to become LinkedIn's investment banker should it ever pursue an initial public offering of stock, Nye said.

For now, LinkedIn is still trying to boost its revenue. Toward that end, LinkedIn also will begin offering a survey service that will poll its members about specific topics for a fee that will be negotiated on a case-by-case basis.

Heading: Sensex opens below 10k; Nifty below 3,000 - Indian Express
Content:
Oil rose over $1 to near $68 a barrel on Thursday, recouping some of previous session's 7.5 per cent losses, as investors shifted their focus to OPEC, which is likely to cut output on Friday to stem a sharp fall in prices.

Oil and commodities slumped for a second straight session on Wednesday as the dollar hit a two-year high against the euro. In addition, signs of a slowdown in China -- the world's fastest-growing economy -- intensified fears of global recession.

US light crude for December delivery rose 87 cents to $67.62 a barrel by 0113 GMT, after rising as much as $1.06 earlier. London Brent crude rose 90 cents $65.42.

"I think it's a technical rebound following the sharp drop last night. Some would see it as a good buy especially when there is an OPEC meeting coming up tomorrow and members have called for a cut in production," said Gerard Rigby, an energy analyst with Fuel First Consulting in Sydney.

Oil has plunged more than 50 per cent from its record high above $147 in July as the financial crisis cuts energy demand in the United States and other industrial countries.

Data from the US Energy Information Administration showed US product demand fell 8.5 per cent over the four weeks ending Oct. 17, compared with year-ago levels, while inventory levels continued to swell.

US crude oil inventories rose 3.2 million barrels in the week to Oct. 17, above analyst expectations for a 2.6 million build. Distillate inventories leaped by 2.2 million barrels while gasoline inventories rose by 2.7 million barrels.

Although the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) has traditionally steered away from price discussions, several OPEC members have emerged last weekend -- when prices touched a 16-month low -- to say that an acceptable price range for oil was between $70-$90 a barrel.

Still, analysts warned that global economic outlook could limit the impact of any oil supply cuts OPEC might agree at an emergency meeting on Friday, and the group's president said output policy would prove a difficult balancing act.

OPEC President Chakib Khelil said oil stocks are high and some member countries are finding it hard to sell their oil.

"It is a double-edged sword. If they cut supplies by too much, they could jeopardise the economic recovery. But if they don't act decisively, their economies may suffer," said Tony Nunan, assistant manager of risk management at Mitsubishi Corp in Tokyo.

Heading: Asia stocks sink on worsening global cues - Indian Express
Content:
The BSE Sensex dropped 4.8 per cent at the open on Thursday to its lowest in more than 2 years after another sell-off in US and Asian markets on fears of a severe global downturn.

Reliance Industries and ICICI Bank were leading the losses.

At 9:58 a.m., the 30-share BSE index had pared some losses to be down 3.81 per cent at 9,782.36, but all its components were in red.

The index was trading at its lowest level since June 2006.

The 50-issue NSE index fell 4.04 per cent to 2,941.20.

The index is down by half in 2008, with foreigners selling a net of $12.2 billion in stocks so far this year, largely reversing 2007's record net buying of $17.4 billion.

Leading private sector firm Reliance Industries, which has the largest weighting in the main index, is forecast to report a modest 2.2 per cent rise in net profit on slimmer refining margins.

Japan's Nikkei and MSCI's measure of other Asia-Pacific stocks were both down 5.5 per cent.

US stocks tumbled to five-year lows on Wednesday with investors grappled with an increasingly dire outlook for the global economy following a raft of disappointing profits and outlooks from major US companies.

Heading: Gold hits 13-month low as dollar surges - Indian Express
Content:
Asian stocks fell to a 4-year low on Thursday on growing fears a global recession would depress corporate earnings, while the dollar rose to a 2-year high against the euro, underpinned by the unwinding of risky trades.

Investors have mostly sought refuge in government debt of the euro zone, Japan and the United States as well as the yen, after credit market stabilisation in the last week unearthed a renewed focus on the adverse impact of the financial crisis on real economies, especially in emerging markets.

The cost of insurance against sovereign debt default in countries such as South Korea, Indonesia and the Philippines soared, with a sense of panic festering two days after Argentina moved to nationalise its pension system. The step was interpreted by investors as a desperate measure to stave off default.

Markets in developing countries, especially those that depend on portfolio flows to balance their current accounts, were abandoned overnight, with almost no one spared from a sharp slowdown in the global economy that has pushed crude prices below $70 a barrel and dragged copper prices to a three-year low.

The outlook for export-dependent Asian economies darkened, hitting the shares of many high-profile companies that have staked their business on overseas sales, such as Samsung Electronics and Canon Inc.

"After a raft of US earnings came out dismally, companies are set to cut costs, mostly by laying off a significant portion of their employees. Worry about massive unemployment and its impact on the real economy is deepening,' said Kim June-kie, a market analyst at SK Securities in Seoul.

The MSCI index of Asia-Pacific stocks outside Japan fell 5.5 per cent to its lowest since October 2004.

The global emerging markets index was down 3.7 per cent to a near 4-year low, and its 35 per cent drop so far in October outpaced the 25 per cent decline on the all-country world index.

Japan's Nikkei share average slumped 5.5 per cent, having now fallen 21 per cent in October alone. Japanese exporters have been undercut by the persistent strength of the yen, which reduces their competitiveness. The yen hit a five-year high against the euro earlier on Thursday.

South Korea's KOSPI index fell 8.5 per cent, led by shares of Samsung Electronics and steel producer POSCO.

Hong Kong's Hang Seng index was down 4.7 per cent at the lowest since April 2005.

Some property stocks managed to gain after the Chinese government late on Wednesday announced policies to increase homeownership.

China Overseas Land's stock rose 2.1 per cent, despite a 6.8 per cent drop in mainland Chinese stocks listed in Hong Kong.

"Yesterday's move can be considered part of an overall effort to give a light stimulus to the economy, but in my view is primarily focused on the real estate sector. These changes also illustrate that the Party is capable of taking proactive steps to deal with a changing economic environment," said Andy Rothman, China macro strategist with CLSA in Shanghai.

"A good time to look at residential developer stocks," he said in a report.

YEN IN DEMAND

The US dollar struck a 2-year high against the euro while the yen hit a near 6-year peak against the European single currency as investors bailed on bets on higher-yielding and emerging market currencies built up in recent years.

The euro slipped 0.3 per cent from late US trade to $1.2815 . In early Asian trade, the European single currency fell as low as $1.2726, its lowest since November 2006, on trading platform EBS. The euro slid as low as 124.15 yen, its lowest since January 2003, before rising to 125.00 yen, down 0.5 per cent on the day.

Analysts at banks such as Citigroup and Morgan Stanley expect the yen to continue strengthening as Japanese banks and investors slash their overseas exposure, though economic conditions in Japan itself are deteriorating.

Japan's trade data showed exports in September were much weaker than expected, with exports to the United States down 11 per cent from the same month last year.

"Demand is weakening across the globe. Not to mention the United States, falls in exports to the European Union are accelerating," said Junko Nishioka, an economist with RBS Securities in Tokyo. "Rising anxiety over the financial sector appears to have affected economic activity."

US light crude oil prices clung to small gains, up 43 cents at $67.18 a barrel, after hitting a 16-month low of $66.20. Oil prices have fallen by a third in October in anticipation of a steeper decline in demand from big consumers such as the United States and China.

Indeed, a report earlier this week showed Chinese annual economic growth in the third quarter slowed sharply to 9 per cent compared with 10.1 per cent in the second quarter.

Heading: India gold futures below 12,000 mark - Indian Express
Content:
Gold extended a 6-per cent decline in New York to hit its weakest in 13 months on Thursday after the dollar surged against the euro, while a sell-off in equities also drove investors to sell bullion to pay losses.

Platinum slipped almost 6 per cent to hit its lowest in more than four years as a stronger dollar put more pressure on the metal, already battered by falling demand from automakers. The prices of gold and platinum have converged to around $700.

Gold was trading at $725.60 an ounce, down $2.05 from New York's notional close on Wednesday, having hit an intraday low of $718.20 -- its lowest level since September 2007.

Bullion has dropped more than a fifth since rising to a two-month high at $931 on Oct 10 as investors ditched gold and other risky assets for cash amid fears of a global recession – a move that also sent other precious metals to multi-year lows.

"Gold's fortune is very much driven by the US dollar. Whilst gold, you might think, should benefit from a safe haven perspective, the downward pressures are dominating it at present," said Darren Heathcote of Investec Australia.

"Physical buying has really started to dry up. India really has its fill of gold for the time being. Given the significant depreciation in the Indian rupee, gold is proving to be too expensive now to buy," he said, referring to the world's largest buyer of the yellow metal.

The dollar index, which measures the US currency's value against a basket of six currencies, edged up to 85.625 after hitting a two-year peak of 86.070 as concerns about a worsening global economy prompted investors to cut risky assets.

The Nikkei average fell 6.6 per cent to its lowest point in more than five years, putting pressure on gold as investors dumped the metal to pay margin calls.

"Technically, there may well be support around $700 but given what's driving the market, it may or may not prove very strong," said Heathcote.

"I think the major support now is probably going to come in somwhere around the $693 level," he said, referring to a level seen in September 2007.

Platinum was trading at $796.00 ounce, down $35.50 from New York's notional close, after falling as low as $782.50, its weakest since July 2004, as poor car sales and a slowing US economy threatened to cut demand for autocalysts.

"There's some selling by speculators in Tokyo, which puts pressure on platinum. It's hard to say where gold and platinum are heading. In this stage, anything can happen," said a dealer in Hong Kong.

"People don't trust anything. They just want the cash. People who have invested in stock markets have lost a lot of money, even small investors are affected. So I don't think they have money to buy gold," he said.

The spread between platinum and gold prices has dropped significantly to less than $100 from more than $1,000 in March, when gold struck record at $1,030.80 and platinum also hit a lifetime high of $2,290 an ounce.

The automotive sector, which accounts for around half of all platinum demand, has been hit hard by the prospect of recession. A spate of carmakers in the US, Europe and Asia have reported falling sales.

Heading: Rupee falls to all-time low of 49.85 - Indian Express
Content:
India's gold futures extended falls on Thursday after breaking below 12,000 rupees per 10 grams a day ago on weak overseas markets.

"Gold is on a negative note, more falls can be seen," said B.G. Manjunath Prasad, senior technical analyst at Way 2 Wealth Securities Ltd.

Foreign gold, which guides the local markets, extended a 6 percent fall to hit its weakest level in 13 months after the dollar surged against the euro, reducing the metal's safe haven appeal.

The benchmark December gold on the Multi Commodity Exchange of India Ltd (MCX) is expected to trade within 11,640 rupees per 10 grams and 11,980 rupees this session, Prasad said.

December silver on the MCX is expected to trade within 16,790 rupees per kg and 17,380 rupees, Prasad added.

Heading: US foreclosure crisis reaches new high - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian rupee continued its slide and hit a new record low of 49.85 against the US dollar in morning trade on Thursday on sustained buying in the greenback amid renewed fears of a global recession.

The Indian currency fell by 55 paise from its overnight close partly because of absence of any intervention by the Reserve Bank of India.

Asian equity markets fell to their four-year low this morning on fears that a global slowdown will adversely impact the corporates' performance.

The dollar also hit a two year high against the basket of currencies in early trade in overseas markets.

In quiet trade at the Interbank Foreign Exchange (forex) market, the domestic currency resumed lower at 49.68/70 a dollar against its last close of 49.30/31 a dollar and fell further to a new intra-day low of 49.85 a dollar in late morning deals.

Forex dealers said foreign banks were continuously buying dollar amid speculation that rupee may breach 50-level against the dollar shortly.

Fears of increased capital outflows continued to weigh on the rupee sentiment.

Indian benchmark indices this morning tumbled to more than 28-month low of 9,681.28, a fall of over 488 points.

Heading: Inflation dips to 11.07 pct on Oct 11 - Indian Express
Content:
The number of American homeowners ensnared in the foreclosure crisis grew by more than 70 per cent in the third quarter of this year compared with the same period in 2007, according to data released Thursday.

Nationwide, nearly 766,000 homes received at least one foreclosure-related notice from July through September, up 71 per cent from a year earlier, said foreclosure listing service RealtyTrac Inc.

By the end of the year, RealtyTrac expects more than a million bank-owned properties to have piled up on the market, representing around a third of all properties for sale in the US

That's bad news for anyone who lives nearby and wants to sell their home. While foreclosure sales are booming in many areas, those properties are commanding deep discounts and pulling down neighbouring property values. "It has a pretty significant impact in terms of pricing," said Rick Sharga, RealtyTrac's vice president for marketing.

RealtyTrac monitors default notices, auction sale notices and bank repossessions. More than 250,000 properties were repossessed by lenders nationwide in the third quarter, 81,000 of which were taken back last month.

Six states - California, Florida, Arizona, Ohio, Michigan and Nevada - accounted for more than 60 per cent of all foreclosure activity in the quarter, with California alone making up more than a quarter of all US foreclosure filings.

Detroit and Atlanta were the only cities outside California, Florida, Nevada and Arizona to make RealtyTrac's list of the 20 hardest-hit metropolitan areas.

The combination of sinking home values, tighter mortgage lending criteria and an economy that many economists think has already slipped into recession has left hundreds of thousands of homeowners with few options. Many can't find buyers or owe more than their home is worth and can't refinance into an affordable loan, with the global credit crisis making loans far less available.

For those who can qualify for a loan, or have cash to invest, there are bargains to be had, especially in ravaged markets like Nevada and California. Last month, foreclosure resales accounted for more than half of existing home sales in California last month, as home sales jumped 65 per cent from a year ago, while the statewide median home price fell 34 per cent to $283,000, according to MDA DataQuick.

RealtyTrac, however, reported foreclosure filings in September were actually down 12 per cent from August. But much of that decline was the result of new state laws that delay the foreclosure process. In California, for example, lenders are now required to contact borrowers at least 30 days before filing a default notice. A similar law in North Carolina gives borrowers an extra 45 days.
