He added: "These colleges lost their recognition mostly due to the non-submission of the identification of the teaching staff as per the NCTE norms; not having a qualified principal, having a building plan for non-educational purposes, not having the land and lease deeds in the name of the trusts, and not having classrooms as per NCTE norms and so on."

Four B.Ed colleges each in Mehsana and Junagadh districts have lost their NCTE recognition. Other colleges being derecognised are in Sabarkantha, Gandhinagar, Surat, Patan, Vadodara, Kheda, Anand, and Porbandar districts.

Heading: Lost in transaction: Unaccounted deals worth Rs 70.5 cr detected - Indian Express
Content:
They were manning the entrance from where women protesters sneaked in

The Surat Police Commissioner has suspended four of his staff, including three women constables, who were on duty during a function attended by Chief Minister Narendra Modi at Khatodara on Sunday. The four were guarding the main entrance of the venue where a group of women entered with banners seeking rescue of a kidnapped girl.

According to the police, a group of 14, including 13 women, entered the Surat Raktdan Kendra building with banner displaying 14 varsh ni chokri ne apharan kartao thi mukti apavo (rescue a 14-year-old girl from kidnappers).

They said Jyoti, daughter of one Baliram Mishra, had been kidnapped by some unidentified people from near her house some time ago. Mishra, they claimed, had contacted the local police and even Commissioner RMS Brar, but failed to get a proper response.

After learning about the incident, the policemen on duty rushed to the venue and arrested Mishra along with 13 others and took them to the Umra police station. They were later released on bail.

The next day, Brar ordered an inquiry under S G Gohil, Assistant Commissioner of Police (F Division), against the police staff deployed at the entrance. Gohil took statements of all the police staff who were on duty that day and submitted his report to Brar.

On the basis of this report, Brar on Wednesday suspended Sub-Inspector BM Vasawa (Umra police station), and constables Tahera Mohammed (Women police station) Aruna Ashok (Mahidharpura police station) and Bharti Mahendra (Katargam police station).

Brar said: "On the report submitted by ACP Gohil, we have taken this step. We will also take strict action against Udhna Inspector A K Qureshi, who was given charge of the entire function."

Heading: Crane topples over, kills three, injures two - Indian Express
Content:
State coffers get richer by Rs 9 crore following Commercial Tax Dept raid on 15 establishments

Extensive raids carried out simultaneously at several locations in the state have unearthed bogus transactions to the tune of Rs 70.50 crore in the last three days. The Commercial Tax Department searched 15 establishments, resulting in estimated VAT income of Rs 9 crore to the state coffers, said an official release on Thursday.

The parties that were raided used to collect commission ranging between 2 and 2.5 per cent of the bill amount, which they would issue to the interested parties without actual physical delivery of goods to them. Thus, they would pocket the commission and the opposite parties would make money out of the bogus bills.

One of the raided parties was found having bill books in the name of seven different firms. Cash dealings revealed fake transactions involving Rs 18 crore during scrutiny of their books of accounts, the release said.

As per the modus operandi, interested persons would get bogus bills from these "firms" and successfully claim VAT credit as genuine entitlement from the Commercial Tax Department on the basis of returns filed. The VAT credit of all traders who have claimed tax credit on the basis of these bogus bills, will be rejected, the release said, adding that this will save Rs 7 crore for the government.

Nine bank accounts with Rs 9 lakh balance were sealed following the search operation and unaccounted cash of Rs 4 lakh was seized from one place. Seized items also include a flat worth Rs 20 lakh and stocks worth about Rs 4 lakh, according to the release.

The Commercial Tax Department had been working on the scam for a month through a close scrutiny of bills, returns, claims and other documents. Details were being gathered about where these bogus bill books were kept and where did they park the money. The raids were then conducted simultaneously, leaving the culprits with no chance to hide any incriminating documents. The raids, conducted under the guidance of J P Gupta and P K Pujari, went on till early morning on Wednesday. They also yielded incriminating documents from an abandoned vehicle on the highway, the release said.

The following firms were found involved in carrying bogus billing: Kamal Enterprises, Maheshwari Traders, P K Enterprise, Siddharth Corporation, Vinayak Trading Co, Devi Impex, Mahalaxmi Marketing and Parikh Agency.

Those filing revised returns in the wake of dealings with the abovementioned firms stand chance of waiver of interest and penalty, the release added.

Heading: Railways to run  special trains during Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
Gujarat ni dharti upar manavta na dushmano ne temni bhasha maaj jawab apaashe.

Enemies of humanity (inflicting terror) on the soil of Gujarat will be replied in their own language, said Chief Minister Narendra Modi this evening while naming a flyover here in the memory of Field Marshal Sam Manekshaw. Modi also came down heavily on those consoling the families of those arrested from Azamgarh and accused in the recent terror attacks.

The Rs 19.10-crore flyover, a major relief from traffic snarls at the Shivranjani crossroad, is part of city's BRTS project.

Welcoming top officials of Army, Navy and Air Force, Modi criticized what he called were attempts to shield those calling Sardar Patel a terrorist and questioned the silence of the UPA Government over this. This was an apparent reference to a Muslim clerics meeting in Azamgarh yesterday where a cleric reportedly called Godse and Patel terrorists.

"It is a misfortune of this country that those indulging in votebank politics are providing a shield to those who have the gall to call the man who integrated princely states into one nation a terrorist," he said. He also said that while the coffin of later Sardar Patel's elder brother Vitthalbhai was kept open for public viewing in Karamsad on his 75th birth anniversary recently, UPA leaders were taking pride on the repeal of POTA and celebrating the relief to detainees.

"Even corners of the eyes of such votebank politicians don't get wet over deaths of innocent people at the hands of terrorists...they go to Azamgarh and comfort their families," Modi said, asking, "Is this their Bharat Bhakti?" He alleged that vote bank politicians by following a policy of appeasement were responsible for the shattering of dreams of true patriots.

Heading: Boy’s severed head found in Anand; police clueless - Indian Express
Content:
Western Railway has decided to run special trains between Ahmedabad and Patna in view of a heavy passenger rush. Accordingly, train number 947/948 will run as 'Chhath Special' between Ahmedabad and Patna while train number 949/950 will run between Ahmedabad and Nanded.

Train number 947 will leave Ahmedabad at 9.30 pm on October 30 and on November 3. Pairing train number 948 will leave Patna at 11.30 pm on November 1 and November 5. It will go via Vadodara, Ratlam, Kota, Agra Fort and Allahabad in both directions with six general and 6 sleeper class coaches, besides others.

Train number 949 will leave Ahmedabad at 3.45 pm on October 27 and make its return journey as train number 950 from Nanded at 10.15 pm on October 29. It will have 14 coaches that would include six general and six sleeper class coaches, said a press release issued by the Divisional Railway Manager, Rajiv Mishra, on Wednesday.

Meanwhile, South Central Railway (SCR) will run six special trains on October 29 between Secunderabad and Rajkot to accommodate the additional number of passengers during Diwali.

Train number 717, Secunderabad-Rajkot Special, will depart from Secunderabad on October 29 and November 12 at 2.50 pm and reach Rajkot at 8 pm the next day, an SCR release said on Wednesday.

The returning train, number 718 Rajkot-Secunderabad Special will depart from Rajkot on October 24, November 7 and 14 at 5 am to reach Secunderabad at 10.30 am the day after.

Heading: Dubious deal: City-based traders booked for forgery - Indian Express
Content:
Decapitated body of a 13-year-old recovered from nearby canal

The decapitated body of a 13-year-old student from Jhakharia was found on banks of the Narmada Canal near the village in Anand taluka.

Sub-Inspector (Anand Rural police) V S Dabhi said Jaideep Patel's severed head was found in the field next to the state highway.

Arvind Ambalal Patel said his son had left home on his scooty for tuition at Jhakharia village at 6 PM. "When he did not return home, the parents lodged a complaint about the missing boy around 9 pm," said Dabhi. On Thursday morning, some villagers saw the decapitated body in the canal and informed the police around 8.30 am.

A student of Class VIII from the Sardar Patel Vidyalaya in Anand town, Jaideep had gone for his maths tuition, and was returning home when the incident occurred. "His tuition got over at 7 pm; we suspect that the incident must have happened between 7.15 pm and 8 pm," said Dabhi.

The police said Arvind Patel is a gram sevak in Khambat. Dabhi denied any family rivalries or any other issue pertaining to Patel or his son that could have led to the incident. "It is rare, as crimes of this type are not typical to Anand," said Anand Superintendent of Police A K Jadeja.

The police are, however, yet to make any leads into the case. "It is not the type of crime that can happen in Anand district. Investigations might take more time, as the family appeared to be distraught with the death of their only son," Dabhi added.

Heading: Junagadh court holds 21 guilty in lion poaching case - Indian Express
Content:
Businessmen accused of duping seven Manawadar-based ginning merchants of Rs 5.35 cr

Seven Manawadar-based ginning merchants have lodged complaints of forgery and cheating against some Ahmedabad-based traders and agents.

According to the police, the merchants had dispatched some 20,000 cottons bales to the Ahmedabad-based traders since January last and had received payment for only 16,000 bales. The payment for the 4,000 bales worth Rs 5.35 crore was delayed and got overdue. Later, it was found that the Ahmedabad-based traders had all gone underground.

After the traders did not make any attempt to make the payment despite the complainants' repeated efforts, a complaint was lodged against them.

Complainants Premji Manawar (Ashish Cotton) have lodged a complaint over the payment of 1,892 bales worth Rs 2, 52, 02,390; Vallabhdas Tank ( Amar Cotton) for 800 bales worth Rs 1,00,92,008, Vijay Patel (Partner – Amar Cotton) for 300 bales worth Rs 42,37,542, and Ashok Prajapati (Partner- Amar cotton) for 300 bales worth Rs 43,28,849. Other complainants include Karan Rambhai (Nootan Ginning) for 100 bales worth Rs 13,26,941, Vimal Lohana (Harshad Ginning) for 100 bales worth Rs 14,03,152 and Suresh Dave (Komal Traders) for 500 bales worth Rs 69, 45,661.

The seven are residents of Manawadar town.

The Manawadar police have registered complaints under Sections 407,420, 465, 467, 468, 471, 472, 474, 114 and 120(B) of the Indian Penal Code and arrested three people, including a trader, an agent and a transporter, who have been sent to police custody till October 27. They have been identified as Anil Thakkar alias Anil Sharma, a trader and a resident of Ahmedabad, Shatish Vithalani, an agent residing in Rajkot and Mohammed Tariq, a transporter and a resident of Ahmedabad.

Manawadar town Sub-Inspector and Investigating Officer M R Godhania said: "All the seven complaints have been registered within the last 15 days at different stages. They are of a similar nature. We have started the interrogation of the three persons on the basis of the complaints."

Godhania said more arrests are likely soon, but some traders and agents involved in the racket have reportedly gone underground.

He said the entire investigation is concentrated in Memco and the Bapunagar area of Ahmedabad.

"Traders and agents involved in the crime are reportedly underground and avoiding their possible arrest. Our prime concern is to arrest the kingpin of the racket and recover the materials, but nothing has been recovered so far," said Godhania.

Heading: Boon turns bane: five die in road mishap, two critical - Indian Express
Content:
A Junagadh court on Thursday convicted all the 21 accused in a case of poaching of six Gir lions and sentenced them to three years imprisonment. It also imposed a penalty of Rs 10,000 each, failing which they will serve additional three months in prison. One convict, Berbai (70), had died during the trial that ran for 18 months.

All the convicts belong to Madhya Pradesh and are associated with the Parghi gang, notorious for poaching.

The incident had occurred in the Babaria range falling under the Gir West forest division in Junagadh. Three lions were killed on March 3, 2007 and the rest were slaughtered on March 29.

Among those convicted, 10 are men and the rest are women. They were arrested on April 18, 2007 and sent to the Junagadh jail on April 25. After an 18-month trial, the court of the additional judicial magistrate found the accused guilty. Judge R K Makwana passed the verdict.

The Junagadh police had registered the case under sections 429 and 120 (B) of the Indian Penal Code and under various provisions of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972.

Those convicted include kingpin Sarkas Lal, Kuntarsinh, Mojersinh and 17 others. All are residents of different villages falling under Khandwa, Panna and Hoshangabad districts of Madhya Pradesh.

Earlier, the incident had created quite a stir in Gujarat, so much so that even Chief Minister Narendra Modi had rushed to Sasan (Gir) to take stock of the situation.

After initial investigation, the case was handed over to CID (Crime).

According to D J Wanakar, Superintendent, Junagadh District Jail, there are 18 minors aged below six who are in jail along with their parents.

Now, the convicts will be packed off to various jails in the state. "The 18 months time period, which the convicts had spent in the Junagadh jail, will be deducted accordingly from three years imprisonment," he said.

Heading: AMU scholar roots for Marxism - Indian Express
Content:
The maiden trip in their new auto rickshaw to a temple in Bhavnagar proved fatal for five people from Ambawadi in the city when they met with an accident near Prahalad Nagar Crossroads, on Thursday morning. Two persons injured in the accident are undergoing treatment in the civil hospital.

A resident of Saurashtra Society in Ambawadi, Ramesh Pargi was an auto rickshaw driver and had bought a new CNG auto rickshaw on Tuesday. To seek blessings from their family deity, Kodhiyar Mata, Pargi decided to take his new vehicle first to the temple in Bhavnagar.

His wife Sonal, and children, Pankaj (8) and Jaishree (3), along with their neighbours, Mukesh Nagwadia and his daughters, Jassy and Aradhana, left for the temple on Wednesday morning.

On their way back, a speeding truck hit the auto rickshaw near Prahalad Nagar Crossroads on S G Highway. "The auto rickshaw was crushed by the truck, and Ramesh and Sonal died on the spot. Mukesh, Jaishree and Aradhana died while undergoing medical treatment. Pankaj and Jassy are in a critical state," said Inspector J J Patel of the Satellite police.

The police are on the look out for the driver of the truck, who gave them a slip and is absconding. The police have seized the truck.

Heading: IT slump: students fear pink slip before the job - Indian Express
Content:
The feminine touch
One can never say that the guys of Golmaal Returns were not good sports. The boys, Ajay Devgan, Arshad Warsi, Tusshar Kapoor and Shreyas Talpade, had to crossdress on director Rohit Shetty's call for a scene that required the guy gang to dress up like women. In the scene, it is Women's Day and so the boys dress up like women to enter a mall, as only women were allowed on that particular day. Shetty says, "I was quite taken aback when Ajay agreed to this scene. He was very gung-ho about it. In fact, none of the guys had any reservations, which made it one of the best scenes in the film." It seems the guys got some strange looks from the women around, but then which man is going to complain when he is the centre of attraction?

Style bhai
Shahid Kapur is apparently the latest style icon on the B-scene. All his movies, from Vivah to Jab We Met to Kismat Konnection, have rocked the box office. Whether they're critically panned or not, the audience seems to love them. And his fan following is increasing by the day. The ladies want to be with him and all the lads want to be him. Shahid's casual and sexy style has been aggressively adopted by the youth today. Now if only he'd deliver a mind-blowing performance, Shahid would have it all.

Crystal clear
Katrina Kaif knows what she wants with her life and nowhere was it clearer than at the Swarovski showroom in Austria, where she was shooting for Subhash Ghai's Yuvraaj.

Apparently, the crew members kept teasing the gorgeous actress that the beautiful and delicate pieces that Swarovski is known for will distract her and that she won't give her full attention to the shooting. But Kat surprised everyone by remaining utterly focused. So impressed was the crew with her undivided attention to the shoot, that they decided to gift her with one of the pieces from the showroom.

Heading: Cleared: single company for all traffic solutions - Indian Express
Content:
The IT boom could well be over, the pink slips extending not only to existing staff but possibly also to Pune's huge inventory of engineering students, who had been banking on another year of big hiring by the sector.

Many engineering students who had been assured jobs after campus interviews last semester have not got their offer letters yet. They are worried whether the letters will come, with recession threatening the industry. NASSCOM estimates that IT recruitments in the city will be down to 200,000 from the original projection of 275,000. "Yes, there will be some effect," said Ganesh Natrajan, chairman of NASSCOM.

"Our campus interviews took place in June, when there was no slowdown on the horizon, and many students got placed. But the worry now is whether these offers will translate into actual jobs in June 2009 at graduation time," said Sandeep Meshram, training and placement officer, College of Engineering Pune (CoEP). Natrajan is still hopeful the students won't be let down. "I am sure all large firms will honour their commitments," he said.

Last week a college in Pimpri-Chinchwad held a joint meeting of placement officers of engineering colleges and HR officers of various companies. "The economic slowdown was discussed. It was observed that apart from some premier institutes, most colleges are feeling the heat," said a placement officer.

Lalit Pawar, training and placement officer of Maharashtra Institute of Technology, corroborated this, saying the number of companies that came calling for campus interviews was 10 per cent of that last year.

The recession is set to lead to downsizing. "It will be minimum bench strength with no leeway for non-performers," said Natrajan.

IT training institutes have begun feeling the heat. "We have started working on remedial measures. The only way to sustain is aggressive marketing and getting more clients to try and retain the existing revenue line," said Narendra Barhate, chairman and MD of Seed Infotech. But Natrajan said there was no need for trainers to press the panic button. "Having a global quality workforce is imperative. We will continue to equip our associates with the best skills," he said.

Barhate said the recession would show the exit route to scores of fly-by-night IT institutes that mushroomed in the last few years. "Recession may throw up another opportunity if companies in the US or Europe outsource their training needs to India," he said.

Heading: Blow to anti-terror squad as SIMI suspects get bail - Indian Express
Content:
SPECIAL PURPOSE VEHICLE: Will need to raise Rs 24,000 cr for flyovers, bridges & Metro rail

Over six months after the civic administration first proposed it, the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) on Thursday cleared the Pune Infrastructure Development Corporation (PIDC), a special purpose vehicle, for resolving the traffic and transport problems of the city. The company will have to raise Rs 24,000 crore for the implementation of projects like flyovers, bridges as also the Metro rail in the city.

"The company would be responsible for the infrastructure to improving the traffic and address the transportation woes of the city. PIDC will not be responsible for public transport though," Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi said.

The SPV proposal would be sent to the state government for final approval as per the Section 66 (41A) of BPMC Act 1949.

The PMC had set aside Rs 75 crore as seed capital in the annual budget (2008-09) for the SPV and had tabled the proposal in standing committee in April, which approved it in September. The civic administration has proposed that the company raise funds from multilateral agencies such as World Bank and various financial institutions .

The projects will be planned on the basis of the comprehensive mobility plan being prepared by Infrastructure Leasing & Financial Services Ltd.

There will be representation of officer-bearers and officers from PMC, FIs and private organisations as directors on the board of the new company. The technicalities for the new body will be finalised after the PMC registers the new company, the commissioner said.

Pardeshi said the company may also take up execution of projects for which the PMC has already prepared technical reports.

The PMC plans to build 16 flyovers, three subways, five parking spaces, a 34-km-long High Capacity Mass Transit Route (HCMTR) and a riverside road.

The new flyovers will be at Bund Garden, Engineering College, Juna Bazaar, Nul Stop, Shimla Office, Khadki, Handewadi, Senapati Bapat Road and Magarpatta.

On a query as to how PIDC would help in improving public transport service, Pardeshi said it would be responsible for raising infrastructure for Metro rail.

Earlier, the proposal was not well received by the political parties fearing that the company would be an independent entity and they would have no control over it. But once it became clear that the company would be affiliated to the PMC, it got the go-ahead.

The SPV proposal was passed by majority vote with the NCP, Shiv Sena and BJP voting in favour while the Congress voted against it. The Congress corporators staged a walk out in protest.

Heading: Maratha body: we do want political reservation - Indian Express
Content:
The state anti-terrorism squad (ATS) suffered a major blow on Thursday when a special court accepted the bail application of three SIMI suspects from the city.

Judge S J Kale passed the order releasing them on a personal bond of Rs 20,000 each and ordered them to visit the ATS office in Pune everyday till the chargesheet is filed.

Ayaz Khan and Imtiyaz Baba Miyan Shaikh of Bhimpura, Camp, and Feroz Mehboob Pathan of Ghorpade Peth had been arrested in August and September.

Feroz was caught with 40 Urdu books; Imtiyaz with an Urdu document and four CDs.

Ayaz was arrested along with Nadim Sheikh in a currency case, and was then was booked under the Unlawful Activities (Protection) Act for helping the others circulate the jihadi literature.

The anti-terrorism squad had claimed that the books and documents contained jihadi literature and the CDs had videos that could have created unrest.

But defence lawyer M M Syed argued that the investigating agencies did not mention details of the contents, nor how the suspects were associated with SIMI.

Syed said that suspects could be tried by the court of the judicial magistrate first class. The assistant public prosecutor insisted there was sufficient prima-facie evidence against the suspects.

According to the ATS, the suspects were linked to alleged SIMI member and gangster Mohammed Bilal Rasool Kagzi of Gujrat, who was arrested by the Mumbai crime brach in an extortion case.

Kagzi, in turn, was associated with the Fazlu Rehman and Banti Pandey gang.

The police said Kagzi came in contact with Ayaz through his brother Feroz Totla, a member of the Fazlu Rehman gang, who was later gunned down by the Mumbai police.

Heading: Rs 32 lakh per hectare of acquired farmland - Indian Express
Content:
Differences surfaced on Thursday between Maratha organisations over political reservation for the community. Just a week after the Maratha coordination committee said it would drop the demand, one of the organisations under its wing, Shivsangram, declared that it wants political reservation after all.

Vinayak Mete, former MLA of NCP and founder of Shivsangram, claimed the support of most Maratha organisations in his demand. "Only two organisations, Maratha Mahasangh and Maratha Seva Sangh, don't want political reservation. I have the support of eight organisations and we want a separate 25 per cent OBC quota for the community in education, jobs and politics," he said.

The umbrella organisation had claimed that Mete's Shivsangram organisation was with them. But interestingly, Mete's name was not included in the list of office-bearers of the umbrella organisations.

Mete said, "We have talked to all important leaders of all parties except Shiv Sena. We will meet Bal Thackeray next week."

Heading: After all the flak, kudos and cash for civic staff who made Games a hit - Indian Express
Content:
Farmers have been offered Rs 32 lakh per hectare of land being acquired for the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation's (MIDC's) Chakan Phase-II .

Last year, the rate for land in Khed and Shirur in the same area acquired for the Bharat Forge Special Economic Zone (SEZ) was fixed at Rs 17 lakh per hectare.

On Thursday, a meeting was conducted under District Collector Chandrakant Dalvi as per the provisions of the MIDC Act under section 33(2). Nearly 1,642 hectares are up for acquisition for this phase from six villages - Varali, Bhambolli, Savardari, Khambure, Vasuli and Shinde.

Deputy Collector and coordinating officer Dnyandev Thube said the deal will be sealed after a final meeting soon. "If there are still some doubts about the land price, authorities will send the rate to the government. Then it will be up to the government if they want to acquire the land," he said. MIDC deputy chief executive officer MIDC SanjayYadav, regional officer for Pune region Purshottam Jadhav, SDO Kiran Mahajan and tehsildars were present.

Heading: Plan mooted to limit PMPML services  to city limits - Indian Express
Content:
In a rare gesture, 10 prominent citizens of Pune, half of them builders, have come together to felicitate 20 employees of the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) for putting in "extraordinary efforts" for the city's civic infrastructure makeover ahead of the recently concluded Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG). The plan is to raise Rs 10 lakh for the felicitation of the selected civic staff.

"Everybody has been criticising PMC. But they worked 24×7 to give a better look to the city for the CYG," said architect Christopher Benninger, who took the initiative of contacting the citizens and making the proposal. "It is high time we start recognising their good work as the municipal corporation has always only been at the receiving end, sometimes due to the apathy of citizens," he said. The idea behind the initiative is to make common people change their way of looking at civic staff and also encourage hardworking PMC employees, he added.

Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi said it is a good initiative by citizens to appreciate the work of the civic staff. "I have already conveyed to my colleagues the news about their being appreciated," he said.

The felicitation ceremony is planned for mid-November. Pardeshi has started short-listing the names of the civic staff who put in "extraordinary" efforts for CYG-related work.

"We have decided to honour employees at the grassroots who worked hard to give a better look to the city for the Games, which had participants from around 70 countries," said Ramprasad Naidu, managing director, Christopher Charles Benninger Architects. The citizens who have come forward to contribute to the cause are Dr KH Sancheti of Sancheti Hospitals, Nitin Nyati of Nyati Builders, the team at Elephant Design, Atul Chordia of Panchsheel Estates, Jitendra Tanti of Suzlon Ltd, R Vasudevan of Vascon Builders, Tanvir Inamdar of Tain Enterprises, Vipul Patel of Swastik Industries, Ajit Bhate and Jaideep Raje of Bhate and Raje Construction Co, Benninger and Naidu.

Each will contribute Rs 1 lakh, said Naidu. While the CYG attracted much media coverage, the key civic staff who made the event possible never got a good word for their efforts and this was an attempt to make amends, he said.

"The kind of work done is remarkable and a lot of it seemed to have happened almost overnight, just like it's done abroad. It shows that we too can work under pressure and deliver results. Given this, I thought I must contribute to this very thoughtful gesture proposed by Benninger," said Dr KH Sancheti. According to Sudhir Sharma of Elephant Designs even this is not enough and there is more that the citizens need to do to show their appreciation. "We are always cribbing that nothing is happening and when it does happen we take it for granted. In an environment where things are difficult to accomplish, we need to commend when good work gets done - and that too by the ordinary workers," said Sharma.

Heading: Postal dept gears up for Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
The city transport utility may soon be asked to limit its exposure to only the city and stop all its services to the rural outskirts. If this happens, it will bring to an end over 23 years of 'rural service' that Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal Limited (PMPML) has put in.

This follows a proposal floated by the Regional Transport Authority (RTA) that PMPML pull out buses from city outskirts and rural routes and start focusing on its core competency: to provide better bus service within the city. If this proposal goes through, then the company will need to add 200 more buses to ply within city limits.

"According to Central Institute of Road Transport (CIRT) norms, the company should have close to 2,500 buses. The MSRTC is already providing services in the rural areas. Since PMPML already has limited buses, it ought to leave the outskirts to the MSRTC and focus on the city," said RTA member Baba Shinde.

While PMPML is quite keen on this proposal, the MSRTC is reluctant and has said that it does not have the resources to press additional buses on these routes.

" If PMPML reduces its buses on these routes, we will not be able to augment our services. We are already short of buses and staff," said P P Nimsarkar, divisional controller, MSRTC. "It was the PMT that insisted on taking up these routes in the mid 1980s. Now, the population in these areas has increased tremendously over the years; its development has been more city-specific and PMPML has been catering to this population. Already the people are finding the existing bus network inadequate; reducing services of PMPML would be an injustice to them," he added.

In many ways things have come a full circle, as it was the erstwhile Pune Municipal Transport in 1985 that had wrested these routes from the MSRTC and insisted on plying its buses on rural routes like Rajgurunagar, Saswad and Paud. "It was a mistake by PMT and it does not mean that it cannot be rectified. Moreover, at that time PMT had the means and was not at a loss. Now it is not so," said Shinde. The RTA has called a meeting on October 27 to discuss the issue further.

To begin with, Shinde is looking at rationalising the routes and coordinate the timings of both buses. "Eventually, we ought to ease off PMPML buses from the outskirts," Shinde said.

PMPML is keen on turning over the routes to MSRTC eventually. "We have near about 200 buses plying on rural outskirts. On these routes we end up competing with the MSRTC, and both organisations lose revenue," Patil said. He added that as PMPML has no bus depots outside city limits buses have to travel empty to the outskirts in the mornings to bring commuters into the city.

In the evenings, the process is reversed, as the return trips are empty. "As the MSRTC already has bus depots in the outskirts, their buses can stay overnight and avoid the empty return trips," Patil said.

Heading: Vandalism of buses: PMPML loses up to Rs one crore - Indian Express
Content:
Special trays to be kept in major post offices to cater to Diwali mail

The Department of Posts of Pune region has made special arrangements for quick processing of Diwali greeting mails. Special arrangements have been made for clearance of letterboxes on the day of Diwali — October 28 as well as have the staff work on Sunday — October 26 to sort out these mails to ensure the Diwali greetings reach well in time.

With this being additional mail, the postal department have made special arrangements of having special plastic trays for catering to this mail. According to Postmaster general, Pune region, SC Jarodia, last year the Pune region handled about 20 lakh diwali greeting cards and this year we are expecting it to touch 25 lakh in addition to normal mail.

"With his being a gigantic task, for the postal department, to handle this mail, in a time bound manner, special arrangements have been made for acceptance of Diwali greetings in important post offices in Pune city,''said Jarodia. Sixteen post offices have been selected for keeping these special trays which include — Pune head office, Pune city, Khadki, Deccan Gymkhana, Shivajinagar, Ganeshkhind, Pimpri, Hadapsar, Market Yard, Parvati, Model colony, Ex-service colony, SP College, Swargate, Yerwada and Chinchwad East.

The postal departments have been instructed to keep adequate stock of postal stamps and stationary to meet the requirement of the Diwali mail.

The offices have been instructed to pre-sort the mails, prepare labeled bundles and put the mail in separate bags for local post offices, district delivery offices and mail offices in the state and other circle concentration centers in India.

"All important post offices and mail offices have also been asked to put rubber stamp indicating Diwali mails on the check slip and label the bags to ensure special treatment of Diwali greetings.

"Bulk mails will also be handled differently,''said Jarodia. Instructions have also been issued to all divisional superintendents and other officers to pay visits to post offices and mail offices for proper monitoring and faster disposal.

Heading: ‘IAF will get Brahmos version by 2012’ - Indian Express
Content:
In the last year, the Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal Limited (PMPML) has incurred losses up to Rs one crore in riot-like situations and subsequent damages to its buses.

The latest incident happened early this week when the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) attacked PMPML buses leading up to a loss of Rs 15 lakh. The company also lost two buses that were burnt by a mob. But unlike private buses, the company has to pay for these buses on its own as it does not have insurance.

"The premium is very high. We find it is less expensive for us if we just pay the liabilities directly," said S B Patil, CMD, PMPML. For old buses, the minimum premium is Rs 35,000; for new buses it is around Rs 55-60,000.

"For a fleet of around 1,200 it will work out to be Rs 6-7 crore, at present," he said.

As a result, it finds it cheaper to avoid insurance. This is the fourth time this year that PMPML has faced riot like attacks on its buses — three times by the MNS and once by a mob which went on rampage after the death of 10-year old-Atharva Dongre.

A senior PMPML officer said, "Generally, in a year, we lose about Rs 50 lakh to Rs one crore because of riot-like violence. This year, it was the MNS, last year we faced the violence due to the Khairlanji incident," he said.

The company also has to pay an additional Rs one crore in liabilities to be paid back to commuters.

This does not include the loss in revenue that PMPML has to contend with. According to PMPML spokesperson, the company lost Rs 25 lakh in revenue on the first day of the latest violence, as it had to stop bus services for many hours.

Heading: Management institutes without affiliation: UoP toughens stand - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian Air Force (IAF) would get its own version of Brahmos — a supersonic cruise missile — by 2012, A Sivanthu Pillai, chief executive officer and managing director, Brahmos Airspace, said on Wednesday.

Pillai was addressing media persons after inaugurating IWAPS 2008, a two-day international workshop on 'Advances in processing of solid propellant rocket motors' at High Energy Materials Research Laboratory (HEMRL) here as part of the Golden Jubilee celebrations of the Defence Research & Development Organisation (DRDO) and centenary celebrations of HEMRL.

"Trials and tests will be carried out by 2011 and it is expected to be inducted into the IAF by 2012," he said, adding that the Army and Navy already had variants of the missile provided by Brahmos Airspace.

Stressing on the importance of research in nanotechnology, Pillai, who is also chief controller, R & D (ACE & NS) at DRDO, said the organisation would lay more emphasis on this domain. "Materials such as nano-aluminium, which will augment weight reduction of equipment, will be increasingly used in various defence applications.

Meanwhile, the DRDO will continue to develop innovative equipment," he said. Around 300 scientists from several countries will participate in the workshop, which will also discuss futuristic development programmes.

Heading: Flat owner didn’t know murdered BPO employee lived in his flat - Indian Express
Content:
The issue of newly started management institutes, that have started their courses without getting affiliation from the University of Pune, came up for the discussion in a meeting of the management council of the university on Thursday. Some members brought the issue to the notice of vice chancellor Narendra Jadhav, who was presiding the meeting.

The University has now decided to take stringent action on such institutes by not granting their terms. That means hundreds of students who have already taken admission to such institutes are going to suffer.

"It is observed that there are some management institutes in the city, which have started their courses without taking affiliation from the university. The institutes say they have permission from AICTE. But according to Maharashtra University Act, even after getting permission from AICTE, affiliation from the university is must to offer degrees to students," said a management council member.

The local inquiry committees of the university, which visits the institutes and recommends for affiliation had brought this issue to the fore last month. "The director of technical education has given permission to start management courses on his own. It is totally illegal and the director can also come under fire in this issue," said another member.

The university has decided to discuss the issue in law committee meeting to be held immediately. Sureshchandra Bhosale, dean of law faculty is heading the law committee consisting of two other members - Dilip Ukey and Rajendra Vikhe- Patil. "As the courses have already started, the institutes will plead to continue them. But the committee will not spare anybody if the procedure is illegal," said a member.

Meanwhile, the university has also decided not to revoke its decision on merging the Ayurveda department with the department of health sciences. The management council had taken the decision to merge the Ayurveda department with the department of health sciences last year and the process was to be completed this month. Some Ayurveda professors had recently demanded to revoke this decision.

Heading: PMC brings green channel to clear priority files - Indian Express
Content:
Owner of the flat in Aditya Breeze Park society Kartik Laxman was not aware that BPO employee Khusboo Mishra of Bhopal, who was murdered on Monday night, was living in his flat.

Meanwhile, alleged murderer Manumohinder Madhuresh Abrol (25) had been nabbed in Bhopal on Wednesday night. He was nabbed with the help of Bhopal police. The Chatuhshrungi police will take him in to as he reaches Pune.

Senior police inspector Sheshrao Suryawanshi said that Khusboo was residing in a flat on the seventh floor of Aditya Breeze Park in Balewadi but the flat owner Laxman was not aware of it.

"Laxman had registered the names of two tenants — Nimisha Gobrel and Mehel Jain — with the police. Both were living in his flat for the last one and half years. But Khusboo joined them about four months ago," he said.

The police said that Gobrel and Jain knew Khsuboo and allowed her to stay with them without informing the owner who lives in Bangalore.

Investigations have revealed that Abrol and Khusboo studied together in a Bhopal college. They completed BE electronics and joined Capgemini BPO in Pune as software developers.

The police suspect that they were in love. The relationship turned sour in the last few months and Abrol murdered her. The police had found Khusboo's naked body lying in a pool of blood at the Aditya Breeze Park residence. Her throat was slit and there were wounds on her back and waist.

Her parents, who were in Pune, said that she was not in a love affair with Abrol. They said it was a one-sided love affair. It was also known that Khusboo had made three complaints to the company authorities against Abrol. The company had issued a notice to Abrol in this regard.

Heading: After CYG medal hound, ASI focussed on Asian Games - Indian Express
Content:
The Pune Municipal Corporation on Thursday announced the setting up of a 'green channel' giving priority to senior citizens, physically-challenged persons, defence personnel, sportspersons and renowned artistes who come for official work to the civic body. The green channel initiative is to give priority to the files related to these categories.

The decision comes after RTI activist Vihar Durve pushed the civic administration to take the initiative for the convenience of the public. However, the persons seeking the special PMC service will have to submit a photocopy of their identity along with their application to the civic administration so that it can be given special treatment.

Heading: To encourage donation, a blood donor day every month - Indian Express
Content:
Although the Army Sports Institute had only ten representatives among the 158 competitors participating in the recently concluded Commonwealth Youth Games, all ten athletes contributed to India's medal tally at the games. The disciplines of boxing, weightlifting and wrestling for which the ASI conducted training camps, each produced medals and contributed to the overall success of the country.

In boxing, ASI had six representatives of which two won gold, one won silver and three won bronze medals. Wrestling saw a solitary representative in Ajit Patil who won gold in the 42 kg category. Three weightlifters, who underwent a training camp in the ASI, won silver medals.

Colonel Satpal Ahlawat, commandant of the ASI, said that intense training of the athletes was the key to success. "I am delighted with the performance of these athletes of the ASI. They trained hard and were focused on their objective. They set a target to secure medals and achieved it."

The ASI had conducted a six-month rigorous coaching camp for the three disciplines — boxing, weightlifting and wrestling. "The training was specific and scientific. Wrestling coach Piararam Sondhi conducted a thorough training camp at the institute. The atmosphere for training was good as there were a variety of wrestlers for the competitors to practice with.

Boxing coach Luis Enrique, who is from Cuba, has done a fantastic job with the young pugilists. Weightlifting coach Imre Zsuga from Hungary is very experienced and has given the young weightlifters some valuable advice," said the Colonel.

Now, the ASI is training its athletes to win medals at the Asian Games. "We will judge our performance on the basis of the Asian Games rather that the Commonwealth games. Our target for the Asian Games is not less than 4 medals."

In CYG, the ASI had no representations for athletics. Colonel Ahlawat said that the athletes, training at the ASI, were too young. "We started our junior athletes programme only in 2006 and hence the athletes were in the age group 14-16 years. We did not have athletes in the age group of 18 and below. However, they are working hard to win medals at the Asian Games."

Heading: Bright and beautiful - Indian Express
Content:
As October is being observed as blood donor month, the State Blood Transfusion Council (SBTC) has decided to observe every 18th as community blood donor day. The SBTC has written to the blood banks across the state to observe the community blood donation day, STBC chief Dr Sanjay Jadhav said.

The Sassoon General Hospital's blood bank, which is the regional blood bank centre, conducted an awareness rally and camp to collect blood, Dr D D Shetty, senior medical officer at Sassoon said. Pune has 22 blood banks and the total collection is an approximate 1.15 lakh units of blood every year.

A major concern is the lack of motivation to donate blood. Hence, the idea behind this community blood donation day is to increase the percentage of voluntary blood donation.

At present, 83 per cent of the blood collected in the state comes from voluntary blood donation drives. Every effort is being made to ensure that there are more avenues for voluntary blood donation, Jadhav said.

According to Jadhav, a total of 10 lakh units of blood are collected in the state every year and now plans are afoot to set up 171 storage centres at tehsils. So far, 58 have been opened. He also pointed out that voluntary blood collection has increased over the years from 3.5 lakh units of blood in 1997 to an approximate 13 lakh blood units in 2008. Meanwhile, the prevalence of HIV in the screened blood has also decreased from 1.8 per cent in 1997 to 0.5 per cent in 2008.

Heading: The fragrance spreads - Indian Express
Content:
Designer sky lanterns or akashdeeps are available in innovative shapes this Diwali

From a traditional homely affair to a commercially productive creation, the akashdeep has always been an intrinsic part of Diwali décor. With the festival knocking at the door, these lighted kandils with designer lamp shades are once again topping the list of Diwali shopping.

Initially made of paper and cane, today the akashdeep are also made of various fabrics. This season what is dominating the scape are the Chinese akashdeep. These are available in myriad shapes, colours and sizes with exquisite tassels attached. Many shops in the city are also offering metallic ones with attached bulbs that command a higher price.

Talking about the significance of these sky lanterns, Quasim Tamboli, whose 100 year old shop in Laxmi Road, has also displayed a huge variety of these lanterns, says, "Akashdeep signifies the light of God. While the Chinese ones are machine made, the paper and cane lamps still depend on human artistry and precision. Also while the demand for fabric made and paper made akashdeep is great, the cane ones do not enjoy much popularity with the common people due to its high cost and non durable nature" adds Tamboli. Incidentally there are also the special Mughal -e-Azam home-made akashdeeps made of rainbow paper that is capturing the attention of the customers. Others have cartoon characters on them.

Admiring the designer lanterns that have flooded the markets, Manisha Patange, a resident of Mukund Nagar, who was busy buying all sorts of decorative items for her home said, "I prefer to have the akashdeep made up of fabric as they look more attractive. For me, like for most others, there is no diwali without the lanterns."

"Apart from the large lamps, there are also tastefully made miniatures akash kandils that are selling like hot cakes. Especially the 'halogen akashdeep', as they have been named, are in high demand. In fact these lamps are also sent to Mumbai as they are mostly made in Pune," informs Zameer Attar, a shop owner in Laxmi road. Made of plastic or hard paper these halogen akashdeeps are adorned with decorative laces on the edges and stand out as beautifully crafted pieces of art. Throwing light on the hard work that goes behind making akash kandils, Attar says, "We start making these kandils six months before Diwali. The manufacturing requires cooperation of the entire family."

While for most of the market , it's only about selling and buying these designer sky lamps, there is Phiroze F Boocha, of Boocha electric stores on M G Road who has actually underlined his Diwali business with a noble cause. He is selling some of these lamps for a special cause. "I have exhibited some akash kandils that have been made by the inmates of a city-based NGO which works for the rehabilitation of alcohol addicts and the proceeds will go to the NGO," said Boocha. Here's to adding one's bit to make the festival of lights a brighter one in more ways than one.

Heading: Back to basics - Indian Express
Content:
Having won many prestigious International awards Kranti Kanade's debutant film Mahek was publicly screened for the first time in the country at the Asian Film Festival

It has been premiered at the 51st London Film Festival, has won the best film award at the Houston International Film Festival and has even been included in the University syllabus at the Otterbein College Ohio. After much globetrotting Mahek was finally unveiled at the Asian Film Festival for the first public screening in the country.

Seeing the world through childrens' eyes and examining their rights, Mahek is about a small girl's journey towards self-understanding. With many more awards and glory to its credit, Mahek in a way exemplifies Pune for the film not only has most of its cast and crew from the city, but has also been entirely shot and edited here. Speaking on its making director Kranti Kanade said, "Shot in just twelve and a half days, there was a certain faith I had in the kids and the senior actors had in me, that has come out so beautifully. Throughout the making of the film we have lived what we have shown in the film. For instance the set would be a smoke free zone since we were working with children. The embargo made many of the crew members quit smoking altogether. Although screened in many foreign countries earlier I was most nervous and scared about the screening here, since Mahek is born in this very soil."

Noted artiste Lalan Sarang who has played an important role in the film also saw it for the first time at the festival. "I have played a small role which is very influential in Mahek's life.Working in the film has been enormously satisfying because of the respect and admiration the young generation has for us. There are many things that we are unaware of and this coming together leads to exchange of experience and knowledge," added Sarang.

The film has used actual sounds without dubbing and the entire process from the conception to the completion has happened in the city except for the final print in Mumbai. "Cinema is personal again. It no more needs a huge budget or a big star cast or relocation from one's own land. This was the attitude and confidence when I began the film, and Mahek proved me right. I believe in pure expressions and the laurels it has won have been very surprising. I am astonished to see that the more personal you speak the more it resonates all over the world. Mahek has been my most personal prayer," added Kanade.

Heading: Promote ethics, honesty in public dealing: Reforms panel - Indian Express
Content:
Fashion's come a full circle this season with cleaner lines, no-fuss clothing and basic styling, designer Varun Bahl dishes out a quick style guide

Forgive the cliche, but it is that time of the year again when you are busy packing one wardrobe to make way for another. These in-between times can be particularly taxing. Why? Well, simply because you can't really forecast the fashion ahead - is the strappy pink number you picked last year worth stepping out in this season as well and what about the tweed coat, a lucky sale pick? Thankfully, such questions are best answered by the experts. And we all got lucky this Thursday. Stepping in to formally launch the 'Rosebys' store in the city was designer Varun Bahl. For the uninitiated, Rosebys is a premium UK brand which has made a foray in the Indian market with its home furnishing line. "We chose Punjab as the launch platform because of people's ability here to appreciate both the quality and premium lifestyle fashion," mentioned Rosebys' India director Nikhil Sen. And how does Rosebys bring Varun Bahl in the picture? "It's an extension of my work. In fact, I had been wanting to do a home collection for a while now and a year back Rosebys London approached me," the designer answers.

Interestingly, this has been a busy year for the designer. He just showcased at the India Couture Week followed by the Wills India Fashion Week. "I have had so many shows that I think I'll keep none for next year," chuckles the tall designer who is set to hit the Chivas Tour in November followed by a charity show in Karachi and then one in Kathmandu. With so many fashion weeks, designers must be exhausted. "Frankly I just go by the Wills one. There are far too many now and that's not a good thing. Even internationally there are just two," Varun makes his point.

As for what winter is looking like, the designer known for his unique way of combining contemporary with vintage, tells that it's back to basics. "The silhouettes are simple, layering is out and the look is clean," lists out Bahl as we quiz him on the colour palette. "Again, black is big but you won't see it being teamed with softer muted tones. The contrasting colours are bright like pink, orange, yellow." As far as skirts go, Bahl says they have "vanished". "Trousers are in and so are coats." And with the wedding season in full flow, Bahl has a word of advise, "Embellishments are less and if there's something that's ornate, it's only the jewellery."

Heading: Training programme to ensure alternative employment - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana Administrative Reforms Commission (HARC) headed by MLA Karan Singh Dalal has made recommendations which are expected to bring about transparency in the state bureaucracy, cut red tapism and make it more answerable to the public at large. The recommendations for more use of information technology in the government departments are also likely to improve the work efficiency. The Commission has made suggestions for making the police system more effective and people-friendly. The 250-page report of the Commission, set up by the Bhupinder Singh Hooda government, is likely to be submitted to the Chief Minister early next week.

The Commission has suggested changes in the organisational structure and methods of operation of the various government departments to improve their efficiency and effectiveness. According to Dalal, the suggestions relate to decentralisation of powers towards promoting efficiency, transparency and responsiveness in the overall dealing of services. It has also recommended ways of creating a friendly environment where government functionaries are courteous to the public.

The Commission has also recommended ways of promoting ethics in governance and honesty in public dealings, besides measures for effective monitoring and evaluation systems relating to both personnel and programmes. It has suggested ways of e-governance in all state government departments.

According to one suggestion made, senior government servants and police officers in the districts will have to put their office and tour timings on the notice board. The senior officers have been recommended to make more tours of the rural areas to be able to relate to the problems of the villagers.

Suggestions have also been made for the improvement in the police force to make it more effective and people-friendly. According to Dalal, the role of the police is of paramount importance in the state administration, but is not limited to registering FIRs and arresting people. The police has to change its colonial image.

The police must have an administrative wing to probe the validity of complaints received and a prosecution wing to pursue such cases in the courts. The Commission has suggested ways for bringing transparency in the recruitment and the transfer policy by making the head of the department more accountable.

Concerned over the high drop-out rate of students of government schools, especially in the primary and the middle school, the Commission has suggested to give more autonomy to the education system, make teaching more interesting and improve the educational standards in the government schools.

Heading: A book on Hooda’s 4 generations - Indian Express
Content:
Haryana State Industrial and Infrastructure Development Corporation Ltd (HSIIDC) has decided to join hands with Infrastructure Leasing and Financial Services (IL&FS) to undertake training programmes for the people whose land has been acquired for setting up of the projects by HSIIDC.

This was decided by the Board of Directors of the Corporation in its meeting held here today. M L Tayal, Principal Secretary to the Chief Minister and Chairman of the Corporation informed that a memorandum of understanding (MoU) will be executed between the two organisations to crystallise the terms of agreement.

IL&FS will conduct training for skills and attitude development programs to enable the oustees to acquire the required skills for alternative employment. The Corporation will be responsible for undertaking a socio-economic impact analysis in the area where land has been acquired, based on which IL&FS will devise appropriate training/skill development programmes.

Tayal said the state government formulated a policy for acquisition of land for setting up of special economic zones, technology cities, industrial parks and industrial model townships through notifications in May 2006 and December 2007.

Under the notification, certain obligations have been imposed on the developer for providing social infrastructure by setting up industrial training institutes, vocational training institutes and polytechnics for providing training to the wards of those of whose land is acquired. Rajeev Arora, Managing Director of the Corporation said HSIIDC is required to acquire land at various identified locations for development of industrial estates, industrial model township, technology parks and allotting plots to various entrepreneurs.

HSIIDC is also under the obligation to develop social infrastructure, especially for development of industrial training institute, for creating special skill sets to match the requirements of the units coming up in the industrial estates and industrial model townships.

Infrastructure Leasing Financial Services Limited is an All India Financial Institution with strategic focus on infrastructure development on commercial format without recourse to budgetary allocation. IL&FS has worked in partnership with Centre and state governments across various infrastructure sub-sectors including transport, water, power, environment etc.

Heading: Four city buses to ply in Sirsa - Indian Express
Content:
Haryana Governor Dr A R Kidwai released a book titled "Bhupinder Singh Hooda: Chaar Pidhiyan" written in Hindi by noted Sanskrit scholar and journalist Partap Singh Shastri at Haryana Raj Bhavan here today.

He congratulated the writer for highlighting the four generations of Hooda's family and giving a vivid description of the historical facts of the Arya Samaj movement and the national freedom struggle by Matu Ram Arya and Dr Ramji Lal Hooda. The book gives details of their contribution towards the national freedom movement and the non-cooperation movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi. Kidwai praised the contribution made by all the four generations of Hooda family in the socio-economic development of the country. He said Haryana had become number one state in the fields of agricultural, industrial, educational, foreign investment and social development. The CM said that his grandfather, Matu Ram contributed towards setting up educational institutions in Rohtak, such as Jat Anglo Sanskrit High School, which played a significant role in spreading education in the backward areas.

Heading: ‘Debt waiver a gimmick, has hit recoveries’ - Indian Express
Content:
After the National Capital Region, Sirsa has become the first district in Haryana to ply city buses. Four buses will be available on four different routes of the city for the local commuters. For the first ten bus stops, the charges will be Rs 5, after which they will have to shell out Rs 10. The four buses have been purchased at a cost of Rs 40 lakh out of the Backward Region Development Fund. Two 40- seater and two 22-seater buses have been introduced. A city bus service committee has been constituted with Deputy Commissioner as its chairman and Anand Biana, a local resident as its secretary. These buses will be operated on no-profit, no-loss basis. After flagging off the four buses, DC V Umashankar told The Indian Express it was a dream project for the city and with the introduction of the buses the transportation problems of the residents would be resolved. Not only will it make commuting easy but has also create jobs for five drivers and five conductors.

DC said Anand Biana has been authorised to look into complaints and suggestions of the people. Progress of the services will be reviewed on the monthly basis and routes can be denotified if required, he added.

Heading: Customs, IA staff clash - Indian Express
Content:
'Subsidies productive way to stimulate economic activity'

Punjab's loan recoveries have been hit by almost 40 to 50 per cent post the announcement of the Debt Waiver and Relief Package 2008. This was just a political gimmick to win elections and has failed to bring any relief to the highly-indebted Punjab farmers who paid their dues timely, Punjab Cooperation Minister Capt Kanwaljit Singh today said.

At a meet-the-press today, though the former finance minister admitted that the ailing economic condition was the core issue confronting Punjab, he differed from the views of Finance Minister Manpreet Badal on the issue of subsidies. Capt Kanwaljit Singh justified subsidies as a productive way to stimulate economic activity.

"Even the union government subsidies oil and fertilizers heavily. The US and European Union (EU) foot bills of around USD 74 billion and USD 172 billion, respectively, on farm subsidies. Punjab will give subsidy to the tune of Rs 1300-1400 crore for the Bathinda Oil Refinery. Subsidies are given throughout the world to stimulate the economy, and are not peculiar to Punjab," he added.

Blaming the policies of the Centre for agrarian crisis being faced by Punjab farmers, he said the minimum support price (MSP) has not kept pace with the steep hike in cost of agri inputs. "We are trying to usher in a strong cooperative movement to reduce costs for marginal farmers and make farming more remunerative. The agriculture sector still is the highest contributor of state revenue at Rs 2,000 crore, against Rs 700 crore from industry and trade," he said.

Capt Kanwaljit Singh stated that Milkfed and Markfed have been directed to promote dairy farming, and production and marketing of high-value crops. "Procurement by Milkfed has increased by almost 30 per cent in the last one year, but we are still not able to meet the high demand for Verka products. Markfed is setting up a Rs 55-crore food processing complex at Ludhiana, and vegetable producing cooperatives will be set up in villages to grow high value crops. The primary agriculture societies are playing a multi-purpose role, and have become a retail source for agri implements such as tractors and harvesters so that small farmers can save on capital expenditure costs," Capt Kanwaljit said.

The minister added that Housefed is launching an ambitious scheme in five districts to provide houses in the range of Rs 6 to 8 lakh. The scheme would gradually be extended to other towns and cities, he stated.

Heading: State officials to meet software giants today - Indian Express
Content:
Not first incident of indiscipline; lack of coordination among depts

Yet another clash between staff members of the Customs and the Indian Airlines at the high-security Rajasansi International airport here late last night has once again exposed the lack of coordination among various departments.

A scuffle took place when some Customs officials objected to the movement of IA staff members inside terminal building when Singapore Airlines flight had landed. Two IA staffers, including Deepak Sharma and Deepak Niman, were allegedly roughed up.

"They attacked us without any provocation. They said we are moving in the prohibited area and started to push us away, without listening to our plea," said Sharma, adding that they have brought the matter to the notice of their seniors.

"The scuffle took place in full public view. What impression will the passengers get," said Mukhwinder Singh, an eyewitness, who had come to see off his relatives.

Agitated over the Customs officials' behaviour, the IA staffers held a protest outside the terminal building and levelled serious allegations of "bullying" against them and said that they would not tolerate this now.

They alleged that the Customs officials, who misbehaved with them, were drunk. However, Customs authorities denied this accusation.

Earlier too, scuffles and verbal duels were reported between Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), various Airlines' staff and even the Customs over minor issues of jurisdiction of a particular area.

"We are committed to maintain decorum and will ensure that discipline is maintained," said Airport Authority of India (AAI) Director (Amritsar) Arun Talwar.

Terming the incident as unfortunate, he said the respective departments have been told that such incidents would not be tolerated.

Amrit Sarup, Sub-Inspector at airport police post, said he has so far received no formal complaint, though he was aware of the incident.

Customs Commissioner Takleshwar Singh said

they were verifying the facts and would take action against the staff members found guilty. "I have directed an assistant commissioner to look into the matter. No doubt there is need for closer coordination, but it is also necessary that one department at the airport does not interfere in other's jurisdiction," he said.

The airport has witnessed about three hijackings in the past and recently drug couriers were nabbed from here.

The incidents of corruption and mismanagements, delays and cancellations of flights and lack of proper infrastructure had earlier disgraced the airport.

Heading: Spice of price makes rice flavour of Punjab agriculture - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab government will hold talks with top software companies, including Wipro, Infosys, Satyam, TCS and Microsoft, tomorrow to attract investment in the IT sector.

Top officials of the government are meeting representatives of nearly two dozen such companies over breakfast at Maurya Sheraton in New Delhi, where Punjab Industry Minister Manoranjan Kalia will also be present.

IBM, Converges and several BPO companies will be part of the government-industry interaction. Companies dealing in venture capital funding will also be present, besides chairman of Cyber Media Pradeep Gupta.

During the two-hour discussion, IT companies will be offered land in dedicated technology corridors that the government has identified in the run-up to the meeting.

Companies will also be promised dedicated power supply, a decision that the government took on Friday at a meeting chaired by Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal. A commitment to relax existing norms with regard to the floor area ratio (FAR) too would be made, said sources.

The government plans to promote Punjab as an "ideal IT destination". Talking to The Indian Express, Punjab Chief Secretary Ramesh Inder Singh, who left for New Delhi this evening, said the Indian chapter of Tiecon-- a California-based business consortium-- was anchoring the event.

He said, "Two land chunks, one at Kapurthala and other around Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) that is coming up at Ropar, have been identified for IT corridors. We are hoping a favorable response from the software giants."

The Punjab government has sought services of Ernst and Young as consultants for promotion of the IT sector. A draft report by the consultant has been submitted.

Earlier, new industry and software companies were shying away from investing in the state for want of uninterrupted power supply. Even the existing companies were not expanding their operations. A 50-acre land has been earmarked for IT SEZ at Kapurthala. At Ropar, nearly 250 acres will be made available for software units.

Punjab Infotech has initiated the process of identifying land banks throughout the state which could be eventually used for commissioning new IT corridors, said MD Infotech R K Verma. "We'll lay out our strategy and action plan and seek their feedback," he said.

Heading: Fortis-Escorts to start stem cell therapy for spinal cord damage - Indian Express
Content:
Area under paddy grows by over 1.5 lakh hectares in one yr

In a setback to the government's much-touted diversification plan, the area under paddy in Punjab has grown by over 1.5 lakh hectares in the past one year. Area under sugarcane, maize and other crops has decreased drastically in the state.

According to official figures available with the Punjab Agriculture Department, area under paddy was 26.60 lakh hectare this year, while last year it was 24.75 lakh hectare.

"Though I have to wait at the mandi to get my crop lifted, I am sure that at least I will get my money, which is not the case if I grow sugarcane," says Bhajan Singh from Panaundiyan village. "I grew vegetables and sugarcane for three years, but then switched back to paddy," he says, while waiting for his crop to dry in Patiala mandi.

Punjab Arhtiya Association general secretary Harjeet Singh says due to good price of basmati and the instant payment that a farmer gets, paddy has emerged as a more lucrative option.

Chief Agriculture Officer, Patiala circle, BS Sohal says non-payment of dues in sugar mills and the assured MSP for paddy are major reasons for the shift. Notably, the government had been dissuading farmers from bringing more area under paddy due to the depleting water table. "Water table is a problem for environmentalists and the government, but at the end of the season farmers want money," Sohal says, while agreeing that this was a dangerous trend.

Waiting at Sangrur mandi, Manohar Singh from Borjiwala village told The Indian Express that paddy assures around 22 quintals per hectare and each quintal is sold for over Rs 800. "Despite the ban on the export of basmati, farmers sow paddy for high returns," he says, adding that numerous farmers in the state are still waiting for their payments for the sugarcane they supplied to cooperative mills some two years ago.

Agriculture officials said while the Central National Food Security Mission was launched in 2007 for paddy and wheat in the districts of Amritsar, Gurdaspur, Tarn Taran, Hoshiarpur, Ferozepur, Bathinda, Sangrur, Barnala, Ropar and Mohali, there is no such scheme for sugarcane or vegetables.

Joint Director, Agriculture (High-Yielding Variety Programme), HS Bhatti, said, "Diversification has taken a beating, but if the trend continues, it will prove dangerous for the state. We will do something to turn away farmers from paddy."

Heading: Akali leaders opposed to observing Oct 31 as ‘Sankalp Diwas’ in Indira’s memory - Indian Express
Content:
In a major initiative, the Fortis-Escorts Heart and Super Specialty Hospital proposes to start stem cell therapy, the first of it kind in the region, soon.

The proposal comes in the wake of the rising number of cases of spinal cord damage, caused due to increasing instances of road accidents, besides several other reasons.

Stem cell therapy has been used to treat cancer, cancerous brain tumours, heart damage, blindness, baldness and missing teeth, by injecting stem cells in damaged parts.

Experts point out that each month, the district records more than 60 cases of spinal injuries. "Of these, at least 10 require stem cell treatment and have to be referred to institutions in Delhi and elsewhere," said Dr RPS Boparai, Orthopedic Surgeon and Medical Superintendent, Guru Nanak Dev Hospital.

Dr Raj Kamal, Neuro Surgeon at Fortis-Escorts Hospital, added that stem cell therapy is not offered in the region, and is mainly pursued in medical institutions in Delhi and other metros. The hospital is going to start this treatment, as all other remedies had proved to be futile in such cases, he said.

"This is one of the most effective therapies. Patients can be cured just by injecting stem cells in the damaged part," Dr Raj Kamal said. He cautioned that getting stem cells for the procedure might prove to be a challenge, as according to the doctors here, they may not be easily available.

Dr HP Singh, Medical Superintendent, Fortis-Escorts Hospital, stated that the hospital has started a weekly Spine Clinic as an initial step in this regard. Added Dr Gaurav Thukral, Deputy Medical Superintendent, Fortis-Escorts Hospital, "The proposal is at the planning stage, and is being pursued seeing the relief it offers to those suffering from spinal injuries."

Heading: Information sought under RTI not given even after six months - Indian Express
Content:
Ahead of Indira Gandhi's death anniversary on October 31, the state government finds itself in a piquant situation over its instructions issued a couple of days ago to observe the day as 'Sankalp Diwas'.

The government's move has invite the ire of the Akali Dal leaders, who sense a political fallout, especially with elections around the corner.

The Akali Dal has been critical of Indira Gandhi's decisions as prime minister, and has used it as a "potent" tool against the Congress during elections. On Tuesday, the state government issued instructions to its Commissioners and DCs to observe the day as Sankalp Diwas. The order asked officials to arrange speeches, debates, national songs etc on the day, at the district headquarters.

The governments communiqué was in response to a letter from the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). Cabinet Minister Capt Kanwaljit Singh said, "As a political party, we have always opposed Indira Gandhi's decisions."

Added Secretary SAD Dr Daljeet Singh Cheema, "What 'sankalp' do we draw from her? Is it on how emergency is imposed? We have never subscribed to her policies". Officials in the government, meanwhile, said the directions were forwarded as a routine matter.

Heading: Bailable warrants against  Amritsar DC - Indian Express
Content:
Under the Right to Information Act (RTI), information must be provided to the applicant within 30 to 40 days. But there are many cases where even after six months, the information is not given. In one such case, Help, an NGO, has been waiting for information applied under RTI since April.

According to Parvinder Singh Kitna, the NGO had filed its application on April 5 to seek information regarding the recovery of Red Cross funds from those IAS officers who had misused them in their respective districts, during their stint as DCs.

The NGO had asked how much amount was to be recovered from which IAS Officer , the total amount to be recovered, the time period for recovery, recovery method to be adopted from the retired IAS officers etc. The RTI application was addressed to the office of Chief Secretary, Punjab. From there, it was referred to the Personnel Department's IAS branch.

Kitna said the NGO received a letter from this branch on September 1, stating that the information regarding these questions was to be provided by the offices of the Commissioners of Jalandhar and Ferozpur divisions. The letter added that 'warning letters' were issued to these two offices in July, August and September, but till date the information was not provided.

More then ten districts fall under the above mentioned Jalandhar and Ferozpur divisions. The NGO is still awaiting the information.

Heading: More ‘dangerous’ trees in Shimla - Indian Express
Content:
The High Court has issued bailable warrants against Deputy Commissioner, Amritsar, for not filing a reply in a contempt of court petition filed against him.

In his petition, an Amritsar resident had demanded contempt of court proceedings against the DC, Chairman Amritsar Improvement Trust, and other functionaries. The petitioner had alleged that he had not been paid by the Trust for his land, which was acquired in 2001.

Heading: Woman mistaken for animal killed by poacher’s bullets - Indian Express
Content:
The Forest Department has surveyed 50 trees in the town that are standing precariously and posing a threat to human life, for which it has decided to approach the High Court to seek permission for felling.

The process to fell 67 trees is already on, for which the High Court's permission was sought in September after heavy rains and falling trees wreaked havoc in Shimla. The court had allowed for felling of only those trees that

were "posing a danger to human life".

Now the forest department has conducted another detailed survey of Shimla town and photographed all such trees that could cause harm by falling due to snowfall in the coming winter season.

A senior forest official said a list of about 50 trees, along with their photographs, would be submitted along with an affidavit to the High Court in the first week of November to seek permission for felling.

A list of another 200 trees partially damaged due to rains is also being prepared, for which the people and departments concerned would be informed about the required protection measures.

The heaviest damage during the monsoon season this year was caused due to falling of trees after heavy rains. Since a blanket ban imposed by the High Court on green felling prevails in the entire state, the forest department had to approach the court in September for permission to bring down dangerous trees.

The court had granted conditional permission in September for felling the trees and had ordered that the forest department should ensure that at least four trees were planted in lieu of each tree cut down and also it should be strictly observed that no fresh construction comes up in places vacated after cutting down of the trees.
