Conservator of Forest, Shimla, S.K. Sharma said the forest department has conveyed the court's conditions to private land owners on whose land the trees were brought down, the CPWD and the Shimla Municipal Corporation. The tree saplings would be planted either in December or next monsoon, he said.

Heading: Industrialists seek Centre’s help to improve Pinjore-Baddi highway - Indian Express
Content:
The police today arrested a farm labourer on the charge of killing a woman at Malepad village, under Darla police station in this district, today.

The victim, Nirmala Devi (40), was found shot dead in the village forest on Tuesday evening. She had gone to collect fodder from the forest when the accused opened fire with a .12-bore gun, killing her on the spot. Her body was recovered with multiple pellet injuries in her back.

The police summoned over 15 gun licence holders of the area to the police station for questioning, after which it was revealed that the shots were fired from a gun belonging to one Balbir Singh of the same village.

Preliminary interrogation of the accused, Raju Bahadur, who was employed as a farm labourer by Balbir Singh, revealed that he had gone to the village forest for poaching. On noticing some movement in the grass, he assumed it was some animal and opened fire, hitting Nirmala Devi.

On seeing that his fire had killed the woman, he returned home and kept quiet about the incident. Police have also registered a case against Balbir Singh under the Arms Act.

Heading: PTA teachers to approach Arjun Singh - Indian Express
Content:
Concerned over the alleged intransigent attitude of the Haryana government towards the improving of condition of National Highway 21-A between Pinjore and Baddi, the members of Baddi-Barotiwala-Nalagarh Industries' Association (BBNIA) have urged the Union Ministry of Transport and Highways to issue necessary directions for the immediate repair and maintenance of the road.

The Association further demanded construction of Baddi-Kona-Chandigarh road via Jayanti Majri and Basolan-Prempura-Nayagram-Chandigarh link roads to avoid long traffic jams at Pinjore.

It also demanded to issue necessary directions to Punjab and Haryana governments to expedite the construction work of Chandigarh-Siswan-Baddi road, which would help in reducing the journey time.

A delegation of the association, which met the Director General, Road Development, expressed concern over the indifferent attitude of Punjab and Haryana governments and said that owing to the poor condition of the road, thousands of commuters, including industrial workers of over 5,000 industries of Baddi industrial belt, were facing great inconvenience.

They said after the announcement of industrial package for Himachal Pradesh, J&K and Uttarakhand, Baddi-Nalagarh area had got a big boost, which had resulted in heavy industrialisation and subsequently, heavy traffic of both passenger as well as goods vehicles on the highway. They also demanded conversion of the highway into eight lanes for smooth flow of vehicular traffic between Pinjore and Baddi.

Heading: Recession yet to hit home - Indian Express
Content:
With no let up in the state government's adamancy on the issue of stopping grant-in-aid to irregular PTA teachers appointed during the previous government, the PTA Teachers' Association has decided to seek the help of Union Human Resource Minister Arjun Singh.

With the latest statement of the BJP government, where Education Minister I.D. Dhiman said that grant to all PTA teachers would be stopped in a phased manner, many other PTA teachers who had not joined the agitation have also pitched in to save their jobs. This could lend more fire to the agitation, which at one point seemed to be waning after the police resorted to mass arrests of protesting teachers earlier this month.

In a meeting held here today, the PTA Teachers' Association worked out a strategy regarding their agitation to save their jobs. "We have been given time for a meeting by HRD Minister Arjun Singh on Friday, when we will seek his help to save our jobs," said Shishu Pal Gazta, general secretary of PTA Teachers' Association.

The teachers who were appointed by the Parent Teachers' Association during the previous government are holding a protest against the government since March against the inquiry ordered by the government into their appointments.

Meanwhile, the state government is daily releasing names of PTA teachers whose appointments were found to be against rules. Education Minister I.D. Dhiman had last week stated that the government had so far stopped grant-in-aid to 788 teachers who were found wrongly appointed.

Today, the Youth Congress came out in support of the PTA teachers and staged a protest rally in Shimla.

The Youth Congress also submitted a memorandum to Governor Prabha Rau and demanded that grant-in-aid of teachers be restored, inquiry into their appointments be conducted on old norms and a policy be made to give stability to PTA teachers.

Heading: ...but buying spree on at Estate Office auction - Indian Express
Content:
Builders sit back, let buyers down...

The slump in the realty sector has forced the developers of private residential projects across the tricity to delay construction, leaving the buyers in a lurch. These projects were mainly launched during the real estate boom in 2005-06.

"Almost all projects in the tricity have been delayed due to the recession. There are not as many buyers as is the supply of apartments by the developers. The rising cost of construction due to the high cost of raw materials like cement and steel, compounded with an increased rates of home loan and inflation, have added to the woes of the developers," said Pavinder Singh, a real estate broker in Chandigarh.

The liquidity crunch due to a wide gap in the demand and supply, resulting in clogged inventory with the developers, is being termed as one of the major reasons for the delay in construction. The shortage of funds has forced the developers to build projects in phases putting the money from the sale of one phase into the other.

Buyers, who had invested in these projects, are at the suffering end due to the additional financial burden. Those who had invested during the pre-launch or launch, around three to four years ago amid real estate boom, are the ones most affected by the delay. Most of the developers promised to handover the possession within a period of two years, a promise that is still hanging fire.

A software engineer working at the IT Park had invested Rs 27 lakh in Jaipuria Sunrise Greens — a real estate project in Zirakpur in 2006. "I was told that the possession would be given by early 2008, but been delayed by almost six months. Since I cannot move into my apartment neither rent it out, I am losing Rs 30,000 as EMI every month. I am suffering because of the delay — paying my rent as well, not to forget the loan instalment," said the engineer on condition of anonymity.

The picture is no different for other projects. Bollywood Heights in Panchkula, Parsvnath King City in Rajpura and Emgreen Residency in Zirakpur are some of the projects that have been delayed. "Earlier the possession time for Bollywood Heights in Panchkula, as promised by the officials, was December 2008, which they have postponed to March 2009. It is uncertain if they will be able to meet the deadline," said an investor.

The developers, however, deny the projects are delayed and claim they are on the right track. "The construction has recently started and the buyers will be given possession in two years from now," said a salesperson of Parsvnath King City, Rajpura.

The salesperson forgot that the same promised was made two years ago as well.

Heading: Engineering students on tenterhooks as companies sit on appointments - Indian Express
Content:
Response worth Rs 95 crore; commercial sites disappoint, 70 per cent of residential plots go under the hammer

The Estate Office managed to sell around 70 per cent of its residential sites (freehold) even as the response for the commercial sites (leasehold) disappointed at the auction on Thursday.

While 34 out of 48 residential sites were sold with a marginal increase than the last auction, only six out of 34 commercial sites could go under the hammer.

The most-expensive residential plot (2-kanal category) was auctioned at Rs 5.57 crore against a reserve price of Rs 3.15 crore. In the last year's auction, the 2-kanal plot was sold at Rs 5.66 crore. Plot Number 565 in Sector 33-B was bought today by Meera Khandelia, of the Khandelia Oil Mills. Interestingly, Meera is a resident of House No. 564 in Sector 33-B and has bought the adjoining plot.

A 1-kanal plot in Sector 36, meanwhile, fetched a maximum of Rs 4 crore against the reserve price of Rs 1.81 crore, as compared to Rs 4.025 crore in 2007. The plot has been bought by a Mohali resident, Harjit Singh.

In all, the Estate Office obtained around Rs 79 crore by auctioning the residential sites and Rs 16 crore through commercial sites.

In different categories of residential sites, 11 plots in 10-marla category were auctioned while nine in 1-kanal category, four in 2-kanal category, five in 14-marla category, two each in 4-marla and 5-marla categories and one in 7-marla category were auctioned.

The most fluctuating auction price was witnessed in the category of 1-kanal plot. While a 1-kanal plot in Sector 38 was auctioned at Rs 2.68 crore, the highest was sold at Rs 4 crore in Sector 36. On the other hand, the lowest auction price for a 10-marla plot was Rs 1.32 crore in Sector 40-A, while the highest went under the hammer at Rs 1.71 crore in Sector 40-B. The lowest auction price for a 14-marla plot was Rs 1.81 crore in Sector 37-A while the maximum was Rs 2.01 crore in the same sector. At 12, maximum residential sites were auctioned in Sector 40, followed by six in Sector 37.

For the disappointing sales of commercial sites, officials blamed their location. Only six sites, including three shop-cum-offices and three booths, were auctioned today. All the three SCOs are in Sector 32-D, while the booths are in Sector 36-D. While a SCO fetched a maximum of Rs 4.75 crore, a booth fetched the highest at Rs 1.15 crore.

The auction started at around 11 am in the jam-packed Majlis Hall at Shivalikview, Sector 17. More than 400 people had come to bid for the residential and commercial sites.

Reserve price norms changed this year
Till last year, the reserve price was to be fixed on the average of previous three auctions plus a five per cent increase. This year, last auction's reserve price plus a five per cent increase was the norm. "We changed the norms and considered only last auction's reserve price. Considering the response of today's auction, particularly in the category of residential sites, we feel that the reserve price could have been kept higher," said UT Estate Officer RK Rao.

Auction at lower rates than prevailing market prices
According to property brokers and consultants, rates in today's auction were lower than the prevailing market rates. RP Malhotra, General Secretary Property Owners' Welfare Association, said: "While the prevailing market rates for residential sites in the sectors where the sites were auctioned today are more than Rs 60,000 per square yard, the auction fetched an average of Rs 55,000 per square yard, around Rs 25 lakh cheaper for a 1-kanal plot."

Not much increase from last year
Even as the Estate Office managed to sell most of the residential sites, today's auction indicated not much of an effect of the global recession on the real estate market. A 2-kanal plot was sold at around Rs 9 lakh less than the last auction. Similarly, there was a marginal dip of around Rs 25,000 in 1-kanal category. Even the 5-marla and 10-marla category plots could be barely sold at an increase of Rs 20 lakh, as compared to the previous auction.

No takers
Residential — Three 1-kanal plots in Sector 40-B; one 1-kanal plot each in Sector 44-A, 38-A and 38-C; two 2-kanal plots in Sector 33-B and another 2-kanal plot in Sector 32-D; a 14-marla plot in Sector 40-B and two 4-marla plots in Sector 42-B.
Commercial — 20 Booths (in Sector 7-C, 24-D, 29-D, 31-C, 33-D, 37, 39, 40 and 44) and seven SCOs (in Sector 31, 32, Dhanas village)

Average auction price marginally more
While the average auction price in residential plots was around Rs 50,300 per square yard, in today's auction, the average auction price came out to be around Rs 55,299 per square yard. The average auction price for commercial sites this year is around Rs 3.18 lakh per square yard.

Heading: Five students beaten up outside Army law institute - Indian Express
Content:
The plummeting sensex is creating a heartburn everywhere and the heat is also being felt in the engineering colleges in the city and its periphery. Though a number of students in the private engineering colleges have received their offer letters, they have not yet been asked to join.

Talking to Newsline, Rayat and Bahra Group placement director Sandeep Kaura said: "With the crashing stock market, companies have less number of projects in hand. Hence, their staff requirement has reduced considerably. Many of our students have been offered jobs but the companies have postponed their joining. It is not only our college but most of the private colleges are facing a similar problem."

He said only Infosys and Wipro have asked the students to join. Companies like Converges and Birla White have indefinitely postponed the joining of students.

The placements for a couple of students from the Punjab Engineering College have been also been postponed by Infosys. But the company denies the charges.

Bani, HR Head, Infosys, Bangalore, said: "We stand by our commitment and we will continue hiring. We have no intention to lay off staff and advice students to not panic."

A senior official from I-Gate, the company who allegedly refused jobs to students who were given offer letters, refuted the allegation and said: "We have absorbed all the students who were given the offer letters. We stand by our commitment and will hire everyone who was selected."

Sources, meanwhile, maintain that companies have graded the engineering colleges and hire accordingly. Colleges in the periphery come under category 'C' while others like Punjab Engineering College (PEC) come under category 'A'.

While colleges are busy handling the slump in the placement activity, companies are justifying themselves saying by claiming that the market crash had no affect on them.

Manjit Brar, Director, IT, Chandigarh, said: "A trickle down affect has to be there. While we were recording a GDP of around 9 per cent last year, it has dropped to 8 per cent. The worst hit will be the companies that are dealing with those which are now bankrupt. The city, thankfully, is not under too much threat."

Heading: AmEx to pay for refusing refund of lost traveller’s cheques - Indian Express
Content:
Injured tell police that the assailants were under the influence of drugs, police wait for medical report

Five students of Army Institute of Law (AIL) were injured, three of them seriously, when a group of outsiders attacked them in front of the main gate of the institute in Sector 68 on Thursday.

The assailants also tried to run over their Skoda Octavia over the targeted students, who managed to save themselves.

Amit Verma, Abhijit Partap, Shubrit Raj Singh, Tushar Anshu and Akshat Sharma, all third semester law students, were rushed to the Fortis Hospital, where they have been admitted for treatment, AIL officiating Registrar Col Jaswant Singh Sandhu told Newsline.

Acting swiftly, Mohali police arrested Kamalpreet Singh and Yadvinder Singh, residents of Sector 68, and confiscated the latter's Skoda, said Swarndeep Singh, Deputy Superintendent of Police (City-II).

The third assailant, identified as Amanpreet Singh Somal, is absconding.

The injured told the police that the assailants were under the influence of drugs, a claim which the police did not want to corroborate before receiving the medical report of the accused.

Akshat, a native of Gurgaon, told the police that around 1.15 pm — soon after they came out of their institute — the three in the Skoda attacked them.

"Without any provocation, they started hurling abuses and attacked us with sticks and batons," a terrified Akshat said. Amit, Abhijit and Shubrit sustained serious head injuries besides multiple fractures.

Preliminary investigations, however, revealed that members of both the groups were involved in a heated exchange on Wednesday night, the DSP said. The trio accused the AIL students of damaging their car –— an act they wanted to avenge and thus attacked them today, he added.

The injured students refuted the allegations while the AIL officiating Registrar failed to pinpoint any provocation behind today's attack.

Ruling out any old enmity, Col Singh said the students were occupied with the blood donation camp in the campus since morning and after it concluded, they headed for Diwali vacations.

AIL principal Dr Anjana Kakkar expressed ignorance about the incident and claimed she was on leave. The assailants were booked for indulging in obscene acts and voluntarily causing injuries under Sections 160, 294, 323 and 325 of the IPC on Akshat's statement, the DSP added.

Heading: ‘Manufacturing defects mount to deficiency in service’ - Indian Express
Content:
Finding American Express guilty of gross unfair trade practices and deficiency in services, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed the bank to pay Rs 25,000 as compensation each to two separate complainants for harassment.

They have also been directed to issue duplicate cheques to the tune of US $ 8000, which they had earlier rejected.

According to the complainant, Kuldeep Singh, in August 2006, he had purchased American Express Traveller's Cheques for a sum of US $8000. It was averred that after procuring the necessary foreign exchange including the above mentioned traveller's cheques, he visited Malaysia to attend a marriage of his friend's daughter.

He alleged that his cheques, that were in a bag, were found to be missing. He immediately contacted the American Express office, where the officials asked him to lodge a complaint with the police and assured him that fresh traveller's cheques would be issued to him.

He alleged that he was never issued fresh cheques, while they had not even been encashed. He added that without any additional cash otherwise available with him, he had to virtually live on other people's funds and borrow money in a foreign country and thereby incurred a debt himself.

The forum ruled that the American Express rejected the refund claim of the complainant in a "casual and mechanical manner without applying their mind" in such important financial transactions from the point of view of the complainant. The second compensation of Rs 25,000 was awarded to Harjinder Singh in a similar case.

Heading: Civic body decides to grant Rs 5 lakh to kin of deceased fireman - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed Ford India to pay Rs 50,000 as compensation for mental harassment and torture following the complainant made by Colonel AS Waid.

In his complaint, Colonel Waid stated that owing to a manufacturing defect, the air-conditioner of his brand new Ford Fiesta car had broken down as many as four times in just two months of its purchase. The forum ruled that the complainant had failed to "enjoy the ride of his new car" and faced harassment in the form of making repeated rounds of the workshop.

Bhagat Ford in Industrial Area has also been directed to replace the AC with a new one. It was alleged that the car had started giving trouble from the very next day of its purchase.

The complainant said that the air-conditioner of the car was not functioning as all the gas had leaked.

After a bubble test, the original cooling oil of the car was replaced.

The problem, however, still persisted and the oil was changed every time he took the car to the workshop with no effect at all, he claimed. The condenser of the AC was also replaced but the problem continued.

The consumer forum ruled that a manufacturing defect mounts to deficiency in service.

Heading: Efforts made to remove social evils are not enough: UT Administrator - Indian Express
Content:
The meeting of the Finance and Contract Committee of the Municipal Corporation today decided to allot the kiosks in the Night Food Street near PGI on a licence basis.

The committee also gave approval for an ex gratia payment of Rs 5 lakh to the family of Amarjit Singh Mavi, the fireman who lost his life on duty while dousing a fire at a house in Sector 22.

The committee also decided to provide water facilities in Faidan village and decided upon the reserve price of the vacant paid parking areas. It also decided to provide consultancy services for the augmentation of water supply and sewerage system in Chandigarh. The rough cost estimate for widening the V5 road in Sector 26 was also

approved. The agenda for the amendment in the water supply bylaws for supplying water at Re 1 per month to the Institute for Blind, Mother Teresa Home, Chandi Kusht Ashram and the Institute for the Deaf and Dumb was also approved.

The committee also made amendments in the the Chandigarh Hand Cart Control and Regulation Bylaws 1989 and the Chandigarh bylaws of hawkers. The estimate for the beautification, strengthening of parking of the rear side of showrooms in Sector 26 was also passed. The meeting was held under the chairmanship of Mayor Pardeep Chhabra and was attended by councillors Davinder Singh Babla, Pallav Mukherjee, Chander Mukhi Sharma and Vijay Singh Rana. Municipal commissioner Dr Roshan Sunkaria,

Additional commissioner-cum-secretary P K Sharma, Joint commissioner T P S Phoolka, Assistant commissioner Parminderpal Singh, Chief engineer S K Bansal were present in the meeting.

Heading: A day after clash, students blame PU officials - Indian Express
Content:
UT Administrator General SF Rodrigues (Retd) inaugurated a two-day regional conference on 'Health, Population and Social Development in Haryana, Himachal Pradesh and Punjab', organised by the Population Foundation of India (PFI) on Thursday with a focus on child sex ratio.

Strongly advocating the need for an action-oriented approach for promoting gender equality and improvement in child sex ratio, General Rodrigues called for a crusade against the unethical practice of female foeticide, through the vigorous implementation of action plans at the ground level and by making it a mass movement, with the active participation of the people.

Expressing anguish over the lackadaisical approach of our society towards female infanticide, General Rodrigues lamented that the efforts made so far have not turned into a mass movement and have merely remained an academic exercise on paper.

He stressed that the need of the hour is, therefore, to reorient our system to reach out to every village and town, to mould public opinion.

Referring to the measures being taken for social development, General Rodrigues, said various programmes have been launched in the UT for the benefit of the whole region. "We have started a programme-Focus: Moral Values and Civic Duties in Education — in all the 110 schools of the UT," Rodrigues told the audience.

"Besides this, as part of the welfare plan of the underprivileged, the Administration plans to implement a plan for the rehabilitation of slum dwellers under which, 25,000 one-room tenements are being constructed to be given out on nominal rent," he said. General Rodrigues also appealed to the members of the PFI to participate in various social development programmes.

He also released a booklet and a wall poster on the occasion. BG Deshmukh, former Cabinet Secretary and vice-chairman of the governing body of PFI, while speaking on the occasion, highlighted upon the goals of the organisation on family planning, reproductive health and other developmental issues.

He said the foundation

had organised state-level conferences as part of its advocacy programmes in various states and helps them frame their population polices and programmes.

Heading: Students demand removal of S-I Uday Pal Singh - Indian Express
Content:
Students at the Punjab University today condemned the clash that occurred in the campus on Wednesday and held the authorities responsible for the security lapse.

The members of the Students' Council claimed that none of their fellow students were involved in the clash, rather it was the outsiders who had created the ruckus. They also said they would approach the authorities and demand an inquiry into the matter.

The members, during a press conference held today in the Student Council office, said it was not for the first time that students from the campus had been falsely implicated in a case.

Addressing mediapersons, Deepak Thakur, joint secretary, said, "It is wrong to allege that the fight that took place yesterday was a clash between two student groups. Both our fellow students, Uday Bhan and Brinder Dhillon, whose names have been submitted in the FIR, have nothing to do with the entire incident. We shall approach the university authorities to look into the matter."

The students also said that the police was falsely implicating them by holding them responsible for the act of outsiders.

Saurabh, a student from the Department of Laws, said: "This is not for the first time that such an incident has occurred where students from the campus have been harassed for absolutely no fault of theirs." He further added, "Sub-Inspector Uday Pal has deliberately arrested a fellow student, Uday Bhan. When we protested and said we wanted to meet our friends, the sub-inspector pushed Uday Bhan and wrote his name in the FIR as well."

The students have also met Dean Students Welfare (DSW) Prof Naval Kishore regarding the matter and suggested a few measures to avoid any such incidents in the future.

The students said that the authorities should make the Students' Centre vehicle-free as that would help to curb any untoward incident to a great extent. Also, outsiders should be given a gate pass and security should be tightened in the campus.

They have also demanded a ban on the entry of outsiders. The PU authorities, meanwhile, seem to be quite upset over Wednesdays' incident and are trying their best to cover up the issue.

The NAAC team is on a visit to the campus for inspection, therefore, the authorities wish to keep all negative things away for obvious reasons. Wednesday's clash had left two students badly injured.

Heading: NH-21 blocked for over an hour, cops clueless - Indian Express
Content:
The students of the Panjab University today filed a formal complaint against Sub-Inspector Uday Pal Singh Sector 11 police station. The complaint states that he harasses students in the campus and deliberately implicates them in false cases.

Harshwardhan, a UILS student, said, "We have filed a written complaint against Sub-Inspector Uday Pal. The entire student fraternity is upset with his attitude. Uday Bhan, a student, has been falsely implicated and his name has been deliberately added in the FIR."

The students said that they had approached the authorities earlier, with their complaint against Uday Pal, but no action was taken. In the past, SOPU members had sat on a dharna outside the V-C's office demanding the removal of Uday Pal Singh from the campus.

A student said: "It is sheer harassment once an FIR is launched against a student. Half of his time is wasted attending court hearings. The police do not even realise that they are playing with the future of the students."

Heading: Marriage proposal turned down, man immolates self in Sector 20-A - Indian Express
Content:
The busy Mohali-Kharar stretch on National Highway-21 remained blocked for almost an hour after a head-on collision between an Indica car and a Qualis at 9.30 on Wednesday night.

The accident happened after a Qualis, which was smuggling liquor from Chandigarh, collided with an Indica, coming from the side of Sunny Enclave in Desumajra village.

The local police were, however, unaware of the incident for almost an hour.

While Station House Officers (SHOs) of Kharar Sadar and the city police station kept passing the buck, Mohali Deputy Superintendent of Police (Traffic) Raka Ghirra, sent the highway police patrol to clear the highway after about 90 minutes.

Kharar Sadar SHO Dalbeer Singh, when contacted, expressed ignorance over the jam and said there might be some problem in the Kharar city area, which falls under the jurisdiction of the city SHO.

Kharar city SHO Manjeet Singh, meanwhile, passed the buck to the Sadar Police.

While the Indica driver, Santosh Kumar, sustained serious injuries, the driver of the Qualis, fled from the spot leaving the consignment behind.

While large quantity of liquor flowed on the highway, 27 boxes and 10 bottles of liquor, meant for sale only in Chandigarh, were recovered.

A case under Sections 61, 1, 14 of the Excise Act was lodged against the absconding driver of the Qualis.

Heading: Justice Nirmal Yadav’s statement recorded - Indian Express
Content:
A 45-year-old man immolated himself outside the house of his colleague, on Wednesday night, when she refused to marry him. He died in the hospital on Thursday morning.

The incident took place outside the residence of the girl at Sector 20-A in Chandigarh. Sources said that Rajiv Verma, a resident of Solan, was an employee of Hot Millions.

He was married and is survived by two children. "Both Rajiv and the girl were close friends. They used to go out and spend a lot of time together. Rajiv fell in love and wanted to marry the girl," sources said.

They added: "He was compelling her to marry him but she refused his proposal and started keeping distance from him."

Rajiv had gone to her residence on Wednesday but she refused to speak to him, after which, he poured petrol over his body and set himself on fire outside her residence.

The neighbours then informed the police and tried to douse the flames.

Rajiv was rushed to the hospital where he later succumbed to his injuries.

Police have registered a case under Section 309 of the

Indian Penal Code (IPC) against the deceased and have started investigations into the matter.

Heading: ‘After Parsis, Sikhs most prone to breast cancer’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Gokhale committee, which has been constituted by Chief Justice of India to investigate the Cash-at-Judge's-Door case, today recorded the statement of Justice Nirmal Yadav, whose name has figured in the case.

The committee, which is expected to return tomorrow to Delhi, recorded the statements of Ravinder Singh, the alleged kingpin.

Ravinder Singh, who is at present in judicial custody was brought to the UT guesthouse, where the committee is staying. Ravinder Singh was grilled for four hours. The statements of Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) and the Kanungo from Solan were recorded by the committee. After recording their statements, the committee then examined Justice Nirmal Yadav, who reached the guesthouse at around 3.50 pm and was then questioned him for over four hours.

It might be recalled that it is the second visit of the committee to the city. The committee has already examined Justice Nirmaljit Kaur, the judge who had lodged an FIR after the packet of Rs 15 lakh was "wrongly" delivered at her residence in Sector 11.

The committee has already recorded the statements

of Sanjeev Bansal, former Additional Advocate General of Haryana and the other accused in its first visit to the city. The committee is likely to submit a report to the Chief Justice of India by the end of this month.

Heading: ICICI Bank asked to pay Rs 2 lakh for deficiency in services - Indian Express
Content:
In its endeavour to spread awareness about Breast Cancer, Grecian Multi Specialty Hospital in Mohali is organising a series of special seminars on breast cancer. Two symposia were organised at the Government College for Girls in Sector 42 and Khalsa College for Women in Sector 26 on Thursday as a part of the awareness programme.

Similar sessions have already been held in Dev Samaj College for Girls in Sector 45 and HJS Dental College in Sector 25 to enlighten women about the high incidence of breast cancer, the "second largest cancer to occur in the country."

Speaking on the occasion, Dr Shivpreet Singh Samra, MD, Grecian Hospital said, "Sikh women are second only to Parsi women, in terms of vulnerability to the occurence of breast

cancer." Dr Samra emphasised upon the need of early detection and spoke about the various treatments available.

Shedding more light upon the varied aspects of breast cancer, Dr S S Nimbran, Consultant Oncologist at the hospital stressed that routine self-examination, mammography and annual consultation with a cancer specialist are the best ways to deal with the problem.

Mammography helps in detection in almost 50 per cent cases, explained Dr Nimbran.

Heading: Police lathicharge SP workers in Varanasi, over 35 injured - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Forum has directed ICICI Bank to pay Rs 2 lakh as compensation for increasing the rate of interest without informing the complainant.

They have directed the bank to credit Rs 33,000 in the account of the complainant and to work out the interest charged. The complainant, Surinder Singh, had taken a home loan of Rs 1 crore from ICICI Bank, which was to be repaid in 140 equated monthly instalments (EMIs) of 1,26,676 each, through electronic clearing services (ECS). He had to ensure that his account had a minimum balance more than one EMI.

The counsel for the complainant argued that the bank had charged Rs 55,100 as processing fees and other charges for sanctioning the said loan. It was also averred that the bank raised the interest from 9 per cent to 9.5 and then to 10.5 per cent, without informing him.

The complainant took another home loan of Rs 15,33,000 at a rate of 11 percent. He was charged Rs 8,604 as processing fee for the same.

He was then told that the EMIs for both the loans were revised to Rs 1,65,095 and Rs 27,232 due to an increase in the rate of interest as per a notification of the RBI. The copy of the same was not supplied to him despite several requests.

The counsel for the complainant said that after this, both these loans were converted into a single loan of Rs 1,24,00,000. The bank stated that the complainant had opted for a floating rate of interest, which can increase or decrease according to the market conditions and as per the RBI guidelines.

Heading: Recruitment scam: UP clears prosecution of 12 IPS officers - Indian Express
Content:
More than 35 Samajwadi Party workers and leaders were injured in a police lathicharge in Varanasi on Thursday.

The workers were holding a protest on the last day of 72-hour "Ghera Dalo Dera Dalo" stir of the party against the Bahujan Samaj Party government. The SP activists had blocked the main gate to Varanasi Collectorate premises.

Party spokesman Rajendra Chowdhary said the BSP government had unleashed a reign of terror against the workers who were staging a peaceful protest. Flaying the state government and local administration for the episode, SP spokesman Rajendra Chowdhary the BSP government had unleashed a reign of terror against the workers who were staging a peaceful protest. The lathicharge was pre-planned to crush an agitation which was getting huge public support.

The police, he said, were particularly brutal in Varanasi and Jhansi. And in Lakhimpur, Sultanpur, Farrukhabad and Kanpur, over a hundred workers were injured. Those injured in the lathicharge in Varanasi include the former chairman of UP Gau Sewa Commission, Dr K P Yadav, district party president Akhilesh Mishra, party president of the city Paras Nath Jaiswal, youth leader Manish Rai and women leaders Sapna

Agrahari, Janki Yadav and Sheila Chaturvedi.

Some of the injured have been admitted at the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Hospital. A worker, Mahesh Yadav, who suffered multiple injuries, has been referred to the Benaras Hindu University Hospital.

Chowdhary said as many as 181 party leaders and activists have been arrested. They include MLA from Gangapur Surendra Patel, former state minister Virendra Singh and the injured leaders.

In Jhansi, over a dozen party workers, including the MLA Deepak Yadav received serious injuries in the lathicharge, he said.

Heading: Polio vaccines from Central depot are ‘ineffective’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh government granted the Anti-Corruption Organisation (ACO) permission on Thursday to prosecute 12 senior IPS officers in connection with the state's much-publicised police recruitment scam.

The officers include Daljit Singh Choudhari, Officer on Special Duty to Minister of State for Home Shri Prakash Jaiswal. An officer of the deputy inspector general rank, Choudhari was chairman of the two boards which had selected constables in Kanpur and Etawah.

The other IPS officers to be prosecuted are B B Bakshi, Akhilesh Mehrotra, Ramendra Vikram Singh, B S Tripathi, S K Mathur, Chavinath Singh, Sunil Kumar Gupta, R N Yadav, Shailendra Pratap Singh, Malkhan Singh Yadav and B K Agrawal. They headed 24 recruitment boards.

In all, the case involves 25 IPS officers who headed 51 recruitment boards that the then chief minister Mulayam Singh Yadav had constituted in 2005-06 to recruit constables in different units of the UP Police.

The ACO had sought permission to prosecute these officers under Sections 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code. The state government's permission covers these charges. The government has also written a letter to the Centre, requesting it to sanction the prosecution of the officers under provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act. Under the law, officers of all-India services can be prosecuted under the Prevention of Corruption Act only after it receives the Centre's permission.

Soon after the formation of the Bahujan Samaj Party government last year, Chief Minister Mayawati had constituted a high-level committee, headed by Additional Director General S K Mishra, to probe the allegations of irregularities in the recruitment of about 18,000 constables.

The Mishra committee found evidence of large-scale irregularities, prompting the state government not only to suspend 25 IPS officers, but also annul the appointments. Later, the government revoked the officers' suspension, but asked the ACO to formally investigate the matter.

Heading: ‘Ditched’ by Mayawati, Ajit Singh to join NDA - Indian Express
Content:
While the fate of around 4.6 lakh doses of Japanese Encephalitis (JE) vaccines lying in a cold storage in Lucknow is still uncertain, now 10 lakh doses of trivalent polio vaccine have been found to be in Stage II of heat exposure.

Both the vaccines for JE and trivalent polio were supplied to the state by the Central Medical Store Depot in Karnal.

The Varanasi depot received the supply of trivalent polio vaccines on October 16. They were to be used in a routine immunisation programme. The state Health department does not want to use a low-efficiency vaccine when both P1 and P3 polio viruses are spreading in the state.

"We were informed about the heat exposure today. In no way can we use this stock to vaccinate children under routine immunisation. We already have the maximum number of polio cases in the country. Use of this stock might increase the polio count," said a senior official of the department.

At present, the department has put the distribution of the stock on hold and is planning to write to the Centre for replacement.

Since the stock is already in Stage II, it will be difficult to keep the stock at depot without further damage to the vaccine.

"We are waiting for details from Varanasi before we write to the Centre," the official added.

The vaccines were to be distributed in four districts of Varanasi division and some adjoining districts. Under routine immunisation, children in the age group of 0-1 year are immunised for six diseases, including polio. The vaccines are provided in government health centres on every Wednesday and Saturday.

Additional Director of Varanasi division Dr M N Yadav said: "We had written to the Karnal depot about this. According to them, the slight yellowish colour of the Vaccine Vial Monitor indicating heat exposure to the vaccine does not make it ineffective. On Friday, senior officials of the department, including the principal secretary, will be in Varanasi for a meeting and we will place the matter before them."

When asked, Regional Director Dr G K Chaudhary, Government of India, maintained they had not been informed of the incident.

According to sources, Central officials had asked the state Health department to use the vaccine, as the efficacy of the vaccine is only slightly reduced in Stage II heat exposure.

Heading: Mulayam, Amar pay ‘apolitical’ visit to Muslim cleric - Indian Express
Content:
Ajit Singh-led Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) is likely to join the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) for the forthcoming Lok Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh.

Sources said details of the seat-sharing arrangement will be made public, when a poll alliance between the two parties is formally announced.

On Thursday, Singh said: "Our talks with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) are moving in right direction but a lot has to be done." He refused to disclose any information regarding his demand for seats in western Uttar Pradesh.  

Sources in the RLD said an announcement regarding Singh's entry into the NDA camp will be made public after Diwali.

"Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati has not only ditched the RLD leader but virtually forced him to embrace the NDA," a source said.

"The political situation in western Uttar Pradesh underwent a complete change after Mayawati decided to field Muslim candidates from key constituencies. Hence, RLD preferred an alliance with the NDA," said an RLD leader. He added the party will gain by entering into an alliance with the BJP.

"The Congress would not have accepted our demand to field our candidates in major western UP parliamentary constituencies like Aligarh, Mathura, Kairana, Muzaffar Nagar, Meerut, Bulandshar, Baghpat and Bijnore," another source cited the reason behind Singh's choice of NDA.

RLD's state president Ram Asray Verma said talks regarding alliance are being discussed at the top level in New Delhi. "I have requested our leaders to demand seats in Bundelkhand, central and eastern UP. The party should contest at least one seat in these three regions," he said.

BJP's state unit president Ramapati Tripathi refused to give any information regarding his party's poll alliance with the RLD.

"The state unit welcomes any decision taken by the national leaders," he said.

Heading: RCF land allotment: Bureaucrat suspended - Indian Express
Content:
Samajwadi Party chief Mulayam Singh Yadav visited the Darul Uloom Nadwatul Ulema and met the All India Muslim Personal Law Board chairman Maulana Rabe Hasan Nadvi on Thursday.

Party general secretary Amar Singh also accompanied the SP leader. Nadwatul Ulema is a prominent Islamic seminary in central Uttar Pradesh.

Ahead of the polls, politicians of all hues are making a beeline for the seminary. The UPA chairperson, Sonia Gandhi is also expected to visit the seminary soon to meet Maulana Nadvi. The meeting of Yadav with the cleric lasted for nearly 30 minutes.

Later, talking to reporters, SP chief said it was a personal visit and had no political purpose.

"I frequently visit Nadwa and have visited him several times in the past," he said. The SP leader, however, admitted that there was a long gap between his last visit and this one. The SP president said he wanted to inquire about the health of Maulana, who has not been keeping well for the last few months. He, however, refused to say anything about his discussion with the cleric.

Welcoming the decision of the Supreme Court to withdraw POTA cases against the Godhra accused, Singh said it was unfortunate that not a single political party had hailed the Supreme Court decision. Even the media did not properly report the developments, he added. Asked about Chief Minister Mayawati's effort to woo Muslims, the SP general secretary said the BSP should first clarify its stand regarding the BJP.

Only afterwords, it should consider the question of minority's support in the coming elections, Singh added.

On October 13, the Bahujan Samaj Party had organised a national Muslim conference in Lucknow, where Mayawati had announced several sops for the community.

Heading: UPA govt on way to launch new projects to woo Muslims - Indian Express
Content:
Former principal secretary (revenue) and senior IAS officer Balwinder Kumar was placed under suspension by the state government on Thursday, allegedly for not bringing the matter of allotment of 189 hectares of land for the proposed rail coach factory at Rae Bareli before the Cabinet.

This is the second time that Kumar has been suspended by the present regime. He was suspended in 2007, when he was the managing director of the Uttar Pradesh State Industrial Development Corporation. He was, however, reinstated without being served a chargesheet.

Kumar's suspension was on the cards as Chief Minister Mayawati had announced on October 19 that the Net Ram committee, appointed to inquire into the alleged lapses over the allotment of land, had recommended action against the officer responsible for not seeking the Cabinet's approval.

On October 12, the day the state government had announced cancellation of land allotment, Kumar was shifted from the Revenue department and posted as a member (judicial) of the Board of Revenue in Allahabad.

The same day, V N Garg, Principal Secretary to the chief minister — who looked after revenue matters in the Chief Minister's Office — was also transferred.

Lucknow Divisional Commissioner Vijay Shanker Pandey, who was also principal secretary to the chief minister and had issued the order of land allotment, was promoted as additional cabinet secretary.

Later, Mayawati had set up a committee headed by another principal secretary, Net Ram, to inquire whether the laid down norms were flouted while allotting the land. After the committee submitted its report, the chief minister had announced in a press conference that the state Cabinet had approved the proposal for the allotment of land for the rail coach factory.

Heading: No hope of justice in Mumbai, say families of docs killed by MNS men - Indian Express
Content:
While Samajwadi Party (SP) and Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) leaders are openly trying to woo Muslims, the Congress-led UPA government is quietly preparing to launch development projects and create job opportunities in Muslim-dominated villages and urban areas of the state.

The projects include public health schemes,

Indira Awaas Yojna, sulabh toilets, arrangement for clean drinking water, electrification, community and aaganwari centres, training for self-employment in dairies, fisheries and silk worming.

An official in the Union Ministry of Minority Affairs claimed solar lights and construction of boundary walls for madarsas, mosques and graveyards, opening of inter colleges for girls at block headquarters are also in the pipeline.

"In the first phase, Muslim-dominated villages and urban areas of Uttar Pradesh will be taken up," he added. Dr M A A Khan, Secretary of Minorities Development in the state government, claimed of having received plans for 21 such districts. Another official in the state Minorities Welfare Department said the Central scheme covers districts where the population of Muslims is above 20 per cent. These include Varanasi, Mau, Azamgarh, Gonda, Balrampur, Balia and Ghazipur in eastern UP and 14 districts of western UP including Saharanpur, Aligarh, Bijnore, Badayun, Meerut, Bareilly and Moradabad. In each district, around Rs 50 crore will be spent for the development projects. At the initial stage, the Centre will provide Rs 500 crore, another official said.

Several Muslims, however, believe these projects are a part of the Congress' attempt to undo the damage caused by the harassment being faced by innocent Muslims in the name of fighting terror.

Dr Khalid Shamim, professor of law at Azamgarh's Shibli National College, said: "It is a damage-control programme by the Congress government."

Maulana Ahmad Shamim, president of Uttar Pradesh Madarsa Association, too, did not sound enthusiastic about the schemes. "The Congress leadership had not taken any action against those responsible for atrocities on Muslim. It has also overlooked the Sachar Committee report or the report of the Srikrishna Commission on anti-Muslim violence in Mumbai," he said.

Heading: Depressed woman kills infant son, attempts suicide - Indian Express
Content:
The families of two doctors who died in their Mumbai home on Tuesday — in an attack allegedly by the activists of the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) — said they have no hope of justice from the Mumbai police and will turn to the Uttar Pradesh government for relief.

The families of Dr Om Prakash and Dr Mayur Prakash Dubey said they would appeal to the District Magistrate and the Senior Superintendent of Police of Jaunpur, their native place. The bodies are expected to arrive in Jaunpur on Friday.

On Tuesday night, four persons were murdered in Mumbai.

Two belonged to the MNS and two were from Jaunpur.

According to Dubey's family friend Babloo Shukla, the MNS mob had attacked the Dubey home. Alongwith Dubey, Om Prakash who stayed in the same house, ran out for help. "Around 50 activists were waiting outside.

Om Prakash received severe injuries on his head," said Shukla.

"Dubey ran to the police van stationed nearby, but the policemen did not provide any help."

Then Dubey was also attacked. The two MNS activists who had entered the house died when the families retaliated in self-defence.

Two of Dubey's family members, Kamta Prasad and his son Bhola, had been arrested for the murder of the MNS men.

Two others, Satyendra Prakash and Jai Prakash, who were seriously injured, have been detained.

But nobody has been arrested for the murder of Om Prakash and Dubey.

The families say that the Mumbai police are not taking action against the MNS members, although their FIR named three persons.

Bharte, the Station House Officer of Manpada, said: "An FIR against three persons who have been named and against 25 others who are unidentified has been registered for the murder of the doctors. No one had been arrested and we are investigating the case."

Dr Dubey's brother Vijay, who lives in Jaunpur, said: "My family has been living in Mumbai for the last 40 years, yet for justice, we have to approach Uttar Pradesh government."

The family was planning a Diwali get-together in Jaunpur and Vijay had been sent back to prepare for the occasion. He said the family was considering returning to Jaunpur and starting afresh.

Heading: Protest against visit of Islamic scholar, admn seeks report - Indian Express
Content:
A woman killed her five-month-old son Yogendera — slitting his throat — and then tried to kill herself with the same kitchen knife at her home at Campbell Road on Thursday.

Rani was undergoing treatment for depression at Chhatrapati Shahuji Maharaj Medical University ever since Yogendera was born in May.

The incident took place around 8.30 am. Rani's husband Rajkumar, an auto driver, had gone to work and their two other children — Vivek (14) and Kanchan (9) — were also not at home at the time of the incident.

"Immediately after hurting herself, she began to cry. When I reached, I found Yogendera lying in a pool of blood. Nearby, Rani was bleeding profusely," said her nephew Nankey, who stays nearby and rushed to the spot after hearing Rani crying. He immediately informed Rajkumar of the incident. "Vegetables were scattered at the room. She was preparing to cook lunch," Nankey added.

The knife used for the crime has been recovered from the spot, said police.

Chowk Circle Officer Atul Chandra said Rani used to take psychotropic drugs as part of her treatment. "We cannot comment on the case till she is fit to give her statement," said Additional Superintendent of Police (West) Paresh Pandey.

Heading: LU suspends 3 students over hostel dispute - Indian Express
Content:
The protest by a section of minority community members against the proposed Allahabad visit of noted Islamic scholar Dr Zakir Naik has forced the administration to reconsider its permission for holding the seminar he was to attend.

Naik, Sankaracharya Swami Adhokshanand and Bishop A R Stephen are invited to attend a seminar on 'Terrorism and Jihad' to be held at KP Community Center on October 30, organised by the Islamic Education and Research Organisation.

Naik recently drew flak from some Muslim organisations, including Sahar Qazi (city priest) Qari Maqbool, on the ground that he had made derogatory remarks against Islam in one of his discourses, which was broadcast on television.

On Thursday, the protesters burnt Naik's effigy and submitted a memorandum to the district magistrate to cancel his visit. Subsequently, the administration sought a report from the Local Intelligence Unit (LIU) on whether Naik's visit can disturb the communal harmony of the city.

The Muhafize Aja Amri Committee has already announced it that it would to hold a demonstration at the district collectorate on October 25 to oppose the visit of the scholar.

District Magistrate Rajeev Agrawal said, "We are looking into the matter and may reconsider our permission for holding the seminar."    

Maqbool, who had earlier supported Naik's visit, made a volte-face and appealed to the community members to boycott the meeting. He said Naik had hurt the religious sentiments of the Muslims.

"Earlier, I welcomed Naik's visit but when I was informed that he had made some objectionable remarks on the Karbala event, I distanced myself from the event," said Maqbool.

Organiser of the seminar, Professor Mohammad Kaleem defended Naik saying he was a noted scholar and people were being misled by those who were kept out of the event. Naik had never made any anti-Islamic remark, he said.

"If his visit is cancelled, it would be extremely unfortunate for Allahabad, which boasts of communal harmony," he added.

Heading: Farmer’s suicide: Cops wait for handwriting analysis - Indian Express
Content:
The Lucknow University (LU) suspended three students reportedly for disputes regarding possession of hostel rooms on Thursday.

Dilip Kanaujia and Anand Vikram Singh (students of BA), were allotted room no. 114 in the hostel. But with Dilip's consent, Prashant, another BA student, used to stay in same room.

Anand lodged a complaint with Chief Proctor A N Singh stating that Parshant was trying to occupy the room and issuing threats. Following this, Prashant was suspended.

Post Graduate students Shashank Mishra and Sudhir Shukla were also suspended for allegedly entering into a scuffle on the campus over the possession of a room in Habibullah Hostel. The two had lodged complaints against each other at the chief proctor's office on Thursday. On Wednesday, Shashank and Sudhir, accompanied by others had entered into a clash at university gate no. 4. The clash reportedly erupted over the possession of room no. 27, allotted to Sudhir. LU has ordered an inquiry into the issue.

Heading: Given a chance, Maoists will like to join mainstream politics, says Somen - Indian Express
Content:
The investigation into the suicide of farmer Suggar Singh Katheria in Etawah's Moorhi village has come to a standstill. The police are waiting for the report from handwriting experts to proceed.

Bhartana Inspector Jitender Singh Parihar said handwriting experts had collected the suicide note and other written text from Katheria's house. Katheria had consumed poison on September 25.

In his suicide note, he had said that he was taking the extreme step under the pressure of BSP legislator from Lakhna, Bheem Rao Ambedkar, who alongwith a few residents of Moorhi, wanted him to vacate the gram sabha land allotted to him.

In 1996, the "patta" for the gram sabha land had been allotted to Katheria for farming by the district administration. Six years later, the "patta" was cancelled, but the case was still pending with the district magistrate.

Ambedkar had approved the construction of a banquet hall from his discretionary fund on the land.

Katheria's elder son Ram Kumar said over the last 25 days, Bhartana police had made "the best possible efforts to tilt the case in favour of the legislator".

Accusing Ambedkar of influencing the investigation, he said, "going by their conduct so far, it seems that the police will soon give a clean chit to the accused."

Additional Superintendent of Police, Etawah, Dharamveer Singh said: "We do not have the necessary evidence to take action against Ambedkar."

He said following the complaint made by Katheria's brother, a case was registered against Ambedkar and six other residents of Moorhi — Brijesh Kumar, Anar Singh, Arjun Singh, Yogendra, Om Prakash and Arvind. Brijesh Kumar and Arvind had been arrested. They had been granted bail since.

"Without favouring any political party or individual, a fair investigation is being carried out by Bhartana police," Singh added.

On his part, the legislator said the case was politically motivated. "This entire belt is dominated by Samajwadi Party and being the lone BSP legislator from the area, I have become their prime target," he said.

The Katheria family had been SP supporters for years, he said. "Therefore, it is possible that the local SP members had poisoned Katheria and placed a suicide note in his pocket."

Regarding the banquet hall on Katheria's land, he said: "I was not aware of the status of the land, as the project had been approved by gram pradhan Dharamveer Singh, who claimed that the land belonged to gram sabha."

Admitting to sanctioning money for the project from his discretionary fund, he said: "It was for the welfare of people of Moorhi village. I derive no personal benefit from the project."

Heading: From new year, autos to run on LPG: Subhas - Indian Express
Content:
A day after the landmine attack on medical personnel in Belpahari, top state Maoist leader "Somen" said that given an opportunity, a large chunk of Maoist cadres would like to join the mainstream political process.

"We will prefer not to work underground and come out in the forefront, but the leftist government here will never allow that," he categorically told The Indian Express on Thursday.

Somen, whose real name is Himadri Sen Roy, was the CPI-ML state secretary in West Bengal. Arrested earlier this year by the Kolkata police for 'waging war against the state', he has been booked for his alleged complicity in the attempted murder of several CPM leaders and police officers. On October 21, he had to be admitted to the Calcutta Medical College and Hospital for an eye operation. He was released on Thursday. The Indian Express caught up with him as he sat in an ambulance, waiting to be taken back to jail by the police.

"I did not know about the Belpahari blast," he said at the outset. It is very disheartening that innocent civilians, in this case, staff of health department, were killed. "One should see that a planned attack should not affect innocent people. The incident is regrettable."

Way back in August 2005, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh had dared the Naxalites to seek redressal of their grievances through the democratic process. "Every political group that claims to represent the interest of people must test its popularity at the polling booth. Go ask the people to vote for you and support you. Come to the legislature and enact the laws that you wish," Singh had said during a visit to Hyderabad as Andhra Pradesh imposed a ban on Naxalites.

Unlike Chhattisgarh, Jharkand, Orissa, Madhya Pradesh and some other states, the CPI-ML is not a banned organisation in West Bengal. But Somen, on his part, said unlike countries like Nepal, where they even have the opportunity to think about participating in the government, the West Bengal government has always used a policy of dominance and suppression.

"The CPM government will not allow our voice and ideology to reach the general public. They have always oppressed us, compelling us to work underground and refusing to let us exist as independent political entity," he said. "The state government should have given us the scope to speak about our beliefs openly to people," Somen, however, added.

Joining the mainstream
* To participate in the democratic process, a party has to get itself registered with the Election Commission, which registers only those who abide by the Indian Constitution and the law of the land.
* The party should file the yearly Income Tax return to the Election Commission.
* Committees and panels of the party should be elected through democratic means by its members or followers.
* The programmes and manifestos of the party needs to be in the public domain.

Heading: A car unit will come up in Singur: Subhas - Indian Express
Content:
Transport Minister Subhas Chakraborty announced on Thursday that all autorickshaws, running on petrol or diesel, will be off the roads after December 31, 2008. From the new year, autos fuelled by LPG will be allowed in Kolkata and other parts of the state.

A division bench of the Calcutta High Court had directed the state government on July 18 this year to ban autos on diesel and petrol by March, 2009. The court had also asked the state to prepare a blueprint by which these public transport vehicles could be smoothly converted to the LPG or CNG mode by March 31 next year.

The minister said the state would help generously in the conversion process. He said the government has discussed the possibility of loans to auto owners with various banks, so that they can buy vehicles compatible with the new fuels. Autos that run on LPG cost Rs 1,26,000. Banks will give loan of Rs 95,000 and the state will disburse Rs 10,000 to owners for each auto. The balance would have to be paid by the owner.

The Transport department has requested oil companies to set up LPG fuel centres at various places in the city and its suburbs. Only 24 LPG outlets function in Kolkata and suburbs at present. The department will continue talks with oil companies to open another 30 LPG outlets, sources said. It is learnt nearly 42,000 licenced autos run in Kolkata, Howrah, North and South 24-Parganas.

Heading: For once, graffiti makes Biman sing Mamata’s tune - Indian Express
Content:
The Tatas might have pulled out the Nano project from Singur, but state Transport Minister Subhas Chakraborty is confident that another car company will set up a manufacturing plant at the site.

Speaking to media at the Writers' Buildings on Thursday, he said discussions were on with other car companies, which have shown interest in setting up a project at the Nano site. He, however, did not disclose the names of the companies.

The minister had earlier announced that an MoU would be signed with a car company on October 31. On Thursday, however, he modified his statement saying: "It (MoU) may not work out in October. But the negotiations will be over by November/December. Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee will announce the project in due time."

Chakraborty's comments are significant as these come a day after an official statement of the state government on the status of Singur. The government is determined to set up an industry on the site, as the land was acquired for industry.

The status of the acquired land at Singur is marred in legal complications. A petition challenging the land acquistion process in Singur is pending in the Supreme Court. Further, the Singur project land is still in the possession of Tatas and the ancillary units. The land cannot be used for any purpose unless the lease, by which the land was allotted to the companies, is repealed. Chakraborty said it would require some time to resolve the legal tangle.

The Save Nano Committee, meanwhile, continued its protest, demanding return of the Tatas to Singur. Representatives of the committee will meet the chief minister at the Writers' Buildings on Friday.

The district CPM leadership, however, felt the movement for the return of Nano will not produce any result. Hooghly district CPM committee member Balai Sabui said they are waiting for a government announcement on Singur. The party will provide assistance to industrial houses to set up a factory on the Nano site.

Trinamool MLA Rabindranath Bhattacharjee indicated that the party may organise a protest demanding the return of land to unwilling farmers after Kali Puja.

Heading: City sees fourth dengue death - Indian Express
Content:
Mamata Banerjee offered, and Biman Bose accepted. For once, the Trinamool chief and the CPM state secretary saw eye-to-eye. The issue: the state election commission's (EC) directive banning election graffiti including posters, banners and hoardings even on private property during the forthcoming Lok Sabha polls.

In separate press conferences, both leaders slammed the EC, saying the directive curtails the cheapest tool of their election campaign. Bose said: "We have a state law regarding graffiti on walls. In West Bengal, this law will prevail."

Bose said election-related graffiti can be put up on walls with permission by the owner. In 2006, the CPM had written a letter to the EC titled "A case of Reforms", which specified the party's stand on the commission's rights and duties. "Everyone has forgotten the letter. We demand that the letter be discussed immediately," said the CPM leader.

Party sources said despite the EC directive, the CPM will not change its campaign strategy of putting up posters and hoardings on walls.

In 1976, a law was enacted in the state stating that no "visual pollution" would be allowed in the name of graffiti, posters and hoardings. In the 2006 Assembly polls, the issue had come to the fore. The EC had specified that since the state had this Act in force, visual pollution should be curbed.

After coming to power for the seventh consecutive term in 2006, the Left Front government wasted no time in repealing the 1976 Act and introduced a new law, which allowed graffiti on walls after due permission from the property owner, both government and private. Citing the present law, Bose said, "We will take up the case with the EC."

Banerjee, meanwhile, said election graffiti is a democratic right of political parties. "If a property owner has no objection, who is the EC to impose a ban on posters?"

Heading: 72 cases of dengue, over 14,000 of malaria - Indian Express
Content:
He had come all the way from Uttar Pradesh to help his father run his new business. But little did Rupesh Kumar Misra know that far from his BIMARU home state, he would be struck down by dengue in a thriving metro.

On Thursday, Misra died at a private nursing home in Bagbazar where he had been admitted since Saturday. This was the fourth life that the city's dengue outbreak has claimed.

According to the locals, the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) hardly carries out any cleaning in ward number 38, where the death was reported. "The whole ward is unhealthy. There are so many of us who are always ill. Even now, two persons are suffering from malaria," said a resident.

"I could never imagine that my son died of dengue. He was so bright and intelligent and had such a soft nature. I had brought him here as he finished his Master's course and wanted to help me with my business," said Prem Nath Misra, his father.

The 23-year-old youth had come from Jaunpur four months ago. He was living with his father at 7A, Bechu Chatterjee Street.

On October 14, Misra was down with high fever. A local doctor asked him to go for malaria tests. Though the results were negative, the fever did not recede. On October 17, he went for a second round of tests, which proved positive for dengue. He was admitted to a private nursing home the next morning.

But despite treatment, his health started deteriorating. According to his father, the last time he spoke to Misra was on the afternoon of October 21. Since then, the youth had been on ventilation support.

"I had dreams for my son. We were like friends and the last time I spoke to him, he pleaded with me to take him home. I hold the KMC responsible for the incident as it has never taken any action to check such diseases," said an inconsolable Prem Nath.

On his part, local councillor Salil Chakraborty squarely blamed the residents. "There have been cases of malaria in my ward, but this was the first time dengue was reported," said Chakraborty. "We always clean the garbage dumps. But we are not responsible for how residents maintain the drains and garbage inside their house. We have asked them to clean up but they never comply," he said.

An awareness campaign will be conducted on October 27, Chakraborty added.
